T., from which God testified his grace, is not to be separated from the expiations which were made through sacrifices, or from the blood of the victims which were offered for the expiation of sins: since God did not otherwise show himself appeased, except where the blood of the victims was sprinkled toward the mercy seat, Lev. XVI. 14. 15. Heb. IX. 12. 13. 14. X. 3. 4. 1 Pet. I. 1. Rev. I. 6. since without the shedding of blood there is no grace, no remission of sins, Heb. IX. 22. By which God testified that He would then at last be propitious to us, when through faith we present to God not the blood of some irrational victim, but the blood of that true expiatory victim, Christ Jesus, by whom alone He is appeased toward us and grants us the remission of sins. Therefore we are commanded to approach with confidence to the throne of grace, that we may receive mercy and grace, because we have a High Priest, Christ, tempted in all things according to our likeness, but without sin, Heb. IV. 15. 16. God sat, declaring His grace, upon the covering of the ark, in which the tables of the law were kept; because Christ had to intervene for the law with His propitiation, in order to avert the wrath of God which the law threatens, and to procure for us the grace of God, and Christ covers with His obedience and fulfillment of the law our sins designated against the law, and thereby averts from us the wrath of God and the curse of the divine law. But above all, that oracle of 1 John II. 2 must be compared here: Christ is the ἱλασμὸς, the appeasement or propitiation for our sins, etc. IV. 10. God loved us, and sent His Son as a propitiation for our sins; and what the Apostle has in Heb. II. 17 concerning Christ the high priest appointed to make propitiation for the sins, from which it is clear that ἱλαστήριον does not denote only that in which God shows Himself appeased, as Socinus contends, to whom Grotius seems here to be pandering; but rather indicates the very appeasement of the wrath of God, and the reconciliation of God through the blood of Christ, and by no means the declaration of some absolute grace (which Scripture does not know). Since the word ἱλαστήριον itself properly implies an appeasement, as does the Hebrew כפר. And therefore, for the full explanation of this type, if it is admitted that the covering of the ark is looked to by the Apostle, these things contribute: (1) As to the efficient cause, that just as that ἱλαστήριον was placed by divine command, so it was proposed by God Himself as the New Testament propitiatory. (2) As to the matter: because that consisted of gold and wood free from rot; this consists of divine and human nature, which was not to see corruption. (3) As to the number, because there was only one propitiatory in the Old Testament in which God showed Himself propitious; so there is one true ἱλαστήριον, outside of which there is no grace, 1 Tim. II. 8. Heb. IV. 16. (4) As to the object: because that was proposed to all, and the Israelites prayed daily with their faces directed toward it: So Christ is divinely proposed as the ἱλαστήριον to all, 1 John II. 2. (5) Especially as to the use and end: For that was there the revelation of the divine will, Exod. XXV. 22, a propitiation, a covering of the law, a sprinkling of sacrificial blood, which was sprinkled toward the propitiatory when the people were to be sprinkled, for whom the expiation was to be made, Lev. XVI. 14. So also we have in this true ἱλαστήριον the revelation of the divine will, John I. 18. the reconciliation and propitiation of God, 1 John II. 2, the covering of our sins, and the aversion of the curse of the law, 2 Cor. V. 21, Rom. IV. 8, Gal. III. 13, and that these effects might follow, there was need for the sprinkling of the blood of the expiatory sacrifice of the New Testament, which was to be poured out before God for His propitiation, when the true High Priest entered the Holy of Holies with His own blood: as also the sprinkling of the faithful, which is done by the blood of Christ, when their hearts are purified through faith in His blood, Acts XV. 9, 1 Pet. I. 1. And so much for that explanation, by which the covering of the ark of the Old Testament is considered to be looked to here. But others prefer that there be a reference here to the ancient sacrifices, by which sins were expiated in the virtue of the blood of Christ, which those sacrifices foreshadowed, representing the passion and satisfaction of Christ as if to the very senses: For when someone had sinned, and was liable to death on account of the sin, a pure and innocent animal was brought, upon which the offense of the sinful man was placed representatively and figuratively, and thus the animal was killed for the man and sacrificed to God, and its blood was in place of the soul of the man liable to death through sin. And thus the victim expiated the sin of the man, and stayed and appeased the wrath of God. By which it is figured not only that God shows Himself propitious to us in Christ, as Socinus says; nor only that Christ has effected something from which it follows that we experience God as propitious, as Crellius wishes, to which Grotian explanation of redemption also seems to return, but that Christ by His very death and the shedding of His own blood has appeased for us God who was angry on account of our sins, and thus by the offering of Himself made into a sweet-smelling savor has rendered God propitious to us, and has obtained for us the remission of sins. For he is called ἱλασμὸς for this reason, 1 John II. 2, IV. 16, because He has rendered God propitious to us, which word implies appeasement and propitiation, as does the Hebrew name כִּפֵּר corresponding to it, Exod. XXX. 10, Num. V. 8, and כֹּפֶר 1 Sam. XII. 3, Ps. XLIV. 8, which the LXX express by ἐξίλασμὸν: as well as the verb כִּפֵּר which they expound by ἱλάσκεσθαι and ἐξιλάσκεσθαι, e.g., Lev. XVII. 11. I have given you the blood upon the altar to make expiation for your souls, for the blood itself shall make expiation for the soul. Cf. Lev. VII. 7, X. 17, XVI. 46. Which verb is therefore also transferred to the expiation through Christ, the true victim offered for us, Dan. IX. 24. Grotius notes that the words 'through faith' are missing in his manuscript: but other copies and versions do not omit them. These indeed teach how each person may attain true righteousness, but the Evangelical, which is Christ's, not the legal or our own, Rom. X. 3. 4. nor by having faith in the blood of Christ, or the doctrine sanctioned by the blood of Christ, as Grotius perverts it, for there is no reason why, leaving the proper meaning, we should take the word αἷματος metonymically for the doctrine sanctioned by the blood, nor does the mere assent of faith offered to the Evangelical doctrine, but the apprehension of Christ as the ἱλαστήριον set forth by God, or trust placed in him, cause us to be made partakers of true righteousness. Furthermore, Grotius refers the blood to faith, as was done by the Syriac, which others, however, prefer to refer to τὸ ἱλαστήριον: so that it may be indicated that that propitiatory is set forth to us in the blood of Christ. Moreover, even if it is referred to the immediately preceding noun, namely that our trust is founded in the blood of Christ, and enjoys the same as its proper object, it still remains that the propitiatory ought to be regarded here not without blood, but in the blood of Christ through faith; for faith both looks upon that propitiatory and regards the blood of Christ; nor are they viewed separately, but conjointly. Indeed, our trust relies upon the blood of Christ shed for us, without which shedding of the blood of Christ there could be no propitiation, nor could Christ be set forth to us in the Gospel as ἱλαστήριον or propitiatory; whence faith thus looks upon this propitiatory set forth in the Gospel, just as it truly is, in that it exhibits God to us as appeased through the blood of Christ. By the mention of the blood of Christ, however, the active obedience of Christ is not excluded, as Piscator wished, but is inferred: because it is from the obedience which Christ spontaneously performed that it came about that He shed His blood for us, inasmuch as He became obedient even unto death, even the death of the cross Phil. II. 8. and in the passion of Christ, which is called His passive obedience, the active obedience shines forth no less than in the other acts of His obedience, which we commonly call active. Nowhere certainly has it shone more clearly that the Lord loved us, than in His passion and wounds.

εἰς ἔνδειξιν δικαιοσύνης ἀυτοῦ) these things are to be referred to the word which preceded, προέθετο. I would prefer to interpret the word δικαιοσύνης here as goodness, rather than as faithfulness in fulfilling promises, because the things that follow do not pertain to the Jews alone, but also to the Gentiles, to whom no promise had been made. Moreover, the Hebrews frequently use צדק and our writers use δικαιοσύνη for goodness, as in 1 Sam. XII. 7, the Latin translates צדקות as mercies. Ps. XXXVI. 11, 2 Cor. IX. 9, 10, and often elsewhere. See what we have said on Matt. VI. 1. The Greek interpreters mostly translate צדק or צדקות as δικαιοσύνη: but as ἐλεημοσύνη in Deut. VI. 25, XXIV. 13, Psalm XXIV. 5, XXXIII. 1, CIII. 6, Is. I. 27, XXVIII. 17, LIX. 16, Dan. IV. 24, IX. 16. Justin, or whoever the writer is, to Diognetus well expresses the sense here: ἦλθε δὲ ὁ καιρὸς ὃν θεὸς προεθέτο λοιπὸν φανερῶσαι τὴν ἑαυτῦ χρηστότητα.

It must be read as ἀυτοῦ (not as Grotius [reads] ἀυτοῦ) so that the justice of GOD himself is regarded, namely; just as the Greek codices have it entirely. Indeed, these things are to be referred, with Grotius, to the word which preceded, προέθετο: And therefore in the Gospel Christ is said to be set forth by God as a true ἱλαστήριον in his blood, to be apprehended through faith, for the showing of his justice. For why did Christ have to appease God for us with his blood, unless because the justice of GOD demanded it, by the force of which we were under the wrath of God and the curse of the law, whence there was need of reconciliation, which could not be effected except by the blood of Christ? Therefore, the word δικαιοσύνης here is not to be explained as goodness, or as faithfulness in fulfilling promises, of which the former is preferred by Grotius; but rather as divine justice, distributive and retributive, the showing of which consists in this, that the sins of the whole world, cast upon Christ, were punished in him, as Isaiah ch. LIII testifies. Divine justice absolutely required satisfaction, which, however, the Gospel teaches was rendered by Christ in our stead.

διὰ τὴν πάρεσιν τῶν προγεγονότων ἁμαρτημάτων ἐν τῇ ἀνοχῇ θεοῦ) that is, ἀυτοῦ, in the Hebrew manner, a noun for a relative: and διὰ with the accusative here signifies the efficient cause, as in Hesiod. Οἵτε διὰ βροτοὶ ἄνδρες ὁμῶς ἄφατοί τε φατοί τε. and διὰ τύχην, διὰ θεὸς in Demosthenes and διὰ τὸν πατέρα in John VI. 57. Although in this place it can also be taken for the antecedent, from which something is inferred. For he explains how GOD made his goodness attested, namely, by the fact that he passed over, that is, overlooked, the sins committed before this time, both by Jews and Gentiles, with a certain great patience (for we have had the word ἀνοχῆς thus also above in II. 4, and it corresponds to the Hebrew חמלה): for παρῆκας is taken thus among the Greeks, Esther VII. 4, where in the Hebrew they read החרשת in the second person. Thus, to pass over by silence or dissimulation is found sometimes in Tacitus. He wishes to say this, however, that their sins at that time were so many and so great that God, if he had wished to act with supreme right, could have left men in those sins, and not opened a way out for them. Since he passed over, or overlooked, those sins for this very purpose, it was a huge document of his goodness. See Acts XVII. 30, 1 Tim. I. 15, 16.

Grotius rightly notes that διὰ with the accusative can be taken for the antecedent, from which something is inferred: for thence we are justified freely, because God in justification remits to us out of grace the sins that have gone before, when we apprehend the ἀπολύτρωσιν of Christ through faith. Πάρεσις is remission, as Varinos and other lexicographers explain πάρεσιν by ἄφεσιν; and among the LXX Interpreters, παρίημι is accustomed to be used concerning dismissal, which is the remission of sins τῶν προγεγονότων, the preceding ones, ἐν τῇ ἀνοχῇ τοῦ θεοῦ, in the tolerance of God, both because God tolerates sinful men up to that point, until, invited to repentance, they perform it and obtain the remission of their sins, and because they obtain remission in no other way than through the ἀνοχὴν, the tolerance and grace, or the gracious indulgence of God. For in the act of justification and the remission of sins before the judgment of GOD, sins are regarded as προγεγονότα, as committed beforehand, since for those sins which we have designated before, we ought to perform repentance and be contrite, so that through faith in Christ we may obtain the remission of the same. Nor does ἀνοχὴ denote only tolerance, but also intermission, desistance, cessation, namely, of exercising wrath and vindictive justice, just as ἀνέχω is to hold back, to imbibe, to cease, to define; which also means to lift up. And thus God in justification lifts up the sinner humbled and prostrate through contrition, remitting to him the sins that have gone before, which had depressed him like a heavy burden, Ps. XXXIX. 5. And what stands out more in justification than ἀνοχὴ and thus ὑπομονὴ, patience, and μακροθυμία, long-suffering of God, as Varinus explains the word ἀνοχῆς, by which he tolerates the sinner with great long-suffering, and restrains vengeance, not exercising it according to the rigor of justice, pardoning sins to him out of grace. Πάρεσις also denotes the relaxation of bonds, by which pact it is insinuated that sins are certain spiritual bonds, binding us to eternal punishment, which are relaxed when we are justified and obtain the remission of sins. Grotius understands the sins not as committed before justification, but before the times of the N.T., which sense other interpreters also render, and they gather it from the opposition to τꭣ̃ νῦν καιρꭣ̃, which has also been done by us in Theol. Apost. Roman, but in a way far different from Grotius, who wishes the sins of the Jews and Gentiles before the Apostolic preaching to be pointed out; especially, however, those of the Jews, and he thinks that by those words ἐν τῷ νῦν καιρῷ that time is referred to, during which the Apostles preached the Gospel, up to the destruction of the city and temple of Jerusalem: as if to say, God overlooked the sins of the Jews up to that point, but finally avenged them with an extreme destruction. These things are foreign here, where the subject is the justification of man before God, not the indulgence granted to the Jews for a time. That this is referred to here, no interpreter that I know of has said: but they have only noted that, in the O.T. the avenging justice of God did not appear in such a way, and God seemed to pass over sins as if unpunished in the forbearance, that indulgence and tolerance which He exhibited to the faithful, not imputing sins, although no expiation of sins had yet been made, namely on account of the future expiation, just as when a creditor indulges a debtor for whom another has certainly made a promise of paying the debt at a later time, and when a judge absolves a defendant on account of the future satisfaction of a mediator or sponsor. Furthermore, we now judge the previously explained sense to be preferable; because (1.) the subject of justification concerns the distinction of times. (2.) God set forth Christ as a propitiation not only in the N.T. but also in the Old, Heb. XIII. 8, Rev. XIII. 8. (3.) Nor was there a dissimulation of sins there, but a remission, and the same was done in view of the propitiation of Christ. (4.) The justice of God was also exhibited at that time, both in the types, where innocent animals were offered for sinners, and in the oracles, testifying that Christ would bear the sins of men, and that their sins would be punished in Him. (5.) Christ was to pay for sins committed before as well as for those following, to show the justice of GOD. But the reason for that dissimulation is different, concerning which Acts XVII. 30 (where another word also occurs, ὑπεριδὼν, which has nothing to do with justification). But this must be observed, that these things are not to be snatched away as if only the sins committed before justification are remitted to us, and not those which are committed by the reborn after receiving grace, but rather that the Apostle implies that we are in need of justification and remission of sins from time to time, Ps. XXXII. 5, 6. Rev. XXII. 11, and that this redounds to our comfort, that they may have hope for the remission of present infirmities which cling to the reborn, since they have obtained the remission of the most numerous and most heavy sins of the past. Rom. V. 2, 1 Tim. I. 15, 16.

Latin:

v. 25. ὃν προέθετο ὁ Θεὸς ἱλαστήριον διὰ τῆς πίστεως ἐν τῷ αὐτοῦ αἵματι.

Ἱλαστήριον כפרת in veteri Testamento dicebatur tegmen arcæ, cui insidens nubes quædam à Deo immissa, certum faciebat populum de suo adversus eum favore. Lev. XVI. 2. Num. VII. 89. Sic & Deus Christi preces illas ratas habendo & propter eas mittendo Spiritum in Apostolos Joh. XIV. 16. ostendit se benè velle humano generi. Cum autem addit διὰ τῆς πίστεως, ostendit, quomodo quisque effectum illius bonitatis, id est, justitiam veram posset assequi, nempè fidem habendo sanguini Christi, id est, doctrinæ per sanguinem Christi sancitæ, sicut fœdera sanciri sanguine solebant. Vide Matth. XXVI. 28. Justinus contra Tryphonem: μηκέτι αἵματι τράγων κὴ προβάτων ἢ σποδῶν δαμάλεως καθαρισαμένους, ἀλλὰ πίστει διὰ τοῦ αἵματος Χριστοῦ κὴ τοῦ θανάτε αὐτοῦ. Et postea pascha ait figuram fuisse Christi, ᾧ τῷ αἵματι μετὰ τὸν λόγον τῆς εἰς αὐτὸν πίστεως χρίονται τὰς οἴκους ἑαυτῶν, τοῦτ’ ἐστιν ἑαυτοὺς, οἱ πιστεύοντες εἰς αὐτόν. Sed in Manuscripto deest τῆς πίσεως.

Quatuor hic observanda sunt: (1) divina πρόθεσις, quæ ad causam principalem Justificationis, gratiam DEI, explicandam facit; quia gratia DEI fuit, quod Christum proposuerit εἰς ἱλαστήριον; uti gratiæ etiam meræ est, quod fidei hoc ἱλαστήριον respicienti imputet ad justitiam. Πρόθεσις enim illa facta est, tùm in æterno Dei consilio, 1. Pet. I. 20. tùm in Prophetarum oraculis, tùm in V. T. typis Apoc. XIII. 8. tùm in missione & exhibitione ipsa Christi ad officium mediatorium 1. Tim. IV. 10. tùm in prædicatione Evangelii, quo luculenter proponitur ipse omnibus ceu verum ἱλαστήριον, ut in ipso consequantur remissione peccatorum & gratiam, quicunque fide illud amplectuntur. (2.) τὸ ἱλαστήριον: qua voce tegmen arcæ respici admitti potest, ex quô Deus se propitium olim testatus est populo, verùm non respectu solùm intercessionis Christi & missionis Spiritus Sancti, (quæ propriè hùc non facit) sed respectu reconciliationis per sanguinem Christi factæ: nam ἱλαστήριον illud V. T. ex quo gratiam suâ testabatur Deus, non est separandū ab expiationibus, quæ fiebant per sacrificia, vel à sanguine victimarum, quæ offerebantur pro expiatione peccatorum: siquidem non aliter Deus se placatum ostendebat, nisi quà victimarum sanguis spargeba- tur versus propitiatorium, Lev. XVI. 14. 15. Ebr. IX. 12. 13. 14. X. 3. 4. 1. Pet. I. 1. Apoc. I. 6. quum sine san- guinis effusione nulla gratia, nulla peccatorum re- missio fiat, Ebr. IX. 22. Quo testabatur Deus, se no- bis tùm demùm propitium fore, cum per fidem san- guinem non hostiæ alicujus ἀλόγε, sed veræ illius victimæ expiatoriæ Christi Jesu sistimus Deo, quo solo nobis placatur, nobisque remissionem pecca- torum indulget. Itaque jubemur μετὰ παῤῥησίας accedere ad thronum gratiæ, ut accipiamus miseri- cordiam & gratiam, quia Pontificem habemus Chri- stum per omnia tentatū secundùm nostri similitudi- nē, sed absq́; peccato, Ebr. IV. 15. 16. Insidebat Deus, gratiam suam declarans, tegmini arcæ, in qua legis tabulæ asservabātur; quia intervenire Christus le- gi debuit, propitiatione sua, ut iram Dei averteret, quam lex minatur, & gratiam Dei nobis concilia- ret, & Christus operit suâ obedientiâ & legis imple- tione peccata nostra contra legem designata, ad- eoque avertit à nobis iram Dei & maledictionem legis divinæ. Sed imprimis conferendum hic ora- culum illud 1. Joh. II. 2. Christus est ἱλασμὸς, placa- mentū vel propitiatio pro peccatis nostris, & c. IV. 10. Deus dilexit nos, & misit Filium suum ἱλασμὸν pro peccatis nostris; & quod habet Apostolus Ebr. II. 17. de Christo summo sacerdote constituto εἰς ἱλάσκε- θαι τὰς ἁμαρτίας, unde liquet ἱλαστήριον non no- tare id solùm, in quo Deus se placatū oftendit, ut Soci- nus contendit, cui hic velificari videtur Grotius; sed indicare ipsam potiùs iræ Dei placationem, Deique per Christi sanguinem reconciliationem, neuti- quam verò absolutæ cujusdam gratiæ (quam igno- rat scriptura) declarationem. Siquidem vox ipsa ἱλαστηρίς propriè placamen inferat, uti & Ebræum כפר. Ideoque ad plenam hujus typi explicationē, si admittitur, tegmen arcæ respici ab Apostolo, hæc faciunt. (1) Quod ad causam efficientem, quod ut il- lud ἱλαστήριον divino mandato positum erat; ita à Deo ipso propositum sit N. T. propitiatorium. (2) Quod ad materiam: quia illud auro constabat, & ligno putredinis experte; hoc divinâ & humanâ natura, quæ corruptionem videre non debuit. (3) Quod ad numerum, quia non nisi unum erat propitiatorium in V. Test. in quo propitium se ostendebat Deus; sic unicum est verum ἱλαστή- ριον, extra quod nulla est gratia, 1. Tim. II. 8. Ebr. IV. 16. (4) Quod ad Objectum: quia proponeba- tur illud omnibus, & facie ad illud directâ quotidiè orabant Israëlitæ: Sic Christus omnibus divinitùs est propositum ἱλαστήριον, 1. Joh. II. 2. (5) Inprimis quoad usum & finem: Ille enim illic erat divinæ voluntatis revelatio, Exod. XXV. 22. propitiatio, le- gis obtectio, sanguinis sacrificialis aspersio, qui ver- sus propitiatorium spargebatur, cum aspergendus erat populus, cujus fieri debebat expiatio. Lev. XVI. 14. Sic etiam habemus in vero hoc ἱλαστηρίῳ divinæ voluntatis revelationem, Joh. I. 18. Dei recon- ciliationem & propitiationem, 1. Joh. II. 2. peccato- rum nostrorum obtectionem, ac maledictionis legis aversionem, 2. Cor. V. 21. Rom. IV. 8. Gal. III. 13. utq; hi effectus sequerentur, opus fuit aspersione sangui- nis sacrificii expiatorii N. T. qui coram Deo fundē- dus erat ad ejus propitiationem, cum sanguine suo ingressus est verus Pontifex Sanctum Sanctorum: ut & aspersione fidelium, quæ fit sanguine Christi, cum per fidem in sanguine ejus corda ipsorum puri- ficantur, Act. XV. 9. 1. Pet. I. 1. Atque hæc de illa ex- plicatione, quâ tegmen arcæ V. T. hîc respici cense- tur. Alii verò hic respectum haberi malunt ad sa- crificia vetera, quibus expiabantur peccata in vir- tute sanguinis Christi, quem illa adumbrabant, passionem & satisfactionem Christi veluti ipsis sen- sibus repræsentantia: Nam cum peccâsset aliquis, & propter peccatum morti obnoxius esset, addu- cebatur pecus purum & innoxium, super quod po- nebatur repræsentativè & λογιφικῶς hominis pec- catoris delictum, atque ita pro homine occidebatur pecus, & immolabatur Deo, eratque sanguis ejus vice animæ hominis per peccatum morti obnoxiæ. Et sic expiabat victima peccatum hominis, iramque Dei fistebat & placabat. Quo figuratum est, non id tantùm, quod in Christo Deus se nobis ostendat propitium, ut Socinus; nec solum id, quod Christus aliquid effecerit, ex quo consequatur, ut Deum nos experiamur propitium, ut Crellius vult, quò & Gro- tiana redire videtur τῆς ἀπολυτρώσεως explicatio, sed quod Christus ipsâ suâ morte, sanguinisq́; proprii effusione Deum ob peccata nostra iratum nobis placa- verit, adeoque oblatione sui ipsius in odorem suavita- tis factâ Deum nobis propitium reddiderit, nobisque remissionem peccatorum impetraverit. Nam ideo ἱλασμὸς dicitur, 1. Joh. II. 2. IV. 16. quod Deum propitium nobis reddiderit, quæ vox placationem & propitiationem infert, uti & Ebræum nomen כִּפֵּר illi respondens Exod. XXX. 10. Num. V. 8. & כֹּפֶר 1. Samuel. XII. 3. Psal. XLIV. 8. quod ex- primunt LXX. per ἐξίλασμὸν: nec non verbum כִּפֵּר quod per ἱλάσκεσθαι & ἐξιλάσκεσθαι expo- nunt, v. g. Lev. XVII. 11. Dedi vobis sanguinem super altare ἐξιλάσκεσθαι περὶ τῶν ψυχῶν τὸ γὰρ αἷμα ἀυτῶ ἀντὶ ψυχῆς ἐξιλάσεται, ad expiandum pro ani- mabus vestris, quia sanguis ipsius animam expiabit. Conf. Lev. VII. 7. X. 17. XVI. 46. Quod proinde verbum etiã ad expiationem per Christum veram victimam pro nobis oblatam transfertur, Dan. IX. 24. Voces διὰ τῆς πίςεως in M. S. suo deesse notat Grotius: sed exemplaria alia & versiones eas non prætermittunt. Docent autem illæ quidem, quo- modo quisque justitiam veram assequi possit, sed Evangelicam, quæ est Christi, non legalem seu no- stram, Rom. X. 3. 4. nec fidē habendo sanguini Chri- sti, seu doctrinæ per sanguinem Christi sancitæ, ut pervertit Grotius, non n. est, quod propriâ relictâ significatione vocem αἷματος metonymicè pro do- ctrinâ per sanguinem sancitâ accipiamus, neque fi- dei tantùm assensus doctrinæ Evangelicæ præbi- tus, sed apprehensio Christi ceu ἱλαστηρίꙋ à Deo pro- positi, vel fiducia in ipsum collocata facit, ut justi- tiæ veræ participes reddamur. Porrò Sanguinem refert Grotius ad fidem, uti à Syro factum, quem ve- rò alii ad τὸ ἱλαστήριον referre malunt: ut indicetur, propitiatorium illud in Christi sanguine nobis pro- positum esse. Cæterùm etiamsi ad immediatè præ- cedens nomen referatur, fiduciam nempè nostram fundari in sanguine Christi, eodemque ceu Obje- cto proprio gaudere, manet tamen illud, quod pro- pitiatoriũ non sine sanguine, sed in sanguine Chri- sti per fidem hic respici debeat; nam fides & pro- pitiatorium illud intuetur, & sanguinem Christi respicit; neque illa sejunctim, sed conjunctim spe- ctantur. Nimirum fiducia nostra nititur sanguine Christi pro nobis effuso, sine qua sanguinis Christi effusione nulla potuit esse propitiatio, nec Chri- stus proponi in Evangelio nobis poterat ἱλαστήριον seu propitiatoriũ; unde fides ita intuetur hoc pro- pitiatorium in Evangelio propositum, prout reve- rà se habet, quà nempe Deum nobis per sanguinem Christi placatum exhibet. Sanguinis autem Christi mentione non excluditur obedientia Christi acti- va, uti Piscator voluit, sed infertur: quia ex obedi- entia, quam spontè præstitit Christus, factum est, quod sanguinem suum pro nobis effuderit, utpote obediens factus usque ad mortem, mortem autẽ cru- cis Phil. II. 8. & in passione Christi, quæ obedientia e- jus passiva dicitur, elucet non minùs activa obedien- tia, quam in aliis actibus obedientiæ ejus, quam activam vulgò vocamus. Nuspiam certè illuxit cla- rius, quod nos dilexit Dominus, quàm in ipsius pas- sione & vulneribus.

εἰς ἔνδειξιν δικαιοσύνης ἀυτοῦ) referenda hæc ad verbum, quod præcessit προέθετο. Vocem autem δικαιοσύνης malim hic de bonitate interpretari, quam de fide in promissis præ- standis, quia quæ sequuntur, non ad Judæos solos perti- nent, sed etiam ad gentes, quibus promissio nulla erat facta. Frequenter autem Hebræi צדק & nostri δικαιοσύνη pro bonitate usurpant, ut 1. Sam. XII. 7. צדקות misericordiis vertit Latinus. Ps. XXXVI. 11. 2. Cor. IX. 9. 10. & alibi sæpe. Vide, quæ diximus ad Matth. VI. 1. Græci interpretes צדק vel צדקות plerumque δικαιοσύνη vertunt: at ἐλεημοσύνη Deut, VI. 25 XXIV. 13. Psalm. XXIV. 5. XXXIII. 1. CIII. 6. Es. I. 27. XXVIII. 17. LIX. 16. Dan. IV. 24. IX. 16. Justi- nus, seu quisquis est scriptor, ad Diognetum bene sensum hic exprimit: ἦλθε δὲ ὁ καιρὸς ὃν θεὸς προεθέτο λοιπὸν φα- νερῶσαι τὴν ἑαυτῦ χρηστότητα.

Legendum est ἀυτοῦ (non ut Grotius ἀυτοῦ) ut spectetur justitia ipsius DEI nempe; quemadmo- dum Græci codices omninò habent. Referenda verò hæc sunt cum Grotio ad verbum, quod præ- cessit, προέθετο : Ideoque in Evangelio propositus dicitur à Deo Christus ceu verum ἱλαστήριον in san- guine suo, per fidem apprehendendus, ad exhiben- dam justitiam suam. Cur enim placare nobis Chri- stus Deum sanguine suo debuit, nisi quia id postu- labat DEI justitia, vi cujus nos eramus sub ira Dei, & maledictione legis, unde reconciliatione opus erat, quæ nonnisi sanguine Christi fieri potuit; Non ergò hic δικαιοσύνης vox vel de bonitate ex- plicanda, vel de fide in promissis præstandis, quorũ illud præfert Grotius; sed potiùs de justitia divina διανεμητικῇ & ἀνταποδοτικῇ, cuj9 ἔνδειξις in eo con- sistit, quod peccata totius mundi in Christum con- jecta in ipso punita sint, teste Es. c. LIII. Satisfactio- ne requirebat omninò justitia divina, quam verò à Christo præstita esse nostri vice, docet Evangelium.

διὰ τὴν πάρεσιν τῶν προγεγονότων ἁμαρτημάτων ἐν τῇ ἀνοχῇ θεοῦ) id est, ἀυτοῦ, more Hebræo, nomen pro relati- vo: & διὰ cum accusativo hic causam efficientem signifi- cat, ut in Hesiodo. Οἵτε διὰ βροτοὶ ἄνδρες ὁμῶς ἄφατοί τε φατοί τε. & διὰ τύχην, διὰ θεὸς apud Demosthenem & διὰ τὸν πα- τέρα Johan. VI. 57. Quanquam hoc loco sumi etiam potest pro antecedente, unde aliquid infertur. Explicat enim, quomodo DEUS bonitatem suam testatam fecerit, nempe eo, quod peccata ante hoc tempus commissa, tam Judæis quam Gentibus, magna quadam patientia (nam sic ἀνοχῆς vocem & suprà habuimus II. 4. respondetque Hebræo חמלה) transiit, id est, dissimulavit: nam sic sumitur παρῆκας apud Græcos, Esther VII. 4. ubi in Hebræo legerunt החרשת in secunda persona. Sic silentio aut dissimulatio- ne transmittere aliquoties est apud Tacitum. Vult autem hoc dicere, peccata eorum tempore tot ac tanta fuisse, ut Deus, si summo jure voluisset agere, potuerit homines in il. lis peccatis relinquere, neque exitum illis aperire. Quæ pec- cata cùm in hunc quidem finem transmiserit, sive dissimula- verit, ingens id fuit bonitatis ejus documentum. Vide Act. XVII. 30. 1. Tim. I. 15. 16.

Rectè notat Grotius, διὰ cum accusativo sumi posse pro antecedente, unde aliquid infertur: nam inde δωρεὰν gratis justificamur, quia Deus in justi- ficatione nobis ex gratia remittit peccata ante- gressa, cum per fidem apprehendimus Christi ἀπο- λύτρωσιν. Πάρεσις est remissio, ut Varinos, & alii Le- xicographi πάρεσιν per ἄφεσιν explicant; & apud LXX. Interpp. παρίημι de dimissione usurpari solet, quæ remissio est peccatorũ τῶν προγεγονότων præce- dentium ἐν τῇ ἀνοχῇ τοῦ θεοῦ in tolerantia Dei, tùm quod eousque homines peccatores toleret Deus, donec invitati ad pœnitentiam eandem agunt, ac remissionem consequuntur peccatorum suorum, tùm quod non aliter, quàm per ἀνοχὴν tolerantiam & gratiam, vel gratiosam indulgentiam Dei,remis- sionem obtineant. Nam in actu justificationis & remissionis peccatorum coram judicio DEI spe- ctatur peccata ut προγεγονότα, ceu commissa anteà, quum ob ea, quæ designavimus anteà peccata, pœ- nitentiam agere ac conteri debeamus, ut per fidem in Christum eorundẽ remissionem consequamur. Neque verò ἀνοχὴ tantùm tolerantiam notat, sed & intermissionem, desistentiam, cessationem exer- cendæ scil. iræ & justitiæ vindicatricis, uti ἀνέχω est retineo, imbibeo, cesso, defino; quod etiam est sursum attollo. Atque ita Deus in justificatione attollit peccatorem per contritionem humiliatum & pro- stratum, remittens ipsi peccata antegressa, quæ ve- luti sarcina gravis ipsum depresserant Ps. XXXIX. 5. Et quid magis in justificatione eminet, quàm ἀνοχὴ adeoque ὑπομονὴ patientia & μακροθυμία longanimitas Dei, quomodo explicat vocem ἀνο- χῆς Varinus, quà peccatorẽ tolerat magna longa- nimitate, & vindictam cohibet, non exercet secundũ rigorem justitiæ, peccata ex gratia ipsi condonans. Notat etiam πάρεσις relaxationẽ vinculorum, quo pacto insinuatur, peccata esse spiritualia quædam vincula, nos ad pœnam æternam obstringentia, quæ relaxantur, cum justificamur, & remissionem pec- catorum consequimur. Grotius peccata non ante justificationem, sed ante tempora N. T. commissa in- telligit, quem etiam sensum alii interpp. reddunt, & ex oppositione τꭣ̃ νῦν καιρꭣ̃ colligunt, quod etiã à nobis factum in Theol. Apost. Romana, sed longè aliter, quàm à Grotio, qui peccata Judæorum & gen- tium ante Apostolicam prædicationem indigitari vult; imprimis autem Judæorum, & verbis illis ἐν τῷ νῦν καιρῷ respici tempus illud putat, quò Apo- stoli prædicârunt Evangelium, ad excidium usque urbis & templi Hierosolymitani: q. d. Deus dissimu- lavit eò usq; Judæorum peccata, tandem autem vin- dicavit extremo excidio. Quæ aliena hîc sunt, ubi de justificatione hominis coram Deo agitur, non de indulgentia ad tempus Judæis concessâ. Quam hîc respici, nemo quod sciam Interpp. dixit: sed id mo- nuêre tantùm, in V.T. non ita apparuisse Dei justi- tiam vindicatricem, visumque Deum peccata ve- lut impunita transmittere ἐν τῇ ἀνοχῇ indulgentiâ illâ, & tolerantiâ, quam exhibebat fidelibus, non imputans peccata, licet nulla adhuc facta esset ex- piatio peccatorum ob expiationem scil. futuram, ut cum creditor indulget debitori, pro quo alius cer- to post tempore debiti exsolvendi sponsionem fe- cit, & cum judex absolvit reum, propter futuram mediatoris vel sponsoris satisfactionem. Cæte- rum præferendum jam censemus prius expositum sensum; quia (1.) de justificatione agitur circa di- scrimen temporum. (2.) Deus proposuit Christum ἱλαστήριον non solùm in N. T. sed etiam in Veteri, Ebr. XIII. 8. Apoc. XIII. 8. (3.) Nec ibi fuit diffi- mulatio peccatorum, sed remissio, eademque facta intuitu propitiationis Christi. (4.) Justitia Dei etiam isto tempore fuit exhibita, cùm in typis, ubi peco- ra innocentia pro peccatoribus oblata sunt, tùm in oraculis, Christum peccata hominum laturum, inque ipso punienda etiam peccata eorum testan- tibus. (5.) Christo luendum tàm pro antegressis peccatis, quàm pro consequentibus, ad ostenden- dam DEI justitiam. Alia autem est dissimulationis illius ratio, de qua Act. XVII. 30. (ubi etiam aliud occurrit verbum ὑπεριδὼν, quæ nihil ad justifica- tionem. Id autem observandum, non eò abripi- enda hæc esse, quasi solùm peccata ante justificatio- nem commissa nobis remittantur, non verò, quæ à renatis, post acceptam gratiam committuntur, sed id potius innuere Apostolum, quod subinde justi- ficatione indigeamus, & peccatorum remissione Ps. XXXII. 5. 6. Apoc. XXII. 11. nostroque hoc ce- dere solatio, quod præsentium infirmitatum, quæ renatis adhærent, remissionem sperare habeant, quum præcedentium numero plurimorum, pon- dere gravissimorum remissionem adepti sint. Rom. V. 2. 1. Tim. I. 15. 16.

## 3:26
v. 26. πρὸς ἔνδειξιν τῆς δικαιοσύνης αὐτῦ.

He repeats what he had said, as he is often wont to do, when he wishes to fix something more deeply in the minds.

ἐν τῷ νῦν καιρῷ.

Which he had just called νυνὶ. He signifies that time during which the Apostles preached the Gospel up to the destruction of the city and temple of Jerusalem. For these things, which he is about to say, concern the Jews most of all.

This is not a bare repetition, which it is not likely the Apostle would have used in such a succinct and vigorous explanation of so great a mystery. Nor did he change the particles without cause: for he previously used the particle εἰς, when he was engaged in explaining the final cause of justification, just as he also says a little later εἰς τὸ εἶναι αὐτὸν δίκαιον; here, however, he uses the particle πρὸς, when he declares the formal cause of justification. For because he had made mention of the remission of sins, which is through ἀνοχὴν Θεῦ, he now adds to it that which is most closely bound to it, ἔνδειξιν τῆς δικαιοσύνης αὐτῦ, namely of Christ, not ἑαυτῦ, of himself or of GOD. He undoubtedly teaches that Christ was set forth as ἱλαστήριον in his blood, so that the righteousness of Christ might be exhibited to sinful men to be embraced by faith ἐν τῷ νῦν καιρῷ, so that appropriating it to themselves through faith in this age, they might shine with it before God, being otherwise destitute of the glory of GOD, and as most miserable sinners might please God in Christ, and thus enjoy the grace of God. For this is the time of grace, in which the garment of the righteousness of Christ is offered to us, to cover the shame of our nakedness before God Apoc. III. 18. and to clothe and adorn us with righteousness, the filth of sins having been removed Es. LXI. 11. Zach. III. 5. Therefore, the time of the New Testament is not here opposed to the time of the Old Testament, in which there occurs no difference with respect to justification: much less is the time of the Gospel preached to the Jews opposed to the time of their destruction, but the time of grace is opposed to the time of divine judgment, where, grace having been rejected in this age, nothing will remain, when the just execution of judgment, the door of grace having been eternally closed to such persons, neither will any further οἰκονομία or ἔνδειξις of the righteousness of Christ remain through the Word and Sacraments 1. Cor. XV. 24. nor will that apprehension and appropriation of the righteousness of Christ through faith have any place: but being destitute of that garment, they will be cast into outer darkness, Matth. XXII. 13.

εἰς τὸ εἶναι αὐτὸν δίκαιον.

Thirdly, but in other words, he repeats the same thing. For 'to be' here is 'to appear', as above III. 4.

καὶ δικαιῦντα τὸν ἐκ πίσεως ἰησῦ.

God not only shows Himself good, but also makes us good, who believe in Him, as was predicted by Isaiah ch. LIII. 11. ἐκ πίσεως is taken here as above II. 8. ἐξ ἐριθείας. 27. ἐκ φύσεως, & IV. 11. ἐκ περιτομῆς, to signify an adjunct. But in the manuscript it is, τὸν ἐκ πίσεως Θεῦ, not badly. For faith through Jesus is carried into God.

With the manuscript set aside, which is rashly opposed to all others, and that gloss on Is. LIII. 11. rejected, (which passage he indeed rightly understands here concerning Christ, unlike what was done in the proper seat, yet he does not rightly explain justification: because God does not justify us by making us good, or inherently righteous, but by remitting sins, and imputing the righteousness of Christ) we deny here that the repetition is empty, since the final cause is explained rather, how God in justification, since it is done with that reason, as the Apostle had handed down, demonstrates His righteousness, namely so, that it may abundantly be evident that God is just, even if He remits sins to us out of grace, as one who does not pass over or forgive sins without redemption, satisfaction, and expiation, and it is declared at the same time that that righteousness is tempered by mercy, and that this shines forth in our justification, because it does not befall us through works, but solely through faith in Jesus with His righteousness imputed to us.

πῦ ὖν ἡ καύχησις.

He shows how wisely GOD chose this way of healing men rather than any other. Καυχᾶσθαι is a middle voice. For it signifies to magnify some thing, and to rely upon it whether for good or for ill: but here that is understood, by which man, as he is by nature φίλαυτος, hopes for something great from his own powers, as that poet: — — — — I myself will prepare a calm mind. The writer to Diognetus says, that through the Gospel is revealed τὸ ἀδύνατον ἡμετέρας φύσεως εἰς τὸ τυχεῖν ζωῆς. Philo treats this passage excellently in his book on the sacrifices of Abel and Cain.

Ἐξεκλείσθη. It is most excluded.

We shall see concerning the sense of Grotius on verse 27: The mind of the Apostle is twofold, that all human boasting is excluded by asserting justification through the sole obedience of Christ, both active and passive, apprehended by faith.

For thus no parts at all of our righteousness and own works are left in the act of justification. Which also Justin, or whoever else that ancient writer of the Epistle to Diognetus may be, taught in that very place in the words immediately preceding, thus explaining the mystery of our salvation: namely, that we, having been convicted from our own works that we are unworthy of life, now the kindness of GOD deems us worthy of it, and since we cannot enter into the kingdom of GOD from that which is situated in us, it is given to us to be able to do so through the power of GOD. Inasmuch as He Himself gave His own Son as the price of redemption for us, the holy for those who had transgressed the law, nothing less than evil for evils, the just for the unjust, the one who knows no corruption for those subject to corruption, the immortal for the mortal. For what else, says the author, could cover our sins, than His righteousness? in whom else can we the unrighteous and impious be held as righteous, than in the ONLY Son of GOD? O sweet exchange! O unsearchable artifice! O benefits exceeding all expectation, that the iniquity of many should be hidden in the one just man, but the righteousness of the one should cause many unjust to be held as righteous! Thus he. For the same reason the Apostle excludes our καύχησιν in 1 Cor. I. 29. 30. 31. when he teaches that Christ has been made righteousness for us, so that he who boasts, may boast in the Lord, Jer. IX. 23. which is, as Jeremiah has elsewhere (ch. XXIII. 6. ch. XXXIII. 16.) that the Lord Himself is our righteousness, and according to Isaiah, in the Lord there is righteousness for us, ch. XLV. 24. because in the Lord the Savior (Christ Jesus) all the seed of Israel is justified, and in Him alone boasts, v. 25. compared with v. 21. 22. Rom. XIV. 11. Phil. II. 10. Act. IV. 12.

Latin:

v. 26. πρὸς ἔνδειξιν τῆς δικαιοσύνης αὐτῦ.

Repetit, quod dixerat, ut sæpè solet, ubi quid altius vult infigere animis.

ἐν τῷ νῦν καιρῷ.

Quod modò dixerat νυνὶ. Significat tempus illud, quo Apostoli prædicarunt Evangelium ad excidium usque urbis & templi Hierosolymitani. Nam Judæos maximè hæc spectant, quæ jam dicet.

Non est hæc repetitio nuda, quà in tàm succinctâ & nervosâ tanti mysterii explicatione usum esse Apostolum, non est verisimile. Neque particulas citra causas commutavit: priùs enim particulam εἰς adhibuit, ubi versabatur in explicanda causa finali justificationis, quemadmodum etiam paulo post ait εἰς τὸ εἶναι αὐτὸν δίκαιον; hîc verò particulam πρὸς usurpat: ubi formalem justificationis causam declarat. Quia enim mentionem fecerat remissionis peccatorum, quæ sit per ἀνοχὴν Θεῦ, jam ei addit, quæ cum ipsâ maximè devincta est, ἔνδειξιν τῆς δικαιοσύνης αὐτῦ, Christi nempè, non ἑαυτῦ, sui ipsius vel DEI. Nimirum id docet, propositum esse Christum ἱλαστήριον in sanguine ipsius, ut exhiberetur hominibus peccatoribus justitia Christi fide amplexanda ἐν τῷ νῦν καιρῷ, quò eam sibi appropriantes per fidem in hoc seculo, eâ fulgeant coram Deo, destituti aliàs gloriâ DEI, miserrimique peccatores Deo in Christo placeant, Deique gratiâ ita fruantur. Hoc enim est tempus gratiæ, quo præbetur nobis justitiæ Christi vestis, ad tegendam turpitudinem nuditatis nostræ coram Deo Apoc. III. 18. & ad vestiendum & ornandum nos justitiâ, ablatis sordibus peccatorum Es. LXI. 11. Zach. III. 5. Non ergò opponitur hîc tempus N. T. tempori V. T. in quo respectû justificationis nulla occurrit differentia: multò minus tempus prædicati Judæis Evangelii opponitur tempori excidii eorum, sed tempus gratiæ, tempori judicii divini, ubi gratiâ in hoc seculo reprobatâ nihil supererit, quum justa judicii executio, occlusâ talibus æternùm gratiæ januâ, neque ulla ampliùs supererit οἰκονομία vel ἔνδειξις justitiæ Christi per Verbum & Sacramenta 1. Cor. XV. 24. nec locum habebit illa per fidem justitiæ Christi apprehensio, & appropriatio: sed destituti veste illâ in exteriores projicientur tenebras, Matth. XXII. 13.

εἰς τὸ εἶναι αὐτὸν δίκαιον.

Tertiò sed aliis verbis idem repetit. Nam esse hîc est apparere, ut supra III. 4.

καὶ δικαιῦντα τὸν ἐκ πίσεως ἰησῦ.

Non tantùm Deus se bonum ostendit, sed & bonos facit nos, qui sibi credunt, ut prædictum fuit ab Esaia c. LIII. 11. ἐκ πίσεως hîc sumitur ut supra II. 8. ἐξ ἐριθείας. 27. ἐκ φύσεως, & IV. 11. ἐκ περιτομῆς, ad significandum adjunctum. Sed in manuscripto est, τὸν ἐκ πίσεως Θεῦ, non malè. Nam fides per Jesum fertur in Deum.

Misso M. S. quod temerè aliis omnibus opponitur, & rejectâ glossâ illâ Ef. LIII. 11. (quem locum rectè quidem hîc de Christo intelligit, secus atque factum in sede propriâ, non tamen justificationem rectè explicat: quia non bonos nos, vel inhæsivè justos efficiendo Deus nos justificat, sed peccata remittendo, & justitiam Christi imputando) negamus hic inanem esse repetitionem, quum explicetur potiùs causa finalis, quomodo Deus in justificatione, cum ea ratione fit, uti tradiderat Apostolus, justitiam suam demonstret, nimirum ita, ut abundè constet, Deum justum esse, etsi nobis ex gratia peccata remittat, utpote qui non sine redemptione, satisfactione, & expiatione peccata transmittit, vel condonat, ac declaretur simul temperatam esse illam justitiam misericordiâ, idque pellucere in nostri justificatione, quod ea non per opera nobis obtingat, sed unicè per fidem in Jesum ejus justitiâ nobis imputatâ.

πῦ ὖν ἡ καύχησις.

Ostendit, quàm sapienter DEUS hanc potiùs viam sa- nandi homines, quam aliam ullam elegerit. Καυχᾶσθαι vox media. Significat enim rem aliquam magnifacere, eáque niti sive benè, sive malè: sed hic ea intelligitur, qua homo, ut est naturâ φίλαυτος, magnum aliquid sperat de viribus suis, ut ille poëta : — — — — æquum animum ipse parabo. Scriptor ad Diognetum ait, per Evangelium patefieri τὸ ἀδύνατον ἡμετέρας φύσεως εἰς τὸ τυχεῖν ζωῆς. Tractat hunc locum egregiè Philo libro de sacrificiis Abelis & Caini.

Ἐξεκλείσθη. Exclusissima est.

De sensu Grotii vers. 27. videbimus: Gemina Apostoli mens est, excludi omnem gloriationem humanam assertâ justificatione per solam Christi obedientiam cùm activam tùm passivam, fide ap- prehensam.

Ita enim nullæ prorsus partes relin- quuntur nostræ justitiæ propriisque operibus in actu justificationis. Quod etiam Justinus, vel quis- quis alius antiquus ille Scriptor sit Epistolæ ad Dio- gnetum, eopse loco verbis immediatè præceden- tibus docuit, ita mysterium salutis nostræ expli- cans: quod nempè convictos è propriis operibus nos vitâ esse indignos, nunc DEI benignitas nos eâ dignetur, & quum non possimus ex eo, quod in nobis situm est, in regnum DEI ingredi, per potentiam DEI nobis id posse detur. Siquidem proprium ipse Filium redemptionis pretium pro nobis dederit san- ctum pro iis, qui legem transgressi erant, nihil mi- nùs quam malum pro malis, justum pro injustis, corruptionis nescium pro obnoxiis corruptioni, im- mortalem pro mortalibus. Quid enim, inquit au- tor, aliud peccata nostra potuit tegere, quam ejus justitia? in quo alio nos iniqui & impii pro justis haberi possumus, quàm in SOLO DEI Filio? O dulcem permutationem! O impervestigabile artifi- cium! O beneficia expectationem omnem superan- tia, ut iniquitas quidem multorum in justo uno abs- condatur, justitia autem unius faciat, ut multi in- justi pro justis habeantur! Hæc ille. Eadem ratio- ne καύχησιν nostram excludit Apostolus 1. Cor. I. 29. 30. 31. cum Christum nobis factum esse justitiam docet, ut qui gloriatur, in Domino glorietur, Jer. IX. 23. quod nempè, uti Jeremias alibi habet (c. XXIII. 6. c. XXXIII. 16.) Dominus ipse sit justitia nostra, & juxta Esaiam, in Domino nobis sit justitia, c. XLV. 24. quia in Domino Salvatore (Christo Jesu) ju- stificatur omne semen Israël, inque eo gloriatur uni- ce, v. 25. collato cum v. 21. 22. Rom. XIV. 11. Phil. II. 10. Act. IV. 12.

## 3:27
V. 27. By what law.

This law, as the following sections show, is taken more broadly for every rule of living.

of works.

Namely, those which, performed by human strength, accustom a man to a certain civil life, such as the law of Moses requires. Augustine in the sermons edited by that excellent man Jacques Sirmond: The fear of men perhaps can restrain the flesh from impurity: but the fear of God alone can restrain the soul.

not.

Certainly not: for often there is not even a need for them to cleanse the heart.

but by the law of faith.

Because God gives righteousness not through labor, but through faith, and He gives faith through the unexpected revelation of heavenly goods, most clear and most certain. Therefore, all things are not from those things which men can accomplish by themselves, but from the benefit of God. Wherefore there is nothing for which we should have confidence in the powers of our nature: we must rely on GOD: all things must be attributed to GOD. This method of healing both makes men most modest and is highly glorious to God. Philo noted the figure of this matter in Noah in his book of Allegories. For he says that he found grace in the sight of the Lord God, having done nothing beforehand.

By works, whose rule is designated by the law in this place, boasting is denied to be excluded, Grotius wrongly understands only works which, performed by human strength, accustom one to a certain civil life: in almost the same way as the Papists wish for works alone to be understood, done from the powers of free will without grace:

See Bellarmine, book 1, on Justification, chapter 19, who gathers this from the pronoun added in the Vulgate, 'of your deeds,' but this is held neither in the Greek nor in the Syriac text, nor in the Clementine Latin edition. That works are wrongly restricted in this way is clear, (1.) because all works universally are designated here, and what is said here about excluded boasting is declared in the following chapter by the example of Abraham, who was established in the midst of a course of good works, as one of whom, even though equipped with works done through grace, it is denied that he had a boasting of righteousness before God. (2.) Because the works of the law are named. But the law is not a norm only of works done by human strength for a certain civil life, but of any good works whatsoever, internal, external, done before regeneration and after the same. (3.) If the reborn had any boasting before GOD from works done by faith in any part of righteousness, they would certainly not boast in the Lord alone, in whom, however, we are taught that one must boast alone, Isa. XLV. 25, Jerem. IX. 24, Dan. IX. 18, Luke XVII. 10, 1 Cor. I. 21, Eph. II. 9, Phil. III. 3.

Furthermore, Grotius says, as far as appears, in an Arminian and Socinian sense, that faith is given through an unexpected revelation of heavenly goods, as if the revelation of eternal life were sufficient for faith, for which, however, there is absolute need of the revelation of Christ's redemption from death and eternal condemnation, and of the acquisition of eternal life made through Christ, which as each of the faithful applies to himself, as having been performed for all and acquired for all: so through faith in Christ he obtains remission of guilt and punishment, and the gift of life and salvation. And by this doctrine of faith, which the Apostle calls the law of faith, in a Hebrew phrase, because תורה (law) denotes doctrine generally, boasting is utterly excluded, as it is taught thereby that righteousness valid before God must be sought in Christ alone: not likewise through the law or doctrine of works. For although the law of deeds convicts and condemns us of sin, and thus takes away from us all boasting in truth; yet according to man, and from the preconceived opinion of the Jews, as if the law were given not only for this end, that we might be justified through it, but also that one might be absolved by those precepts which can be entirely fulfilled by us, or that the observance of the law, however much it can be performed by us, might contribute some Symbolum to our justification and salvation, boasting is not excluded by the law of deeds, but boasting is left to works either in full or at least in some part. Isidorus Clarius Brixianus in his Annotations on the N.T., printed with the Antwerp text on chapter III of Romans, says: God alone can provide righteousness, since He alone is righteous. The reason for boasting is excluded, and the law of faith has achieved this, that we might learn that he who boasts, boasts in vain, and the law of faith shows man how much he is nothing of himself, and relies solely on the beneficence of GOD.

Latin:

V. 27. Διὰ ποίε νόμε.

Νόμος hic, ut sequentia ostendunt, laxiùs sumit pro omni vivendi regula.

τῶν ἔργων.

Nempè quæ humanis viribus præstita hominem affue- faciunt ad civilem quandam vitam, qualem exigit lex Mo- sis. Augustinus in sermonibus à viro optimo Jacobo Sir- mondo editis : Timor hominum fortè potest carnem ab im- munditia temperare: animam autem nonnisi timor Dei.

ὐχί.

Non sanè: nam illis sæpè ne opus quidem ad cor re- purgandum.

ἀλλὰ διὰ νόμε πίσεως.

Quia justitiam Deus dat non per laborem, sed per fi- dem, & fidem dat per non expectatam revelationem cœ- lestium bonorum, clarissimam & certissimam. Omnia ergò non ex eis, quæ homines per se efficere possunt, sed ex Dei beneficio. Quare nihil est, quod fiduciam in naturæ nostræ viribus habeamus: DEO nitendum: DEO omnia accepta ferenda sunt. Hæc sanandi ratio & homines mo- destissimos facit, & Deo summè gloriosa est. Figuram hu- jus rei in Noë Philo notavit libro ἀλληγορῶν. Ait enim eum χάριν ἑυρεῖν ἐναντίον κυρίου τῶ Θεῶ μηδὲν πρότερον ἐργασά- μενον.

Per τὰ ἔργα, quorum regulâ lege h. l. designa- tâ, excludi gloriatio negatur, Grotius perperam opera solùm intelligit, quæ humanis viribus præ- stita assuefaciant ad civilem quandam vitam: eo- dem ferè modo, uti Papistæ opera sola intelligi volunt ex viribus liberi arbitrii sine gratia facta:

vid. Bellarm. l. 1. de Justific. c. 19. qui id colligit è pronomine in vulgata addito, factorum Tuorum, sed id nec in Græco, nec in Syriaco textu habetur, neque in Clementina editione Latina. Perperam autem ita restringi opera, patet, (1.) quia univer- saliter opera omnia hic designantur, & quod hic de exclusa gloriatione dicitur, Abrahami in me- dio cursu bonorum operum constituti exemplo de- claratur cap. sequenti, utpote de quo, etsi instru- cto operibus per gratiam factis, negatur, quod gloriationem justitiæ coram Deo habuerit. (2.) Quia legis opera nominantur. At lex non est nor- ma tantùm operum humanis viribus ad civilem quandam vitam factorum, sed quorumvis bono- rum operum, internorum, externorum, ante rege- nerationem, & post eandem factorum. (3.) Si renati ulla parte justitiæ gloriationem haberent coram DEO ex operibus ex fide factis, utique in solo Do- mino non gloriarentur, in quo verò solo glorian- dum esse docemur Esa. XLV. 25. Jerem. IX. 24. Dan. IX. 18. Luc. XVII. 10. 1. Cor. I. 21. Eph. II. 9. Phil. III. 3.

Porro fidem per non exspectatam revelationem cœlestium bonorum dari, Arminiano & Sociniano, quantum apparet, sensu dicit Grotius, quasi reve- latio æternæ vitæ ad fidem sufficiat, ad quam verò omninò opus est revelatione redemtionis Christi à morte & æterna condemnatione, & acquisitionis vi- tæ æternæ per Christum factæ, quam uti quisque fi- delium sibi applicat, ceu pro omnibus præstitam, & omnibus acquisitam: ita per fidem in Christum re- missionem culpæ, & pœnæ, ac donum vitæ, & salutis consequitur. Atque hac doctrina fidei, quam le- gem fidei vocat Apostolus, phrasi Ebræâ, quia תורה lex doctrinam generatim notat, excluditur penitus gloriatio, utpote quà docetur, in solo Christo esse justitiam coram Deo valentem quæ- rendam: non item per legem vel doctrinam ope- rum. Quanquam enim lex factorum nos peccati convingat, & condemnet, adeoque omnem glo- riationem κατ᾿ ἀλήθειαν nobis adimat; κατ᾿ ἀνθρω- πον tamen, & ex præconcepta Judæorum opinione, quasi lex non tantùm hoc fine data sit, ut per eam justificaremur, sed etiam iis absolvatur præ- ceptis, quæ omninò à nobis impleri possint, vel legis observatio, quantacunque à nobis præstari queat, Symbolum aliquod conferat ad nostri ju- stificationem & salutem, per legem factorum non excluditur gloriatio, sed vel in folidum gloriatio operibus relinquitur, vel minimum aliqua ex par- te. Isidorus Clarius Brixianus in Annot. in N. T. cum textu Antverp. excusis in c. III. ad Rom. So- lus Deus, inquit, justitiam præstare potest, cum so- lus sit justus. Exclusa est gloriandi ratio & lex fi- dei id præstitit, ut disceremus, cum, qui gloriaretur, frustrà gloriari, & fidei lex ostendit homini, quan- tum per se nihil sit, & sola nitatur DEI bene- ficentia.

## 3:28
V. 28. Λογιζόμεθα ἷν πίσει δικαιοῦσθαι ἄνθρωπον.

In the Manuscript it is λογιζόμεθα γὰρ: as if he were saying: For we think these things, which we ought to think, that righteousness has come to us without labor as a gift of God. Thus λογίζεσθαι is taken in Mark XI. 31, Heb. XI. 19, 2 Cor. IX. 7, Phil. IV. 8. This thought represses that boasting.

An old manuscript codex cannot prejudice all others; and the continuity of the Apostolic treatment or disputation teaches that an inference is instituted here from those things which have already been disputed, just as the word λογίζεσθαι also imports a logical inference, or a conclusion deduced from premises; where Theophylact explained it, συλλογιζόμεθα, we gather by arguing, and Augustine in 'On the Spirit and the Letter,' chapter 13, rendered it WE GATHER. Xenophon, book 1 of the Cyropaedia, 'ἐκείνων δὲ ἐπελάτο ἅ ποτε ἐγω καὶ σὺ ἐλογιζόμεθα,' which we concluded with firm reasons. Therefore the Vulgate is not correct: 'We think therefore'; since it should rather be rendered: We reason therefore: we firmly conclude by comparing the weight of reasons. Cf. Rom. VIII. 18. For the justification of faith ascribes all glory to God in full, the justification of works leaves boasting to man; such as, however, can be worth nothing in the eyes of GOD. And therefore we conclude that a man is justified by faith alone without works done according to the law, so that he who boasts, may boast only in GOD.

χωρὶς ἔργων νόμε.

Without the works of the law: that is, even if the works of the law are absent, as was happening among the Gentiles.

Was it then happening among the Jews with the works of the law? Nay, the Apostle teaches that both Jews and Gentiles are justified by faith alone without the works of the law: and he excludes the works of the law altogether from the article of justification:

Therefore, the blessed Luther, wishing to correctly express the emphasis of the Apostle's words, employed an exclusive particle, which, although it does not occur here ῥητῶς (expressly), is nevertheless contained κατὰ διάνοιαν (according to the sense) in the Apostle's discourse, ohn deß Gesetzes Werck, that is, alone through faith, as is explicitly held in the parallel passage, not unless ἐὰν μὴ through faith we are justified Gal. II. 16. which particle ἐὰν μὴ and εἰμὴ Dietenberger himself not rarely rendered by the word Allein: just as Eccius also explained it in Ap. XXI. ult. The Jesuit Hunnaeus acknowledges in prodidagm. Dial. sol. 31. that an exclusive is equivalent to 'only' or 'alone' in a locution affirming something about one thing and denying the same about another. But such is the opposition here: faith justifies, not works. Therefore, this exclusive is equivalent to: we are justified by faith alone. And what else is it to be justified by faith without works, than to be justified by faith alone? In what manner the blessed Luther solidly defended the little word Allein in his version—on account of which the Papists make an amazing amount of noise—from German idiom, he himself T. V. Jen. Germ. f. 141. 143. He was preceded in similar examples by Holy Scripture, Conf. Deut. VI. 13. 14. with Matth. IV. 10. and Marc. XIII. 32. with Matth. XXIV. 36. He was preceded by the LXX Interpreters Gen. III. 11. τότε μόνη μὴ φαγεῖν. Deut. VI. 13. ἀυτῶ μόνῳ λατρέυσεις see XXIII. 9. 2. Deut. XII. 32. XXII. 27. XXXII. 19. 1. Samuel. X. 19. XVIII. 8. 2. Reg. VII. 7. XIX. 11. XXIII. 9. 2. Par. XX. 12. Esth. III. c. IV. 13. Job. XVII. 1. Cant. VIII. 1. Jer. XVII. 4. Zach. VIII. 19. He was preceded by the Latin Vulgate Lev. XXI. 2. Deut. VI. 13. c. X. 20. XII. 32. XXII. 27. XXXII. 39. 1. Sam. X. 19. XVIII. 8. 2. Reg. VII. 7. XIX. 11. XXIII. 9. 2. Paral. XX. 12. Esth. III. 2. IV. 13. Job. XVII. 1. Dan. XI. 4. Zach. VIII. 19. He was preceded by the Chaldean version of Jonathan Gen. XXXII. 10. with my staff alone I crossed over; he was preceded by the Syriac version Rom. IV. 5. To him who does not work, but ܒܠܚܘܥ only believes, to which the Arabic version is compared; he was preceded by the Italian translation published at Venice in the year 1546, Gal. II. 16. ma solo per la fide, by faith alone; he was preceded by the German published at Augsburg in the year 1477, Würzburg 1483, Strasbourg 1505, Galat. II. 16. rendering it nur durch den Glauben, and the brother Nass. admits in his writing against the Formula of Concord f. 248 that the particle Nur is equivalent to the particle Allein. Add that the Bibles recently published at Frankfurt in the year 1662 by the authority of the Archbishop of Mainz add an exclusive particle in Lev. XXI. 2. Deut. VI. 13. X. 20. and in other places where the Latin Vulgate has it, even if it is not read in the original text. Add also that the Fathers and other writers have used the exclusive particle quite often in this very matter, whence Erasmus in Ecclesiastes, or on the method of preaching, book III. p. 798: The word 'alone,' stoned with so many clamors in this century in Luther, is reverently in the Fathers heard; concerning which see Hamelmann, who in a special book produced 40 testimonies from the Greek and Latin Fathers for justification by faith alone. There also appear from the Papists Jodocus Coccejus, Vol. II, Thesaurus, Book III, art. 1, who, for the same opinion, praised not only that of Hilary, Canon 8 on Matthew, 'Faith alone justifies,' but also the author of the commentaries on the Epistles of Paul among the works of Ambrose, on chapter 3 of Romans: 'They have been justified freely, because doing nothing and rendering nothing in return, they have been justified by faith alone as a gift of God,' as also Origen on chapter 3 to the Romans: 'He says that the justification of faith alone is sufficient,' and Theodoret on chapter 3 to the Romans: 'By faith alone we all receive the remission of sins: the Lord Christ procured our salvation in his blood, demanding from us faith alone,' and he approved several other similar things, such as Basil, Homily 22 on Humility, Chrysostom, Sermon on faith and the law of nature, and Botius on Romans 4. Arnobius, Book II against the Gentiles, Peter Chrysologus, Sermon 34, Claudius Marius Victor, Book III on Genesis concerning Abraham, Primasius on chapter 2 of Galatians, Bede on Psalm 77, Haymo on Galatians 3, Bernard, Sermon 22 on the Song of Songs. Concerning which Cardinal Hosius also wrote thus in Epistle 17 to Ruardus Tapper: 'Not only Augustine and Ambrose, but also Bernard and many other Doctors have used this way of speaking, that faith alone justifies'; Johannes Hoffmeister the Augustinian also has similar things in his Harmony of the Augsburg Confession, Fabricius, p. 46. 'Before this tumult arose in the Church of God, no one was offended by that particle "Alone," which the tender ears of some can now hardly bear; for no one ever called St. Ambrose to account because he affirmed that men are justified by faith alone.' Nor indeed are there lacking those among the Papists who admit that the Apostle in this passage teaches that a man is justified by faith alone: Hugo the Cardinal on chapter 3 of Romans: 'Where is your boasting? It is excluded, since faith alone justifies, and not the law.' Lombard on chapter 3 to the Romans, and Peter of Tarantasia, the Dominican (later Pope Innocent V), in his gloss on this passage, have it thus: 'We reckon that a man is justified by faith without the works of the law.' For works follow the one justified, they do not precede the one to be justified, but by faith alone without preceding works a man becomes just. Thomas on chapter 3 to the Romans, lecture 4: 'The Apostle shows that Jews and Gentiles are equal as to the state of grace, by showing that justification is brought about by the faith of Christ alone.' Henry of the Order of Hermits of St. Augustine (who died at Erfurt in 1488) on this passage, lectures 29 and 30: 'We reckon that a man is justified by faith without the works of the law': the Apostle shows the truth stated, namely, that faith alone justifies. Cardinal Jacob Sadolet on chapter 3 to the Romans, Book 1 of his Commentaries. Relying on this faith in God, let us assert that first point, which we hold to be undoubted and certain, that by faith alone toward God through Jesus Christ we can be saved, and that there is no other name under heaven in which salvation is proposed to the world. Wilhelm, Count of Isenburg, of the Teutonic Order, in his 'Responsibility regarding the accusation of the theologian (Jacob Hochstraten)': 'So we hold now that man is justified without the contribution of the works of the law, alone through faith.' Pererius, Disputation 4 on Genesis, chapter 15, p. 742, n. 43: 'Paul,' he says, 'in Romans 3 proves that no one is justified before God by his own works, but only freely through the faith of Christ.' And Melchior Canus, Bishop of the Canary Islands, established this as the scope of this Epistle in his Relection on the Sacraments, part 2. The chief argument and indeed the scope of the whole Epistle to the Romans is to show that neither the law of nature nor of Scripture has provided righteousness, but faith alone. I pass over the fact that B. Menzer, in his Exegesis of the Augsburg Confession, art. 4, p. 144, testifies that he inspected in the Jesuit library at Confluentia ancient German Bibles edited before Luther, in which is found in Romans 3 the exclusive particle: 'Allein durch den Glauben, ohne die Wercke der Ee.' And that Reihing the Jesuit himself, in his Catholic Manual against Dr. Hoë, p. 392, admits that in the German Bibles printed at Nuremberg in the year 1483, the exclusive 'Allein' exists.

Moreover, that the Papists wish only the works of the ceremonial law to be excluded by the 'works of the law'—such as Lombard on chapter 3 to the Romans, Daventria on art. 4 of the Augsburg Confession, Alphonsus Virvesius, Philippics 5, Eder in his Oeconomia Biblica, p. 645, Alphonsus de Castro against heresies, title 'Heretical Faith,' Renatus Benedictus in his Panoplia, Johannes Paulus Windeck in his disputation on Justification, Freiberg, 1610, aphorism 33 (to which Grotius also seems to incline)—is so weak that it is refuted even by modern Papists, with Thomas himself leading the way on chapter 3, who says: 'The Apostle speaks here of all works, as well ceremonial as moral: for works are not the cause that anyone is just before God, but rather they are the executions and manifestations of justice'; and Dominicus à Soto on chapter 3 of Romans, who says that all holy commentators, and especially Augustine in 'On the Spirit and the Letter,' chapter 4, agree that moral precepts are also noted here, namely the Decalogue itself, whose works do not justify by themselves. See Salmero and Toletus, Estius, Justinianus, Pererius, as also Cornelius à Lapide on this passage, and also Bellarmine, Book 1 on Justification, chapter 16. For this purpose Salmero urges this: 'Paul excludes the works of the law from justification, and we ought not to limit what he himself did not limit.' There are also other arguments in the text: namely, that the discourse is about that law from which is the knowledge of sin, v. 20, and which convinces the whole world that it is subject to God, v. 19, which is certainly the moral law, etc.

To another refuge, therefore, the Papists betake themselves, namely that the Apostle excluded only works done from the powers of nature alone: whom the Jesuits themselves, primarily Vasquez in 1. 2. T. II. Disp. 210. cap. 8. n. 73., refute, inasmuch as Paul nowhere conceded such works: whence they contend that the Apostle speaks of works done before faith without the grace of GOD, which are elicited by the force of the law: but they can be pressed first by the argument which Salmero brought against the former exception: that we ought not to limit what Paul did not limit. Then also by the argument of Vasquez opposed to the second exception, that Paul nowhere concedes such works, inasmuch as Vasquez himself, even if he wishes works of the law to be understood as done from the mere knowledge of the law without the Spirit of grace, grants in the cited place that such works cannot be done, nor does Paul concede that any are done. What need is there, therefore, for those things to be excluded which cannot even be done? Or why would the Apostle argue that no one is justified by works done by their own powers without grace, when not even any of the Jews thought this, but it was a constant belief among the Hebrews that the purgation of sins is done by GOD alone, as Bellarmine admits, l. III. de Justific. c. IV. ad 1. Add that the Apostle brings forward the example of Abraham in place of confirmation in c. IV. to demonstrate that no one is justified by the works of the law; who, however, did not work then from the mere knowledge of the law without grace, whence Vasquez himself, the most subtle of the Jesuits, is forced to admit that Abraham was also denied by Paul to have been justified by works, after he had been gifted with the Spirit of grace; who furthermore refutes the exception of those who say that Paul excludes works from justification only by reason of merit, but not by way of cooperation, which explanation he says is without foundation, and by the Council of Trent is refuted. Conf. Theol. Apostolica Romana, & Exegema A. Confess. artic. IV.

Latin:

V. 28. Λογιζόμεθα ἷν πίσει δικαιοῦσθαι ἄνθρωπον.

In Manuscripto λογιζόμεθα γὰρ: quasi dicat: Hæc enim cogitamus, quæ cogitare debemus, justitiam nobis sine labore Dei dono advenisse. Sic λογίζεσθαι sumitur Marci XI. 31. Hebr. XI. 19. 2. Cor. IX. 7. Phil. IV. 8. Hæc cogi- tatio reprimit illam καύχησιν.

Non potest anus M. S. codex præjudicare cæ- teris omnibus; & συνέχεια tractationis vel dispu- tationis Apostolicæ docet, hic illationem institui ex iis, quæ jam disputata sunt, quemadmodum etiam vox λογίζεσθαι importat Logicam illatio- nem, vel conclusionem è præmissis deductam; ubi Theophil. exposuit, συλλογιζόμεθα argumentando colligimus, & Augustinus de Spirit. & liter. cap. 13. reddidit COLLIGIMUS. Xenoph. l. 1. παιδείας, έκεί- νων δὲ ἐπελάτο ἅ ποτε ἐγω καὶ σὺ ἐλογιζόμεθα quæ rationibus firmis conclusimus. Non ergò rectè vulgata: Arbitramur enim; quum reddendum sit potiùs: Ratiocinamur igitur: rationum momentis collatis firmiter concludimus. Conf. Rom. VIII. 18. Fidei enim justificatio omnem gloriam Deo in so- lidum adscribit, operum justificatio homini gloria- tionem relinquit; qualis tamen nulla valere po- test in oculis DEI. Ideoque sine operibus juxta le- gem factis fide sola hominem justificari concludimus, ut qui gloriatur, in DEO tantùm glorietur.

χωρὶς ἔργων νόμε.

Sine operibus legis: id est, etiamsi absint opera legis, ut in gentibus fiebat.

Ergonè in Judæis cum operibus legis id fie- bat? Imò tùm Judæos, tùm gentes sola fide sine operibus legis justificari docet Apostolus: & ope- ra legis ab articulo justificationis prorsus excludit:

Idcircò B. Lutherus emphasin verborum Aposto- li rectè expressurus particulam exclusivam adhi- buit, quæ etsi ῥητῶς hîc non occurrat, καὼ διάνοιαν tamen in oratione Apostoli continetur, ohn deß Gesetzes Werck, id est, allein durch den Glauben, uti in loco parallelo disertè habetur, non nisi ἐὰν μὴ per fidem nos justificari Gal. II. 16. quam parti- culam ἐὰν μὴ & εἰμὴ Dietenberger ipse non rarò reddidit per vocem Allein: ut & Eccius Ap. XXI. ult. eam exposuit. Agnoscit utique Jesuita Hun- næus in prodidagm. Dial. sol. 31. quod exclusivæ tantùm aut sola æquivaleat locutioni de aliquo ali- quid affirmanti, & de alio idem neganti. At talis hic est oppositio, fides justificat, non opera. Ergò hæc exclusiva æquipollet: nos sola fide justificari. Et quid aliud est, fide nos justificari sine operibus, quàm sola nos fide justificari? Quo pacto B. Vox sola tot clamoribus lapidata hoc Seculo in Luthero reverenter in Pa- tribus auditur; Quo de vid. III. art. 1. qui in eandem sententiam non tantùm illud Hilarii Can. IIX. in Matth. So- la fides justificat, laudavit, sed & autoris commen- tar. in Epist. Pauli apud Ambros. in c. III. Rom. Justificati sunt gratis, quia nihil operantes neque vi- cem reddentes solâ fide justificati sunt dono DEI, ut & Origenis in c. III. ad Rom. Dicit sufficere solius fidei justificationem, & Theodoreti in c. III. ad Rom. Solâ fide illatâ peccatorum remissionem accipimus omnes: Dominus Christus in suo sanguine salutem nostram procuravit, solam à nobis fidem exigens, & pluscula alia similia approbavit, utpote Basilii Hom. XXII. de Humilit. Chrysost. Serm. de fide & lege natur. Botii ad Rom. IV. Arnobii l. II. contr. Gentes, Petri Chrysologi Serm. XXXIV. Claudii Marii Victor. l. III. in Genes. de Abrahamo. Pri- masii in cap. II. Gal. Bedæ in Ps. LXXVII. Haymon. in Gal. III. Bernh. Serm. XXII. in Cantic. Quo de etiam Cardin. Hosius Ep. XVII. ad Ruardum Tap- perum ita perscripsit: Non solum Augustinus & Ambrosius, sed etiam Bernhardus & alii multi Do- ctores usi sunt hoc loquendi genere, quod sola fides justificet; similia etiam habet Johannes Hoffmei- sterus Augustinianus in Harmon. Confess. August. Fabricii p. 46. Ante exortum hunc in Ecclesia Dei tumultum Nemo fuit offensus particulâ illa Sola, quam jam teneræ quorundam aures ferre vix pos- sunt; Nemo siquidem unquam in jus vocavit D. Ambrosium, quod affirmavit, homines solâ fide ju- stificari. Nec verò desunt, qui è Pontificiis solâ fide hominem justificari hoc loco Apostolum do- cere fatentur: Hugo Cardinalis in cap. III. Rom. Ubi est gloriatio tua, nulla est, ex quo sola fides justi- ficat, & non lex. Lombardus in cap. III. ad Rom. & Petrus de Tarantasia, Dominicanus, (posteà P. R. Innocentius V.) in gloss. sup. h. l. sic habent: Arbitramur hominem justificari fide sine operibus legis. Sequuntur enim Opera justificatum, non præ- cedunt justificandum, sed sola fide sine operibus præ- cedentibus fit homo justus. Thomas in cap. III. ad Rom. lect. IV. Ostendit Apostolus, Judæos & gen- tes esse æquales, quantum ad statum gratiæ, osten- dendo solâ fide Christi fieri justificationem. Henri- cus Ludovici Ordinis Eremit. S. Augustini (qui anno 1488. Erphordiæ mortuus) ad h. l. lect. 29. & 30. Arbitramur hominem justificari fide sine operibus legis: ostendit Apostolus veritatem indi- ctam, scil. quod sola fides justificat. Jacob Sadole- tus Cardinalis in cap. III. ad Rom. l. 1. Comment. Hâc fide in Deum freti asseveremus primum illud, quod indubitatum certumque retinemus, solâ fide er- ga Deum per Jesum Christum posse nos salvos fieri, neque aliud nomen sub cælo esse, in quo salvos mundo sit proposita. Wilhelmus Comes Isenburgicus Ordi- nis Teurinici in der Verantwortung auff die Be- schuldigung des Theologen (Jacobi Hochstraten) So halten wirs nun, daß der Mensch gerechtfer- tiget werde, ohn Zuthun der Werck des Gesetzes, allein durch den Glauben. Pererius Disp. IV. in Genes. c. XV. p. 742. n. 43. Paulus, inquit, Rom. III. probat, neminem justificari coram DEO ex suis operibus, sed tantum gratis per fidem Christi. Atque hunc scopum constituit hujus Epistolæ Mel- chior Canus Episcopus Canariensis in Relect. de Sacram. part. II. Totius Epistolæ ad Romanos præci- puum argumentum atque advò scopuset, ostendere, nec naturæ, nec Scripturæ legem justitiam præstitis- se, sed solam fidem. Taceo, quod B. Menzerus in Exeg. A. Conf. art. IV. p. 144. testetur, se inspe- xisse Confluentiæ in Bibliotheca Jesuitarum anti- qua Biblia Germanica ante Lutherum edita, in quibus habetur Roman. III. particula exclusiva: Allein durch den Glauben, ohne die Wercke der Ee. Quodque ipse Reihingius Jesuita in Manuali Ca- tholico contra D. Hoë p. 392. fateatur, in Bibliis Germanicis ante Lutherum Anno 1483. Norin- bergæ impressis extare exclusivam Allein.

Cæterùm quòd Papistæ per opera legis solius Ceremonialis legis opera excludi tantùm velint, ut- pote Lombardus in c. III. ad Rom. Daventria ad art. IV. August. Confess. Alphonsus Virvesius Phi- lip. V. Ederus in Oeconom. Bibl. p. 645. Alphonsus de Castro adversus hæreses tit. Fides hæret. Rena- tus Benedictus in Panopl. Joh. Paulus Windeck in disp. de Justif. Freiberg. Anno 1610. aph. 33. (quò etiam inclinare videtur Grotius) adeò dilutum est, ut à modernis Papistis etiam id profligetur, Thomâ ipso in cap. III. præeunte, qui, loquitur hic Apostolus, inquit, de omnibus operibus, tàm ce- remonialibus quàm moralibus: Opera enim non sunt causa, quod aliquis sit justus apud Deum, sed potiùs sunt exequutiones, & manifestationes justi- tiæ; & Dominico à Soto in cap. III. Roman. qui, omnes Sanctos enarratores, & cumprimis Augusti- num de Spiritu & litera c. IV. consentire ait, præce- ptiones etiam hic subnotari morales, nempè Deca- logum ipsum, cujus opera per se non justificant. Vid. Salmero & Toletus, Estius, Justinianus, Pererius, ut & Cornel. à Lap. in h. l. nec non Bellarm. l. 1. de justific. cap. 16. Eam in rem Salmero hoc urget: Paulus opera legis excludit à justificatione, neque debemus limitare, quod ipse non limitavit. Sunt autem & alia in textu argumenta: quod nempè de ea lege sermo sit, ex qua est agnitio peccati, v. 20. & qua totum mundum Deo obnoxium esse con- vincit v. 19. quæ utique lex momlis est, &c.

Ad aliud ergò κενσφύγετον se recipiunt Papi- stæ, quod nempè Apostolus tantùm excluserit ope- ra facta ex solis naturæ viribus: quos verò refel- lunt ipsi Jesuitæ imprimis Vasquez in 1. 2. T. II. Disp. 210. cap. 8. n. 73. siquidem nusquam Paulus talia opera concefferit: unde contendunt, loqui Apostolum de operibus ante fidem factis sine DEI gratiâ, quæ ex vi legis eliciuntur: sed urgeri pri- mùm possunt argumento, quod adversus prio- rem exceptionem Salmero adduxit: non debere nos limitare, quod Paulus non limitavit. Deinde etiam argumento Vasquii secundæ exceptioni opposito, quod nusquam Paulus talia opera con- cedat, siquidem Vasquius ipse, etsi opera legis ex solâ legis notitiâ sine Spiritu gratiæ facta intelli- gi velit, largiatur l. c. talia opera fieri non posse, nec Paulum concedere aliqua fieri. Quid ergò opus est illa excludi, quæ ne fieri quidem pos- sunt? aut cur disputaret Apostolus, neminem o- peribus propriis viribus sine gratia factis justifi- cari, quum ne quidem ullus Judæorum id existima- rit, sed constans apud Ebræos fides fuerit, quod pur- gatio peccatorum à solo DEO fiat, ut fatetur Bellarm. l. III. de Justific. c. IV. ad 1. Adde, quod Apostolus Abrahami exemplum confirmationis loco adducat c. IV. ad id demonstrandum, quod nemo per opera legis justificetur; qui verò non ex solâ legis notitiâ sine gratiâ tum operatus est, unde fateri coactus ipse Vasquezius Jesuitarum subtilissimus, Abrahamum etiam à Paulo negari justificatum fuisse ex operibus, postquam donatus fuisset Spiritu gratiæ; qui prætereà refutat eorum exceptionem, qui ajunt, Paulum excludere opera à justificatione tantùm ratione meriti, non autem per modum cooperationis, quam explicationem dicit esse sine fundamento, & à Concilio Tridentino confutari. Conf. Theol. Apostolica Romana, & Exe- gema A. Confess. artic. IV.

## 3:29
V. 29. Is He the God of the Jews only, is He not also of the Gentiles? Yes, also of the Gentiles.

There is a reason here why the way through the law was not the best: because it was not suitable for so many peoples: for indeed men of all peoples could not come to sacrifice at Jerusalem. Θεὸς is placed here once, but in the explanation it must be taken twice. Is that true GOD, the maker of this world and of the human race, willing to be only GOD, that is, the preserver and benefactor of the Jews, as many of the Jews think?
