Non quomodo Grotius de- tractemur propter inobedientiam Adami, sed quales constituti simus, docet Apostolus: nimirum peccatores & injusti per imputationem inobedientiæ Adami, neque hic de morte agitur, sed de peccato, quod in accurata hac tractatione à morte distinxit Apostolus ceu causam ab effectu. Locus 1. Reg. I. 21. alienus est. Ibi enim particula כ subintelligi, more Hebræis recepto, commode potest: nos erimus sicut peccatores. Hic vero ei locus nullus est. πολλοὶ autem hic omnino dicuntur, qui modo πάντες dicti: omnes ergo intelligendi, nec excipi ullus potest. Nulla enim hic διαςολὴ est Rom. III. 21. omnes in lumbis Adæ fuerunt, omnes in ipso peccarunt vers. 12. ideo omnes peccatores constituti sunt, & super omnes condemnatio venit. Obedientia autem Christi hic non proponitur nobis ut in Christo summo præmio repensata, sed ut pro nobis præstita, nobisque omnibus imputabilis; qui per eandem omnes justi constitui possimus, & ex intentione voluntatis divinæ gratiosissimæ debeamus. Id autem recte dicitur futurum pro præsente durabili adhiberi, locumque Esaiæ, quem in Annotatis ad Es. LIII. 11. insigniter depravavit Grotius, hic non obscure respici. Habemus ergo hic justitiam & obedientiam Christi, quæ imputa- tur nobis in justificatione nostra, in judicio divi- no per fidem, vel cum fide apprehenditur, quem- admodum inobedientia Adami imputata est po- steris ejus. Uti enim hic peccatores constituti sunt imputatione inobedientiæ Adami, sic justi nos constituimur imputatione obedientiæ vel justitiæ Christi.

Pontificii Bellarminus, Becanus, & alii ex hac comparatione colligunt obedientiam Christi non esse formalem justificationis nostræ causam, sed effi- cientem; siquidem opponatur obedientia Christi inobedientiæ Adami, & sicut per hanc injusti, ita per illam justi constitui dicamur. At injusti per inobedientiam Adami constituimur non formali- ter, sed efficienter & meritoriè. Sed hæc opposita non sunt, imo nec inobedientia Adami injustos, nec obedientia Christi justos nos posset efficere, nisi imputativè per illam injusti, per hanc justi consti- tueremur. Nam si non imputaretur nobis Adami inobedientia & obedientia Christi, neutiquam vel illa vel ista nostra esset. Sunt enim actus singu- lares & individui, adeoque proprii eorum,à quibus fiunt, & personales. Actus autem proprios & per- sonales formaliter esse communes contradicto- rium est. Ideoque oportet imputari, ac proinde ipsam Adami inobedientiam necessum est impu- tatam esse posteris, nec minus necessum est nobis imputari obedientiam Christi. Non autem im- putaretur nobis inobedientia Adami, nisi meruis- set Adam inobedientia sua hanc pœnam, ut & sibi in condemnationem imputaretur inobedientia, & posteris ejus universis: quia Adamus is fuit, in quo esse censebatur universum genus humanum, & in quo id acceperat justitiam originalem per natu- ram; unde apostasia & inobedientia Adami cen- se batur totius humani generis, quod in lumbis ejus erat, apostasia & inobedientia, & in Adamo peccaverunt omnes, adeoque jam tum, cum pecca- vit Adam, damnatum fuit universum genus hu- manum, factumque reum apostasias & inobe- dientiæ adversus DEUM; unde & Augustino pec- catum Originis, quod per carnalem generationem attrahimus ab Adamo pœna dicitur primi peccati, vel inobedientiæ Adami. Quomodo autem pœ- na esset in posteris peccati primi, nisi posteris pri- mum illud peccatum imputaretur? Et fatetur Bel- larm. l. IV. de amiss. grat. c. 10. peccatum Adæ ita omnibus posteris imputari, ac si omnes idem pecca- tum patravissent, adducens S. Bernhardi dictum: Nostra est Adami culpa, quia etsi in alio nos tamen peccavimus, & nobis justo Dei judicio imputabatur licet occultò. Similiter imputari haud posset nobis obedientia Christi, nisi meruisset Christus obe- dientiam legi præstando, ut nobis imputaretur illa obedientia, utpote pro nobis præstita: quia Christus is fuit, qui surrogabatur in judicio divino nostri loco, non tantum ut pro nobis pœnam peccati lueret, ac justitiæ divinæ satisfaceret, 1. Cor. V. 14. 21. sed etiam ut pro nobis legem impleret, & obedien- tiam præstaret, quam nos præstare non potera- mus, Rom. IIX. 3. c. X. 4. Gal. IV. 6. ideo ejus obe- dientia censetur totius humani generis obedientia, & cum fide apprehenditur à nobis, nostra fit per λογισμὸν & imputationem in judicio Dei obedie- tia, tam vere ac si nosmetipsi eam præstitissemus. Sic ergo & efficienter & meritoriè Christus est causa nostræ justificationis, quia loco humani generis obedientiam DEO præstitit, & formaliter, quia fidei nostræ imputatur Christi obedientia, & per fidem apprehensa nostra æstimatur in judicio Dei. Si dicas, neminem constitui justum nisi per inhæren- tem justitiam, dico contra, eum esse vere apud Deum justum, cui imputatur aliena, nempe Chri- sti, justitia. Nam id cum fiat à DEO, vere etiam fieri oportet. Sumus ergo justi, & vere justi apud DEUM per hanc imputatam justitiam, & quidem multo magis, multoque augustius, quam qui ex inhærente sua justitia æstimantur. Si cum Sta- pletono dicas, καθασθήσονται inhærentem justitiam inferre, uti servus super omnia bona constitutus Luc. XII. 44. & inimicus quis DEI constitui Jac. IV. 4. dicitur: respondeo, τὸ καθισῆναι non signi- ficare præcise inhærens quid, sed veritatem, & cer- titudinem ejus quod agitur; agi autem aliter atque aliter nihil obstat. Ita constituitur paries albus per inhærentem albedinem, constituitur quis Dominus super bona non per inhærentiam, sed per σχέσιν: constituitur amicus DEI per affectum Dei amantis, qui inhæret DEO, non ei, qui amatur. Per ju- stitiam ergo Christi imputatam vere justi apud Deum constitui possumus, neque verius aut à Domino suo quisquam super bona aut inimicus vel amicus DEI constituitur. Conf. Chamier in Panstr. de justif. l. XXI. c. 2. Pertinent huc egre- giæ Patrum sententiæ, locum Apostolicum insi- gniter illustrantes: Justinus Martyr in expos. fid. inquit: Quandoquidem peccato hoc Adam morti genus humanum subjecit, & naturam cunctam de- bito obnoxiam reddidit, Filius cum DEUS esset, & homo, transgressionem lapsumque Adæ revocavit atque abolevit, ac quatenus homo, cum sine crimine innocenter vitam egit, tum voluntariam subiit mor- tem, per conversationem quidem summam & exa- ctam lapsum ἀφανίζων tegens, ne videatur, per mor- tem autem indebitam debitum extinguens. Idem in Epist. ad Diognet. Quid aliud potuit peccata no- stra tegere, quam ejus justitia; In quo alio nos ini- qui & impii PRO JUSTIS HABERI pos- sumus, quam in solo DEI Filio: ô dulcem permu- tationem! ô impervestigabile artificium! ô bene- ficia expectationem omnem superantia! ut iniqui- tas quidem multorum in uno justo abscondatur, ju- stitia autem unius faciat, ut multi injusti pro JUSTIS habeantur. Irenæus l. V. adv. hæres. cap. XIV. Dissolvens enim, quæ ab initio in ligno facta fuerat, hominis inobedientiam, obediens fa- ctus est usque ad mortem, mortem autem crucis, eam, quæ in ligno fuerat, inobedientiam sanans. Quem in primo quidem Adam offendimus non fa- cientes ejus præceptum, in secundo Adam reconci- liati sumus obedientes usque ad mortem facti: quod explicatur C. XV. de donatione justitiæ Christi: Nobis, inquit, donat eam, quæ est ad faciliorem nostram conversationem & subjectionem. Ambro- sius in 2. Cor. IV. 1. Sicut in Adam omnes moriun- tur, ita & in Christo omnes vivificabuntur. Adam enim forma mortis est, causa peccati, Christus vero forma vitæ est propter justitiam. Cyrillus Alex. Tom. III. libr. de rect. fid. ad Reginam: Absurdum est, nos quidem hæredes factos supplicii primi paren- tis, corruptione per inobedientiam immissa, non autem fieri participes justitiæ secundi, qui ad vitam nos revehit per maximam illam obedientiam. Quando igitur dicit Scriptura, per obedientiam unius justificatos esse multos non hominem simpliciter quempiam nobis similem in hoc derelictum esse dica- mus, sed incarnatum potius & obedientem pro no- bis factum Patri Filium. Et l. XI. in Joh. c. 25. Quemadmodum in prævaricatione primi hominis, ut in primitiis generis nostri morti addicti sumus, in ipso primo audientes, terra es, & ad terram rever- teris, eodem & arbitror modo per obedientiam & justitiam Christi, in quantum legi seipsum subjicit, quamvis legis autor esset, benedictio ac vivificatio, quæ per spiritum est ad vitam, nostram penetravit naturā. Item l. XII. c. 16. Sicut condemnatio per primum A- dam in omnes penetravit; sic justificati Christi bene- dictio per unum ad omnes extensa est. Testatur id Paulus dicens: Sicut enim per unius delictum in omnes homines in condemnationem, sic etiam per unius justitiam in omnes homines in justifica- tionem vitæ: Ægrotavimus ergo per primum Ada- mum inobedientiæ maledictionisque morbo, locu- pletati autem sumus per secundum Adamum per obedientiam & benedictionem.

Autor enim legis ut DEUS, mandata legis servavit ut homo. Atha- nas. de incarnat. verb. Impossibile est puritatem & innocentiam in humana naturæ exhiberi, nisi Deus credatur in carne esse, qui justitiam omni peccato liberam in mundum introduxit, cujus quia PAR- TICIPES redditi sumus, vivemus & salvabimur: Illud enim, non est justus in terra, qui bonum fa- ciat & non peccet, in commune ad omnes homines pertinet. Unde ex cælo descendit, qui IMMACU- LATAM ex se justitiam daturus erat. Idem ad- versus eos, qui damno afficiunt genus nostrum eo quod negat, Servatorem ex natura nostra sum- sisse primitias. Necessarium est, maximeque ne- cessarium credere Script. S. confiteri ex nostro genere primitias, celebrare singularem assumentis in genus humanum Amorem, obstupescere magnæ œconomiæ atque dispensationis miraculum, non timere execra- tionem legis,) Christus enim nos à maledictione legis liberavit) IMPLETIONEM LEGIS à primitiis (Christo) factam TOTI MASSÆ ADSCRIBE- RE, λογίζεσθαι IMPUTARE. Gregor. Nysse- nus orat. II. in Cantic. Christus in SE TRANSLA- TIS peccatorum meorum sordibus PURITA- TEM SUAM mecum COMMUNICAVIT, meque pulchritudinis, quæ in ipso est, PARTICI- PEM fecit. S. Augustinus T. IX. tract. III. in Joh. Omnes qui ex Adamo cum peccato, peccatores; omnes qui per Christum justificati, justi non in se, sed in ILLO, nam in se si interroges, ADAM sunt, in illo si interroges, Christi sunt. Idem Serm. VI. de verb. Apost. T. X. Ipsum Christum, qui non no- verat peccatum, Deus Pater pro nobis peccatum fe- cit, ut nos simus justitia DEI in ipso: videte duo, JU- STITIA DEI, non NOSTRA, in IPSO, non in NOBIS. Item Tom. XIII. in verbis ad Laurent. C. XL. Ipse ergo peccatum, ut nos justitia, nec nostra, sed DEI; nec in nobis, sed in ipso. Sicut ipse pecca- tum, non suum, sed nostrum, nec in se, sed in nobis. Et T. IIX. in Enarr. Ps. XXX. Conc. I. in tua justitia erue me, & exue me. Quia non invenisti in me justi- tiam meā, erue me in tua, hoc est, illud me eruat, quod me justificat, quod ex impio piū facit, quod ex iniquo justum. Adde quæ habet Ep. XXIII. ad Bonif. Ab Adamo contraximus reatum, quoniam eramus in Adam, quando peccavit. Chrysost. hom. X. ad cap. V. ad Rom. Ob id sursum ac deorsum voci huic UNIUS insistens, ea assidue in medium affert, cum dicit: Quemadmodum per unum hominem peccatum in mundum introiit; &, si unius peccato multi mortui sunt: &, non sicut per unum, qui peccaverat, venerat mors, ita & donū; &, judicium ex unius delicto ad condemnationem, & rursus, quemadmodum enim per inobedientiam unius hominis peccatores constituti sunt multi, nec de- sistit: ut cum tibi Judæus dixerit, Quo pacto uno re- ge agente Christo universus orbis salvus factus est? possis illi respondere: Quo pacto uno inobediente Adā

universus orbis condemnatus est? Leo I. Epist. LXX. ad Juvenal. Ut autem repararet omnium vitam, recepit omnium causam, & vim veteris chirographi, quod solus inter omnes non debuit, pro omnibus solvendo vacuavit, ut sicut per unius res- tum omnes facti fuerant peccatores, ita per unius justitiam omnes fierent INNOCENTES, inde in homines manante justitia, ubi est humana suscepta natura. Anshelmus in cap. V. ad Rom. Per unius justitiam venientem in omnes homines electos, itum est in justificationem, ut PARTICIPATIONE JUSTITIÆ Christi justificentur. Bernhard. Ep. CXC. ad Innocent. Homo qui debuit, homo qui sol- vit. Nam si unus, inquit, pro omnibus mortuus est, ergo omnes mortui sunt, ut videlicet satisfa- ctio unius omnibus IMPUTETUR, sicut omnium peccata unus ille portavit. Item : Quid ex se agere poterat, ut semel amissam JUSTITIAM reparet homo, servus peccati, vinctus diaboli ? Assignata est ei proinde ALIENA, qui caruit sua. Et serm. ad milit. templ. cap. XI. Mors in Christi morte fu- gatur, & Christi justitia nobis IMPUTATUR. Et porro : unus peccavit, & omnes tenentur REI. Et unius INNOCENTIA soli REPUTABITUR uni? Unius peccatum omnibus operatum est mor- tem, & unius JUSTITIA uni vitam restituet? Ita- ne DEI justitia magis ad condemnandum, quam ad restaurandum valuit? Aut plus potuit Adam in malo, quam Christus in bono? Adæ peccatum impu- tabitur mihi, & Christi JUSTITIA non pertine- bit ad me?

PARS III.

Παρασκευαστικὴ commonefaciens de causa subin- gressæ legis.

## 5:20
Vers. 20. But the law entered in.

The Jew could say: If the matter stands thus, that Christ is the cause of life, just as Adam is of death, what then did the law of Moses do? Responding to this question he says: the law intervened obliquely between the beginning of sin and the beginning of new righteousness. Thus παρεισῆλθον Gal. II. 4. παρεισέδυσαν Jude 4.

but that the trespass might abound.

To the Hebrews it is often said to be that which appears; and so just as περισσεύειν is to appear more abundantly above III. 7. and here 15. so also πλεονάζειν here and below VI. 1. II. Cor. IV. 15. II. Thess. I. 3. you have both πλεονάσαι and περισσεῦσαι joined together 1. Thess. III. 12. Through the law sin became more known above II. 9. 12. III. 20. IV. 15. below VII. 8.

but where sin abounded.

ὗ here signifies after, just as in Latin 'ubi' is used. For markers of place are accustomed to be transferred to the signification of time.

grace did superabound.

He did not consider it enough to say ἐπερίσσευσεν, but added an intensifying preposition, so that it might be understood that the benevolence of GOD appeared much more illustriously than the baseness of sin had appeared before. Paul loves such comparisons as ὑπερεκτείνω, ὑπερεκχύνομαι, ὑπεραίρομαι, ὑπεράνω, ὑπεραυξάνω, ὑπερνικάω, ὑπερυψόω. Thus he has ὑπερπερισσεύομαι also II. Cor. VII. 4. and ὑπερπερισσῶς Mark VII. 37. ὑπερπλεονάζω 1. Tim. I. 14.

It is true that the law intervened unexpectedly, but that it intervened between the beginning of sin and the beginning of new righteousness is nowhere taught: it intervened, however, to convict sin, and to denounce wrath, and to demand a curse Rom. III. 20. c. IV. 11. Deut. XXVII. v. ult. Gal. III. 27. it demanded, indeed, perfect obedience if anyone wishes to obtain life Levit. XVIII. 5. Luc. X. 28. Gal. III. 12. Since, therefore, all are convicted of sin and the guilt of condemnation by the voice of the law, and no one after the fall can perform perfect obedience, God out of His immense grace destined His own Son as Mediator, who would satisfy for our sins, and in our place perform obedience to the law. Concerning which Theodore Abucara, Bishop of Caria, Disp. XV. c. 5. God by His just judgment from us it demanded all things which are written in the law: since we were not able to pay these, for that reason our Lord himself paid them for us, and he assumed the curse and condemnation to which we were liable, and of his own accord took upon himself those things which we ought to have suffered, he himself bore them. The law therefore παρεισῆλθε, that it might compel us, that we might seek this mediator, and thus it became a schoolmaster for us unto Christ Gal. III. 24. not that the benevolence of GOD might appear only more illustriously than the baseness of sin, but that the Grace of GOD might unfold itself more abundantly in us, by which the power of sin exerts itself more fully in those who are of a contrite heart and humble Spirit. The Apostle therefore teaches that the law of Moses intervened, and was solemnly promulgated, not that sin might be abolished through it, or that we might be justified, but that sin and its punishment might be set more clearly before our eyes, and the grace of GOD exhibited in Christ might be the more desired, and be more pleasing. And thus far we admit that manner of speaking, by which active verbs among the Hebrews are taken declaratively Lev. XIII. 14. 2. Sam. XV. 4. Prov. XVII. 15. Furthermore the law was given, says Augustin. de medic. pœnit. cap. I. that it might show the wounds of sinners, which it might heal by the blessing of grace. In reality, however, the grace of GOD is more abundant even than any sins whatsoever, it superabounds where sins abound, provided it is apprehended by true faith: because it is immense, and procured for us by the λύτρῳ of immense price, namely the blood of the eternal Son of GOD himself. Sin is an infinite evil by reason of its Object, because it is committed against an infinite good; but the Satisfaction and justice of Christ is infinite, not only by reason of the Object, to whom it was rendered, but also by reason of the Subject, because it proceeds from an infinite person, from whom it obtains a value of infinite price. Sin is the work of the devil and man, but grace is of GOD, the Satisfaction and Justice of Christ is not of a mere man, but of the true and infinite GOD. Concerning the grace of GOD Chrysost. homil. III. de pœnit. As much as a spark compares to the sea, so much does the malice of man compare to the clemency of GOD. Although the sea is great, it receives a measure, but the clemency of GOD has no end. Concerning the merit of Christ S. Cyrill. Alex. Exeg. ad Valer. de Verbi incarnat. which is found in Concil. Ephes. T. VI. cap. 17. But in what way could one who died for all, pay a just price for all, if we say that that suffering was of some mere man? But if indeed the Word according to his human nature suffered, he transferred the sufferings of the flesh as his own into himself, and claimed them for himself, then at last we most rightly assert that the death of one according to the flesh PREPONDERATED the life of all men. And another, Cyril Bishop of Jerusalem Catech. illumin. XIII. Nor should you marvel that the whole world was liberated through him: for he had not been a simple man, but the only-begotten Son of GOD dying for it: since the sin of even one man Adam could bring death to the world, if therefore by the transgression of one death reigned in the world: why should not the justice of one much more reign in life? If the first-formed man brought universal death from the earth; will he who created him from the earth not bring eternal life, since he himself is life?

Latin:

Vers. 20. νόμος δὲ παρεισῆλθεν.

Poterat dicere Judæus : Si ita se res habet, ut Christus sit causa vitæ, sicut mortis Adamus, quid ergo egit lex Mo- sis? Huic quæstioni respondens ait : lex de transverso in- tervenit inter exordium peccati & exordium novæ justitiæ. Sic παρεισῆλθον Gal. II. 4. παρεισέδυσαν Judæ 4.

ἵνα δὲ πλεονάσῃ τὸ παράπτωμα.

Hebræis sæpe esse dicitur quod apparet ; Itaque sicut περισσεύειν est abundantius apparere supra III. 7. & hic. 15. ita & πλεονάζειν hic & infra VI. 1. II. Cor. IV. 15. II. Thess. I. 3. utrumque πλεονάσαι & περισσεῦσαι junctim habes 1. Thess. III. 12. Per legem magis innotuit peccatum supra II. 9. 12. III. 20. IV. 15. infra VII. 8.

ὗ δὲ ἐπλεόνασεν ἡ ἁμαρτία.

ὗ hic valet postquam, sicut & Latine usurpatur ubi. Solent enim locorum notæ ad temporis significationem transferri.

ὑπερεπερίσσευσεν ἡ χάρις.

Non satis habuit dicere ἐπερίσσευσεν, sed præpositionem augentem addidit, ut intelligeretur multo illustrius appa- ruisse DEI benevolentiam, quam ante apparuerat peccati turpitudo. Amat tales comparationes Paulus ut ὑπερεκτεί- νω, ὑπερεκχύνομαι, ὑπεραίρομαι, ὑπεράνω, ὑπεραυξάνω, ὑπερ- νικάω, ὑπερυψόω. Sic ὑπερπερισσεύομαι habet & II. Cor. VII. 4. & ὑπερπερισσῶς Marc. VII. 37. ὑπερπλεονάζω 1. Tim. I. 14.

Verũ est intervenisse de transverso legem, sed in- tervenisse inter exordiũ peccati, & exordium novæ justitiæ nuspiã docetur : intervenit autẽ ut argueret peccatum, & iram denunciaret, ac maledictionem Rõ. III. 20. c. IV. 11. Deut. XXVII. v. ult. Gal. III. 27. postularet vero obedientiam perfectam si vitam cõ- sequi quis velit Levit. XIIX. 5. Luc. X. 28. Gal. III. 12. Quum ergo omnes de peccato & reatu conde- mnationis voce legis convincantur, nec ullus post lapsum obedientiam perfectam præstare possit, Deus ex immensa gratia Filium proprium Me- diatorem destinavit, qui pro peccatis nostris satis- faceret, nostrique loco obedientiam legi præsta- ret. Quo de Theodorus Abucara Episcopus Ca- rum. Disp. XV. c. 5. Deus justo judicio suo a nobis omnia exigebat, quæ in lege scripta sunt: quæ cum solvendo non essemus, idcirco pro nobis Dominus no- ster illa persolvit, & maledictionem condemnatio- nemque, cui obnoxii eramus, assumsit, ultroque in se recepit, quæ pati debueramus, illa ipse pertulit. Lex ergo παρεισῆλθε, ut nos compelleret, ut media- torem hunc quæreremus, & ita nobis pædagogus facta est ad Christum Gal. III. 24. non ut ap- pareret tantum illustrius DEI benevolentia, quam peccati turpitudo, sed ut abundantius sese expli- cet Gratia DEI in nobis, quo plenius vis pecca- ti se exerit in iis, qui contrito corde & humili Spi- ritu sunt. Docet ergo Apostolus, legem Mosis intervenisse, ac solenniter promulgatam esse, non ut per eam aboleretur peccatum, aut nos justifi- caremur, sed ut peccatum ejusque pœna nobis cla- rius ob oculos poneretur, gratia vero DEI in Christo exhibita eo magis desideraretur, gratior- que esset. Atque hactenus admittimus modum illum loquendi, quo verba activa apud Ebræos declarative accipiuntur Lev. XIII. 14. 2. Sam. XV. 4. Prov. XVII. 15. Adhæc data est lex, ait Augustin. de medic. pœnit. cap. I. ut vulnera ostenderet peccatorum, quæ gratiæ benedictione sa- naret. Revera tamen gratia DEI abundantior etiam est quantiscunque peccatis, superabundat, ubi abundant peccata, modo vera fide appre- hendatur: quia immensa est, & λύτρῳ immensi pretii sanguinis nempe ipsiusmet æterni DEI Filii nobis parta. Peccatum infinitum malum est ratione Objecti, quia committitur contra infini- tum bonum; Satisfactio autem & justitia Christi infinita est, non solum ratione Objecti, cui præ- stita, sed etiam ratione Subjecti, quia à persona infinita proficiscitur, à qua infiniti pretii valo- rem consequitur. Peccatum diaboli & homi- nis opus est, gratia vero DEI est, Satisfactio & Justitia Christi non meri hominis, sed veri & in- finiti DEI. De gratia DEI Chrysost. homil. III. de pœnit. Quantum scintilla se habet ad mare, tantum hominis malitia ad DEI clementiam. Pelagus tametsi magnum est, mensuram recipit, DEI vero clementia finem non habet. De meri- to vero Christi S. Cyrill. Alex. Exeg. ad Valer. de Verbi incarnat. quæ habetur in Concil. E- phes. T. VI. cap. 17. Quo pacto autem unus pro omnibus mortuus, justum pro omnibus pretium exolvere potuit, si perpessionem illam puri cujus- piam hominis fuisse dicamus? Quod si vero verbum secundum humanam naturam passum proprias carnis perpessiones quasi proprias in se transtulit, sibique vindicavit, tunc demum unius mortem secundum carnem omnium hominum vita PRÆ- PONDERASSE rectissime afferimus. Et alter Cyrillus Hierosolymitanus Episcopus Catech. illu- min. XIII. Neque mireris totum esse per illum mun- dum liberatum: non enim simplex homo fuerat, sed Filius DEI unigenitus pro illo moriens: quan- doquidem unius etiam viri Adam peccarum potuit mortem adferre mundo, si ergo transgressione unius mors regnavit in mundo: cur non multo ma- gis justitia unius vita regnet? Si protoplastus de terra universalem mortem attulit; qui creavit il- lum de terra nunquid vitam non adferet æternam, cum ipse sit vita?

## 5:21
Vers. 21. Ἵνα ὥσπερ ἐβασίλευσεν ἡ ἁμαρτία ἐν τῷ θανάτῳ. It shows its powers through death, see above 14.

οὕτω καὶ ἡ χάρις βασιλεύσῃ. May the benevolence of GOD show its powers.

διὰ δικαιοσύνης. Through the obedience of Christians.

εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον. Which obedience leads to eternal life.

διὰ Ἰησοῦ χριστῦ τῦ κυρίυ ἡμῶν,. Which is to say, just as he effects that justice in us, so he himself is about to give us eternal life, so that after the Father we owe all things to him.

The particle ἵνα is taken here τελικῶς (as a final cause), by which the end is expressed both of justification through the imputation of the justice of Christ, as the principal Object, in which the Apostle is occupied, and of superabundant grace, when sin abounds, so that indeed grace may no less, nay rather more, dominate through justice unto life, than sin has dominated unto death. But what this justice is, is clear partly from what has preceded, namely not inherent justice, or the obedience of Christians, which the Apostle has excluded from the circle of justification, but imputed or alien justice, the obedience of Christ himself, by which he taught that we are constituted just: partly from opposition: because to sin, which dominates in death, the justice of Christ is opposed, to that disobedience of Adam the obedience of Christ, to the sin of Adam the δικαίωμα of Christ; partly from the effect, because not the justice of Christians, but only the obedience of Christ is the cause of life: and through justice it is imputed to us by faith: and thus grace dominates unto eternal life through JESUS Christ our Lord, by whom he redeemed us for himself as a peculiar possession, and purchased us with his own blood 2. Petr. II. 4. through whom that imputation of justice is meritoriously. For the Apostle attends to this respect here: but not insofar as he himself effects justice in us, and is about to give eternal life to us. Which, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, is common to him, just as we owe all those things not after the Father, but with the Father and the Holy Spirit, because these three are one 1. Joh. V. 7. But that is foreign to this place, because it is only a matter of that which is proper to Christ our Lord. Ἐν θανάτῳ Erasmus and Schmalzius render in death; but others more correctly take ἐν for εἰς, as this particle is taken in Matth. XVI. 28. Luc. XXIII. 41. Eph. I. 12.; because the opposition εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον demands it. And thus much concerning the Fifth chapter.

SUBSECTION II. Containing an exposition of the Apostolic doctrine concerning the righteousness of faith.

ARTICLE I. Defending it from the objections of those who slander it.

Latin:

Vers. 21. Ἵνα ὥσπερ ἐβασίλευσεν ἡ ἁμαρτία ἐν τῷ θανάτῳ. Vires suas ostendit per mortem, vide supra 14.

οὕτω καὶ ἡ χάρις βασιλεύσῃ. Benevolentia DEI vires suas ostendat.

διὰ δικαιοσύνης. Per obedientiam Christianorum.

εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον. Quæ obedientia ducit ad vitam æternam.

διὰ Ἰησοῦ χριστῦ τῦ κυρίυ ἡμῶν,. Quod scilicet sicut justitiam illam in nobis efficit, ita vitam æternam ipse nobis daturus est, ut post Patrem ipsi omnia debeamus.

Particula ἵνα hic τελικῶς accipitur, qua finis exprimitur tum justificationis per justitiæ Christi imputationem, ceu Objecti principalis, in quo occupatur Apostolus, tum superabundantis gra- tiæ, cum abundat peccatum, ut scilicet non mi- nus, imo amplius dominetur gratia per justitiam ad vitam, quam dominatum est peccatum in mor- tem. Quænam autem ista sit justitia partim ex antegressis constat, nimirum non justitia inhærens, vel obedientia Christianorum, quam è circulo ju- stificationis exclusit Apostolus, sed justitia im- putata vel aliena ipsius Christi obedientia, qua nos justos constitui docuit: partim ex opposi- tione: quia peccato, quod dominatur in morte, opponitur justitia Christi, illi Adami inobedien- tiæ Christi obedientia, Adami delicto Christi δικαίωμα; partim ex effectu, quia non justitia Christianorum, sed solum obedientia Christi causa est vitæ: & per justitiam nobis per fidem imputatur: adeoque gratia dominatur ad æter- nam vitam per JESUM Christum Dominum nostrum, qua nos redemit sibi in peculium, & proprio mercatus est sanguine 2. Petr. II. 4. per quem est illa justitiæ imputatio meritorie. Hunc enim respectum hic attendit Apostolus: non autem quatenus ipse efficit justitiam in nobis, & vitam æternam daturus nobis est. Quod cum Patre & Spiritu S. ipsi commune est, uti omnia illa ipsi non post Patrem, sed cum Patre & Spi- ritu S. debemus, quia hi tres unum sunt 1. Joh. V. 7. Id vero hic loci alienum est, quia solum de eo agitur, quod proprium est Christo Domino nostro. Ἐν θανάτῳ Erasmus & Schmalzius red- dunt in morte; alii autem rectius ἐν pro εἰς acci- piunt, uti Matth. XVI. 28. Luc. XXIII. 41. Eph. I. 12. hæc particula sumitur; quia id poscit oppositio εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον. Atque hæc de capite Quinto.

SUBSECTIO II. Doctrinæ Apostolicæ de Justitia fidei ἔκθεσιν continens.

ARTICULUS I. Vindicans eam ab objectionibus calumniantium.

## 6:1 Argument
CHAPTER VI.

ARGUMENT.

A twofold objection is met. The first is, as if it seemed that one must sin so that grace may abound. This is refuted by the end of Baptism, namely that we have been baptized into the death of Christ, and buried with Christ, and rise again through Baptism grafted into the same, so that just as He was raised from the dead, so we also might walk in newness of life; then by the crucifixion of the old man, that is, so that dead with Christ we might also live with the same GOD, nor should sin reign in our natural body, and also from the condition of the justified, because we are not under law, but under grace. The other objection is that those who are not under law seem to be able to sin with impunity. To which the Apostle replies that we are therefore freed from sin so that we may serve righteousness, and present our members to the service not of sin, but of righteousness, and that the end of the servitude of sin is death, but the end of the servitude of GOD is eternal life, yet in such a way that by sin we indeed deserve death as a wage; but from grace in Christ Jesus, to those serving GOD, eternal life is obtained.

PARTITION OF THE CHAPTER.

The division of the chapter is thus easily established: for since he refutes a twofold objection and calumny against the doctrine of justification by faith, there are two parts to it: the first concerning the grace of God in the forgiveness of sin, because he had said that where sin abounded, grace did much more abound, whence it seemed to follow that one must sin strenuously, so that grace might abound the more. The second, refuting the objection concerning the state of the justified, that they are not under the law, but under grace, as if from the fact that they are not under the law, it follows that it is permitted for them to sin. The Apostle resolved both in such a way that he further consolidated the principal theme, which is concerning justification by grace through faith, in refuting these ἐγκλήματα.

PART I. The former objection, concerning the grace of GOD in the forgiveness of sin superabounding over any sins whatsoever, is refuted.

The Apostle first proposes this objection: Then indeed he refutes the same. It arises from the amplification of the grace of GOD, to which alone the Apostle ascribed justification, namely that GOD freely and out of grace forgives sins, and that this grace of GOD prevails over all sins, so much so that as sin abounds, divine grace superabounds, whence a doubt arises, whether one must remain in sin, so that grace may be more abundant, which was the slander of the Pseudo-Apostles, who opposed themselves to the Apostolic doctrine of gratuitous justification by faith. To which, therefore, the Apostle replies in such a way that he brings in the necessity of renewal and new obedience and divine life, and teaches that it not only well consists with the doctrine of gratuitous justification, but entirely redounds from the same.

Ver. 1. What then shall we say?

He spoke thus also above in IV. 1. and it is accustomed to be added to questions, as below in 21. 'We shall say' is also used by our writers in the present tense, as in Matthew VII. 4. The Apostle returns to that concerning which he himself and other Apostles were being defamed by the unbelieving Jews acting in Rome, and which he had touched upon in III. 8. But then he had not fully replied to it. Because in order for that to be done usefully, certain things had to be premised first, which are contained in the remaining part of the third chapter and in the fourth and fifth chapters, as these are now divided. For in Paul's epistle these were continuous. He says therefore now: What then is it that we say? Do we say those things which those Jews are spreading about us?

Shall we continue in sin that grace may abound?

In that manuscript in England is ἐπιμένομεν. This coheres correctly with that which preceded. Or do we say: Shall we persevere in sins, that the beneficence of GOD may appear more? Concerning the word χάριτος, as also concerning the word πλεονάσῃ, we have spoken above: The antecedent was true, that it was most glorious to GOD to gather to Himself a people from those who had been idolaters and involved in many flagrant crimes; But the inference was wicked: therefore that there is no evil if those who are called also persevere in sinning, so that GOD may again have mercy on them with greater glory. This consequence was falsely attributed to the Apostles and their followers, who both taught and showed by their deeds the contrary. Tertullian well: The matter was done by compensation: we have gained much, so that we may perform something. Likewise: Liberty in Christ has done no injury to innocence. The law of piety, holiness, humanity, truth, chastity, justice, mercy, benevolence, and modesty remains.

Latin:

CAPUT VI.

ARGUMENTUM.

Occurritur objectioni geminæ. Prima est, quasi peccandum esse videatur, ut gratia ab- undet. Quæ refellitur à fine tum Baptismi, quod nempe baptizati simus in mortem Christi, & sepulti cum Christo, & resurga- mus per Baptismum insiti eidem, ut quem- admodum ipse resuscitatus est ex mortuis, ita & nos in novitate vitæ ambulemus; tum crucifixionis veteris hominis, hoc est, ut mortui cum Christo cum eodem etiam DEO vivamus, nec dominetur peccatum in naturali corpore nostro, nec non à justi- ficatorum conditione, quia non su- mus sub lege, sed sub gratia. Altera ob- jectio est, quod qui sub lege non sunt, vi deantur impune peccare posse. Cui respon- det Apostolus, quod ideo liberemur à pecca- to, ut serviamus justitiæ, & membra nostra sistamus servitio non peccati, sed justitiæ, quodque servitutis peccati finis sit mors, servitutis vero DEI finis sit vita æterna, ita tamen, ut peccato quidem mereamur mortem ceu stipendium; ex gratia autem in Christo Jesu servientibus DEO obtingat vita æterna.

PARTITIO CAPITIS.

ITa facile constat partitio capitis: cum enim geminam diluat Objectionem & calumniam doctrinæ de justificatione per fidem oppositam, duæ sunt ejusdem partes: Prima de gratia Dei in condona- tione peccati, quod abundante peccato superabundare gratiam dixerat, unde consequens videbatur, peccandum esse strenue, ut eo magis abundet gratia. Al- tera diluens objectionem de statu justi- ficatorum, quod non sint sub lege, sed sub gratia, quasi inde, quia sub lege non sunt, sequatur, quod peccare ipsis liceat. Utrū- que ita expedivit Apostolus, ut princi- pale thema, quod est de justificatione ex gratia per fidem in diluendis hisce ἐγκλή- μασι ulterius consolidarit.

PARS I. Objectio prior, à gratia DEI in condonatione peccati super- abundante præ quibusvis pec- catis, diluitur.

PRimum autem proponit Apostolus hanc obje- ctionem: Deinde vero diluit eandem. Ori- tur illa ex amplificatione gratiæ DEI, cui soli ad- scripsit Apostolus justificationem, quod nempe DEUS gratis & ex gratia peccata condonet, at- que hæc DEI gratia peccatis universis prævaleat, adeo ut uti abundat peccatum, superabundet divina gratia, unde dubium enascitur, anne ma- nendum sit in peccato, ut abundantior sit gratia, quæ calumnia erat Pseudo-Apostolorum, doctri- næ Apostolicæ de justificatione gratuita per fi- dem sese opponentium. Ad quam proinde ita respondet Apostolus, ut necessitatem renovationis ac novæ obedientiæ & vitæ divinæ adferat, eamque cum doctrina de gratuita justificatione non mo- do probe consistere, sed ex eadem omnino redun- dare doceat.

Vers. 1. Τί ὖν ἐρῦμεν.

Sic & supra locutus est IV. 1. & solet addi interroga- tionibus, ut infra 21. ἐρῦμεν nostris scriptoribus etiam in præsenti dicitur, ut Matth. VII. 4. Redit Apostolus ad id, de quo ipse & Apostoli alii per Judæos incredulos Romæ agentes infamabantur, & quod attigerat III. 8. Sed tunc non plene ei responderat. Quia ut id utiliter fieret quæ- dam prius erant præstruenda, quæ continentur cætera parte capitis tertii & capitibus quarto & quinto, ut nunc ista dis- secta sunt. Nam in Pauli epistola fuere hæc continua. Ait ergo nunc: Quid ergo est quod dicimus? An ista dicimus, quæ Judæi illi de nobis spargunt?

Ἐπιμενῶμεν τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ ἵνα ἡ χάρις. πλεονάσῃ;

In Manuscripto illo in Anglia est ἐπιμένομεν. ,, Recte cohæret hoc cum eo, quod præcessit. An,, dicimus: Perseveremus in peccatis, ut magis ap-,, pareat DEI beneficentia? De voce χάριτ,,, ut & de voce πλεονάσῃ diximus supra: Antece-,, dens verum erat, DEO maxime fuisse glorio-,, sum ex iis qui idololatræ multisque flagitiis in-,, voluti fuerant populum sibi colligere; Sed ini-,, qua erat illatio: ideo nihil mali esse, si & vocati,, peccare perseverent, ut rursum DEUS majore,, cum gloria eorum misereatur. Hoc consequens,, falso attribuebatur Apostolis, & eorum sectato-,, ribus, qui contrarium & docebant & factis,, ostendebant. Tertullianus bene: Compensatio-,, ne res acta est: lucrati sumus multa, ut aliqua,, prastemus. Item: Libertas in Christo nullam inno-,, centia fecit juriam. Manet lex pietatis, sanctitatis,, humanitatis, veritatis, castitatis, justitiæ, miseri-,, cordiæ, benevolentiæ, pudicitiæ.

## 6:2
Μὴ γένοιτο. It is the expression of one turning away, as above III. 4. 6. 13.

The future tense can be conveniently retained in both places. What then shall we say? Or what shall we answer to those who are of the contrary part? Shall we remain in sin, that grace may abound? The emphasis is on the word ἐπιμένειν, since the preposition ἐπὶ intensifies the meaning; so that it is not simply to persist and persevere in sin, but to indulge in sin, to loosen the reins; as ἐπιμενεῖν is said of that which flourishes, blooms, and exerts its power most potently in something, as noted by the blessed Weller on this passage from a comparison of 1 Cor. XIII, 13, John III, 36, chapter IX, 41. But the occasion for this objection and calumny is not from the calling of idolaters and flagrant sinners, but from the justification of sinners and the gratuitous pardon of iniquities, nor does it return to that which the Apostle touched upon in Rom. III, 8, although this is a twin objection, but he vindicates his assertion concerning grace prevailing over sins, so that however much the offense abounds, the divine grace nevertheless superabounds in the pardon of sins. The very words of the Apostle imply this: as Oecumenius rightly says on this passage:

Because he had said above, where sin abounded, grace abounded, lest to some of unsound mind that exhortation might seem to be an encouragement to sin, he refutes it, saying: God forbid! which is a phrase usually employed regarding things that are admittedly absurd. This expression μὴ γένοιτο corresponds to the Hebrew חלילה Gen. XVIII. 25, ch. XLIV. 7, 2 Sam. XX. 20. Far be it! And it is an expression of one abominating something as profane. The Apostle refutes this accusation partly from the means of justification on the part of God, Baptism; partly from the meritorious cause, the passion and crucifixion of Christ; partly from the state and condition of the justified: on which occasion he simultaneously addresses and dilutes another accusation and objection. He therefore assumes Baptism, not only because it is most known to all and to be received by all, but also because it is a medium both of regeneration, through which faith in Christ, by which we are justified, is procreated and exists in us, and of renewal, which is connected to justification. Tit. III. 5. This argument from the end of Baptism the Apostle elegantly executes, explaining the mystery which is veiled in this Sacrament, namely, in what manner we are baptized into the death of Christ, so that we may be rendered participants not only of the primary fruit of the death of Christ, which is seen in justification, but also of the other fruit, redundant from the former, among the justified. For just as Christ suffered and died both for the merit, which is communicated to us in the remission of sins, and for the example ὑπογραμμὸν leaving it to the justified for imitation 1. Petr. II. 21, so in Baptism we are rendered participants of both fruits, nor can one be torn from the other, because we are both justified and saved διὰ λύτρου παλιγγενεσίας, and we die to sin, that we may live to righteousness, through the washing of the renewal of the Holy Spirit. Tit. III. 5.

We who have died to sin.

A manner of speaking accepted among the Hebrews. Philo in his book on Allegories: 'This does not happen unless the king of Egypt, the godless and pleasure-loving way, dies and departs from the soul.' And in the book 'That the worse is wont to attack the better': 'The most paradoxical thing is that it is both destroyed and lives; it is destroyed from the mind of the foolish, but it lives the happy life in God.' But also among the Philosophers. For Porphyry also compares wisdom to death, saying: 'Nature therefore releases the body from the soul, but the soul itself from the body.' Marcus Antoninus in book VII: 'As one who has died, one must live the rest according to nature.'

For whatever, changed from its own boundaries, departs, / This is immediately the death of that which was before.

To die to sin is to no longer live in sin, just as to die to the law Gal. II. 19 is to no longer live according to the law.

How shall we still live in it?

πῶς here does not show the absolutely impossible, but the indignity of the thing, as in Matth. VI. 28, Gal. IV. 9. It is unworthy if, having been washed, we wallow in the mire 2. Petr. II. 22. Hence now the Apostle begins to oppose the true doctrine to that which was falsely imputed to him, so that Christians might have something to reply to the objectors with the Apostle's own words. Therefore he now addresses the Christians.

To die to sin is not to no longer live in sin: because thus the sense would be identical: those who no longer live in sin, how shall they still live in sin? but to die to sins, so that we put them off and lay them aside, bid them farewell, mortify them, and as far as possible extinguish them: as the dead are extinguished. Whence those who thus seriously die to sin, in no way live in sin, nor do they permit sins to revive in themselves. Which is otherwise called crucifying, putting off, and laying aside the old man, the lusts of the flesh or the flesh with its wicked lusts Gal. V. 25, Col. III. 9, Eph.

IV. 22. But it is one thing to die to sin in the sixth case, another in the third case. To die to sin, in the sixth case or in sin, is when we are overcome and mortified by sin, so that we must perish in sin, with sin prevailing against us and killing us. In the third case, it is when we overcome and mortify sin, so that sin may die in us, lest it rule over us, concerning which death Ambrose T. III. de fid. resurrect. says: 'Blessed is the death which is a refuge from guilt, dedicated to the Lord, separates us from the mortal, consecrates us to the immortal.' B. Rungius Disp. XII. on this Epistle: 'To die to sin,' he says, 'signifies not only a certain common abstinence from the purpose of sinning, but a certain antipathy, such as is between the dead and the living, or the inability which is in the dead with respect to performing the actions of life.' Thus to live to sin is to be delighted by it, and to practice it in daily actions. Therefore the Apostle considers it unworthy and absurd that we who are justified should live in sin, indulge in sins, and be delighted, so that they may live in us, and we seek life and pleasure in them. Since those who are dead to sin are justified, they have not only obtained the remission of sins, but have also renounced it, resist it, repress and mortify it, and as much as is in them, extinguish it. Which duty of theirs from Baptism the Apostle is now about to prove. The Papists wish to extort from this their dogma concerning the total removal and extirpation of sin, because spiritual death excludes every sense of good; but the metaphorical expression is not to be urged, nor extended beyond the mind of the Holy Spirit against the analogy of faith. The justified die to sin, as far as the dominion of sin is concerned, so that it may be abolished, not as far as every sense of sin is concerned, which does not expire except with bodily death. For the Apostle speaks of the dominion of sin, that sin does not rule over the justified, and that they do not serve that sin, verses 6, 8, 12, 13, 14, but he does not teach that they are without sin and the sense of sin. And thus also to die to the law, Gal. II. 18, 19, and in this place not to be under the law, verse 14, is not to be entirely devoid of the law or to have fully cast off every sense of the law, but not to be subject to the tyranny of the law, and not to experience or fear its curse; just as to continue in sin is to be overwhelmed by sins and to experience their power, so to be dead to sin is to be freed from the dominion and oppression of sin, but not to be entirely free from sin and its sense, since the justified still have need of daily mortification, so that they may be more and more freed from the same.

Latin:

Μὴ γένοιτο. Aversantis est, ut supra III. 4. 6. 13.

Retineri commode utrobique potest futurum tempus. Quid igitur dicemus? Vel quid respon- debimus τοῖς ἐξ ἐναντίας? Manebimus in peccato, ut gratia abundet? Emphasis est in voce ἐπι- μένειν, quum præpositio ἐπὶ Significationem inten- dat; ut non simpliciter tantum sit persistere & per- severare in peccato, sed indulgere peccato, fræna laxare; uti ἐπιμενεῖν manere Illud dicitur, quod viget, floret & potentissime vim suam in aliquo exerit, notante B. Wellero ad h. l. è collatione 1. Cor. XIII, 13. Job. III. 36. cap. IX. 41. Non vero oc- casio huic objectioni & calumniæ est è vocatione idololatrarum, & flagitiosorum, sed è justifica- tione peccatorum, & gratuita condonatione ini- quitatum, neque ad id redit, quod Rom. III 8. attigit Apostolus, etsi hæc gemina sit objectio, sed assertum suum vindicat de gratia prævalente pecca- tis, ita, ut quantumcunque abundet delictum, superabundet tamen divina gratia in pecca- torum condonatione. Id verba ipsa Apostoli inferunt: ut recte Oecumenius in hunc locum:

Quia supra dixerat, ubi abundavit peccatum, abun- davit gratia, ne quibusdam non sanæ mentis ea vi- deretur adhortatio ad peccatum, refutatur dicens : Abfit! quod de iis usurpari solet, quæ in confesso est esse absurda. Vox hæc μὴ γένοιτο respondet Ebræo חלילה Gen. XVIII. 25. cap. XLIV. 7. 2. Sam. XX. 20. Absit! Estque vox tanquam pro- phanum aliquid abominantis. Refellit autem cri- minationem hanc Apostolus partim è medio ju- stificationis ex parte D E I, Baptismo; partim è causa meritoria, passione & crucifixione Christi ; partim è statu & conditione justificatorum: qua occasione simul alteram criminationem & obje- ctionem aggreditur & diluit. Baptismum ideo assumit, non tantum quia omnibus notissimus, ab omnibus suscipiendus, sed etiam quia medi- um est & regenerationis, per quod fides in Chri- stum, qua justificamur, in nobis procreatur, & exsistit, & renovationis, quæ justificationi con- nexa est. Tit. III. 5. Quod argumentum à fine Baptismi eleganter exequitur Apostolus myste- rium explicans, quod in hoc Sacramento velatum est, qua ratione nempe in mortem Christi bapti- semur, ut non tantum fructus mortis Christi primarii, qui conspicitur in justificatione, partici- pes reddamur, sed etiam fructus alterius, è priori redundantis, penes justificatos. Ut enim Chri- stus passus & mortuus tum ob meritum, quod communicatur nobis in remissione peccatorum, tum ob exemplum ὑπογραμμὸν ad imitationem relinquens justificatis 1. Petr. II. 21. ita in Bapti- smo utriusque fructus participes reddimur, nec alter ab altero divelli potest, quia & justificamur & salvamur διὰ λύτρου παλιγγενεσίας, & τῇ ἁμαρ- τίᾳ peccato morimur, ut justitiæ vivamus, per la- vacrum renovationis Spiritus Sancti. Tit. III. 5.

Ϊ Οἵτινες ἀπεθάνομεν τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ.

Loquendi genus receptum apud Hebræos. Philo li- bro de Allegoriis : Τοῦτο δ᾽ οὐ γίνεται ἐὰν μὴ τελευτήσῃ κὴ ἀποθάνῃ ἐκ τῆς ψυχῆς ὁ βασιλεὺς τῆς Αἰγύπτου, ὁ ἄθεος καὶ φιλήδονος τρόπος. Et libro pejorem insidiari meliori : Ἄθελ τὸ παραδοξότατον ἀνῄρηταί τε καὶ ζῇ· ἀνῄρηται μὲν ἐκ τῆς τοῦ ἄφρονος διανοίας, ζῇ δὲ τὴν ἐν Θεῷ ζωὴν εὐδαίμο- να. Sed & apud Philosophos. Nam & Porphyrius sapi- entiam morti comparat dicens : Φύσις μὲν ἄρα λύει σῶμα ἐκ ψυχῆς, ψυχὴ δὲ αὐτὴ ἀπὸ σώματος. Marcus Antoni- nus libro VII. ὡς ἀποτεθνηκότα δεῖ τὸ λοιπὸν ζῆσαι κατὰ τὴν φύσιν.

Nam quodcunque suis mutatum finibus exit, Continuo hoc mors est illius, quod fuit ante.

Ἀποθανεῖν ἁμαρτίᾳ est non amplius vivere in peccato, sic- ut ἀποθανεῖν νόμῳ Gal. II. 19. non ultra secundum legem vivere.

Πῶς ἔτι ζήσομεν ἐν αὐτῇ.

πῶς hic non τὸ πάντως ἀδύνατον, sed rei indignitatem ostendit, ut Matth. VI. 28. Gal. IV. 9. Indignum est, si loti in lutum revolvimur 2. Petr. II. 22. Hinc jam inci- pit Apostolus doctrinæ, quæ ipsi falso imputabatur, veram opponere, ut haberent Christiani, quod ipsis Apostoli verbis regererent objectatoribus. Itaque Christianos jam alloquitur.

Ἀποθανεῖν ἁμαρτίᾳ non est non amplius vivere in peccato: quia sic identicus foret sensus : qui non amplius vivunt in peccato, quomodo vivent adhuc in peccato? sed mori peccatis, ita ut illa exuamus ac deponamus, iis valedicamus, illa mor- tificemus, quoad fieri potest illa extinguamus : uti mortui extinguuntur. Unde qui ita serio mo- riuntur peccato, nullatenus vivunt in peccato, nec peccata in sese reviviscere permittunt. Quod alias dicitur crucifigere, exuere, & deponere veterem hominem, concupiscentias carnis vel carnem cum concupiscentiis pravis Gal. V. 25. Col. III. 9. Eph.

IV. 22. Aliud autem est mori peccato in casu sex- to, aliud in casu tertio. Mori peccato, in casu sexto vel in peccato, est cum à peccato supera- mur & mortificamur, ut in peccato pereundum sit, peccato adversus nos prævalente, nosque oc- cidente. In casu tertio est cum nos peccatum su- peramus & mortificamus, ut peccatum in no- bis intereat, ne dominetur nobis, de qua mor- te Ambros. T. III. de fid. resurrect. Beata mors, quæ culpæ refuga, Domino dedita, à mortali nos sepa- rat, immortali nos consecrat. B. Rungius Disp. XII. in hanc Epist. Mori peccato, inquit, signi- ficat non modo vulgarem quandam abstinentiam à proposito peccandi, sed quandam ἀντιπάθειαν, qua- lis est inter mortuos, & vivos, aut ἀδυναμίαν, quæ in mortuis est, respectu actionum vitæ efficienda- rum. Ita vivere peccato est eo delectari, idque quotidianis actionibus usurpare. Ideo ergo Apo- stolus pro indigno & absurdo habet, nos justifi- catos vivere in peccato, indulgere peccatis, & delectari, ut illa vivant in nobis, & nos vitam in illis & oblectationem quæramus. Siquidem mortui peccato sint justificati, non tantum re- missionem peccatorum consequuti sunt, sed et- iam renunciarint, ei resistant, reprimant ac mor- tificent, & quantum in ipsis est extinguant. Quod eorum debitum è Baptismo jam probaturus est Apostolus. Pontificii hinc extorquere volunt do- gma suum de omnimoda peccati sublatione & ex- tirpatione, quia mors spiritualis omnem boni sensum excludat; sed non urgenda est metapho- rica locutio, neque extendenda ultra mentem Spiritus Sancti contra analogiam fidei. Moriun- tur justificati peccato, quantum ad dominium pec- cati, ut id aboleatur, non quantum ad omnem peccati sensum, qui non nisi cum morte corpo- rali expirat. Nam Apostolus de dominio pec- cati loquitur, quod justificatis peccatum non do- minetur, quodque non servant illi peccato vers. 6. 8. 12. 13. 14. non vero eosdem sine peccato & peccati sensu esse docet. Atque ita etiam τὸ mo- ri legi Gal. II. 18. 19. & hoc loco non esse sub lege vers. 14. non est expertem plane esse legis sive omnem sensum legis plene exuisse, sed ty- rannidi legis non esse subjectum, & maledictio- nem ejus non experiri, aut metuere, ut ἐπιμένειν in peccato est peccatis obrutum esse & vim eo- rum experiri, sic mortuum esse peccato est à pec- cati dominio & oppressiooe liberatum esse, non autem plane à peccato ejusque sensu liberum esse, siquidem justificati adhuc quotidiana mor- tificatione opus habeant, ut magis magisque ab eadem liberentur.

## 6:3
V. 3. Or do you not know?

Do you not remember? So also below VII. 1.

That as many of us as were baptized into Christ Jesus.

That is, into the name or doctrine of JESUS Christ, as in Acts XIX. 6.

Into his death we were baptized.

Ignatius to the Trallians: You seem to me not to be living according to man, but according to Jesus Christ, who died for us, so that by believing into his death you might become partakers of his resurrection through baptism. Justin in his dialogue with Trypho: As also Christ our Christ redeemed us, who were baptized in the most grievous sins which we committed, through his being crucified on the wood and through water, having sanctified us. And afterwards: For Christ, being the firstborn of every creature and the beginning again of another race, has become the one who is born again by him through water and faith and wood, which contains the mystery of the cross. Then: I said that through water and faith and wood, those who are preparing themselves and repenting of the sins they have committed will escape the judgment of God that is about to come. Those who were baptized were required to make a profession of faith, in which this also was included, that Christ for our sins was dead, that is, for the abolishing of sins. See above IV. 25. Christ also gave up his own life for us; And we ought to do the same for his sake, how much more to give up wicked desires? What death is to the body of Christ, that baptism is to sin.

The force of the Apostolic argument is this: Those who have been baptized into the death of Christ are dead to sin, so that they may no longer live to it. Those who have been baptized into Christ Jesus have been baptized into the death of Christ. Therefore, those who have been baptized into Christ Jesus are dead to sin, so that they may no longer live to it. For the major proposition to be established, it must be observed that those who are baptized into the death of Christ die to sin as far as the debt is concerned; but as for the act, those finally die to sin who are justified through faith in Christ, which liberation from the guilt of sin is followed by liberation from the dominion of sin. For the question here is about the debt, and what is inferred by the force of the Apostolic doctrine. For we are baptized into the death of Christ, who died for us and because of our sins, not so that he might seal the doctrine concerning the abolition of sin by his martyrdom, as Grotius wishes, which could have been done by other Saints, and was done, but so that by the merit of his passion and death he might acquire for us liberation from sins, and furthermore in his passion and death he wished to leave us an example of obedience, trust, charity, patience, meekness, humility, and other virtues, which we may imitate by the power of the Holy Spirit: of both of whose fruits we are rendered participants when we are baptized into the death of Christ, and consequently we are baptized into the death of Christ for the sake of both ends, so that we may both be liberated by the death of Christ from the guilt of sin, and the Holy Spirit may be poured out upon us, by whose power we may be rendered free from the dominion of sin, so that, dead to sin, we may no longer live to it, but to our Lord, and follow in his most holy footsteps. These ends are subordinate; for liberation from the guilt of sin or justification is followed by liberation from the dominion of sin, so that the justified may not live to sin, but, dead to sin, may live to the Lord, who liberated them from the guilt and curse of sin, and may serve him. For Christ died for all for this reason, that those who live (which life begins in Baptism) should not live for themselves, but for him who died for them and rose again. 2 Cor. V. 15. Athanasius, Vol. 1, on the incarnation of the Word of GOD. And therefore, he says, we are baptized into his death, because his death was not a punishment for sin, nor comparable to the death of Adam, but an expiation of sin and of the death arising through sin.

Latin:

V. 3. Ἢ ἀγνοεῖτε.

Annon meministis? Sic & infra VII. 1.

Ὅτι ὅσοι ἐβαπτίσθημεν εἰς χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν.

Id est, in nomen seu doctrinam JESU Christi, ut Actor. XIX. 6.

Εἰς τὸν θάνατον αὐτῶ ἐβαπτίσθημεν.

Ignatius ad Trallenses: Φαίνεσθέ μοι ἐ κατ᾿ ἄνθρωπον ζῶντες, ἀλλὰ κατὰ Ἰησοῦν χριστὸν, τὴν δι᾽ ἡμᾶς ἀποθανόντα, ἵνα πιστεύοντες εἰς τὸν θάνατον αὐτῶ διὰ τὸ βαπτίσματος κοινωνοὶ τῆς ἀναστάσεως ἀυτῶ γένησθε. Justinus colloquio cum Try- phone: ὥς κὶ ἡμᾶς βεβαπτισμένους ταῖς βαρυτάταις ἁμαρτίαις ἂς ἐπράξαμεν διὰ τῶ σταυρωθῆναι ἐπὶ τῶ ξύλω κὶ δι᾽ ὕδατος ἁγιά- σας ὁ χριστὸς ἡμῶν ἐλυτρώσατο. Et postea: Ὁ γὰρ χριστὸς, πρω- τότοκος πάσης κτίσεως ὢν κὶ ἀρχὴ πάλιν ἄλλε γένες γέγονεν, τῶ ἀναγεννηθέντος ὑπ᾿ ἀυτῶ δι᾽ ὕδατος κὶ πίστεως κὶ ξύλε, τῶτο μυ- στήριον, τῶ σταυρῶ ἔχοντος. Deinde: Εἶπον δὲ δι᾽ ὕδατος καὶ πίστεως καὶ ξύλω οἱ προπαρασκευαζόμενοι κὶ μετανοῦντες ἐφ᾽ οἷς ἥμαρτον ἐκφεύξονται τὴν μέλλεσαν ἐπέρχεσθαι τῶ Θεῶ κρίσιν. Qui baptizabantur, ab iis exigebatur professio fi- dei, in qua & hoc erat, Christum ob peccata nostra esse mortuum, id est, ad abolenda peccata. Vide supra IV. 25. Christus etiam vitam suam pro nobis abdicavit; Et nos idem facere debemus ipsius causa, quanto magis abdicare pravas cupidines? Quod mors corpori Christi hoc baptismus peccato.

Vis argumenti Apostolici haec est: Qui in mortem Christi baptizati sunt, peccato mortui sunt, ut eidem non amplius vivant. Qui in Christum Jesum baptizati sunt, in mortem Christi sunt baptizati. E. qui in Christum Jesum baptizati sunt, peccato mortui sunt, ut eidem non amplius vivant. Major propositio ut constet, observandum, quod illi quidem, qui baptizantur in mortem Christi, peccato moriantur quantum ad debitum; quoad actum autem peccato moriuntur illi demum, qui per fidem in Christum justificantur, qui liberationem a peccati reatu sequitur liberatio a dominio peccati. De debito enim hic quaestio est, & quid inferatur, vi doctrinae Apostolicae. Nam in mortem Christi baptizamur, qui pro nobis & propter peccata nostra mortuus est, non ut martyrio suo doctrinam de abolitione peccati obsignaret, ut Grotius vult, quod ab aliis Sanctis fieri poterat, & factum est, sed ut merito passionis & mortis suae liberationem a peccatis nobis acquireret, ac praeterea in passione & morte sua exemplum obedientiae, fiduciae, caritatis, patientiae, mansuetudinis, humilitatis, aliorumque virtutum nobis relinquere voluit, quod virtute Spiritus S. imitemur: cujus utriusque fructus participes nos reddimur, quum baptisamur in mortem Christi, ac proinde utriusque finis causa in mortem Christi baptizemur, ut & liberemur morte Christi a peccati reatu, & Spiritus S. effundatur in nos, cujus virtute liberi reddamur a dominio peccati, ut peccato mortui, amplius non vivamus eidem, sed Domino nostro, ejusque sanctissimis vestigiis insistamus. Fines hi subordinati sunt; nam liberationem a reatu peccati vel justificationem consequitur liberatio a dominio peccati, ut justificati non vivant peccato, sed peccato mortui Domino, qui eos a peccati reatu & maledictione liberavit, vivant, atque servant. Nam ideo mortuus est Christus pro omnibus, ut qui vivunt, (quae vita in Baptismo incipit) non sibi vivant, sed ei, qui pro ipsis mortuus est, & resurrexit. 2. Cor. V. 15. Athanas. T. 1. de incarn. verb. DEI. Atque ideo, inquit, in mortem ejus baptizamur, quia mors illius non poena peccati, neque comparabilis cum morte Adae, sed peccati mortisque per peccatum enascentis expiatio fuit.

## 6:4
V. 4. We were buried with him through baptism into death.

He shows that not only the words of baptism, but its very form implies this. For the immersion of the whole body into the stream, so that it was no longer seen, bore the image of the burial which is given to the dead. Thus Gal. II. 12. Buried with him in baptism.

Into death.

Also to represent the death of Christ to the eyes.

As is the death, so is the burial. We are dead to sin, in baptism, because we have put off sin: Sin also must be buried. Which is adumbrated in the immersion in baptism, therefore we are said to be buried with Christ through baptism into death, not to represent the death of Christ, but to testify to and seal the death of sin: For he is dealing with the death of sin as the underlying matter, or the principal object at present, and he confirms the same from the burial of Christ, just as he did before from the death of Christ. Those who take it concerning the death of Christ do not attend to the fact that the Apostle is already dealing with the burial of Christ. It should therefore have been said to him, we are buried with him through baptism, not into his death but into HIS BURIAL. But because he says into death, he indicates the death OF SIN. Indeed we have died with Christ, just as we are said here to be buried with him, for from this, that the Apostle says we are buried with him, it is to be gathered that he also understands that we have died with Christ, and we have died with Christ, because since Christ died for us, it is the same as if we ourselves had died 2 Cor. V. 14. and as Christ when he was dying was burdened with our sins, for which he was delivered unto death: so in death he laid down the burden of our sin, and was burdened with no sin further; so also we, having died with him, lay down our own burden of sin. Similarly we are buried with Christ, because when Christ was buried our sins were buried, who brought our iniquities into the sepulcher, not that he was still burdened with them, but that he laid them down in death, and through his burial he put them away from sight, and entombed them: concerning which Isaiah chapter LIII. 9. prophesied: Christ placed wickedness into his sepulcher: that he buried the sins of men, which he had taken upon himself, and had carried in his body upon the wood of the cross, in his burial, so that they might be hidden from the face of GOD, and this tyrant might not be troublesome to us by his force and dominion; after their putting away was done in death Heb. IX. 16. This therefore, both what was done to the sins of men in the death and burial of Christ, in respect of which men are said to have died with Christ, and to be buried with the same, concerns all men universally, because he had taken upon himself the sins of all men. In Baptism, however, an individual application must be made, so that those who are baptized may both die with and be buried with Christ on both counts, so that they may be rendered participants of these benefits of Christ, so that sin is not merely put off, or laid down, so that liberated from its guilt, they may also become free from its dominion, until they are also liberated from the sense of the same in the blessed departure, and eternal life, to which they are regenerated and renewed in baptism: but so that sin also may be buried, hidden, or concealed, so that it may neither infest nor disturb us with its curse, nor with its dominion.

That just as Christ was raised from the dead.

For the body rising from the water also bore an image of this thing.

Through the glory of the Father.

That is, by the power which glory follows. This is what is called κράτος ἰσχύος in Eph. 1:19, 10, for which in Colossians 1:11 it is called κράτος τῆς δόξης. Just as עז, which is accustomed to be translated as ἰσχὺς, is translated as δόξα in Psalm 68:36, Isa. 12:2, 45:24.

So also we might walk in newness of life.

A Hebraism, ἐν καινότητι ζωῆς for in new life. Now this day brings another life: it demands other morals. If we wish to rise with Christ, it is necessary that we imitate him; which imitation in those who have lived far otherwise is like a certain resurrection. For just as the separation of the soul from the body is the death of the body, so the separation of the soul from GOD is the death of the soul.

This is the third argument, why those justified by faith ought not to live in sins, taken from the purpose of Baptism. The first was: because through Baptism we die to sin. The second: because through baptism we must rise again, as Christ rose again, provided that we are made partakers of the fruits of Christ's resurrection. Christ rose from the sepulcher: and we must rise again. He was awakened from the dead through the glory of the Father, that he might live a new life devoid of sin, with sin holding no further right over Christ. And we from the dead we are awakened and rise again spiritually, to a new life, in which sin no longer dominates us; we have been made alive and have risen with Christ, because Christ, having died for us, sustained our person, and brought to us the life obtained by his death through his ἀναζωοποιήσει (making alive) and ἀναστάσει (resurrection): because as in Adam all die, so in Christ all are made alive 1 Cor. XV. 22. This is indeed appropriated to each one through Baptism, by which we are awakened and brought back into spiritual life, so that we may henceforth walk in newness of life. B. Gerhard observes here p. 187 that the death of Christ effects renewal in us both meritoriously, because he merited for us by his death the Holy Spirit, who renews our nature; and also typically and exemplarily, because in the death of Christ an example of the mortification of the flesh is set before us, and in his resurrection an example of the renewal of the Spirit. Coccejus explains that we are buried with CHRIST through Baptism, because Baptism is for us a sign of the communion of Christ's burial, or because that pertains to us. The burial, he says, of Christ is ours, as is his death. The latter, as a ransom; the former, as a legal argument that the guilt is finished and the curse removed. For, he who had been suspended from the tree was ordered to be buried before evening, lest the land be defiled, Deut. XXI. 23. Indeed, if the ending of the curse were not affirmed by the burial of the one suspended by Israel, they would defile their land; which had been given to them as an inheritance, nay, as a pledge of the true inheritance. Through baptism, therefore, it is sealed to us that the curse has been ended through the death and burial of Christ, and consequently that we, who are in him, are free from every curse. He does not inappropriately [say] these things about this passage p. 308, provided that a medium is substituted for a sign; because Baptism is not only a sign, but a medium of communion with Christ. Gregor. Nazianz. acclaims this here, orat. XLII. Christ is from the dead, rise together: Christ is to himself, return. Christ is from the sepulchre, be loosed from the stains of sin. The gates of hell are opened, and death is oppressed, and the old Adam is put off, and the new is perfected. If any be a new creature in Christ, be renewed. And Orat. XL. Therefore, let us be buried with Christ through baptism, that we may also rise with him: (into the water) that we may also be lifted up together: let us ascend with him, that we may also be affected together. Concerning which, in Nicetas's Comment. it is held: The water bears the image of death, receiving the body as if into a sepulchre. But the service sends forth a life-giving force, renewing our souls from the death of sin to their former life. Let us descend, as Christ into the sepulchre, so we also into baptism; that just as he [was raised] from the sepulchre of the dead, so we also may be carried on high from the tomb of sin and dead works. For baptism indeed designates and indicates the rejection of the works of the flesh, and cleanses and expiates the soul from the filth and uncleanness contracted from the contagion of carnal affection. But since Baptism contains a descent and an ascent, I will add this upon it: Let us ascend with him, just as he [ascended] into heaven, so we into that sublimity to which Baptism promotes us, that we may also be affected together with glory (by adoption, namely) and be made heirs of the heavenly kingdom, just as he was made heir of the seat at the right hand of the Father. These are from Nicetas's Comment. T. II. Oper. Nazianz. p. 1049.

Διὰ τῆς δόξης, 'by the glory,' some take as the efficient cause, as it is 'by the glorious power' 1 Cor. VI. 14. John XI. 40. And thus Christ was awakened by the glorious power of the Father, so that the Son and the Holy Spirit are not to be excluded, because the power of these is one and the same John II. 19. c. X. 17. 1 John V. 7. Others explain it as the final cause, that Christ was awakened for the sake of the glory of the Father, so that the Father might be glorified, just as we also ought to rise again spiritually, and walk in newness of life for the sake of the glory of the Father. Which is not inconvenient or foreign to the scope of the Apostle.

Latin:

V. 4. Συνετάφημεν σὺν ἀυτῷ διὰ τοῦ βαπτίσματος εἰς τὸν θάνατον.

Ostendit non verba tantum baptismi, sed & ipsam ejus formam hoc innuere. Nam immersio totius corporis in flumen, ita ut non conspiceretur amplius, imaginem gerebat sepulturae quae datur mortuis. Sic Gal. II. 12. Συνταφέντες ἀυτῷ ἐν τῷ βαπτίσματι.

Εἰς τὸν θάνατον.

Ad repraesentandam etiam oculis Christi mortem.

Qualis mors, talis sepultura est. Peccato mortui sumus, in baptismo, quod peccatum exuerimus: Peccatum etiam sepeliendum est. Quod adumbratum in immersione in baptismo, ideo cum Christo sepulti dicimur per baptisma εἰς τὸν θάνατον, non ad repraesentandam mortem Christi, sed ad mortem peccati testandam, & obsignandam: Nam de morte peccati ceu materia substrata, vel praecipuo in praesenti objecto agit, & e sepultura Christi eandem confirmat, uti antea e morte Christi. Qui de Christi morte accipiunt, id non attendunt, quod de sepultura Christi jam agat Apostolus. Dicendum ergo ei fuisset, consepulti sumus cum ipso per baptisma, non in mor- tem sed in SEPULTURAM EJUS. Quia vero dicit εἰς θάνατον, mortem PECCATI indicat. Nimirum commortui sumus Christo, uti conse- peliri cum ipso hic dicimur, ex hoc enim quod consepultos nos dicit Apostolus, colligere est, quod intelligat etiam nos commortuos esse cum Christo, commortui autem cum Christo sumus, quia Christo pro nobis mortuo perinde est, ac si ipsi mortui essemus 2. Cor. V. 14. & ut Christus cum moreretur, peccatis nostris onustus fuit, ob quæ in mortem traditus est: ita in morte peccati no- stri sarcinam deposuit, & nullo amplius peccato onustus fuit; ita & nos commortui cum ipso, peccati sarcinam propriam deponimus. Similiter consepulti sumus cum Christo, quia Christo sepul- to nostra sepulta sunt peccata, qui iniquitates no- stras sepulchro intulit, non quod iis adhuc onu- stus fuerit, sed quod eas in morte deposuerit, per sepulturam vero suam à conspectu abdicavit, & contumulavit: quo de Esaias cap. LIII. 9. vati- cinatus est: Posuit Christus improbitatem in sepul- chrum suum: quod peccata hominum, quæ in se susceperat, & super lignum crucis in corpore suo portaverat, in sepultura sua sepelierit, ut à facie DEI absconderentur, & nobis vi & dominio suo non molestus sit hic tyrannus; post eorum ἰθέησιν in morte factam Ebr. IX. 16. Hoc ergo utrumque, quod in morte & sepultura Christi pec- catis hominum factum, cujus respectu commor- tui homines cum Christo, & consepulti cum eodem dicuntur, universaliter omnes homines concernit, quia omnium hominum peccata in se susceperat. In Baptismo vero individualis debet fieri appli- catio, ut qui baptizantur utrinque & peccato com- moriantur, & consepeliantur cum Christo, ita ut participes horum beneficiorum Christi reddan- tur, peccatum non exuatur modo, vel deponatur, ut à reatu ejus liberati, liberi etiam à dominio ejus fiant, donec liberentur quoque à sensu ejusdem in beata ἀναλύσει, & æterna vita, ad quam in ba- ptismo regenerantur, & renovantur: sed ut pec- catum quoque sepeliatur, condatur, vel abscon- datur, ut nec maledictione sua, nec dominatu nos infestet, & inquietet.

Ἵνα ὥσπερ ἠγέρθη χριστὸς ἐκ νεκρῶν.

Nam & hujus rei imaginem gerebat corpus ex aqua resurgens.

Διὰ τῆς δόξης τοῦ πατρὸς.

Id est, per potentiam, quam gloria sequitur. Hoc est, quod κράτος ἰσχύος dicitur Eph. I. 19. V. 10. pro quo ad Colossenses I. 11. dicitur κράτος τῆς δόξης. Sicut עז quod ἰσχὺς verti solet, vertitur δόξα Psalm. LXVIII. 36. Esa. XII. 2. XLV. 24.

Οὕτω καὶ ἡμεῖς ἐν καινότητι ζωῆς περιπα- τήσωμεν.

Hebraismus ἐν καινότητι ζωῆς pro in vita nova. Nunc hic dies aliam vitam adfert: alios mores postulat. Si surgere cum Christo volumus, necesse est eum imite- mur; quæ imitatio in iis qui longe aliter vixere, est vel- ut resurrectio quædam. Nam sicut separatio animi à corpore est mors corporis, ita separatio animi à DEO est mors animi.

Tertium hoc est argumentum, cur justificati per fidem in peccatis vivere non debeant, à Ba- ptismi fine desumtum. Primum erat; quia per Baptismum morimur peccato. Alterum; quia per baptismum resurgendum nobis est, ut Chri- stus resurrexit, siquidem fructus resurrectionis Christi participes reddimur. Christus e sepulchro resurrexit: & nobis resurgendum est. Excitatus est e mortuis per gloriam Patris, ut vitam novam peccati expertem vivat, peccato nullum jus am- plius in Christum obtinente. Et nos è mortuis excitamur & resurgimus spiritualiter, ad vitam no- vam, in quá nobis peccatum ampliùs non domi- netur; vivificati sumus & resurreximus cum Chri- sto, quia Christus pro nobis mortuus personam nostram sustinuit, vitam morte sua partam ἀνα- ζωοποιήσει & ἀναστάσει sua nobis adduxit: quia sicut in Adamo omnes moriuntur, ita in Christo omnes vivificantur 1. Cor. XV. 22. Id vero unicuique appro- priatur per Baptismum, quo in vitam spiritualem excitamur, & reducimur, ut deinceps in novitate vitæ ambulemus. B. Gerhardus observat hic p. 187. mortem Christi renovationem in nobis efficere cum meritorie, quia promeruit nobis sua morte Spi- ritum Sanctum, qui Naturam nostram renovat; tum typice & exemplariter, quia in morte Christi proponitur nobis exemplar mortificationis carnis, in resurrectione vero exemplar renovationis Spiri- tus. Coccejus nos per Baptismum esse CHRISTO consepultos explicat, quod Baptismus nobis sit signaculum communionis sepulturæ Christi, sive quod ea ad nos pertineat. Sepultura, inquit, Chri- sti nostra est, ut mors. Hæc, ut lytron, illa, ut argu- mentum legale finiti reatus & execrationis ablatæ. Nam, qui suspensus fuerat de ligno, jubebatur se- peliri ante vesperam, ne terra fœdaretur, Deuter. XXI. 23. Nempe, si exsecrationis finitio non per se- pulturam suspensi affirmaretur ab Israële, terram suam fœdarent; quæ ipsis hæreditas, imo pignus ve- ræ hæreditatis, data erat. Per baptismum igitur nobis obsignatur, finitam esse execrationem per mor- tem & sepulturam Christi, & proinde nos, qui su- mus in ipso, ab omni execratione liberos esse. Hæc non inconcinne ille circa h. l. p. 308. modo pro signaculo medium substituetur; quia Baptismus non signaculum tantum est, sed medium commu- nionis cum Christo. Acclamat hic nos Gregor. Nazianz. orat. XLII. Christus ex mortuis, simul surgite: Christus ad sese, redite. Christus ex sepul- chro, peccati maculis solvamini. Portæ inferi ape- riuntur, & mors opprimitur, & vetus Adam de- ponitur, & novus perficitur. Si qua nova in Chri- sto creatura renovemini. Et Orat. XL. Proinde cum Christo per baptismum sepeliamur, ut & cum eo resurgamus; (in aquam) ut simul etiam extol- lamur: cum eo ascendamus, ut simul quoque afficia- mur. Quo de in Nicetæ Comment. habetur: Aqua mortis imaginem refert, corpus velut sepulchro ac- cipiens. Servitus autem vivificam vim emittit, animas nostras à peccati morte ad priorem vitam renovans. Descendamus, ut Christus in sepulchrum, ita nos quoque in baptismum; ut quemadmodum ille ex mortuorum sepulchro, ac nos etiam è peccati tumulo ac mortuis operibus in sublime feramur. Baptismus siquidem operum carnis abjectionem de- signat & indicat, animamque à sordibus & spurci- tie, ex carnalis affectus contagione contracta, lustrat & expiat. Quoniam autem Baptismus descensum atque ascensum continet, hoc super adjiciam: Cum eo ascendamus, quemadmodum videlicet ille in cœ- lum, ita nos in eam sublimitatem ad quam prove- hit Baptismus, ut simul quoque gloria afficiamur, (per adoptionem scilicet) ac regni cœlestis hæredes efficiamur, quemadmodum ille sedis in dextra patris hæres factus est. Hæc Nicetæ Comment. T. II. Oper. Nazianz. p. 1049.

Διὰ τῆς δόξης per gloriam nonnulli accipiunt de causa efficiente, ut est per potentiam gloriosam 1. Cor. VI. 14. Joh. XI. 40. Ita autem per potentiam gloriosam Patris excitatus est Christus, ut non excludendus sit Filius & Spiritus S. quia una ea- demque est horum potentia Joh. II. 19. c. X. 17. 1. Joh. V. 7. Alii de causa finali explicant, quod propter gloriam Patris excitatus Christus sit, ut glorificetur Pater, quemadmodum & nos refur- gere debemus spiritualiter, & in novitate vitæ ambulare propter gloriam Patris. Quod non in- commodum aut alienum est à scopo Apostoli.

## 6:5
V. 5. εἰ γὰρ σύμφυτοι γεγόναμεν τῷ ὁμοιώματι τοῦ θανάτου αὐτοῦ.

In Greek, those things are called συμφύεσθαι which grow together into one, like certain plants Luke VIII. 7, from which the translation is taken and used regarding friendship in Plato and Plutarch. Therefore, αὐτοῦ (his) is understood here from the following Genitive αὐτοῦ, as is often the case. We have grown together with Christ, to the likeness of his death, namely, in desires, as he in the functions of life.

ἀλλὰ καὶ τῆς ἀναστάσεως ἐσόμεθα.

Namely, we shall be σύμφυτοι (grown together) with him in the likeness of the resurrection. Thus we shall rise again in his likeness. The former similarity is of the genus, this is of the species, or of the proximate genus. Where comforts are opposed to troublesome things, the particles εἰ and ἀλλά are accustomed to be used. Thus in Virgil:

If the high house does not vomit from its proud doors a wave of those greeting in the morning from all its halls. Then after a few verses follows: But secure rest and a life ignorant of deceit, rich in various wealth, etc.

The Apostle confirms what he had said about the end of Baptism, because in Baptism we are made σύμφυτοι (grown together) with the likeness of Christ's death, therefore also with his resurrection. The Apostle alludes to our institution or implantation, by which we are inserted into Christ through Baptism, as into the tree of life Rev. XXII. v. 11, and the true vine John XV. 1, 5, and the olive tree Rom. XI. 17, 18, 19, and we draw spiritual sap from him, so that we may be made conformable to him, in death and resurrection: and the Apostle concludes: If we have been implanted in Christ, so that we may be like him in death, we shall also be implanted in him, so that we may be like him in resurrection. Chrysostom has here: By the name of plantation, he signifies the fruit which we have received from it. For just as the body of Christ buried in the earth brought forth fruit, the salvation of the world: so also ours buried in Baptism brought forth fruit, righteousness, sanctification, adoption, and countless other goods, and it will finally bring the gift of the resurrection.

Latin:
