Hi enim verè sunt, quorum propriè miseretur Deus & planè non privative tantum: sed etiam collativè, ut loquuntur Ose. II. 19. 2. Cæterum talia vasa fieri dicuntur nominatim præparatione divina. Quod de prioribus minimè dictum fuit: Ut constet senten- tia Prophetæ, Perditio tua ex te Israel: tantum ex me salus tua. Et emphasin habet singularem præpositio (in voce προητοίμασεν) Quam enim ex nobis non habemus, ut simus (sequeretur enim ortu ipso nostro nos priores fuisse) tam non ex nobis esse significatur, ut tales simus: quia ortus etiam hujus ipsius principium nobis ipsis longè sit antiquius. Nam quod alibi dicit Apostolus, si quis seipsum mundarit ab istis, erit vas in honorem sanctificatum, non de præparatione ista vel causa electionis istic disputat Apostolus, nec libero arbitrio patrocinatur, quasi in potestate & viribus hominum sit, aggregare se ad numerum filiorum Dei: sibique ipsis autores esse suæ adoptionis; sed admonitio duntaxat proponitur, qua credentes jubet esse dissimi- les impiis, qui in quibusvis sordibus volutantur, & fideles, qui jam electi & vocati sunt, in puros usus se accommodare præcipit. Simpliciter ergo tantum ad sanctitatem vocat, & id monet, quod est alibi dictum ab eodem, Mundamini, qui fertis vasa Domini, im- mundum ne tangite. 3. Finis additur, manifestatio divitiarum gloriæ, id est, bonitatis immensæ. Hic remotior finis est; Propior est, cujus alibi meminit Apostolus, Elegit nos Deus in Christo ante constitu- tionem mundi, ut essemus sancti & inculpabiles co- ram ipso in dilectione. Hactenus B. Mylius.

PARS IV. Βεβαιωτικὴ.

Confirmans ulterius gratiam Dei in adoptione gentium & justificatione per fidem in Christum Judæis plerisque frustra justitiam legis sectantibus.

## 9:25
Ver. 25. As also he says in Hosea.

Namely God, who is introduced speaking by the Prophet; The Apostle brings forward these places to show the freedom of God in making a distinction between those who have sinned from causes known to himself. The place is Hosea 1 and 2. At the same time he shows that in those ancient things there was a figure of greater things.

I will call them my people, which were not my people; and her beloved, which was not beloved. And it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people; there shall they be called the children of the living God.

These last things are from the Greek of the LXX, except that in the Greek there is not ἐκεῖ, and after κληθήσονται is placed καὶ, which is a slight difference. But the things which precede are taken from the end of chapter II, not in exactly the same words, but with the sense preserved. There is there in the Greek: καὶ ἀγαπήσω τὴν ἐκ ἠγαπημένην, or as other books have, καὶ ἐλεήσω τὴν ἐκ ἐλεημένην καὶ ἐρῶ τῷ ἐ λαῷ με, λαός με εἶ σύ. Hosea, however, is dealing in the same place, as we said to him, with the ten tribes led away by the Assyrians, from whom a few were to return to their homeland together with Judah and Benjamin, and were again to be the people of God. Why those, and not others? For reasons that are just, but not evident to men. Thus also in his own time Paul signifies that God uses equal freedom.

Grotius errs in two ways: First, in the purpose of the proof adduced, which is not to show the freedom of God in making a distinction between those who have sinned, but to teach the divine grace which reveals itself in the adoption of the Gentiles into the people, which does not happen except through the intervention of faith. For they do not become the people of God and the children of God except through faith in Christ. 2 Cor. VI. 14, 15; John I. 12; Gal. III. 27. Secondly, regarding the sense of the prophetic prediction, which he himself snatches away to a few certain ones from the ten tribes who were to return to their homeland with the Jews: which false interpretation we refuted at Hosea II. 25. And it is manifest that the Prophet says that he will be the people of God who previously had not been the people of God, and that the Apostle is speaking here of the adoption of the Gentiles, not of the Israelites.

Latin:

Vers. 25. ὡς καὶ ἐν τῷ Ὡσηὲ λέγει.

Nempe Deus, qui a Propheta loquens introducitur; Lo- ca hæc adducit Apostolus, ut ostendat Dei libertatem in fa- ciendo discrimine inter eos, qui deliquere ex causis ipsi sibi cognitis. Locus est Oseæ I. & II. Simul ostendit in rebus illis antiquis figuram fuisse rerum majorum.

Καλέσω τὸν ἐ λαὸν μὲ, λαὸν μὲ, καὶ τὴν ἐκ ἠγαπημένην, ἠγα- πημένην, καὶ ἔςαι ἐν τῷ τόπῳ ἑ ἐῤῥέθη ἀυτοῖς ἐ λαός μὲ ὑμεῖς, ἐκεῖ κληθήσονται ὑοὶ Θεὲ ζῶντος.

Postrema hæc sunt ex Græco LXX. excepto, quod in Græco non est ἐκεῖ & post κληθήσονται ponitur καὶ, quod le- ve est discrimen. Quæ verò præcedunt, desumpta sunt ex fine capitis II. non planè iisdem verbis, sed sensu salvo. Est ibi in Græco: καὶ ἀγαπήσω τὴν ἐκ ἠγαπημένην, aut ut alii li- bri habent, καὶ ἐλεήσω τὴν ἐκ ἐλεημένην καὶ ἐρῶ τῷ ἐ λαῷ με, λαός με εἶ σύ. Agit autem eodem loco Oseas, ut ad eum diximus de decem tribubus abductis per Assyrios, ex quibus pauci simul cum Juda & Benjamino erant redituri in pa- triam, & rursum futuri Dei populus. Cur illi, non alii; ob causas æquas, sed hominibus non patentes. Sic & suo tem- pore significat Paulus usum Deum pari libertate.

Duobus modis errat Grotius: Primum in scopo adductæ probationis, qui non est ostendere Dei libertatem in faciendo discrimine inter eos, qui deliquerunt: sed docere divinam gratiam, quæ se patefacit in adoptione gentium in populum, quæ non fit, nisi interveniente fide. Nam populus Dei, & filii Dei non fiunt nisi per fidem in Chri- stum. 2. Cor. VI. 14. 15. Joh. I. 12. Gal. III. 27. Se- cundo, quoad sensum vaticinii Prophetici, quod abripit ipse ad paucos quosdam è decem tribubus cum Judæis redituris in patriam: quam ψευδερμη- νείαν confutavimus ad Os. II. 25. Et manifestum est, quod eum futurum dicat Propheta populum Dei, qui prius populus Dei non fuerat, quodque de gentium adoptione, non Israelitarum hic lo- quatur Apostolus.

## 9:27
Vers. 27. But Isaiah cries out concerning Israel.

ὑπὲρ, here is the same as περὶ, as in 1 Cor. X. 30, 2 Corinth. VII. 4, IX. 2, XII. 5, naturally, because the Hebrews use על here.

The Apostle uses a vigilant voice: crying out the Prophet over Israel, saying, i.e., that this had been predicted openly and manifestly, so that no one could plead ignorance unless they were lazily dozing. B. Luther rendered the little word ὑπὲρ as: für Israel, while the Vulgate has pro Israel: because this is the native meaning of that preposition, according to which it introduces the final cause or the Object, whose benefit we wish to be promoted, as the blessed Weller observes here.

If the number of the children of Israel be as the sand of the sea, the remnant shall be saved. For he will finish the word and cut it short in righteousness, because the Lord will make a shortened word upon the earth.

The passage is Isa. 10:22, which in Greek is read thus: and if the people of Israel be as the sand of the sea, their remnant shall be saved. Finishing and cutting short the word in righteousness, because the Lord will make a shortened word in the whole world. Where first the transposition is evident; for in the correct order ὅτι ought to have preceded λόγον συντελῶν. However, in the Pauline text, such as we now have it, it is quite absurd that γὰρ is placed first, then ὅτι. This reading is entirely interpolated from the LXX. The old reading, however, exists in that Manuscript which I cite so often, and it has it thus: for the Lord will make a word finishing and cutting short upon the earth, which are sufficient, and sufficiently express that which Isaiah intends. The huge devastation of the land of Judea, which Sennacherib had brought about, which by excellence is called the earth or the world. The few who betook themselves to Jerusalem, left behind as survivors from the slaughter, whom the Hebrews call שאר, the Greek interpreters call λοιπὸς, ἐπιλοιπὸς, κατάλοιπος, ὑπόλοιπος, λἐμμα, κατάλειμμα, ἐγκατάλειμμα, ὑπόλειμμα: the Latins call them relics, as Virgil:

The relics of the Danaans and of cruel Achilles. For God had done what is accustomed to be done in calculating accounts, where after those things are struck out by which expenses are equaled to receipts, some small sum remains which is owed. A similar expression is found in the same Isaiah 28:22. What God had done then, it should not be a wonder if He does it again and leads a few from many to true salvation, for whatever reasons it seemed good to Him. That causes were not lacking to God for why He should do so, Paul shows by not omitting that ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ.

Grotius thinks less reverently of the original text; when he says that it quite absurdly places γὰρ first and then ὅτι: which until now no one, even among the most sharp-sighted critics, has noticed. Secondly, he rashly amends infinite other [codices] from one codex. And thirdly, this is so much the more inconvenient, because it is manifest that the LXX Interpreters, whom the Apostle had followed, agree with the received codices. Fourthly, it is asserted again without proof that the Apostolic reading was interpolated from the LXX Interpreters, and not that the Apostle followed the LXX Interpreters according to custom. Fifthly, while Grotius says that Paul notably brought in that ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ and did not omit it, does he not acknowledge that the codices which do not omit it are to be preferred to that Manuscript which omits it? Sixthly, he affirms without proof that by the name γῆς, not the world but the land of Judea is designated here. Another thing is clear from the Prophetic text: which teaches that righteousness had overflowed through the whole world from those relics: among which relics the Apostles certainly were, announcing righteousness to the whole world. Seventhly, that the passage in the Prophet concerns the devastation of the land of Judea brought about by Sennacherib, and the few who betook themselves to Jerusalem and were left behind, can neither be taught from the Prophetic text, nor does it agree with this Apostolic explanation: which looks to spiritual relics of all people, not those surviving from a bodily slaughter. Eighthly, we showed at Isa. 10:21 that the Prophet deals with the saving of the relics of the Israelites or leading them to salvation, both from the Prophetic text and from this Pauline exposition, which place the Apostle brings here to prove that they are saved not by the merits of works but by grace through faith in Christ, just as the Gentiles are, and so also the Israelite relics. Therefore, ninthly, the causes are not kept silent as to why some were brought to salvation before others: but they are brought forward, indeed they are demonstrated among other things by the Apostle even from this prophecy: and Grotius seems not obscurely to acknowledge this when he says: Paul shows that causes were not lacking to God for why He should do so, by not omitting that ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ. For he teaches that the relics will be saved, not by some absolute decree, nor through the merits of works, but by righteousness apprehended by faith: because they will not lean upon or trust in anything except the Holy One of Israel in Christ the Lord, concerning whom see what we have said at that place: Whence it is evident that the place of the Prophet has been most aptly brought in here, compare also our annotations at Isa. 28:22. We add what the blessed Mylius handed down here (page 338): The Hebrew original has it thus: A finished destruction, overflowing will be righteousness. How the Lord Jehovah of hosts will make a consummation and abbreviation in the midst of the earth. The sum of the passage is that the Lord threatens destruction or excision to His people. However, this verse seems to contain two things; 1. The manner of the thing, that God will use a certain precision in casting off His people, and a sudden abbreviation as it were: For unless the days had been shortened, hardly even the relics themselves would have been saved. 2. The fruit or outcome of the thing is noted. For with that excision of the people consummated: righteousness, he says, will abound. For with the casting off of the Israelite people having been done, the Gospel of Christ, in which the righteousness of God is revealed from faith to faith, was propagated into the whole world not by a thin leading of rivulets: but by a great rush of torrents, as it were. This is the same thing that he says below, their fall is the riches of the world and their diminution is the riches of the Gentiles. The inept gloss of certain Papists concerning the Gospel pericopes, and of others concerning the abbreviated Gospel, that namely the Gospel is freed from the verbose burdens of the law, which is found in Gagnæus, Toletus, Pintus and others, is not suitable, nor is the exposition of certain Fathers, Cyprian lib. 3 c. 2 against the Jews, Jerome Epist. to Algas. qu. 10, concerning the emptying of Christ or even concerning the fewness of the years in which Christ preached. But those who refer this passage to the doctrine of Predestination, so that they may maintain that the reprobation of the Israelite people depended likewise upon a decree of the divine will, err in two ways, as the blessed Mylius notes. 1. That they bind what is of foreknowledge in God to predestination, which is a vicious mixing of different kinds. 2. That they refer what is of punishment and outcome to guilt and the cause of evil.

Latin:

Vers. 27. Ἡσαΐας δὲ κράζει ὑπὲρ τῦ Ἰσραὴλ.

ὑπὲρ, hic est idem, quod περὶ de ut 1. Cor. X. 30. 2. Co- rinth. VII. 4. IX. 2. XII. 5. nimirum, quia Hebræi על hic usurpant.

Utitur vigilanti voce Apostolus: Clamare Prophetam super Israelem dicens, q. d. palam & manifeste prædictum hoc fuisse, ne quis ignorantiam nisi supinè oscitans prætexere posset. Voculam ὑπὲρ B. Lutherus reddidit: für Israel, cum vulgata pro Israel: quia hæc nativa est Præpositionis istius significatio, juxta quam causam finalem seu Objectum, cujus commodum promotum volumus, infert, ut observat hic B. Wellerus.

Ἐὰν ᾖ ὁ ἀριθμὸς τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραὴλ ὡς ἡ ἄμμος τῆς θαλάσσης τὸ κατάλειμμα σωθήσεται. Λόγον γὰρ συντελῶν κὶ συντέμνων ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ ὅτι λόγον συντετμημένον ποιήσει κύριος ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς.

Locus est Esa. X, 22. qui in Græco sic legitur: κὰι ἐὰν γένηται ὁ λαὸς Ἰσραὴλ ὡς ἡ ἄμμος τῆς θαλάσσης, τὸ κατάλειμμα αὐτῶν σωθήσεται. Λόγον συντελῶν καὶ συντέμνων ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ, ὅτι λόγον συντετμημένον κύριος ποιήσει ἐν τῇ οἰκυμένῃ ὅλῃ. Ubi primum evidens est trajectio; nam recto ordine ὅτι debebat præcedere λόγον συντελῶν. In Paulino autem textu, qualem nunc habemus, satis absurdum est, poni primum γὰρ, deinde ὅτι. Omnino hæc lectio interpolata est ex LXX. Vetus autem lectio extat in Manuscripto illo, quem toties laudo, & sic habet: λόγον γὰρ συντελῶν καὶ συντέμνων ποιήσει κύριος ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, quæ sufficiunt, satisque exprimunt id, quod vult Esaias. Ingentem vastitiem terræ Judææ, quæ per excellentiam γῆ sive οἰκυμένη, intulerat Sennacheribus. Pauci, qui Hierosolyma se recepere relicti tanquam ex clade superstites, quos Ebræi שאר dicunt, Græci interpretes λοιπὸς, ἐπιλοιπὸς, κατάλοιπος, ὑπόλοιπος, λἐμμα, κατάλειμμα, ἐγκατάλειμμα, ὑπόλειμμα: Latini reliquias, ut Virgilius:

Reliquias Danaum atque immitis Achilli. Deus enim fecerat, quod in rationibus putandis fieri solet, ubi post expuncta ea, quibus expensa acceptis æquantur, exigua aliqua summa restat, quæ debeatur. Similis locutio apud eundem Esa. XXVIII. 22. Quod tunc fecerat Deus, non mirum sit rursus faciat & de multis paucos ad veram salutem perducat, quos quibusque de causis, ipsi visum. Non defuisse Deo causas cur ita faceret, ostendit Paulus non omittendo illud ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ.

Minus reverenter de textu originali sentit Grotius; cum eum satis absurdè primum γὰρ deinde ὅτι ponere ait: quod hactenus nemo etiam ex oculatissimis Criticis advertit. Deinde temerè ex uno codice infinitos alios emendat. Idque tertio tantò inconvenientiùs, quod manifestum sit LXX. Interpp. quos sequutus erat Apostolus, codicibus receptis consentire. Quarto interpolatam esse lectionem Apostolicam è LXX. Interpp. non vero sequutum esse pro more Apostolum LXX. Interpretes iterum precariò asseritur. Quinto dum notanter Paulum illud ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ adduxisse, non omisisse ait Grotius, annon agnoscit codices, qui illud non omittunt, Manuscripto isti, qui omittit, præferendas esse. Sextò nomine γῆς non οἰκυμένην hic sed terram Judaicam designari, sine probatione affirmat. Aliud è textu Prophetico liquet: qui è reliquiis istis per totum orbem redundasse justitiam docet: inter quas reliquias utique Apostoli fuere, justitiam toti orbi annunciantes. Septimo de vastitate terræ Judaicæ per Sennacheribum illatà, deque paucis, qui se Hierosolyma recepere relictis apud Prophetam agi nec à textu Prophetico doceri potest, nec huic explicationi Apostolicæ, convenit: quæ reliquias spirituales universorum respicit, non ex clade corporali superstitum. Octavò de servandis Israelitarum reliquiis vel ad salutem perducendis agere Prophetam tum è textu Prophetico, tum ex hac ἐκθέσει Paulina ostendimus ad Es. X. 21. quem locum hic adducit Apostolus, ut probet non ex operum meritis sed ex gratia per fidem in Christum salvari uti gentes, ita etiam Ismeliticas reliquias. Idcirco Nono causæ non tacentur, cur alii præ aliis ad Salutem adducti: sed adferuntur, imò demonstrantur inter alia ab Apostolo etiam ex hoc vaticinio: nec obscurè id agnoscere videtur Grotius, cum ait: Non defuisse Deo causas, cur ita faceret, ostendit Paulus non omit- tendo illud ἐν δικαιοσύνῃ. Nam reliquias salvatum iri, non absoluto quodam decreto, nec per operum merita docet, sed justitia fide apprehensa: quia non innitentur aut confident nisi Sancto Israel in Chri- sto Domino, quo de vid. quæ ad illum locum diximus: Unde constat appositissime locum Pro- phetæ hic adductum esse, conf. etiam annotata nostra ad Es. XVIII. 22. Addimus quæ hic B. Mylius tradidit (pag. 338.) Hebræa origo sic habet: Interitus concisus, exundans erit justitia. Quomodo consum- mationem & abbreviationem faciet Dominus Jehova exercituum in medio terræ. Summa loci est, quod in- teritum populo suo Dominus comminatur seu exci- sionem. Duo autem versus iste continere videtur; 1. Modum rei, Deum præcisione quadam in abjicien- do populo suo, & repentina quasi abbreviatione usu- rum esse: Nisi enim abbreviati fuissent dies, vix ipsæ etiam reliquiæ salvæ fuissent factæ. 2. Notatur fru- ctus seu eventus rei. Excisione enim ista populi con- summata: abundaturam inquit justitiam. Abjectio- ne enim populi Israelitici facta Evangelium Christi, in quo revelatur justitia Dei ex fide in fidem propa- gatum est in omnem orbem terræ non tenui rivalo- rum ductu: sed magno quasi torrentium impetu. Hoc idem est, quod infra dicit, lapsus ipsorum est divitiæ mundi & diminutio ipsorum est divitiæ gentium. Inepta Papistarum quorundam de pericopis Evan- gelicis, & aliorum de Evangelio abbreviato glossa, quod nempe Evangelium à legis laciniosis oneri- bus expeditum sit, quæ apud Gagnæum Toletum, Pintum & alios reperitur, nec conveniens quo- rundam Patrum Cypriani lib. III. c. 2. cont. Jud. Hier. Epist. ad Algas. qu. 10. expositio de exinani- tione Christi vel etiam de paucitate annorum, quibus Christus prædicavit. Qui verò locum istum refe- runt ad Prædestinationis doctrinam, ut sic reproba- tionem populi Israelitici à decreto itidem divinæ voluntatis pependisse obtineant, bifariam, notan- te B. Mylio, peccant. 1. Quod prævisionis est in Deo, ad prædestinationem adstringunt, quæ est diversorum generum vitiosa commixtio. 2. Quod pœnæ est & eventus, ad culpam & causam mali referunt.

## 9:29
Vers. 29. as Esaias has before said.) This is a perfect tense here, instead of a pluperfect, in the Hebrew manner, for he wishes to say: as Esaias had said in the former things, that is, in chapter 1.

Except the Lord of Sabaoth had left us a seed, we had been as Sodoma, and we had been made like unto Gomorrha.

These things are written here word for word from the LXX. The Prophet speaks there, however, of the devastation and slaughter made by Rezin and Pekah, at which time God preserved a few, if you compare them with the rest, shut up in Jerusalem, from whence the people might grow again. That which is reserved from the harvest for seed is very small, but from it come new harvests. Thus Ezra in Josephus XI. 5. besought God to preserve a seed and a remnant from their calamity and captivity at that time, and to have pity on them by restoring them again to Jerusalem and their own land. Thus also God in the times of Paul led a few of the Jews to the way of eternal salvation. Why not more, and why these, not others, the causes are almost hidden. Justin against Trypho: that because of our wickedness God hid from us the ability to understand the wisdom which is in his words, except for some to whom, by the grace of his great compassion, as Esaias said, he left a seed for salvation, so that our race might not perish completely like the Sodomites and Gomorrahites, as Gomorrah is used here for the Dative כעמרה. A similar manner of speaking is in the Greek of Hosea IV. 6. my people is made like as not having knowledge. Both constructions are in one clause of Ezekiel XXXII. 2. you were made like a lion of the nations, you are like a dragon. Sodom and Gomorrah were desolate cities. The Lord of Sabaoth יהוה צבאות, is the God of the Angels or of the stars: for the Hebrew word can signify either of these. See what we have said at Matthew XXIV. 29.

We showed in the Annotations on that prophecy that the passage of Isaiah ch. 1 does not treat of the slaughter and devastation by Rezin and Pekah, but of the most recent devastation of Jerusalem: which is especially evident also from this Apostolic proof. For he thus argues from an equal case: Just as at that time God preserved a few physically shut up in Jerusalem, so also in his (the Apostle's) time God brought a few from among the Jews to salvation; which argument would have seemed to the Jews ἀνακόλουθον (inconsequent), and less firm; for from whence could the force of the consequence be proven to them? The Apostle therefore teaches to divine grace that some seed was left in the most recent universal destruction, and that survivors were preserved as a remnant, from which, as if from seed, new harvests might be expected, provided they do not through unbelief reject the grace exhibited in Christ. For how was this seed holy, which God preserved no less from eternal than from temporal destruction, unless they were those few faithful, to whom indeed the nations were to be added, by the power of the Prophetic oracles. For the name of seed is also said σχετικῶς (relatively) to God, because the faithful are God's seed, to whom salvation comes through faith: as it is said of the Messiah in Isaiah 53, that he shall see his seed; to which the Evangelical promise in verse 26 contributes: At that time you shall be called the city of righteousness, the faithful city, concerning which [see] in the annotations on Isaiah 1. Others, for the demonstration of this matter—that through faith in Christ salvation comes to these remnants no less than to the Gentiles—think that this συμπέρασμα (conclusion) is brought forward, which the Apostle now subjoins.

Latin:

Vers. 29. καθὼς προείρηκεν Ἡσαΐας.) Præteritum perfe- ctum hic est, pro plusquam perfecto, more Hebræo, vult enim dicere: sicut in prioribus, id est, cap. 1. dixerat Esaias.

Εἰ μὴ κύριος Σαβαὼθ ἐγκατέλιπεν ἡμῖν σπέρμα, ὡς Σόδο- μα ἂν ἐγενήθημεν, καὶ ὡς Γόμοῤῥα ἂν ὡμοιώθημεν.

Sunt huc descripta verbotenus ex LXX. Loquitur autem ibi Propheta de vastitate & occidione, facta per Resinem, & Phaceen, quo tempore paucos, si cum cæteris conferas, Hierosolymis conclusos Deus servavit, unde iterum cresce- ret populus. Quod ex messe ad sementem reservatur, per- exiguum est, sed inde veniunt novæ messes. Sic Esdras apud Josephum XI. 5. παρεκάλει τὸν θεὸν σπέρματι κᾀ λείψα- νον ἐκ τῆς τότε συμφορᾶς αὐτῶν κᾀ αἰχμαλωσίας περισῶσαι κᾀ πάλιν εἰς ἱεροσόλυμα κᾀ τὴν οἰκείαν γῆν, ἀποκαταστήσαντα λα- βεῖν οἶκτον αὐτῶν. Sic etiam Deus Pauli temporibus Ju- dæorum paucos ad viam salutis æternæ perduxit. Cur non plures, & cur hos, non alios, causæ pene ipsum. Justinus contra Tryphonem: ὅτι διὰ τὴν ἡμετέραν κακίαν ἀπέκρυψεν ὁ θεὸς ὑφ' ἡμῶν τὸ δύνασθαι νοεῖν τὴν σοφίαν, τὴν ἐν τοῖς λόγοις ἀυτοῦ, πλὴν τινῶν οἷς κατὰ χάριν τῆς πολυεπλαγχνίας ἀυτῶ, ὡς ἔφη Ἡσαΐας, ἐγκατέλιπε σπέρμα εἰς σωτηρίαν, ἵνα μὴ ὡς Σοδο- μιτῶν καὶ Γομοῤῥαίων τέλεον καὶ τὸ ἡμέτερον γένος ἀπόληται, ὡς Γομοῤῥα politum hic pro Dativo כעמרה. Par loquendi genus in Græco Oseæ IV. 6. ὡμοιώθη ὁ λαός με ὡς ὐχ ἔχων γνῶσιν. Utraque constructio est in uno commate Ezechielis XXXII. 2. λέοντι ἐθνῶν ὡμοιώθης συνάγεις δράκων Sodoma & Gomorrha urbes desolatæ. Κύριος Σαβαὼθ יהוה צבאות, est Deus Angelorum vel astrorum: vox enim Hebræa utrumvis horum potest significare. Vi- de, quæ diximus ad Matth. XXIV. 29.

Locum Esaiæ c. 1. non de clade & vastitate per Resinem & Phaceen, sed de novissima devastatione Hierosolymæ agere in Annot. ad istud vaticinium ostendimus: quod imprimis etiam ex hac Aposto- licæ probatione constat. Ita enim à pari argumen- tatur: Sicut illo tempore paucos Hierosolymis conclusos Deus corporaliter servavit, ita etiam suo (Apostoli) tempore Deum paucos ex Judæis ad salutem adducere, quod argumentum Judæis visum fuisset ἀνακόλυϑον, minusque firmum; un- de enim consequentiæ vis probari ipsis poterat? Id ergo docet Apostolus gratiæ divinæ acceptum fe- rendum esse, quod semen aliquod relictum fuerit, in universali excidio novissimo, & superstites serva- tæ reliquiæ, unde velut è semine novæ messes ex- pectari possint, modò non per incredulitatem gra- tiam in Christo exhibitam reprobent. Quomodo enim semen hoc sanctum fuit, quod Deus sospita- vit non minus ex æterno, quam è temporali exitio, nisi pauci illi fideles, ad quos verò erant aggregan- dæ gentes, vi oraculorum Propheticorum. Nam & σχετικῶς ad Deum nomen seminis dicitur, quia Dei semen sunt fideles, quibus salus per fidem con- tingit: uti de Messia dicitur Es. LIII. quod visurus sit semen; Quo facit promissio Evangelica v. 26. Isto tempore vocaberis civitas justitiæ, urbs fidelis, quo de in annot. ad Es. 1. Alii ob hujus rei de- monstrationem, quod per fidem in Christum, salus istis reliquiis non minus, quam gentibus contin- gat, hoc adferri συμπέρασμα, quod jam subjun- git Apostolus, censent.

## 9:30
Verse 30. What then shall we say?

What then do we say? Since he has shown that God is free and that one should not object to his dispensation regarding benefits, even if the causes are not open to us, he now shows that there were causes for God to act in this way rather than how the Jews had wished him to act.

that the Gentiles, who did not pursue righteousness, have attained righteousness.

The participle of the present tense is here to be taken as a pluperfect. The Gentiles, who had not sought righteousness (according to God), have attained that righteousness, that is, they have arrived at that righteousness. The same sense as below in 10:20. Διώκειν (to pursue) is used here as ζητεῖν (to seek) is there. The Hebrew רדף is also taken thus, as in Psalm 34:14, where in the Greek: seek peace and pursue it. As also in 1 Peter 3:11: let him seek peace and pursue it. See also Deuteronomy 16:21, Proverbs 15:7, 21:2. See also below 12:13, 14:19, 1 Corinthians 14:1, Philippians 3:12, 14, 1 Thessalonians 5:15, 1 Timothy 6:11, 2 Timothy 2:22. Thus also Aristotle: for the sake of these they pursue those things, and Xenophon: one must pursue those who are sympathetic.

but righteousness which is of faith.

That true righteousness, to which God willed there be no access except through faith.

Latin:

Vers. 30. Τί ὖν ἐρῦμεν.

Quid ergo dicimus? cum ostenderit liberum Deum neque dispensationi ejus circa beneficia obstrependum, etiamfi causæ nobis non pateant, jam ostendit fuisse Deo causas ita potius agendi, quam quomodo eum agere voluissent Ju- dæi.

ὅτι ἔϑνη τὰ μὴ διώκοντα δικαιοσύνην, κατέλαβε δικαιο- σύνην.

Participium præsentis temporis hic sumendum pro plus- quamperfecto. Gentes, quæ non quæsiverant justitiam (se- cundum Deum) assecuti sunt eam justitiam, id est, ad eam justitiam pervenere. Idem sensus, qui infra X. 20. Διώκειν hic, quod ibi ζητεῖν. Sumitur sic & רדף Hebræum ut Ps. XXXIV. 14. ubi in Græco: ζήτησον εἰρήνην καὶ δίωξον αὐτήν. Quomodo & 1. Petr. III. 11. ζητησάτω εἰρήνην καὶ διωξάτω αὐτήν. Vide & Deuter. XVI. 21. Proverb. XV. 7. XXI. 2. Vide & infra XII, 13. XIV. 19. 1. Cor. XIV. 1. Phil. III. 12. 14. 1. Thess. V. 15. 1. Tim. VI. 11. 2. Tim. II. 22. Sic & Aristo- teles : τούτων γὰρ χάριν τἀκεῖνα διώκουσι, & Xenophon: χρὴ τοὺς συγνώμονας διώκειν.

δικαιοσύνην δὲ τὴν ἐκ πίσεως.

Veram illam justitiam, ad quam Deus aditum nisi per fidem noluit.

## 9:31
Verse 31. But Israel, pursuing the law of righteousness, did not attain to the law of righteousness.

Νόμος (law) here signifies a way. For the Hebrew תּוֹרָה is from ירה to direct, which is also translated as ὁδηγεῖν (to lead); φϑάνειν (to attain) corresponds to the Hebrew נגע, which is to arrive, 2 Chronicles 28:9, Ecclesiastes 8:14, 12:1, and often in Daniel. The Jews were seeking the way of that righteousness which would please God, but most in vain.

The conclusion shows that the Apostle is not arguing about the freedom of God regarding the dispensation of benefits, but about justification through faith in Christ, by which he simultaneously paves the way for himself to the following chapter: What then shall we say? i.e., It would indeed be a consequence of what has been said, which might seem strange and absurd: but the truth itself expresses its assertion to us. What that is, he shows by an elegant contention. For he opposes the Gentiles and the Jews to one another, and whereas the former seemed far to be postponed to the latter, they are preferred, which contains the first indication of the paradox. The second is that he says it is a unique event for the Jews to be excluded from righteousness, while the Gentiles aspired to the same. The third, in which the cause of doubting, or the nerve of the paradox, may most lie, is in the condition of each people. The Gentiles, he says, who did not follow righteousness, have attained the same: the Jews, who did follow the same, have not attained righteousness at all, as B. Mylius has it here. Τὸ διώκειν (to pursue) is not merely to seek a thing, whether lost or otherwise desired, but to pursue and follow after, as appears from the collation of the passages cited, and from verse 31. Nor is there any reason why we should move the word νόμου (law) here from its customary meaning, and believe that a way is denoted by it. Since the proper sense can be retained, and is most convenient. The Jews were not only seeking the way of righteousness, but were pursuing the law of righteousness, and legal righteousness. For by the law of righteousness the Apostle understands the law of Moses, through which the Jews wished to obtain righteousness and salvation: But in the latter place, the predicate being exhibited in the same verse, he did not attain to the LAW OF RIGHTEOUSNESS, by the word νόμου the reason and norm is signified, according to which God justifies: which may become clear from the opposition of the Gentiles and the added δηλώσει, that the discourse is concerning that righteousness which is through faith, for when the Jews did not attain to the law of righteousness, which the Gentiles κατέλαβε. But that is the reason for obtaining righteousness and salvation, namely that righteousness which is from faith. I add that also in the following αἰτιολογίᾳ the Apostle declares himself v. 32, rendering the cause, why the Jews did not attain the reason of righteousness? because they wished to be justified not from faith; but from the works of the law (the particle ὡς corresponds to the כ of truth of the Hebrews). Whence it appears that they are said not to attain to the law of righteousness: in so far as they did not attain the true reason by which we are justified, which the Gentiles attained, even if these did not pursue righteousness, i.e., in such a way that they wished to be justified by the works of the law: But those pursued legal righteousness in every way. Concerning which the blessed Mylius (p. 340) not inaptly: A wonderful, yet proper and perpetual condition of Evangelical righteousness is proposed here for us to behold. It is always apprehended more easily and greedily by those who do not pursue righteousness, than by those who do: The Scribes and Pharisees, whom the confidence of their own righteousness inflated, spurned Christ with his grace: publicans and harlots flocked to him in crowds. Whence it had been said by Christ: Publicans and harlots go before you into the kingdom of God. Thus among the Gentiles from the common people, infamous for public corruption of morals, many more were converted to Christ than from the Philosophers. The cause of the matter depends on the sense of corruption and one's own misery. For the more easily they acknowledge this, the more they are contaminated by open crimes, and the less they have in themselves which they can pretend toward their own righteousness: the more greedily they have been accustomed to seize the righteousness and salvation offered to them from elsewhere. Nor indeed is the RIGHTEOUSNESS, WHICH IS FROM FAITH, that righteousness to which there is no access except through faith in the Grotian sense, who understands INTERNAL AND INHERENT RIGHTEOUSNESS: to which faith in Christ is the way: but it is the righteousness of Christ himself, which is said to be ἐκ πίστεως from faith and διὰ πίστεως through faith, because it is not ours otherwise than through faith. For the discourse is concerning the καταλήψει τῆς δικαιοσύνης, the apprehension of that righteousness by which we are justified, which does not happen except through faith. It is said to be from faith, therefore, because not ἐξ ἔργων νόμου, but ἐκ πίστεως that righteousness by which we are justified before God comes to us: just as ἐξ is the same as from, from faith, that is, from FAITH, since it is interchanged with the particle διὰ THROUGH Faith. The blessed Selneccerus concerning the word καταλαμβάνειν notes, that it is one thing to do, another to attain, just as also κατειληφὸς and τὸ καταλάβον is that which happens beyond hope, effort, and all thought.

Latin:

Vers. 31. Ἰσραὴλ δὲ διώκων νόμον δικαιοσύνης,εἰς νόμον δικαιο- σύνης ὁυκ ἔφϑασε.

Νόμος hic viam significat. Hebræum enim תּוֹרָה est à ירה dirigere, quod & ὁδηγεῖν vertitur: φϑάνειν respondet Hebræo נגע quod est pervenire, 2. Paralip. XXVIII. 9. Ec- clesiastæ VIII. 14. XII, 1. & apud Danielem sæpe. Judæi quærebant viam justitiæ ejus, quæ Deo placeret, sed frustra plerique.

Non de libertate Dei circa dispensationem be- neficiorum, sed de justificatione per fidem in Chri- stum differere Apostolum conclusio docet, quâ si- mul ad sequens caput viam sibi sternit, quid igitur dicemus? q. d. Consectaneum ex his, quæ dicta sunt, fuerit equidem, quod mirum atque absurdum videri queat: sed cujus assertionem veritas ipsa nobis expri- mit. Quid id verò sit eleganti contentione ostendit. Opponit enim gentiles & Judæos inter sese, & cum his illi postponendi longe viderentur, præferuntur, quod primum paradoxi indicium continet. Secun- dum illud est, quod est eventus proprium Judæis à ju- stitia exclusis, gentiles ad eandem aspirasse inquit. Tertium, in quo maxime dubitandi causa, seu para- doxi nervus latere queat, est in conditione utriusque populi. Gentes, inquit, quæ non secutæ sint justitiam, eandem assecutas esse: Judæos, qui secuti sint eandem, justitiam minime assecutos fuisse, ut hic habet B. My- lius. Tὸ διώκειν non est nudè quærere, rem sive amissam, sive aliàs desideratam, sed persequi & se- stari, utrum è collatione locorum adductorum, tum è vers. 31. apparet. Nec est, cur vocem νόμου hic à significatione usitata dimoveamus, & viam eâ notari credamus. Quum sensus proprius retineri possit, & convenientissimus sit. Non quærebant tantum viam justitiæ Judæi, sed sectabantur justitiæ legem, & legalem justitiam. Nam per legem justitiæ legem Mosis intelligit Apostolus, per quam justitiam & salutem volebant consequi Judæi: Posteriori verò loco versu eodem prædicatum exhibente, ad LEGEM JUSTITIÆ non pervenit, voce νόμου ratio & norma significatur, juxta quam Deus justificat: quod ex oppositione gentium & δηλώσει addita, quod sermo sit de illa justitia, quæ est per fidem, elucescat, cum enim ad legem justitiæ non pervenere Judæi, quam κατέλαβε gentiles. At ea est ratio justitiam & salutem consequendi, justitiam nempe eam, quæ est ex fide. Addo quod etiam in consequente αἰτιολογίᾳ Apostolus sese declaret v. 32. causam reddens, cur rationem justitiæ assequuti non sint Judæi? quia non ex fide; sed ex operibus legis (particula ὡς respondet כ veritatis Ebræorum) justificari voluerunt. Unde apparet ad legem justitiæ non pervenire dici eosdem: quatenus veram rationem, quà justificamur, assequuti non sunt, quam assequuti sunt gentiles, etsi hi non sectati sint justitiam sc. ita, ut per opera legis justificari voluerint: Illi autem justitiam legalem omnibus modis sectati sint. Quo dé B. Mylius (p. 340.) non inconcinnè: Mira quidem, sed propria & perpetua conditio Evangelicæ justitiæ nobis hic spectanda proponitur. Facilius & avidius illa semper apprehenditur ab his, qui non sectantur justitiam, quam qui sectantur: Christum cum sua gratia Scribæ & Pharisæi, quos propriæ justitiæ fiducia inflabat, aspernabantur: publicani & meretrices catervatim ad ipsum confluebant. Unde dictum à Christo fuerat: Publicani & meretrices præeunt vobis in regno Dei. Sic inter gentiles ex vulgo, publica morum corruptione infami, multo plures ad Christum sunt conversi, quam ex Philosophis. Causa rei pendet ex sensu corruptionis & miseriæ propriæ. Huc enim quo facilius agnoscunt, quò apertis flagitiis contaminati sunt, quoque minus in se habent, quod ad justitiam propriam prætexere possint: eo justitiam ac salutem aliunde sibi oblatam avidius arripere consueverunt. Nec verò JUSTITIA, QUÆ EST EX FIDE, est justitia illa, ad quam nonnisi per fidem aditus est Grotiano sensu, qui JUSTITIAM INTERNAM & INHÆRENTEM intelligit: ad quam via sit fides in Christum: sed est justitia ipsa Christi, quæ ἐκ πίστεως ex fide & διὰ πίστεως per fidem esse dicitur, quia non aliter nostra est, nisi per fidem. Nam de καταλήψει τῆς δικαιοσύνης apprehensione justitiæ illius, qua nos justificamur, sermo est, quæ non fit, nisi per fidem. Ideo ex fide esse dicitur, quia non ἐξ ἔργων νόμιε, sed ἐκ πίστεως obtingit nobis justitia illa, qua coram Deo justificamur: prouti ἐξ idem est, quod à, ex fide, id est, à FIDE, quum permutetur cum particula διὰ PER Fidem. B. Selneccerus de verbo καταλαμβάνειν notat, quod sit aliud agendo, aliud assequi, quemadmodum & κατειληφὸς & τὸ καταλάβον est, quod præter spem, studium & omnem cogitationem accidit.

## 9:32
Vers. 32. Why.) He moves the question, in order to answer, and to show that not all the causes of this divine dispensation are in secret.

ὅτι ὁὐκ ἐκ πίστεως) They ran, but as it pleased them, not as God showed. God always made the most of faith, and willed it to be the way to righteousness, as is to be seen in Heb. XI. and above IV, 3. But now he is not content with any faith, but requires that which is carried into Jesus, and through Jesus into God. This question is not raised so that the causes of divine liberty and dispensation may be brought into the light to some extent, but so that it may be taught that most Jews are rejected from salvation for the same causes for which those who are condemned are condemned: namely, because they reject Christ, and do not receive righteousness through faith in Christ, but wish to aspire to salvation by their own righteousness of works. Nor indeed is any other faith required now for salvation or in the time of the New Testament than that which was required of old; since there has always been one and the same method of obtaining salvation, one and the same faith, Acts 15:11, Eph. 4:5.

ἀλλ’ ὡς ἐξ ἔργων νόμου. Understand 'attaining,' as if they were about to arrive at that righteousness through the works of the Mosaic law, in which they were greatly deceiving themselves. For that law was not given for that purpose: but partly, like human laws, though with greater authority, to preserve civil society, and partly to separate that people as far as possible from other peoples, and its observance produced nothing other than public tranquility, and privately, impunity and certain temporal goods. But if men placed the whole righteousness which God demands in that external obedience alone which was shown to the law of Moses, then the law was not only of no benefit for that purpose, but brought no small impediment to it. Wherefore those who were so minded were truly following devious paths.

Not only are those laws considered which pertained to the civil society of the Jewish people and separated them from other peoples, such as the forensic and ceremonial laws, but primarily the moral laws; nor did the Jews seek only temporal or secular tranquility from the works of the law, about which no dissertation is instituted here, but they wished to obtain true righteousness before God and salvation through the works of the law, having repudiated the righteousness of the Messiah, which is the reason the Apostle gives why most Jews are excluded from salvation, because they were seeking another method of salvation: nor indeed does the Apostle teach only that salvation cannot be obtained through external obedience performed to the law, but he simply excludes the observance of the law from the method of obtaining salvation and teaches that it consists solely in faith in Christ: and since the Jews, having repudiated Christ, sought salvation through the works of the law, by showing that they fall away from salvation, he confirms that this is the only method of salvation through faith in Christ. Because they were not seeking righteousness and salvation from faith, but as if from works. This argument is twofold, which nevertheless can be reduced to one head, namely that they erred in the manner of seeking righteousness. They sought it, therefore, where it could not be found, namely from the works of the law. They did not seek it where it could be found, namely from faith. They were therefore like those who, while making a journey, indeed hasten much and carry a heavy burden, but enter upon a path that is completely different and leads away from the place to which they are tending. For just as the latter recede further from their destination the faster they run, so those who prefer to seek righteousness from works rather than from faith wander further from the goal of salvation; as the blessed Mylius holds here. Nor indeed did the Jews require only external obedience to the law for salvation, but as much as they themselves thought was prescribed by the law, although they erred in explaining the meaning of the law no less than in seeking righteousness through the law: since for the most part they understood the law as concerning external obedience, not requiring the internal purification of the heart so much, indeed, while they were ignorant of that internal evil of original concupiscence, they thought nothing of that cleansing which is done through faith, which is absolutely necessary.

προσέκοψαν γὰρ τῷ λίθῳ τῶ προσκόμματος.) Those who are traveling are accustomed to strike against stones and injure their feet, and thus be hindered from continuing their journey. See John 11:9. So therefore some stumble at the word. 1 Peter 2:8. What Peter says there about the Gospel, Paul says here about Christ, because the Christ who is preached and the Gospel are the same: his Gospel must be considered together with his cross.

For this is what offended most Jews. They could not believe in Christ and his Gospel except with the greatest danger of losing their property, country, friendships, honors, and perhaps their life. But to believe in GOD does not cost less: as we are taught by the affairs of Abraham. He who desires to arrive at the true faith, which leads to divine righteousness, must be so minded that he is prepared to embrace and profess it even with the greatest loss of things pertaining to this life, and to equate nothing to GOD, much less prefer anything before him. John 5:44, 7:17, 8:47. See also Luke 2:34. Καθὼς γέγραπται· ἰδὲ ἐγὼ τίθημι ἐν Σιὼν λίθον προσκόμ- ματος καὶ πέτραν σκανδάλου, καὶ πᾶς ὁ πιστεύων ἐπ' αὐτῷ ὀυ κα- ταισχυνθήσεται.) Part of these words is taken from Isaiah 28:16. Where in the Greek it is: ἰδὼ ἐγὼ ἐμβάλλω εἰς τὰ θε- μέλια Σιὼν λίθον πολυτελῆ. &c. After some words it follows: καὶ ὁ πιστεύων, ὀυ μὴ καταισχυνθῇ. And that is the place from which the words of Peter are taken, 1 Pet. 2:6. But those which are placed here in the middle are from another place, 8:14 of the same Prophet, where the Greek today has the negation: ὀυχ ὡς λίθου προσκόμματι συναν- τήσεσθε, ὀυδὲ ὡς πέτρας πτώματι. But in the Hebrew it is: And he shall be to you, namely God, for a sanctuary: (that is, for an asylum) but for a stone of stumbling and for a rock of offense to the two houses of Israel. He rightly joined these places, because in both it is a matter of the times of Sennacherib, and God's protection is promised to those who, remaining within Jerusalem, persisted in the law of GOD. It was accepted among the Hebrews that every liberation of the ancients bore the figure of that liberation which was to be expected in the times of the Messiah: upon which hypothesis the Apostles build many things here and there; in the former place the LXX elders of the law more correctly read in the Hebrew לא יחיש than what we said the Masoretes preferred, לא יבוש, to the passage of Isaiah itself. Καταισχύνεσθαι means to be deceived, as we said above in verse 5. The allegorical sense is that those who do not believe in the Gospel are hindered from continuing on the path that leads to true righteousness. But those who do believe in it are by no means deceived, but will obtain what they desire. The Gospel is said to be placed in Zion, because from there that message goes forth to other nations, as was predicted in Psalm 110:2.

The stumbling block against which the Jews were striking is not established here as the cross of Christians or the danger of losing goods, but Christ himself is called the stone of stumbling and the rock of offense: both by reason of his person and by reason of his office: because the Jews were most scandalized by the humiliation, passion, and cross of Christ himself, in which, however, the true and only way of salvation is situated (Acts 4:12; 1 Cor. 1:21, 23, 30); nor did they receive the doctrine of Christ, or Christ himself as the true and only Mediator, through faith, but rejected him, and having put him aside, believed that they would obtain salvation through the works of the law. That which he reproves in them, and that this is the cause of their reprobation, the Apostle teaches, having brought forward for that matter a twofold prophetic testimony: the one from Isa. 28:16 concerning the stone placed in Zion, upon which those who are to be saved are to be built, since those who believe in him do not flee, but dwell confidently and lean upon him securely, and thus are not put to shame, as the prophetic passage is explained here by our Apostle and by St. Peter (1 Ep. 2:8), which is also clear from the collation of other passages (Ps. 118:22; Acts 4:11; Isa. 8:14; Matt. 21:42; Luke 2:34; ch. 20:17) to sound concerning Christ: the other from Isa. 8:14, where Christ is called the stone of stumbling and the rock of offense, which is evident from the context and the parallel passage in Luke 2:34, as well as from the present apostolic citation. These testimonies are indeed linked together as if they were one and the same testimony, because they proceeded from one Spirit through the same Prophet, in which v. in distinguishing them from their proper seat, the action of God, who places that stone in Zion, is not to be confused with the event by which that stone became a stone of offense: which God certainly did not place as a stone of stumbling, but so that one might believe in him as the rock of salvation; for the stone, as it is placed by God, is truly precious, and is placed as the head of the corner, upon which the Church is to lean and which is the foundation of salvation, so that he who believes in him has no need to flee, nor be put to shame, but may be secure and gloriously overcome. For also consequences are wont to be taken for antecedents, and actions which are signs of some affection are taken for the affections themselves, as to strike is taken for to grieve inwardly, to laugh for to rejoice, to put the hand over the mouth for keeping silent, Job 8. 21. Ps. 126. 2. Gen. 21, 6. Luke 6, 21. 25. Job 40, 35. Micah 7, 16. as he who believes, let him not make haste, i.e., let him have no need to flee either out of excessive anxiety or trepidation of heart and fear, and since haste is the effect and consequence of confusion, and flight is a hasty withdrawal from the eyes of men, therefore, he who believes is said not to be put to shame, and furthermore, by way of litotes, not to flee; not to be put to shame is to stand firm, to remain secure, and to live immune from ignominy with honor and glory, nay rather, to be delivered in divine judgment from all ignominy and confusion, and to obtain glory and eternal salvation, as is manifest from this Apostolic allegation and application, if you look to the intention and scope and the force of the confirmation, and also from the Prophetic text itself (concerning which see our annotations in the illustrated Old Testament). The intention, therefore, of God placing a cornerstone in Zion is not that it should be a stone of stumbling, but this is an accidental outcome, and the blame for it lies in men stumbling against that precious stone and rock of salvation. Who 'stumble at the word' according to Peter; which can be understood of the substantial Word, Christ, inasmuch as He is that stone of stumbling; or if it be taken of the word of the Gospel, of the principal Object of the same, which is not our cross, but the cross and passion of Christ, on account of which the Gospel is called the word of the cross, 1 Cor. 1. 18, concerning Christ crucified, who is a scandal to the Jews, v. 23, but to those who believe, the true and uniquely salvific Wisdom, 1 Cor. 2. 2. For although Christians ought to endure the cross, and even meet death itself for the sake of the name of the Lord, yet that is not what is being treated here, but the cause of salvation is being discussed, as also of rejection from salvation. But the cause of salvation is not the endurance of the cross, but faith in Christ: just as the unbelief of the Jews or the rejection of Christ is established as the cause of the destruction of the Israelites by the 'stumbling' against the stone of stumbling. Concerning the sense of the prophecies of Isaiah, which he depraves both in this place and in its proper seat, because he snatches it away to a temporal liberation, referring it only typically to the liberation of the Messiah, we have spoken in the annotations to the Old Testament, and we have discussed the corruptions of Grotius, so that there is no need to add anything further here.

SUBSECTION II. Asserting the righteousness of Christ as the meritorious and formal cause of the justification of both Jews and Gentiles.

Latin:

Vers. 32. Διὰ τί.) Quæstionem movet, ut respondeat, & ostendat, non omnes divinæ hujus dispensationis causas esse in abscondito.

ὅτι ὁὐκ ἐκ πίστεως) Cucurrerunt, sed quà ipsis libebat, non quà monstrabat Deus. Deus semper fidem fecit maximi, eamque esse viam voluit ad justitiam, ut videre est Hebr. XI. & supra IV, 3. At nunc non quavis fide contentus est, sed eam requirit, quæ in Jesum, & per Jesum in Deum fertur. Non movetur haec quaestio, ut divinae libertatis & dispensationis causae quadantenus in aprico po- nantur, sed ut doceatur, ob easdem causas rejici Judaeos plerosque a Salute, ob quas, qui conde- mnantur, condemnantur: nimirum, quod reji- ciant Christum, nec per fidem Christi justitiam su- scipiant, sed propria operum justitia ad salutem adspirare velint. Nec vero alia fides requiritur nunc ad salutem vel tempore N. T. quam quae olim requisita fuit; quum una eademque semper fue- rit consequendae salutis ratio, una eademque fi- des, Act. XV. 11. Eph. IV. 5.

ἀλλ’ ὡς ἐξ ἔργων νόμου. Subaudi φθάσοντες, tanquam perventuri ad illam Justi- tiam per opera legis Mosaicae, in quo multum se fallebant. Non enim in id data erat ea lex: sed partim, ut, sicut leges humanae, majori tamen auctoritate, societatem civilem, conservaret, partim ut illum populum ab aliis populis quam longissime secerneret, nec aliud observata pariebat quam publice tranquillitatem, privatim vero impunita- tem, & bona quaedam temporaria. Quod si in illa sola exteriore obedientia, quae Mosis legi exhibebatur, pone- rent homines justitiam totam, quam Deus exigit, jam lex non tantum ad id non proderat, sed ei non exiguum adfe- rebat impedimentum. Quare qui sic animati erant, vere devia sectabantur.

Non tantum spectantur leges illae, quae ad so- cietatem civilem populi Judaici faciebant, eundem- que ab aliis populis secernebant, quales erant fo- renses, & Ceremoniales, sed imprimis leges Mo- rales, nec sectabantur tantum ex operibus legis Judaei tranquillitatem temporalem, vel secularem, de qua hic non instituitur dissertatio, sed per opera legis veram coram Deo Justitiam & salutem con- sequi volebant, repudiata Messiae Justitia, quam causam reddit Apostolus, cur a salute excludantur plerique Judaei, quia aliam salutis rationem secta- bantur: neque vero id tantum docet Apostolus, quod per solam externam obedientiam legi praesti- tam Salus obtineri nequeat, sed simpliciter legis ob- servantiam a ratione consequendi salutem excludit & sola fide in Christum eam constare docet: & quū Judaei Christo repudiato per opera legis salutem quaesierint, eos a salute excidere ostendens hanc unice rationem esse salutis per fidem in Christum eo ipso confirmat. Quia non ex fide, sed velut ex operibus justitiam & salutem quaerebant. Bimem- bris est haec ratio, quae tamen ad unum caput reduci potest, nimirum quod in modo quaerenda justitia er- raverint. Quaesiverunt ergo eam, ubi inveniri non poterat, nimirum ex operibus legis. Non quaesive- runt, ubi inveniri poterat, scilicet ex fide. Similes ergo eorum fuerunt, qui iter faciendo, multum qui- dem festinant, & onus grave sustinent, viam vero plane diversam & a loco, quo tendunt, abducentem ingrediuntur. Ut enim illi eo longius recedunt ab illo, quo celerius currunt: ita a scopo salutis longius aber- rant, qui ex operibus malunt, quam ex fide justitiam requirere; uti hic habet B. Mylius. Nec vero Ju- daei solam exteriorem obedientiam legis ad salutem requirebant, sed tantam, quantam ipsi putabant a lege praescriptam esse, etsi in explicanda legis sen- tentia, non minus, quam in quaerenda per legem justitia errarent: quum maximam partem legem de externa obedientia intelligerent, interiorem cordis purificationem non adeo requirentes, imo qua ignorabant internum istud concupiscentiae Originalis malum de mundatione illa, quae per fi- dem fit, qua omnino opus est, nihil cogitantes.

προσέκοψαν γὰρ τῷ λίθῳ τῶ προσκόμματος.) Solent qui iter faciunt, interdum in lapides impingere & pedes laedere, ac sic impediri ne iter prosequantur. Vide Joh. XI. 9. Sic ergo quidam προσκόπτουσι τῷ λόγῳ. 1. Petr. II. 8. Quod Petrus ibi dicit de Evangelio, id hic Paulus de Christo, quia idem est Christus praedicatus & Evangelium: considerandus Evangeliumque ejus simul cum sua cruce.

Hoc enim est quod Judæos plerosque offendebat. Non po- terant Christo Evangelioque ejus credere, nisi cum maxi- mo periculo amittendæ rei familiaris, patriæ, amicitiarum, honorum, forte & vitæ. At DEO credere minoris non constat: ut ex Abrahami rebus docemur. Eum qui ad veram fidem, quæ ad justitiam divinam ducit, pervenire cupit, oportet ita esse animatum, ut paratus sit verum etiam cum maximo rerum ad vitam hanc pertinentium damno, amplecti & profiteri, nihilque DEO æquare, nedum ante- ferre. Joh. V. 44. VII. 17. VIII. 47. Vide & Luc. II. 34. Καθὼς γέγραπται· ἰδὲ ἐγὼ τίθημι ἐν Σιὼν λίθον προσκόμ- ματος καὶ πέτραν σκανδάλου, καὶ πᾶς ὁ πιστεύων ἐπ' αὐτῷ ὀυ κα- ταισχυνθήσεται.) Pars horum verborum desumta est ex Efaiæ XXVIII. 16. Ubi in Græco est: ἰδὼ ἐγὼ ἐμβάλλω εἰς τὰ θε- μέλια Σιὼν λίθον πολυτελῆ. &c. Sequitur post aliqua verba: καὶ ὁ πιστεύων, ὀυ μὴ καταισχυνθῇ. Et is locus unde deprompta & Retri verba 1. Pet. II. 6. At quæ in medio hic sunt posita, ex altero sunt loco VIII. 14. ejusdem Prophetæ, ubi Græca habent hodie negationem: ὀυχ ὡς λίθου προσκόμματι συναν- τήσεσθε, ὀυδὲ ὡς πέτρας πτώματι. At in Hebræo est: Et erit vobis, Deus scilicet, in sanctuarium: (id est pro asylo) in lapidem autem offensionis & in petram scandali duabus domi- bus Israël. Recte autem ista loca conjunxit, quia in utroque agitur de temporibus Sennacharibi, Deique tutela iis pro- mittitur, qui intra Hierosolyma manentes in lege DEI per- stiterint. Erat autem receptum inter Hebræos omnem li- berationem veterum figuram gessisse ejus liberationis quæ expectanda esset temporibus Messiæ: cui ὑποθέσει multa passim superstruunt Apostoli in loc. priore LXX. senes legis rectius in Hebræo לא יחיש quam quod Masoretæ prætu- lere לא יבוש diximus ad ipsum Esaïæ locum. Καταισχύν- εσθαι est falli, ut diximus supra V. 5. Sensus ἀλληγορικὸς est qui Evangelio non credunt, eos impediri, ne viam insistant quæ ad veram justitiam ducit. Qui vero ei credunt, eos, neutiquam falli, sed quod cupiunt adepturos. Dicitur au- tem Evangelium positum in Sione, quia inde ad gentes alias is sermo prodit, ut prædictum fuit Pf. CX. 2.

Offendiculum, in quod impingebant Judæi hic non constituitur crux Christianorum aut pericu- lum amittendorum bonorum, sed Christus ipse la- pis offendiculi, & petra Scandali dicitur: cum ratio- ne personæ, tum ratione officii: quia humiliatione, passione & cruce ipsius Christi maxime scandali- zabantur Judæi, in qua vero vera & unica salutis ratio sita est Act. IV. 12. 1. Cor. I. 21. 23. 30. nec do- ctrinam Christi, aut ipsum Christum ceu verum at- que unicum Mediatorem suscipiebant per fidem, sed reprobabant, eoq; posthabito per opera legis sese salutem consequuturos credebant. Quod in ipsis reprobat, & causam reprobationis eorum es- se, docet Apostolus, adducto in eam rem gemino Prophetico testimonio: altera ex Ef. XXIIX, 16. de lapide in Sione posito, super quem extruendi sint salvandi, quum illi, qui credunt in eum, soli no fugiant, sed confidenter habitent, & securi eo inni- tantur, adeoque non pudefiant, ut ab Apostolo nostro hic, & à S. Petro 1. Ep. II. 8. locus Prophe- ticus explicatur, quem de Christo sonare etiam ex aliorum locorum collatione Pf. CXIIX. 22. (Act, IV. 11.) Ef. IIX. 14. Mat. XXI. 42. Luc. II 34. c. XX. 17. liquet: altero ex Ef. IIX. 14. ubi Christus lapis of- fendiculi & petra scandali dicitur, quod è contextu & loco parallelo Luc. II. 34. nec non præsenti alle- gatione Apostolica constat. Ea vero testimonia ita inter se colligantur, ac si unum idemq; testimoni- um sit, quia ab uno Spiritu per eundem Prophetam prodiêre, in quibus v. è sede propria discriminan- dis, actio Dei, in Sion lapidem illum ponentis, non commiscenda cum eventu, quo lapis ille factus la- pis offensionis: quem utique Deus non in lapidem offendiculi posuit, sed ut credatur in eum, ceu pe- tram salutis; lapis enim quà à Deo ponitur, uti vere pretiosus est, ita in caput anguli, cui inniti Ec- clesia & fundamentum salutis ponitur, ut, qui cre- dit in eum, non fugere opus habeat, neque pude- fiat, sed securus sit, & gloriose superet. Nam & con- sequentia pro antecedentibus, actiones quæ signa ali- cujus affectus sunt, pro affectibus sumi solent, ut percutere simul pro intime dolere, ridere pro lætari, manum super os ponere pro tacere, Job. 8. 21. Ps. 126. 2. Gen. 21, 6. Luc. 6, 21. 25. Job. 40, 35. Mich. 7, 16. ut qui credit, non festinet, i. e. no opus habeat vel ex an- xietate nimia, vel trepidatione cordis & timore fu- gere, & cum effectus & consequens confusionis sit festinatio, & fuga sit subductio festina ab oculis ho- minum, ideo, qui credit, dicitur, non pudefieri, ac porro κατὰ μείωσιν non fugere, non pudefieri est con- sistere, fecurum permanere, & ab ignominia im- munem cum honore & gloria vivere, imo in ju- dicio divino ab omni ignominia & confusione li- berari, & gloria ac salute æterna potiri, ut ex hac Apostolica allegatione, & applicatione si intentio- nem & scopum, ac vim confirmationis respicias, nec no è textu ipso Prophetico, (quo de vid. annot. nostra in Bibliis V. T. illustratis) manifestum est. In- tentio ergo Dei lapidem angularem in Sion pone- tis, non est, ut sit lapis offendiculi, sed hic est even- tus accidentalis, & culpa ejus sita est in hominibus in lapidem illũ pretiosum & petram salutis impin- gentibus. Qui προσκόπτωσι τῷ λόγῳ secundum Petrum; quod de λόγω substantiali Christo intel- ligi potest, utpote qui est lapis ille offendiculi; aut si de verbo Evangelii accipiatur, de Objecto præci- puo ejusdem, quod non est crux nostra, sed crux & passio Christi, ob quam Evangelium verbum cru- cis dicitur 1. Cor. I. 18. de Christo crucifixo, qui Judæis scandalum est v. 23. credentibus vera & uni- ce salvifica Sapientia 1. Cor. II. 2. Quanquam enim crucem tolerare debeant Christiani, & propter nomen Domini mortem etiam ipsam obire, non id tamen hic agitur, sed de causa salutis disseritur, ut & rejectionis à salute. Causa autem salutis non est crucis tolerantia, sed fides in Christum: uti Ju- dæorum a̓πιστια vel reprobatio Christi per τὸ προσκόπτειν impingere in lapidem offendiculi de- signata causa exitii Israëlitarum constituitur. De sensu vaticiniorum Esaiæ, quem & hoc loco, & in sede propria depravat, ea quod ad literalem sensum abripiens ad liberationem temporalem, nec nisi typice referens ad Messiæ liberationem in an- notatis ad V. T. diximus, & corruptelas Grotij discusfimus, ut opus non sit hic quicquam porro addere.

SUBSECTIO II. Justitiam Christi, ceu causam meritoriam & for- malem justificationis qua Judæorum, qua gentium adserens.

## 10:1 Argument
CHAPTER X.

ARGUMENT AND PARTITION.

The Apostle, having testified to his sincere affection of mind for the Israelites, complains that they, not acknowledging the righteousness of God, have established their own righteousness, showing the difference between the two: that the former is obtained through faith, the latter through works; that the former does not require our ascent or descent, but relies solely on Christ's descent from heaven and resurrection from the dead, which, being proposed by the word of faith, if they are received by faith, we obtain justification and salvation. Forasmuch as all who believe in Him shall not be confounded, and all who call upon the name of the Lord, whether they be Jews or Gentiles, shall be saved: and therefore it was preached to all, since we cannot believe without a herald, and the sound of the Gospel has been sent out into the whole world: and the conversion of the Gentiles to God and their own unbelief had already been predicted to Israel by Moses as well as by Elijah.

These parts are: I. The confirmation of the righteousness of faith and the refutation of one's own, taken from Moses up to v. 8. II. A further demonstration of righteousness through faith, from the Prophets, namely Isaiah and Joel, up to v. 13. III. The necessity and propagation throughout the world of the word of the Gospel, by which the righteousness of faith is announced, which is taught from Isaiah and David, so that it may be established that righteousness and salvation pertain no less to the Gentiles than to the Israelites, which is confirmed by the Mosaic-Prophetic prediction of the faith of the Gentiles and the infidelity of the Israelites, up to v. 21.

PART I. CHAP. X. The confirmation of the righteousness of faith and the refutation of one's own, instituted from Moses.

V. 1. Brethren.

He addresses the Jews, who had already given their names to Christ.

ἡ μὲν εὐδοκία τῆς ἐμῆς καρδίας.

Εὐδοκία καρδίας here is the benevolence of the mind. רצון in the Psalms often. See Luke II. 14.

καὶ ἡ δέησις ἡ πρὸς τὸν θεὸν ὑπὲρ τῶ ἰσραήλ ἐσιν εἰς σωτηρίαν.

עתרו שלום ואמרו Jer. XXXIII. 6. I wish them all good things, even eternal ones. He removes from himself the suspicion of hatred.

Latin:

CAPUT X.

ARGUMENTUM ET PARTITIO.

Sinceram animi affectionem de Israëlitis testa- tus Apostolus, queritur, quod non agnoscen- tes Dei justitiam stabiliverint propriam justitiam, utriusque discrimen ostendens, quod illa per fidem obtineatur, hæc per ope- ra: illa non indigeat nostro ascensu vel descensu, sed unice nitatur Christi de- scensu è cœlis & resurrectione à mor- tuis, quæ verbo fidei proposita, si suscipian- tur fide, justificationem & salutem conse- quimur. Siquidem omnes in ipsum credentes, non confundantur, omnes nomen Domini invocantes, sive Judæi fuerint, sive gentes, salventur: atque ideo omnibus prædicatum fuerit, quum sine præ- conio credere nequeamus, & emissus sonus Evangelii sit in totum orbem: atque Israëli jam à Mose ut & Elia gentium ad Deum con- versio ipsorumque ἀπισία prædicta sit.

PArtes hæ sunt I. Justitiæ fidei confirmatio pro- priæq; profligatio, è Mose facta usq; ad v. 8. II. Justitiæ per fidem ulterior demonstratio, è Prophetis Esaia nempe, & Joële usque ad v. 13. III. Verbi Ev- angelii, quo justitia fidei annunciatur, necessitas & per orbem propagatio, quæ ex Esaia & Davi- de docetur, ut constet gentes non minus, quam Israëlitas attinere justitiam & salutem, quod præ- dictione fidei gentium, & infidelitatis Israëlitarum Mosaïco-Prophetica statuminatur usque ad v. 21.

PARS I. CAP. X. Justitiæ fidei confirmatio propriáque profli- gatio è Mose instituta.

V. 1. Ἀδελφοὶ.

Alloquitur Judæos, qui jam Christo nomen dederant.

ἡ μὲν εὐδοκία τῆς ἐμῆς καρδίας.

Εὐδοκία καρδίας hic est animi benevolentia. רצון in Psal- mis sæpe. Vide Luc. II. 14.

καὶ ἡ δέησις ἡ πρὸς τὸν θεὸν ὑπὲρ τῶ ἰσραήλ ἐσιν εἰς σωτηρίαν.

עתרו שלום ואמרו Jer. XXXIII. 6. Opto il- lis bona omnia, etiam æterna. Amolitur à se odii suspicionē.

## 10:2
V. 2. μαρτυρῶ γὰρ αὐτοῖς.

Thus Luke X. 22. ἐμαρτυρει αὐτῷ. The same construction is in Acts XV. 8, XXII. 5, Gal. IV. 15, Col. IV. 13; it is said of those who provide testimony which benefits another.

ὅτι ζῆλον Θεῦ ἔχουσι.

A certain zeal toward God. Thus ζῆλος τῶ ὄικε σε Ps. LXIX. 10, John II. 17. All nouns of this kind have sometimes the genitive of the subject, sometimes of the object.

ἀλλ᾽ ἐ κατ᾽ ἐπίγνωσιν.

Ἐπίγνωσις is the same as γνῶσις, as in 1 Kings VII. 14, Prov. II. 5, Hosea IV. 6, VI. 6, above I. 28, III. 20, Eph. I. 17, and elsewhere often. They go where they are going, not where they ought to go: that diminishes the fault, it does not remove it. They ought to learn better things, especially in such obvious light.

Although the discourse is about the Jews, and the Apostle testifies to his affection toward them, it does not appear, however, that he addressed the Jews themselves here by the name of brothers: but rather that he addresses all to whom this Epistle was written, which indeed was directed no less to those converted from the Jews than from the Gentiles, as is evident from the inscription. Because they were brothers, even if not by kinship of the flesh, yet by spiritual communion. That ignorance is said to diminish guilt, not remove it, we admit regarding simple ignorance, as they call it, but not regarding affected ignorance, from which, although not a few of the Jews suffered, yet it must be judged that most of them, because they were fascinated by a preconceived opinion which they had imbibed from tender years through Pharisaic corruptions (as we see happening today in the Papacy, even though the Light of the Gospel shines everywhere in the world), were occupied by an ignorance of pure negation rather than of depraved disposition, of whom therefore the Apostle not only has pity, but also testifies that they had a zeal, but not according to knowledge, for GOD or the law of GOD.

Latin:

V. 2. μαρτυρῶ γὰρ αὐτοῖς.

Sic Luc. X. 22. ἐμαρτυρει αὐτῷ. Eadem constructio Act. XV. 8. XXII. 5. Gal. IV. 15. Coloss. IV. 13. dicitur de iis, qui testimonium præbent, quod alteri prosit.

ὅτι ζῆλον Θεῦ ἔχουσι.

Studium quoddam erga Deum. Sic ζῆλος τῶ ὄικε σε Ps. LXIX. 10. Joh. II. 17. Nomina omnia ejusmodi modo genitivum habent subjecti modo objecti.

ἀλλ᾽ ἐ κατ᾽ ἐπίγνωσιν.

Ἐπίγνωσις idem quod γνῶσις ut 1. Reg. VII. 14. Prov. II. 5. Oseæ IV. 6. VI. 6. supra I. 28. III. 20. Eph. I. 17. & alibi sæpe. Eunt, qua itur, non qua eundum est: id culpam mi- nuit, non tollit. Discere debeant meliora, maxime tam obvia luce.

Etsi sermo sit de Judæis, & affectum erga eos- dem testetur Apostolus, non apparet tamen, eum Judæos ipsos nomine fratrum hic compellasse: quin potius omnes alloquatur ad quos exarata est hæc Epistola, quæ vero non minus ad conversos è Judæis, quam è gentibus directa est, ut ex ἐπιγρα- φῇ constat. Quia fratres erant, etsi non carnis cognatione, tamen spirituali communione. Quod ignorantia minui culpam, non tolli dicitur, de ignorantia simplici, quam vocant, admittimus, non item de affectata, qua etsi non pauci è Judæis labo- rarent, plerosque tamen, quia præconcepta opi- nione, quam per Pharisäicas corruptelas à teneris instillatas imbiberant, fascinati erant (ut hodie in Papatu, etsi fulgeat passim in orbe Lux Evange- lica, fieri videmus) ignorantia potius puræ ἀπο- φάσεως, quam pravæ διαθέσεως occupatos fuisse, censendum est, quorum proinde non miseretur tantum Apostolus, sed zelum etiam, quod DEO vel lege DEI, at non secundū scientiam testatur.

## 10:3
V. 3. For being ignorant of the righteousness of God.

That is, from God, as is said in Philippians 3:9. That true and internal righteousness, which is pleasing to God, proceeds from God himself revealing himself and calling men to himself. An example of which Paul gave above regarding Abraham in 4:2, 3. Of this, most of the Jews were not thinking.

Grotius does not touch the hinge of the Apostolic disputation, being occupied with Papist-Remonstrant and Socinian opinions. And therefore he perverts everything in that disputation. The discourse here is not about INTERNAL or INHERENT righteousness, which they make the formal cause of justification, but about the IMPUTED righteousness of CHRIST, which the Apostle had asserted above to be the formal cause of our justification. For the discussion here is about the righteousness which (1.) χωρὶς ἔργων, without works, comes to us (2.) Which is imputed to us through faith. (3.) About the righteousness or OBEDIENCE of CHRIST, by which we are justified as he had taught. (4.) concerning the righteousness which is ἐκ πίστεως, from faith, as was said in v. 30 of the preceding chapter, not ἐξ ἔργων νόμε, from the works of the law, which demands most perfect works, without any defect, Deut. XXVII. 26. (5.) concerning righteousness not our own or proper, because the Jews wished to set up τὴν ἰδίαν δικαιοσύνην, their own righteousness, which the Apostle rejects, but ALIEN, and thus the righteousness of Christ. For proper righteousness is opposed to alien, our righteousness to the righteousness of Christ, inherent righteousness to imputed righteousness, the righteousness of works to the righteousness of faith, legal righteousness to Evangelical righteousness. (6.) Concerning the righteousness which we have not through our own fulfillment of the law, for this is impossible for us, Rom. IIX. 3, but through the fulfillment made by Christ in our place, who is τέλος νόμε εἰς δικαιοσύνην παντὶ τῶ πισέυοντι. Therefore that righteousness is called ἡ τῶ Θεῦ δικαιοσύνη, the righteousness of God, not only because it is revealed by GOD, for even that righteousness which is exhibited in the law can be said to be revealed by GOD, from whom the law is, nor only because it proceeds from GOD, calling men to Himself: since even the obedience which is rendered to the law must be ascribed to GOD, as the author and cause of our renewal and sanctification, from whom is both the willing and the performing: but because it is the righteousness of GOD Himself, namely of Christ, that God blessed forever above all, who is Jehovah, our righteousness, Jerem. XXIII. 5, which is called ἐκ Θεῦ in Phil. III. 9, because Christ was made righteousness for us by God, 1 Cor. I. 30, and it is solely from the grace of God that the righteousness of Christ is our righteousness, and is imputed to us. Blessed Mylius rendered the words 'the righteousness of God' somewhat differently, but with the same meaning, p. 343. He calls it the righteousness of GOD, not that which He uses in judging, while He distributes rewards to the pious and exacts punishments from the impious: but that which He communicates to us in His Son, and by which alone we can stand in His judgment. Giselber. l. IIX. Altercat. (in B. Weller p. 582) has it thus: I call it the righteousness of GOD, not that by which God is righteous, but that by which He clothes man, when He freely justifies the impious. To this righteousness the Law and the Prophets bear witness. The Law indeed by this very fact, that by commanding and threatening, and by justifying no one, it sufficiently indicates that man is justified by the gift of GOD through the life-giving Spirit: the Prophets, however, because the coming of Christ fulfilled that which they predicted. But the Apostle clearly testified in Phil. III. 9 that this righteousness is not our own proper or inherent INTERNAL righteousness, so that I may be found IN HIM (Christ) not having MY righteousness, τὴν ἐκ νόμε, that which is FROM THE LAW, (is that inherent and internal righteousness of ours not from the law, is it not prescribed by the law and to be estimated according to the law as a rule, and should one not trust in it?) ἀλλὰ τὴν διὰ πίσεως, but that which is through the faith of Christ, or in Christ, τὴν ἐκ θεῦ δικαιοσύνην ἐπὶ τῇ πίσει, that RIGHTEOUSNESS which is from God in faith: It is from GOD, because it is from the mere grace of God: because it is a righteousness not our own, such as the law requires, which no one of us finds in himself, nor can find after the fall: because the law is spiritual, but we are carnal, but he destined and ordained an alien one, namely that of CHRIST Himself, and takes the same in our place, and imputes it to us through faith, which comes to us only in faith and through faith, when indeed we apprehend it by faith: and thus the same is reckoned to us as if it were our own righteousness. And Paul gave an example of this in Abraham above in c. IV. 2, 3, to whom faith was imputed for righteousness, which he taught in v. 5, 6 was WITHOUT WORKS, and thus also without that internal inherent righteousness. Of this righteousness of Christ, most Jews were not thinking, attempting to set up their own righteousness, as the Apostle testifies.

καὶ τὴν ἰδίαν δικαιοσύνην ζητῦντες ςῆσαι. ἱσάναι, העמיד, is among other things to approve power, and to grant a right to someone. Most Jews wished to establish for the sake of eternal salvation that external righteousness which is prepared through frequent actions and is of some value in human society. It is καθῆκον, not κατόρθωμα, as Cicero distinguishes in the third and fourth books of De Finibus, and in the first of De Officiis.

Grotius perverts the term 'proper righteousness,' as if it denotes only EXTERNAL righteousness: for is not INTERNAL righteousness also to be held as that proper righteousness; or did the Jews hold only EXTERNAL righteousness as the cause of eternal salvation, and not also INTERNAL righteousness? They were indeed stuck for the most part in externals, but they nevertheless urged internal righteousness, namely the love of God with all the mind, with all the soul, with all the heart, as is evident from the example of both the lawyers, Luke X. 37, and the Pharisees, Matt. XXII. 37. But Paul, who is rashly judged by Cicero, who was taught nothing about the righteousness of the Gospel, rejects the opinion of the Jews, not only insofar as they urged only external righteousness, of which no apex is held, but insofar as they set up their PROPER righteousness, and constituted as the cause of salvation both internal and that external righteousness about which Moses writes, saying concerning the precepts of the law, 'He who shall do them shall live in them,' as is held in v. 5: who however did not prescribe or demand only external obedience or righteousness, but primarily internal of the mind, soul, heart, and indeed of the whole mind, soul, and whole heart, under that perfection which is found in no mortal: whence we must flee to Christ, who is τέλος νόμου, the fulfillment of the law, and has been made righteousness for us by GOD. Rightly to this verse Blessed Mylius: He calls it proper righteousness, which consists in the merit of one's own works, and which men have from themselves. By the word 'to establish' its infirmity is noted. For that which totters and wavers in itself is established, and therefore needs props by which it may be established. But a vain attempt is noted by the other word. For this establishment is sought only: it is not obtained.

they did not submit themselves to the righteousness of God.

Learned men rightly advise that here the passive form stands for the reciprocal: Niphal, as the Hebrews say, for Hithpael: concerning which locution we treated at Acts 13:48. They did not subject themselves to the righteousness of God, that is, they did not enter upon the way by which it might be obtained, namely, faith. Many would arrive at wisdom, if they did not think they had already arrived. The same thing happened to those Jews. Not unlike that is the statement of Philo: 'There are also those who seemed to take care (namely, of the seeds of hope), having embraced self-love before piety, they attributed the causes of their successes to themselves, and all were blameworthy, but the only one worthy of acceptance is he who attributed his hope to God.'

That gloss is not to be admitted, 'they did not subject themselves to the righteousness of God, that is, they did not enter upon the way by which it might be obtained, namely, faith.' The Apostle says more: they did not subject themselves to the righteousness of God, that is, they did not admit the righteousness of God, they rejected the same, because they reprobated Christ himself, who is Jehovah our righteousness. How could they admit or receive through faith the righteousness of Christ, who rejected and condemned Christ himself? It is therefore a meiosis: they were unwilling to be subordinated or to subject themselves to the righteousness of Christ, for: they utterly rejected the righteousness of Christ, just as they are said to have spurned the counsel of God concerning salvation in Luke 7:30, and to have thrust away the word of God in Acts 13:46. The blessed Mylius also properly observed the emphasis in the word 'subject': That he says the Jews were not subjected to the righteousness of God, that is, not humbled before God, so that they might confess themselves to be miserable and in need of the grace and mercy of God, and might apprehend by faith the righteousness which God offered to them in Christ. The cause of this evil depends on the preceding member.
