Others more correctly explain that ἐν Ἠλίᾳ as being about Elijah, just as ב occurs for על in Ps. LXXXVII. 3, and the particle ἐν is taken in Matt. X. 32, Luke XII. 8. The word λέγων is wrongly called into doubt because of the authority of one manuscript; nor does it hinder the sense at all.

Latin:

V. 2. ἐκ ἀπώσατο ὁ κύριος τὸν λαὸν ἁυτῶ ὃν προέγνω.

Negatione aperta respondet objectioni. Nunquam DEUS totum populum ex Israele ortum amavit, ita ut ad veram justitiam & quæ ei cohæret salutem omnes dedu- ceret, sed quosdam. Non ergo iidem sunt aut pares planè quos approbavit in hoc, & quos nunc despicit. Aliquos à DEO repelli nihil erat novi. Vide Deut. XXIX. 28. ubi est in Græco ἐξέβαλον ἀὐτός.

Temerè in suspicionem corruptelæ vocatur textus receptus Græcorum lectio è versu secundo sine dubio orta. Unus autem codex cæteris o- mnibus præjudicare non potest. Sensus est: non abjecisse DEUM populum suum simpliciter: tùm quod non universum abjecerit, tùm quod non ex mero beneplacito; Quem autem & quomodo non abjecerit, verf. 2. exponitur. Prius, quod non o- mnes abjecerit, exemplo suo probat Apostolus: Alterum, quos non reprobavit, v. 2. explicat. Nec dextrè à Grotio illud προέγνω accipitur. Non enim est, prius approbavit, sed prævidit: nec illo sensu Rom. IIX. 29. id adhibetur. Non approba- tio pietatis, sed prævisio fidei designatur ab Aposto- lo. Nam ex fide prævisa facta est electio 1. Petr. I. 2. 2. Thess. II. 13. Non ergò reprobavit DEUS, quorum fidem ipse prævidit, in populo Israeliti- co. Quid verò huc faciat, quod non despexerit Dominus populum suum, quem prius approbavit? vel quod non iidem sint quos approbavit, & quos jam despicit? Nam de eo dubium esse nullum po- terat, olim Judaicum populum DEO probatum fuisse, hunc autem ab illo diversum esse: sed de eo disserit Apostolus, quomodo, & ex qua causa Deus populum suum jam reprobet, vel abjiciat? Nam ad illum populum pertinebat Paulus, quantum ad cognationem sanguinis, & de illis fratribus suis se- cundum carnem, quos abjectos suprà doluit, agit: non ex odio mero DEI abjectos, nec omnes re- probatos esse docens, non enim abjectos, quos prævidit DEUS credituros, sed incredulos tantum & induratos. Novit enim Deus suos 2. Timoth. II. 9. Non ergò universum populum abjectum esse dicit, quia præcognoverit eundem, id est, quia & novit jam, qui credant, & novit qui olim credi- turi sunt in Christum, qui inter abjectos nun- quam reputandi sint, etsi videatur totum prope- modum abjecisse populum. Quod exemplo si- mili illustrat, quomodo tempore Eliæ, cum se so- lum inter veros DEI cultores superesse crederet Propheta, Dominus sibi septem millia fidelium in occulto servarit, id ad rem præsentem appli- cans. Plebs ergò præscita, plebs non repulsa dicen- te Autore libr. de vocat. gentium l. 1. c. 10. hi sunt, qui in Christo justificati sunt; & quod de omni Israe- le dici videtur, in his tantum, quos sibi gratia Electio reliquos fecit, ostenditur. Ideò Chrysostomus & Græca scholia h. l. ἐκ ἀπώθητε ἀπὸ Θεῦ, ἀλλ’ ἑαυ- τὺς ἀπωθεῖτε. Non estis rejecti à DEO, sed vos vosmet ipsos repellitis. LXX. vocem געל exprimunt hoc verbo ἀπωθεῖν, quod est amoliri cum fastidio & nausea. Vid. Ezech. XVI. 5. 44. 45. exprimunt etiam ita vocem מאס rem fastidio quodam tan- quam abominabilem abjicere. Jer. VII. 29. Amos II. 4. c. V. 21. ut נטש & פרע derelinquere, de- nudare. Judæi ἀπωθεῖσθαι λόγον aversari, abji- cere Evangelium dicuntur, Act. XIII. 46. c. VII. 37. Ipsi ergò non ex odio simplici abjecti, sed quia Ev- angelium Dei abjecerunt, & reprobarunt.

ἢ ἐκ οἴδατε ἐν Ἠλίᾳ τί λέγει ἡ γραφὴ. Id est, in illa parte libri Regum, qui quod res Eliæ conti- neret, ideò μετωνυμικῶς de ejus nomine appellatur.

ὡς ἐντυγχάνει τῷ θεῷ κατὰ τὸν Ἰσραὴλ λέγων. λέγων abest in Manuscripto. Benè: nam sicut ἐντυγχά- νειν ὑπέρ τινος, est negotium alicujus commendare, ita ἐ- ντυγχάνειν κατά τινος, est aliquem accusare. Vide 1. Macc. VIII. 32. X. 61. 63. 64. XI. 21.

Illud ἐν Ἠλίᾳ rectius alii exponunt ferè de Elia, ut ב pro על occurrit Pf. LXXXVII. 3. & particu- la ἐν accipitur Matth. X. 32. Luc. XII. 8. Vox λέ- γων perperam in dubium vocatur ob unius codicis M. S. autoritatem: nec sensui quicquam officit.

## 11:3
V. 3. Lord, they have killed thy prophets and digged down thine altars, and I am left alone and they seek my life. In the Greek of 1 Kings according to the Hebrews, and according to the Greeks 3 Kings XIX. 10, the words are nearly the same: they have digged down thine altars and killed thy prophets with the sword, and I am left most alone, and they seek my life to take it. That ἐγὼ ὑπελείφθην, or ὑπολέλειμμαι μόνος, or μονώτατος, is the same as what is in Horace: Now I remain. What ζητῦσι τὴν ψυχήν με means is clear from those things which were said at Matt. II. 20. Those altars which are said to have been overturned were those which the pious in the ten tribes had built for themselves, from the time they were not permitted to go to the temple, at which time the law concerning building altars elsewhere seemed to cease. Thus Kimchi.

It is said rashly that the divine law concerning the building of altars ceased: for if it ceased in fact, it ceased wickedly. If by right, who could have derogated from divine law by right? Therefore, some think that altars in the plural is said by enallage for altar, others explain it more correctly concerning the two altars of incense Exod. XXX. 1. Cf. 1 Kings VI. 20, VIII. 64, and concerning the altars of burnt offering Ex. XXVII. 1.

Latin:

V. 3. κύριε τὲς προφήτας συ ἀπέκτειναν καὶ τὰ θυ- σιασήριά συ κατέσκαψαν, κἀγὼ ὑπελείφθην μόνος καὶ ζητῦσι τὴν ψυχήν μγ. In Græco 1. Regum juxta Hebræos, juxta Græcos III. Regum XIX. 10. verba sunt propè eadem: τὰ θυσιαστήριά σε κατέσκαψαν καὶ τὲς προφήτας συ ἀπέκτειναν ἐν ῥομφαίᾳ, καὶ ὑπολέλειμμαι ἐγὼ μονώτατος, καὶ ζητῶσι τὴν ψυχήν με λα- βεῖν αὐτήν. Illud ἐγὼ ὑπελείφθην, vel ὑπολέλειμμαι μόνος, aut μονώτατος, idem est, quod apud Horatium: Nunc ego resto. Quid sit ζητῦσι τὴν ψυχήν με patet ex iis, quæ dicta ad Matth. II. 20. Altaria illa, quæ eversa dicuntur, ea erant, quæ pii in decem tribubus sibi struxerant, ex quo permissi non erant ad templum ire, quo tempore lex de altaribus alibi struendis cessare videbatur. Ita Kimchi.

Legem divinam de altaribus extruendis cessasse temerè dicitur: nam si de facto cessavit, improbè cessavit. Si de jure, ecquis jure juri divino dero- gare potuit? Altaria igitur alii in plurali per enal- lagen dicta putant pro altari, alii de duobus alta- ribus suffitus Exod. XXX. 1. Conf. 1. Reg. VI. 20. IIX. 64. & de altaribus holocausti Ex. XXVII. 1. rectius explicant.

## 11:4
V. 4. But what saith the answer of God unto him? χρηματίζειν is said of every manner by which God signifies something to men beyond the ordinary, as Matt. II. 12, 22, Luke II. 26, Acts X. 22, Heb. VIII. 5, XI. 7. But here χρηματισμός is properly that thin voice which the Hebrews call בת קול, the mention of which is in the aforementioned place 1 Kings XIX. 12.

There is no mention in the book of Kings, or anywhere in the sacred scriptures, of that kind of revelation which the Rabbis assign to the name בת קול, daughter of a voice: indeed, the Talmudists in the tract Sanhedrin ch. 1 maintain that a revelation of this kind took place only in the second temple, and after the times of the Prophets. See Hotting. Thes. Philol. p. 615.

I have reserved to myself seven thousand men who have not bowed the knee to Baal. In the Greek of Kings, after God foretold the slaughters which Jehu and Elisha were about to produce, it follows: and thou shalt leave in Israel seven thousand men, all the knees which have not bowed the knee to Baal. But Paul follows the Hebrew more closely, where there is והשארתי, which is according to the conjugation κατέλιπον, but by a very accepted locution, especially after a conjunction, it signifies καταλείψω, I will leave remaining seven thousand. And I think that in other Greek versions, which Paul had seen, there was κατέλιπον. The opposition was also softened by Paul: for what is in the Hebrew and Greek seven thousand all the knees, which have not bowed themselves to Baal, here is, seven thousand, who have not bowed the knee to Baal, with the same sense. But why here in the feminine τῇ Βάαλ? In Tobit it is read βάαλ τῇ δαμάλει, where other manuscripts have δυνάμει. But in the history of Ahab, to which these things pertain, we see Baal expressly distinguished from the calves, and in this Ahab's guilt is made graver than Jeroboam's, because Jeroboam worshipped only the calves, but Ahab worshipped Baal, and that by the example of the Sidonians, 1 Kings XVI. 31. Not badly, therefore, do learned men feel that the noun εἰκόνι is to be understood here, which word you have placed for idol in Deut. IV. 16, 2 Chron. XXXIV. 7, Ezek. VII. 20, VIII. 5, Isa. XL. 18, 28.

Dan. III. 1. and following. And specifically concerning Baal, 4 Kings XI. 19. and generally, where mention is made of any idol, even of Moloch, the LXX are accustomed to say τὴν βάαλ, as Jud. III. 7. Hosea II. 8. Jer. II. 8. in the Greek: XI. 14. XIX. 5. XXXII. 35. 1 Sam. VII. 13. Zeph. I. 4. The sense in the oracle is manifest, that GOD would bring it about that those who had neither bent their knees to the image of Baal, nor given it a kiss, would remain untouched by those calamities coming upon the ten tribes, just as those who observed the law are examples from the destruction of Jerusalem brought about by Nebuchadnezzar; Ezek. IX. 4. These were they whom God in those times ἔγνω, that is, acknowledged as his own.

We have spoken elsewhere of the word Baal. It pleases some that the feminine gender is used for the sake of ignominy, just as Hos. X. 3. Jerome observes in the same place that the idols of Jeroboam עגלות, calves, are spoken of in the feminine gender by way of mockery. Others note that the ancients worshipped the same name in both sexes, and that there was no distinction of sex. Just as Hermes Trismegistus calls God ἀῥῥενοθήλυν. And thus Baal is attributed by the LXX both the masculine, 2 Kings X. 11, 17, Jer. V. 2, Hos. XI. 2, and the feminine gender, 1 Kings XIX. 18, Jer. XIX. 5, Zeph. I. 4. Let Selden be seen in De Diis Syris, Syntagm. 2, c. 2. And Arnobius, l. 3, adv. gent., falsely mocks the heathens, who were accustomed to say in their prayers, whether you are God or Goddess: and that Ceres with the breasts is introduced, and also Lancia, Lucina Juno, namely so that with new offspring also arising, whatever the prior age had taken away, a recurring substitution might replace, as he speaks most elegantly; as B. Weller has it, p. 620. The sense of the oracle, however, is not about saving from the calamities coming upon those ten tribes those who had not worshipped Baal, but about the seven thousand faithful who survived in the time of Elijah in the kingdom of Israel, whom GOD preserved from the worship of Baal, and thus not about the benefit of their liberation from external evils, who abstained from idolatry, but about the conservation of the Church or of the faithful in the worship of one GOD, and in the true faith under public idolatrous worship and in the midst of infidels. Whence by this example the Apostle teaches, not that GOD is about to rescue certain ones from imminent destruction, but that although the people are for the most part blinded and hardened, many nevertheless, whose number is known to GOD alone, are to be converted to Christ and are to adhere to him with true faith, and are to attain eternal salvation.

Latin:

V. 4. ἀλλὰ τί λέγει ἀυτῷ ὁ χρηματισμός. χρηματίζειν dicitur de omni ratione, qua Deus homini- bus aliquid præter ordinem significat, ut Matth. II. 12. 22. Luc. II. 26. Act. X. 22. Hebr. VIII. 5. XI. 7. Sed hic propriè χρηματισμός est vox illa tenuis, quam Hebræi vocant בת קול, cujus mentio dicto loco 1. Reg. XIX. 12.

Nulla in libro Regum, aut uspiam in sacris literis mentio fit generis istius revelationis, quod assignant Rabbini nomini בת קול filia vocis: quin & hujusmodi revelationem in templo demum secundo, & post Prophetarum tempora locum ha- buisse Talmudici in codice Sanhedrim c. 1. perhi- bent. Vid. Hotting. Thes. Philol. p. 615.

κατέλιπον ἐμαυτῷ ἑπτάκις χιλίες ἄνδρας ὅϊτινες ἐκ ἔκαμψαν γόνυ τῇ Βάαλ. In Græco Regum postquam prædixit Deus clades, quas Jehu & Elisæus erant edituri, sequitur: καὶ καταλείψεις ἐν ἰσραὴλ ἑπτα χιλιάδας ἀνδρῶν πάντα γόνατα ἃ ἐκ ὤκλασαν γόνυ τῷ βάαλ. Sed Paulus Hebræum pressius sequitur, ubi est והשארתי, quod est secundum conjugationem κατέ- λιπον, at locutione valde recepta, maximè post copulam, valet καταλείψω, reliqua faciam septem millia. Et puto in aliis Græcis versionibus, quas viderat Paulus, fuisse κατέ- λιπον. Emollita quoque a Paulo est oppositio: nam quod in Hebræo & Græco est septem millia omnis genu, quæ se non flexerunt Baali, hic est, septies mille, qui genu non flexere Baali, sensu eodem. Sed cur hîc in fœminino τῇ Βάαλ; In Tobia legitur βάαλ τῇ δαμάλει, ubi alii codices δυνά- μει. Sed in Achabi historia, ad quam hæc pertinent, vide- mus Baalem disertè distingui à vitulis, & in hoc culpam Achabi graviorem fieri quam Jeroboami, quod Jeroboa- mus vitulos tantùm, Achabus autem Baalem coluerit, id- que Sidoniorum exemplo, 1. Reg. XVI. 31. Non malè igitur viri docti sentiunt hic subaudiri nomen εἰκόνι, quod vocabulum pro idolo positum habes Deuter. IV. 16. 2. Pa- ralip. XXXIV. 7. Ezech. VII. 20. VIII. 5. Esa. XL. 18. 28.

Dan. III. 1. & sequentibus. Et nominatim de Baale IV. Regum XI. 19. & generaliter, ubi simulachri alicujus, etiam Molochi, mentio τὴν βάαλ solent dicere LXX. ut Jud. III. 7. Oseæ II. 8. Jerem. II. 8. in Græco: XI. 14. XIX. 5. XXXII. 35. 1. Sam. VII. 13. Sophon. I. 4. Sensus, in oraculo manifestus est, effecturum DEUM ut cladibus illis super tribus decem venturis intacti manerent, qui Baalis imagini nec genua flexerant, nec osculum dederant, plane sicut qui legem observarunt, exempli sunt ab excidio Hierosolymorum facto per Nabuchodonosorem; Ezech. IX. 4. Hi fuêre, quos Deus illis temporibus ἔγνω, id est, pro suis agnovit.

De voce Baal aliàs diximus. Fœmininum genus ignominiæ causà adhiberi nonnullis placet, uti Os. X. 3. idola Jeroboam עגלות vaccas in fœminino genere per irrisionem dici Hieronymus ibidem observat. Alii notant veteres idem nomen in utroque sexu coluisse, nec sexus discrimen fuisse. Sicut Hermes Trismegistus Deum ἀῥῥενοθήλυν appellat. Atque sic Baal à LXX. & masculinum 2. Reg. X. 11. 17. Jer. V. 2. Os. XI. 2. & fœmininum genus 1. Reg. XIX. 18. Jer. XIX. 5. Zephan. I. 4. tribuitur. Videatur Seltenius de Diis Syris Syntagm. 2. c. 2. Et falsè ridet Arnob. l. 3. adv. gent. ethnicos, qui consuevere in precibus dicere, sive tu Deus es, sive Dea: & introduci Cererem mammosam, nec non Lanciam, Lucinam Junonem, nempe ut nova quoque suboriente fœtura, quicquid prior ætas abstulisset, recidiva substitutio subrogaret, ut elegantissimè loquitur; ut habet B. Wellerus p. 620. Sensus autem oraculi non est de servandis à cladibus super decem tribus venturis illis, qui non venerati fuerint Baalem, sed de superstitibus tempore Eliæ fidelium in regno Israëlis septem millibus, quos DEUS à cultu Baal præservavit, adeoque non de beneficio liberationis eorum à malis externis, qui ab idololatria abstinuère, sed de conservatione Ecclesiæ vel fidelium in cultu unius DEI, & verà fide sub publico idololatrico cultu & in medio infidelium. Unde hoc exemplo docet Apostolus, non quod DEUS quosdam ab imminente excidio erepturus sit, sed quod populo maximam partem excæcato & indurato, multi tamen, quorum numerus soli DEO notus, ad Christum convertendi, eique verà fide adhæsuri sint, ac salutem æternam consequuturi.

## 11:5
V. 5. οὕτως ἐν τῷ νῦν καιρῷ λεῖμμα κατ᾽ ἐκλογὴν χάριτος γέγονεν. That is, a few were rescued from the common depravity of the Jews by a benefit proceeding from the supreme goodness of God. λεῖμμα is שאר or שריד, which is also κατάλειμμα above IX. 27, a few out of many; ἐκλογὴ is any benefit of GOD. In the Gospel, all those things which lead to eternal life. χάρις, from which ἐκλογὴ flows, is the goodness of GOD. This benefit was the calling through the Gospel. In Pereck Melek we read the saying of Rabbi Sinai: Of six hundred thousand, only two entered into the land of Canaan: the same will happen in the days of the Messiah.

The Apostle is not speaking of the benefit of calling, but of conversion: for he had taught in the preceding chapter that the calling was universal. But this conversion is of certain remnants of Israel: and the aphorism is known: many are called, few are chosen. Matt. XX. 16, c. XXII. 14. Nor is every benefit of GOD called ἐκλογὴ: but by this, an election made out of grace is noted: which, although it may be diverse, does not however extend itself to all benefits. The Apostle indicates an ἐκλογὴν or election κατὰ πρόγνωσιν τῆς πίσεως, made according to the foreknowledge of faith, not on account of works or merits, but out of grace, since God chose ὃν προέγνω, whom he foreknew: therefore not by the mere and simple will of GOD: and thus that such also remain from the Israelites, whose faith God foreknew, or whom he saw would believe in Christ, but would not, with the others, stubbornly reject Christ: even if they are only a λεῖμμα, or remnants, like those seven thousand Israelites in the time of Elijah. For he said that the Apostle called it an election of grace, because it was not made with a view to works, but to faith alone, or on account of Christ, apprehended by faith, in which one man ἐν χάριτι καὶ ἠγαπημένῳ ἐχαρίτωσεν ἡμᾶς Rom. V. 15, Eph. I. 6, and thus ἐξελέξατο ἐν ἀυτῷ πρὸ καταβολῆς κόσμυ v. 14. The saying of Sinai deserves no applause; for it does not agree with the Prophetic oracles concerning the conversion of many to the Lord in the time of the Messiah, and concerning the inheritance of the ends of the earth to be given to Christ, Ps. II, Ps. LXXII, Ps. CX, Is. II, Dan. VII, Zech. IX and XV, etc., nor were few saved in the days of the Messiah, with the Apostles being sent out primarily into the whole world, so far is it from the case that that comparison of two to six hundred thousand should be admitted; which indeed, even if we stop within the Israelites, leaves little or no hope for the Jews, to whom, however, the Apostle teaches here that hope remains.

Latin:

V. 5. οὕτως ἐν τῷ νῦν καιρῷ λεῖμμα κατ᾽ ἐκλογὴν χάριτος γέγονεν. Id est, communi vitiositati Judæorum erepti sunt pauci beneficio profecto ex summa Dei bonitate. λεῖμμα est שאר vel שריד quod & κατάλειμμα supra IX. 27. pauci de multis, ἐκλογὴ est quodvis DEI beneficium. In Evangelio omnia ea, quæ ad æternam vitam ducunt. χάρις, unde fluit ἐκλογὴ, est DEI bonitas. Hoc beneficium, fuit vocatio per Evangelium. In Pereck Melek legimus dictum Rabbini Sinai: In terram Canaan introierunt de sexcentis millibus bini tantum: idem fiet in diebus Messiæ.

Non de beneficio vocationis, sed conversionis loquitur Apostolus: nam vocationem universalem fuisse cap. præced. docuerat. Conversio autem hæc reliquiarum quarundam est Israëlis: & notus est aphorismus: multi sunt vocati, pauci electi. Matth. XX. 16. c. XXII. 14. Neque omne DEI beneficium ἐκλογὴ dicitur: sed per hanc electio è gratia facta notatur: quæ etsi diversa sit, non tamen ad omnia beneficia sese extendit. Apostolus indicat ἐκλογὴν vel electionem κατὰ πρόγνωσιν τῆς πίσεως secundum prævisionem fidei factam non propter opera vel merita, sed ex gratiâ quandoquidem elegisse Deum ὃν προέγνω, quem prævidit: non ergò merâ & simplici DEI voluntate: itaque tales etiam ex Israëlitis superesse, quorum fidem Deus præviderit, vel quos viderit in Christum credituros, non verò cum cæteris Christum pervicaciter reprobaturos: etsi λεῖμμα tantùm sint, vel reliquiæ, uti septem millia illa Israëlitarum tem- pore Eliæ. Electionem enim gratiæ dixisse Aposto- lum, quod non facta sit intuitu operum, sed fidei solius, vel propter Christum, fide apprehensum, in quo uno homine ἐν χάριτι καὶ ἠγαπημένῳ ἐχαρί- τωσεν ἡμᾶς Rom. V. 15. Eph. I. 6. adeoque ἐξελέξατο ἐν ἀυτῷ πρὸ καταβολῆς κόσμυ v. 14. Dictum Sinaï nullum meretur applausum; nam nec Propheticis id convenit oraculis de conversione plurimorum ad Dominum Messiæ tempore, deque hæreditate finium terræ Christo dandâ Psal. II. Psal. LXXII. Ps. CX. Es. II. Dan. VII. Zach. IX. & XV. &c. ne- que pauci in diebus Messiæ servati sunt, emissis im- primis Apostolis in totum terrarum orbem, tan- tum abest, ut illa comparatio duorum ad sexcenta millia admittenda sit; quæ profectò etiamsi sista- mus intra Israëlitas, Judæis spem exiguam relin- quit, aut nullam, quibus tamen spem restare Apo- stolus hic docet.

## 11:6
V. 6. εἰ δὲ χάριτι ὀυκ ἔτι ἐξ ἔργων.

That is, so that the benefit might be more distinguished, God had done this even for those whose pious deeds had not preceded. Men of a life previously flagitious were called and obeyed no less than those who had lived more uprightly.

ἐπεὶ ἡ χάρις ὀυκ ἔτι γίνεται χάρις.

This is said comparatively. A benefit can also be conferred upon those who work, but then the magnitude of the benefit appears less; it is an oxymoron. But it is not the same thing that is treated here, and what was treated above at the beginning of chapter IV; there it was about the effects of righteousness, here about the causes: there it is λογίζεται κατὰ χάριν. Here λεῖμμα χάριτι γέγονε. Indeed, eternal life is also there a χάρισμα VI. 23; thus we receive χάριν ἀντὶ χάριτος John I. 16.

εἰ δὲ ἐξ ἔργων ὀυκ ἔτι ἐστὶ χάρις, ἐπεὶ τὸ ἔργον ὀυκ ἔτι εστὶν ἔργον.

These are rightly missing in the Manuscript, nor does the Latin interpreter read them, nor Origen, nor Ambrose, nor Chrysostom.

The Apostle teaches with care that election is gratuitous, and not made in view of works or merits: so that we may understand that justification and salvation also are obtained gratuitously, χωρὶς ἔργων without our works and merits. And therefore that ἀντίθεσις is not superfluous or surreptitious, as Grotius wishes with certain Papists, which Theophylact, Oecumenius, as also the Heidelberg and English editions of Chrysostom, and also Photius and the Greek Scholia have, but added for the sake of greater βεβαιώσεως, which, since according to Salmeron and Cajetan it contributes to the integrity of the Apostle's discourse, could more easily have fallen out of one or two codices than be foisted into countless others. The authority of one M.S. is certainly not so great that we should desert the others: which Beza observes are read with the greatest consensus, with the exception of the Claromontanus alone, along with that Syriac version: to which it also (and not undeservedly) seems clearly necessary for completing the antithesis of works and faith, so much so that hardly any testimony is found more clearly, by which every opinion of merit is once and for all removed, since the Apostle expressly denies that a work is a work, which avails from grace and not from debt. Rashly, therefore, are those things restricted to prevenient grace; since in the whole business of salvation the Apostle wishes no place to be left for our works, neither for obtaining the grace of justification, nor for attaining eternal glory: nor would grace in any way be grace, if it were not gratuitous in every way, if we were chosen from foreseen works, even in the smallest part, just as a work would not be a work, if it required the help of grace in any way. These are also ineptly restricted to the Israelites of that time, since they were spoken generally about an entirely gratuitous election, even if on the occasion of a dissertation concerning the remnant of the Israelites κατ᾽ ἐκλογὴν χάριτος. Which grace of election, however, does not exclude the πρόγνωσιν of faith, inasmuch as the Apostle has hitherto demonstrated that it is necessary for justification and salvation and without which no one can be justified and saved: nor does God otherwise justify or save us in time than He chose us for salvation from eternity, since the decree and the execution of the decree ought to harmonize and agree exactly. Nor indeed does the Apostle treat here of calling, but of election; not that those who were called, whose pious deeds had not preceded, were not also called, but he teaches that election and therefore also justification was and is done without regard to works. That these things are said comparatively is no indication. For it is not about benefits in general, of which it is undoubted that some can be conferred upon those who work, but about the grace of election, which excludes works entirely. And it is the same grace of which the Apostle had treated in chapter IV: where it is not about the effects of justice but its causes, and τὸ λογίζεται κατὰ χάριν excludes all works from our justification and salvation, and leaves no parts for them, just as works are entirely excluded here from the causes of election, when ἐκλογὴ χάριτος is explained: if by grace, not by works, otherwise grace would not be grace. The Apostle does not by any means signify by these words: that the benefit might be more distinguished, he called even those from the Jews whose pious deeds had not preceded, as Grotius perverts it: but he explains in what sense and why he called the remnant of the Israelites λῖμμα, κατ' ἐκλογὴν χάριτος, namely so that it might be established (which is what the Apostle primarily proposed to teach) that salvation is not obtained from works, but from grace, whether you look at the Israelites or the Gentiles: since even those remnants of Israel are chosen only by grace, and saved only by grace. Therefore, after he had said they were chosen by grace, he adds: But if by grace, then certainly not by works; otherwise grace would not be grace. But that the Apostle rises from that hypothesis of the saved remnants of the Israelites and of election to the universal genus of justification and salvation, he both teaches that there is an ὁμογένειαν in the whole business of justification and salvation, and openly confirms the exact ἀρμονίαν of our election and justification. Which observation has a notable use against the Calvinists. Furthermore, since the Apostle opposes grace diametrically to works proceeding from man, by the word grace nothing proceeding from man can be signified, but what descends solely from GOD, namely gratuitous favor and mere mercy. It is therefore entirely frivolous that the Papists interpret grace as infused qualities and the newness of life engendered by the Holy Spirit. For the works of the reborn are works nonetheless, and they come under the same complex of genus as any other works. And yet the Apostle distinguishes not some works, but indefinitely all, ἀντιδιηρημένως against grace. Therefore, works, whatever they may be, can in no way come under the complex of grace, as B. Mylius rightly gathers. It is likewise gathered, with him observing, so that I may add this for the sake of the new Majorists and Syncretists, I point to the Calixtines, what is to be thought of their pernicious mixture, who in the business of salvation institute a coupling of works with grace, prattling that we are justified (or saved) partly by the mercy of GOD, partly by our own powers: partly by the λύτρῳ of Christ: partly by our merits: partly by faith: partly by works of charity, these things are clearly ἀσύστατα, and, as Paul testifies, contradictory. For grace is not grace in any way, unless it is gratuitous in every way, as Augustine speaks somewhere, and as Bernard says: Whatever you attribute to merits is lacking to grace. I do not want, therefore, a merit that excludes grace.

ret. The same sense as above IX. 31. But he does not find here the cause why it did not attain, which must be sought from IX. 31. and X. 3.

ἡ δὲ ἐκλογὴ ἐπέτυχεν. Ἡ ἐκλογὴ here stands for ἐκλεκτοὶ, just as we had περιτομὴν above and δικαιοσύνην for the circumcised and for the just. Thus also Daniel said XI. 15. מבחרוו, that is, ἐκλογὰς ἀυτῶν for chosen men. But ἐκλεκτοὶ are to be understood with effect, as κλητοὶ above, those to whom the greatest benefits from GOD have accrued, and who have not neglected to use them.

ὁι δὲ λοιποὶ ἐπωρώθησαν. The rest, who spurned this benefit, hardened, that is, not only did they not cast off their vices, but they became even worse, which appeared most of all from their cruelty toward Christians. Πωρῶν, the same as σκληρύνειν. John XI. 40. 1 Cor. II. 14. whence πώρωσις below 25. Elsewhere πώρωσις signifies slowness in understanding something. The Hebrew כהה is translated by πωρῶν, elsewhere by βαρύνειν, concerning which word see above IX. 17. elsewhere by ἐκτυφλῶν.

These things are foreign to the Apostolic treatment. The question is not whether those very people who were once loved are now despised by GOD? but why most Israelites are excluded from salvation, with only certain others attaining salvation? The Apostle teaches that most were not excluded by an absolute hatred of God, but that, just as election was made κατὰ πρόγνωσιν of faith, so the Israelites were reprobated because of unbelief. Therefore, he does not dissimulate or keep silent about the cause, but points it out, which from the collation of the above, because these explain each other, the reception and rejection of the justice of Christ, and also faith and ἀπισία or unbelief, shines forth more clearly. The cause of hardening also was not some absolute hatred of God, but the ἀπισία of the Jews and the rejection of the Messiah. John XII. 38. 39.

Latin:

V. 6. εἰ δὲ χάριτι ὀυκ ἔτι ἐξ ἔργων.

Id est, quo insignius esset beneficium, fecerat hoc Deus etiam in eos, quorum pia facta non præcesserant. Vocati sunt & paruere non minus homines vitæ ante flagitiosæ, quàm qui emendatius vixerant.

ἐπεὶ ἡ χάρις ὀυκ ἔτι γίνεται χάρις.

Hoc comparativè dictum. Potest & in operantes bene- ficium conferri, sed tunc minus apparet beneficii magni- tudo, est ὀξύμωρον. Non est vero id. m, quod hic tractatur, & quod supra initio capitis IV. ibi de justitiæ effectibus, hic de causis tractatur: ibi λογίζεται κατὰ χάριν. Hic λεῖμ- μα χάριτι γέγονε. Imò & vita æterna ibi χάρισμα VI. 23. ita accipimus χάριν ἀντὶ χάριτος Joh. I. 16

εἰ δὲ ἐξ ἔργων ὀυκ ἔτι ἐστὶ χάρις, ἐπεὶ τὸ ἔργον ὀυκ ἔτι εστὶν ἔργον.

Hæc rectè desunt in Manuscripto, nec legit Latinus inter- pres, sed nec Origenes, nec Ambrosius, nec Chrysostomus.

Gratuitam esse electionem, non verò operum vel meritorum intuitu factam cum cura docet Apostolus: ut justificationem & salvationem et- iam gratuitò, χωρὶς ἔργων sine operibus ac meritis nostris obtingere intelligamus. Ideoque non su- perflua est illa ἀντίθεσις aut irreptitia, uti cum Pa- pistis quibusdam vult Grotius, quam Theophylactus, Oecumenius, ut & editio Heidelb. & Anglic. Chry- sost. nec non Photius & Scholia Græca habent, sed majoris βεβαιώσεως causâ addita, quæ cum juxta Salmer. & Cajet. ad integritatem sermonis Apost. faciat excidisse faciliùs potuit uno atque altero co- dice, quàm innumeris aliis ingeri. Unius M. S. autoritas profectò tanti non est, ut cæteros de- seramus: quos summo consensu, uno Claromon- tano excepto, cum Syriacâ versione illa legere ob- servat Beza: cui etiam ea (nec immeritò) planè necessaria videtur explendæ operum & fidei an- tithesi adeò quidem, ut vix ullum inveniatur aper- tiùs testimonium, quo omnis opinio meriti semel tol- latur, quum disertè neget Apostolus, opus esse opus, quod ex gratia valeat non ex debito. Temere er- gò illa restringuntur ad gratiam prævenientem; quum in toto salutis negotio nullum operibus nostris, neque ad obtinendam justificationis gra- tiam, neque ad consequendam æternam gloriam locum relictum velit Apostolus: nec gratia ullo modo esset gratia, si non gratuita esset omni mo- do, si ex operibus prævisis eligeremur, vel mini- ma ex parte, sicuti neque opus esset opus, si gra- tiæ subsidium ullo modo requireret. Inepte etiam restringuntur hæc ad Israëlitas istius temporis, quum generaliter dicta sint de electione prorsus gratuitâ, etsi occasione dissertationis de reliquiis Israëlitarum κατ᾽ ἐκλογὴν χάριτος. Quæ tamen electionis gratia non excludit fidei πρόγνωσιν, ut- pote quam necessariam esse ad justificationem & salutem & sine quâ justificari ac salvari neminem posse, hactenus demonstravit Apostolus: non ali- ter autem nos Deus justificat aut salvat in tempo- re, quàm elegit nos ad salutem ab æterno, quum decretum & exequutio decreti harmonicè & ex- actè convenire debeant. Neque verò hîc de vo- catione, sed de electione agit Apostolus; non quod vocati etiam illi, quorum pia facta ante non præ- cesserant, sed quod electio adeoque & justifica- tio citra intuitum operum facta sit, & fiat, docet. Comparativè autem hæc dici nullum est indicium. Non enim de beneficiis in genere, quorum non- nulla in operantes conferri posse indubium est, sed de electionis gratia agitur, quæ opera pror- sus excludit. Et eadem est gratia, de qua c. IV. egerat Apostolus: ubi non de justitiæ effectibus sed causis tractatur, & τὸ λογίζεται κατὰ χάριν opera omnia excludit à nostra justificatione & salute, nullasq; illis partes relinquit,æque uti opera pror- sus hîc excluduntur ab electionis causis, cum ἐκ- λογὴ χάριτος explicatur: si ex gratia non ex ope- ribus, alioqui gratia non esset gratia. Non utique hisce verbis id significat Apostolus: quo insignius esset beneficium, vocavit è Judæis etiam eos, quo- rum pia facta non præcesserant, ut pervertit Gro- tius: sed explicat, quo sensu & cur λῖμμα reli- quias Israëlitarum dixerit, κατ' ἐκλογὴν χάριτος, nempè ut constaret, (quod præcipuè Apostolo propositum est docere) salutem non obtingere ex operibus, sed ex gratia sive Israëlitas spectes sive gentiles: siquidem reliquiæ etiâm illæ Israëlis non nisi ex gratia electæ, nonnisi ex gratia salventur. Ideò postquam dixerat ex gratia electas, addit: Si autem ex gratia, utique non ex operibus; alioquin gratia non esset gratia. Quod verò ab hypothesi ista salvatarum reliquiarum Israëlitis, & electionis ad genus universum justificationis & salutis Apo- stolus assurgit, tum ὁμογένειαν esse in justificatio- nis & salutis universo negotio docet, tùm ἀρμο- νίαν exactam electionis & justificationis nostræ apertè confirmat. Quæ observatio insignem con- tra Calvinianos usum habet. Porrò cum gratiam operibus ab homine profectis è diametro oppo- nat Apostolus, gratiæ vocabulo nihil ab homine profectum significari potest, sed quod à DEO uni- cè descendit, nimirum favor gratuitus & mera mi- sericordia. Frivolum ergo plane est, quod gratiam de infusis qualitatibus, & per Spiritum S. ingenera- ta novitate vitæ, interpretantur Pontificii. Nam opera renatorum opera sunt nihilominus, atque sub eundem generis complexum, cum aliis quibusvis operibus veniunt. Atqui opera non quædam, sed indefinitè omnia, contra gratiam ἀντιδιηρημένως Apo- stolus distinguit. Ergo venire sub complexum gra- tiæ opera, qualiacunque tandem illa sunt, nullo modo possunt, ut rectè colligit B. Mylius. Colligitur iti- dem eodem observante, ut id in gratiam Novo- rum Majoristarum & Syncretistarum, Calixtinos indigito, addam, quid de pernitiosa eorum mixtu- ra sentiendum sit, qui in negotio salutis, operum cum gratia copulationem instituentas, partim misericor- dia DEI, partim nostris viribus: partim Christi λύτρῳ: partim nostra meritis: partim fide: par- tim operibus caritatis nos justificari (vel salvari) garriunt, ἀσύστατα sunt hæc planè, & teste Paulo contradictoria. Gratia enim non est gratia ullo mo- do, ni sit gratuita omni modo, ut Augustinus alicubi loquitur, & ut Bernhardus inquit: Deest gratiæ, quidquid meritis deputas. Nolo ergò meritum, quod gratiam excludat.

ret. Idem sensus, qui supra IX. 31. Causam autem, cur non sit assecuta, hic non reperit, quæ petenda est ex IX. 31. & X. 3.

ἡ δὲ ἐκλογὴ ἐπέτυχεν. Ἡ ἐκλογὴ hic pro ἐκλεκτοὶ, quomodo περιτομὴν supra & dicaioσύνην habuimus pro circumcisis & pr. justis. Sic & Daniel dixit XI. 15. מבחרוו, id est, ἐκλογὰς ἀυτῶν pro vi- ris electis. ἐκλεκτοὶ autem sunt cum effectu intelligendi, ut supra κλητοὶ, ii, quibus maxima à DEO beneficia obtigere, quique eis uti non neglexere.

ὁι δὲ λοιποὶ ἐπωρώθησαν. Reliqui, qui hoc beneficium aspernati sunt, induruere, id est, non tantum non exuère vitia, sed & pejores effecti sunt, quod maximè apparuit ex ipsorum in Christianos sævitia. Πωρῶν, idem quod σκληρύνειν. Joh XI. 40. 1. Cor. II. 14. unde πώρωσις infra 25. Alibi πώρωσις tarditatem in re aliqua comprehendenda significat. Hebræum כהה ver- titur per πωρῶν, alibi per βαρύνειν, de quo verbo supra IX. 17. alibi per ἐκτυφλῶν.

Aliena hæc sunt ab Apostolica tractatione. Non quæritur an illi ipsi, qui olim amati fuerint, jam à DEO despecti sint? sed cur Israëlitæ plerique excludantur à salute reliquis solùm quibusdam sa- lutem consequentibus? Non ex absoluto Dei odio exclusos plerosque, sed uti electio facta est κατὰ πρόγνωσιν fidei, ita ob incredulitatem reprobatos esse Israëlitas, docet Apostolus. Causam ergo non dissimulat aut tacet prorsus, sed indigitat, quæ ex collatione superiorum, quia hæc mutuò se expli- cant, justitiæ Christi susceptio, & rejectio, nec non fides & ἀπισία vel incredulitas luculentius efful- get. Indurationis etiam causa non fuit odium Dei quoddam absolutum, sed ἀπισία Judæorum & re- probatio Messiæ. Joh. XII. 38. 39.

## 11:8
V. 8. (καθὼς γέγραπται) Isa. XXIX, 10. ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Θεὸς πνεῦμα κατανύξεως.

He expressed the sense from memory, as often. For in Isaiah the Prophet speaks to the people themselves, and says: πεπότικεν ὑμᾶς κύριος πνεύματι κατανύξεως. The former change is of the less moment, because the Prophet also in the same verse passes from the second person to the third, as other Prophets often do. Nor is the latter of any moment, since to give a Spirit of κατανύξεως is the same as to provide it to be drunk. But κατάνυξις in this place is not from κατανύττειν to prick, whence κατενύγησαν Acts II. 37. but from the old κατανύω. The simple is νύω for νέω, which remained in Latin as nuo, whence nutus and nutare. Hence νύζω, νυσός, and νυσάζω, which is to nod, that is, to shake the head, as is the habit not only of those dozing, and old men, who nod to everything for everyone, as Catullus says, but also those whom a stupor has invaded. The Hebrew noun in Isaiah is תרדמה which Aquila translates as καταφορᾶς, Theodotion as ἐκστάσεως. How the same noun signifies רדם Ps. LXVIII. 29. and 1 Sam. XXVI. 12. תרדמה is translated as θάμβος, and in Joh. IV. 13. & XXXIII. 15. as φόβος. The Hebrew verb also, רדם, from which these nouns have their origin, is translated not only by νυσάζειν, but also by ἀποσκαρίζειν. In Daniel also VIII. 10. & X. 9. by metonymy it signifies to fall, and is translated in the one place by κατανύσσομαι, in the other by πίπτειν, in the same sense. There is therefore a Spirit of κατανύξεως, such a commotion of the mind, which makes men senseless and as it were prostrate, which without doubt happened to many Jews, when that huge army of Sennacherib invaded the land and pitched camp at the city of Jerusalem, of which time Esaias treats: but it is most aptly applied to the Jews themselves, who after they abhorred Christ with his cross, could not know what was true righteousness, and much less attain it; and thus they fell into the most grievous evils, both of this age and of the next.

This passage is relevant here, because it treats not only of that extreme blinding and hardening of the people, which befell them at the coming of the Messiah, so that the prophecies concerning the Messiah were even to them like a sealed book, and the veil of Moses covered their heart, as they were those who clung solely to the law of righteousness, and could not recognize the righteousness of Christ, even though it shines in the oracles of the Old Testament, because of that Mosaic veil, whence the Apostle deduces their πώρωσιν or hardening, as if from its proper cause, 2. Cor. III. 14. but also because it deals with the destruction and confusion of the wisdom of the Pharisees and lawyers and others, and thus their blinding, Is. XXIX. 14. the cause of which was that the infirmity of Christ was a scandal to them, and they would not recognize the Lord in His wisdom, or receive through faith Christ, who is the power of God and the wisdom of God, whom they rather extremely opposed and persecuted, and finally drove to the cross. 1. Cor. I. 18. 19. 24. c. II. 8.

Eyes for not seeing and ears for not hearing.

These things are taken from Isaiah VI. 10. where it is in Greek: they heard heavily with their ears and closed their eyes, lest they should see with their eyes and hear with their ears. That τῶ μὴ βλέπειν is in place of a noun placed in the genitive in the Hebrew manner to signify an adjunct. But it is well ascribed to GOD here, because in Isaiah it is ascribed to the Jews themselves, because, just as Pharaoh first hardened his heart, then God hardened the heart of Pharaoh, so also, for those who did not want to see conspicuous things, the power of judgment is dulled for them in the future as well. We have dealt sufficiently with the passage of Isaiah at Matt. XIII. 14. and Acts XXVIII. 26. Indeed, the matter stands thus: For when the wrath of the gods harms someone, first the good mind is taken away from him, and it turns to a worse opinion, so that he may not know any of the things in which he sins. Using which passage the orator Lycurgus against Socrates says: the gods, he says, do nothing sooner than pervert the mind of wicked men. Velleius Paterculus expressed this sense thus: Indeed, the matter stands so that God generally corrupts the counsels of him whose fortune He is about to change. But Ammianus Marcellinus: The senses of men are wont to be dulled and blunted when the fates are laying their hands upon them. Nor did the ancient Jews think otherwise, as appears also from Philo and Josephus: and Christians. There is an epistle of Cyprian, LV. It is a work of GOD not to understand faults, lest repentance follow. As it is written: And God gave them a spirit of compunction, that they might not return, that is, and be healed, and be cured by prayers and just satisfactions after sins. And in the sermon on the lapsed: Nor let the error of the thoughtless or the vain stupor of some move us, who, when they are held in such a great crime, are struck with blindness of mind, so that they neither understand their faults nor lament them. This is a greater plague of an indignant GOD. Salvian, book VI, on the government of GOD: For their crimes had so preceded all, that they did not even fear their own danger. Captivity was foreknown and was not feared. For fear had been taken away from the sinners, so that there could be no caution. And so, with the barbarians almost in the sight of all, there was no fear of men, no guarding of cities; such was the blindness of minds, or rather of sins, that although without doubt no one wanted to perish, yet no one did anything to prevent perishing.

That prophecy of Isaiah also makes most for the matter here: because he prophesies concerning the extreme times of the Jewish polity, in which God was to be full of glory to the whole world, and St. John explains it concerning the time of Christ, c. XII, and gives the cause, that they would not see with seeing eyes nor hear with hearing ears Christ the King of glory, whose glory Isaiah saw there in c. VI, nor turn themselves to Him, and although many most notable miracles were in their sight, they did not believe in Him, John XII. 37. For St. John teaches that this extreme unbelief of theirs was the cause of their hardening, comparing to that matter especially the prophecies of Isaiah c. LIII. 1. and c. VI. 9. Which the Apostle also deduces in Acts XXVIII. 25 from this Isaianic passage, where, with the Jewish people rejected, the righteousness of God, which we have in Christ, has come to the Gentiles, it being taught that when they would not hear the Gospel concerning Christ, these indeed did hear, verses 25, 28.

ἕως τῆς σήμερον ἡμέρας. This is construed with ἐπωρώθησαν, which had preceded, with the others inserted by way of a parenthesis. Paul added this providently: for God does not harden all whom He hardens forever, but He allows some to sin gravely, or even to fall into dangers, so that He may thus rouse them as if from sleep, and take new trials whether they are willing to accept the good things they neglected. For among those Jews, concerning whom Christ had used this passage of Isaiah in Matt. XIII. 14, Mark IV. 12, Luke VIII. 10, John XII. 40, there were those who, by the conscience of the parricide committed against Christ and the fear of the evils which the Apostles were threatening, received the Gospel previously spurned, Acts II. 37, 38, 39, 40, 41. Speaking of the same hardening, Paul in 2 Cor. III adds ἄχρι τῆς σήμερον and ἕως σήμερον. These things are true concerning the conversion of some of the Jews through the preaching of Peter; but they do not fit this passage. For the Apostle speaks of the Jews who were hardened in his own time; but those who were converted in Peter's Pentecostal sermon were no longer hardened. That ἕως τῆς σήμερον ἡμέρας, therefore, indicates rather that that hardening did not begin recently, but had already lasted a long time, and was not expiring now, but still flourishing: which God was finally to punish with the final destruction of Jerusalem, πανωλεθρίᾳ. Although, however, even among those Jews, of whom the prophecy of Isaiah is cited in John XII, there may perhaps have been some who were converted at the feast of Pentecost, it is not certain that those who were hardened were then converted: and John cited this prophecy in his ἐυαγγελιογραφίᾳ long after the Pentecostal sermon. Moreover, the Apostle uses this in general of most Israelites, that they remain hardened: namely, was not faith foreseen? whom he distinguishes from those hardened ones, as they come under the name of election.

Latin:

V. 8. (καθὼς γέγραπται) Esa. XXIX, 10. ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Θεὸς πνεῦμα κατανύξεως.

Sensum expressit memoriter, ut sæpe. Nam in Esaia ad ipsum populum loquitur Propheta, & ait: πεπότικεν ὑμᾶς κύριος πνεύματι κατανύξεως. Prior mutatio eò minoris mo- menti, quod & Propheta eodem commate à secunda persona in tertiam transit, ut & alii Prophetæ sæpè. Nec altera ullius est momenti, cum dare Spiritum κατανύξεως idem sit quod eum porandum præbere. Est autem κατάνυξις hoc lo- co non à κατανύττειν pungere, unde κατενύγησαν Act. II. 37. sed à veteri κατανύω. Simplex est νύω pro νέω, quod in La- tinis mansit nuo, unde nutus & nutare. Hinc νύζω, νυσός, & νυσάζω, quod est nutare, id est, caput concutere, ut solent non tantùm dormitantes, & senes, qui Omnia omnibus annuunt, ut ait Catullus, verum etiam quos invasit stupor. Nomen Hebræum in Esaia est תרדמה quod Aquila vertit κατα- φορᾶς Theodotion ἐκστάσεως. Quomodo idem nomen va- lens רדם Pf. LXVIII. 29. & 1. Sam. XXVI. 12. תרדמה vertitur θάμβος, & Joh. IV. 13. & XXXIII. 15. φόβος. Verbum quoque Hebræum רדם unde istis nominibus origo, vertitur non modò per νυσάζειν, sed & per ἀποσκα-ρίζειν. In Daniele etiam VIII. 10. & X. 9. per μετωνυμίαν significat cadere, vertiturque altero loco per κατανύσσομαι, altero per πίπτειν, sensu eodem. Est ergò Spiritus κατανύ- ξεως talis animi commotio, quæ homines vecordes ac velut extensos facit, quod multis haud dubiè evenit Judæis, cum ingens ille Sennacheribi exercitus terram invasit & ad ur- bem Hierosolyma castra posuit, de quo tempore agit Esa- ias: sed optimè id ipsum aptatur Judæis, qui postquam Christum cum sua cruce exhorruerunt, quæ esset vera ju- stitia cognoscere, multoque magis eam adipisci nequive- re; ac sic in gravissima mala, tum hujus, tum alterius se- culi inciderunt.

ctus hîc locus ille est, quia non tantùm de extrema illa excæcatione, & induratione populi tractat, quæ obtigit ei sub adventum Messiæ, adeò ut vaticinia de Messia etiam fuerint eidem instar libri obsignati, & velum Mosis cor eorum operuerit, utpote qui soli legis justitiæ inhærebant, & justitiam Christi, et- si in oraculis V. Test. fulgeat, cognoscere nequi- bant, ob velum illud Mosaicum, unde πώρωσιν vel indurationem eorum, tanquam à causa pro- pria deducit Apostolus, 2. Cor. III. 14. sed etiam quia de sapientiæ Pharisæorum & legisperitorum, aliorumque interitu & confusione, adeoque ex- cæcatione eorum agitur, Es. XXIX. 14. cujus cau- sa fuit, quod scandalo ipsis esset infirmitas Christi, nec agnoscere Dominum voluerint in Sapientia sua, vel Christum, qui est Dei virtus, & Dei Sapi- entia per fidem suscipere, quem potius ipsi extre- mè aversati & persequuti sunt, tandemque in cru- cem egerunt. 1. Cor. I. 18. 19. 24. c. II. 8.

Ὀφθαλμὺς τῶ μὴ βλέπειν καὶ ὦτα τῶ μὴ ἀκύειν.

Depromta hæc ex Esaïæ VI. 10. ubi est in Græco: τοῖς ὠσὶν αὐτῶν βαρέως ἤκυσαν κὰι τὺς ὀφθαλμὺς ἐκάμμυσαν, μή- ποτε ἴδωσι τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς κὰι τοῖς ὡσὶν αὐτῶν ἀκύσωσι. Illud τῶ μὴ βλέπειν est vice nominis in genitivo positi more Hebræo ad significationem adjuncti. Benè autem DEO hîc adscribitur, quod in Esaïa ipsis Judæis, quia, sicut Pha- rao prius induravit cor suum, deinde Deus cor Pharaonis, ita &, qui videre conspicua noluerunt, eis in posterum et- iam judicii vis hebetatur. De loco Esaïæ satis egimus ad Matth. XIII. 14. & Act. XVIII. 6. Nimirum ita se res habet: Ὄταν γὰρ ὀργὴ δαιμόνων βλάπτῃ τίνα, Τύτῳ τὸ πρῶτον ἐξαφαιρῖται φρενῶν Τὸν νῦν τὸν ἐσθλὸν, ἐὶς δὲ τὴν χείρω τρέπει Γνώμην, ἵν' εἰ δῇ μηδὲν ὧν ἁμαρτάνει' Quo loco utens Lycurgus Orator contra Socratem: οἱ θεοὶ, inquit, ὐδὲν πρότερον ποιῦσιν ἢ τῶν πονηρῶν ἀνθρώπων τὴν διάνοιαν παράγυσι. Quem sensum sic expressit Velle- jus Paterculus: Quippe ita se res habet, ut plerumque cui for- tunam mutaturns est Deus consilia corrumpat. Ammianus verò Marcellinus: Solent manum injectantibus fatis hebcta- vi sensus hominum & obtundi. Nec aliter sensere Judæi veteres, ut ex Philone etiam & Josepho apparet: & Chri- stiani. Cypriani est Epistola LV. Ine est DEI non intelligere delicta, ne sequatur pœnitentia. Sicut scriptum est: Et dedit illis Deus spiritum transpunctionis, ne revertartur scilicet & curentur, & deprecationibus & satisfactionibus justis post pec- cata sanentur. Et sermone de lapsis: Nec nos quorundam moveat aut error improvidiis, aut stupor vanus, qui cum te- nentur in tam grandi crimine, percussi sunt animi cæcitate, ut nec intelligant delicta nec plangant. Indignantis DEI ma- jor hæc plaga est. Salvianus lib. VI. de gubernatione DEI: Nam ita cunctos crimina sua præcesserunt, ut nec metuerent periculum suum. Prænoscebatur captivitas nec formidabatur. Ablatus quippe erat à peccatoribus timor, ne posset esse cautela. Itaque barbaris penè in conspectu omnium sitis, nullus metus erat hominum, non custodia civitatum, tanta animorum, vel tanta potius peccatorum cæcitas fuit, ut cum absque dubio nul- lus perire vellet, nullus tamen id ageret, ne periret.

Illud etiam Esaïæ vaticinium maximè ad rem hîc facit: quia de extremis temporibus politia Ju- daica, quibus gloriâ Deus plenus erat futurus uni- versis orbis, vaticinatur, & de tempore Christi ex- plicat id S. Joh. c. XII. causamque reddit, quod Re- gem gloriæ Christum, cujus gloriam Esaias ibi vi- dit c. VI. oculis videntibus non videre, auribus au- dientibus non audire voluerint, nec sese ad ipsum convertere, & quanquam multa maximè insignia miracula in conspectu ipsorum fuerint, in ipsum tamen non crediderint Joh. XII. 37. Nam hanc ἀπισίαν eorum extremam causam fuisse indura- tionis eorum S. Johannes docet, in eam rem im- primis vaticinia Esaïæ c. LIII. 1. & c. VI. 9. con- ferens. Quod etiam Apostolus Act. XXIX. 25. ex hoc loco Esaiano deducit, ubi, cor populo Ju- daico reprobato, gentibus justitia Dei, quam in Christo habemus, obtigerit, doceri quum illi au- dire noluerint Evangelium de Christo, hæ verò audierint vers. 25. 28.

ἕως τῆς σήμερον ἡμέρας. Construitur hoc cum ἐπωρώθησαν, quod præcesserat, cæteris per παραθήκης modum interjectis. Provide hoc addidit Paulus: non enim omnes, quos indurat Deus, in perpetuum indurat, sed quosdam gravia peccare, aut et- iam in pericula incidere sinit, ut sic eos velut ex somno excitet, novaque experimenta capiat, an bona neglecta ac- cipere velint. Nam inter illos Judæos, de quibus hunc Esaiæ locum usurpaverat Christus Matth. XIII. 14. Marc. VI. 12. Luc. VIII. 10. Joh. XII. 40. fuêre illi, qui conscien- tia parricidii in Christum commissi & metu malorum, quæ Apostoli minabantur, Evangelium prius spretum recepêre Act. II. 37. 38. 39. 40. 41. De eadem obduratione loquens Paulus 2. Cor. III. addit ἄχρι τὸ σήμερον & ἕως σήμερον. Vera hæc sunt de Judæorum quorundam per concionem Petri conversione; sed loco huic non congruunt. Nam de Judæis suo tempore obtu- ratis loquitur Apostolus; Illi verò, qui in con- cione Petri Pentecostali conversi sunt, non erant amplius indurati. Illud ergò ἕως τῆς σήμερον ἡμέ- ρας id potius indicat, non nuper cœpisse, sed jam durasse diu, non expirare nunc, sed vigere adhuc illam indurationem: quam Deus πανωλεθρίᾳ finali Hierosolymitana tandem puniturus erat. Quan- quam verò etiam inter illos Judæos, de quibus Joh. XII. Esaiæ vaticinium adhibetur, nonnulli fortassis fuerint in festo Pentecostes conversi, ipsos tamen induratos tum conversos fuisse, non constat: & adhibuit Johannes hoc vaticinium in sua ἐυαγγελιογραφίᾳ longè post Pentecostalem concionem. Cæterum in genere id usurpat Apo- stolus de plerisque Israelitis, quod indurati per- maneant: Num sc. fides prævisa non fuit? quos ab induratis illis discriminat, utpote qui ἐκλογῆς nomine veniunt.

## 11:9
V. 9. And David says, Let their table be made a snare, and a trap, and a stumbling block, and a recompense unto them. Concerning a similar kind of men, namely, Ps. LXIX. 23. in the Greek there: Let their table be made before them a snare and a recompense and a stumbling block. Which agree very well with the Hebrew, except that there it is the future יִהְיֶה, but which is often taken among the Hebrews for the precative. Moreover, שְׁלוֹמִים is rightly translated ἀνταπόδομα or ἀνταπόδοσις, just as interpreters very often translate שׁלם as ἀποδιδόναι. Paul, as is the custom of those who cite something from memory, expressed the sense well, and most of the words, though not scrupulously. For first he omits ἐνώπιον ἀυτῶν, which is usually added to the table, as in Ps. XXIII. 5. Ezech. XXIII. 41. Then after εἰς παγίδα he adds κᾐ εἰς θήραν, that is, a capture, which is made by a snare, so that what is signified here by a snare may be more easily understood. For ἀνταπόδοσιν he put ἀνταπόδομα, and inverted the order, placing εἰς σκάνδαλον before it. David speaks of the same people as in Ps. XLI. 10, who, although they had been so familiar to him that they daily attended his banquets, had foully slandered him to Saul and had plotted his destruction. From the spirit of the law, he wishes them like for like. And by the table, he understands the participants of the table by metonymy. He wishes, therefore, that their friends and guests may deceive them, so that they may find what they had done to David, and thus stumble into the evils which are σκάνδαλα to our Hellenists. In a mystical sense, the table can be understood as the altar, Malach. I. 7, and by the altar, synecdochically, the temple, in which, when it was set on fire, many Jews partly perished in the flames and were partly captured.

The Holy Psalmist does not prophesy concerning a similar kind of men, but concerning the Israelites of the New Testament time who were to be punished for the cause of the parricide committed against Christ: whose words, even if the Apostle does not bring them in word for word, it must be believed that this was done on purpose, as the Holy Spirit dictated as it pleased Him, and not because the Apostle did not hold all the words precisely in his memory; for the holy men of God wrote moved by the Holy Spirit and from θεοπνευστία, what they wrote, not from memory, which is often fallible and untrustworthy. But that is not to be endured, nor is it said without insult to the Holy Spirit, that David, from the spirit of the law, wished like for like upon the enemies who had slandered him to Saul and had plotted his destruction. Who that spirit of the law is, from Holy Scripture it had to be taught: which v. knows only one Spirit, by whom the faithful are governed: nor is it fitting for David, who brought these things forth by divine inspiration, to repay evil with evil, and to wish for the like to those seeking his own destruction. For this is contrary to the divine law: which commands to forgive, and to do good to enemies, and to pray for them, not to imprecate evils upon them. Nor is this a wish, but a Prophecy, and a prediction: and since it is in the future in the Hebrew text, the text of the Apostle must be explained from that, inasmuch as the Optative is interchanged with the future indicative: because, what the Prophets predict, GOD signs with His divine FIAT, so that we may be certain that it will be fulfilled, and will indubitably come to pass. The Apostle therefore takes for a fact, (as here B. Mylius p. 365.) what Christ had once predicted would happen through an imprecation, relying on this principle, because that which Christ once imprecated cannot but come to pass. But again he makes a conjecture from the punishment concerning sin in the previous verse. Their table is turned into a snare, a trap, a ruin, that is, all their institutions, benefits, and privileges, tend to their own destruction. Therefore they suffer nothing but the punishment of hardening. For we use tables, not only to receive from them the blessing of food and nourishment; but also to transact any business of our calling. Whatever, therefore, they may do in all things, whatever they may undertake, he indicates that it results in their own destruction, so that they may perceive death from that source from which they could have perceived life: darkness, from where they could have had light: in short, that they may experience as many destructions as the heap of benefits had been prepared for their salvation. In the other verse, the darkening of the eyes is put for blindness of mind, the shaking of the loins or the bending of the back, for the weakening of strength, so that they are said to be at once deprived of reason and intelligence, and utterly enervated in strength. For these two are the aids for doing things rightly, first that counsel may shine forth; then that the ability to execute what you have well deliberated may be at hand. To be deprived of both of these is most certainly to be in a most unhappy state. But we have taught in the annotations on Ps. LXIX. that David is not speaking of himself, but rather introducing Christ prophesying concerning His own passion. Which is also evident concerning Ps. XLI. 10. from the collation of Job XIII. 18. Acts I. 6.

Latin:

V. 9. καὶ Δαβὶδ λέγει, γενηθήτω ἡ τράπεζα ἀυτῶν εἰς παγίδα, καὶ εἰς θήραν, κᾐ εἰς σκάνδαλον, εἰς ἀνταπόδομα ἀυτοῖς. De simili scilicet hominum genere Ps. LXIX. 23. in Græ- co ibi: γενηθήτω ἡ τράπεζα ἀυτῶν ἐνώπιον ἀυτῶν εἰς παγίδα καὶ εἰς ἀνταπόδοσιν καὶ εἰς σκάνδαλον. Quæ optimè cum He- bræo conveniunt, nisi quod ibi est futurum יִהְיֶה sed quod sæpe apud Hebræos sumitur pro precativo. שְׁלוֹמִים autem rectè vertitur ἀνταπόδομα vel ἀνταπόδοσις, sicut & in- terpretes שׁלם sæpissimè vertunt ἀποδιδόναι. Paulus, ut solent, qui memoriter aliquid citant, sensum benè expres- sit, & verba pleraque non tamen scrupulosè. Nam pri- mum omittit ἐνώπιον ἀυτῶν, quod solet addi mensæ, ut Psal. XXIII. 5. Ezech. XXIII. 41. Deinde post εἰς παγίδα addit κᾐ εἰς θήραν, id est, capturam, quæ fit per laqueum, ut faci- lius intelligatur id, quod hic significatur per laqueum. Pro ἀνταπόδοσιν posuit ἀνταπόδομα, & ordinem invertit, præponens illud εἰς σκάνδαλον. Loquitur David de iisdem, de quibus Ps. XLI. 10. qui cum adeò familiares ipsi fuissent, ut quotidiè conviviis ipsius interessent, ipsum apud Sau- lem fœdè calumniati erant, pernitiemque ei struxerant. Eis ex spiritu legis optat paria. Et per mensam intelligit mensæ participes per μετωνυμίαν. Optat igitur, ut amici & convivæ eorum eos decipiant, ut quod Davidi fecerant, ipsi inveniant & sic impingant in mala, quæ nostris Helleni- stis σκάνδαλα. Mystico sensu mensa potest intelligi altare, Malach. I. 7. & per altare συνεκδοχικῶς templum, quo in- censo multi Judæi partim flammis interiere, partim capti sunt.

Non de simili hominum genere, sed de Israeli- tis tempore N. T. parricidii in Christum commissi causâ puniendis vaticinatur Hiero-Psaltes: cujus verba etsi non κατὰ πόδα adducat Apostolus, id tamen de industria factum esse credendum est, ita dictante Spiritu S. prout ipsi placuit, non verò quod memoriâ haud tenuerit præcisè omnia ver- ba Apostolus; scripsêre enim sancti Dei homi- nes agitati à Spiritu S. & ex θεοπνευστίᾳ, quæ scri- psêre, non ex memoria, quæ sæpè labilis & infida est. Id verò ferendum non est, nec citra contu- meliam in Spiritum S. dicitur, quod David inimi- cis, qui eum apud Saulem calumniati erant, & per- nitiem ipsi struxerant, ex Spiritu legis paria opta- rit. Quisnam ille Spiritus legis sit, è Scriptura S. docendum erat: quæ v. nonnisi unum Spiritum, quo fideles gubernantur, novit: nec Davidi, qui hæc ex inspiratione divina protulit, convenit, ma- la malis rependere, & pernitiem sui quærentibus paria optare. Hoc enim legi divinæ adversum est: quæ condonare jubet, ac benefacere inimicis, atque orare pro ipsis, non imprecari iisdem mala. Neque votum hoc est, sed Prophetia, & vaticinium: & quum futurum in Ebræo textu sit, explicandus inde textus est Apostoli, siquidem permutetur Optativus cum futuro indicativo: quia, quod prædicunt Prophetæ, DEUS divino suo FIAT sub- signat, ut certi simus, id impletum iri, atque indu- bitatò futurum. Sumit ergò Apostolus pro facto, (ut hic B. Mylius p. 365.) quod futurum olim per imprecationem Christus prædixerat, eo nixus prin- cipio, quia non possit non fieri, quod semel Christus imprecatus fuit. Iterum autem ex pœna de pecca- to in priori versu conjecturam facit. Mensa ipso- rum versa est in laqueum, pedicam, ruinam, id est, omnia instituta, beneficia, privilegia, ipsis vergunt in exitium. Ergò non nisi indurationis pœnam pa- tiuntur. Mensis enim utimur, non tantum ad ac- cipiendam inde victus atque alimoniæ benedictio- nem; sed expedienda etiam negotia quævis vocatio- nis nostræ. Quidquid ergò agant illi rerum omni- um, quidquid capessant, in exitium ipsis cedere in- dicat, ut mortem inde sentiant, unde poterant vi- tam percipere: tenebras, unde lucem: denique toti- dem exitia experiantur, quatenus beneficiorum cu- mulus paratus ipsis in salutem fuerat. In altero versu obscuratio oculorum, pro cæcitate mentis, nu- tatio lumborum seu inflexio dorsi, pro labefactatione virium ponitur, ut simul & ratione atque intelligen- tia privati, & viribus enervati prorsus esse dican- tur. Hæc enim duo rerum rectè gerendarum adju- menta sunt, primum ut præluceat consilium; tum ut in promptu sit facultas exequendi, quæ probè con- sulueris. Quo utroque orbatus, in statu infelicissimo versari est certissimum. Non autem Davidem de se loqui, sed introducere potius Christum de pas- sione sua vaticinantem in annot. ad Ps. LXIX. do- cuimus. Quod etiam de Ps. XLI. 10. è collatione Job. XIII. 18. Act. I. 6. constat.

## 11:10
V. 10. Let their eyes be darkened that they may not see. That is, until they may not see. But this is wont to be said of grave miseries, as can be seen in Lam. V. 17. And this, and what follows, clearly corresponds to the Greek of the LXX interpreters.

and bow down their back always. מתניהם properly signifies their loins, but because of proximity that name is also wont to be put for the back, as in Psalm LXVI. 10. thou hast laid afflictions upon our back. That σύγκαμψον is put for the Hebrew המעד which is to move and also to weary. For Aquila translates מעד as ὁ ἀκριβαστὴς, to be weak, to fail. But to bow the back has the same value as to weary: for by both is signified the imposition of heavy burdens, and through that, servitude, such as happened to countless Jews through Titus.

Therefore the Psalm treats of these punishments of the Jews not mystically, but according to the letter. Which the Apostle has most appropriately cited, because in the same place it treats of the punishments which Christ sustained for us, paying for those things which He did not take away v. 5., and the intercession of Christ for the faithful is introduced, by which He sought that they be freed from eternal confusion on account of His merit, v. 7. 8. but to the hardened, such as were especially those who had driven Him to the cross, and there had given Him gall and vinegar to drink v. 22., He threatened and predicted eternal destruction v. 25. because they are not to arrive at the righteousness of GOD, nor are they to be inscribed with the righteous in the book of life v. 28. 29. The cause therefore of their ruin and destruction is ἀπισία and unbelief, and not indeed the absolute will of GOD.

PART II. APOLOGETICO-PARÆNETICA, For the grace of God toward the Israelites, which the Gentiles ought especially to acknowledge humbly in themselves.

Latin:

V. 10. σκοτισθήτωσαν ὁι ὀφθαλμοὶ ἀυτῶν τῶ μὴ βλέπειν. Id est, ἕως τῶ μὴ βλέπειν. Solet autem hoc dici de gra- vibus miseriis, ut videre est Lam. V. 17. Et hoc, & quod sequitur, planè Græco interpretum LXX. respondet.

καὶ τὸν νῶτον ἀυτῶν διὰ παντὸς σύγκαμψον. מתניהם propriè lumbos eorum significat, sed ob vi- cinitatem solet id nomen & pro dorso poni, ut Psal. LXVI. 10. έθου θλίψεις ἐπὶ τὸν νῶτον ἡμῶν. Illud σύγκαμψον posi- tum est pro Hebræo המעד quod est commovere atque et- iam lassare. Nam מעד Aquila ὁ ἀκριβαστὴς vertit, ἀτονεῖν, facessere. Idem autem valet curvare dorsum, quod las- sare: utroque enim significatur onerum gravium impositio, & per id servitus, qualis innumeris Judæorum evenit per Titum.

De his ergò pœnis Judæorum non mysticè, sed secundum literam Psalmus agit. Quem conve- nientissimè adduxit Apostolus, quia in eodem de pœnis, quas Christus pro nobis sustinuit persol- vens ea, quæ non rapuit v. 5. agitur, & intercessio Christi pro fidelibus introducitur, quà propter meritum suum eos à confusione æterna liberari petiit, v. 7. 8. induratis autem, quales imprimis erant ii, qui ipsum in crucem egerant, ibique felle & aceto potarant v. 22. minatus est, & prædixit æternum exitium v. 25. quod perventuri non sint ad justitiam DEI, nec cum justis inscribendi sint in librum vitæ v. 28. 29. Causa ergò interitûs & exitii eorum est ἀπισία & incredulitas, non verò absoluta DEI voluntas.

PARS II. APOLOGETICO-PARÆNETICA, Pro gratia Dei erga Israelitas, quam agnoscere in sese imprimis debeant humiliter gentiles.

## 11:11
V. 11. I say then.

The same locution, which is above 1. Do I say this, which is imputed to me?

Did they stumble that they should fall?

Do I say they have so stumbled that they fall, that is, that they remain in a fall: for words are often taken in the sense of duration. Πταίειν מכשול is usually used of one who is pushed, but נפל, which is translated by πίπτειν, often has the meaning of lying down, as when it is said in Rev. XVIII. 2. ἔπεσεν ἔπεσε, that is, he lies flat: and therefore κατακλίνεσθαι is used for it in Exod. XXI. 18. And in the same sense ῥίπτεσθαι in Luke IV. 22. and ταπεινοῦσθαι in Esther VI. 13. Isa. III. 24. in Ps. XXXVII. 24. ὅταν πέσῃ & καταραχθήσεται. כי יפל לא יוטל It is the same as what is said here: he shall not remain forever in the fall. By this, however, the Apostle indicates what he said above, when he said ἕως σήμερον ἡμέρας.

He speaks of the intention of GOD, not of the event; therefore that comparison with the preceding words ἕως σήμερον ἡμέρας is null. Moreover, the intention of God was neither that they should fall, nor that they should remain in a fall and ruin: much less that they should stumble. For Christ was therefore placed as a foundation in Zion, that they might be built up into him through faith: not that they might stumble through unbelief. By the judicial and consequent will of God, indeed, those who stumble against the cornerstone and rock of salvation fall: but God is of such grace that He does not wish even them to remain in ruin, but that they should be converted and live. Ezek. XVIII. 23. ch. XXXIII. 11.

but by their trespass salvation has come to the Gentiles, to provoke them to jealousy.

To that σωτηρία is understood ἐγένετο, which the Syriac supplied. The sense is: God for a time abandoned many of the Jews because of their contumacy, so that the Gentiles might the more easily arrive at true righteousness; which is here called salvation by metonymy, so that, having observed their holiness and spiritual gifts, those Jews might, out of emulation for such honor, embrace those things which they had spurned. See above X. 19. The unbelief of the Jews served the Gentiles in two ways: First, because in that way it appeared that no injustice was done to the Jews by GOD, because He called the Gentiles to those things which they themselves had repudiated: concerning which see on Matt. XXIV. 14. Secondly, because if the greatest part of the Jews had believed in Christ, that would have hindered the Gentiles from being received into the body of the Church unless they were circumcised and subject to the law of Moses, as can be seen in Acts XV. 1. and XXI. 20. But now, being a much smaller part, they could not impose the law on the others. Thus out of darkness God made light to exist, with truly admirable wisdom. παραζηλῶσαι הכעיס.

These things are to be understood not τελικῶς (as an end), but ἐκβατικῶς (as a result): for this was a matter of event and divine direction, not that GOD willed that the Israelites should fall, but, because they were going to fall by their own fault, He directed this fall of theirs for good, partly regarding the Gentiles for their salvation, and partly regarding the Israelites, so that He might snatch them from destruction through the emulation of the Gentiles. The intention of GOD, therefore, was to stimulate the Jews to emulation through the faith and salvation of the Gentiles. The assumption of the new people was directed toward the provocation of the old to emulation: so that, indeed, the Israelites, seeing the crowded conversion of the Gentiles to God, might be stirred by serious emulation and themselves submit their minds to the doctrine of the Gospel. Thus, therefore, the Apostle concludes: If GOD had utterly cast away the people of Israel, its salvation could not be sought even now. But it is being sought: Therefore He has not utterly cast away the Israelites. That obstacle concerning circumcision has little weight. For both circumcision and other things pertaining to the Old Testament could be abrogated by divine authority, to which the Jews converted to Christ would have offered no resistance, just as the Apostles called from the Jewish nation, being divinely admonished, did not reject the uncircumcised Gentiles, but received them with joy.

Latin:

V. 11. λέγω ὄν.

Eadem locutio, quæ supra 1. An hoc dico, quod mihi imputatur?

μὴ ἔπταισαν ἵνα πέσωσι.

An dico eos ita lapsos ut cadant, id est, ut in casu ma- neant: nam sæpe verba sumuntur in sensu durationis. Πταίειν מכשול poni solet de eo, qui impellitur, נפל autem, quod per πίπτειν vertitur, sæpe jacendi habet significationem, ut cum dicitur Apoc. XVIII. 2. ἔπεσεν ἔπεσε, id est, planè jacet: ideoque pro eo ponitur κατακλίνεσθαι Exod. XXI. 18. Et eodem sensu ῥίπτεσθαι Luc. IV. 22. & ταπεινοῦσθαι Esther. VI. 13. Esa. III. 24. in Psal. XXXVII. 24. ὅταν πέσῃ & κατα- ραχθήσεται. כי יפל לא יוטל Idem est quod hic dicitur: non manebit semper in lapsu. Per hoc autem indicat Apostolus, quod supra, cum dixit ἕως σήμερον ἡμέρας.

De intentione DEI loquitur, non de eventu; ideò illa collatio cum verbis præcedentibus ἕως σήμερον ἡμέρας nulla est. Intentio autem Dei, nec ut caderent, fuit, nec ut in casu & ruina maneant: multò minus ut impingant. Nam Christus-ideò in fundamentum positus est in Zion, ut superstru- antur in ipsum per fidem: non ut impingerent per incredulitatem. Judiciariâ quidem & conse- quente Dei voluntate, illi, qui impingunt in la- pidem angularem & petram salutis, ruunt: sed eâ est Deus gratiâ, ut nec illos in ruina manere ve- lit, sed ut convertantur, & vivant. Ezech. XIIX. 23. c. XXXIII. 11.

ἀλλὰ τῷ αὐτῶν παραπτώματι ἡ σωτηρία τοῖς ἔθνεσι εἰς τὸ παραζηλῶσαι αὐτὲς.

Ad illud σωτηρία subauditur ἐγένετο, quod supplevit Sy- rus. Sensus est: Deus Judæorum plurimos ob contuma- ciam ipsorum ad tempus dereliquit, ut eò facilius gentes pervenirent ad veram justitiam; quæ hic per μετωνυμίαν sa- lus dicitur, ut conspecta ipsorum sanctimonia & donis spiri- tualibus, Judæi illi æmulatu tanti honoris amplecterentur ea, quæ spreverant. Vide supra X. 19. Judæorum incredu- litas duobus modis serviit gentibus: Primum quod ea ra- tione apparuit nullam injuriam à DEO Judæis fieri, quod Gentes vocaret ad ea, quæ ipsi repudiaverant: de quo vide ad Matth. XXIV. 14. Deinde quod si Judæorum pars ma- xima in Christum credidisset, ea obstititset, ne gentes, nisi circumcisæ & legi Mosis subditæ, ad corpus Ecclesiæ recipe- rentur, ut videre est Act. XV. 1. & XXI. 20. Nunc verò multo minor pars cum essent, legem dare cæteris non potue- re. Ita ex tenebris Deus lucem fecit exsistere, sapientiâ su- nè admirabili. παραζηλῶσαι הכעיס.

Intelligenda hæc sunt non τελικῶς, sed ἐκβατι- xῶς: nam hoc eventûs & directionis divinæ fuit, non quod voluerit DEUS, ut caderent Israelitæ, sed, quia casuri erant propriâ culpâ, hunc eorum casum in bonum direxerit, partim quoad gentiles in salutem eorum, partim quoad Israelitas, ut eos per æmulationem gentium exitio eriperet. Inten- tio itaque DEI fuit, ut ad æmulationem exstimu- laret Judæos per fidem & salutem gentium. As- sumptio novi populi directa fuit ad veteris pro- vocationem ad æmulationem: ut nempe Israeli- tæ cernentes confertam gentilium ad Deum con- versionem seriâ æmulatione irritati & ipsi doctri- næ Evangelii animos suos submitterent. Ita ergò colligit Apostolus: Si omninò DEUS abjecisset po- pulum Israeliticum, salutem ejus fieri non posset, ut etiamnum quæreret. At quærit eam: Ergò non omninò Israelitas abjecit. Illud de circumcisione obstaculum parum momenti habet. Nam & cir- cumcisio & alia ad V. T. pertinentia divinâ auto- ritate abrogari poterant, cui Judæi ad Christum conversi minimè restitissent, quemadmodum A- postoli è gente Judaica vocati admoniti divinitus, non reprobarunt gentiles incircumcisos, sed eos cum gaudio susceperunt.

## 11:12
V. 12. Now if their trespass is the riches of the world, and their failure the riches of the Gentiles.

Paraptoma, that is, what was just now ptaisin, the unbelief of the multitude of the Jews: hettema the fewness of the believing Jews. So also in the Greek of Isaiah XXXI. 8. oi de neaniskoi esontai eis hettema, that is, they shall be few. That unbelief of the multitude, and the fewness of the believing Jews, became the opulence of the world or of the Gentiles, because GOD seized that occasion to call the Gentiles, of which Gentiles an innumerable multitude believed. It is Paul's custom to call every abundance plouton, as we said above II. 4. IX. 23.

how much more their fullness.

How much more will the multitude of believing Jews (concerning which below 26.) by their example and doctrine lead others still from the Gentiles to the faith? Pleroma here is multitude, as also below 15.

The blessed Mylius more correctly makes the Apostle argue thus: The power of salvation and prosperity for good is certainly more potent than that of a fall and destruction. But the power of the Israelitic fall for good was such that it resulted in the salvation of the Gentiles. Therefore the power of their salvation and conversion for good will certainly be greater. He calls the rejection of Israel, using mild words, a fall and a diminution: he calls the fullness of the same a rich conversion, by which the Jews are converted not individually, but as it were in a flock, whether that had happened long ago; or whether it is yet to happen at some time hereafter. If the past tense is taken, the Apostle hints that if the Jews had believed in great numbers, that would have in no way hindered the salvation of the Gentiles. For the preaching of the Gospel would nevertheless have flowed to the Gentiles, and that with even greater fruit, if they had seen that the Gentiles had also received it commonly from the Jewish nation, from whence it had proceeded. If the future is taken, a solemn and brilliant conversion of the Israelitic people is signified by the Apostle. Thus the blessed Mylius: who indeed takes it as future; but we shall teach that the past is rather regarded thereafter. In which way also the blessed Hunnius: But here it could have been objected: if therefore the Gentiles were enriched from the fall of the Jews, it follows that, if the Jews had stood in the faith, the Gentiles would not have been admitted to the fellowship of the faith. The Apostle answers by inversion: If the fall was an occasion for the calling of the Gentiles; much more would the fullness of the Jews have served the conversion of the Gentiles. Those things explain each other, paraptoma auton and hettema auton, just as ploutos kosmou and ploutos ethnon: it was not the fewness of the believers from the Israelitic people that was the salvation of the Gentiles: but the diminution or rejection, by which, on account of the paraptoma of the head, they suffered a diminution, and of their honor, who had been the glorious people of GOD, they suffered a hettema. For hettema properly and by common usage imports a diminution, but not a fewness. And to the guilt a punishment had to be added. Nor is the discourse now about the believers, but about the unbelievers, not about the remnant of those to be saved, but about the multitude of perishing Israelites. And so we take it of the past rather than of the future, of that which could have happened, not of that which will happen. We add concerning the word hettema, which our blessed Weller has here p. 629. The hettema itself, derived from hettasthai, is to be at war. For νίκη and ἥττη are correlatives, and as the former signifies victory, so the latter signifies defeat, and those things which are accustomed to follow from defeat, 2 Pet. II. 19, 20; hence the word מס which the LXX rendered by ἥττημα in Isa. XXXI. 8, and B. Luth. in the vernacular: und deine junge Mannschafft wird zinßbar werden. ἥττημα is therefore the defect or downfall of the Jews, who, being conquered in the spiritual battle by the Devil and succumbing to their own malice, lost all the glory and grace of GOD, and left this to the Gentiles, who rejoiced in so many spoils, Isa. IX. 41.

Latin:

V. 12. εἰ δὲ τὸ παράπτωμα αὐτῶν πλῦτος κόσμα, καὶ τὸ ἥττημα αὐτῶν πλῦτος ἐθνῶν.

Παράπτωμα, id est, quod modò πταίσιν, incredulitas multitudinis Judæorum : ἥττημα paucitas Judæorum cre- dentium. Sic & in Græco Esaïæ XXXI. 8. οἱ δὲ νεανίσκοι ἔσον- ται εἰς ἥττημα, id est, pauci erunt. Illa incredulitas multi- tudinis, & paucitas Judæorum credentium, facta est opu- lentia mundi sive gentium, quia occasionem istam arripuit DEUS gentes vocandi, quarum Gentium innumera multi- tudo credidit. Mos Pauli est omnem abundantiam vocare πλῦτον, ut diximus supra II. 4. IX. 23.

πόσῳ μᾶλλον τὸ πλήρωμα αὐτῶν.

Quanto magis multitudo Judæorum credentium (de quo infra 26.) exemplo suo ac doctrina alios adhuc è gentibus ad fidem perducet ? πλήρωμα hic est multitudo, ut & infra 15.

B. Mylius rectius Apostolum ita facit argu- mentantem: Salutis & prosperitatis ad bonum vis est utique potentior, quam lapsus & exitii. At lapsus Israelitici ea ad bonum vis fuit, ut in salutem genti- libus cesserit. Ergo salutis & conversionis eorun- dem vis ad bonum utique major erit.
