Quia vexillum vel trophæum signum est Dominii, sicut sub vexillo Principis populus, sub vexillo Ducis exercitus agere aut militare dicitur, id est, sub regimine. Quod in Ebræo est, ad illum gentes requirent, h. e. requirendo ad eum confluent, in Græco habetur, in illo gentes sperabunt, sensu eodem. Qui enim requirunt & concurrunt ad Messiam, illi in eodem sperant: & spes atque expectatio bonorum cœlestium, quæstionis & concursus illius tùm causa impulsiva, tùm finalis est, ut rectè B. Glassius in Not. ad Epist. Dom. II. Advent. p. 204. Conf. Gen. XLIX, 10. Psalm. XXXIV. 5. 6.

## 15:13
V. 13. And the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing.

The God of hope is that God whom our hope looks to, as we said above 5. May that GOD fill you not with quarrels and disputes, but with tranquility (for he calls that joy) and concord, yet in such a way that you retain the common faith: for GOD does not approve of peace with the detriment of faith in Christ.

so that you may abound in hope by the power of the Holy Spirit.

That from that tranquility and concord your hope in God may grow, by the help of the Holy Spirit, who does not love the contentious. See Gal. V. 22. Ephes. IV. 3. περισσεύειν יתר to be made fruitful,

But if anyone has labored for such peace, it was done by Grotius. The proof is not only his exchanges and the writings of Rivet, but also what we have often noted as said by Grotius for syncretism with the Arminians, the Socinians, and the Jews themselves. Certainly no solid peace, approved by God, no joy in the Holy Scriptures has a place where faith in Christ is exiled. But the Apostle is not speaking so much of concord and peace with others, as of the tranquility and peace of the faithful heart, whose companion is joy in the Holy Spirit, and whose parent is trust in Christ. Rom. V. 1. And the Apostle had already prayed before for the Romans for the gift of concord v. 5. 6. but now he prays for them for the kingdom of grace; which in ch. XIV. 17. he had said consisted in righteousness, which is through faith, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit: with the addition of the hope of the kingdom of glory: because the ultimate end of faith is eternal salvation. Conf. Is. XLV. 17. But he is called the God of hope both objectively, because he is our hope, and effectively, because he is the author of hope, which the latter we approve more: for he is also called the God of grace, the God of consolation, the God of peace, 2 Cor. I. 3. Heb. XIII. 20.

PART II. EXCULPATORY. Concerning both the writing and the delayed arrival. PERTAINING TO THE EPILOGUE OF THE WHOLE EPISTLE.

With the whole treatment now finished, there remains the epilogue of our Epistle: in which first there is the excuse for the letters and the delayed arrival, then the request for prayers, and also the votive prayer from ch. XV. v. 14 to the end: and furthermore in ch. XVI. the commendation of Phoebe, and the greetings both Pauline and of the Church, with an exhortation to avoid the heterodox, and an Apostolic vow: likewise also greetings made in the name of others with a repetition of the vow: and finally the doxology of GOD.

Latin:

V. 13. ὁ δὲ θεὸς τῆς ἐλπίδος πληρώσαι ὑμᾶς πάσης χαρᾶς καὶ εἰρήνης ἐν τῷ πιστεύειν.

Ὁ Θεὸς τῆς ἐλπίδος est is Deus, quem spes nostra respicit, ut diximus supra 5. Ille DEUS vos impleat non rixis & jurgiis, sed tranquillitate (id enim χαρὰν vocat) & concordia, ita tamen ut communem fidem retineatis: neque enim DEUS pacem probat cum detrimento fidei in Christum.

εἰς τὸ περισσεύειν ὑμᾶς ἐν τῇ ἐλπίδι ἐν δυνάμει πνεύματος ἁγίου.

Ut ex illa tranquillitate & concordia spes vestra in Deum crescat, ope Spiritus S. qui non amat contentiosos. Vide Gal. V. 22. Ephes. IV. 3. περισσεύειν יתר fœcundari,

At si quisquam pro tali pace laboravit, à Gro- tio id factum. Argumento sunt non tantùm amœ- bæa ejus, & Riveti scripta, sed etiam quæ sæpius , è Grotio pro Syncretismo cum Arminianis, So- cinianis, ipsísque Judæis dicta, notavimus. Nulla utique pax solida, Deoque probata, nullum gau- dium in S. S. locum habet, ubi fides in Christum exulat. Sed non loquitur tàm de concordia Apo- stolus, & pace cum aliis, quàm de tranquillitate & pace cordis fidelis, cujus comes est gaudium in Spi- ritu S. parens verò est fiducia in Christum. Rom. V. 1. Et precatus jam antea erat Apostolus Ro- manis donum concordiæ v. 5. 6. jam verò preca- tur iis regnum gratiæ; quod c. XIV. 17. in justi- tia, quæ est per fidem, pace & gaudio in Sp. S. situm esse dixerat: addità spe regni gloriæ: quia finis ultimus fidei est salus æterna. Conf. Es. XLV. 17. Deus autem spei dicitur tùm objectivè, quia spes nostra est, tum effectivè, quia autor est spei, quod posterius magis probamus: nam & ita Deus gratiæ, Deus consolationis, Deus pacis dicitur, 2. Cor. I. 3. Ebr. XIII. 20.

PARS II. EXCUSATORIA. Tum Scriptionis, tum dilati adventus. AD EPILOGUM TOTIUS EPISTO- LÆ PERTINENS.

Absolutà jam tractatione universâ superest Epilogus nostræ Epistolæ: in quo primum excu- satio literarum & dilati adventûs, tùm precum po- stulatio, nec non votiva precatio c. XV. à v. 14. ad finem habetur: ac porrò c. XVI. commenda- tio Phœbæ, & salutationes tùm Paulinæ tùm Eccle- siæ, cum adhortatione fugiendorum heterodoxo- rum, & voto Apostolico: itemque salutationes aliorum nomine factæ cum iteratione voti: ac deni- que δοξολογία DEI.

## 15:14
V. 14. But I myself am convinced, my brothers,

The Apostle is accustomed to soften his admonitions as if applied out of superabundance, so that he may the more excite his own to duty. A similar manner of speaking is in 2 Tim. I. 5. And in the Epistle to the Hebrews VI. 9. And what he says was true, but in the part of those to whom he writes.

that you yourselves are full of goodness.

I hope that you of your own accord, without my admonition, will abstain from condemnations and contempt.

filled with all knowledge.

Being sufficiently aware that most of you are [aware] of Christian liberty.

δυνάμενοι καὶ ἄλλους νυθετεῖν.

To instruct others, that is, the more unskilled, concerning that liberty.

The Apostle's excuse is not to be referred only to those things which he had warned about regarding condemnations and contempt in the preceding chapter and the beginning of this chapter: but to the whole Epistle: by which he softens both his instruction and his moral admonitions: because he wrote to them, and indeed a little more freely, not because he was doubtful about their goodness or their knowledge of sacred things, but rather persuaded, and that they were full of ἀγαθωσύνη or goodness, and filled with all necessary knowledge, so that some of them might even be able to instruct and admonish others, which I believe is evident both in the didactic part and in the hortatory part, because he also wished to recall some things to their memory for the grace given to him, or by recalling them to admonish them, and to show himself among them as a faithful minister of Christ among the Gentiles, especially because he has Christ working in him both in word and deed; which he has demonstrated elsewhere throughout the world. But that statement, that they are full of goodness or charity and knowledge, is both to be taken only synecdochically, as regarding some in the Roman Church, and also to be understood concerning fullness according to parts, not as to degrees, namely that they have knowledge of all parts of doctrine, and have exercised themselves in all works of goodness, yet not in that degree of perfection that they could not be further informed by the Apostle or through the Holy Scriptures, or that they stood in need of no admonition.

Latin:

V. 14. πέπεισμαι δὲ ἀδελφοί μη, καὶ ἀυτὸς ἐγὼ περὶ ὑμῶν.

Solet Apostolus monita sua emollire quasi ex superab- undanti adhibita, ut eò magis suos ad officium excitet. Simile loquendi genus 2. Timoth. I. 5. Et in Epist. ad Hebr. VI. 9. Et verum erat quod dicit, sed in parte eorum, qui- bus scribit.

ὅτι καὶ ἀυτοὶ μεσοί ἐστε ἀγαθωσύνης.

Spero vos sponte vestra sine meo monitu absituros à condemnationibus & contemptu.

πεπληρωμένοι πάσης γνώσεως.

Satis intelligentes esse vos plerosque libertatis Christianæ.

δυνάμενοι καὶ ἄλλους νυθετεῖν.

Alios, id est, imperitiores instituere de ista libertate.

Excusatio Apostoli non referenda tantùm ad ea, quæ de condemnationibus, & contemptu cap. præcedenti & initio hujusce capitis monuerat: sed ad totam Epistolam: quâ & informationem & moralia sua monita emollit: quod non sive de bo- nitate ipsorum, sive de scientia rerum sacrarum ambiguus, sed persuasus potius, & plenos eos ἀγαθωσύνη vel bonitate, & repletos omni neces- saria cognitione, ut alios etiam nonnulli ex ipsis instituere ac monere possint, ipsis tamen scripse- rit, & quidem paulò liberiùs, quod cùm in parte didascalica, tùm in parænetica patere arbitror, quod & pro gratia sibi data iis nonnulla in me- moriam revocare, vel memorans monere volue- rit, & penes ipsos se exhibere fidelem Christi in- ter gentes ministrum, imprimis quia Christum in se habeat & verbo & facto operantem; quod passim per orbem aliàs demonstravit. Illa autem, quod pleni sint bonitate vel charitate & scientiâ, tùm Synecdochicè tantùm accipienda, quoad non- nullos in Ecclesia Romana, tum intelligenda etiam de plenitudine secundum partes, non quoad gradus, quod scilicet notitiam habeant de omnibus doctrinæ partibus, & in omnibus bonitatis operibus sese exercuerint, non tamen in eo perfectionis gradu, ut ab Apostolo vel per S. S. non informari possent amplius, aut nulla monitione indigerent.

## 15:15
V. 15. τολμηρότερον δὲ ἔγραψα ὑμῖν ἀδελφοὶ ἀπὸ μέρους.

That is, a little more freely, as the Syrian takes it here: for ἀπὸ μέρους and ἐκ μέρους diminishes something from that which is said, as below 24. 1 Cor. XIII 9. 12. 2 Cor. I. 14. II. 5.

ὡς ἐπαναμιμνήσκων ὑμᾶς διὰ τὴν χάριν τὴν δοθεῖσάν μοι ὑπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ.

As if he were saying I urge him who is already hastening, and he excuses the necessity of his office; for by grace he understands metonymically the Apostleship itself, as above XII. 6. reminding מעורר.

Latin:

V. 15. τολμηρότερον δὲ ἔγραψα ὑμῖν ἀδελφοὶ ἀπὸ μέρους.

Id est, paulò liberius, ut hic accipit Syrus: nam ἀπὸ μέρους & ἐκ μέρους diminuit aliquid de eo, quod dicitur, ut infra 24. 1. Cor. XIII 9. 12. 2. Cor. I. 14. II. 5.

ὡς ἐπαναμιμνήσκων ὑμᾶς διὰ τὴν χάριν τὴν δοθεῖσάν μοι ὑπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ.

Quasi dicat σπεύδοντα καὶ ἀυτὸν ὀτρύνω, & necessitatem officii excusat; nam per χάριν intelligit μετωνυμικῶς ipsum Apostolatum, ut supra XII. 6. ἐπαναμιμνήσκων מעורר.

## 15:16
εἰς τὸ εἶναί με λειτουργὸν ἰησοῦ χριστοῦ εἰς τὰ ἔθνη.

To be, for to be seen; so that I may prove by deeds that I am a minister of Christ sent to the Gentiles. See above XI. 13.

ἱερουργοῦντα τὸ ἐυαγγέλιον τοῦ Θεοῦ.

While I perform a priesthood not Levitical, but Christian, according to the prophecy of Isaiah LXVI. 21.

ἵνα γένηται ἡ προσφορὰ τῶν ἐθνῶν ἐυπρόσδεκτος.

Not offering cattle to God, but many men converted to God through me. He persists in the similitude of a victim; therefore he says acceptable, which is the same as well-pleasing, which we had above XII. 2. where see the remarks. You have the word acceptable also below 34. 2 Corinthians VI. 2. VIII. 12. 1 Peter II. 5. Luke IV. 19. acceptable corresponds to the Hebrew רָצוֹן.

ἡγιασμένοι ἐν πνέυματι ἁγίῳ.

Not with salt, as the Levitical victims, but with the Holy Spirit himself. See what is said in Mark 9:49.

By the grace given to the Apostle, the gifts seem to be understood rather than the Apostleship itself: because concerning the office, for which those peculiar gifts were given to the holy Apostle, it follows in v. 16: that I should be a minister of Christ. Moreover, the Priesthood of the Apostle is rightly said not to be Levitical, I add, nor Melchizedekian, much less Mass-related; because the Levitical Priesthood had to cease in the New Testament. The Melchizedekian was fulfilled in Christ, and was proper to him, but Scripture is utterly ignorant of a Mass-related one, and in so far as an unbloody sacrifice is feigned to be offered by such priests in the Papacy, it is contrary to Holy Scripture, which acknowledges no propitiatory unbloody Sacrifice, because without the shedding of blood there is no remission of sins, Heb. 9:22, nor does it teach any sacrifice of the New Testament, except the bloody one of the passion and death of Christ, who offered himself to God for a sweet-smelling savor, Eph. 5:2, and by one oblation perfected forever them that are sanctified, Heb. 10:34. By this very word, says Flacius, or phrase ἱερουργῶντα (ministering) the Gospel, the Apostle abundantly indicates what sacrifice remains in the New Testament, and what is the office of the ministers of this Testament, namely, by preaching the Gospel to show to all that one propitiatory sacrifice of the Lamb of God, which, once offered, fully expiated the sins of the whole world, according to that: You shall proclaim the death of the Lord.

Latin:

εἰς τὸ εἶναί με λειτουργὸν ἰησοῦ χριστοῦ εἰς τὰ ἔθνη.

Esse, pro conspici; ut factis probem me ministrum esse Christi ad Gentes missum. Vide supra XI. 13.

ἱερουργοῦντα τὸ ἐυαγγέλιον τοῦ Θεοῦ.

Dum obeo sacerdotium non Leviticum, sed Christianum ex vaticinio Esaiæ LXVI. 21.

ἵνα γένηται ἡ προσφορὰ τῶν ἐθνῶν ἐυπρόσδεκτος.

Non pecudes DEO offerens, sed homines multos per me ad Deum conversos. Persistit in similitudine victimæ; ideò dicit ἐυπρόσδεκτος, quod idem cum ἐνάρεστος, quod supra habuimus XII. 2. ubi dicta vide. Vocem προσδέκτος habes & infra 34. 2. Corinth. VI. 2. VIII. 12. 1. Petr. II. 5. Luc. IV. 19. δεκτὸς respondet Hebræo רָצוֹן.

ἡγιασμένοι ἐν πνέυματι ἁγίῳ.

Non sale, ut Leviticæ victimæ, sed ipso Spiritu S. Vide quæ dicta Marci IX. 49.

Per gratiam Apostolo datam dona potius intelligenda videntur, quàm Apostolatus ipse: quia de officio, ob quod illa peculiaria dona S. Apostolo data sunt, sequitur v. 16. ut essem minister Christi. Rectè autem Sacerdotium Apostoli dicitur non Leviticum esse, addo nec Melchisedecianum, nedum Missaticum; quia Leviticum Sacerdotium cessare debuit in N. T. Melchisedecianum implebatur in Christo, eique proprium erat, Missaticum autem Scriptura ignorat penitus, & quà sacrificium incruentum offerri à talibus Sacerdotibus fingitur in Papatu, refragatur Scripturæ S. quæ nullum agnoscit Sacrificium propitiatorium incruentum, quia sine sanguinis effusione non sit peccatorum remissio Ebr. IX. 22. nec ullum Nov. Test. docet sacrificium, nisi passionis & mortis Christi cruentæ, qui seipsum obtulit Deo in odorem suavitatis Eph. V. 2. & unicâ oblatione consummavit omnes, qui sanctificantur, Ebr. X. 34. Hoc ipso verbo, ait Flacius, aut phrasi ἱερουργῶντα Evangelium abunde indicat Apostolus, quodnam sacrificium restet in Novo Testamento, & quod sit officium ministrorum hujus Testamenti, nempe prædicando Evangelium omnibus ostentare illud unicum agni DEI propitiatorium sacrificium, quod semel oblatum plenè totius mundi delicta expiavit, juxta illud: Mortem Domini annunciabitis.

## 15:17
V. 17. ἔχω οὖν κάυχησιν ἐν χριστῷ ἰησοῦ πρὸς τὸν Θεόν.

The sense is: since I have brought so many to the faith, I have something to rejoice in regarding the things of God, not as if I had done these things by myself, but through Jesus Christ. Καυχᾶσθαι means sometimes to rely, sometimes to rejoice on account of something. הִלֵּל is sometimes translated as καυχᾶσθαι, elsewhere as ἀγαλλιᾶν. Thus עָלַז is translated by both, and no less עָלַץ & רָנַן.

Latin:

V. 17. ἔχω οὖν κάυχησιν ἐν χριστῷ ἰησοῦ πρὸς τὸν Θεόν.

Sensus est: cum tam multos ad fidem adduxerim, habeo quod læter in rebus DEI, non quasi per me ista effecerim, sed per Jesum Christum. Καυχᾶσθαι modo inniti, modo lætari ob rem aliquam. הִלֵּל interdum καυχᾶσθαι vertitur, alibi ἀγαλλιᾶν. Sic עָלַז per utrumque vertitur, nec minus עָלַץ & רָנַן.

## 15:18
V. 18. οὐ γὰρ τολμήσω λαλεῖν.

I would scarcely dare to utter. It is an honest προθεραπεία (preliminary apology) for self-praise, such as Paul employs many, as in 2 Cor. 12:1 and following.

τῶν ὧν οὐ κατειργάσατο χριστὸς δὲ ἐμοῦ εἰς ὑπακοὴν ἐθνῶν.

What he did not do, that is, how many and great things he did for the obedience of the Gentiles, namely, to bring it about.

Those words ὦ γάρ τολμήσω are applied differently by interpreters. Origen explains it thus: I would not wish to arrogate to myself the praise of others' deeds, I will only say those things which Christ accomplished through me myself. Ambrose thus: as if Paul could not mention anything of those things which pertain to praise, which were not performed through him by the help of God. To which also the translation of blessed Luther tends, as does the exposition of Erasmus: I would not dare to speak anything of my own deeds, but only of those which Christ performed through me. Which sense is to be preferred to the Grotian: for the reason is given for what he had said, that he indeed had glorying, but in Christ, in those things which pertain to God: because I would not dare, he says, to speak anything, unless Christ works it in me, as blessed Mylius rightly observed, that is to say, that all his things proceed from divine guidance and impulse, both as to his λόγον (word), i.e., his writings and sermons, and as to his ἔργον (work), i.e., his deeds, journeys, studies, and plans: in which deeds as well as words Christ worked particularly through the Apostle by signs, wonders, and the power of the Holy Spirit.

Latin:

V. 18. οὐ γὰρ τολμήσω λαλεῖν.

Vix audeam eloqui. Est honesta προθεραπεία περιαυτολογίας, quales multas adhibet Paulus, ut 2. Cor. XII. 1. & sequentibus.

τῶν ὧν οὐ κατειργάσατο χριστὸς δὲ ἐμοῦ εἰς ὑπακοὴν ἐθνῶν.

Quid non fecerit, id est, quàm multa & magna fecerit ad gentium obedientiam, nempe efficiendam.

Aliter illa ὦ γάρ τολμήσω applicantur ab Inter- pretibus. Origenes ita exponit: Nolim alienorum factorum laudem mihi arrogare, tantùm ea dicam, quæ per meipsum effecit Christus. Ambrosius ita: quasi Paulus non possit quicquam commemorare eorum, quæ ad laudem pertinent, quæ per ipsum præ- stitæ non sint auxilio DEI. Quò etiam abit B. Lu- theri translatio, ut & Erasmi ἔκθεσις: non ausim quicquam loqui de factis meis, sed tantum de iis, quæ Christus per me gessit. Qui sensus Grotiano præ- ferendus: nam causa redditur ejus, quod dixerat, se habere quidem gloriationem, sed in Christo, in iis, quæ ad Deum spectant: quia non ausim, in- quit, quicquam loqui, nisi id in me operetur Chri- stus, ut rectè observavit B. Mylius, q. d. sua o- mnia à divino ductu atque impulsu proficisci, tùm quà λόγον h. e. scriptiones & conciones suas, tùm quà ἔργον h. e. res gestas, profectiones, stu- dia & consilia: in quibus rebus gestis pariter & verbis peculiariter per signa, prodigia, & virtutem Sp. S. operatus est per Apostolum Christus.

## 15:19
V. 19. ἐν δυνάμει σημείων καὶ τεράτων.

These are often accustomed to be joined together as in Matt. XXIV. 24, John IV. 48, Acts II. 43, 30, V. 12, VII. 36, XIV. 3, 2 Cor. XII. 12. Such were the casting out of demons, the healing of every kind of disease, and the raising of the dead.

These are rightly accepted in a general sense: which, however, others are accustomed to distinguish, so that they note σημεῖα as miracles in curable diseases, and τέρατα in incurable ones. But that distinction is not observed in the Scriptures. Perhaps more conveniently, Origen ad h. l. says that signs are those in which, since there is something wonderful, it is indicated when something is about to happen, but prodigies are those in which only something wonderful is shown: although Origen notes that even this distinction is not always observed.

ἐν δυνάμει πνεύματος Θεᾶ.

In the Manuscript ἐν δυνάμει πνεύματος ἁγίε, as Athanasius cites it. This pertains to those revelations which are discussed in 2 Cor. XII. and the gifts of tongues. These were the signs of Paul's priestly service, much more magnificent than the turban and the robe and the bells.

This can be referred either to designating the Holy Spirit as the principal cause of the signs and wonders, or also to the power of the Holy Spirit exerting itself in the preaching and letters of the Apostle: not only regarding the revelations made to him and the gifts of tongues, by which he handed down what was divinely revealed, but also regarding the efficacy and ἐνέργειαν of the Word, which is the power of GOD unto salvation, which is preached ἐν δυνάμει πνέυματος by the power of the Holy Spirit with fruit and saving effect, through which also κατειργάσατο χριστὸς Christ worked for the obedience and conversion of the Gentiles. He attributes all these things to the Spirit of GOD, says Flacius, because by Him he was directed and performed miracles, preached, made progress, and finally the same also moved the hearts of the hearers.

ὥστε με ἀπὸ ἱερεσαλὴμ) That history is touched upon which is in Acts IX. 26.

καὶ κύκλῳ.

This κύκλῳ is placed here adverbially, for 'around', as in John VI. 3, Gen. XXIII. v. 17, XXXV. 5, XLI. 48, Exod. VII. 24, and often elsewhere. So also Matt. III. 34, VI. 6, 36, Luke IX. 12. He understands Phoenicia, other parts of Syria, and Arabia, Acts IX. 20, XII. 25, XIII. 1, Gal. I. 17.

μέχρι τῶ Ἰλλυρικῶ.

Rightly; for Macedonia, which Paul traversed, touches Dalmatia, which is a part of Illyricum, and the Illyrian sea itself. In that region is Apollonia, mentioned in Acts I. See Ptolemy.

πεπληρωκέναι τὸ ἐυαγγέλιον τῶ χριστ That is, to have fulfilled the duty of preaching the Gospel: It is a metonymy. Thus πληρώσαντες τὴν διακονίαν is said in Acts XII. 25, τὸ ἔργον ἐπλήρωσαν in Acts XIV. 25, and πληρῶσαι τὸν λόγον τῶ Θεῶ in Coloss. I. 25.

Others translate that καὶ κύκλῳ indeed as 'and in the surrounding regions.' But it is more correctly explained as 'in a circuit,' or 'through a circuit,' as the Vulgate has it, in which the particle καὶ is omitted: concerning which Flacius Illyricus says: He narrates that he filled all places around the Mediterranean Sea from Jerusalem as far as Illyricum with the doctrine of the Gospel, and performed many miracles there, so that from this effect the true mark of an Apostle and the presence of Christ around him might be recognized. He says, therefore, that he filled all things in a circuit with the Gospel, because if a line is drawn from Jerusalem through Syria, Asia Minor, Troas, Macedonia, and Greece, as far as Illyricum, it makes a semicircle, and if you then lead it back from there through Achaia, the Peloponnese, and Crete to Jerusalem, it will be a full circle, which Paul filled with the doctrine of the Gospel. I have, however, supplied 'all places,' because that seems to be entirely implied in the phrase 'in a circuit': and because it follows 'preaching the Gospel where Christ was not named,' and a little later he says: 'But now when I have no place in these regions.' Others translate it as 'in the surrounding regions,' which conflicts with the truth of history, because Paul did not preach much in the regions surrounding Jerusalem. Piscator also explains the 'filling of the Gospel' metonymically, that is, the duty of preaching the Gospel; which is more convenient than if you were to explain it with Toletus, that to fill the Gospel is to have summoned a multitude of men to the faith of the Gospel, just as to fill a net is nothing other than to catch a copious multitude of fish. B. Wellerus observes in Aristides that the phrase πεπληρωκέναι τὸ γιγνόμενον means to have accomplished that which it was proper to be done, to have fulfilled all the requirements of a contest: thus Paul to have fulfilled the Gospel, that is, whatever the Gospel required of him as a minister of Christ, that he had fulfilled in all respects from Jerusalem to Illyricum. The Gospel did indeed require of him that by word and work he should lead the Gentiles to the obedience of Christ; he demonstrates that this was clearly and studiously fulfilled by him, yet in such a way that he refers all things entirely to Christ. B. Mylius notes that this was done in the space of 18 years, because this Epistle was written when the full course of so many years had elapsed since his conversion, from which an indication can be taken of the divine power exerted through the ministry of the Apostle.

Latin:

V. 19. ἐν δυνάμει σημείων καὶ τεράτων.

Solent hæc sæpe conjungi ut Matth. XXIV. 24. Johan. IV. 48. Act. II. 43. 30. V. 12. VII. 36. XIV. 3. 2. Cor. XII. 12. Talia erant dæmonum ejectio, morborum omnis gene- ris sanatio, mortuorum resuscitatio.

Rectè hæc generatim accipiuntur: quæ tamen alii solent distinguere, ut σημεῖα miracula in mor- bis sanabilibus, τέρατα in incurabilibus notent. Sed id discrimen non observatur in Scripturis. Fortè commodius Origenes ad h. l. Signa dicit, in quibus cum sit aliquid mirabile, indicatur, quum aliquid futurum, prodigia verò, in quibus tantum- modo aliquid mirabile ostenditur: quanquam nec istud discrimen observari semper notet Origenes.

ἐν δυνάμει πνεύματος Θεᾶ.

In Manuscripto ἐν δυνάμει πνεύματος ἁγίε, quomodo citat Athanasius. Hoc ad illas revelationes, de quibus agi- tur 2. Cor. XII. & linguarum dona pertinet. Hæc erant Paulinæ ἱερυργίας signa, multò magnificentiora quàm ci- daris & poderes & tintinnabula.

Referri potest hoc vel ad causam signorum & prodigiorum principalem Spiritum S. designandam, vel etiam ad virtutem Sp. S. in præconio & literis Apostoli sese exerente: non tantùm quoad reve- lationes ipsi factas, & dona linguarum, quibus di- vinitus revelata tradebat, sed etiam quoad effica- ciam, & ἐνέργειαν Verbi, quod est potentia DEI ad salutem, quod ἐν δυνάμει πνέυματος virtute Sp. S. prædicatur cum fructu & effectu salutari, per quod etiam κατειργάσατο χριστὸς operatus est Chri- stus ad obedientiam, & conversionem gentium. Spi- ritui DEI hæc omnia tribuit, inquit Flacius, quia eo rectus & miracula fecit, prædicavit, profecit, & denique idem etiam corda auditorum promo- vit.

ὥστε με ἀπὸ ἱερεσαλὴμ) Tangitur illa historia, quæ est Act. IX, 26.

καὶ κύκλῳ.

Hoc κύκλῳ hîc adverbialiter ponitur, pro circum, ut Joh. VI. 3. Genes. XXIII. v. 17. XXXV. 5. XLI. 48. Exodi VII. 24. & alibi sæpè. Sic & Matth. III. 34. VI. 6. 36. Luc. IX. 12. Intelligit Phœnicem, Syriæ alia, & Arabim, Act. IX. 20. XII. 25. XIII. 1. Gal. I. 17.

μέχρι τῶ Ἰλλυρικῶ.

Rectè; nam Macedonia quam peragravit Paulus, Dal- matiam attingit, quæ pars Illyrici, & ipsum mare Illyricum. In eo tractu est Apollonia nominata Actorum I. vide Ptole- mæum.

πεπληρωκέναι τὸ ἐυαγγέλιον τῶ χριστ Id est, implesse munus prædicandi Evangelii: Est μετα- νυμία. Sic πληρώσαντες τὴν διακονίαν dicitur Act. XII. 25. τὸ ἔργον ἐπλήρωσαν Actor. XIV. 25. & πληρῶσαι τὸν λόγον τῶ Θεῶ Coloss. I. 25.

Illud καὶ κύκλῳ reddunt quidem alii, & in cir- cumjacentibus regionibus. Sed rectius explicatur in circuitu, vel per circuitum, ut vulgata habet, in quâ particula καὶ omissa: quo de Flacius Illyricus: Narrat se omnia loca circa mare mediterraneum à Jerusalem usque ad Illyricum Evangelii doctrinâ complevisse, & ibi multa miracula edidisse, ut ex hoc effectu vera nota Apostoli presentiaque circa eum Christi agnoscatur. Idcò autem dicit se omnia in circuitu Evangelio replevisse, quia si linea ducatur à Jerusalem per Syriam, minorem Asiam, Troadem, Macedoniam, & Greciam, usque ad Illyricum, vel- uti semicirculum efficit, quàm si porrò inde per Acha- jam, Peloponesum, & Cretam, Hierosolymam redu- cas, erit plenus circulus, quem Paulus doctrinâ Ev- angelii complevit. Supplevi autem omnia loca, quia id omnino videtur subintelligi in voce, in circuitu: & quia sequitur ambiens predicare Evangelium, ubi non est nominatus Christus, & aliquantò post inquit: Nunc autem cum non habeam locum in hisce regionibus. Alii vertunt, in circumjacenti- bus regionibus, quod pugnat cum veritate historiæ, quia Paulus non multum concionatus est in circum- jacentibus regionibus circa Hierosolymam. Im- pletionem Evangelii etiam Piscator metonymicè explicat, id est, Evangelii predicandi munus; quod convenientius est, quàm si cum Toleto exponas, implere Evangelium est multitudinem hominum ad Evangelii fidem convocasse, sicut rete implere nihil aliud est, quàm copiosam piscium multitudi- nem comprehendere. B.Wellerus apud Aristidem observat phrasin πεπληρωκέναι τὸ γιγνόμενον esse, id quod fieri par erat, effecisse, omnes numeros cer- taminis implevisse: sic Paulum implevisse Evange- lium, id est, quicquid Evangelium à se tanquam à λειτόργῳ τῶ χρισῶ requisiverit, id se numeris omni- bus à Jerusalem usque ad Illyricum implevisse. Re- quirebat vero Evangelium ab ipso, ut λόγω ̀ κῃ ἕργῳ verbo & opere, ad obedientiam Christi adduceret gentes, hoc à se studiosè planè impletum esse demon- strat, ita tamen, ut omnia Christo accepta in soli- dum referat. Quod 18. annorum spatio factum esse notat B. Mylius, quòd tot annorum à conver- sione exactorum completo curriculo scripta fue- rit hæc Epistola, unde indicium sumi possit virtu- tis divinæ per Ministerium Apostoli exertæ.

## 15:20
V. 20. οὕτω δὲ φιλοτιμέμενον εὐαγγελίζεσθαι) Although φιλοτιμεῖσθαι draws its origin from the desire for honor, by usage it has been transferred to everything that we do with great zeal and contention. For thus it is used by Plato, Xenophon, Plutarch, others, and our Apostle in 2 Cor. 5:9, 1 Thess. 4:11.

ὐχ ὅπυ ὠνομάσθη χρισὸς, ἵνα μὴ ἐπ’ ἀλλότριον θεμέλιον οἰκοδομῶ) Paul truly declares this about himself, that in most places he had cast the seeds of the Gospel. He uses the similitude of a foundation elsewhere in this matter as well, 1 Cor. 4:10, Eph. 2:20.

Latin:

V. 20. οὕτω δὲ φιλοτιμέμενον εὐαγγελίζεσθαι) φιλοτιμετ- σθαι quanquam ab honoris appetitu originem trahit, usu tamen traductum est ad id omne, quod studio magno ac contentione agimus. Ita enim usurpat Plato, Xenophon, Plutarchus, alii, & noster Apostolus 2. Cor. V. 9. 1. Thess. IV. 11.

ὐχ ὅπυ ὠνομάσθη χρισὸς, ἵνα μὴ ἐπ’ ἀλλότριον θεμέλιον οἰκο- δομῶ) Vere de se hoc prædicat Paulus, plerisque in locis se jecisse Evangelii semina. Similitudine autem fundamen- ti, & alibi hac in re utitur 1. Cor. IV. 10. Eph. II. 20.

## 15:21
ἀλλὰ καθὼς γέγραπται) that is, I have done. An ellipsis, such as above in 3.

Οἷς μὴ ἀνηγέλη περὶ ἀυτῶ ὄψονται, κὰι οἳ ὐκ ἀκηκόασι συνήσυσι) The words themselves of the LXX in Isaiah 52 at the end. They shall see things not before mentioned, and they shall understand things not before heard, which, said in the first sense about those who were to see the outcome of the prophecies of Jeremiah, is best referred in a mystical sense to the Gospel.

The passage of Isaiah ch. 52:15 looks to the times of the New Testament and the beginning of the preaching of the Gospel, and the proper office of the Apostles, which was to announce the Gospel to those who have not heard, whence the Lord also willed this prophecy to be fulfilled through the Apostle Paul. It is not therefore only allegorized in a secondary sense, nor is the mystical sense looked to, but the fulfillment of the same according to the letter is designated. Compare Rom. 10:15 with Isa. 52:7 and the present passage. Therefore the holy Apostle contends with a certain praiseworthy ambition (φιλοτιμίᾳ) that the Gospel be preached where Christ had not yet been named, so that he might not build upon a foundation that was foreign or laid by another. Concerning the Grotius-style depravation of the prophetic passage, see what we have said on that passage. Φιλοτιμούμενον, with the accusative placed for the nominative by Hebraism, the Apostle said by antiphrasis.

Latin:

ἀλλὰ καθὼς γέγραπται) feci scilicet. Ellipsis, qualis su- pra 3.

Οἷς μὴ ἀνηγέλη περὶ ἀυτῶ ὄψονται, κὰι οἳ ὐκ ἀκηκόα- σι συνήσυσι) Verba ipsa LXX. apud Esaiam LII. in fine. Vi- debunt res non ante mentiatas, & intelligent non ante audita, quod, primo sensu dictum de iis, qui videre even- tum vaticiniorum Jeremiæ, mystico sensu optimè ad Ev- angelium refertur.

Locus Esaiæ c. LII. 15. respicit tempora N. T. & initium prædicationis Evangelii, ac proprium Apostolorum officium, quod erat annunciare Evangelium iis, qui non audierunt, unde etiam per Paulum Apostolum vaticinium hoc impleri voluit Dominus. Non ergò tantùm παρωσικῶς al- legatur, nec mysticus sensus respicitur, sed com- plementum ejusdem secundùm literam designa- tur. Conf. Rom. X. 15. cum Esa. LII. 7. & præsent. loco. Idcirco contendit cum quadam laudabili Φιλοτιμίᾳ S. Apostolus, prædicari Evangelium ubi nondum nominatus erat Christus, ne super alienum, vel ab alio jactum fundamentum ædifi- caret. De depravatione loci prophetici Grotia- na, vid. quæ ad illum locum à nobis dicta. Φιλοτι- μύμενον, accusativo per Ebraismum pro nomina- tivo posito, dixit Apostolus per antiphrasin.

## 15:22
V. 22. Διὸ καὶ ἐνεκοπτόμην τὰ πολλὰ ἐλθεῖν πρὸς ὑμᾶς) Often, when I wished to come to you, I was hindered, namely because the care of the peoples to whom the knowledge of the Gospel had not yet reached, as it had now reached the Romans, was drawing me elsewhere. We have ἐγκόπτειν in the sense of hindering also in Gal. 5:7 and 1 Thess. 2:18. In the glossary, ἐγκόπτω, I cut into, I impede. A similitude drawn from chariots or ships, into which a stake is driven.

Latin:

V. 22. Διὸ καὶ ἐνεκοπτόμην τὰ πολλὰ ἐλθεῖν πρὸς ὑμᾶς) Sæpe, cum scilicet vellem ad vos venire, inhibitus fui, nempe quia aliò trahebat me cura populorum, ad quos nondum, ut jam ad Romanos, Evangelii notitia perve- nerat. ἐγκόπτειν sensu inhibendi habemus & Gal. V. 7. & 1. Thess. II. 18. In glossario ἐγκόπτω, incido, impedio. Si- militudo ducta à curribus aut navibus, quibus palus infi- gitur.

## 15:23
V. 23. νυνὶ δὲ μηκέτι τόπον ἔχων ἐν τοῖς κλίμασι τούτοις) not finding a place where foundations are now to be laid. Ἐν τοῖς κλίμασι τούτοις, in these regions, namely of Greece. In the glossary: κλῖμα, a region, a tract. Thus we have the climates of Achaia, Syria, Cilicia, 2 Cor. 11:10, Gal. 1:21. Geographers properly call a climate the space which is intercepted by two parallels: but historians take it sometimes more narrowly, sometimes more broadly.

Ἐπιποθίαν δὲ ἔχων τῶ ἐλθεῖν πρὸς ὑμᾶς διὰ πολλῶν ἐτῶν) See above 1:11. ἐπιποθία here is what ἐπιπόθησις is in 2 Cor. 7:7, 11, Acts 19:21.

The word ἐπιποθεῖν denotes being led by a huge desire, and when the verb ἔχω is added to the noun derived from it, the significance is increased, as ἐπιθυμίαν ἔχειν in Phil. 1 is more than ἐπιποθεῖν. Compare Rom. 1:28.

V, 24. ὡς ἐὰν πορεύωμαι εἰς τὴν ἰσπανίαν ἐλεύσομαι πρὸς ὑμᾶς) In the manuscript ὡς ἄν: And thus the Greek Fathers read. Thus ὡς ἄν 1 Corinthians XI. 34. In the manuscript there is also εἰς Σπανίαν. Other codices: εἰς τὴν Σπανίαν. Strabo writes thus, and the old Glossary, and the Scholiast. Juvenal on Satire XIV and Martianus Capella, as we have noted on him. The manuscripts of Justin and Curtius have it thus: and the Jews write ספרנה as Kimchi on Obadiah: sometimes also corruptly ספניה as noted by others. Paul had many journeys in mind, which he was not permitted to execute, whether by the dictation of the Spirit, or by arising vocations, which seemed to require being anticipated. There are those who think Paul went to Spain after his first defense of his case before Nero: certainly Clement in his epistle to the Corinthians says he was a herald both in the East and in the West.

Latin:

V. 23. νυνὶ δὲ μηκέτι τόπον ἔχων ἐν τοῖς κλίμασι τούτοις) non inveniens locum, ubi nunc fundamenta jacienda sint. Ἐν τοῖς κλίμασι τότοις, in his regionibus, Græciæ scilicet. In Glossario: κλῖμα regio, tractus. Sic κλίματα Achaiæ, Sy- riæ, Ciliciæ, habemus 2. Cor. XI. 10. Gal. I. 21. Propriè κλῖμα vocant Geographi spatium, quod à duobus paralle- lis intercipitur: Sed historici modo arctius, modo latius sumunt.

Ἐπιποθίαν δὲ ἔχων τῶ ἐλθεῖν πρὸς ὑμᾶς διὰ πολλῶν ἐτῶν) Vide supra I. 11. ἐπιποθία hîc quod ἐπιπόθησις 2. Cor. VII. 7. 11. Act. XIX. 21.

Vox ἐπιποθεῖν notat ingenti desiderio duci, & cum verbum ἔχω nomini inde deducto additur, augetur significatio, ut ἐπιθυμίαν ἔχειν Phil. I. plus quàm ἐπιποθεῖν. Conf. Rom. I. 28.

V, 24. ὡς ἐὰν πορεύωμαι εἰς τὴν ἰσπανίαν ἐλεύσομαι πρὸς ὑμᾶς) In Manuscripto ὡς ἄν: Et sic legêre Græci Patres. Sic ὡς ἄν 1. Corinth. XI. 34. In Manuscripto etiam est, εἰς Σπανίαν. Alii Codices: εἰς τὴν Σπανίαν. Scribit sic Strabo & Glossarium vetus & Scholiastes. Juvenalis ad Satyram XIV. & Martianus Capella ut ad eum annotavimus. Sic habent & Codices Justini & Curtii Manuscripti: & Judæi scribunt ספרנה ut Kimchi ad Obadiam: interdum & cor- rupte ספניה ut ab aliis notatum. Multa itinera in ani- mo habuit Paulus, quæ exequi situs non est, sive per dicta- tum spiritus, sive per vocationes enascentes, quæ præver- tendæ videbantur. Sunt, qui in Hispaniam ivisse Paulum putant post primam causæ dictionem apud Neronem: certè Clemens in epistola ad Corinthios ait eum fuisse præ- conem & in oriente & in occidente.

## 15:24
ἐλπίζω γὰρ διαπορευόμενος θεάσασθαι ὑμᾶς) because he wished to take his journey from Greece through Italy into Spain: but to visit Rome in passing.

Καὶ ὑφ' ὑμῶν προπεμφθῆναι ἐκεῖ) through Gaul, of course, and Italy, which was very well known. See a similar matter in Acts XVII. 15.

Ἐὰν ὑμῶν πρῶτον ἀπὸ μέρες ἐμπλησθῶ) ἀπὸ μέρες. Not as much as I would like, but as much as will be permitted. See what we said above 15. ἐμπλησθῶ: such as that: To satisfy with a final embrace of your own. The Syrian thought the translation was taken from perfumes.

The word θεάσασθαι is emphatic, and denotes looking at something with some peculiar attention and admiration, just as comedies are watched. But that he said he hoped he would see the Romans, he speaks as a man, not as an Apostle, for the things which holy men had by revelation were certain to them, not doubtful events: Therefore he is accustomed to add if GOD wills 1 Cor. VI. 19. chap. XVI. 7. 1 Thess. II. 18. For the rest of the Apostles did not undertake their journeys by their own will, but followed the leading of the Holy Spirit Acts III. 14. Cf. B. Wellerus on this passage. Whether Paul came to Spain or not, however, is doubtful. Cornelius à Lapide, while affirming it with many others, praises St. Hippolytus, Athanasius, Cyril, Sophronius, Epiphanius, Chrysostom, Theodoret, Jerome, Gregory the Great, Isidore, Bede, Ado, Metaphrastes, and Baronius in his annals of Christ 61. He does not, however, conceal that Thomas, Pererius, and Scotus deny it, and that the Pontiffs Gelasius and Innocent I seem to favor them: whom Pererius indeed excuses.

Latin:

ἐλπίζω γὰρ διαπορευόμενος θεάσασθαι ὑμᾶς) quia ex Græ- cia per Italiam iter in Hispaniam capere volebat: obiter vero Romam invisere.

Καὶ ὑφ' ὑμῶν προπεμφθῆναι ἐκεῖ) per Galliam scilicet & Italis optimè cognitam. Similem rem vide Act. XVII. 15.

Ἐὰν ὑμῶν πρῶτον ἀπὸ μέρες ἐμπλησθῶ) ἀπὸ μέρες. Non quantum vellem, sed quantum licebit. Vide quæ dixi- mus supra 15. ἐμπλησθῶ: tale illud: Amplexu extremo sa- tiare tuorum. Syrus ab odoribus sumptam translatio- nem putavit.

Verbum θεάσασθαι emphaticum est, notatque voluptatem peculiari aliqua attentione & admi- ratione spectare, sicut spectantur Comœdiæ. Quod autem sperare se dixit, se Romanos visu- rum, ut homo loquitur, non ut Apostolus, nam quæ ex revelatione habebant viri sancti, certa ipsis erant, non eventus dubii: Ideò solet adde- re si DEUS voluerit 1. Cor. VI. 19. cap. XVI. 7. 1. Thess. II. 18. Reliqui enim pro arbitrio itinera sua susceperunt Apostoli, sed ductum Spiritus Sancti secuti sunt Actor. III. 14. Conf. B. Welle- rus in h. l. Utrum autem in Hispaniam vene- rit Paulus nec ne, dubium est. Cornelius à La- pide id affirmante cum plurimis laudat, S. Hyp- polytum, Athanasium, Cyrillum, Sophronium, Epiphanium, Chrysost. Theodoreturn Hierony- mum, Gregor. M. Isidorum, Bedam, Ado Metaphr. & Baronium ad annal. Christi 61. Non dissimulat tamen Thomam, Pererium, Scotum, id negare, & videri iis favere Gelasium & Innocentium I. Pon- tifices: quos verò excusat Pererius.

## 15:25
V. 25. νυνὶ δὲ πορεύομαι εἰς ἱερουσαλὴμ διακονῶν τοῖς ἁγίοις) bringing to them what I have collected from everywhere for their use. See what we said in the prolegomena to this epistle, πορεύομαι, that is, I am girded for the journey. See what was said on Matthew XXVI. 28.

Cornelius did not pay attention, when he said that λειτυργῆσαι is read here in the Greek text, and concluded from that that alms are ἡ λειτυργία and a sacrifice, and that alms-givers are λειτυργοὶ or Priests and a sacrifice to GOD. For it is not λειτυργῆσαι that is held in the Greek, but διακονεῖν, and the word λειτυργίας is a general term for service, not indeed specifically implying priesthood. Which Grotius also observed below at v. 27.

Latin:

V. 25. νυνὶ δὲ πορεύομαι εἰς ἱερουσαλὴμ διακονῶν τοῖς ἁγίοις) ferens illis, quæ undique in eorum usum collegi. Vide quæ diximus in prolegomenis ad hanc epistolam, πορεύομαι, id est iter accinctus sum. Vide quæ dicta ad Matth. XXVI. 28.

Oculos non adhibuit Cornelius, cum in Græ- co textu hic legi λειτυργῆσαι dixit, atque inde conclusit, quod eleemosyna sit ἡ λειτυργία & sa- crificium, & eleemosynarii sint λειτυργοὶ sive Sa- cerdotes & sacrificium DEI. Non enim in Græco habetur λειτυργῆσαι, sed διακονεῖν, & λειτυργίας vox generalis est ministerium, non verò speciatim sacerdotium importans. Quod ad v. 27. infra ob- servavit etiam Grotius.

## 15:26
V. 26. For Macedonia and Achaia were pleased) That is, the Churches which are in Macedonia and Achaia were pleased. He silently invites the Romans to similar acts of liberality.

To make a certain contribution for the poor of the saints in Jerusalem) that is, to make a portion of their wealth for those poor people. In the Glossary, κοινωνία is communication. Concerning the name of the poor, we spoke at Matt. XXVI. 11. The poor of the saints, that is, the poor who are among the Saints. Such are: Black poplars, oblong eggs.

Latin:

V. 26. ἐυδόκησαν γὰρ Μακεδονία καὶ Ἀχαΐα) Placuit enim Macedoniæ & Achaiæ, id est Ecclesiis quæ sunt in Mace- donia & Achaia. Tacite Romanos ad pares liberalitates invitat.

Κοινωνίαν τινὰ ποιήσασθαι εἰς τὺς πτωχὺς τῶν ἁγίων ἐν Ἱε- ρυσαλήμ) id est, facere pauperibus illis partem de suis opibus. In Glossario κοινωνία communicatio. De nomine πτωχῶν diximus ad Matth. XXVI. 11. πτωχὺς τῶν ἁγίων, id est pauperes, qui sunt inter Sanctos. Talia sunt: Nigra la- parum, oborum oblonga.

## 15:27
V. 27. For they were pleased) It is an excellent anaphora, together with an epanorthosis.

And they are their debtors) Properly, a debtor is one from whom something can be exacted by law. Concerning both these meanings of debt, we spoke in book II of The Law of War and Peace, VII. 4. XIV. 6. XXII. 16. Thus someone is said to owe thanks. See Gellius, book 5. Thus we had the word ὀφειλέται above I. 14. VIII. 12. חובים.

For if the Gentiles have shared in their spiritual things) Since they received the prophecies about Christ from them and believed in Christ by their example. Note that κοινωνεῖν, like the Latin participare, is said in the sense of both acting and suffering.

The Gentiles did not only receive prophecies about Christ from the Jews (although if there were room for the corruptions of Grotius, very few prophecies about Christ would remain in the O.T.) so that they believed in Christ by their example, but the Gentiles were also informed about Christ through the Jewish Apostles, namely, not other holier and Apostolic men, and were gathered and admitted to the communion of the Church, which was in the Jewish people, Eph. II. Regarding κοινωνία, Erasmus notes that alms are expressed by that civil term, as if it were not a benefit to be helped by money, but a common fund which we have with others, when it is necessary to share it with them; but the word ἐυδοκεῖν, because it is to be approved from the heart, when a thing pleases well and from the heart, hints at readiness and cheerfulness in the active contribution of the kingdom, which is also pleasing to GOD. Heb. IX. 7.

They also owe it to serve them in carnal things) You have an equal argument in 1 Cor. IX. 11. He calls those things carnal which pertain to sustaining this life; to serve, here is עבד, to minister, namely to someone's needs. Thus the Apostle called it a minister of need in Philipp. II. 5. and this very gift itself a ministry of the service in 2 Cor. IX. 12.

Latin:

V. 27. ἐυδόκησαν γὰρ) Est egregia ἀναφορὰ, simul cum ἐπανορθώσει.

Καὶ ὀφειλέται αὐτῶν εἰσι) Propriè debet, à quo in jure exigi quid potest. De utroque hoc debendi significatione diximus libr. II. de Jure Belli & Pacis, VII. 4. XIV. 6. XXII. 16. Sic gratiam debere aliquis dicitur. Vide Gel- lium l. 5. Sic vocem ὀφειλέται habuimus supra I. 14. VIII. חובים .12

εἰ γὰρ τοῖς πνευματικοῖς αὐτῶν ἐκοινώνησαν τὰ ἔθνη) Cum prophetias de Christo ab illis acceperint & eorum exemplo in Christum crediderint. Nota κοινωνεῖν sicut Latinum parti- cipare & agendi & patiendi sensu dici.

Non tantùm Prophetias de Christo à Judæis gentes accepêre (quamvis si Grotii corrupte- lis locus esset, paucissimæ Prophetiæ in V. T. de Christo reliquæ forent) ut exemplo eorum in Christum crediderint, sed etiam per Judæos Apostolos nempe, non alias sanctiores & Apo- stolicos viros gentes de Christo informatæ sunt, & ad communionem Ecclesiæ, quæ in populo Judaico erat, congregatæ & admissæ, Eph. II. De κοινωνία notat Erasmus eleemosynam civili isto vocabulo exprimi, quasi non sit beneficium juvari pecunia, sed censum quem habemus cum aliis communem, cum opus est illis impartiri; vox verò ἐυδοκεῖν, quia est ex animo probari, cum res benè & ex animo placet, promptitudinem & hilaritatem in κοινωνίᾳ activa regni innuit, quæ etiam DEO grata est. Ebr. IX. 7.

ὀφείλεσι καὶ ἐν τοῖς σαρκικοῖς λειτυργῆσαι αὐτοῖς) Par ar- gumentum habes 1. Cor. IX. 11. σαρκικὰ vocat, quæ ad hanc vitam sustentandam pertinent λειτυργῆσαι, hic est עבד inservire, nempe alicujus necessitatibus. Sic λειτυρ- γὸν χρείας dixit Apostolus Philipp. II. 5. & ipsam hanc lar- gitionem διακονίαν τῆς λειτυργίας 2. Cor. IX. 12.

## 15:28
V. 28. Having therefore performed this and sealed to them this fruit) is a metonymy. For things that are deposited are accustomed to be sealed. Thus Suetonius in Claudius spoke of a sealed dowry. And he calls that which is born from beneficence fruit. Thus fruits of repentance Matt. III. 8. with mercy and good fruits. James III. 17.

Thus also Flacius says that by the sealing it is shown that ministers ought to handle alms with the best faith, and that they do it as if by a given and accepted bond: and Blessed Wellerus, explaining this matter, where they faithfully returned the collected and entrusted alms sealed to them. According to Beza, it commends both his own diligence and faith to be shown in money, and that of others to be guarded in that matter, in the manner of the ancients, who used to seal with a ring what they wanted to be kept in safety. But something else seems to be hinted at by Blessed Erasmus Schmid: which, however, he does not express. The fruit seems to be indicated as that which is to be sealed of the preaching of the Gospel, and of righteousness, which reached the Gentiles by divine blessing, and was sealed to the faithful Jews by this contribution also, and for the confirmation of himself in the faith, and for the excitement of mutual charity and equal beneficence: for beneficence also pertains to the confirmation and obligation of faith, which is done through fruits and redundantly through true faith.

I will go through you into Spain) even here the better books have into Spain. But it is said through you, that is, through your lands, just as let us go to me, that is, to my house. Such is that: the neighbor Ucalegon is burning.

Latin:

V. 28. τῦτο ὖν ἐπιτελέσας καὶ σφραγισάμενος αὐτοῖς τὸν καρπὸν τῦτον) est μετωνυμία. Nam consignari solent, quæ deponuntur. Ita consignatam dotem dixit Suetonius in Claudio. Et fructum vocat id, quod ex beneficentia na- scitur. Sic καρποὶ μετανοίας Matth. III. 8. μετὰ ἐλέυς καὶ καρπῶν ἀγαθῶν. Jac. III. 17.

Ita etiam Flacius per obsignationem ostendi ait, ministros optima fide eleemosynas tractare oportere, seque id veluti dato acceptoque chi- rographo facere: & B. Wellerus exponens h. m. ubi eleemosynam collectam & commissam fide- liter illis obsignatam reddidêre. Commendat se- cundum Bezam tum suam in pecunia præferen- dam, tum aliorum in ista custodiendam diligen- tiam ac fidem, more veterum, qui annulo obsi- gnabant, quæ in tuto volebant reposita. Sed aliud innui videtur B. Erasmo Schmidio: quod tamen quid sit, non exprimit. Obsignandus videtur fru- ctus indigitari præconii Evangelii, & justitiæ, qui penes gentes divina benedictione pervenit, & hac quoque κοινωνίᾳ fidelibus Judæis obsigna- batur, & ipsius in fide confirmationem, & ad mutuæ charitatis, parilisque beneficentiæ exci- tationem: nam beneficentia pertinet quoque ad confirmationem & obligationem fidei, quæ per fructùs fit & vera fide redundanter.

ἀπελεύσομαι δι ὑμῶν εἰς τὴν ἱσπανίαν) etiam hîc libri meliores εἰς τὴν Σπανίαν. Dictum autem est δι ὑμῶν, id est per vestras terras, sicut eamus ad me, id est, domum meam. Tale illud: proximus ardet Ucalegon.

## 15:29
V. 29. In the fullness of the blessing of the gospel of Christ I shall come) In that manuscript, as also in others, in the fullness of the blessing of Christ, just as Origen, and Ambrose, and the Latin interpreter read, that is, I shall come with the most abundant gifts of Christ, to confirm you, of course. See above I. 11. πλήρωμα signifies abundance, as Job I. 16. So also Cant. V. 13. ἐυλογία is everything that is liberally conferred upon us ברכה Eph. I. 3. Gal. III, 14. For it is a translation from the word to the things, ἐυλογημένη ἐν πληρώματι, is in the inscription of the Ignatian Epistle to the Ephesians.

Latin:

V. 29. ἐν πληρώματι ἐυλογίας τῦ ἐυαγγελίε τῦ χριστῦ ἐλεύσομαι) In Manuscripto illo, ut & in aliis, ἐν πληρώ- ματι ἐυλογίας χριστῦ, quomodo legit & Origenes, & Am- brosius, & Latinus interpres, id est, veniam cum uberri- mis Christi donis, ad vos confirmandos scilicet. Vide supra I. 11. πλήρωμα abundantiam significat, ut Job. I. 16. Sic & Cant. V. 13. ἐυλογία omne id, quod in nos li- beraliter confertur ברכה Eph. I. 3. Gal. III, 14. Est enim translatio à voce ad res ἐυλογημένη ἐν πληρώματι, est in in- scriptione Ignatianæ Epistolæ ad Ephesios.

## 15:30
V. 30. And through the love of the Spirit) through that love which the Holy Spirit has wrought in us.

to strive together with me in prayers for me to God) in prayers by prayers. He said not to help, but to strive together, because prayers are a certain struggle, as appears in Coloss. IV. 12. The struggle of Jacob with the Angel bore the figure of that struggle.

The Greek συναγωνίζεσθαι is to assist, but one who is struggling and laboring. Victory against Satan, the world, and the flesh is obtained through the word, faith, and prayers, with which one must therefore fight 2. Corinth. I. 10. Ephes. VI. 18. 2. Thessal. III. 1. But there is no consequence here, if Paul implores the prayers of the Romans, that it is much more permitted to invoke without any injury to GOD the aid of the Saints reigning in Heaven with Christ. For the living hear us, but the dead are ignorant of us Isa. LXIV. 16. We have commands, examples, and promises concerning soliciting and performing the mutual intercessions of the living, but not of the dead. The intercessions of the living do not derogate from the mediatorial office of Christ: but when Papists seek and implore the intercessions of the dead, that is joined with the Sacrilege of the Mediatorial office of Christ; who alone by the virtue of his merit intercedes for us in the heavens 1. Tim. II. Nor is that entreaty of the living an invocation of them, as Papists invoke the holy dead: but a calling upon and an imploring of the duty of Christian Charity. And how can omnipresence be attributed to the saints, so that they can be heard by all who invoke them anywhere throughout the world: Finally, we ask the living that they may descend into the struggle with us, and fight with prayers against common enemies, which does not befit the holy dead, who are no longer in the militant, but in the triumphant Church.

Latin:

V. 30. Καὶ διὰ τῆς ἀγάπης τῦ πνεύματος) per illam di- lectionem, quam in nobis effecit Spiritus Sanctus.

συναγωνίσασθαι μοι ἐν ταῖς προσευχαῖς ὑπὲρ ἐμῦ πρὸς τὸν θεὸν) ἐν ταῖς προσευχαῖς per preces. Dixit autem non βοη- θεῖν, sed συναγωνίσασθαι, quia preces certamen quoddam sunt, ut apparet Coloss. IV. 12. Ejus certaminis figuram gessit certamen Jacobi cum Angelo.

Græcum συναγωνίζεσθαι est opitulari, sed cer- tanti & laboranti. Victoria adversus Satanam mundum & carnem obtinetur per verbum, fidem ac preces, quibus proinde pugnandum 2. Corinth. I. 10. Ephes. VI. 18. 2. Thessal. III. 1. Nulla verò hic est Consequentia, si Paulus Romanorum pre- ces implorat, multò magis licet invocare sine ul- la injuria DEI opem Sanctorum in Cœlo cum Christo regnantium. Nam vivi nos audiunt, mor- tui verò ignorant nos Esa. LXIV. 16. de vivo- rum mutuis intercessionibus solicitandis & præ- standis habemus mandata, exempla, promissa, non autem de mortuorum. Vivorum intercessio- nes non derogant Christi mediatorio officio: at cum mortuorum intercessiones expetunt & im- plorant Papistæ, conjunctum id est cum Sacrile- gio muneris Mediatorii Christi; qui solus vir- tute meriti sui pro nobis interpellat in cœlis 1. Tim. II. Neque illa exoratio precium penes viventes est invocatio eorum, uti sanctos defun- ctos invocant Papistæ: sed compellatio & officii Christianæ Charitatis imploratio. Et quomodo sanctis tribui potest omnipræsentia, quod exau- diri possint omnes, qui ubivis ipsos invocant per orbem: Denique viventes petimus, ut nobiscum quasi in certamen descendant, & precibus con- tra communes hostes pugnant, quod non con- venit sanctis defunctis, qui non sunt amplius in militante, sed in triumphante Ecclesia.

## 15:31
V. 31. That I may be delivered from those who do not obey in Judea) that I may escape their hands. For he foresaw the danger from their cruelty, see Acts XXI. 11. and following. A similar manner of speaking 1. Thess. III. 2. 2. Cor. I. 10.

And that my service) this work, which I have undertaken in collecting and carrying the money. For such things are called by the name of service, as Acts VI. 1. above XII. 7, 1. Corinth. XVI. 5. 2. Cor. VIII. 4. IX. 1. 12. that to Jerusalem: towards the Christians who are at Jerusalem; a locution similar to that which is above 26.

may be acceptable to the saints) so that, namely, the Jews who had believed in Christ may sincerely love those called from the Gentiles, having seen this kindness of theirs toward them.

Latin:

Καὶ ἵνα ἡ διακονία με) opera hæc, quam sumpsi in col- ligendis perferendisque pecuniis. Talia enim διακονίας nomine vocantur, ut Act. VI. 1. supra XII. 7, 1. Corinth. XVI. 5. 2. Cor. VIII. 4. IX. 1. 12. ἡ εἰς Ἱερυσαλὴμ: erga Christianos, qui sunt Hierosolymis; locutio similis ei quæ supra 26.

εὐπρόσδεκτος γένηται τοῖς ἁγίοις) ut nempe Judæi, qui in Christum crediderant, vocatos ex gentibus sincerè ament, conspecta hac ipsorum in se beneficentia.

## 15:32
V. 32. That I may come with joy to you) Joyful at such a good success of the work.

through the will of God) that is, with GOD prospering my journey to you. Thus in the will of God above in the same matter I. 10.

And may find rest together with you) ἀναπαύεσθαι נוח is to receive comfort, as is to be seen 1. Corinth. XVI. 18. 2. Cor. VII. 13. Philem. v. 7. 20. Συναναπάνεσθαι is to give and receive comfort. The sense is clearly the same as that above in the word συμπαρακληθῆναι I. 12. Genesis IV. 29. where the meaning of the name Noah is explained, in the Greek: this one shall give us rest from our works and from the sorrows of our hands. In the Latin: He shall comfort us from the works and labors of our hands. Ὁ δὲ Θεὸς τῆς εἰρήνης) THE GOD of peace, the author. A form of speaking, such as above 5. Θεὸς τῆς παρακλήσεως. He says this, that he may the more avert the Romans from quarrels. μετὰ πάντων ὑμῶν) May He be present with you, favor you, help you. See what [is said] to Matt. XXVII. 20. and to Luke I. 28.

He who prays that his ministry to the faithful, which he was performing for them by the offering of alms or κοι- νωνίᾳ, and which he was also about to perform for them in the communication of spiritual goods, may be acceptable? Because there were among the converted Jews those to whom Paul was suspected as an enemy of Judaism and a patron of the Gentiles, Acts XXI. 21. seqq. Therefore συναναπάυ- σωμαί ὑμῖν, which is properly, I shall rest together with you, indicates a common refreshment with them, by which he himself might be mutually cheered by their progress in the faith, and they by the sight and grace divinely granted. Conf. Acts XXVIII. 31. Rom. I. 11, 12.

Latin:

V. 32. ἵνα ἐν χαρᾷ ἔλθω πρὸς ὑμᾶς) Lætus tam bono operis successu.

διὰ θελήματος Θεῦ) id est, DEO, iter meum ad vos prosperante. Sic ἐν θελήματι τῦ Θεῦ supra in re ea- dem I. 10.

Καὶ συναναπαύσωμαι ὑμῖν) ἀναπαύεσθαι נוח est solatium accipere, ut videre est 1. Corinth. XVI. 18. 2. Cor. VII. 13. Philem. v. 7. 20. Συναναπάνεσθαι est solatium dare & acci- pere. Sensus planè idem, qui supra in verbo συμπαρα- κληθῆναι I. 12. Genes. IV. 29. ubi explicatur significatio vocis Noë, in Græco: ὗτος διαναπαύσει ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ τῶν ἔργων ἡμῶν καὶ ἀπὸ τῶν λυπῶν τῶν χειρῶν ἡμῶν. In Latino: Iste consolabitur nos ab operibus & laboribus manuum no- strarum. Ὁ δὲ Θεὸς τῆς εἰρήνης) DEUS pacis auctor. Loquendi genus, quale supra 5. Θεὸς τῆς παρακλήσεως. Hoc dicit, ut hoc magis Romanos à rixis avertat. μετὰ πάντων ὑμῶν) Vobis adsit, faveat, opituletur. Vide quæ ad Matth. XXVII. 20. & ad Lucam I. 28.

Qui precatur, ut ministerium suum fidelibus, quod iis præstabat offerenda Eleemosyna vel κοι- νωνίᾳ, quodque in communicatione etiam bono- rum spiritualium ipsis præstiturus erat gratum sit? Quia erant inter Judæos conversos, quibus suspe- ctus erat Paulus quasi Judaismi hostis, & gentium Patronus Act. XXI. 21. seqq. Idcirco συναναπάυ- σωμαί ὑμῖν, quod propriè est, conrequiescam vobis, communem cum ipsis refocillationem, quâ mutuo exhilararentur ipse è profeclibus eorum in fide, & illi è conspectu & gratia divinitus concessa, indicat. Conf. Act. XXIIX. 31. Rom. I. II. 12.

## 16:1 Argument
CHAPTER XVI. AND THE LAST.

The Apostle commends Phoebe, and bids [them] greet Prisca and Aquila, and their domestic Church, Epaenetus, and other saints; and he speaks greeting to them in the name of the Churches, and beseeches them to flee from the heterodox, and prays for the crushing of Satan, and the grace of Christ. He greets them also in the name of Timothy, and of certain other Saints, and again prays for the grace of the Lord for all: finally, with a divine celebration for the manifestation of the Gospel, he ends the Epistle.

There are two parts: The former is affective, declaring the affection of love, as it is then of the Apostle himself toward Phoebe, whom he commends, and toward the Romans, whom he greets, and most of whom he praises at the same time: and also toward all, partly by greeting, partly by dissuasion, partly by prayer: then of others, in whose name he speaks greeting to them: and sealing the Epistle with his own hand with the customary prayer, v. 24. The other is doxological, attributing glory to GOD.

PART I. AFFECTIVE. V. 1. I commend also to you.

Just as certain Epistles are merely commendatory, of which Paul also makes mention in 2 Cor. III. and examples exist in Cicero, so also are parts or additions of certain Epistles. He commends Phoebe, both that she may be helped in her business, and that she may hold her place there, as was the custom in the Synagogues. Concerning commendatory epistles there is Canon VI of Antioch and XI of Constantinople.

Phoebe.

Just as Phoebus is a man's name in Martial, so Phoebe is a woman's.

being a deaconess.

In Judea, male deacons could also minister to women: For there was freer access to women there than in Greece, where the women's quarters were closed to men. Therefore, the Churches in Greece had need of a twofold help from women. Some were elder women or presiding women who formed the morals of women, and before the Synod of Laodicea were ordained by the laying on of hands, as can be seen in Canon XI of that Synod. Others were deacons, in Latin also deaconesses, which Pliny in his letter to Trajan translates as ministers, who relieved poor or sick women with money and service.

Of the church which is in Cenchreae.

Cenchreae, the port of Corinth on the Saronic Gulf. See Acts XVIII. 18.

Latin:

CAPUT XVI. ET ULTIMUM.

Commendat Apostolus Phœben, & salutare jubet Priscam & Aquilam, & Ecclesiam eorum domesticam, Epænetum, aliosque sanctos; & salutem illis dicit nomine Ecclesiarum, atque obsecrat, ut hetero- doxos fugiant, vovetque Satanæ contri- tionem, & Christi gratiam. Salutat etiam nomine Timothei, & aliorum quo- rundam Sanctorum, omnibusque iterum gratiam Domini precatur: tandem cele- bratione divina, pro manifestatione Ev- angelii, finit Epistolam.

Partes duæ sunt: Prior παθητικὴ affectum amo- ris declarans, utpote tùm Apostoli ipsius er- ga Phœben, quam commendat, & erga Roma- nos, quos salutat, ac plerosque simul deprædicat: nec non erga universos, partim salutatione, par- tim dehortatione, partim voto: tum aliorum, quo- rum nomine ipsis salutem dicit: manuque sua ob- signans consueto voto Epistolam, v. 24. Altera est δοξολογικὴ, DEO gloriam tribuens.

PARS I. ΠΑΘΗΤΙΚΗ. V. 1. συνίσημι δὲ ὑμῖν.

Sicut Epistolæ quædam sunt merè συςατικαὶ, quarum & Paulus meminit 2. Cor. III. & exempla exstant apud Ciceronem, ita & Epistolarum quarundam partes sive ad- jectiones. Commendat Phœben, tùm ut adjuvetur in ne- gotiis, tùm ut locum suum ibi teneat, sicut in Synagogis moris erat. De Epistolis commendatitiis est Canon VI. Antiochenus & XI. Constantinopolitanus.

Φοίβην.

Sicut Phœbus nomen viri apud Martialem, sic Phœbe mulieris.

ὖσαν διάκονον.

In Judæa Diaconi viri etiam mulieribus ministrare po- terant: Erat enim ibi liberior ad fœminas aditus, quam in Græcia, ubi viris clausa γυναικωνῖτις. Ideò duplici in Græcia fœminarum auxilio Ecclesiæ opus habuêre. Alte- ræ erant πρεσβύτιδες sive προκαθήμεναι quæ fœminarum mores formabant, & ante Laodicenam Synodum mani- bus impositis ordinabantur, ut videre est Canone ejus Syno- di XI. Aliæ erant διάκονοι, Latinè etiam diaconissæ, quod Plinius in Epistola ad Trajanum vertit ministras, quæ fœ- minas pauperes aut ægrotas pecunia atque opera suble- vabant.

Τῆς ἐκκλησίας τῆς ἐν Κεγχρεαῖς.

Cenchreæ portus Corinthi ad Saronicum sinum. Vide Actor. XVIII. 18.

## 16:2
V. 2. that you may receive her in the Lord) That is, for the sake of Christ, whom she has faithfully served.

worthy of the saints) That is, as it is fitting to receive saints. Thus the adverb worthily often governs the genitive, which the adjective governs.

And assist her in whatever matter she may have need of you) Julian in a letter says that the religion of the Galileans (so he calls Christians) had grown much through their philanthropy toward strangers. Moreover, here to assist is the same as the Latin to be present, to help.

For she herself has been a patron of many, and of me myself) He did not say helper, but adorning her with a clearly magnificent title, he said patron, that is, protectress. Thus at Athens they were called defenders of foreigners. And Plutarch is accustomed to render the Latin word Patron with the Greek term for patron.

From this recommendation it appears that the conclusion added to the Epistle is genuine, because this Epistle was transmitted to the Romans through Phoebe. Who was in the ministry of the Church of Cenchreae, a small town distant from Corinth by 70 stadia: not that she preached publicly, which the Apostle does not grant to women (1 Cor. XIV. 34; 1 Tim. II. 12), but that she instructed privately, and that according to the rite of the primitive Church she ministered to the saints in distributing alms or caring for the sick. He commends her (1) for her religion. For she was a sister, i.e., a companion in the Christian religion. (2) for her office: She was a minister of the saints. (3) for her faithfulness: for she herself served many, and among these even Paul. Concerning the word patron, Suidas says: The patrons of sojourners living in Athens were called patrons. For it was necessary for simple sojourners to take on some Athenian citizen as a patron. And it is clear from Hesychius that it is so called: To whom the care and guardianship of strangers and sojourners was committed. Baronius, in the year of Christ 58, no. 55, thinks that Mary and Tryphaena and Tryphosa, and also Persis, whom the Apostle mentioned in the following verses, were of the same office as Phoebe: but the words, who labored much in the Lord, do not prove this; since labor in the Lord could be of a different kind, and Priscilla, together with her husband Aquila, is also said to have labored in instructing Apollos in the Christian faith. Whom the Apostle calls his fellow-workers a little later: and Baronius acknowledges that such private instruction was not forbidden to women, even if they were ordered to be silent in the Church in public, and that besides instruction and the office of deacons, there were still presiding women in the early Church who would form the morals of women, as was rightly noted by Grotius.

Latin:

V. 2. ἵνα αὐτὴν προσδέξησθε ἐν κυρίῳ) Id est ob Christum, cui fideliter inserviit.

ἀξίως τῶν ἁγίων) Id est, sicut Sanctos excipi oportet. Sic saepe adverbium ἀξίως regit Genitivum, quem regerit adjectivum.

Καὶ παραστῆτε αὐτῇ ἐν ᾧ ἂν ὑμῶν χρῄζῃ πράγματι) Julianus in Epistola multum crevisse ait Galilaeorum (sic ille Christianos appellat) religionem per τὴν πρὸς τοὺς ξένους φιλανθρωπίαν. Est autem hic παριστάναι ut & Latinis adesse, opitulari.

Καὶ γὰρ αὕτη προστάτις πολλῶν ἐγενήθη, καὶ αὐτοῦ ἐμοῦ) Non dixit παραστάτις adjutrix, sed magnifico plane titulo eam exornans dixit προστάτιν, id est Patronam. Sic Athenis dicebantur peregrinorum defensores. Et Plutarchus Latinam vocem Patroni προστάτην solet reddere.

Ex hac commendatione apparet, veram esse clausulam Epistolae adjectam, quod per Phoeben transmissa fuerit Romanis haec Epistola. Quae in ministerio fuit Ecclesiae Cenchreensis, oppiduli distantis a Corintho 70. stadiis: non quod verbum publice praedicaverit, quod mulieribus non concedit Apostolus 1. Cor. XIV. 34. 1. Tim. II. 12. sed quod privatim informavit, quodque juxta ritum primitivae Ecclesiae Sanctis ministraverit in distribuendis eleemosynis, aut curandis aegrotis. Commendat eam (1.) a religione. Fuit enim ἀδελφὴ, h. e. Christianae religionis socia. (2.) ab officio: Fuit administra sanctorum. (3.) a fidelitate: ipsa enim pluribus servivit, & inter hos Paulo etiam. De voce προστάτης Suidas: Inquilinorum Athenis degentium Patroni προστάται vocabantur. Necesse enim erat simplices inquilinos aliquem civem Atheniensem assumere Patronum. Et ex Hesychio patet ita dictum: Cui cura & tutela advenarum & inquilinorum commissa erat. Baronius ad ann. Christi 58. n. 55. ejusdem muneris cum Phoebe fuisse & Mariam & Tryphaenam ac Tryphosam, nec non Persidem, quarum mentionem in sequentibus fecit Apostolus, existimat: sed id verba, quae multum laboravit in Domino, non probant: quum diversi generis labor in Domino esse potuerit, & Priscilla una cum marito Aquila etiam in informando Apollo in fide Christiana laborasse dicatur. Quos paulo post συνέργους suos vocat Apostolus: nec informationem ejusmodi privatam mulieribus prohibitam fuisse, agnoscit Baronius, etsi in publico jussae sint tacere in Ecclesia, & praeter informationem ac munus τῶν διακόνων adhuc fuisse προκαθημένας in Veteri Ecclesia, quae foeminarum mores formarent, recte notatum fuit Grotio.

## 16:3
V. 3. Greet Priscilla and Aquila.

Origen teaches that Prisca was written in this place, just as some manuscripts have it, and the Latin reads: and he conjectures that she is the same one who is called Priscilla in the Acts. Correctly: for the names of women were sometimes stated simply, sometimes as diminutives. Thus Livia, the wife of Drusus, is Livia to Tacitus, but always Livilla to Suetonius. Thus those who are Claudia to Tacitus are Claudilla to Suetonius. Such are Secundilla, Tertulla, Quartilla, for Secunda, Tertia, Quarta. Learn from this that the edict of Claudius against the Jews did not flourish for long, having sharp beginnings, as such things usually do, but a careless end, as Tacitus says.

My fellow-workers in Christ Jesus.

Paul deservedly honors them with this name, since not only the man, but also the woman, devoted effort to bringing others to Christianity. Acts XVI. 26.

The wife is placed before the husband on account of her greater fervor and piety, as the Syrian Scholiast notes. Chrysostom, on 1 Corinthians XIV. 34, rightly observes that private admonition is not forbidden to women, but only the public preaching of the word, which we have also noted before. He prohibits them from the precedence that occurs in the midst of the Churches, and from a seat in the pulpit, but not from the word of doctrine: for he does not cut off the method which pertains to private use, but that which takes place in the middle and in the common theater, which is appropriate for the Doctors themselves: although some rightly maintain that public instruction is not prohibited for women in an extraordinary manner and in a case of necessity; but only ordinarily, and outside a case of necessity: just as it is established that Prophetesses were also once raised up by God himself, who publicly announced the will of God. Priscilla and Aquila seem to have returned to Rome from Corinth after the death of Claudius, by whom they had been driven from Rome, when Nero was made Emperor.

Latin:

V. 3. ἀσπάσασθε Πρίσκιλλαν καὶ Ἀκύλαν.

Origenes docet hoc loco Πρίσκαν scriptum fuisse hoc loco, quomodo & habent quidam Manuscripti, & legit Latinus: & conjicit eandem esse quae in Actis Priscilla dicitur. Recte: nam foeminarum nomina modo simpliciter enunciabantur, modo ὑποκοριστικῶς. Sic Livia Drusi uxor Tacito, quae semper Suetonio Livilla. Sic quae Claudiae Tacito, Suetonio Claudilla. Tales sunt Secundilla, Tertulla, Quartilla, pro Secunda, Tertia, Quarta. Discas hinc edictum Claudii contra Judaeos non diu viguisse, acribus, ut ferme talia, initiis, incurioso fine, ut loquitur Tacitus.

Τοὺς συνεργούς μου ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ.

Merito hoc nomine eos ornat Paulus, cum non vir tantum, sed & mulier aliis ad Christianismum perducendis operam dederint. Act. XVI. 26.

Praeponitur uxor marito ob fervorem majorem & pietatem notante Scholiaste Syro. Non interdici foeminis privatam commonefactionem, sed tantum publicam verbi praedicationem recte observat Chrysostomus ad 1. Corinth. XIV. 34. quod de etiam antea monuimus. Praecedentiam, quae fit in medio Ecclesiarum, illis prohibet, sedemque in pulpito, non doctrinae verbum: non enim doctrina rationem, quæ ad privatum usum pertinet, ampu- tat, sed eam, quæ in medio fit, & in communi thea- tro, quæ ipsis congruit Doctoribus: quamvis non- nulli extraordinariè, & in casu necessitatis etiam mulieribus non prohibitam esse publicam infor- mationem, rectè statuant; sed solum ordinariè, & extra casum necessitatis: quemadmodum Pro- phetissas etiam à Deo ipso olim excitatas esse con- stat, quæ publicè voluntatem Dei annuncia- runt. Reversi Priscilla & Aquila Romam Co- rintho videntur post mortem Claudii, à quo Roma pulsi erant, Nerone Imperatore creato.

## 16:4
Verse 4. who for my life laid down their own necks) In that sedition, of which mention is made in Acts 18:17. Moreover, the expression τράχηλον ὑποτιθέναι is proverbial, in the same way as 'to give necks' and 'to offer necks'. It is found in Cicero and Juvenal. Thus also 'to expose one's head to dangers' is a frequent expression.

Others refer it to the sedition at Ephesus stirred up by Demetrius in Acts 19:24. But it is more correctly referred to that Corinthian one, as appears from the circumstances of Acts 18.

to whom not only I give thanks, but also all the churches of the Gentiles) Namely, those which are around Corinth.

Latin:

Vers. 4. οἵτινες ὑπὲρ τῆς ψυχῆς μυ τὸν ἑαυτῶν τράχηλον ὑπέθηκαν) In ista seditione, cujus mentio Actor. XVIII. 17. Est autem proverbialis locutio τράχηλον ὑποτιθέναι, quo- modo dare cervices & præbere cervices. Est apud Cicero- nem & Juvenalem. Sic & caput objicere periculis, fre- quens locutio.

Alii ad seditionem Ephesi per Demetrium exci- tatam Act. XIX. 24. referunt. Sed rectius refer- tur ad illam Corinthiacam, ut ex circumstantiis Act. XVIII. apparet.

οἷς ὐκ ἐγὼ μόνος ἐυχαρισῶ, ἀλλὰ κὶ πᾶσαι αἱ ἐκκλησίαι τῶν ἐθνῶν) Nempe quæ circa Corinthum.

## 16:5
and the church in their house) Paul speaks in the same way about their house in 1 Corinthians 16:20. Because the Christians were returning recently from exile, it is credible that when Paul wrote these things, there were no common assemblies of Christians at Rome, nor Presbyters, whom Paul would otherwise have greeted. But in such a time, every house is a Church, just as Tertullian says: Where there are three, there is a Church, even if they are laymen. See Beza on Acts 21:4.

From this most sweet appellation (of Church) we are taught that marriage is so far from hindering the exercise of piety, that it is as it were a compendium of common operation in a public assembly, which the Holy Spirit represents to us in any pious family. Then we are also warned of what kind of person everyone ought to show themselves to be in their own home as well. For if there is a Church of God even in a familiar assembly, one must live piously and honestly, not only publicly: but also in a domestic assembly, as this blessed Mylius.

Verse 5. Greet Epaenetus my beloved. Great praise to be exceptionally loved by him who loved everyone.

Epaenetus, who is believed to have been one of the 70 Disciples. Dorotheus in his Synopsis hands down that he was Bishop of Carthage, but Baronius notes at the year of Christ 58, number 56, that no mention of him is found among African Ecclesiastical writers.

who is the firstfruits of Achaia unto Christ. Origen and the Latin interpreter read 'of Asia'. And even now some codices have it thus: and thus Jerome cites it several times, and I judge that to be correct. For Epaenetus is not the firstfruits of Achaia, but Stephanas in 1 Corinthians 16:15. Thus are called those who had believed first in each nation, with the similarity drawn from those offerings which are תרומות to the Hebrews, and ἀπαρχαὶ to the Hellenists. See above 8:23. 11:6. Clement also uses ἀπαρχὰς in the same sense in his Epistle to the Corinthians regarding those who believed first.

These are not sufficient reasons why we should prefer 'of Asia' instead of 'of Achaia'. For even if Stephanas is numbered among the firstfruits of Achaia in 1 Corinthians 16:15, nothing prevents Epaenetus from being able to be reckoned among the same, if he himself was converted together with Stephanas: for it is by no means inconvenient for several to be converted at once. Moreover, the different writing of one or another cannot prejudice the common reading of the codices: with which Chrysostom and Theodoret agree.

Latin:

κὰὶ τὴν κατ' οἶκον αὐτῶν ἐκκλησίαν) Eodem modo de illo- rum domo loquitur Paulus 1. Cor. XVI. 20. Quia recens ab exilio redibant Christiani, credibile est, cum hæc Pau- lus scriberet, nullos Romæ fuisse communes Christiano- rum conventus, neque Presbyteros, quos alioqui salutaret Paulus. Tali autem in tempore quæque domus Ecclesia est, sicut Tertullianus ait: Ubi tres, Ecclesia est, licet laici. Vide Bezam ad Act. XXI. 4.

Ex hac suavissima (Ecclesiæ) appellatione do- cemur, conjugium pietatis exercitio adeò non ob- stare, ut operationis communis in cætu publico, quasi compendium quod tam Spiritus Sanctus in pia quavis familia nobis repræsentet. Tum illud etiam monemur, qualem domi suæ quoque præbe- re sese quivis debeat. Nam si in familiari etiam cætu Deo sua est Ecclesia, piè projecto, honeste- que est vivendum, non publicè tantum: Sed in cætu etiam domestico, ut hic Beatus My- lius.

Vers. 5. ἀσπάσασθε Ἐπαινετὸν ἀγαπητόν μυ. Magna laus eximiè diligi ab eo, qui omnes dilige- bat.

Epanetum, qui creditur fuisse è LXX. Discipu- lis. Dorotheus in Synopsi tradit Carthaginiensem fuisse Episcopum, sed nullam ejus mentio- nem reperiri apud Africanos Scriptores Eccle- siasticos notat Baronius ad Annum Christi 58. nu- mer. 56.

ὅς ἐστιν ἀπαρχὴ τῆς Ἀχαΐας εἰς χριστὸν. Ἀσίας legit Origenes & Latinus interpres. Et nunc quoque nonnulli codices sic habent: & sic aliquoties ci- tat Hieronymus, & id rectum arbitror. Nam ἀπαρχὴ Achajæ, non Epænetus, sed Stephanas 1. Cor. XVI. 15. Sic vocantur, qui in quaque gente primi crediderant, simi- litudine ducta ab illis oblationibus, quæ תרומות He- bræis, ἀπαρχαὶ Hellenistis. Vide supra VIII. 23. XI. 6. usurpat ἀπαρχὰς eodem sensu de his, qui primi credide- runt, etiam Clemens in Epistola ad Corinthios.

Causæ hæ sufficientes non sunt, cur loco Ἀχαΐας præferamus Ἀσίας. Etsi enim Stephanas primitiis Achajæ annumeretur 1. Cor. XVI. 15. nihil tamen obstat, quò minus etiam Epænetus inter easdem censeri possit, si una cum Stephanâ ipse conversus fuerit: simul enim plures uno con- verti minimè inconveniens est. Unius autem & alterius diversa scriptio non potest præjudicare communi codicum lectioni: cui consonat Chry- sostomus & Theodoretius.

## 16:6
Verse 6. Greet Mary. The name expresses the Syriac מַרְיָם. See on Matthew 1:16. The name was very frequent, because of the sister of Moses being so called.

who labored much for us. That is, for our sake.

She was a holy woman, celebrated with this eulogy, that she had labored much in them; namely, in the duties of piety and Christian hospitality; with which she had affected the faithful living at Rome: and Paul imputes these to himself also, although he had not yet seen Rome: for the goods and benefits of friends are common, especially among Christians.

Latin:

Vers. 6. Ἀσπάσασθε Μαριάμ. Nomen exprimit Syriacum מַרְיָם. Vide ad Matth. I. 16. Nomen erat valdè frequens, ob sororem Mosis ita dictam.

ἥτις πολλὰ ἐκοπίασε εἰς ἡμᾶς. Id est, pro nobis.

Fœmina fuit sancta, hoc elogio celebrata, quòd multum laboraverit in ipsis; officiis nimi- rum pietatis & Christianæ hospitalitatis; quibus fi- deles Romæ degentes affecerat: eaque Paulus sibi etiam imputat, licet Romam nondum vide- rit: amicorum enim bona ac beneficia sunt com- munia, præsertim inter Christianos.

## 16:7
Vers. 7. Andronicum) Since this man was a Jew, being a kinsman of Paul, this Greek name is expressed from the Jewish: which I think was מַצְא־נִצַח Masinissa among the Carthaginians. καὶ Ἰουνίαν) She seems to have been the wife of Andronicus, whose name was פְּעֵרָה. τοὺς συγγενεῖς μου) because perhaps Andronicus had married an heiress as a relative. καὶ συναιχμαλώτους μου) The discourse grows. For it is a greater honor to be a participant of sufferings for Christ than of blood. He treats Aristarchus with equal honor Coloss. IV. 10. and Epaphras, Philem. 23. but Paul was often in chains, as can be seen 2. Cor. VI. 5. Clement in his Epistle to the Corinthians concerning Paul: ἑπτάκις δεσμὰ φορέσας. οἵτινές εἰσιν ἐπίσημοι ἐν τοῖς Ἀποστόλοις) That is, who are well known even to the other Apostles: as the Syriac also seems to have understood it: nor is that a wonder, since it follows: οἳ καὶ πρὸ ἐμοῦ γεγόνασιν ἐν Χριστῷ) That is, in the Church of Christ: these were either from those LXX, who were present with the Apostles at Pentecost, or from the first ones converted through Peter.
