Adjun- git autem sibi eundem non tantum modestiæ & humilitatis, sed etiam alios sibi conciliandi causa : quia in magna penes Corinthios authoritate fuit Sosthenes.

## 1:1 Argument
PART I. OF THE EPISTLE. CORRECTIVE-DIDACTIC. CHAPTER I.

ARGUMENT AND PARTITION.

The inscription having been premised, with the prayer for grace, and the celebration of GOD for the grace exhibited to the Corinthians, and the sealing of the preserving grace, the Apostle exhorts to concord, not without correction on account of the schism of those who were not discordant in faith, and with a tacit disparagement of the cause of the same, namely the persuasion of singular wisdom, having proposed first the divine εὐδοκία (good pleasure) concerning saving men through the proclamation of Christ crucified, who although he is a scandal to the Jews, and foolishness to the wise of the world, is nevertheless to the elect the power of GOD, and the wisdom of GOD, and has been made for us by GOD wisdom, and righteousness, and sanctification, and Redemption, so that we may glory uniquely in him. Flacius not inelegantly thus: After the Gratulation v. 10, which has the force of exhorting, 12, he taxes the dissensions of the Corinthians, 17, and recalls them from pride to humility: 20, For overturning all the wisdom of the world, 23, 24, he erects the preaching of the cross alone.

Furthermore, he calls himself an Apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of GOD, so that he may testify that he was also sent immediately, not out of arrogance, but for the sake of authority, concerning whose calling see Acts 9 and 22. By which very thing he establishes the canonical authority of this Epistle, because it was written by an Apostle of Christ called by divine will, and inspired by the Holy Spirit, John 16:13. But when he calls himself an Apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of GOD, he distinguishes Christ from GOD, not by reason of essence (for he is one God with the Father), but by reason of person: just as he neither denies that he is an Apostle of GOD, nor that he was sent by the will of Christ: but he acknowledges GOD the Father as the source of his calling, but implies that he was called and sent by Christ, who appeared to him: so that meanwhile that which Christ testified in John 5:19 may remain, whatever things the Father does, these the Son also does likewise. But there is one calling by which Paul is said to be called, and another by which the Corinthians are said to be called. Paul was called to the Apostolic office: the Corinthians to faith in Christ and the communion of the saints.

to the church of God which is in Corinth. Thus speaks both Clement, and Ignatius often. sanctified in Christ Jesus. We have already said that Clement also speaks thus. Ignatius also: to the sanctified church.

Latin:

PARS I. EPISTOLÆ. ΕΠΑΝΟΡΘΩΤΙΚΟ - ΔΙΔΑΚΤΙΚΗ. CAPUT I.

ARGUMENTUM ET PARTITIO.

Præmissa inscriptione, gratiæ appreactione, & DEI progratia Corinthiis exhibita cele- bratione, gratiæq, conservatricis obsigna- tione, adhortatur Apostolus ad concordi- am, non sine correptione ob schisma eorũ, qui in fide discordes non erant, & tacita causæ ejusdem, persuasionis nempe singu- laris sapientiæ suggillatione, proposita im- primis εὐδοκία divina de salvandis homi- nibus per præconium de Christo crucifixo, qui etsi Judæis scandalum, sapientibus mundi stultitia est, electis tamen potentia DEI, & sapientia DEI, nobisque à DEO sapientia, & justitia, & sanctificatio, & Redemptio factus est, ut unice in ipso glo- riemur. Flacius non inconcinne ita: Post Gratulationem v. 10. quæ vim ha- bet exhortandi, 12. taxat dissidia Co- rinthiorum, 17. eosq; à fastu ad hu- militatem revocat: 20. Nam ever- tens omnem mundi sapientiam, 23. 24. solam crucis prædicationem erigit.

Porro se dicit Apostolum Jesu Christi per vo- luntatem DEI, ut immediate etiam se missum testetur, non ex arrogantia, sed autoritatis gratia, de cujus vocatione vid. Act. IX. & XXII. Quo ipso adstruit autoritatem hujus Epistolæ canoni- cam, quod eadem ab Apostolo Christi per divi- nam voluntatem vocato, & per Spiritum Sanctum inspirato conscripta sit Joh. XVI. 13. Cum vero Apostolum Jesu Christi per voluntatem DEI se dicit, Christum à DEO distinguit, non ratione essentiæ (unus enim est cum Patre Deus,) sed ra- tione personæ : quemadmodum nec negat se Apo- stolum DEI esse, nec voluntate Christi se missum esse: sed DEUM Patrem vocationis suæ fontem agnoscit, à Christo verò, qui sibi apparuit, voca- tum & missum innuit: ut maneat interim quod Christus Joh. V. 19. testatus est, quæcunque Pater facit eadem similiter & Filius facit. Alia autem est vocatio, qua Paulus, alia qua Corinthii vocari di- cuntur. Paulus ad Apostolicum officium vocatus est: Corinthii ad fidem in Christum & commu- nionem sanctorum.

τῆ ἐκκλησίᾳ τῶ Θεῶ τῆ ὔσῃ ἐν Κορίνθῳ. Ita loquitur & Clemens, & Ignatius sæpe. ἡγιασμένοις ἐν Χριςῷ Ἰησῦ. Sic & Clementem loqui jam diximus. Ignatius quo- que : ἐκκλησίᾳ ἡγιασμένῃ.

## 1:2
V. 2. To the called saints, with all who call upon the name of our Lord Jesus Christ in every place, both theirs and ours.

There are three parts: I. Entrance and preparation up to v. 9. II. Exhortation to concord, and correction on account of schism, up to v. 17. III. Information concerning the Gospel of the cross of Christ, which is not to be preached with wise words, inasmuch as it is foolishness to the world, but to those being saved it is the power and wisdom of GOD, up to the end, v. 31.

He shows that the calling is common to all, and therefore that there ought to be one body, not only of one place, but of all places, for instance the Church of Achaia and Macedonia, in which Paul was at that time.

PART I. CHAP. I. PROOEMIUM or PREFACE.

He adorns the Corinthian Church with excellent titles, both so that they might more easily admit the Apostolic corrections, which proceeded not from a sinister affection but from a desire for their salvation, and so that they might attend more diligently to what he teaches those sanctified in Christ, called, saints, calling upon the name of the Lord. Conf. Col. III. 12. 2. Tim. II. 19. Although indeed atrocious crimes, confusions, abuses, and errors had flourished among the Corinthians, nevertheless, as Heshusius rightly observes on p. 8, he does not derogate the august name of Church from this assembly. For because he had preached the pure doctrine of the Gospel in that place, he does not doubt that GOD has His own there, who rightly call upon God, truly believe in the mediator, and are temples of the Holy Spirit. Neither the Epicureans, who deform the Church with crimes, nor hypocrites or heretics, who mix themselves with the pious. V. 1. παῦλος κλητὸς ἀπόςολος.. See what was said at Rom. 1. διὰ θελήματος Θεῦ. Thus Clement writes to the Corinthians, κλητοῖς ἡγιασμένοις ἐν θελήματι Θεῦ. In the Epistle of Ignatius to the Roman Church: πεφωτισμένῃ ἐν θελήματι Θεῦ. καὶ Σωσθένης ὁ ἀδελφὸς. Paul teaches modesty from the very beginning, associating with himself a man much his inferior (he seems, however, to be the one whose mention is in Acts XVIII. 17).

Although the Apostle associates Sosthenes with himself, he nevertheless speaks for the most part in the singular in this Epistle.

rum to the assembly, they utterly cut off the Church: For the Church is forced to bear these as cancers in the world. The Anabaptists, Donatists, and Cathari are therefore mistaken, who seek such a Church on earth in which no evil men are mixed with the good: And in which no schisms and scandals arise: For the Evangelical net encloses good and bad fish, until the Angels on the shore select the good from the bad. Chrysostom beautifully teaches how all these things contribute to the Apostle's design of admonishing concerning schism and other vices. You see, he says, how in individual expressions he depressed their swelling, through everything accustoming the mind to heaven. He calls it the Church of GOD, showing that it ought to be united. For the name of Church is not a name of separation, but of union, and concord, and consensus. To those sanctified in Christ Jesus. Again he places the name of Jesus, but by no means the name of men. But what is sanctification? A washing, a purgation. For he calls to memory their very uncleanness, from which he liberated them: and he persuades them not to be of too proud and elated a mind: for they were saved not by those things which they did rightly, but by the kindness and clemency of GOD. To the called saints. For he says this very thing, that they were saved by faith. For you did not approach first, but you were called. Wherefore not even this whole thing is yours. Although even if you had approached, when you were subject to innumerable evils, not even then is it yours, but it is freely from GOD. Therefore, writing also to the Ephesians, he said: By grace you have been saved through faith, and this is not of yourselves, nor is your faith complete. For you did not believe first, but being called, you obeyed. But he does not look only to the Churches of Achaia and Macedonia, but to all the faithful who call upon the name of the Lord ἐν παντὶ τόπῳ, in every place, implying a communion of faith with all throughout the whole world, which persuades that unity and concord are to be cultivated not only with the members of the same Church, but with all the faithful, so that all may call upon God with one mind, and serve the Lord with one shoulder. This Epistle, therefore, is Catholic, inscribed and consecrated to all who call upon the name of the Lord, even if it was directed to the Corinthians and inscribed to them particularly. From which it appears that the Apostle did not wish to bar anyone from the reading of Scripture, much less the Laity in general, which the Pope does, because he consecrated the same to all the faithful in every place. By ἐπικαλεῖσθαι, however, is understood invocation, or the profession of the divine name, and thus (by Synecdoche) the entire Christian worship, the chief part of which is fiducial invocation. Which Chrysostom observes: Although those letters were written only to the Corinthians, he nevertheless mentions all the faithful who are on earth, showing that the Church which is in the whole world ought to be one, although separated in many places: and much more the one which is at Corinth. But if place separates, yet the Lord joins them, since He is common. Chrysostom indeed draws those αὐτῶν τε καὶ ἡμῶν to τὸν Κύριον, but the pronoun ἡμῶν had already been added to that name, and these pronouns are to be referred immediately to the words ἐν παντὶ τόπῳ: Meanwhile, Chrysostom's argument remains firm, that the Lord is common: for because Jesus Christ is invoked as Lord in every place, He is acknowledged as Lord by all. Thus, those who are in different places, as Chrysostom rightly says, if they do not have lords, but one only, places are nothing to them for concord, since the Lord, who is one, joins them. I do not say, he says, that you ought to be in concord only with the Corinthians, since you are Corinthians: but also with all who are in the whole world, since you have a common Lord.

Moreover, although many hypocrites and impious men were mixed into the Corinthian Church, the Apostle nevertheless calls them sanctified, not making the faithful, with the Papists, adulterers or unjust, for he says they were such formerly, and asserts they were washed, and sanctified, and justified 1 Cor. VI. 13. but taking the denomination from the better part. For those are properly of the Church, but others, although they are in the Church, are not of the Church: the former properly constitute the Church, as it is the communion of saints, the latter indeed adhere by external profession to the assembly of the saints, yet they are not members of the living Church. In vain, however, do the Calixtine Innovators say that the Pontificians and Calvinists, even not obstructing their own errors, are to be admitted into mystical communion, because the Apostle adorns them also with these titles of Church and sanctified in the Lord, from whom erroneous dogmas were being scattered: as for instance concerning the resurrection of the dead and others, because not so much those who were scattering them, as those who were seduced by them, were still moving in that Corinthian Church by external profession, yet a fundamental error denying the resurrection of the flesh, which the Apostle refers among the θεμέλια & στοιχεῖα τῆς ἀρχῆς τῶν λο- γίων τοῦ Θεοῦ Heb. V. 12. c. VI. 1. 2. is not to be held, or those who cherish the same can be considered holy, and sanctified in the Lord, and calling upon the name of the Lord with true faith: because a fundamental error in faith cannot consist with faith: but this denomination is made by Synecdoche from the better and superior part: therefore Ambrose warned that the Apostle wrote to two peoples in one congregation, so that there might be a rebuke of the bad, but praise of the good. It is the custom, says August. Ep. LIX. of Scripture, to speak of a part as if of the whole, just as he praises the Corinthians in the first parts of his Epistle as if all were such, when some of them were praiseworthy, and afterwards in some places of the Epistle he rebukes them as if all were culpable, because of certain ones who were such.

Partes tres sunt: Ingressus & præparatio usque ad v. 9. II. Parænesis ad concordiam, & cor- reptio ob schisma, ad v. 17. III. Informatio de Ev- angelio de cruce Christi, quod non verbis sapien- tibus prædicandum, utpote quod mundo stultitia, salvandis vero DEI potentia est & sapientia, usque ad finem, v. 31.

Ostendit vocationem omnibus esse communem, ac pro- inde unum esse corpus debere, non tantum unius loci, sed omnium locorum, puta Achajæ & Macedoniæ, in qua tum erat Paulus, Ecclesiam.

PARS I. CAP. I. PROOEMIUM vel PRÆFATIO.

Corinthiacam Ecclesiam titulis egregiis ornat, tum ut facilius correptiones Apostolicas, non ex sinistro affectu, sed desiderio salutis ipsorum pro- fectas admittant, tum ut diligentius, quid sancti- ficatos in Christo, vocatos, sanctos, nomen Domini invocantes doceat, attendant. Conf. Col. III. 12. 2. Tim. II. 19. Quanquam vero atrocia apud Co- rinthios viguerant scelera, confusiones, abusus & errores, tamen, ut recte Heshusius p. 8. obser- vat, augustum nomen Ecclesiæ non derogat huic cœtui. Quia enim puram in isto loco prædicave- rat Evangelii doctrinam, non dubitat, quin DEUS habeat ibi suos, qui recte Deum invocent, vere cre- dant in mediatorem, & sint templa Spiritus Sancti. Nec Epicurei, qui sceleribus deformant Ecclesiam, nec hypocritæ aut hæretici, qui sese immiscet pio- V. 1. παῦλος κλητὸς ἀπόςολος.. Vide quæ dicta ad Rom. 1. διὰ θελήματος Θεῦ. Sic Corinthiis, κλητοῖς ἡγιασμένοις ἐν θελήματι Θεῦ scribit Clemens. In Epistola Ignatii ad Ecclesiam Roma- nam : πεφωτισμένῃ ἐν θελήματι Θεῦ. καὶ Σωσθένης ὁ ἀδελφὸς. Modestiam ab initio jam docet Paulus, hominem mul- to sibi imparem (videtur autem is esse, cujus mentio Act. XVIII. 17.) sibi socians.

Quamvis societ sibi Sosthenem Apostolus, in singulari tamen plerumque loquitur in hac Epi-

rum cœtui, penitus exscindunt Ecclesiam: Hæc enim tanquam carcinomata ferre cogitur Ecclesia in or- be. Errant ergo Anabaptistæ, Donatistæ & Cathari, qui talem Ecclesiam quærunt in terris, in qua nulli sint mali admixti bonis: Et in qua nulla exorian- tur schismata & scandala: Evangelica enim sage- na concludit bonos & malos pisces, donec Angeli in littore seligant bonos à malis. Chrysostomus pul- cre docet, quomodo omnia hæc ad institutum Apostoli de Schismate aliisque vitiis monituri faciant. Vides, inquit, quomodo in singulis dictio- nibus depressit eorum tumorem, per omnia mentem cœlo assuefaciens. Ecclesiam DEI vocat, ostendens eam oportere esse unitam. Nomen enim Ecclesiæ non est nomen separationis, sed unionis, & concordiæ, & consensus. Sanctificatis in Christo Jesu. Rur- sus ponit nomen Jesu, nequaquam autem nomen ho- minum. Quid est autem sanctificatio? Lavacrum, purgatio. In memoriam enim revocat ipsam eorum immunditiam, à qua eos liberavit: & suadet ne nimis superbo & elato sint animo: non enim iis quæ recte gesserunt, sed DEI benignitate & clementiâ sunt servati. Vocatis sanctis. Etenim hoc ipsum dicit, fide fuisse salvos. Non enim accessistis primi, sed vocati estis. Quamobrem ne hoc quidem par- vum totum est vestrum. Quanquam etiam si ac- cessissetis, quum malis innumerabilibus essetis obno- xii, ne sic quidem vobis, sed DEO est gratis. Pro- pterea ad Ephesios quoque scribens dicebat: Gratia salvi facti estis per fidem, & hoc non ex vobis, neque fides vestra est integra. Neque enim vos prius cre- didistis, sed vocati obedistis. Non autem tantum Achajæ & Macedoniæ Ecclesias respicit, sed fide- les omnes, qui nomen Domini invocant ἐν παντὶ τόπῳ, in omni loco, communionem fidei cum uni- versis per totum terrarum orbem innuens, quæ non cum ejusdem Ecclesiæ membris solum uni- tatem & concordiam esse colendam suadeat, sed cum fidelibus omnibus, ut omnes una mente Deum invocent, uno humero Domino serviant. Epistola ergo hæc Catholica est, omnibus, qui in- vocant nomen Domini, inscripta & consecrata, etsi ad Corinthios directa fuerit, iisque inscripta pe- culiariter. Ex quo apparet, à Scripturæ lectio- ne arcere noluisse Apostolum quenquam, ne- dum Laicos in universum, quod Papa facit, quia omnibus eandem consecravit fidelibus ubique lo- corum. Per ἐπικαλεῖσθαι vero invocatio, vel pro- fessio nominis divini, adeoque (Synechdochice) totus cultus Christianus intelligitur, cujus præci- pua pars est fiducialis invocatio. Quod observat Chrysostomus: Etsi eæ literæ solum scriptæ sint ad Corinthios, meminit tamen omnium fidelium, qui sunt in terra, ostendens, quod, quæ est in toto orbe terrarum, Ecclesiam oportet esse unam, licet multis locis separatam: & multo magis eam, quæ est Co- rinthi. Si autem locus separat, sed Dominus eos conjungit, quum sit communis. Trahit quidem Chry- sostomus illa αὐτῶν τε καὶ ἡμῶν ad τὸν Κύριον, sed illi nomini additum jam erat pronomen ἡμῶν, & hæc pronomina immediate ad verba ἐν παντὶ τόπῳ referenda: Interim argumentum Chryso- stomi firmum manet, quod Dominus communis sit: quia enim in omni loco Jesus Christus ceu Dominus invocatur, ab omnibus Dominus agno- scitur. Ita qui sunt in diversis locis, ut recte Chry- sost. si non habeant dominos, sed unum solum, eis loca nihil absunt ad concordiam, quum Dominus, qui est unus, eos conjungat. Non dico, inquit, quod cum Corinthiis solum, quum Corinthii sitis, vos con- cordes esse oporteat: sed etiam cum omnibus qui sunt in toto orbe terrarum, quum communem habea- tis Dominum.

Cæterum etsi in Ecclesia Corinthiaca hypo- critæ & impii multi admixti fuerint, sanctificatos tamen dicit Apostolus, non fideles, cum Papistis, adulteros, aut injustos faciens, tales enim fuisse quondam dicit, & ablutos, & sanctificatos, & justi- ficatos asserit 1. Cor. VI. 13. sed à potiori denomina- tionem petens. Nam illi proprie de Ecclesia sunt, alii vero etsi in Ecclesia sint, non tamen de Eccle- sia: illi proprie constituunt Ecclesiam, utpote quæ communio sanctorum est, alii adhærent quidem externa professione cœtui sanctorum, non tamen membra vivæ Ecclesiæ sunt. Nequicquam vero inde Novatores Calixtini Pontificios & Calvinia- nos, etiam non obstantibus ipsorum erroribus, in communionem mysticam admittendos dicunt, quod Apostolus eos quoque istis Ecclesiæ & sancti- ficatorum in Domino titulis ornet, à quibus erro- nea dogmata spargebantur: utpote de resurrectione mortuorum & alia, quia non tam illi qui ea spar- gebant, quam qui ab iisdem seducti erant, in Ec- clesia illa Corinthiaca adhuc externa professione versabantur, non tamen vel non habendus fun- damentalis error negans resurrectionem carnis, quam inter θεμέλια & στοιχεῖα τῆς ἀρχῆς τῶν λο- γίων τοῦ Θεοῦ refert Apostolus Ebr. V. 12. c. VI. 1. 2. vel qui eundem fovent sancti, & sanctificati in Domino, & cum vera fide nomen Domini invo- cantes censeri possunt: quia error fundamentalis in fide, cum fide nequit consistere: sed est Synec- dochica hæc denominatio à potiori & meliori par- te facta: ideo monuit Ambrosius, Apostolum in una plebe duobus scripsisse populis, ut increpatio ma- lorum sit, laus vero bonorum. Est mos, inquit August. Ep. LIX. Scripturæ, ita loqui de parte tan- quam de toto, sicut Corinthios in primis Epistolæ suæ partibus ita laudat, tanquam omnes tales sint, cum essent laudabiles quidam eorum, & postea in non- nullis Epistolæ locis ita reprehendit, tanquam omnes culpabiles essent, propter quosdam qui tales erant.

## 1:3
V. 3. Χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη. See Rom. I. 7.

Chrysostom again applies this to his purpose: If peace is from grace, why are you of a proud and haughty spirit? Why do you swell up so much, when you have attained salvation by grace? But if you have peace with God, why do you attach yourself to others? For this is to dissent and be agitated by sedition. These are his words. But it is certain that all spiritual goods are comprehended in the wish for grace and peace: For grace is the fountain of all goods: even if we are overwhelmed by divine benefits, if we do not have peace with GOD, that grace will be of no benefit to us at all: therefore, just as grace is saving, so also peace in the Lord JESUS is indicated as the property of the faithful. The Apostle makes God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ the source of grace and peace; so that he may teach us that we have these no less from the Lord Jesus Christ than from GOD the Father, lest anyone, with the Arians, imagine the Father to be the principal cause and Christ only the instrumental one: therefore he does not say, ἀπὸ πατρὸς διὰ Ἰησοῦ, but ἀπὸ πατρὸς καὶ κυρίου.

Latin:

V. 3. Χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη. Vid. Rom. I. 7.

Chrysostomus iterum applicat ad institutum: Si pax est ex gratia, cur superbo & elato es animo? cur adeo intumescis, quum salutem assequutus gra- tia? Si autem pacem habes apud Deum, cur te aliis adscribis? hoc enim est dissidere & agitari seditione. Hæc ille. Sed certum est, gratiæ & pacis voto comprehendi omnia bona spiritualia: Fons enim omnium bonorum est gratia: etsi maxime bene- ficiis divinis obruamur, nec pacem habeamus cum DEO, gratia illa nobis minime salutaris erit: ut ergo salutaris gratia, ita & pax in Domino JESU propria fidelium indicatur. Gratiæ autem & pa- cis fontem facit Apostolus Deum Patrem, & Do- minum Jesum Christum; ut non minus à Domino Jesu Christo, quam à DEO Patre nos ea habere doceat, ne quis cum Arianis Patrem causam prin- cipalem, Christum solùm instrumentalem fingat: ideo non ait, ἀπὸ πατρὸς διὰ Ἰησοῦ, sed ἀπὸ πατρὸς καὶ κυρίου.

## 1:4
V. 4. I give thanks to my God. Rom. I. 8. for the grace of God.

Here the noun which preceded is placed for the relative pronoun, here and below 8. 1. Thess. III. 12. 2. Thess. I. 7. 8. and elsewhere.

Chrysostom also adapts this thanksgiving specifically to the Apostle's purpose: You see how he corrects them everywhere. For where there is grace, there are no works: where there are works, there is no longer grace. If, therefore, it is grace, why are you puffed up, and why do you think magnificently of yourselves? From where have you been inflated? Which was given to you. And through whom was it given? Was it by me, or by another Apostle? By no means; but by Jesus Christ.

Latin:

V. 4. Εὐχαριστῶ τῷ Θεῷ μου. Rom. I. 8. ἐπὶ τῇ χάριτι τοῦ Θεοῦ.

Est hic nomen quod præcessit positum pro relativo ἀυτῦ hic & infra 8. 1. Thess. III. 12. 2. Thess. I. 7. 8. & alibi.

Accommodat etiam hanc εὐχαριστίαν speciali- ter Chrysostomus ad institutum Apostoli: Vides quemadmodum ubique eos corrigit. Ubi enim est gratia, non sunt opera: ubi sunt opera, non amplius est gratia. Si est ergo gratia, cur efferimini, & de vobis magnifice sentitis? undenam inflati estis? Quæ data est vobis. Et per quem data est? Num per me, aut per alium Apostolum? Nequaquam; sed per Jesum Christum.

## 1:5
Verse 5. ἐπλυτίσθητε. That is, you abound. See Rom. II. 4. 2. Cor. IX. 11. ἐν αὐτῷ. Through Christ.

He notably says they are enriched ἐν αὐτῷ in Christ, so that he may confound the boasting of human strength, wisdom, justice, and holiness. All riches are obtained in Christ, all treasures of divine wisdom, because he himself has been made wisdom for us, and in him are all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge Col. II. 3. Riches and treasures of justice, because he has been made justice for us, and in him is our justice, Is. XLV. 23. Phil. III. 7. 9. Riches and treasures of holiness, because he has been made sanctification for us Is. IIX. 14. Riches and treasures of redemption, because he has been made redemption for us, and in him is plenteous redemption Ps. CXXX. 7. Compare Eph. I. 18. Moreover, he seems to allude to the riches of the Corinthians, to show in whom true riches are situated, not in coins or lands and other wealth, but in the word and knowledge.

ἐν παντὶ λόγῳ. There is a difference: for ἐν παντὶ had preceded. He understands here, however, the gifts of tongues. κὰι πάσῃ γνώσει. Here he understands the gifts of prophecy.

Because he addresses the whole Church, all those sanctified in Christ, the gifts of tongues or prophecy are not to be understood here, which are not common to all saints and those calling upon one GOD, and which look to ministering gifts, not to sanctifying ones, and thus are proper to the Ministers of the Word, and do not belong to all the faithful: but these things are to be understood concerning the gifts of explaining the sacred mysteries of the Word, and the knowledge of the same; that they may have not only the knowledge of things necessary to be believed, but also be able to discourse and speak about them: For there are many, as Chrysostom says, who indeed have knowledge, but do not have the word. Like the unlearned, and those who cannot openly express what they have in their mind. But you, he says, are not of this kind, but are fit both to understand and to speak. Pareus prefers to understand the Word of God by λόγον, because it precedes knowledge: but we prefer the aforementioned explanation. Knowledge is prior in the order of nature, but not in the order of dignity.

Latin:

Vers. 5. ἐπλυτίσθητε. Id est, abundatis, Vid. Rom. II. 4. 2. Cor. IX. 11. ἐν αὐτῷ. Per Christum.

Notanter ditatos ἐν αὐτῷ in Christo dicit, ut humanarum virium, sapientiae, justitiae & sancti- tatis jactantiam confundat. Omnes divitiae in Christo obtinentur, omnes thesauri divinae sapien- tiae, quia ipse factus est nobis sapientia, & in ipso omnes thesauri sunt sapientiae & cognitionis Col. II. 3. divitiae & thesauri justitiae, quia ipse factus nobis est justitia, & in ipso est justitia nostra, Es. XLV. 23. Phil. III. 7. 9. divitiae & thesauri sanctitatis, quia ipse nobis factus est sanctificatio Es. IIX. 14. divitiae & thesauri redemptionis, quia ipse factus nobis est redemptio, & in ipso est copiosa redemptio Ps. CXXX. 7. Conf. Eph. I. 18. Alludere autem videtur ad di- vitias Corinthiorum, ut ostendat, in quonam verae divitiae sitae sint, non in nummis sive fundis aliisque opibus, sed in verbo & scientia.

ἐν παντὶ λόγῳ. Est διαφορὰ: nam praecesserat ἐν παντὶ. Intelligit au- tem hic dona linguarum. κὰι πάσῃ γνώσει. Hic intelligit dona Prophetiae.

Quia alloquitur totam Ecclesiam, omnes san- ctificatos in Christo, non hic dona linguarum aut Prophetiae intelligenda, quae non sunt omnibus sanctis & unum DEUM invocantibus commu- nia, & ad dona ministrantia, non ad sanctificantia spectant, adeoque Ministrorum Verbi propria sunt, non omnibus fidelibus competunt: sed de donis haec accipienda explicandi sacra Verbi my- steria, & cognitionis eorundem; quod non tan- tum rerum creditu necessariarum cognitionem habeant, sed etiam de iis disserere, ac loqui possint: Sunt enim multi, ut Chrysostomus παραδέδξ?,* qui scientiam quidem habent, verbum autem non habent. Ut idiotae, & qui non possunt aperte expri- mere quae habent in mente. Sed vos, inquit, non estis hujusmodi, sed & ad intelligendum & dicendum estis idonei. Pareus per λόγον mavult Verbum Dei intelligere, quia cognitionem praecedit: sed prae- ferimus laudatam explicationem. Prior est or- dine naturae cognitio, sed non ordine dignitatis.

## 1:6
V. 6. καθὼς τὸ μαρτύριον τῦ Χρισῦ ἐβεβαιώθη ἐν ὑμῖν. He calls the Gospel the testimony of Christ, as below II. 1. 2. Tim. I. 8. βεβαιῦτ is to confirm the truth of a thing by testimony Mark XVI. 20. Philipp. I. 7. Thus an oath is said to be εἰς βεβαίωσιν Heb. VI. 6. It corresponds to the Hebrew הקים.

Latin:

V. 6. καθὼς τὸ μαρτύριον τῦ Χρισῦ ἐβεβαιώθη ἐν ὑμῖν. Μαρτύριον Χρισῦ vocat Evangelium, ut infra II. 1. 2. Tim. I. 8. βεβαιῦτ est rei veritatem testimonio confirmare Marc. XVI. 20. Philipp. I. 7. Sic juramentum dicitur esse εἰς βεβαίω- σιν Hebr. VI. 6. Respondet Hebraeo הקים.

## 1:7
V. 7. ὥστε ὑμᾶς μὴ ὑστερεῖσθαι ἐν μηδενὶ χαρίσματι. That is, so that you have nothing less than those who are Christians elsewhere. See Rom. III. 23. ἀπεκδεχομένους τὴν ἀποκάλυψιν τῦ Κυρίο ἡμῶν Ἰησῦ Χρισῦ. While he praises those who await the resurrection, he silently chastises those who think otherwise. Ἀποκάλυψις Ἰησῦ Χρισῦ is the very time of the resurrection. 1. Petr. I. 7. & Rom. IIX. 18.

The discourse is not about the external confirmation of the Word which happens through miracles, but about the internal confirmation, which happens through the testimony of the Holy Spirit. Compare 2. Cor. I. 20. seqq. 1. Thess. I. 4. 5. A contradiction occurs here to Chrysostom, how can he call them carnal and children soon after, who have been made rich in every word and knowledge, so that they lack nothing in every grace? He responds that it can be said that when they had believed from the beginning, and had attained charisms or gratuitous gifts (for they were emulous and inflamed with zeal), they became more negligent afterwards. Or if this is not so, it must be said that these things are not said to all, neither this nor that: but the former to those who were liable to accusations, but the latter to those who were distinguished by praises. But what he adds, if the praises are not very close to the truth, they were inserted for a certain purpose, does not befit Apostolic authority and Holy Scripture. to all-encompassing truth. Therefore Gregory the Great, Homily XI on Ezekiel. Did Paul lie, he says: Far be it, but because there were some among the Corinthians filled with every grace, and there were some cut off in the favors of persons, he began with the praises of the perfect, so that by a modest invective he might reach the reproof of the imperfect. He rightly observes, however, that not all-encompassing perfection is ascribed to them, which admits no defect: but that the word ὑσερῦσθαι is used.

Latin:

V. 7. ὥστε ὑμᾶς μὴ ὑστερεῖσθαι ἐν μηδενὶ χαρίσματι. Id est, ita, ut nihil minus habeatis quam qui alibi sunt Christiani. Vide Rom. III. 23. ἀπεκδεχομένους τὴν ἀποκάλυψιν τῦ Κυρίο ἡμῶν Ἰησῦ Χρισῦ. Dum eos laudat, qui resurrectionem exspectant, tacite aliter sentientes castigat. Ἀποκάλυψις Ἰησῦ Χρισῦ est ipsum tempus resurrectionis. 1. Petr. I. 7. & Rom. IIX. 18.

Non de confirmatione externa Verbi quae fit per miracula, sed de confirmatione interna, quae fit per testimonium Spiritus S. sermo est. Conf. 2. Cor. I. 20. seqq. 1. Thess. I. 4. 5. Occurrit hic ἐναν- τιοφανεία Chrysostomus, quomodo qui divites facti sunt in omni verbo & cognitione, ut nihil eis desit in omni gratia, eos carnales & pueros mox appellet? respondens dici posse, quod quum ab initio credi- dissent, & charismata seu gratuita dona effent asse- quuti, (aemulabantur enim & zelo erant incensi) evaserunt postea negligentiores. Aut si hoc non ita ha- bet, dicendum est, quod non omnibus neque hac, ne- que illa dicuntur: sed illa quidem iis, qui erant obno- xii criminationibus, hac autem iis, qui erant laudibus insignes. Quod vero addit, si laudes non sint val- de affines veritati, certo tamen consilio insertae sunt, non convenit Apostolicae autoritati, & Scripturae S. omnimodae veritati. Ideo Gregor. M. I hom. XI. in Ezech. An, inquit, mentitus est Paulus: Absit, sed quia erant inter Corinthios quidam omni gratia repleti, & erant quidam in personarum favoribus exscisi, coepit a laudibus perfectorum, ut modesta in- vectione ad reprehensionem pertingeret imperfecto- rum. Recte tamen observat, non omnimodam perfectionem illis adscribi, quae nullum admittat defectum: sed verbum ὑσερῦσθαι adhiberi.

## 1:8
V. 8. ὃς καὶ βεβαιώσει ὑμᾶς ἕως τέλες ἀνεγκλήτες. It can be referred either to Christ or to God, but more correctly to God because of what follows, God is faithful. But God confirms not by compelling, but by arming those who labor and pray with always new aids: he does what is his part: below X. 13. ἀνεγκλήτος, that is, just and holy, as Col. I. 22. ἀνώμυς, ἀμωμήτυς Philipp. II. 13. 1. Thess. II. 10. c. III. 13. Ephes. I. 27. Philipp. II. 15. Coloss. I. 22. 2. Petr. III. 14. Jude 29. Apoc. XIV. 5. ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῦ Κυρίε ἡμῶν Ἰησῦ χρισῦ. For εἰς τὴν ἡμέραν, that is, so that in that day of Christ you may appear such, Ephes. V. 27. A similar way of speaking, but through εἰς Ephes. IV. 30.

We admit it is referred to God, not so much because God is faithful follows, as because he hopes for and promises the confirmation from the same, to whom he gives thanks for the grace first received v. 4. and because Christ is distinctly named here in the present verse, in the day of the Lord: but the end of life is understood: and confirmation is made through the word, through which the strength of faith, the grace of further renewal, so that the inner man is renewed more and more from day to day 2. Cor. IV. 16. and we are transformed from glory to glory into the image of Christ 2. Cor. III. 17. so that we also obtain the spirit of sealing Ephes. I. 13. 14. The expectation of the revelation of Jesus Christ, which will happen on the last day, teaches that Christ is not absent now from the Church, to which he promised he would be present even to the consummation of the age, Matt. XXVIII. 20. but at least his presence does not appear, or is not revealed: which will then be revealed to the whole world. At whose coming the faithful are so far from trembling, that at every moment they are both prepared for the coming of Christ the judge, and await the same with the desire of their heart, Tit. II. 15. Rom. VIII. 23. Phil. III. 20. 2. Pet. III. 11. Acts XXII. 20. Concerning which Augustine says: If we love Christ, we ought to desire his coming. For it is perverse to fear that he whom you love might come; to pray 'thy kingdom come,' and to fear that you might be heard.

The faithful are called Ἀνέγκλητοι [blameless], not on account of a perfect observance of the law, which is found in no one, but both on account of the imputed righteousness of Christ, because they are cleansed by the blood of Christ from all sin 1. John 1. 7. and are constituted righteous by the obedience of Christ Rom. V. 19. and also on account of their anxious flight from sins against conscience, by which they take care, lest, having been purified from sins, they be contaminated by the filth of sins, 2. Pet. II. 20. and cleanse themselves from all defilement of flesh and spirit, perfecting sanctification in the fear of God 2. Cor. VII. 1. Which sanctification, however, is imperfect here, Rom. VII. 14 seqq. 2. Cor. III. 17. Rightly, therefore, the blessed Hunnius: He calls them blameless, because both in this age the sins of the faithful are covered by the blood of Christ, and by the power of the Spirit they lead a blameless life, and one immune from the grosser sins, which Paul calls works of the flesh. And finally in the day of the Lord JESUS CHRIST they will be in every part irreprehensible, having now put on the most perfect habit of inherent righteousness in Commentar. h. l. p. 34. Although, says the blessed Selneccerus, we are not ἀναμάρτητοι [sinless], yet we are ἀνέγκλητοι [blameless] Rom. VIII. 1.

Latin:

V. 8. ὃς καὶ βεβαιώσει ὑμᾶς ἕως τέλες ἀνεγκλήτες. Potest vel ad Christum, vel ad Deum referri, sed rectius adDeum ob id quod sequitur πισὸς ὁ Θεός. Confirmat au- tem Deus non cogendo, sed laborantes & orantes novis semper auxiliis armando: facit quod suarum est partium: infra X. 13. ἀνεγκλήτος, id est, justos ac sanctos, ut Col. I. 22. ἀνώμυς,αμωμήτυς Philipp. II. 13. 1. Thess. II. 10. c. III. 13. Ephes. I. 27. Philipp. II. 15. Coloss. I. 22. 2. Petr. III. 14. Ju- dae 29. Apoc. XIV. 5. ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῦ Κυρίε ἡμῶν Ἰησῦ χρισῦ. Pro εἰς τὴν ἡμέραν, id est, ut in illa die Christi tales appa- reatis, Ephes. V. 27. Simile loquendi genus, sed per εἰς Ephes. IV. 30.

Admittimus ad Deum referri, non tam quia sequitur πισὸς ὁ Θεὸς, quam quia ab eodem sperat & promittit τὴν βεβαίωσιν, cui pro accepta primum gratia gratias agit v. 4. & quia Christus hic distin- cte nominatur versu praesenti, ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῦ Κυρίε: Finis autem intelligitur vitae: & confirmatio fit per verbum, per quod robur fidei, renovationis ulterio- ris gratiam, ut de die in diem magis magisque reno- vetur homo interior 2. Cor. IV. 16. & de claritate in claritatem transformemur in Christi imaginem 2. Cor. III. 17. ut & obsignationis spiritum consequi- mur Ephes. I. 13. 14. Expectatio revelationis Jesu Christi, quae fiet in novissimo die, docet, Chri- stum non abesse nunc ab Ecclesia, cui promisit sese adfuturum usque ad consummationem seculi, Matth. XX IIX. 20. sed saltem praesentiam ejus non apparere, aut revelari: quae tum revelabitur toti orbi: ad cujus adventum tam non trepidant fide- les, ut omnibus momentis & parati sint ad Christi judicis adventum, & eundem cum desiderio cor- dis sui expectent, Tit. II. 15. Rom. IIX. 23. Phil. III. 20. 2. Petr. III. 11. Actor. XXII. 20. Quo de Augustinus: Si Christum amamus, adventum ejus desiderare de- bemus. Perversum enim est, eum, quem diligis, timere, ne veniat; orare adveniat regnum tuum, & timere ne exaudiaris.

Ἀνέγκλητοι autem dicuntur fideles, non ob per- fectam legis observantiam, quae in nemine reperi- tur, sed tum ob imputatam Christi justitiam, quia purgantur sanguine Christi ab omni peccato 1. Joh. 17. & obedientia Christi justi constituuntur Rom. V. 19. tum ob peccatorum contra conscientiam sollicitam fugam, qua cavent, ne purificati a pecca- tis contaminentur peccatorum sordibus, 2. Petr. II. 20. & mundant se ab omni inquinamento car- nis & spiritus, perficientes sanctificationem in ti- more Dei 2. Cor. VII. 1. Quae tamen sanctificatio hic imperfecta est, Rom. VII. 14 seqq. 2. Cor. III. 17. Recte itaque B. Hunnius: Inculpatos autem dicit, quia & in hoc seculo peccata fidelium tecta Christi sanguine sunt, & virtute Spiritus vitam agunt in- culpatam, & a crassioribus peccatis, quae Paulus ope- ra carnis appellat, immunem. Et tandem in die Do- mini JESU CHRISTI erunt omni ex parte ir- reprehensibiles, induti jam perfectissimo inhaerentis ju- stitiae habitu in Commentar. h. l. p. 34. Etsi, in- quit B. Selneccerus, non fimus ἀναμάρτητοι, tamen sumus ἀνέγκλητοι Rom. IIX. 1.

## 1:9
V. 9. πιστὸς ὁ Θεὸς δι’ οὗ ἐκλήθητε εἰς κοινωνίαν τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.

If he has called you, that you may imitate the holiness of Christ, he will also give what is necessary for this. See concerning this communion 1. John I. 3. πιστὸς ὁ Θεὸς from Isaiah XLIX. 7.

Three foundations of the hope of βεβαιώσεως [confirmation] & divine preservation unto the end are here: First, the faithfulness of GOD. Deut. XXXII. 4. Ps. XXXVII. 23. 24. 1 Cor. X. 13. Second, the end of the calling, because He called us for this reason, not that He might abandon us, but that He might preserve us in faith unto eternal life, which is the end of faith, 1 Pet. I. 11. Rom. XI. 29. Third, the communion of Christ, because those who are in this communion are children of God & heirs of God, and joint-heirs of Christ Rom. VIII. 16. 17. provided they do not fall away from faith by their own fault Heb. III. 14. 1 Pet. I. 9. Is. LIV. 10. Faithful, he says, is God, that is, true, says Chrysost. But if He is true, He will also do those things which He promised. He promised, however, that He would make us partners of the only-begotten Son. For to this also He called us. For His gifts and the calling of God are of such a kind that repentance does not fall upon it. Chrysostom also notes here a tacit rebuke: You have been called into the fellowship of the only-begotten, and do you attach yourselves to men? &c. These things, however, must be opposed to the Papists, who deny that we can be certain of perseverance in faith & salvation, and call the faithfulness of God into doubt. Cf. Rom. VIII. Heb. XI.

PART II. Exhortation to concord, & rebuke concerning Schism.

Latin:

V. 9. πισὸς ὁ Θεὸς δι’ ὗ ἐκλήθητε εἰς κοινωνίαν τῦ ὑἷῦ αὐτῦ τῦ Κυρίο ἡμῶν Ἰησῦ χρισῦ.

Si vocavit vos, ut Christi sanctimoniam imitemini, dabit etiam, qua ad hoc sunt necessaria. Vide de hac commu- nione 1. Joh. I. 3. πιστὸς ὁ Θεὸς ex Esaia XLIX. 7.

Tria hic fundamenta spei βεβαιώσεως & conservationis divinæ usque ad finem : Primum DEI fidelitas. Deut. XXXII. 4. Ps. XXXVII. 23. 24. 1. Cor. X. 13. Alterum vocationis finis, quia ideo nos vocavit, non ut relinqueret, sed ut conservaret nos in fide ad vitam æternam, quæ finis fidei, 1. Petr. I. 11. Rom. XI. 29. Tertio communio Christi, quia, qui in communione hac sunt, filii Dei & hæredes Dei sunt, ac cohæredes Christi Rom. IIX. 16. 17. modo à fide propria culpa non deficiant Ebr. III. 14. 1. Petr. I. 9. Es. LIV. 10. Fidelis, inquit, est Deus, hoc est, verus, ait Chrysost. Si autem est verus, ea etiam faciet, quæ promisit. Promisit autem se facturum nos socios Filii unigeniti. Nam ad hoc quoque nos vocavit. Sunt enim ejus dona hujusmodi & Dei vocatio, ut in ea non cadat pœnitentia. Notat etiam hic correptionem tacitam Chrysostomus : In unigeniti vocati estis societatem, & vos hominibus addicitis ? &c. Opponenda autem hæc Papistis, qui nos certos esse posse de perseverantia in fide & salute negant, & fidelitatem Dei in dubium revocant. Conf. Rom IIX. Ebr. XI.

PARS II. Parænesis ad concordiam, & ob Schisma correptio.

## 1:10
Vers. 10. ἵνα τὸ αὐτὸ λέγητε πάντες. That you all say the same thing. Speak the same thing in those matters which pertain to the rule of faith, a part of which is the dogma concerning the resurrection. The opinions of philosophers are various: all Christians ought to think the same thing, in the rule, I say, of faith.

κὶι μὴ ἦ ἐν ὑμῖν σχίσματα. And that there be no schisms among you. Then, that you do not make parties in the Church on any other occasion either. We have had σχίσμα in John concerning the variety of studies. Here, and below XI. 18. XII. 25. it denotes something more, that is, those who are separated. Clement also uses it thus in the said Epistle.

ἦτε δὲ κατηρτισμένοι. נכונים, perfect, as the Syrian translates here. See Luke VI. 40. Be such as it behooves you to be.

ἐν τῶ αὐτῶ νοῖ. That you may believe the same thing: whence it followed that they should also speak the same things, just as he had already begun to say.

ἐν τῇ αὐτῇ γνώμῃ. This now refers to the affections of the mind, which is explained elsewhere by φρονεῖν and φρόνημα. Thus γνώμη is taken in Rev. XVII. 13. 2 Macc. IX. 20. Plato and Demosthenes also use it thus.

The Apostle does not require only that the Corinthians speak the same thing regarding the rule of faith, or concerning those things which are expressly contained in it, but in general regarding all dogmas of religion, even those which do not directly pertain to the rule of faith, nor are formally contained in it: because he prohibits all schisms: which arise even then, when the rule of faith is undermined by some indirectly, as was being done by those who were causing dissensions, when they were inventing schismatic denominations according to those who agreed in faith, just as if Peter, Apollo, and Paul differed from each other in doctrine, or Christ were divided among them, or they wanted to be denominated from them, as if they depended on them in faith; whence consequently he was corrupting the rule of faith, as the Apostle shows: Was Paul crucified for you, or were you baptized in the name of Paul? For there is no doubt that the crucifixion done for us, and the reception of baptisms into the faith and profession of him in whose name we are baptized, pertain to the rule of faith: therefore the authors of that schism were undermining it indirectly. Therefore Paul wants them to be κατηρτισμένοι, perfect, ἐν τῶ αὐτῷ νοὶ, ἐν τῇ αὐτῇ γνώμῃ, not regarding only some things, but regarding all things, not regarding only those things which are formally contained in the rule of faith, but also regarding those things which virtually pertain to it, so that it may not be undermined in any way, either directly or indirectly, and that from there some schism might arise.

For schism is from σχίζω, to tear, when unity

of the Church is torn by dissensions. Because the Church is one body, under one head, Christ, which ought not to be split into parts and torn: lest Christ be split. They are accustomed otherwise to distinguish between heresy and schism: that heresy is a dissension in faith, but schism is a dissension in rites, and morals, and charity: or even in those things which are about the faith, and do not directly pertain to the rule of faith. Jerome in Epist. ad Tit. Heresy, he says, has a perverse dogma: Schism separates equally from the Church on account of a special dissension. Augustine l. de fide & Symbol. c. IV. Heretics, he says, violate the faith itself by thinking falsely about God: but Schismatics dissent from fraternal charity by iniquitous dissensions, although they believe those things which we believe. But Schism is taken either γενικῶς, and denotes any tearing of the Church whatsoever, or εἰδικῶς, as it is distinguished from heresy: so that the latter brings about a tearing through dissension from the rule or in the foundation of the faith, but Schism not indeed through dissension from the faith, but in questions about the faith, or in rites, yet so that the body of the Church is thereby split. In the former way it is taken here: but in the latter it seems to be taken c. IX. 18. I hear that there are schisms among you, and I partly believe it: for it is necessary that έ αἱρέσεις ALSO there be heresies among you: where heresy is judged to be indicated as something graver than schism. Wherefore, that every schism may be excluded here, the Apostle warns that they speak the SAME: For he who invents new words usually generates new dogmas at the same time. Therefore also κακοφωνίαι, new phrases and formulas of speech, are to be avoided, both lest fights and dissensions and schisms arise from them, and lest new dogmas be introduced; on the contrary, the ὑποτύπωσις ὑγιαινόντων λόγων 2. Tim. I. 13 is to be retained holily and undefiledly, both as to the Phrases contained in Holy Scriptures, and as to the exegetical ones received in the Church, and convenient for excluding heterodox opinions, explaining and guarding the proper mind of Scripture, such as for example are ὁμουσία, ἐνσάρκωσις, ἕνωσις ὑποσατικὴ, κοινωνία ἰδιωμάτων and similar modes of speaking accustomed in the Church, and approved by the Symbols of public Confessions. In the word κατηρτισμένοι there is emphasis: because ἀρτισμὸς is the reduction of joints and bones to their places, when they have been dislocated, and are useless for their acts: just as in schism the members of the Church are torn, so that they are useless for the worship of God, prayers and charity, and other good operations. And therefore he wishes the Corinthians to be κατηρτισμένοι, joined together, i.e., not dislocated, or if they have been dislocated by schism, to be joined together again and reduced to unity. But he requires unity not only in words and modes of speaking: but primarily in mind and opinion. [Those] contained in the letters, as well as those exegetical [terms] received in the Church, and suitable for excluding heterodox opinions, explaining and guarding the proper mind of Scripture, such as, for example, ὁμουσία, ἐνσάρκωσις, ἕνωσις ὑποσατικὴ, κοινωνία ἰδιωμάτων and similar modes of speaking accustomed in the Church, and approved by the Symbols of public Confessions. In the word κατηρτισμένοι there is emphasis: because ἀρτισμὸς is the reduction of joints and bones to their own places, when they are dislocated and useless for their acts: just as in schism the members of the Church are torn, so that they are useless for the worship of God, prayers and charity, and other good operations. And therefore he wishes the Corinthians to be κατηρτισμένυς, joined together, i.e., not dislocated, or if they have been dislocated by schism, to be joined together anew and reduced to unity. But he requires unity not only in words and modes of speaking: but primarily in mind and opinion. For when we speak the same thing, distraction is indeed guarded against: but unless we think the same thing, there is no solid unity. For when different opinions are hidden under the same words, the agreement is only plastered over, as Pareus rightly says here. Which indeed the Calvinists, and especially the Syncretists among them, such as Pareus himself was, ought to have observed. For nothing is more common to them than what Irenæus already complained about heretics in his time: ὅμοια μὲν λαλῦσιν, ἀνόμοια δὲ φρονῦσιν. B. Hunnius noted here three degrees of symphony. The first of which turns on speech; that all may speak the same thing concerning those things which pertain to common piety. The second is, that they be of the same mind. He uses, however, the emphatic word κατηρτισμένοι, by which he wishes that Christians be as it were bound and compacted into the same mind, and a pious conjunction of souls. A third degree is subjoined, in the same opinion, under which he understands a uniform judgment concerning things pertaining to the form of Christianity. These three degrees are so connected that the last is seen to be the fountain and cause of the middle, and the middle of the first. Since indeed from the same sentiment in religion exists that conjunction of mind and will. This again causes those who agree in sentiments and wills to speak the same thing. See Commentar. p. 32.

Latin:

Vers. 10. ἵνα τὸ αὐτὸ λέγητε πάντες. Idem loquamini in iis, quæ ad regulam fidei pertinent, cujus pars est dogma de resurrectione. Philosophorum varia sunt placita : Christiani omnes idem sentire debent, in regula, inquam, fidei.

κὶι μὴ ἦ ἐν ὑμῖν σχίσματα. Deinde, ne etiam alia quavis occasione partes faciatis in Ecclesia. σχίσμα apud Johannem de studiorum varietate habuimus. Hic, & infra XI. 18. XII. 25. aliquid amplius, id est, segreges notat. Usurpat sic & Clemens in dicta Epistola.

ἦτε δὲ κατηρτισμένοι. נכונים, perfecti, ut hic vertit Syrus. Vide Luc. VI. 40. Estote quales vos decet esse.

ἐν τῶ αὐτῶ νοῖ. Ut idem credatis : unde sequebatur ut & loquerentur eadem, sicut jam dicere cœperat.

ἐν τῇ αὐτῇ γνώμῃ. Hoc jam ad affectus animi refertur, quod alibi explicatur per φρονεῖν & φρόνημα. Sic γνώμη sumitur Apoc. XVII. 13. 2. Macc. IX. 20. Utuntur sic & Plato & Demosthenes.

Non id tantum requirit Apostolus, ut idem loquantur Corinthii quoad regulam fidei, vel de iis, quæ expressè in eadem continentur, sed in universum quoad omnia dogmata religionis, etiam ea, quæ directè ad regulam fidei non pertinent, nec formaliter in eo continentur : quia omnia schismata prohibet: quæ etiam tum oriuntur, cum per indirectum regula fidei à quibusdam labefactatur, uti fiebat ab iis, qui dissensiones pariebant, cum denominationes schismaticas qua eos, qui in fide consentiebant, fingebant, non secus ac si Petrus, Apollo & Paulus à se invicem doctrina discreparent, vel Christus inter ipsos divisus esset, aut ab istis denominari volebant, quasi ab ipsis in fide dependeret; unde per consequens regulam fidei corrumpebat, ut ostendit Apostolus : Num Paulus pro vobis crucifixus, aut num baptizati estis in nomen Pauli? Crucifixionem enim pro nobis factam, & baptismos susceptionem in fidem & professione ejus, in cujus nomine baptizamur, ad regulam fidei pertinere, dubitandum non est : Eam ergo indirecte labefactabant Schismatis istius autores. Ideo Paulus vult, ut κατηρτισμένοι perfecti sint, ἐν τῶ αὐτῷ νοὶ, ἐν τῇ αὐτῇ γνώμῃ, non quoad nonnulla tantum, sed quoad omnia, non qua ea tantum, quæ formaliter in regula fidei continentur, sed quoad ea etiam, quæ virtualiter ad eam pertinent, ne ulla ratione eadem seu directe seu indirecte labefactetur, indeque Schisma aliquod exurgat.

Schisma enim à σχίζω lacero est, cum unitas

Ecclesiæ laceratur per dissidia. Quia Ecclesia corpus unum est, sub uno capite Christo, quod in partes scindi, & lacerari non debet: ne Christus scindatur. Solent alias distinguere inter hæresin & schisma: quod hæresis sit dissidium in fide, schisma vero dissidium in ritibus, & moribus, ac charitate: vel etiam in iis, quæ circa fidem sunt, nec directe ad regulam fidei faciunt. Hieronymus in Epist. ad Tit. Hæresis, inquit, perversum dogma habet: Schisma propter specialem dissensionem ab Ecclesia pariter separat. Augustinus l. de fide & Symbol. c. IV. Hæretici, inquit, de Deo falsa sentiendo ipsam fidem violant: Schismatici autem dissensionibus iniquis à fraterna charitate dissentiunt, quamvis ea credant, quæ credimus. Sed Schisma vel γενικῶς accipitur, & lacerationem quamvis Ecclesiæ notat, vel εἰδικῶς, prout ab hæresi distinguitur: ita ut hæc per dissensum à regula vel in fundamento fidei lacerationem invehat, Schisma autem non quidem per dissensum à fide, sed in quæstionibus circa fidem, aut in ritibus, ita tamen ut corpus Ecclesiæ inde scindatur. Illo modo hic sumitur: hoc vero videtur sumi c. IX. 18. Audio schismata inter vos esse, & ex parte credo: oportet enim έ αἱρέσεις ETIAM hæreses inter vos esse: ubi hæresis ceu aliquid gravius schismate indigitari censetur. Quapropter ut omne schisma hic excludatur, monet Apostolus, ut IDEM loquantur: Nam plerumque qui fingit nova verba, simul nova dogmata gignit. Idcirco etiam κακοφωνίαι, novæ phrases & loquutionum formulæ, vitandæ, tum ne pugnæ & dissensiones ac schismata inde oriantur, tum ne dogmata nova invehantur; contra retinenda sancte & intemerate ὑποτύπωσις ὑγιαινόντων λόγων 2. Tim. I. 13. tum qua Phrases in S. Literis contentas, tum qua exegeticas earundem in Ecclesia receptas, & heterodoxis sententiis excludendis convenientes, Scripturæ propriam mentem exponentes, & custodientes, quales v. g. sunt ὁμουσία, ἐνσάρκωσις, ἕνωσις ὑποσατικὴ, κοινωνία ἰδιωμάτων & similes modi loquendi in Ecclesia consueti, Symbolis que publicarum Confessionum probati. In voce κατηρτισμένοι emphasis est: quia ἀρτισμὸς reductio est artuum & ossium ad sua loca, cum luxata sunt, & ad actus suos inutilia: quomodo in schismate membra Ecclesiæ lacerantur, ut ad cultum Dei, preces & charitatem, aliasque operationes bonas inutilia sint. Ideoque vult, Corinthios esse κατηρτισμένυς coagmentatos, h. e. non luxatos, aut si schismate luxati sint, coagmentari denuò & ad unitatem reduci. Sed unitatem non tantum requirit in verbis & modis loquendi: verum imprimis in mente & sententia. Cum enim idem loquimur, cavetur quidem distractio: sed nisi idem sentiamus, non est solida unitas. Quando enim sub iisdem verbis diversæ occultantur sententiæ, tantum incrustata est consensio, ut recte hic Pareus. Quod vero imprimis Calviniani, & ex his maxime Syncretistæ, qualis Pareus ipse fuit, observasse debebant. Nam nihil iis solemnius est, quam quod de hæreticis suo tempore jam questus est Irenæus: ὅμοια μὲν λαλῦσιν, ἀνόμοια δὲ φρονῦσιν. B. Hunnius notavit hic tres gradus symphonias. Quorum primus vertitur in sermone; ut idem loquantur omnes de his, quæ ad communem pietatem pertinent. Secundus est, ut eàdem sint mente. Utitur autem emphatico verbo κατηρτισμένοι, quo vult, ut Christiani sint quasi colligati & compacti in eandem mentem, & piam animorum conjunctionem. Tertius subjungitur gradus, in eadem sententia, sub qua de rebus ad Christianismi formam spectantibus uniforme judicium intelligit. Hi tres gradus ita connexi sunt, ut postremus medii, medius primi cernatur esse fons atque causa. Siquidem ex eadem in religione sententia existit illa mentis vo- luntatisque conjunctio. Hæ rursum efficit, ut idem loquantur, qui sententiis & voluntatibus concordant. Vid. Commentar. p. 32.

## 1:11
V. 11. ὑπὸ τῶν Χλόης. I think the children of the deceased Chloe are indicated.

Whether Chloe is the name of a woman or a man is ambiguous: yet it seems more to be the name of an honored matron: but that she was already deceased at that time cannot be pronounced with certainty. However, this notification was not a denunciation or a certain betrayal; because it was done not to an enemy, but to an Apostle, as to a common Father, not for the sake of causing evil, but of averting the evil that was creeping in, not so that the schismatics might be punished, but so that they might be led back into the way: not so that the Church might be afflicted, but so that it might be freed from the affliction which the dissensions were producing, and might in turn be knit together. For when our vices are reported to those whose business it is not to be ignorant of them, and that for the sake of their being cured, for our own and the common good, it is not betrayal, but faithfulness, pertaining to the duty of charity. Whence the Apostle does not hesitate to name them publicly, because he knows their duty is free from crime; nor does he fear envy for them, but rather by naming them he praises their deed, and gains authority for them.

ὅτι ἔριδες ἐν ὑμῖν εἰσι. With this word Clement also expresses schisms.

Latin:

V. 11. ὑπὸ τῶν Χλόης. Puto indicari mortuæ Chloës liberos.

Chloë an fœminæ, an viri nomen sit, ambiguum est: Plus tamen matronæ honoratæ nomen id esse videtur: sed eam defunctam tum jam fuisse certo pronunciari non potest. Non autem hæc signifi- catio delatio, vel proditio quædam fuit; quia facta est non hosti, sed Apostolo, ceu communi Patri, non malum conciliandi, sed malum, quod serpebat, avertendi causa, non ut schismatici punirentur, sed ut in viam reducerentur: non ut Ecclesiæ affli- geretur, sed ut ab afflictione, quam pariebant dis- sensiones, liberaretur, & vicissim coagmentaretur. Quando enim vitia nostra deferuntur ad eos, quo- rum interest ea non ignorare, idque ut curentur, nostro & communi bono, non est proditio, sed fidelitas, ad officium charitatis pertinens. Unde Apostolus hos non dubitat publice nominare, quia novit officium eorum crimine vacare; neque veretur eis invidiam, sed potius nominando fa- ctum eorum collaudat, eisque autoritatem con- ciliat.

ὅτι ἔριδες ἐν ὑμῖν εἰσι. Hac voce schismata etiam Clemens exprimit.

## 1:12
V. 12. Λέγω δὲ τοῦτο. Note the explanation, as, I say, the Latin. ἕκαστος ὑμῶν λέγει, ἐγὼ μέν εἰμι Παύλου, ἐγὼ δὲ Ἀπολλὼ, ἐγὼ δὲ Κηφᾶ;

This is to be understood not of all, but of many: as below XIV. 26. And, I am of Paul, of Apollo, of Cephas, namely a follower. Some think Paul used these names to denote other men, from whom the factions at Corinth drew their names. They use as an argument that below IV. 6. Paul says that he had transformed the things he had said into himself and Apollos. But there it is a matter of the modesty which all ministers of the Gospel ought to display, by referring all things to the goodness of God. But here what he says was a matter understood from the family of Chloe. Add that Clement in his Epistle, speaking of this time, not obscurely shows what had been done: Ἀναλάβετε τὴν ἐπιστολὴν τοῦ μακαρίου Παύλου τοῦ Ἀποστόλου, τί πρῶτον ὑμῖν ἐν ἀρχῇ τοῦ ἐυαγγελίου ἔγραψεν; ἐπ' ἀληθείας πνευματικῶς ἐπέστειλεν ὑμῖν, περὶ ἀυτοῦ τε καὶ Κηφᾶ καὶ Ἀπολλώ. Διὰ τὸ καὶ τότε προσκλίσεις ὑμᾶς πεποιῆσθαι· ἀλλ' ἡ πρόσκλισις ἐκείνη ἧττον ἁμαρτίαν ὑμῖν προσήνεγκεν. προσεκλίθητε γὰρ Ἀποστόλοις μεμαρτυρημένοις, καὶ ἀνδρί δεδοκιμασμένῳ παρ' ἀυτοῖς· νυνὶ δὲ κατανοήσατε, τίνες ὑμᾶς διέστρεψαν, &c. Where, speaking wittily, he calls the sects προσκλίσεις: which Cicero translates somewhere as propensions. By the Apostles, however, distinguished by miracles, there is no doubt that Peter and Paul are understood by Clement; and by the approved man, Apollos. Therefore, some at Corinth were instructed by Apollos after the departure of Paul, others by Paul himself, others who had come from Judea, by Peter, and under those names they handed down different dogmas: a kind of which we know from Clement of Alexandria was also done under the name of Matthias.

Therefore Grotius does not make the Corinthians themselves, or the members of that Church, the schismatics or the authors of the schisms, but false teachers rampant among them, who scattered different dogmas under the pretext of information or tradition received from Apollos, Peter, or Paul. But the Apostle argues against the Corinthians themselves: ἕκαστος ὑμῶν: nor does he hand down anything here about false dogmas scattered by others, but he reproves them for useless divisions, because while they agreed in faith, both they themselves and their teachers to whom they adhered, Peter, Paul, Apollos, they were nevertheless split into parties on account of the diverse gifts of the teachers; since for some Apollos was in admiration on account of his eloquence, Acts XIII, for others Peter on account of his authority and elderly prudence, for others Paul on account of his singular wisdom and knowledge of the Scriptures, etc. Ineptly the Papists, Sanderus de ritib. monach. l. VI. c. 4. Bellarm. l. 2. de R. P. c. 8. from the order, as if it were a gradation, infer the primacy of jurisdiction of Peter: for not even an order of dignity is concluded, because otherwise Apollos would be more worthy than Paul, let alone an order of jurisdiction. But more inept is Baronius at the year of Christ 57, excusing those who said they were of Cephas; because it was the same as if they had said they were of Christ: for by equal right it would be said that it was also the same when some said they were of Paul, as if they said they were of Apollos. Chrysostom, however, observes that all four are reproved as schismatics, and Salmero gives the reason for this, because they wrongly opposed the ministers of Christ both to each other and to Christ, which reason appears from the following words, μεμέρισται ὁ χριστὸς, and this is the nerve of it; He who, regarding the efficacy and end of the proclamation, is not divided from the ministers, and whose ministers, by reason of virtue and end, are not divided from one another, they ought not to be separated from their hearers as heads of distinct sects.

ἐγὼ δὲ χρισῦ.

For there had come from Judea certain men who had heard Christ himself teaching, and they wished the things which he had said about the new birth to be the same as those which he had said about the resurrection, falsely and perniciously: namely, as offshoots of the Sadducees.

That such heretics as offshoots of the Sadducees are designated here is supported by no evidence. That those who wished to be named only after Christ are to be understood from the names of the remaining schismatics is apparent: however much they did not differ in the doctrine of faith. This Pareus also acknowledges: He now reveals what kind of schisms and what sort of disputes theirs were. They were contending about their teachers, whom some preferred over others as more perfect, with emulation and mutual contempt. Hence, one Church was being split into four sects. Those instructed by Paul called themselves Paulines. Others preferred Apollos, a teacher fervent in spirit and exceptional in eloquence and zeal, to Paul, and preferred to be called his disciples. Others wished to follow Peter, greater than both, as the prince of the Apostles, rather as their master. A few sounder ones were content with the name of Christ, the last and held in contempt as if they were general. Whence it is clear that the Calvinists rashly snatch this prohibition of the names of schismatics among those who agree in the doctrine of faith, for the abdication of distinguishing names among those who dissent in faith: such as when the Zwinglians, Calvinists, or the Reformed who dissent from us in faith are distinguished by similar διακριτικοῖς names. Add here the decision of Pareus himself: But is it not permitted to call heretics by the names of their authors, so that they may be avoided? Why should it not be permitted, when it is certain concerning the heresy? For thus Scripture calls the Nicolaitans, the Libertines. But it must be provided that those who are not heretics are not held to be such. And yet the Calvinists have been convicted of heresy quite often. Rightly, therefore, are they called by the name of their preceptor and heresiarch. However, there is no one who boasts of that consensus with us in the foundation of faith: which the blessed Lord Hutter, Dr. D. Sigwart, the blessed Lord D. Hülsemann, and we in the 'gründlichen Beweiß' in the name of the Theological Faculty of Wittenberg. In this, however, Pareus does not deserve assent, in that he affirms that the household of Chloe, Gaius, Crispus, baptized by Paul, and a few other Christians called themselves alone those who did not wish to communicate in the schism. For even those who called themselves Christians from Christ, insofar as they separated themselves from others through schism by that name appropriated only to themselves, were guilty of schism. Rightly the blessed Baldwin: To glory in the name of Christian alone, when it is a matter of the confession of doctrine, is just as much a vice as to make the Church depend on the gifts of teachers, and to be denominated from them alone. Therefore, those who say 'I am of Christ' are also placed among the schismatics. For this has the appearance as if all the ministers of Christ were being despised, as if Christ were dealing with us without them, and we were in no way helped in our Christianity by their work. Both, therefore, are to be avoided: Nor should one depend solely on teachers, which is what those do who, through schism, boast of the names of their teachers, one of this man, another of that, even if they otherwise agree in doctrine: nor should the name of Christian be boasted of in such a way as if you despise the ministers of Christ, through whom He deals with us. The middle way, therefore, between these extremes is to be a Christian, we who have given faith to Christ in baptism, and acknowledge Him alone as our redeemer and master; yet to receive a surname from that teacher who has especially propagated the doctrine of Christ among us: in which sense Patianus, that Bishop of Barcelona in Spain, said: Christian is my name, Catholic is my surname.

Latin:

V. 12. Λέγω δὲ τοῦτο. Nota ἐξηγήσεως, ut, inquam, Latinus. ἕκαστος ὑμῶν λέγει, ἐγὼ μέν εἰμι Παύλου, ἐγὼ δὲ Ἀπολλὼ, ἐγὼ δὲ Κηφᾶ;

Intelligendum hoc non de omnibus, sed de multis: ut infra XIV. 26. Et, sum Pauli, Apollo, Cephæ, nempe se- ctator. Quidam putant Paulum hæc nomina usurpasse, ut alios homines denotaret, unde factiones Corinthi nomina trahebant. Argumento utuntur, quod infra IV. 6. dicat Paulus, se ea, quæ dixerat, transformasse in se & Apollon. Verum ibi agitur de modestia, quam præ se ferre debent omnes Evangelii ministri, omnia ad Dei bonitatem refe- rendo. At hic quod dicit res erat intellecta ex Chloës fa- milia. Adde quod Clemens in Epistola de hoc tempore lo- quens non obscure ostendit, quid actum fuerit: Ἀναλάβετε τὴν ἐπιστολὴν τοῦ μακαρίου Παύλου τοῦ Ἀποστόλου, τί πρῶτον ὑμῖν ἐν ἀρχῇ τοῦ ἐυαγγελίου ἔγραψεν; ἐπ' ἀληθείας πνευματικῶς ἐπέ- στειλεν ὑμῖν, περὶ ἀυτοῦ τε καὶ Κηφᾶ καὶ Ἀπολλώ. Διὰ τὸ καὶ τότε προσκλίσεις ὑμᾶς πεποιῆσθαι· ἀλλ' ἡ πρόσκλισις ἐκείνη ἧττον ἁμαρτίαν ὑμῖν προσήνεγκεν. προσεκλίθητε γὰρ Ἀποστόλοις με- μαρτυρημένοις, καὶ ἀνδρί δεδοκιμασμένῳ παρ' ἀυτοῖς· νυνὶ δὲ κα- τανοήσατε, τίνες ὑμᾶς διέστρεψαν, &c. Ubi χαριεντίζων sectas appellat προσκλίσεις: quod Cicero vertit alicubi propensio- nes. Per Apostolos autem miraculis insignes, non dubium, quin intelligantur Clementi Petrus & Paulus; & per virum probatum Apollos. Alii ergo Corinthi ab Apollo instituti post Pauli abitum, alii ab ipso Paulo, alia qui è Judæa ve- nerant, à Petro, sub illis nominibus alia atque alia dogmata tradebant: quale quid & sub Matthiæ nomine factum ex Clemente Alexandrino cognoscimus.

Non ergo Grotius schismaticos vel autores schismatum facit ipsos Corinthios, vel Ecclesiæ istius membra, sed falsos doctores in illis grassan- tes, qui alia atque alia dogmata sub prætextu in- formationis seu traditionis ab Apollo, Petro, vel Paulo acceptæ sparserint. At arguit Apostolus ipsos Corinth. ἕκαστος ὑμῶν: nec de falsis dogma- tibus quicquam hic tradit ab aliis sparsis, sed ob scissiones inutiles ipsos reprehendit, quod quum in fide consonarent tum ipsi, tum doctores eorum quibus adhærescebant, Petrus, Paulus, Apollo, in partes tamen scinderentur ob diversa doctorum dona; quum aliis Apollo in admiratione fuerit ob eloquentiam, Act. XIII. aliis Petrus ob autorita- tem & senilem prudentiam, aliis Paulus ob singula- rem sapientiam & Scripturarum notitiam, &c. Inepte Papistæ, Sanderus de ritib. monach. l. VI. c. 4. Bellarm. l. 2. de R. P. c. 8. ex ordine, quasi gra- datio sit, colligunt Petri primatum jurisdictionis: nam ne quidem ordo dignitatis concluditur, quia alias Apollo dignior foret Paulo, nedum ordo ju- risdictionis. Ineptior autem est Baron. ad ann. Chr 57. excusans eos, qui dixere se esse Cephe; quia perinde id fuerit, ac si dixissent se esse Christi: nam parili jure diceretur, perinde etiam fuisse, cum dixere quidam se esse Pauli, ac si dicerent, se esse Apollo. Chrysost. autem observat, omnes quatuor fortes, ceu schismaticos reprehendi, ejusque cau- sam reddit Salmero, quod perperam ministros Christi & sibi invicem, & Christo opponerent, quæ ratio apparet è verbis sequentibus, μεμέρισται ὁ χριστὸς, ejusque hic est nervus; qui quoad efficaciam & fi- nem præconii à ministris divisus non est, & cujus ministri ratione virtutis & finis divisi à se invicem non sunt, illi non debent separari ab auditoribus suis tanquam capita distinctarum sectarum.

ἐγὼ δὲ χρισῦ.

Venerant enim ex Judæa quidam, qui ipsum Christum docentem audierant, &, quæ ille de nova genitura dixerat, eadem esse volebant cum iis, quæ dixerat de resurrectione, falso ac perniciose: Sadducæorum scilicet traduces.

Tales hæreticos Sadducæorum traduces hic de- signari nullo documento constat. Eos, qui à Chri- sto nominari tantum volebant intelligi ex reliquo- rum Schismaticorum nominibus apparet: utut nulli discreparint in fidei doctrina. Quod agnoscit etiam Pareus: Qualia schismata & cujusmodi li- tes eorum esse cognovit, nunc aperit. De Doctoribus suis contendebant, quos alii aliis ut perfectiores cum æmulatione & contemptu mutuo præferebant. Hinc in quatuor sectas una scindebatur Ecclesia. A Paulo instituti Paulinos se nominabant. Alii Apollo docto- rem spiritu fervidum eloquentia & zelo eximium Paulo anteferebant, ejusque discipuli dici malebant. Alii Petrum utroque majorem Apostolorum princi- pem magistrum potius sectari volebant. Pauci sanio- res Christi nomine contenti erant, postremi & con- temtim habiti quasi generales. Unde patet temere Calvinianos hoc nominis schismaticorum inter eos, qui in fidei doctrina consentiunt, interdictum abripere ad neminum discretivorum inter eos, qui dissentiunt in fide, abdicationem: qualia sunt, cum Zvingliani, Calviniani, aut similibus διακριτικοῖς nominibus Reformati à nobis in fide dissentientes insigniuntur. Adde hic Parei ipsius decisionem: Sed annon licet, hæreticos nominibus suorum autho- rum appellare, ut caveantur? Quidni liceat, quan- do de hæresi constat? Sic enim scriptura Nicolaitas, Libertinos appellat. Sed providendum, ne hæretici habeantur qui non sunt. Atqui de hæresi convicti sunt sæpius Calviniani. Recte ergo à nomine sui Præceptoris & hæresiarchæ appellantur. Nullus autem est ille, quem jactitat in fundamento fidei nobiscum consensus: Quod Pareo solide demon- stravit B. Dn. Hutterus, Dr. D. Sigvvartus, B. Dn. D. Hülsemannus, & nos im gründlichen Beweiß nomine Facult. Theologicæ Wittenbergensis. In eo tamen assensum non meretur Pareus, quod do- mesticos Chloes, Cajum, Crispum, à Paulo baptiza- tos, aliosque paucos Christianos se dixisse solum, qui schismati communicare noluærint, affirmat. Nam & illi, qui à Christo Christianos se dicebant, quate- nus ab aliis sese per schisma separabant illo nomi- ne sibi solum appropriato, schismatis rei erant. Recte B. Balduinus: Solo nomine Christiani gloria- ri, quando de confessione doctrinæ agitur, adeoque in vitio est, ac à donis doctorum Ecclesiam pendere, & ab iis solis denominari. Ideo inter schismaticos & illi ponuntur, qui dicunt: ego sum Christi. Hoc enim speciem habet, ac si omnes Christi ministri contemne- rentur, quasi absque illis Christus nobiscum ageret, nosque ipsorum opera, in Christianismo nostro, ni- hil adjuti simus. Utrumque ergo vitandum est: neque à solis doctoribus pendendum, quod faciunt, qui per schisma doctorum suorum nomina jactant, alter hujus, alter alterius, licet alias in doctrina con- veniant: neque etiam Christiani nomen ita jactan- dum, ac si despicias ministros Christi, per quos nobis- cum agit. Medium igitur inter haec extrema est Chri- stianum esse, qui Christo fidem dedimus in baptismo, & ipsum solum redemtorem ac magistrum nostrum agnoscimus; à doctore vero illo, qui doctrinam Christi praecipue inter nos propagavit, quasi cogno- men accipere: quo sensu dixit Patianus, Episcopus ille Barcilone in Hispania: Christianus mihi no- men est, Catholicus cognomen.

## 1:13
V. 13. μεμέρισται ὁ χριστός; By Christ he understands the Gospel of Christ, and asks whether it is different elsewhere? He signifies that this cannot be, since Christ has forbidden there to be many teachers and has commended unity to His own. Matt. XXIII. John XVI. 1. 21. 22.

μὴ Παῦλος ἐσταυρώθη ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν; Did Paul obtain for you all the benefits pertaining to eternal life by his own death? This belongs to Christ alone.

ἢ εἰς τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ Παύλου ἐβαπτίσθητε; Namely, so that you might derive a name from him, just as those whom John the Baptist had baptized did from him. See Matt. IX. 14. Mark II. 18. Luke VII. 18. & 24. John III. 25. Acts X. 37. Add what we have said on Matthew XXVIII. 19.

There is no reason why we should here understand by Christ the Gospel about Christ, a use of the word which is nowhere found. The Apostle means this: that Christ is one, not divided, who is the sole head of the Church. Consequently, the mystical body of Christ also ought to be one, not torn and divided. Furthermore, the Apostle teaches that we are to be named after Him by whom we have been redeemed, and in whose name we have been baptized; namely, as regards the κυριακὰ names, because there is no Lord but one, through whom we have been redeemed, in whose name we have been baptized, and upon whose authority we depend in divine matters: Yet, for that reason, the διακριτικὰ names, which are used to distinguish Orthodox teachers from heterodox ones, are not excluded: for even the disciples of John were called disciples of John, not as the author of the doctrine and Lord, whom he himself acknowledged to be Christ alone: See John I. 23. 25. 27. ch. III. 27. 29. ch. I. 7. 8. but because they were instructed in his school, so that they might be distinguished by this name from the disciples of the Pharisees: who are indeed distinguished also from the disciples of JESUS. John IV. 1. but not on account of doctrine, or baptism, but on account of the diversity of school or instruction; which, however, caused no schism: because Saint John referred his own to Christ as the sole authentic Master, and that true light illuminating all men, the Bridegroom of the Church, who comes from heaven and is above all, while he professed himself to be only a minister and friend of the bridegroom, John III. 29. 31. ch. I. 27. nor did John baptize in his own name, but in the name of JESUS, about whom he informed the people, so that they might believe in Him, that He is the Christ or Messiah promised to the world. Acts XIX. 4. 5. Compare what Luther, Vol. II. Jena, German, on both kinds, p. 92. seqq.

Latin:

V. 13. μεμέρισται ὁ χριστός; Per Christum intelligit Christi Evangelium, & quaerit, an id alibi sit aliud? Fieri id non posse significat, cum vetue- rit Christus multos esse doctores & unitatem suis commen- darit. Matth. XXIII. Joh. XVI. 1. 21. 22.

μὴ Παῦλος ἐσταυρώθη ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν; Num Paulus vobis omnia beneficia ad vitam aeternam pertinentia sua morte impetravit? Hoc Christi solius est.

ἢ εἰς τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ Παύλου ἐβαπτίσθητε; Nempe ut ab ipso nomen duceretis, sicut à Johanne Ba- ptista ii, quos ille baptizaverat. Vide Matth. IX. 14. Marc. II. 18. Luc. VII. 18. & 24. Joh. III. 25. Act. X. 37. Adde, quod diximus ad Matthaeum XXVIII. 19.

Non est, quod hic per Christum Evangelium de Christo intelligamus, qui vocis usus nuspiam reperitur. Id vult Apostolus: unum esse Christum, non divisum, qui caput Ecclesiae est unicum. Cor- pus proinde etiam Christi mysticum debere unum esse, non discissum & divisum. Porro ab eo deno- minandos nos esse docet Apostolus, à quo redem- ti, & in cujus nomen baptizati sumus; scilicet quo- ad nomina κυριακὰ, quia non est Dominus nisi unus, per quem redemti, in cujus nomen baptizati su- mus, à cujus autoritate in rebus divinis pendea- mus: Nec tamen ideo nomina διακριτικὰ, quae ob doctores Orthodoxos ab heterodoxis discernendos ad- hibentur, excluduntur: nam & à Johanne dicti sunt discipuli Johannis non ceu doctrinae authore & Domino, quem Christum solum & ipsa agno- scebat: Vid. Joh. I. 23. 25. 27. cap. III. 27. 29. c. I. 7. 8. sed quia in schola ejus informati erant, ut discernerentur hoc nomine à Pharisaeorum di- scipulis: qui à JESU quidem discipulis etiam distinguuntur. Joh. IV. 1. non autem ob doctrinam, aut baptismi, sed ob scholae vel informationis diver- sitatem; quae tamen schisma nullum inferebat: quia Sanct. Johannes suos ad Christum ceu Ma- gistrum authenticum unicum, & veram illam lu- cem omnes homines illuminantem remittebat, Sponsum Ecclesiae, qui de caelo venit, & super omnia est, se vero ministrum & sponsi amicum tantum pro- fitebatur Joh. III. 29. 31. c. I. 27. neque in sui no- men baptizavit Johannes, sed in nomen JESU, quo de populum informavit, ut in eum, quod sit Christus vel Messias mundo promissus, crede- rent. Act. XIX. 4. 5. Conf. quae Luth. T. II. Jenens. Germ. de utraque specie p. 92. seqq.

## 1:14
V. 14. εὐχαριστῶ τῷ θεῷ ὅτι οὐδένα ὑμῶν ἐβάπτισα. Namely, by my own hands.

εἰ μὴ Κρίσπον καὶ Γάϊον. Crispus the ruler of the synagogue, Acts XIIX. 8. Gaius, a host of Paul at some time, when he was in the city of Corinth, Rom. XVI. 23.

Latin:

V. 14. εὐχαριστῶ τῷ θεῷ ὅτι οὐδένα ὑμῶν ἐβάπτισα. Ipse nempe meis manibus.

εἰ μὴ Κρίσπον καὶ Γάϊον. Crispum Archisynagogum Act. XIIX. 8. Cajum hospi- tem aliquo tempore Pauli, cum in urbe Corinthi esset, Rom. XVI. 23.

## 1:15
V. 15. ἵνα μή τις εἴπῃ ὅτι εἰς τὸ ἐμὸν ὄνομα ἐβάπτισα. So that no one might be able to boast of such a thing about me, even under any pretext. For ἐβάπτισα that Manuscript has ἐβαπτίσθητε, just as the Latin also reads, with the same sense.

Latin:

V. 15. ἵνα μή τις εἴπῃ ὅτι εἰς τὸ ἐμὸν ὄνομα ἐβάπτισα. Ne quis vel ulla specie tale quid de me jactare possit. Pro ἐβάπτισα Manuscriptus ille habet ἐβαπτίσθητε, quomodo & Latinus legit, pari sensu.

## 1:16
V. 16. ἐβάπτισα δὲ καὶ τὸν Στεφανᾶ οἶκον. This is a correction of the previous statement. The Greeks think this Stephanas was a Philippian jailer, who, having been converted, immigrated to Corinth.

λοιπὸν οὐκ οἶδα εἴ τινα ἄλλον ἐβάπτισα. Namely, of those who now dwell in Corinth. He said he did not know this, because it could happen that others had migrated there from elsewhere.

He congratulates himself on that small number of those baptized:
