Si causam ministerialem respicias, non fieri debet vel à solis verbi ministris, vel ab Ecclesia sola: Sed à ministerio & cœtu Ecclesiæ simul: uti Aposto- lus & se absentem quidem corpore, sed præsentem spiritu nominat, & Ecclesiam congregatam in no- mine Jesu Christi una cum suo spiritu, ubi temere Grotius non omnes Christianos, sed optimos in- telligit. Quinam enim ita congregandi forent, quive optimi censendi, in obscuro fuisset. Neque illic καὶ τῦ ἐμῦ πνεύματος tantum notatur Pau- lum Spiritu visurum, quæ futura sint, sed innui- tur præsentia, & autoritas, quia si non corpora- liter, tamen spiritu præsens, conscius & consen- tiens esse debet Ecclesiæ minister, & Episcopus, quem referebat Apostolus, ejusque autoritate in- stituenda est excommunicatio. Ad formam ex- communicationis pertinet traditio in potestatem Satanæ, quæ infert tum exclusionem è regno DEI, utpote cui regnum, id est, potestas Satanæ oppo- nitur : Quâ removetur talis è consortio Ecclesiæ, & communione sanctorum non tantum quà publicum Ecclesiæ cœtum, & admissionem ad verbum DEI in ista particulari Ecclesia audiendum ac sacra- menta usurpanda : sed etiam quà privatam cum fidelibus familiarem conversationem, nisi politica, vel œconomicæ necessitudinis ratio postulet, ut è v. 11. colligere est : Non capietis cum ipso cibum : tum peculiarem potestatem Satanæ, quam permit- tere eidem Deus velit in tales. Unde ejecti extra societatem Ecclesiæ, ejusque bonis privati, ty- rannidi Diaboli, cujus potestas est extra Ecclesiam, ita exponuntur, ut in eos magis quam ante gras- setur, & in omne malum eos impellat. Recte de eo Theoder. ad h. l. Φρίκοις μέσον συνεκρότησε δι- καςήριον. Horrore plenum judicium constituit. Primum enim omnes in nomine Domini coë- git. Deinde etiam seipsum per gratiam spiritus introduxit, & ipsum etiam Dominum præsidere, & sententiam proferre ostendit, & lictori trade- re, & finis præscribere, ut corpus solum castiget. Animæ enim ex salutari disciplina medicamentum conficit. Hinc autem docemur, quod eos, qui se- gregantur, & ab Ecclesiastico corpore separan- tur, invadit Diabolus, illos gratia destitutos in- veniens. Et in 1. Tim. II. 20. Ab Ecclesiastico enim corpore separati, & divina gratia nudati erudeliter ab adversario flagellabantur, incide- bant in morbos, & difficiles afflictiones. Tra- duntur autem Satanæ, non ut plene potestati Dia- bolicæ committantur, quod conjunctum est cum æterno exitio, sed εἰς ὄλεθρον τῆς σαρκὸς, quod de morte quidem & afflictione corporis Chrysostomus, Theophylactus, Anshelmus, & autor glossæ interli- nearis intelligunt : Alii generalius de flagellis à Satana immittendis, sive per externam afflictio- nem corporis, sive per internas conscientiæ angustias horrores, & terrores, quales Hymenæus, & Phile- tus experti 1. Tim. I. 20. explicant, nec nisi temere

Thomas Erastus negavit, talem potestatem in Ecclesia dari, qua possit pertinaces facinorosos ita ejicere à communione Ecclesiastica, ut Sata- næ etiam tradantur ad affligendam animam anxie- tate ; contrá quem hac de re à Bellarmino & Sua- rez u. s. & Sandero de clave Dividis & peculiari- ter Theodoro Beza actum est. Finis excommuni- cationis & cribrationis istius Satanæ, partim ἀφαι- ρετικὸς est, ut intereat caro, cum fieri dicitur εἰς ὄλεθρον τῆς σαρκὸς interitus nempe libidinofæ car- nis, quæ nova contritione & crucifixione veteris hominis ita domari debet, ut intereat, quo pacto explicat Augustinus l. III. c. 1. contra Parmen. ad interitum carnis, id est, ut per pœnitentiam, quo- niam Satanæ traditus erat, interimeret sceleratam carnis concupiscentiam, quemadmodum etiam fi- nis similis expressus est, cum Hymenæus, & Ale- xander Satanæ traditi sunt, ut nempe discerent non blasphemare : Partim θετικὸς, ut spiritus sal- vus sit : Qui mortificatâ carne suscitatur, veteri- que homine corrupto novus prodit, qui salutem tandem consequitur : Ut spiritus sit salvus, hoc est, ut miser tandem peccator salvus fiat spiritu, vel juxta spiritum, seu juxta novum spiritualem hominem, ut Gal. VI. 18. dicitur, qui seminat in spiritu, de spiritu metet vitam æternam : Et quem- admodum caro & sanguis seu natura nostra qua corruptibilis est, regnum DEI possidere non pos- sunt 1. Cor. XV. 20. Ita nec qua peccato obno- xia : Ideoque oportet carnem interire, ut spiritus salvetur, & hominem nostrum externum corrum- pi, ut is, qui intus est, renovetur de die in diem 2. Cor. IV. 11. nosque transformemur in imaginem Christi à claritate in claritatem cap. III. 18. donec ab hac imperfectione transeamus ad perfectionem, cum evacuabitur, quod ex parte est, & perfectum veniet, vel succedet 1. Cor. XIII. 20. Unde monet Apostolus, ut has promissiones habentes mundemus nos ab omni inquinamento carnis, & spiritus perficientes sanctificationem in timore DEI 2. Cor. VII. 1. Si enim spiritu facta carnis mortificaverimus, vivemus. Rom. IIX. 13. & liberati à peccato, servi autem facti justitiæ fructum nostrum habemus in sanctificationem, finem vero vitam æternam Rom. VI. 22. Finis ergo hujus traditionis in potestatem Satanæ non est, ut sceleratus vel animâ, vel corpore pereat, sed ut à peccato ad resipiscentiam & vitam æternam reducatur. Et dum domatur carnis lascivia, crucifigitur vetus homo, mortificatur, & corrumpitur; salvus vero evadit spiritus. Atque in eam sententiam explicat Ambrosius & Anselmus, nec non Augustinus l. III. contra Parm. c. 2. ὄλεθρον τῆς σαρκὸς, carnalis voluptas intereat, quem tamen cum Chrysostomo, & Theophylacto, Theodoreto Oecumenius & Cornelius à Lapide &c. de ægritudine corporis, vulneribus, aut plagis, quibus macerari debuerit à Diabolo, accipiunt, ut caro atteratur, carnisque vigor intereat, ut ita humiliatus resipiscat, ut spiritus salvus sit, id est, ut anima & mens hac pœna resipiscens & renovata salva sit in die judicii. Quod vero non exclusive accipiendum de sola anima, etsi ea proprium subjectum sit resipiscentiæ, & renovationis. B. Hunnius noster, effectus, inquit, hujus operis est pœna temporalis, qua homo excommunicatus à Satana divexatur tentationibus, & conscientiæ pavoribus, vel aliis à DEO immissis calamitatibus affligitur, quibus caro ipsius subigitur, & domatur, ut Spiritui S. ad salutarem conversionem in animo eliciendam locus esse queat, ut spiritus, adeoque cum spiritu corpus quoque in die Domini salvetur. Cui explicationi etiam calculum addit B. Hülsemannus, allegans pro eadem cum Tertull. lib. IV. contr. Març. c. 6. Cyprian. Ep. XXI IX. & XL. & Augustino l. c. Hugonem, Thomam, Salmeronem, Estium, Melanchthonem, & Hemmingium, sed officere videntur tum oppositio carnis & spiritus, quæ sensu Paulo familiari accipienda non pro corpore & anima, sed pro homine exteriori vel novo, uti à Christo etiam accipitur Joh. III. 5. tum quod hoc non tam ad finem traditionis in potestatem Satanæ ex intentione Pauli, & Ecclesiæ faciat, ut homo corpore & anima affligatur à Satana, quam ad potestatis illius formale, cui committitur ad carnis interitum & spiritus salutem, tum quod oppositio illa ægre salvetur, aut explicari possit, cum non tantum spiritus, id est, anima in die Domini salutem adipisci debeat plenariam, sed cum spiritu etiam corpus: Nec afflictiones illæ ad corpus tantum referantur, sed imprimis ad animam, quæ terroribus, & horroribus sit divexanda, ut sentiatur in conscientia ira DEI, misereque torqueatur. Quæ è discussione Socinianæ ψευδερμηνείας uberius deinde constabunt.

Finis ergo est non damnatio, sed salus facinorosorum, ut spiritus salvus sit in die Jesu Christi. Ideoque excommunicatio non infert excisionem totalem, qualis erat Ananiæ & Sapphiræ Act. V. Ad hanc enim Petrus non Satanæ usus est traditione, sed virtute Christi: Non privationem bonorum, possessionum, & dominii, qualem Papistæ Bellarminus, Suarez u. S. & Sanderus de clave Da- vid. è potestate excommunicationis deducunt, vi ejusdem Reges ipsos ac Principes regnis, & dominiis, ac possessionibus suis exuentes: Sed suspensionem, & privationem virium ac beneficio- rum Ecclesiæ, atque anxietatis animæ, quibus à Satana exagitantur, qui in ejus potestate sunt, tum afflictionem quandoque etiam corporis. Est autem hæc pœna Ecclesiastica, non politica ideo- que ex eadem non colligere licet, hæreticos ceu excommunicatos capitali supplicio afficiendos esse, quod fit à Bellarm. l. 3. de laic. c. 21. proceden- te à majori ad minus, ast non in eodem sed di- verso pœnarum genere. Unde ἀσυλλογισία ori- tur, à pœna scil. Ecclesiastica ad politicam V. B. Gerhardus de Magistrat. §. 362.

Porro circa objectum excommunicationis ob- servandum, quod objectum excommunicationis majoris non sint Reges & Principes. Major enim excommunicatio, B. Hülsemanno de correptione fra- terna p. 302. monente, quæ Christianis interdi- cit libero ac voluntario commercio edendi, bi- bendi, conversandi cum excommunicato, in Re- gibus tam non habet locum, quam nec in conju- gibus, ne reddant conjugale debitum, in filiis ne parentibus officia debita præstent; in servis & subditis, ne Dominis suis servitia exhibeant. Spi- ritualis enim animæ pœna non dissolvit vincula, quæ jus divinum, naturæ & gentium colligaverunt; Sed illa tantum quæ baptismi & sacramenti Cœnæ communione contracta sunt: quod per beneficium Ecclesiæ collatum non est, neque alicui auferri po- test per censuram Ecclesiæ. Conf. etiam B. Luthe- rus de Banno Tom. I. Jen. Germ. & in admonitio- ne ad Ecclesiasticos Augustæ congregatos Anno 1530. Tom. V. Jen. Germ. Laudat hanc B. Hülseman- ni sententiam B. Dannhauerus in lib. conscien- tiæ aperto part. II. p. 1133. Si quæstio sit de excom- municatione positiva extrema majori ac tamen in- ferenda in invitum ac refractarium, an in Regem hujusmodi rigor distringi debeat? Laudat & simi- lem M. Antonii de dominis sententiam in l. VI. de Rep. Eccles. c. 9. p. 751. Si sumamus excom- municationem pro pœna illa ordinaria rigorosa, qua solemus ex nostrorum fidelium societate aliquem ex- cludere, ita ut sit nobis tanquam Ethnicus & pu- blicanus, cum prohibitione, ne fideles ipsius utan- tur consuetudine & consortio, certe neque potest neque debet supremus princeps excommunicari. Non po- test, quia qua ratione hæc excommunicatio nihil operatur in filiis respectu patris, in Dominis, respe- ctu familiæ, in uxore, respectu viri, quia, ut passim docent Scholastici & Summistæ, excommunicatio hæc nihil potest contra jus naturæ, eodem profecto jure, ut pater perpetuo debet curam gerere filiorum & familiæ, ita etiam quisque rex curam debet gerere totius sui populi, & populus ex necessitate indiget cura & gubernatione sui regis. Sed neque ex pru- dentia debet, etiamsi posset rex tali excommunica- tione excommunicari, ex regula optima Augustini. Concludit M. Antonius: Moraliter itaque loquen- do consilium hujusmodi separationis, juxta Augu- stini regulam semper & inane erit, & perniciosum, imo ut idem asserit, & impium, & superbum & sa- crilegum. Addit notanter B. Hülsemannus: quin etiam ad minorem Regum & Principum excom- municationem caute & lente procedendum est ob inseparabile periculum schismatis & ad majus ma- lum ab Ecclesia avertendum, si pertinaces illi fue- rint & emendari nolint. Idque etiam in aliis per- sonis observandum, cum periculum schismatis & ruinæ Ecclesiæ metuendum. Suspendendam vel et- iam omittendam esse excommunicationem son- tium, si schisma in totâ communitate, aut majus malum, quam est toleratio peccatorum, inde ori- turum appareat. Neque propterea, quod quidam peccatores non excommunicantur, deserendam esse communionem externam cum innocentibus, inter quos illi vivunt. Ubi ad præceptum Apo- stoli in hoc capite v. ult. Auferte malum de me- dio vestri sic respondet S. Augustinus: In hac vel- ut angustia quæstionis non aliquid novum aut in- solitum dicas, sed quod sanitas observat Ecclesiæ, ut cum quisquam fratrum, id est, Christianorum intus in societate Ecclesiæ constitutorum, in aliquo tali peccato fuerit deprehensus, ut anathemate di- gnus habeatur, fiat hoc, UBI PERICULUM SCHISMATIS NULLUM EST, atque id, cum ea dilectione, de qua ipse alibi præcipit di- cens, non ut inimicum eum existimetis, sed corri- pite ut fratrem. Non enim estis ad eradicandum, sed ad corrigendum. Quæ addit illic S. Augusti- nus, digna sunt, quæ etiam hic legantur. Quod si se non agnoverit, neque pœnitendo correxerit, ipse foras exiet, & per propriam voluntatem ab Eccle- siæ unitate dirimetur. Nam & ipse Dominus cum servis, volentibus zizania colligere, dixit: sinite utrumque crescere, usque ad messem; præmisit causam dicens, ne forte, cum velitis colligere zi- zania, eradicetis simul & triticum. Ubi satis osten- dit, cum metus iste non subest, sed omnino de fru- mentorum certa stabilitate certa securitas manet; id est, quando ita cujusque crimen notum est omni- bus, & omnibus execrabile apparet, ut vel nullos prorsus, vel non tales habeat defensores per quos possit schisma exurgere; non dormiat severitas dis- ciplinæ, in qua tanto est efficacior emendatio pra- vitatis, quanto diligentior conservatio charitatis. Tunc autem hoc sine labe pacis & unitatis, & sine læsione frumentorum fieri potest, cum congregatio- nis Ecclesiæ multitudo ab eo crimine, quod est ana- thematizatum, aliena est. Ivo Carnotensis Ep. CXLIV. ad Paschalem: Causam, inquit, Regum temperetis, ne contingat de eo illud Salomonis: Qui multum emungit, elicit sanguinem. Et Epist. CXXXII. ad Senonensem: Et quia dispensationes rerum temporalium Regibus attributæ sunt, & Ba- silei, id est fundamentum populi, & caput ejus sunt, si aliquando potestate sibi concessa abutuntur, non sunt à nobis graviter exasperandi. Sed ubi Sacer- dotum admonitionibus non acquieverunt, divino ju- dicio sunt reservandi.

Crellius Socinianus negat simplicem excommu- nicationem hic designari: "Vult significari amplius quiddam, ad quod sc. singulari Domini Jesu poten- tia & Apostolica autoritate sit opus:. Nec de iis, qui temporaliter tantum ab Ecclesiæ consortio arcentur jure dici posse, eos Satanæ potestati tradi, cum nul- lum idcirco, neque secundum carnem, neque secun- dum spiritum jus in ipsos Satanæ detur. Itaque non dubium ipsi videtur, quin variæ afflictiones corpo- ris à Satana inferendæ his verbis significentur, non aliter, ac si Satanæ tanquam carnifici cuidam ve- xandus quispiam castigandusque tradatur. Per carnis autem perditionem non appetitus carnalis mortem quandam metaphoricam, sed ipsius cor- poris veram ac propriam mortem & destructionem, quamvis non subito, sed per varias afflictiones & dolores sensim illatam significari vult. Siquidem nec Satanas per se rei bonæ minister sit idoneus, & perditioni carnis non vita ex spiritus arbitrio exa- cta, sed salus in die Domini nostri opponatur: Et denique Græca vox ὄλεθρος durior esse videatur, quam ut hanc spiritualem carnis mortem designet, necuspiam hoc sensu ab Apostolo usurpetur. Quo etiam abeunt commenta Jona Schlichtingii in Comm. ad hunc locum. Sed hæc non officiunt communi Patrum & Theologorum nostratium aliorumque Interpretum sententiá, qui in eo consentiunt, quod hic de excommunicatione sermo fit. Nam etsi δύναμις vel potentia Jesu ad id requiratur, ut quis Satanæ tradatur, non tamen ea est extraordinaria vel miraculosa potestas: Etsi Apostolus sese conjungat cœtui Ecclesiastico in hoc actu, non tamen ut Apostolus, sed ut Ecclesiæ minister hic spectatur è 1. Cor. IV. 1. nec Apostolicæ autoritatis hoc proprium est. Quod ad miracula pertinere, & ideo Ecclesiam sibi arrogare non debere, ut aliquem Satanæ tradat, temeré assumit Schlichtingius. Nam ita & peccata ligare pro miraculo habendum fuerit. Posse Ecclesiam preces fundere ad Christum, ut immundos, præsertim apostatas, blasphemos & persecutores Satanæ tradat, fatetur Schlichtingius. Et cum preces Ecclesiæ exaudire velit, atque exaudiat Christus: Annon precibus suis Ecclesia tales in potestatem Satanæ tradere queat? Excommunicationem enim tales preces adjunctas habere, & ideo vocari Anathema Maran Atha c. XVI. 22. agnoscit hic Schlichtingius. Quapropter dubium non est, eos, qui ita excommunicantur, Satanæ tradi, quod hic etiam factum. Quos & conscientiæ anxietatibus, quandoq; etiam afflictionibus torquere solet, potestate in eos accepta. Quod ex Theodoreto antea observatum; potuisse tamen aliquid extraordinarii in exemplo præsenti, quando afflictiones animæ & corporis singulares efficacia precum Apostoli ad educendam ab exitio æterno animam per seriam resipiscentiam, intervenisse, non omnino inficias iverim, quod tantum profert Apostolus, ut homo à flagitio insolito tandem liberatus & è faucibus Satanæ per illas ipsas afflictiones Satanicas ereptus fuerit. Nec vero preces solum fundit ad Deum Ecclesia, sed judiciariam fert sententiam, in cœlis ratam, quo de B. Hunnius noster: Monemur excommunicationem legitimam non esse inane terriculamentum, aut fulgur ex pelvi, sed actionem & sententiam coram Deo ratam & efficacem, adeoque temporalium & æternarum pœnarum judicio prægnantem. Vere enim tales traduntur Satanæ juxta sententiam immotam Christi Matth. 16. & 18. ut & Joh. 20. Et cur per ὄλεθρον τῆς σαρκὸς non indicetur mors impropria appetitus carnalis? siquidem quod ad Dei & Ecclesiæ intentionem (etsi non Satanæ) finis istarum afflictionum sit vera pœnitentia, quæ peccati agnitionem infert, quamq; sequitur mortificatio carnis, ut concupiscentiæ extinguantur, & vetus homo aboleatur. Nec vero per ὄλεθρον τῆς σαρκὸς ipsa corporis mors, & destructio significatur, sic enim potius ὄλεθρον τῦ σώματος dixisset, neq; vel hoc incesti, vel Hymenei, vel Alexandri 1. Tim. I. 20. vel aliorum exemplis constat, ab Apostolo ita eos percussos, aut Satanæ ad percutiendum traditos, ut corporalibus afflictionibus lenta morte afficerentur, quo se ad pœnitentiam præpararent, ut spiritus salvaretur; de tali miraculosa percussione altum in scripturis silentium est. Ex adverso vero liquet, servatum esse huncce facinorosum etiam in vita temporali è 2. Cor. VII. 7. Quid etiam attinebat Ecclesiam orare, ut veniam resipiscenti mœcho concederet, nisi ab Ecclesia simul & Apostolo Satanæ potestati traditus fuisset. Ab illis namque vicissim à Satana liberandus erat, per quos ei traditus fuerat. Tum si affligendus is fuit à Satana usq; ad mortem, atque ea ratione & intentione, ab Apostolo, autoritate non pastorali, sed Apostolica traditus fuit Satanæ, cur Apostolus obsecrat Corinthios, ut veniam ipsi concedant?

Rationes Crellii adversus receptiorem τῦ ὄλέ- θρε τῆς σαρκὸς significationem, nullum robur ha- bent. Nam etsi Satanas per se & ex intentione propria non sit rei tam bonæ minister: Esse tamen potest, quod ad ipsum, ex accidenti præter suam intentionem juxta ordinationem & directionem divinam, cum Deus tentationes, etiam Diabolicas, nôrit ad finem bonum dirigere: ut hic in aprico est, ad salutem animæ dirigi afflictiones Satanæ, quod negare non potest Crellius: Cæterum, inquit, bis verbis, ut & sequentibus, quibus traditionis Sa- tanæ finis indicatur, potestati Satanæ limites quidem ponuntur, non ut corpus tantum affligat, in animam nullum jus habeat; nec repentina morte hominem extinguat, sed lentis ictibus consumat, quo pœniten- tiam agere, & vitam corrigere, ac proinde sempi- ternam salutem in adventu Domini nostri Jesu Christi consequi possit. Non secus ac Satanæ quoque illius, cui Jobus fuerat permissus, potestas circumscripta fuit, licet non eadem modo: Ibi quidem, ne vitæ Jobi noceret, his vero ne cælesti istius hominis saluti. Porro carnis perditioni opponitur quidem salus in die Domini nostri Jesu Christi; sed nominatur ita finis ultimus positivus, non excluditur intermedius, sed includitur, utpote vivificatio spiritus, quæ di- recte & immediate opponitur mortificationi car- nis, quam denique consequitur salvatio in die Do- mini. Quod tertio Græcam vocem ὄλεθρον durio- rem dicit, quam ut spiritualem carnis mortem desi- gnet, vanum atque frivolum est. Annon enim alias ejusmodi voces adhibentur ab Apostolo? uti v. c. θανατῶτε Rom. IIX.13. Νεκρώσατε τὰ μέλη τὰ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς Col. III.5. Τὴν σάρκα ἐσταύρωσαν Gal.V.24. Ὁ ἔξω ἄνθρωπος διαφθείρεται 2. Cor.V. 16. Ἀπογε- νόμενοι ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις 1. Petr.II.24. &c. Nec sem- per vox ὄλεθρος totalem interitum notat: sæpe affli- ctionem tantum designat, ut ex usu LXX. Interpp. & concordantiis Kircheri videre est. Nuspiam vero annihilationem omnimodam infert, ac ne qui- dem, cum de ipsa damnatorum pœna agitur. Annon vero θανάτωσις, διαφθορὰ τῆς σαρκος satis ὀλέθρου vel perditionis sunt? Crucifixio enim & mortifica- tio ac corruptio ad interitū carnis tendunt; Quem, si omnino omnimoda destructio urgeatur in hac voce ὄλεθρος carnis potius vel veteri homini cōvani- re finaliter in extirpatione peccati, quã corpori no- stro in cinerefactione manifestū est. Illud enim pla- ne esse desinit, hoc non definit, nec in nihilum abit, quia resuscitabitur olim gloriose in novissimo die.

Quod ad quartum, quod nuspiam vox ὀλέθρου τῆς σαρκὸς de mortificatione carnis ab Apostolo usurpetur, Resp. Nec uspiam eam de totali annihilatione cor- poris humani usurpari, imo hanc analogiæ fidei de resurrectione mortuorum καθδιάμετρον adversari. Et sufficit, quod Synodymæ voces, quas adduxi- mus, ab Apostolo adhibeantur. Vox ὀλέθρου nu- spiam cum voce τῆς σαρκὸς occurrit, imo binis tã- tum vicibus sed de interitu in inferno, qui afflictio- nis est gravissimæ, non annihilationis, adhibetur in N. T. Satis autem afflictionis est carni nostræ & veteri homini, cum crucifigitur, corrumpitur, in- teritum deniq; illi adfert. Tandem observandum Socinianorum σόφισμα, quo hic exsculpere hy- pothesin suam prrorsus ἀθεόλογον & hæreticam co- nantur Crell. pariter, & Schlichtingius, ex opposi- tione carnis & spiritus, quod caro perdenda dicatur, spiritus vero salvandus, quod nempe corpus hominis penitus intereat & annihiletur: Spiritus vero solus h. e. anima superstes maneat in diem Jesu Christi. Mortem fore totalem abolitionem corporis & an- nihilationem, quia vox ὀλέθρου exitium notat, falso colligitur. Nam nec exitium omnimodum ea vox importat; neque cum exitium notat, abolitionem per annihilationem infert, ut videre est 2. Thess.I.9.

1. Tim. VI. 9. Impios enim in die extremo non anni- hilatum iri, sed in æternum ignem conjiciendos Scriptura docet, nec id inficiari audent Sociniani. Nam etsi solum spiritus dicatur servari, non tamen id denegatur eo ipso corpori, utpote olim ad æter- nam salutem resuscitando, quia non opponitur spiritus corpori, ut hominis divisio in animam & corpus insinuetur, sed caro & spiritus, ut alias fre- quenter fit, Rom. VII. 14. seqq. Gal. V. 17. &c. sibi opponuntur, & ita carni interitus, imo etiam to- talis abolitio convenit. Spiritus autem salvari di- citur, quia non nisi novus & spiritualis homo ad vitam æternam pervenit. Non ergo dividit homi- nem Apostolus, quasi eum partim interire, partim servari velit. Nam nec corpus interire potest, sine divulsione ab anima, nec anima servari, absq; cor- poris salute, relicto scil. in morte perpetua cor- pore: Sed occurrit hic illa Paulo familiaris antithe- sis carnis & spiritus pro veteri & novo homine. Nec de pœna miraculosa & excommunicatione hic agi- tur. Nam reprehenduntur Corinthii, quod non pridem incestum è medio sui sustulerint; qui vero de non edito miraculo reprehendi non poterant: mandatur, ut tollant: quibus certe mandari mira- culum non potuit. Ad miracula Apostolorum non opus erat solenni Ecclesiæ conventu. Ad tollen- dum vero istum congregatio Ecclesiæ in nomine Jesu requirebatur. Finis traditionis in potestatem Satanæ erat non ut incestuosus occideretur, sed ut spiritu resipisceret, carne mortificata, nec intereat deniq;. Sicut eodem fini illi Satanæ traditi 1. Tim. I. 20. non ut interficerentur, & è medio tollerentur, sed ut resipiscerent, & discerent non blasphemare. Ideo tolli jubetur incestuosus, non ut non sit, vel è medio hominum tollatur; sed ut non toleretur in medio Ecclesiæ, non commisceatur fratribus, non cibus cum ipso sumatur v. 11. Neque vero Corinthii eum sustulerunt miraculo, qui tamen sine dubio executi sunt mandatum Apostoli; sed publica ob- jurgatione eum abdicarunt ab Ecclesia, uti è 2. Cor. II. 6. constat ἐπιτιμίαν ὑπὸ πλειόνων objurgationem à pluribus factam ipsi suffecisse. Unde non aliter Ambrosius, & Augustinus hunc locum explicant, quam de excommunicatione ejus. Chrysostomus quidem & Hieronymus accessisse putant miracu- losam pœnam, sed id ex textu colligi nequit, & in vita mansisse hominem, non miraculo periisse, in aprico est, nec diffitetur Crellius.

Effugio utitur vanissimo, quod id factum, quia egit pœnitentiam, quodque decretum Apostoli non ab- solutum fuerit, sed hypotheticum. Quo pacto ita ha- bebit decretum: Jam decrevi, ut is, qui sc. hoc pa- travit, in nomine Domini nostri Jesu Christi con- gregatis vobis & meo nomine, una cum potestate Domini nostri Jesu Christi tradatur Satanæ ad in- teritu carnis, h. e. ut Satanæ à me & vobis tradatur affligendus, ut, nisi resipiscat, corpus intereat: Spi- ritus autem salvus sit. Si vero resipiscat, corpus in- tereat. Ecquisnam vero illam glossam admittet, & ubi, obsecro, hypothesis illa in textu? Annon sa- piunt omnia simplex decretum? Uti simpliciter mandatur, ne commisceantur cum eo, ut tollant eum è medio sui. Annon finis, cur Satanæ traden- dus, est tum ut caro intereat, tum ut spiritus salvus sit? Si vero ideo à Satana affligendus erat, ut lentis ictibus consumeretur, quo pœnitentiam agere posset, & corpore pereunte spiritus salvaretur, ut interpretatur Crellius, annon eo pacto pœnitentia medium quoddam salvandi spiritus erit, non vero liberandi corpus ab interitu & exitio? Sed mitti- mus tandem detorsiones istas Socinianorum, qui- bus hic utique sanior fuit Grotius, ὄλεθρον τῆς σαρ- κὸς exstinctionem carnalium affectuum, quæ sit ira di- vinæ sensu, intelligens. Cui tamen in eo calcu- lum adjicere non possumus, quod πνεῦμα de ani- mo apud Deum deposito explicet, quia spiritus, cum carni opponitur, non ipsam animam ὀσιωδῶς spe- ctatam notat, nec de animâ apud Deum depositâ hic quicquam habetur, sed de hominis pœnitentis & mortificati carne, spirituque consequenter vivifi- cati salute, cujus causâ ceu medicinale remedium excommunicatio hic instituenda erat.

PARS II. De fermenti expurgatione.

## 5:6-8
Vers. 6. 8 Your boasting is not good. You are undeservedly pleased with such a teacher, more a philosopher than a Christian.

Who that Doctor is, neither Grotius explains, nor does it appear from the text, where there is no trace of such a Doctor who is more a philosopher than a Christian. Perhaps he followed Chrysostom, who understands that boasting by which they boasted on account of the incestuous man, who was learned and eloquent, and the same a Pseudo-Apostle Doctor. But these things are destitute of foundation, even if Theophylact followed Chrysostom as is his custom: He shows, he says, in this place that the Corinthians had allowed this adulterer to repent in no way, because they considered his wisdom to be a glory. For he was held among them as one of the wise. Others place the boasting in this, that each one, flattering himself and trusting in his own supposed holiness and innocence, silently rejoices in his heart, but that he has not fallen so enormously as that incestuous man, as B. Weinrichius and B. Hunnius explain. And thus also almost B. Mylius: If I am not mistaken, the Apostle had understood that boasting by which they had excused only one in the whole city, given over to that wickedness. Others assign here an argument taken from equity: You wish to boast of the excellence of your Church, especially of your Doctors, it is therefore just that you should remove such foul things, on account of which you are not undeservedly ill-spoken of by others: Your boasting is not good. You falsely arrogate to yourselves the riches of heavenly wisdom, and the kingdom over sin and the Devil, when you connive at such diabolical crimes, as B. Balduinus has it. But the Apostle wishes to proceed from this special correction of the tolerated incestuous person to a general exhortation concerning purging out any leaven whatsoever and avoiding dealings with any wicked persons. Wherefore he also warns that that one thing greatly detracts from their glory, and that from it greater harm could easily arise. For he refers entirely in these words to those things which he had previously objected to them through irony, 'you are already satisfied, you are already rich, you already reign,' as if to say: You boast indeed in this way; but by this one example it is evident that your boasting is vain. This is not good praise, that you tolerate such a public and notorious scandal, and are still puffed up. Do you not know that a little leaven also leavens the whole lump? By this one example of such a flagrant act of fornication, adultery, and most grave incest, the lump or mystical body of the Church can be much corrupted. Since vices easily penetrate to others, who are incited to the same by impunity, and by them not being removed, they are defiled.

And a grape touched by a grape takes on its color.

Tertullian translates ζυμοῖ as 'desipit,' that is, he makes it sour, because leaven infects the whole mass of mixed flour with its flavor and acidity. Which is called φύραμα, and afterwards is rendered as 'conspersio' (lump) from φυρᾶν, that is, from mixing. So that you may be a new lump, or a new mass, and your Church may be new and pure.

Οὐκ ὄιδατε ὅτι μικρὰ ζύμη ὅλον τὸ φύραμα ζυμοῖ. The same proverb is in Gal. V. 9. The Hebrews by 'leaven' understand metaphorically everything which has the power of corrupting others, whether it be a dogma, or an example, or something else. See what is said at Matt. XVI. 5. Thus the book Zeror in the institution of the Passover interprets חמץ that is leaven mystically as יצר הרע the evil appetite.

That proverb in Gal. V. 9. concerning the leaven of the doctrine of the Pseudo-Apostles, just as in Matt. XVI, 6. concerning the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees, occurs, but here it is concerning the leaven of a scandalous life. From both there is great danger, unless it is purged out. But the sharper the leaven is, the more power it has to leaven the lump. Such was that of the most serious wickedness, tolerated with boasting of purity and excellence, a certain scandal to the Church.

Every vice of the mind is so much the more conspicuous in itself, the greater the person is considered to be who commits the crime. For the Corinthians were exalting themselves above others in the highest degree.

Latin:

Vers. 6. 8 καλὸν τὸ καύχημα ὑμῶν. Immerito vobis placetis isto tali doctore, philosopho magis, quam Christiano.

Quisnam ille Doctor sit, nec Grotius explicat, nec è textu apparet, ubi nullum talis Doctoris phi- losophi magis quam Christiani vestigium. Forte Chrysostomum sequutus est, qui gloriationem eam intelligit, qua ob incestuosum virum doctum, & facundum, eundemque Doctorem Pseudo-Apostolum gloriati sunt. Sed hæc fundamento destituuntur, etsi Chrysostomum pro more sequutus Theophy- lactus: Ostendit, inquit, hoc loco Corinthios nihil permisisse adulterum hunc pœnitere, quia bujus sa- pientiam gloriæ ducerent. Erat enim is apud eos ba- bitus è sapientibus unus. Alii gloriationem in eo ponunt, quod unusquisque sibi abblandiens, & in sua quasi sanctimonia & innocentia confidens taci- te in sinu suo gaudeat, sed non ita enormiter lapsum esse, atque incestuosus ille, ut exponit B. Weinrichius, & B. Hunnius. Atque ita etiam fere B. Mylius: Ni fallor, eam gloriationem intellexerat Apostolus, qua unum duntaxat in civitate tota esse excusaverant, flagitio isti deditum. Alii argumentum ab æquo pe- titum hic assignant : Gloriam vultis de excellentia vestra Ecclesiæ, imprimis Doctorum vestrorum, æquum igitur est, ut removeatis ejusmodi fæda, ob quæ non immerito male auditis apud alios: Alios non est bona gloriatio vestra. Falso vobis arrogatis divitias sapientiæ cœlestis, & regnum super pecca- tum & Diabolum, cum ad ejusmodi diabolica sce- lera conniveatis, ut B. Balduinus habet. Sed pro- gredi vult Apostolus ab hac speciali ἐπανορθώσει tolerati incestuosi ad generalem παραίνεσιν de quo- vis fermento expurgando & vitandis commerciis cum quibusvis sceleratis. Quapropter etiam monet, unum illud valde ipsorum gloriæ derogare, & ex eo facile majus damnum oriri posse. Respicit enim omnino his verbis ea, quæ supra ipsis per ironiam objecerat, jam saturati estis, jam ditati, jam regna- tis q. d. Gloriamini quidem ita; Sed vel hoc uno exemplo constat, gloriationem vestra vanam esse. Non bona laus hæc est, quod tantum scandalum publicum & notorium toleretis, & adhuc inflati sitis. An nescitis paululo etiam fermenti totam massam fermentari? Potest hoc uno exemplo tati flagitii scortationis, adulterii, & incestus gravissi- mi multum corrumpi massa vel corpus mysticum Ecclesiæ. Quum vitia facile penetrent ad alios, qui impunitate ad eadem incitantur, iisque non sublatis coinquinantur.

Uvaq; contacta livorem ducat ab uva.

Tertullianus ζυμοῖ vertit, desipit, id est, desipi- dam facit, quia totam farinæ commixtæ massam sapore & acore suo inficit fermentum. Quæ φύ- ραμα dicitur, & postea conspersio redditur ἀπὸ τοῦ φυρᾶν id est à miscendo. Ut sitis nova consper- sio, vel nova massa, & sit vestra Ecclesia nova & pura.

Οὐκ ὄιδατε ὅτι μικρὰ ζύμη ὅλον τὸ φύραμα ζυμοῖ. Iedm proverbium Gal. V. 9. Hebræi per ζύμην intelli- gunt μεταφορικῶς omne id, quod alia corrumpendi vim habet, sive dogma sit, sive exemplum, sive aliud aliquid. Vide quæ dicta ad Matth. XVI. 5. Ita liber Zeror in institu- tione paschatis חמץ id est fermentum mystice interpreta- tur יצר הרע malum appetitum.

Proverbium illud Gal. V. 9. de fermento do- ctrinæ Pseudo-Apostolorum uti Matth. XVI, 6. de fermento Pharisæorum & Sadducæorum occur- rit, hic vero de fermento scandalosæ vitæ. Ab utro- que magnum est periculum, nisi expurgetur. Quo autem fermentum acrius est, eo magis massam fermentandi vim habet. Tale erat illud sceleris gravissimi, tolerati cum gloriatione puritatis & excellentiæ, certum Ecclesiæ scandalum.

Omne animi vitium tanto conspectius in se Est, quanto major crimen qui patrat habetur. Efferebant enim sese præ aliis maxime Corin- thii.

## 5:7
V. 7. Purge out therefore the old leaven. Everything through which the Church can be corrupted. The sense, as I have said, is the mystical sense of the precept in Exod. XII. 19. He added 'old', just as he said elsewhere 'the old man' in Rom. VI. 6. What is here Ἐκκαθάρατε, that in the LXX version in Exodus is ἀφανεῖτε.

That you may be a new lump. עריסה or שאר. See what is said in Rom. IX. 21. Ignatius to the Magnesians: 'Put away therefore the evil leaven which has become old and sour, and be changed into a new leaven of grace.' Justin in his dialogue with Trypho: 'Wherefore also after the seven days of eating unleavened bread, God commanded to leaven a new lump for yourselves; this is the practice of other works, and not the imitation of the old and base ones.'

As you are unleavened. מצות, which is in Exod. XII. 8. is elsewhere translated as unleavened, whence also those days of the Passover are called unleavened bread or unleavened days by Josephus, as also in Matt. XXVI. 17. Mark XIV. 1, 12. Luke XXII. 1, 7. Acts XII. 4. XX. 6. Hence the men themselves are called unleavened, who abstain from leaven, just as they are called without food, without wine. Mystically in this place they are so called, who guard themselves from all those things by which morals are accustomed to be corrupted. You are, that is, you ought to be according to your profession. See Rom. VI. 2.

The mystical sense of the ceremonial precept of Ex. XII. 9. is not explained, but an illustration and admonition is made through a fitting similarity from the ancient Passover. Just as in that nothing of leaven ought to be tolerated, and even all the corners of the house had to be searched so that no leaven would be left behind; so much more in the house of the Lord, which is the Church of God, even those leavens of vices must be purged out, while now we are to celebrate the perpetual Passover, and the solemnity of the true paschal lamb, which was foreshadowed by those lambs in the Old Testament, is for us not annual, but constant and daily. An argument can be drawn from a figure and type, and concluded to the antitype, or at least a similarity of a convenient thing can be employed for the sake of illustration. Yet for that reason a double sense of the same precept does not arise, one literal, the other mystical. For it is one thing for the voice or the same sentence in one and the same place to have a double sense, one literal, the other mystical; it is another, while one and the same literal sense remains, which only sounds concerning the type, because in the type or some deed, and in that, as it was expressly a precept, something hidden had been foreshadowed, in the deed itself, I say, not in the preceptive words, which speak solely of the type, for that to be found also by a certain reason in the antitype, because of the mutual agreement and similarity of both, not because of a double sense of the same words, and ambiguity. Nor are they called unleavened, both those who abstain from leaven, and those who guard themselves from all those things by which morals are accustomed to be corrupted. But there is a single sense of the word in the precept of unleavened bread, which is by no means called so because it abstained from leaven, but because there was no leaven in it. This is applied in the application of the similarity or in the antitype in such a way, that those who wish to be considered truly Christian and faithful must also be unleavened, and without leaven of both corrupt doctrine and wicked life. Which is not only when one abstains, and

one guards against such leaven; but when it is not tolerated and is purged out with every effort. Concerning the rite of the purging of leaven, and unleavened bread in the O. T. See Ex. XII. 10, 16 to 20. Ch. XIII. 6, 7. Lev. XXIII. 6. Deut. XVI. 3, 4. by which it was signified that the feast of the Passover was to be celebrated with all leaven removed through true repentance. That the Interpreters do not wrongly apply that which specifically concerns the horrendous scandal arising from the crime of incest to be exterminated from the Church of the Corinthians, since that is primarily inculcated in the general precept: There is no doubt, however, that it is now commanded in general that all the old leaven be eliminated, because of the added final cause, that you may be a new lump; since there is no new lump in which any leaven remains; nor should the Corinthians have been merely freed from that scandal, but they ought to have been immune from any leaven whatsoever, whether of doctrine or of vices, and to that end, as far as in them lies, to purge out all the old leaven, that they may be a new lump.

Furthermore, the old leaven is called both the evil congenital in itself, and by reason of redundant sins, which, derived from the transgression of the first man and from the first origin of our nature, always sprouts forth and diffuses itself in us, and like leaven ferments and corrupts us, unless it is continuously purged and its powers are taken away by repentance and the mortification of the flesh Gen. VIII. 21. Rom. VII. 14. Chap. VI, 12. 13. Col. III. 5. seqq. Heb. XII. 1. Just as leaven penetrates the whole mass and converts it into an acid taste, and thus corrupts it: So also do false doctrine and vices and public scandals.

A new lump is called that by which we are renewed in true wisdom, justice, and holiness to the image of GOD, to which we were first created Col. 3, 9. Eph. 4, 24.

AS YOU ARE UNLEAVENED: Which is to be understood of right, as it is said among the Hebrews that something is or is done which ought to be done, and is to be accepted of the reborn, who are ἄζυμοι, and pure from the old leaven partly by reason of justification, because, purified by the blood of Christ, they have obtained the remission of sins, and by the imputed most pure innocence of Christ are constituted just before God Rom. III. 25. 28. C. IV. 5. c. V. 9. 19. 1. John I. 7. partly by reason of sanctification, because by the power of the Holy Spirit the evil motions of the old concupiscence having been repressed, they are renewed, the powers of the old leaven having been restrained, having become a new mass, the old man has been mortified, the new has emerged, so that they may be a new creature in Christ Gal. VI. 16. But because that renewal is done only in part and not in full, and the remnants of the flesh still fight against the firstfruits of the Spirit which we receive, there is need for a continuous purging of the old leaven and mortification of the flesh, and thus we are to be renewed more from day to day, so that the old and exterior man may be corrupted, but the new and interior man may receive strength, until we aspire to the perfect renewal, which is to be expected only in the other life. Whence rightly the Blessed Selneccerus in this place: We are unleavened not yet by consummation, but by imputation through and because of the Son and by the beginning through the Holy Spirit. For we always have something in us which must be purged by us at every moment through faith in the use of the sacraments, in prayers, in patience, humility, and other fruits of faith.

Καὶ γὰρ τὸ πάσχα ἡμῶν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἐτύθη χρισὸς.

He continues the allegory he began. Just as the Israelites were freed from destruction by the blood of the paschal lamb smeared on the doorposts: So also Christians are freed from the common destruction of the human race by the blood of Christ sprinkled on their hearts, that is, by faith conceived from the passion of Christ. That lamb had to be without blemish: And Christ was without blemish. Add what we said on Luke XXII. 16. Christ therefore is the mystical passover, that is, the paschal lamb: Because Josephus calls the passover a sacrifice.

Thus θύσατε τὸ πάσχα [sacrifice the passover] Exod. XII. 21. Deut. XVI. 2. 5. 6. ἐσφαξαν τὸ πάσχα [they slaughtered the passover] Ef. VI. 20. 2. Paral. XXX. 15. 17. XXXV. 1. 6. 11. The word ἡμῶν [our] shows that Paul is speaking of the mystical, not the Jewish passover.

These things are not ill said. Passover is understood not as the passing over, which the name implies; nor as the feast celebrated in memory of the liberation and the passing over of the Angel Exod. XII. 13. but as the paschal lamb, not indeed that typical one of the Old Testament: but the antitype of the same, because it is added our passover. Therefore the trope of the Sacramentarians has no foundation here, just as Pareus wishes the thing signified to be predicated of the sign, because the paschal lamb was a sign of Christ, but passover is understood metaphorically of the paschal lamb of the N. T. foreshadowed by the paschal lambs of the O. T. which is so called because of the similarity with them; and that partly by reason of the immolation, because he was sacrificed for us, by which word the slaughter, the shedding of blood, and the offering made in our place is inferred, as we showed in Socinismo profligato; partly by reason of the eating, because as the paschal lamb in the O. T. had to be eaten roasted, and indeed without leavened bread in the unleavened cakes. So Christ, by the fire of divine wrath, when he was offered for our sins, as if roasted, is proposed to us to be eaten in the Word and Sacraments, so that we may continually celebrate the feast of the passover in the enjoyment and memory of our liberation made through the shedding of his blood, which the Apostle is now about to warn us must not be done in the old leaven: Partly by reason of the sprinkling of the blood of Christ, with which the doorposts of our hearts must be smeared, so that by that sprinkling through faith we may be made in the very act participants of the redemption made by the blood of Christ shed for us, from the power of Satan and death.

Latin:

V. 7. Ἐκκαθάρατε ὖν τὴν παλαιὰν ζύμην. Omnia per quæ corrumpi potest Ecclesia. Sensus, ut dixi, mysticus præcepti Exod. XII. 19. Vetus addidit, sicut alibi dixit veterem hominem Rom. VI. 6. Quod hic est ἐκκαθάρατε, id in versione LXX. in Exodo est ἀφανεῖτε.

Ἵνα ἦτε νέον φύραμα. עריסה vel שאר. Vide dicta Rom. IX. 21. Ignatius ad Magnesios: ὑπέρθεσθε ὖν τὴν κακὴν ζύμην τὴν παλαιω- θεῖσαν, τὴν σεσηπῦαν, καὶ μεταβάλλεσθε εἰς νέαν ζύμην χάρι- τος. Justinus colloquio cum Tryphone: Διὸ καὶ μετὰ τὰς ἑπτα ἡμέρας τῶν ἀζυμοφαγιῶν, νέαν ζύμην φυρᾶσαι ἑαυτοῖς ὁ Θεὸς παρήγγειλε; τῦτό ἐστιν ἄλλων ἔργων πρᾶξιν, καὶ μὴ τῶν παλαιῶν καὶ φαύλων τὴν μίμησιν.

Καθώς ἐσε ἄζυμοι. מצות, quod est Exod. XII. 8. alibi vertitur ἄζυμοι, unde & dies illi Paschatis ἄζυμα aut ἄζυμοι ἡμέραι Josepho, ut & Matth. XXVI. 17. Marc. XIV. 1. 12. Luc. XXII. 1, 7. Act. XII. 4. XX. 6. Hinc homines ipsi ἄζυμοι, qui fermento abstinent, quomodo dicuntur ἄσιτοι, ἄοινοι. Mystice hoc loco sic vocantur, qui sibi cavent ab omnibus iis, per quæ corrumpi mores solent. Estis, id est, esse debetis secundum vestram professionem. Vide Rom. VI. 2.

Non exponitur sensus mysticus præcepti cere- monialis Ex. XII. 9. sed illustratio, & commoni- tio fit per similitudinem concinnam à paschate ve- teri. Sicut in illo nihil fermenti tolerari debuit, omnes etiam anguli domus pervestigandi erant, ut nihil fermenti relinqueretur; ita magis in domo Domini, quæ est Ecclesia Dei, etiam illa fermen- ta vitiorum expurganda sunt, dum jam celebran- dum sit nobis pascha perpetuum, & solemnitas agni veri paschalis, per agnos illos in veteri Testa- mento adumbrati, nobis non sit anniversaria, sed jugis & quotidiana. A figura & typo argumentum peti potest, & concludi ad antitypum, vel certe illustrationis causa adhiberi similitudo rei conve- niens. Non tamen idcirco sensus ejusdem præcepti geminus exurgit, alius literalis, alius mysticus. Aliud enim est vocis, vel sententiæ ejusdem in uno eo- demque loco geminum esse sensum, alium litera- lem, alium mysticum; aliud, manente uno & eodem sensu literali, qui tantum de typo sonat, quia in typo vel facto aliquo, illo que, uti ῥητῶς præceptum id erat, aliquid occulti adumbratum fuerat, in facto ipso, inquam, non in verbis præ- ceptivis, de typo unice loquentibus, id reperiri etiam certa ratione in antitypo, ob utriusque mu- tuam convenientiam & similitudinem, non ob ver- borum eorundem sensum geminum, & ἀμφιλο- γίαν. Nec ἄζυμοι dicuntur, tum qui fermento abs- tinent, tum qui sibi cavent ab omnibus iis, per quæ corrumpi mores solent. Sed unicus est vocis sensus in præcepto panis azymi, qui minime ita dicitur, quod fermento abstinuerit, sed quod nihil fermenti in eo fuerit. Hoc ἀποδόσει similitudinis vel in antitypo ita adhibetur, quod debeant etiam ἄζυ- μοι esse, & sine fermento cum pravæ doctrinæ, tum sceleratæ, qui vere Christiani & fideles censeri volunt. Quod non sit tantum, cum abstinetur, &

cavetur à tali fermento; sed cum non toleratur omnique studio expurgatur. De ritu expurgationis fermenti, & panum azymorum in V. T. Vid. Ex. XII. 10. 16. ad 20. C. XIII. 6. 7. Lev. XXIII. 6. Deut. XVI. 3. 4. quo significabatur, festum paschatos, remoto per veram pœnitentiam omni fermento, celebrandum esse. Quod speciatim quidem ad horrendum illud enatum ex flagitio incesti offendiculum ex Ecclesia Corinthiorum exterminandum non male applicant Interpretes, quippe in generali præcepto illud imprimis inculcatum: No dubium tamen, jam in universum omne vetus fermentum eliminandum præcipi, ob additam causam finalem, ut sitis nova conspersio; quum nova conspersio non sit, in qua aliquid fermenti reliquum est; nec Corinthii tantum ab illo scandalo liberati, sed immunes esse debuerint à quovis sive doctrinæ, sive vitiorum fermento, eoque fine quantum in ipsis est, omne fermentum vetus expurgare, ut sint nova conspersio.

Porro Vetus fermentum dicitur tum malum congenitum per se, tum ratione redundantium peccatorum, quod inde à primi hominis prævaricatione, & à prima naturæ nostræ origine derivatum semper propullulat, & diffundit sese in nobis, & instar fermenti nos fermentat, & corrumpit, nisi continuo expurgetur, viresque ipsi per pœnitentiam & carnis mortificationem adimantur Gen. IIX. 21. Rom. VII. 14. Cap. VI, 12. 13. Col. III. 5. seqq. Ebr. XII. 1. Quemadmodum fermentum totam massam penetrat, & in acidum saporem convertit, adeoque corrumpit: Ita & falsa doctrina & vitia & scandala publica.

Nova conspersio dicitur, quâ in vera sapientia, justitia, & sanctitate ad imaginem DEI, ad quam primum conditi eramus, renovamur Col. 3, 9. Eph. 4, 24.

SICUT ESTIS INFERMENTATI: Quod de jure intelligendum, ut Hebræis fieri vel esse dicitur quod fieri deberet, & de renatis accipiendum, qui ἄζυμοι sunt, & puri à fermento veteri partim ratione justificationis, quia sanguine Christi purificati remissionem peccatorum consecuti, & imputatâ Christi innocentia purissima justi coram Deo constituti Rom. III. 25. 28. C. IV. 5. c. V. 9. 19. 1. Joh. I. 7. partim ratione sanctificationis, quia virtute Sp. S. malis concupiscentiæ veteris motibus repressis renovati, fermenti veteris viribus coërcitis, nova massa facti, homo vetus mortificatus est, novus emersit, ut nova creatura sint in Christo Gal. VI. 16. Quia vero renovatio illa ex parte tantum non ex asse facta, & cum primitiis Spiritus, quas accipimus, pugnant adhuc reliquiæ carnis, continua expurgatione veteris fermenti, & mortificatione carnis opus est, adeoque de die in diem magis renovandi sumus, ut vetus & exterior homo corrumpatur, novus vero & interior homo vires accipiat, donec ad perfectam renovationem adspiremus, quæ in altera demum vita expectanda est. Unde recte B. Selneccerus in h. l. Azymi sumus non-dum consummatione, sed imputatione per & propter Filium & inchoatione per Spiritum S. Semper enim habemus aliquid in nobis, quod singulis momentis nobis expurgandum est per fidem in usu sacramentorum, in orationibus, in patientia, humilitate, & aliis fructibus fidei.

Καὶ γὰρ τὸ πάσχα ἡμῶν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἐτύθη χρισὸς.

Prosequitur cœptam ἀλληγορίαν. Sicut sanguine agni paschalis, allito postibus, liberati sunt Israëlitz ab excidio: Ita & Christiani per sanguinem Christi aspersum cordibus, id est, per fidem ex passione Christi conceptam, liberantur à communi exitio humani generis. Agnus ille sine vitio esse debuit: Et Christus sine vitio fuit. Adde quæ diximus ad Luc. XXII. 16. Christus ergo mysticum pascha, id est, agnus paschalis: Quòd pascha θυσίαν vocat Josephus.

Sic θύσατε τὸ πάσχα Exod. XII. 21. Deut. XVI. 2. 5. 6. ἐσφα- ξαν τὸ πάσχα Ef. VI. 20. 2. Paral. XXX. 15. 17. XXXV. 1. 6. 11. Vox ἡμῶν oftendit Paulum de mystico, non de Judaico pa- schate loqui.

Non male hæc dicuntur. Pascha intelligitur non de transitu, quem nomen importat; nec de festo in memoriam liberationis & transitus Angeli ce- lebrato Exod. XII. 13. sed agnus paschalis, non ille quidem Veteris Testamenti typicus: sed antitypus ejusdem, quia additur pascha nostrum. Non ergo fundamentum hic habet tropus Sacra- mentariorum, quemadmodum Pareus signatum de signo prædicari vult, quia agnus paschalis fuit signum Christi, sed pascha intelligitur Metaphorice de agno paschali N. T. adumbrato per agnos pascha- les V. T. qui ob similitudinem cum illis sic voca- tur; idque partim ratione immolationis, quia pro nobis ἐθύθη, quo vocabulo mactatio, sanguinis effu- sio atque oblatio nostri loco facta infertur, ut in So- cinismo profligato ostendimus; partim ratione man- ducationis, quia ut aslatus manducandus erat, & quidem sine pane fermentato in azymis agnus paschalis in V. T. Ita Christus igne iræ divinæ, cum offerretur pro peccatis nostris, velut aslatus, no- bis manducandus in Verbo & Sacramentis pro- ponitur, ut festum paschatos in fruitionem & memoriam liberationis nostræ per effusionem sanguinis sui factæ jugiter celebremus, quod ut non in fermento veteri fiat jamjam moniturus est Apostolus: Partim ratione aspersionis sanguinis Christi, quo cordis nostri postes illinendi sunt, ut ea aspersione per fidem nos actu ipso participes reddamur redemptionis sanguine Christi pro no- bis effuso, à potestate satanæ & mortis factæ.

## 5:8
V. 8. Ὢste ἑορτάζωμεν [Therefore let us keep the feast].

Ἐορτάζειν [To keep a feast] חגג in the law of Moses is to abstain from every work, so that things may be made sacred to God. In the mystical sense, to serve God so perpetually that all works are sacrifices Is. LXVI. 23. Philo: a feast of the soul, the perfect joy in virtues. Thucydides saw something of this matter, when he says: a feast is nothing else than doing what is necessary.

Μὴ ἐν ζύμῃ παλαιᾷ [Not with old leaven].

ביצר הרע [in the evil inclination] in evil desires.

Μηδὲ ἐν ζύμῃ κακίας κὰι πονηρίας [Nor with the leaven of malice and wickedness].

Much less in wicked and crafty actions; such as was that of the one defending incest through philosophical arguments.

Ἀλλ’ ἐν ἀζύμοις [But with unleavened bread].

It is understood, breads. But by breads are mystically to be understood actions, as those by which the mind is fed.

Of sincerity and truth.

The former is opposed to malice, the latter to wickedness. Sincerity is the flight from impurity, truth from simulation, Jerome against Pelagius in his dialogue, book 1. The Passover is celebrated with bitterness, the Passover of sincerity, of truth.

Therefore, a perpetual Passover is commanded to Christians through abstinence from the works of diabolical servitude, or sins, and the offering of spiritual sacrifices of praise, prayers, etc., so that through faith we may present the one propitiatory sacrifice to God, and consecrate and offer ourselves entirely to God as a holy, living, and pleasing sacrifice. Ps. 51:19, Ps. 110:3, and 141:2, Is. 58:13, Rom. 12:1, Heb. 13:15, 16, Rev. 5:8, ch. 18:4. For just as we have that true Passover in our midst perpetually, Matt. 18:10, ch. 28:20, so it behooves us also to keep holiday perpetually and solemnly, and to celebrate the paschal festival continuously in a spiritual manner, not in the old leaven of depraved concupiscence of sin innate to us, which is to be restrained, and as far as possible, purged out through the mortification of the flesh and the putting off of the old man: Nor in the leaven of malice of actual sins, of wickedness, which exerts itself most in the propagation of false doctrine. Rom. 16:18, Eph. 4:14, 2 Pet. 3:16. But in unleavened actions and the pursuit of sincerity and truth, of integrity, or purity of life, and of the truth of divine doctrine. The Hunnian paraphrase is correct here: Just as the Jews of old could not and ought not to celebrate their Levitical Passover while using leavened bread for consumption and eating; so, since we in our sacred rites do not deal with a type or shadow, but with the truth and substance of the New Testament once foreshadowed through the figure of the Mosaic law, namely Christ, that Lamb of God who takes away the sins of the world: It is altogether fitting that, from the correspondence of type and antitype, we too should decently celebrate the Passover of the New Testament by enjoying through faith the benefits of His passion and death. But with this festival, there is no commerce with that old leaven of malice and wickedness; rather, the solemnity of our Passover is to be celebrated in bread lacking leaven, that is, in sincerity and truth, namely, in the simplicity of uncorrupted doctrine and the chastity and purity of a new life: cf. Phil. 1:10, 11. Joh. I. 4. that sincerity may produce a clean life, and truth may exclude all deceit, as Ambrose says. Theophylact does not reject our interpretation, along with Chrysostom, whom he followed: He argues from these that every time is a feast and is celebrated by Christians on account of the magnitude of the good things which have been granted to them freely. For this reason (he says) the Son of GOD was sacrificed, that He might make you spend joyful and festive days, not in the old leaven of Adam, nor in a life (which is far worse) full of wickedness. For he is indeed called evil who performs evil deeds, but he is called wicked who, with an iniquitous mind and a certain depth of malice, carries out what is evil: But in the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth, that is, in a life that is purer and upright, in contrast to wickedness, and of truth, that is, true, not feigned, and without guile, which, in order to distinguish it, he also called malice. Or you may, with 'truth,' he says, refer the old types to be separated from this truth, which offered nothing of themselves; or you may understand by 'sincerity' purity itself, which consists in work and actions, and 'truth' as contemplation. These are the words of Theophylact. Heshusius has this to say on this passage: To celebrate a feast day is, through allegory, to illuminate the glory of God with holy works, faith, patience, liberality toward the poor, invocation, thanksgiving, and every kind of virtue. The old leaven signifies the old depravity of the flesh, which is prone to every kind of vice, just as Paul himself explains: The leaven of malice and wickedness: By which words he signifies first all kinds of impious opinions and impure desires, luxury, lusts, avarice, emulation: Then also the frauds, deceits, and impostures by which both false dogmas and wicked morals are cunningly covered. He wishes these carnal vices to be purged and avoided: And God to be worshipped in sincerity and truth: This is in the confession of sound and uncorrupted doctrine, and a holy life devoid of all hypocrisy and fraud. Clement of Alexandria, book 8 of the Stromata: The entire life of a just man, he says, is a certain celebrated and holy feast day. The Vulgate rendered the word 'let us keep the feast' more narrowly as 'let us feast': Yet the chief thing in the feast of the Passover was the eating of the paschal lamb, which is also primarily required in our Passover mystically. For this Lamb, sacrificed for us, offers Himself to be eaten by us, partly spiritually through faith, in that continuous and perpetual festival of the New Testament, and partly sacramentally, in the Eucharist to confirm faith in us and to seal the certainty of eternal salvation. The feast of the Passover of the Old Testament lasted for seven whole days, during which it was not permitted to use any leaven. By which we are admonished never to return to that old leaven, or to use or enjoy it. For the number seven is the number of perfection, and just as we measure all time by the number and course of the week, so the whole of our life ought to be a week of the new passover and of unleavened bread, until from month to month, from sabbath to sabbath, all flesh (of the elect) shall come, to bow down before the Lord Isa. LXVI. 23.

But it is rashly proven from this that the Sacrament must be celebrated with unleavened bread: because it is a question of unleavened bread in this place not taken properly, that is, unfermented loaves, but in a metaphorical sense, namely of the Christian life, which ought to be free from the leaven of false doctrine and wicked impiety: and thus physical leaven is not excluded, but moral; not of bread, but of pursuits and actions; not from the bread, but from the heart, and life or conversation. But unleavened or fermented bread is indifferent in the use of the Eucharist.

PART III. On avoiding communion with the wicked.

Latin:

V. 8. Ὢste ἑορτάζωμεν.

Ἐορτάζειν חגג in lege Mosis est abstinere ab omni opere, ut Deo sacra fiant. In mystico sensu ita perpetuo Deo servire, ut omnia opera sint sacrificia Es. LXVI. 23. Philo: ἑορτὴ ψυχῆς, ἡ ἐν ἀρεταῖς εὐφροσύνη τελεία. Vidit aliquid hujus rei Thucydides, cum dicit: ἑορτὴ ὀδὲν ἄλλο ἐσὶν, ἢ τὸ τὰ δέοντα πράττειν.

Μὴ ἐν ζύμῃ παλαιᾷ.

ביצר הרע in malis cupiditatibus.

Μηδὲ ἐν ζύμῃ κακίας κὰι πονηρίας.

Multo minus in actionibus improbis atque versutis; qualis erat illa incestum per philosophicas rationes defen- dentis.

Ἀλλ’ ἐν ἀζύμοις.

Subauditur, panibus. Per panes autem mystice intelli- gendæ actiones, ut quibus pascatur animus.

Εἰλικρινείας κὰι ἀληθείας.

Prius illud opponitur κακίᾳ, alterum πονηρίᾳ. Εἰλικρί- νεια est fuga impuritatis, ἀλήθεια simulationis, Hierony- mus contra Pelagium dialogo l. Pascha cum amaritudinibus editur, pascha sinceritatis, veritatis.

Pascha itaque perpetuum Christianis imperatur qua abstinentiam ab operibus servitutis diabolicæ, vel peccatis, & oblationem sacrificiorum spiritua- lium laudis, precum, &c. ut per fidem unicum sacrificium propitiatorium Deo sistamus, nosque totos Deo in hostiam sanctam vivam & Deo pla- centem consecremus & offeramus Ps. LI. 19. Ps. CX. 3. & CXLI. 2. Es. LIIX. 13. Rom. XII. 1. Ebr. XIII. 15. 16. Ap. V. 8. Cap. IIX. 4. Ut enim ha- bemus pascha illud verum in medio nostri perpe- tuo Matth. XIIX. 10. cap. XXIIX. 20. ita feriari etiam perpetuo solenniter nos oportet, & jugiter celebrare modo spirituali paschalem festivitatem, non in fermento veteri pravæ concupiscentiæ pec- cati nobis agnati, quod est compescendum, & quoad fieri potest, expurgandum, per carnis mor- tificationem, & veteris hominis depositionem: Nec in fermento κακίας malitiæ peccatorum actualium, πονηρίας versutiæ, quæ in falsa doctrinæ propagatio- ne sese maxime exerit. Rom. XVI. 18. Eph. IV. 14. 2. Petr. III. 16. Sed in ἀζύμοις actionibus & stu- dio εἰλικρινείας κὰι ἀληθείας integritatis, vel puritatis vitæ, & veritatis doctrinæ divinæ. Recte hîse ha- bet paraphrasis Hunniana: Quemadmodum olim Judæi suum pascha Leviticum celebrare non pote- rant nec debebant, adhibitis in usum & esum fer- mentatis panibus; Sic quoniam nos in nostris sacris non typum tractamus aut umbram, sed veritatem & substantiam N. T. per figuram Mosaicæ legis olim adumbratam, videlicet Christum, agnum illum DEI, tollentem peccata mundi: Omnino convenit, ut ex typi & antitypi convenientia nos quoque Novi Test. pascha decenter celebremus, fide perfruendo bene- ficiis passionis & mortis ipsius. Cum hac autem fe- stivitate nihil commercii est veteri illi fermento ma- litia & versutia; sed nostri paschatis solennitas ce- lebranda est in panibus fermento carentibus, hoc est, in sinceritate & veritate, nimirum incorruptæ doctrinæ simplicitate, & novæ vitæ castimonia ac puritate: conf. Phil. I. 10. 11. 2. Joh. I. 4. ut since- ritas mundam vitam faciat, & veritas omnem fraudem excludat, dicente Ambrosio. Non abnuit nostræ interpretationi Theophyl. cum Chrysostomo, quem sequutus est: Arguit ex his omne tempus fe- stum esse & celebre Christianis propter bonorum ma- gnitudinem, quæ illis gratis sunt concessa. Propter- ea (inquit) immolatus est DEI Filius, ut te lætos & celebres dies agere faciat, non in antiquo Adæ fer- mento, neque in vita (quod longe deterius est) ne- quitiæ plena. Nam malus is utique dicitur, qui mala exequitur, nequam vero, qui mente iniqua, & malitiæ quadam profunditate, quæ mala sunt, pera- git: Sed in azymis sinceritatis, & veritatis, hoc est, in vita puriori & integra, ad nequitiæ differentiam, & veritatis, id est vera, non simulata, & sine dolo, quod ut secernat, & malitiam dixit. Vel poteris cum veritatis inquit, & veteres typos à veritate hac segregandos referre, qui nihil præ se ferebant; vel pro sinceritate puritatem ipsam intelliges, qua opere con- stat & actionibus: & contemplationem pro veritate. Hæc Theophylactus. Heshusius ita habet in hunc locum: Festum diem celebrare est per allegoriam sanctis operibus, fide, patientia, liberalitate in pau- peres, invocatione, gratiarum actione, & omni vir- tutum genere illustrare DEI gloriam. Fermentum vetustum significat veterem pravitatem carnis, quæ ad omnis generis vitia est proclivis, sicuti ipse Paulus exponit: Fermentum malitiæ & nequitiæ: Qui- bus vocabulis primum omnis generis impias opinio- nes, & impuras cupiditates, luxuriam, libidines, avaritiam, æmulationem: Deinde & fraudes, dolos & imposturas, quibus & falsa dogmata & scelerati mores callide teguntur, significat. Hæc vitia car- nalia vult expurgari & vitari: Et Deum coli in sinceritate & veritate: Hoc est sanæ & incorruptæ doctrinæ confessione, & sancta & omnis hypocriseos & fraudum experte vita. Clemens Alexandrinus l. VIII. Stromatum: Universa, inquit, vita viri justi est quidam celebris & sanctus dies festus. Vul- gata angustius verbum ἑορτάζωμεν reddidit epule- mur: Præcipuum tamen id in Paschatos festo erat, comestio agni paschalis, quæ etiam imprimis in paschate nostro requiritur mystice. Hic enim agnus pro nobis mactatus manducandum sese præbet nobis, partim spiritualiter per fidem, in illa continua perpetuaque N.T. festivitate, partim vero sacramentaliter, in Eucharistia ad confirman- dam in nobis fidem, & sanciendam certitudinem æternæ salutis. Paschatos festum V. T. durabat in dies septem integros, in quibus non licebat ullo uti fermento. Quo admonemur, ne unquam ad fermentum illud vetus redeamus, vel eo ἐχρσίως utamur, fruamur. Est enim septenarius per- fectionis numerus, & ut tempus omne hebdo- madum numero & decursu metimur, ita tota nostra vita hebdomas paschatis novi & azymorum esse debet, donec de mense in mensem, de sabbato in sabbatum veniet omnis (electorum) caro, ut incurvet, se coram Domino Ef. LXVI. 23.

Temere autem hinc probatur, azymis celebrandum esse Sacramentum: quia de azymis agitur hoc loco non proprie dictis, hoc est, panibus infermentatis, seu sensu metaphorico, vitæ sc. Christianæ, quæ fermento falsæ doctrinæ & impietatis sceleratæ carere debet: Adeoque non excluditur fermentum physicum, sed morale, non panis, sed studiorum & actionum; non ex pane, sed ex corde, & vita vel conversatione. Indifferens vero est panis azymus, vel fermentatus in usu Eucharistiæ.

PARS III. De vitanda cum flagitiosis communione.

## 5:9
V. 9. I wrote to you in the epistle.

In some epistle written heretofore, which has perished, as many have. We owe thanks to GOD that so many have been preserved, to which if both the life of individuals and the government of the Church are directed, it will be well.

Not a few understand the present Epistle here; such as Chrysostom, Theophylact, and others, in which this Apostle had spoken about excommunicating the incestuous man. Some wish the second to the Thessalonians to be designated, which he wished to be read to all the holy brethren in all the Churches, just as he wished the first 1 Thess. V. 27., inasmuch as in it he had warned that they should withdraw themselves from every brother walking disorderly, 2 Thess. III. 6. However, not only Calvin, Beza, Maldonatus, Pareus, Drusius, and other Reformed take these words to refer to another prior epistle to the Corinthians, written before this one was prescribed, which no longer survives: Estius also among the Papists, but among our own as well, with Ambrose leading the way, Mylius, Aegidius Hunnius, Rungius, Gesnerus, Balduinus, Lucas Osiander, Hesbusius. Which opinion we have embraced in our S. Critic. But with the distinction applied on account of the Papists, who contend that canonical books have perished, between a particular and a universal Canon; a temporal and a perpetual one, that by divine providence He willed this epistle, of which the Apostle speaks at present, which is first in order, to serve only a certain and particular Church of that time; nor did He ordain it for the perpetual canonical use of the whole Church, as the remaining canonical ones, whence He also allowed the same to perish: In what way, however, nothing was lost to the integrity of the canon of scripture ordained for the use of the universal Church; Nor can it be considered imperfect with the Papists, because its perfection is to be estimated not from the numerical quantity of books, but from the quality and sufficiency of the doctrines and the end of the scripture. Nor can it be taught that anything else, as far as the substance of religion is concerned, was contained in that lost epistle which is not had in the remaining canonical scriptures which still survive, which the Papists have only in the treasures of traditions, since even the Papists themselves find it necessary to confess that those things which survive written by the Prophets and Apostles contain all things necessary to be known for salvation, as we have taught in our System. Theol. Nor does the otherwise Papizing Grotius deny this.

Not to keep company with fornicators.

He understands 'fornicators' here, not indeed catamites, as some wish; but those who use harlots, which both the preceding things show and those which follow VI. 10. 15. and the places Sir. XXIII. 21. 22. 'to keep company' here and 2 Thess. I. 4. 'to associate' John IV. 9. 'to have dealings' Acts X. 28.

Latin:

V. 9. Ἔγραψα ὑμῖν ἐν τῇ ἐπιστολῇ.

In aliqua epistola antehac scripta, quæ intercidit, ut multæ. Satis DEO debemus, quod tot servatæ sunt, ad quas si & singulorum vita & regimen Ecclesiæ dirigatur, bene erit.

Intelligunt non pauci hic Epistolam præsentem; utpote Chrysostomus, Theophylactus, & alii, in qua de excommunicando incestuoso dixerat hic Apostolus. Nonnulli posteriorem ad Thessalonicenses, quam omnibus sanctis fratribus in Ecclesiis omnibus legi, ceu priorem voluerit 1. Thess. V. 27. designari volunt, utpote in qua monuerat, ut subtraherent se ab omni fratre ambulante inordinate, 2. Thess. III. 6. De alia tamen priori ad Corinthios, antequam hæc præscripta esset, exarata, quæ non amplius supersit, hæc accipiunt non solùm Calvinus, Beza, Maldonatus, Pareus, Drusius, aliique Reformati: Estius item è Pontificiis, sed è nostris quoque, præeunte Ambrosio, Mylius, Ægidius Hunnius, Rungius, Gesnerus, Balduinus, Lucas Osiander, Hesbusius. Quam sententiam amplexi sumus in Critico S. Sed adhibità ob Pontificios, qui libros canonicos interiisse contendunt, distinctione inter Canonem particularem & universalem; temporalem & perpetuum, quod divinâ providentiâ hanc, de qua in præsenti loquitur Apostolus, in ordine primam epistolam, inservire tantùm voluerit certæ, & particulari Ecclesiæ istius temporis; nec ad usum Canonicum perpetuum totius Ecclesiæ ordinârit ut reliquas Canonicas, unde etiam interire eandem passa fuit: Quo verò pacto nihil decessit integritati canonis scripturæ ad usum Ecclesiæ universalis ordinati; Neque imperfectus ille cum Pontificiis haberi potest, quia perfectio ejus non è quantitate numerica librorum, sed qualitate & sufficientia dogmatum & fine scripturæ æstimanda est. Neque aliud quid, quantum ad substantiam religionis, in deperdita illa epistola contentum fuisse, quod non habeatur in reliquis, quæ adhuc supersunt, Canonicis scripturis, quod in thesauris traditionum solùm habeant Papistæ; doceri potest, quum ea quæ scripta supersunt à Prophetis, & Apostolis omnia scitu necessaria ad salutem continere vel ipsimet Pontificii fateri necesse habent, ut in System. Theol. docuimus. Neque id diffitetur cæteroquin Papizans Grotius.

Μὴ συναναμίγνυσθαι πόρνοις.

Πόρνους hic intelligit, non sane catamitos, ut quidam volunt; sed scortis utentes, quod & præcedentia ostendunt & quæ sequuntur VI. 10. 15. & loca Sir. XXIII. 21. 22. συναναμίγνυσθαι hic & 2. Thess. I. 4. συγχρῆσθαι Joh. IV. 9. Κοινωθεῖν Act. X. 28.

## 5:10
V. 10. And not altogether with the fornicators of this world then.

I did not write that concerning non-Christians. That καὶ does not appear in the manuscript, and it is more correctly absent.

Why are catamites not included, such as

was called Ganymede, and afterwards were called shameless and effeminate: And why, on the authority of one manuscript, should the particle καὶ be expunged from all the others? Furthermore, the Apostle limits what he had written concerning avoiding communion with fornicators, meaning that he wishes this warning to be understood not of fornicators of this kind or outside the Church, but of those in the Church who are called Christians and believers, yet indulge in fornication. Because if all who were in the world, among the Gentiles, who hardly considered fornication a crime and a disgrace, were to be avoided, one would have to go out of the world. Although fornication was indeed very frequent among Christians, so much so that the first Council of Jerusalem considered nothing more necessary to warn about among moral matters than that πορνείαν (fornication) must be fled, Acts XV. However, because they at least avoid public scandals more, and strive for external honesty, even if often with hypocrisy; he warns not of those fornicators who were in the world, as they were too frequent; but he warns that Christians are to be avoided, and he extends his warning further to similar vices, namely that they should not communicate with those who are whitewashed by the Christian name while being addicted to the same, but should flee and avoid their community: such as the covetous, extortioners, idolaters, revilers, and other criminals of this sort; all of whom, even those who were outside the Church among the Corinthians, it was impossible to avoid, because the whole city swarmed with such people.

H ͂ς to the covetous.

He adds other kinds of vices. Πλεονέκται are those who defraud another in contracts and promises. To do this is πλεονεκτεῖν, בצע to the Hebrews, whence also the name בצע, πλεονεξία, and πλεονέκτημα.

Πλεονεκτικὸς is called a defrauder and a deceiver by Aristotle, as Budaeus says. Πλεονεκτεῖν also signifies to be defrauded, 2 Cor. VII. 2, Chap. XII. 18. Moreover, πλεονέκτης is the same as πλεονεκτικός.

H ἅρπαξιν (to the extortioners).

ἁρπαγὴ is more than πλεονεξία. For ἁρπαγὴ has force joined to it, as raptus and rapina among the Latins.

A covetous person is one who secretly steals another's property through fraud; an extortioner is one who does so by open force. Thieves are similar to extortioners, because the latter steal another's property while the owner is unwilling, but not unaware; the former while the owner is both unaware and unwilling: just as the covetous do so not while the owner is unwilling, but while he is unaware and deceived.

Η to the idolaters.

Here first occurs that word. What the Hebrews call עובד עבודה, the Hellenists call εἰδωλολατρείαν, not because word corresponds to word, but because it was best understood in this way, which they intended, because the Gentiles in their public worship used idols, that is, standing images. The Jews did not use them. Hence the word remained even among Christians, not because it bound them according to the commandment of the Decalogue, but because that use of the word had prevailed in that sense.

There is no doubt that the commandment concerning not making graven images, which is to be referred to the first commandment, concerning idolatry, because it is not the making of images but the worship of them that is prohibited, as we noted at Ex. XX, binds Christians, who are likewise forbidden, as the Jews were, to make images in order to adore them. Schlichtingius here also refutes Grotius, because those who fashion Him with mortal forms sin no less against the majesty of GOD than those who bestow heavenly honors upon another than Him. But this latter is done by the Socinians themselves, when they worship Christ with divine worship, whom they believe to be truly different in nature from God.

Ἐπεὶ ὀφείλετε ἄρα ἐκ τῶ κόσμυ ἐξελθεῖν.

It would do no harm if this could be done, but this would be too burdensome. Almost all commerce of human life would cease, which is expressed ὑπερβολικῶς.

Latin:

V. 10. Καὶ ἐ πάντως τοῖς πόρνοις τῇ κόσμε τότε.

Non id scripsi dè non Christianis. Illud καὶ in Manuscripto non apparet, & abest rectius.

Cur non comprehendantur catamiti, qualis

Ganymedes vocatus est, & post impudici & effœmi- nati dicti: Et cur ob unius Manuscripti autorita- tem e cæteris omnibus expungenda particula καὶ? De cætero limitat Apostolus, quod scripserat de vitanda communione cum scortatoribus, quod non de scortatoribus hujusmodi vel extra Ecclesiam, sed in Ecclesia, qui Christiani, & fideles audiunt, scortationibus tamen indulgent, hoc moni- tum intellectum velit. Quia si omnes, qui in mundo erant, inter gentes, scortationem vix pro scelere & flagitio habentes vitandi, mundo exeundum fo- ret. Licet autem inter Christianos valde frequens etiam fuerit scortatio, adeo ut prima Synodus Hie- rosolymitana nihil magis inter moralia necessum habuerit monere, quam πορνείαν scortationem fu- giendam esse, Act. XV. Quia tamen illi publica ad minimum scandala magis cavent, ac externæ honestati, utut sæpe cum hypocrisi, student; non de iis, qui in mundo erant, scortatoribus, utpote nimis frequentibus; sed de Christianis vitandis monet, ac monitum suum porro extendit ad simi- lia vitia, ne scilicet iisdem deditis Christiano no- mine dealbatis, communicent, sed communita- tem eorum fugiant, & vitent: ut sunt, avari, rapa- ces, idololatræ, convitiatores, & furfuris hujus aliis facinorosi; Quos omnes, etiam qui extra Eccle- siam inter Corinthios erant, vitari impossibile erat, quia tota urbs talibus scatebat.

H ͂ς πλεονέκταις.

Addit alia vitiorum genera. Πλεονέκται sunt, qui in con- tractibus & promissis fraudant alterum. Id facere est πλεον- εκτεῖν בצע Hebræis, unde & nomen בצע πλεονεξία, καὶ πλεονέκτημα.

Πλεονεκτικὸς Aristoteli dicitur fraudator, & cir- cumscriptor dicente Budæo. Πλεονεκτεῖν etiam frau- dari significat 2. Cor. VII. 2. Cap. XII. 18. Est autem πλεονέκτης idem, quod πλεονεκτικός.

H ἅρπαξιν.

Plus est ἁρπαγὴ quam πλεονεξία. Nam ἁρπαγὴ vim ha bet adjunctam, ut raptus & rapina apud Latinos.

Avarus est, qui clam aliena rapit per fraudes; Rapax qui per vim apertam. Raptoribus similes sunt & fures, quia illi aliena rapiunt invito, sed non inscio Domino; isti & inscio & invito: Sicut avari non invito quidem, sed inscio & decepto.

Η εἰδωλολάτραις.

Hic primum occurrit ea vox. Quod Hebræi dicunt עובד עבודה id Hellenistæ dicunt εἰδωλολατρείαν, non quod vox voci respondeat, sed quod sic optime intelligeretur, quod vellent, quia gentes in cultu suo publico utebantur simulacris, id est imaginibus exstantibus. Judæi non ute- bantur. Hinc vox mansit etiam apud Christianos, non quod secundum decalogi præceptum eos obligaret, sed quia ille vocis usus illo sensu invaluerat.

Dubium non est, quin præceptum de non fa- ciendis sculptilibus, quod ad primum est referen- dum præceptum, idololatriam concernens, quia non imaginum factura, sed cultura prohibita est, ut ad Ex. XX. monuimus, obliget Christianos, qui pariter ut Judæi imagines facere, ut easdem adorent, prohibentur. Refutat hic etiam Gro- tium Schlichtingius, quod non minus peccent con- tra DEI majestatem, qui eum mortalibus effin- gunt formis, quam qui alium ab ipso cœlestibus afficiunt honoribus. Ast hoc posterius fit ab ipsis Socinianis, cum Christum divino cultu colunt, quem vero natura diversum à Deo credunt.

Ἐπεὶ ὀφείλετε ἄρα ἐκ τῶ κόσμυ ἐξελθεῖν.

Nihil noceret, si hoc fieri posset, sed nimis hoc grave esset. Intercideret ferme omne vitæ humanæ commercium, quod ὑπερβολικῶς exprimitur.

## 5:11
Νυνὶ δὲ ἔγραψα ὑμῖν.

Nuni here is not added for the sake of a distinction of time, as if Paul were writing something else now than he had written before, but it has the force of an adversative, in the way that νῦν is taken below in VII. 14 and XII. 20, and νυνὶ below in XII. 18 and XV. 20. Thus it is often placed in Cicero: nunc vero (but now).

Not to associate with anyone who bears the name of brother if he is a fornicator, or a reviler, or a covetous person, or an idolater, or a drunkard, or a swindler,

If any brother is named, that is, wishing to be called a Christian. See Acts 6:3. Friendship with such sinners disgraced the Church, not so with those who were outside the Church. To the names of the vicious just mentioned, he adds here with equal right λοίδορος and drunkards. Λοιδορία corresponds to the Hebrew words ריב and רבה: The former signifies strife, the latter reproach and insult. See John 9:8, Acts 23:4, above 4:12, 1 Peter 2:23. You have here, therefore, the principal causes of excommunication.
