While therefore to the Ephesians, in whom faith had been kindled through the Gospel, the light of wisdom, the heat of charity, and the brightness of holiness are conferred by that very seal impressed upon their heart as if it were wax, they are sealed, and thus then more and more are they conformed to the Spirit as the archetype and seal of holiness pressing, then they are distinguished from the flock of the Devil, then they are more confirmed concerning the certainty of the promises. Not otherwise than a letter is confirmed by a seal. For while the Gospel is written by the pen of the Holy Spirit in their hearts, they become the letter of GOD, 2 Cor. III. 3. But after they have been made the letter of GOD, they are sealed. By the former act, faith is begotten in their hearts; by the latter, it is strengthened, so that, fighting bravely against every doubt, it may rest thoroughly in the truth of GOD. Since the end of sealing is confirmation, Esth. VIII. 8, the distinguishing of the genuine from the supposititious, and the custody of the sealed, so that it may not easily be injured or taken away, Dan. VI. 17, Matt. XXVII. 66. The use of this seal of the Holy Spirit is both the confirmation and certification of the faithful concerning the truth of the Christian doctrine, concerning the grace of justification and the certainty of plenary redemption, Eph. I. 13, ch. IV. 30, 1 Cor. II. 12, 1. John V. 13, which internal certification comes to us through the word and the sacraments, as external means and seals, Rom. IV. 11, 1 John V. 6, and then the distinction from infidels, which we have from the internal motions of the Holy Spirit, 1 John III. 14, 18, 19, 24, ch. IV. 13, and then the custody against enemies, especially the forward ones, Rom. VIII. 13, Eph. IV. 10.

Finally, God is said to have given an earnest, not because He made them conscious of spiritual gifts, of which they were entirely participants, not only conscious: But because He gave the Spirit Himself into the hearts of the faithful, who is the earnest of the future inheritance. Wherefore the Apostle attributes three things to GOD, which make for the certainty of the faithful, or for the βεβαίωσιν and confirmation, which they have from God. First, that they are certain of the truth of the Evangelical doctrine, concerning which the anointing which they have received from the Holy Spirit renders them certain. For it is the Spirit who testifies, because the Spirit is truth, John V. 6. Then that He renders the same persons certain of justification through faith in Christ, which is performed through the obligation of the Holy Spirit, who not only illuminates our hearts through the word of grace and excites and works faith in them; but also seals divine grace in us through the seals of the sacraments, and internal testimony through the word in our hearts, Rom. VIII. 16. Finally, God renders us certain of the heavenly inheritance, and thus of our election to glory through the earnest and pledge which He gives us into our hearts, namely the Holy Spirit, who is the pledge of our inheritance, Eph. I. 14. Therefore these things are not to be restricted with Beza to the ministers alone, or to the mere certainty of their own proclamation, because the Apostle is now proving the truth of the promises of GOD and of his doctrine from a divine confirmation made not only to himself and his colleagues, but also to the Corinthians themselves. Whence Calvin and Piscator and Aretius make these gifts common. Aretius wishes this to be Paul's argument: I have gifts in common with you, of constancy and not of levity, the anointing, the sealing, and the earnest of the Holy Spirit. Therefore I am not fickle. Nor indeed, as some Papists, Vega, Pererius, and others wish, is this certainty to be appropriated only to very holy men. For the association of the Apostles and other faithful in the identity of certainty, which also occurs in 1 Cor. II. 12, 1 John III. 5, ch. IV. 16, ch. V. 2, 4, 14 seqq., is a most open document that the certainty of the Apostles is wrongly distinguished from the certainty of other believers concerning faith and the grace of GOD. Concerning which see B. Höpfner, disp. IX. de justif. ch. 2, art. 3, § 6.

Rashly also is this anointing snatched away by Salmeron, Cornelius à Lapide, Tirinus, and Menochius to the anointing of the sacrament of confirmation, as they call it, for which they require a Bishop and material chrism. But what Bishop anointed Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy, what Bishop anointed the Corinthians? Or where is there anything here about material anointing? No less ineptly is this seal dragged by Bellarmine to an indelible character, lib. II. de eff. Sac. c. 20, Greg. de Valentia T. IV. disp. 3, q. 4, of which there is not a jot or tittle here or elsewhere in scripture, nor a character, as Becanus, Cajetan, and Vasquez do not deny, which at any rate, according to them, does not belong to believers alone, nor is it believed to be common to the faithful of the Old Testament, nor does it confirm grace that makes one pleasing, or make for the strengthening of believers in Christ, so that they may adhere as living members; all of which things are proper to the sealing of which the Apostle treats here. To the sign of the cross Menochius, with Lombard, Thomas, and Lyranus, snatches these things in vain: since there is no trace here of a visible sign, and Suarez, Cornelius à Lapide, and Tirinus explain it as a character in the soul, whence the sign of the cross cannot be understood at the same time. And not only Vasquez, but Thomas also, as well as Salmero, confess that the Holy Spirit is that seal which is comprehended by the word σφραγισάμενος. Justinian, however, explains it both of the Holy Spirit who is conferred in baptism; and of the efficacious grace proper to the elect, in which latter he easily has the Calvinists agreeing, but not the Prophets and the Apostles. Finally, in vain do the Papists seek here all those effects which they have assigned at will to their fictitious sacrament of confirmation, as may be seen in Lyra, Cornel. à Lapide, Tirinus, and Menochius, namely the confirmation of faith, the copious collation of grace and charity through the anointing of the charism, the sign of the cross on the forehead, and an indelible character in the soul, and the pledge of the spirit, which nevertheless neither Justinian nor Estius, their most learned interpreters, could find here, and not even Vasquez, or any of the ancient Papists, let alone the Fathers, with whom the Papistic sacrament of confirmation is a mere non-entity. I pass over the fact that those effects which are here insinuated by the Apostle under different metaphors, although they can be distinguished by a certain reasoning, are accepted as the same inference by Chrysostom, Theodoret, and Theophylact.

Regarding the likeness of the earnest, this is still to be observed, that 'earnest' is not sufficiently and aptly enough rendered by 'pledge' in the Vulgate, since earnest and pledge differ, as noted by Jerome as well as Estius and Justinian. And although the Hebrew ערבון for a pledge also occurs in Gen. 38:17, Neh. 5:3, the word 'earnest' implies more, and it has been accustomed to be used peculiarly in matrimonial contracts concerning the earnest, which is given by the betrothed for the sake of the marriage faith as a sign and pledge of the betrothal made; and also in contracts of buying and selling, where the earnest is a part of the price (μέρος τῦ παντὸς, as Chrysostom has it in Eph. 1:14) which is paid in advance, so that assurance may be given for the remaining sum to be paid. In which sense that word is also applied to the symbol which was given to him in the ἐρανοῖς of the companions, who was ordered to prepare a banquet as a sign of future payment, concerning which see Casaubon, book 3, animadversions on Athenaeus, chapter 31. Chrysostom applies this sense to this cause, Tom. 3, sermon 1 on the resurrection. The earnest is a part of the whole and an assurance of the whole. Just as therefore in banquets, he who receives an earnest has assurance and is secure about the whole: So also you, when you have received the earnest of the Spirit, ought no longer to doubt about the remaining goods stored up for you. Nor is the word 'earnest' used only of things, but also of persons, such as of hostages, who are given in war for the sake of protecting faith, who are called sons of pledges in 2 Kings 14:14, 2 Chron. 25:24, and of sureties, who by their own faith guarantee that which others owe, Gen. 43:9. Wherefore the Holy Spirit is also likened to a pledge, which is deposited for mutual money or a thing promised or owed as an ἐνέχυρον, as Chrysostom calls it, because by it something is rendered ἒχυρον, that is, fortified, firm, and safe; because the Holy Spirit is given to us as a pledge in such a way that He makes the promised salvation firm and certain for us: And it is an earnest, as it were a seal given by Christ the bridegroom to his mystical bride, Hos. II. 19, in confirmation of the future nuptials, which he himself will celebrate with her in the heavens, Rev. XXI. 19, ch. XIX. 7, and it is a part of the payment, inasmuch as we receive the Holy Spirit and his gifts here as a guarantee of the whole sum that will follow, while we still walk by faith, not by sight, 2 Cor. V. 7. Those firstfruits of the Holy Spirit, which are conferred upon us here, are a certain small portion of the gifts to be communicated to us one day, and at the same time an undoubted testimony concerning the obtaining of the plenary inheritance of celestial happiness. What more? That the Holy Spirit himself is also a hostage given to us for the sake of the war ceasing and the covenant of peace being kept, as Chrysostom explains, Eph. I. homil. 2. Just as when there is war between nations, they give hostages: So also GOD gave his Son as a pledge of covenants and peace, and gave also the Holy Spirit, who is from him. Finally, the Holy Spirit is also a guarantor and sponsor of GOD among men, in applying [salvation]: just as the Son of GOD is the sponsor of men before GOD in acquiring salvation. For then, when the promise of salvation is applied to us through divine instruments, the Holy Spirit acts as it were as a bail, and pledges to us that GOD will be faithful to us; just as David prays in Ps. CXIX. 122, 'Be surety for thy servant for good,' that is, be as it were a guarantor, who may assist me, and comfort me, and defend me, so that I may be safe, just as guarantors in judgment are accustomed to assert those for whom they stand surety, as B. Höpfner has elegantly executed these things in disp. IX. de justif. aph. VI. §. 21. seqq.

Latin:

V. 22. ὁ καὶ σφραγισάμενος ἡμᾶς) Qui & externis te- stimonii apparere voluit spiritus illius vim atque naturam. Vide Eph. I. 13. Instrumentis fides accedit ex testium si- gnis. Vide Rom. IV. 11. 1. Cor. IX. 2.

Καὶ δὺς τὸν ἀῥῥαβῶνα τῦ πνεύματος ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ἡμῶν) Conscios nos facit illorum donorum spiritualium, quæ dona spiritualia sunt arrhabo futuræ vitæ spiritualis, infra V. 5. Eph. I. 14. Arrhabo ערבון vox est primitus Hebraica, ac proinde & Phœnicia, à Phœnicibus eximiis mercatoribus in Græciam venit. Origo vocis à ערב, quod est ἐγγυᾶν fide-jubere. Vide Gen. XXXVIII. 18. Arrha- bo pars est pretii, & spondet pro toto pretio. Vide, quæ diximus ad 1. Corinth. XV. 46. Latini arrhabonem ἀπο- κόπτοντες arrham dicunt. Sed & arrhabonis vox est apud Plautum, Terentium, Varronem.

Non opus est, ut recedamus ab ordinarià vo- cis δὲ significatione: Qui verò confirmat nos. Do- cet enim, non cur ista omnia cedant ad hono- rem DEI, sed quod præcipuum in hac tractatio- ne est, unde βεβαιότητα vel certitudinem de do- ctrina Evangelii, & promissionibus divinis ha- beant, tùm ipse cum collegis suis, tùm fideles Co- rinthii, ut in Christum fiduciam collocare possint indubitatam, & firmam, in quo omnes promif- fiones veritatem suam habent, nimirum non ab humana quadam traditione, vel autoritate, quæ fidem divinam, fideiq; certitudinem gignere non potest, sed à DEO ipso, qui confirmat corda no- stra, dum ungit nos unguento illo pretiosissimo lætitiæ, vel conscientiæ maximè tranquillæ & læ- tissimæ, oleo nempe Spiritus Sancti. Alludi ad unctionem typicam Veteris Testamenti, uti mani- festum est; ita dubitari nequit, quin imprimis respiciant unctionem Christi, in quem confirma- mur, utpote qui propter nos consortes suos un- ctus est immensis Spiritus Sancti donis, ut Pro- pheta, Sacerdos, & Rex noster esset, nosque Pro- phetas, Sacerdotes & Reges faceret, Apoc. I. & V. Quo de Theophylactus hic: Idemque nos & unxit, & signavit, hoc est, Prophetas & Sacerdotes & Reges nos ille effecit. Istiusmodi namque est, qui est in baptismo perlotus. Prophetas quidem, quia quod nequit oculus intueri, ipsi perspicimus, audimusque, quod auris nunquam auditu percepit. Sacerdotes vero, quia necesse est, ut DEO nos ipsos hostiam offeramus, viventem, sanctam, & illi acceptam. Reges demum constituit, quia nos ille sibi in filios adscivit, cujus in ditione sunt omnia, futurique & coelestis imperii fecit heredes. Atqui ut in Veteri Testamento sacerdotes ipsi & Reges oleo ungebantur, sic & nos hoc tempore Spiritu oblinimur, ejusque & pignus, quod Deus immisit cordibus nostris, excipi- mus. Et quemadmodum id pignoris contulit, sic & reliqua nobis est procul dubio largiturus. Pignus autem dicit hoc loco Spiritus dona. Pulchre B. Bal- duinus: Quemadmodum olim athletae ungebantur, ut membra redderentur solidiora, & ad sufferendum conflictum habiliora: Ita oleum illud laetitiae fortifi- cat cor nostrum adversus tentationes Satanae, mun- di, & carnis nostrae, quibus promissiones Dei impe- tuntur. Tria ergo praestat haec unctio Spiritus S. primo recreat & exhilarat spiritualiter, uti unguen- tum & oleum recreat corporaliter, Ps. XLV. 8. De- inde facit nos Prophetas, Sacerdotes, & Reges; uti uncti olim Prophetae, Sacerdotes & Reges oleo sacro. Vid. 1. Reg. XIX. 16. de Elisaeo Propheta, Ez. XXIX. de sacerdote, 1. Sam. X. 1. C. XVI. 13. de Rege ungendo. Tertio facit, ut luctemur for- titer contra mundum, peccatum & satanam, quem- admodum olim luctatores congressuri inungi so- lebant. Caeterum obsignasse dicitur Deus Corin- thios, non signasse, ut Vulgata habet, fatente Caje- tano, Justiniano, Cornelio a Lapide; non quod ap- parere in iis fecerit doctrinae Apostolicae sigilla miracula. Nam & ipsum Apostolum & socios Sil- vanum & Timotheum signarat Deus per miracu- la ab Apostolo edita apud Corinthios: Sed quod fidei certitudinem in ipsis signarit, quomodo sa- cramenta signacula fidei dicuntur e Rom. IV. 11. Et quum sigillum vel de rebus dicatur, ut sunt li- terae, Esth. III. 12. cap. VIII. 8. 1. Reg. XXI. 8. quae obsignantur; lapis Danielis VII. 17. Matth. XXVII. vel de veritate, quae obsignatur, Joh. III. 33. de pec- catis a DEO obsignatis, Dan. IX. 24. &c. vel de personis, tum quae obsignantur ob alios, ut ab iis cognoscantur, uti Filius a Patre nostri causa ob- signatus dicitur Joh. VI. 27. tum quae ipsae confir- mantur de aliquo beneficio conferendo vel col- lato: Hic non de sigillo quoad manifestationem respectu aliorum, sed quoad confirmationem per- sonae, quae obsignatur, sermo est. Quum sigillum vel de instrumento aut signaculo, quo obsigna- mus quid, vel de imagine inde expressa, seu signa- tura dicatur, hic Spiritus Sanctus tamen ipse ceu signaculum, ab imagine, quam in nobis exprimit, separari nequit, quia ipse Spiritus Sanctus com- municatur nobis, non tantum dona Sp. S. fides, certitudo gratiae, pax conscientiae, & similia, quae Spiritus Sancti effecta sunt; neque absens, sed gratiose praesens nos obsignat, ac de gratia certos reddit, tum in cordibus nostris clamet Abba Pa- ter, nobisque testimonium reddat, quod filii Dei simus, Rom. IIX. 11. Gal. IV. 6. Joh. Crocius ita in Comment. ad Eph. p. 114. de hac obsignatione habet: Lombardus & Hugo imaginem DEI refor- matam in nobis intelligunt. Id placet. Obsignando imprimitur imago sigilli. Sic fidelibus imprimitur Spiritus S. imago. Quaenam illa? Sapientia & san- ctitas, cujus praecipua pars est charitas. Ea impri- mitur in sanctificatione. Dum igitur Ephesiis, in quibus fides erat per Evangelium accensa, confertur lux sapientiae, calor charitatis, & nitor sanctimonia eo ipso sigillo cordi ipsorum tanquam cera impresso, ob- signantur, adeoque tum magis & magis conformantur Spiritui tanquam sanctitatis archetypo & sigillo im- primenti, tùm discernuntur à grege Diaboli, tùm magis confirmantur de promissionum certitudine. Non aliter atque epistola sigillo confirmatur. Dum enim Evangelium stylo Spiritus Sancti in eorum cordibus scribitur, fiunt epistola DEI, 2. Cor. III. 3. At postquam facti sunt DEI epistola, obsignantur. Priori actu gignitur fides in eorum cordibus; po- steriori roboratur, ut contra dubitationem omnem fortiter pugnans in DEI veritate penitus acquie- scat. Quum obsignationis finis sit confirmatio, Esth. IIX. 8. discretio genuini à supposititio, & ob- signati custodia, ne facilè lædatur vel auferatur Dan. VI. 17. Matth. XXVII. 66. Sigilli hujusce Spiritus Sancti usus est tùm confirmatio & cer- tificatio fidelium de veritate doctrinæ Christia- næ, de gratiâ justificationis & certitudine plenariæ redemptionis, Eph. I. 13. cap. IV. 30. 1. Cor. II. 12. 1. Joh. V. 13. quæ interna certificatio per verbum & sacramenta, ceu externa media & sigilla nobis obtingit, Rom. IV. 11. 1. Joh. V. 6. tùm discretio ab infidelibus, quam habemus ex internis Spiritus Sancti motibus, 1. Joh. III. 14. 18. 19. 24. cap. IV. 13. tùm custodia adversus hostes imprimis procaces, Rom. IIX. 13. Eph. IV. 10.

Arrhabonem denique dedisse Deus dicitur, non quod conscios fecerit donorum spiritualium, quo- rum omninò participes erant, non solum conscii: Sed quod Spiritum ipsum dederit in corda fide- lium, qui arrhabo est futuræ hæreditatis. Qua- propter tria DEO tribuit Apostolus, quæ ad cer- titudinem fidelium faciunt, vel ad βεβαίωσιν & confirmationem, quam à Deo habent. Primum quod certi sint de veritate doctrinæ Evangelicæ, quâ de certos reddit unctio, quam acceperunt Spi- ritus S. Nam Spiritus est, qui testatur, quod Spiri- tus sit veritas, Joh. V. 6. Deinde quod certos eosdem reddat de justificatione per fidem in Christum, quod præstatur per obligationem Spiritus S. qui non modo illuminat corda nostra per verbum gra- tiæ & fidem in iisdem excitat, atque operatur; sed etiam obsignat divinam gratiam in nobis per sigil- la sacramentorum, & internam testificationem per verbum in cordibus nostris, Rom. VIII. 16. De- nique certos nos reddit Deus de hæreditate cœ- lesti, adeoque de electione nostra ad gloriam per arrhabonem & pignus, quod nobis dat in corda nostra, Spiritum nempe Sanctum, qui est pignus nostræ hæreditatis, Eph. I. 14. Non ergò hæc cum Beza ad solos ministros restringenda, vel ad solam certitudinem præconii ipsorum, quia probat jam Apostolus veritatem promissionum DEI & do- ctrinæ suæ à divina confirmatione non sibi tantum & collegis suis, sed etiam Corinthiis ipsis factâ. Unde Calvinus & Piscator atque Aretius hæc com- munia faciunt dona. Aretius Pauli argumentum hoc esse vult: Dona habeo vobiscum communia constantia & non levitatis, unctionem, obsignatio- nem, & arrhabonem Spiritus S. Ergo levis non sum. Neq; verò, quod Papistæ nonnulli Vega, Pererius, aliique volunt, certitudo hæc tantum viris valdè sanctis approprianda. Apostolorum enim & alio- rum fidelium consociationem in identitate certi- tudinis, quæ etiam occurrit 1. Cor. II. 12. 1. Joh. III. 5. cap. IV. 16. cap. V. 2. 4. 14. seqq. apertissimum do- cumentum est, perperam distingui certitudinem Apostolorum ab aliorum credentium certitudine de fide & gratia DEI. Quo de vid. B. Höpfnerus disp. IX. de justif. cap. 2. art. 3. §. 6.

Temerè etiam hæc unctio à Salmerone, Corne- lio à Lapide, Tirino, Menochio abripitur ad unctio- nem sacramenti confirmationis, quod vocant, ad quod requirunt Episcopum & chrisma materiale. Quis verò Episcopus Paulum, Sylvanum, & Ti- motheum, quis Corinthios unxit? Aut ubi hic quicquam de unctione materiali? Nec minus in- eptè sigillum hoc trahitur à Bellarmino ad chara- cterem indelebilem lib. II. de eff. Sac. c. 20. Greg. de Valentia T. IV. disp. 3. q. 4. de quo nullus vel hic vel alibi in scriptura apex, vel character, haud dif- fitente Becano, Cajetano, Vasquezio, qui utiq; juxta ipsos non solis credentibus convenit, nec com̄unis esse creditur fidelibus Vet. Testam. nec gratiam gratum facientem confirmat, aut ad obfirmatio- nem credentium in Christum facit, ut ipsi tan- quam membra viva adhæreant; quæ verò omnia obsignationi, de qua hic agit Apostolus, propria sunt. Ad signum crucis Menochius cum Lombar- do, Thoma, & Lyrano, frustrà hæc rapit: quum hic de signo visibili nullum sit vestigium, & Suarez, Cornelius à Lapide, ac Tirinus de charactere in ani- ma explicent, unde non potest simul crucis signum intelligi. Nec Vasquez tantum, sed Thomas quoq; ut & Salmero fateantur, Sp. S. esse sigillum illud, quod verbo σφραγισάμενος comprehenditur. Ju- stinianus verò tùm de Sp. S. qui in baptismo con- fertur, exponat; tùm de gratia efficaci electorum proprià, in quo posteriori facilè annuentes habet Calvinianos, non autem Prophetas & Apostolos. Frustrà denique hic omnia illa effecta quærunt Pa- pistæ, quæ suo fictitio sacramento confirmationis pro lubitu assignarunt, ut apud Lyrarum, Cornel. à Lapide, Tirinum, Menochium videre est, nimi- rum confirmationem fidei, copiosam gratiæ & chari- tatis per charismatis unctionem, collationem, signum crucis, in fronte ac characterem indelebilem in ani- ma ac pignus spiritus, quæ tamen nec Justinianus, nec Estius doctissimi ipsorum Interpretes invenire hic potuere, ac ne Vasquez quidem, aut ullus Vete- rum Pontificiorum, nedum Patrum, penes quos Papisticum confirmationis sacramentum est me- rum non-Ens. Taceo, quod illa effecta, quæ hic ab Apostolo sub diversis Metaphoris insinuantur, etsi certà ratione distingui possint, ut idem inferentia à Chrysostomo, Theodoreto, Theophylacto accipiantur.

De arrhabonis similitudine id adhuc observan- dum, quod arrhabo per pignus non sufficienter & accommodè satis reddatur in Vulgata, quum arrha & pignus differant, notante Hieronymo ut & Estio & Justiniano. Et quamvis Ebræum ערבון de pignore etiam occurrat Gen. XXXVIII. 17. Neh. V. 3. plus tamen infert vox arrhæ, & peculiariter usurpari consuevit in contractibus matrimonialibus de arrha, quæ ob conjugii fidem à sponsis datur in signum & pignus factæ sponsionis; nec non in contractibus emtionis & venditionis, ubi arrha est pars pretii (μέρος τῦ παντὸς, ut habet Chrysosto- mus in Eph. I. 14.) quæ in antecessum solvitur, ut fides fiat reliquæ summæ persolvendæ. Quo sensu adhibetur etiam vox illa de symbolo, quod in ἐρα- νοῖς ei dabatur sodalium, qui jubebatur convivi- um parare in signum futuræ solutionis, quo de Casaub. lib. III. animadvers. in Athen. cap. 31. Quem sensum applicat huic causæ Chrysostomus Tom. III. serm. 1. de resurrect. Arrh रणनीति pars to- tius & de toto fides. Sicut igitur in conviviis, qui ac- cipit arrhabonem, fidem habet & securus est de toto: Ita & tu cum acceperis arrhabonem Spiritus, non jam dubitare debes de cæteris bonis tibi repositis. Nec tantum de rebus adhibetur arrhæ vox, sed etiam de personis, utpote de obsidibus, qui in bello dantur fidei tuendæ gratia, qui filii arrhabonum dicuntur 2. Reg. XIV. 14. 2. Chron. XXV. 24. & de fidejussori- bus, qui fide sua jubent esse, quod alii debent, Gen. XLIII. 9. Quapropter & pignori assimilatur Spiri- tus Sanctus, quod pro mutua pecunia vel re pro- missa aut debita deponitur ceu ἐνέχυρον, uti vocat Chrysostomus, quod illo reddatur aliquid ἒχυρον. id est, munitum, firmum, & tutum; quia ita pignori nobis datur Spiritus Sanctus, ut firmam certamque nobis faciat promissam salutem: Et arrha est, quasi signaculum à Christo sponso datum sponsæ mysticæ, Os. II. 19. in confirmationem futurarum nuptiarum, quas ipse in cœlis cum eadem celebrabit, Apoc. XXI. 19. cap. XIX. 7. & pars est solutionis, prout Sp. S. ejusque dona hìc accipimus in fidem summæ totius secuturæ, dum ambulamus adhuc per fidem, non per speciem, 2. Cor. V. 7. Primitiæ illæ Spiritus Sancti, quæ hic in nos conferuntur, portiuncula sunt quædam donorum nobis olim communicandorum, & simul indubitatum testimonium de plenaria cœlestis felicitatis hæreditate consequenda. Quid? quod ipse Spiritus Sanctus etiam obses nobis sit belli cessantis, & fœderis pacis servandi causa datus, ut explicat Chrysost. Ephes. I. homil. 2. Sicut cum bellum est gentibus adversus gentes, dant obsides: Ita & DEUS dedit Filium suum fœderum ac pacis pignus, dedit & Spiritum Sanctum, qui est ex ipso. Denique Spiritus Sanctus est quoque fidejussor, & sponsor DEI apud homines, in applicanda: sicut Filius DEI est sponsor hominum apud DEUM in acquirenda salute. Tunc enim quando nobis applicatur promissio salutis per divina organa, Spiritus Sanctus quasi vadimonium obit, ac spondet nobis, DEUM nobis fidelem fore; sicut orat David Psal. CXIX. 122. Sponde pro servo tuo in bonum, id est, esto quasi fidejussor, qui mihi assistat, ac me soletur, ac defendat, ut salvus sim, sicut fidejussores in judicio solent asserere illos, pro quibus spondent, uti eleganter hæc exequutus est B. Höpfnerus disp. IX. de justif. aph. VI. §. 21. seqq.

## 1:23
V. 23. 'But I call God for a witness upon my soul') It is a perfect oath, but in a most serious matter. Thus Job XVI. 18, 'Behold, my witness is in heaven, and he that voucheth for me is on high.' See what has been said by us at Matt. V. 34. 'Upon my soul,' that is, with my greatest harm, if I deceive. Such is that oath in Job XXII. 23, יהוה הוּא יִבקש 'Let God avenge.' Thus, 'may I not live,' a formula of swearing among Cicero and Martial; 'may I not be safe,' among Cicero elsewhere.

The second chapter begins here in the version of B. Luther, which also happens in the Syriac translation and in Chrysostom, who begins a new homily here: And these things cohere with those which follow in the second chapter, where the Apostle pursues further the cause of the delay of his arrival. He returns, however, with these words to that from which he had digressed for the sake of commending the certainty of the doctrine of the Gospel, namely, to free himself from every suspicion of levity. For he shows the cause which held him back, namely, that he would not have to use his severe censure upon uncorrected vices upon his arrival. Above, he transferred the blame to an incumbent necessity, by which he was hindered and could not come as he had promised: Here he uses another μεταστάσει (change of plan), I did not come, I confess, but I changed my plan for your good, even if I could have come. I changed it for a good end, not out of levity. Others do not take that 'upon my soul' as an execration, 'let God destroy me if I have spoken the truth,' but in this way, 'I call God as a witness of my mind.' Estius rightly observes that these do not attend to the phraseology of Scripture, and therefore we easily admit that the Apostle so calls GOD to witness that he provokes Him as his avenger and judge upon his soul, if he has not spoken the truth. Whence St. Augustine, epist. 89, quæst. 5, rightly teaches from the present passage that an oath is not illicit for Christians, if necessity demands it, such as was imposed here upon the Apostle because of the slander of his detractors. Which is to be observed against the Anabaptists and other fanatics, who contend that oaths are simply prohibited to Christians.

'That to spare you I came not as yet to Corinth') There were also other causes why he deferred his journey to Corinth, but this was not the least, that he wanted them to be thoroughly corrected before his arrival, lest he be forced to use harsher words or deeds. See 1 Cor. IV. 21 and below XII. 20, 21.

The Vulgate did not well render that 'no longer' (non ultra). It is, however, 'not yet' (non adhuc), that is, not as yet, as the Ambrosian [manuscript] has it. The Apostle illustrates that cause in the last chapter, v. 10: 'I write these things being absent, that being present I may not deal more harshly according to the power which the Lord has given me.' And therefore to spare is not to deal more harshly.

Latin:

V. 23. Ἐγὼ δὲ μάρτυρα τὸν Θεὸν ἐπικαλοῦμαι ἐπὶ τὴν ἐμὴν ψυχήν) Est juramentum perfectum, sed in re gravissima. Sic Job. XVI. 18. ἰδὺ ἐν ὀυρανοῖς ὁ μάρτυς μου, ὁ δὲ συνίστως με ἐν ὑψίστοις. Vide, quæ à nobis dicta ad Matth. V. 34. In animam meam, id est, cum maximo meo malo, si fallo. Tale illud jusjurandum Job. XXII. 23. יהוה הוּא יִבקש Deus vindicet. Sic, ne vivam, jurandi formula apud Ciceronem & Martialem, ne salvus sim, apud Ciceronem alibi.

Caput secundum hic orditur versio B. Lutheri, quod etiam fit in Syriaca translatione & apud Chrysostomum, novam hic homiliam incipientem: Et cohærent hæc cum iis, quæ in capite secundo sequuntur, ubi causam retardati adventus sui amplius persequitur Apostolus. Redit autem his verbis eò, unde propter commendationem certitudinis doctrinæ Evangelicæ digressus fuerat, ut nempe omni levitatis suspicione se liberet. Ostendit enim causam, quæ ipsum retraxerit, ne scilicet sub adventum sua severa animadversione vitiis nondum correctis sibi utendum foret. Suprà transsulit culpam in necessitatem incumbentem, qua præpeditus non potuit venire, ut promiserat: Hîc alià utitur μεταστάσει, non veni, fateor, sed vestro bono mutavi consilium, si maximè venire potuissem. Bono fine mutavi, non ex levitate. Illa ἐπὶ τὴν ψυχὴν alii non de execratione accipiunt, perdat me Deus, nisi vera dixero, sed hoc modo, Deum invoco testem animi mei. Hos autem ad scripturæ phrasin non attendere, rectè observat Estius, ideoque facilè admittimus, Apostolum ita DEUM testari, ut vindicem ac judicem ipsum in animam suam provocet, nisi veritatem dixerit. Unde S. Augustinus epist. 89. quæst. 5. è præsenti loco recte docet, non illicitum esse Christianis juramentum, si id necessitas postulet, qualis hic imposita erat Apostolo ob obtrectatorum calumniam. Quod contra Anabaptistas aliosque fanaticos, prohibita simpliciter Christianis esse juramenta, contendentes, observandum.

Ὅτι φειδόμενος ὑμῶν ὀυκέτι ἦλθον εἰς Κόρινθον) Erant & aliæ causæ, cur iter differret Corinthum, sed hæc non mi- nima, quod vellet eos ante adventum suum penitus cor- rigi, ne aut verbis aut factis asperioribus uti cogeretur. Vide 1. Cor. IV. 21. & infra XII. 20, 21.

Vulgata non bene reddidit illud ὀυκέτι non ul- tra. Est autem non adhuc, id est, nondum, ut ha- bet Ambrosianus. Caufam illam cap. ult. v. 10. ita illustrat Apostolus: Hoc absens scribo, ut non præsens durius agam pro potestate, quam Dominus mihi dedit. Ideoque parcere est non durius agere.

## 1:24
V. 24. 'Not that we have dominion over your faith') It is an ἀνθυποφορὰ (counter-objection). For he seemed to have spoken imperiously, not sparing. Therefore he removes this suspicion from himself. We wish nothing to be believed by you except what Christ has commanded. If we were to impose anything according to our own pleasure, this would be to exercise dominion over the faith, as here: over the people peculiar to God, as 1 Pet. V. 3.

'But we are helpers of your joy') With GOD and Christ, and under them we labor for this, that you may become participants of joy, namely, eternal. Thus 'joy' is taken in Heb. XII. 2.

Thus the false Apostles are noted at the same time obliquely, and the Corinthians, who bore with those who were lording it over them and commanding everything, and as it were exacting tributes, ch. XI. 20. We do not deny that this refers to faith, as the words themselves sound, because the Apostle had warned them about the heads of faith which were being corrupted by false teachers, and he wanted it to be kept undefiled, not as lording it over their faith, but as an ambassador of Christ. Concerning which Theophylact, with Chrysostom preceding him, [says]: not that I have a right over your faith: for faith is of free will, and compels nothing in one who is unwilling to believe. However, they are not referred to faith alone; but also to the holiness of life, which is a consequence of faith, and coheres with it in an inseparable bond; for he had also exhorted them to amend that, not by way of lordship, but as a minister of the word, and a curator of souls, not out of some affected command, as if they were compelled to believe or to live by his own will, but out of love and zeal for their salvation. Nor indeed do only Lords punish, but also Fathers and Tutors. Since therefore Paul did not wish to lord it over the faith, how much less does lordship over the faith befit the Roman Pontiff, by which he orders those things to be believed which Christ did not command. Others make an elliptical expression with Theodoret and Oecumenius in Photius: not that we lord it over you in faith, that is, on account of your faith, which you learned by our teaching, or in the name of faith, as Erasmus expressed it, because the Apostle did not write τῆς ὑμῶν πίσεως, but ὑμῶν τῆς πίσεως. This explanation is approved by Gagny and Estius. But Camerarius rightly warned that the placement of the article brings no weight to this or that sense. Beza also judged it clearly forced. Paul and Timothy called themselves fellow-workers of the joy of the Corinthians, that is, of those things which make for the joy not to be suppressed but preserved: joining themselves with the faithful in the Corinthian Church, and making them their fellow-workers in that matter, both to excite them the more, and because they judged them not unworthy of that title, inasmuch as they stood in the faith. For faith is the cause of joy in the Lord. Therefore, for the sake of humility, they associate themselves with the Corinthians rather than with God, which the opposition of lordship over faith demands, which, so far from affecting, they profess themselves to be nothing but their fellow-workers in those things by which joy in the Lord can be fostered, which they wished to take diligent care that it not be disturbed by defection from the faith or a wicked life.

Τῇ γὰρ πίσει ἑσήκατε) The past tense in the Hebrew manner for the present. You stand by faith, that is, through faith, namely the working one, you are in that state, so that you can hope for that eternal joy with the best right. Therefore I devote so much effort, that that faith may remain with you. I seek nothing, I demand nothing else. He does not here provide the reason why they do not wish to lord it over their faith, because they persist in it constantly, even though the commentary of Theophylact tends in that direction: In those things, indeed, which concern the faith, you stand in a right state: Whence it happens that I have nothing of which I can accuse you, but in other matters you are weaker and wavering, from which if you do not withdraw your foot having been corrected, I shall deservedly be able to affect you with punishment and sorrow, just as I myself have been affected with sadness for your sake. But this eulogy means this, that they themselves are able to cooperate entirely with them in fostering and preserving joy, because they stand by faith, through which we rejoice and glory even in tribulations, Rom. V. 3. To stand by faith is to stand in the faith, as Gal. V. 1. to stand in liberty. He opposes joy and the peace of conscience to tyrannical terror, and at the same time makes it the proper end of the Gospel. Castalio rendered it: Not that we take away your confidence, but we have consulted for your joy. Against whom Beza inveighs deservedly: I beseech you, however, what is the height of impudence, to dare anything in interpreting, if this is not it?

Latin:

V. 24. Οὐχ ὅτι κυριέυομεν ὑμῶν τῆς πίσεως) Est ἀνθυ- ποφορὰ. Videbatur enim imperiofe dixisse, non parcens. Itaque removet à se hanc suspicionem. Nihil volumus à vobis credi, nisi quæ Christus præcepit. Si quid pro no- stro lubitu imponeremus, hoc esset dominatum exercere in fidem, ut hic: in populum peculiarem Deo, ut 1. Pet. V. 3.

Ἀλλὰ συνεργοί ἐσμεν τῆς χαρᾶς ὑμῶν) Cum DEO & Christo, ac sub illis in id laboramus, ut gaudii fiatis parti- cipes, nempe æterni. Sic χαρὰ sumitur Hebr. XII. 2.

Notantur ita simul obliquè falsi Apostoli, & Corinthii, qui dominantes ac omnia imperantes, & velut tributorum exactores eosdem ferebant cap. XI. 20. Ad fidem hæc referri, ut verba ipsa sonant, non abnuimus, quia de fidei capitibus, quæ corrumpebantur à falsis doctoribus monue- rat Apostolus, eamque intemeratam servari vo- lebat, non ut dominans fidei eorum, sed ut lega- tus Christi. De quo Theophylactus, præeunte Chry- sostomo, non quod sit mihi jus in fidem vestram: liberæ namque voluntatis fides est, neque quicquam cogit nolentem credere. Non autem referuntur ad fidem solum; sed etiàm ad sanctitatem vitæ, quæ fidei consequens est, & cum eâ indivulso ne- xu cohæret; nam & ad illam emendandam hor- tatus erat, non per modum dominatus, sed ceu verbi minister, & curator animarum, non ex affe- ctato quodam imperio, quasi ex suo arbitrio vel credere, vel vivere cogantur, sed salutis ipsorum amore & studio. Neque vero soli Domini pu- niunt, sed etiam Patres & Præceptores. Quum er- gò Paulus noluerit dominari fidei, quanto minus convenit Pontifici Romano dominatus in fidem, quo ea credi jubet, quæ Christus non præceperit. Alii ellipticam loquutionem faciunt cum Theo- doreto & Oecumenio apud Photium: non quod do- minemur vobis fide, id est, propter fidem vestram, quam nostro Magisterio didicistis, vel nomine fidei, ut Erasmus expressit, quod Apostolus non scripse- rit τῆς ὑμῶν πίσεως, sed ὑμῶν τῆς πίσεως. Quæ ex- plicatio Gagneo & Estio probatur. Sed recte mo- nuit Camerarius, articuli collocationem nihil mo- menti ad hunc vel illu sensum afferre. Beza etiam id judicavit planè violentum. Συνεργὸς autem sese dixere Paulus & Timotheus gaudii Corinthiorum, id est eorum, quæ ad gaudium non supprimendum sed conservandum faciunt: conjungentes se cum fidelibus in Ecclesia Corinthiacâ, ipsosq; facientes ea in re cooperarios suos, cùm ut eosdem magis excitarent, tùm quod eo titulo non indignos ju- dicarent, utpote qui in fide stabant. Fides enim causa est gaudii in Domino. Sese ergò humilitatis causâ potius Corinthiis, quam Deo associant, quod poscit oppositio dominatus fidei, quem, tantum abest, ut affectent, ut non nisi cooperarios ipso- rum sese profiteantur in iis, quibus gaudium in Domino foveri potest, quod ne defectione à fide aut improba vita turbent, sedulò cavere voluere.

Τῇ γὰρ πίσει ἑσήκατε) Præteritum more Hebræo pro Præsenti. Statis fide, id est, per fidem, nempe operantem, in eo statu estis, ut illud æternum gaudium jure optimo spe- rare possitis. Ideo tantum operæ impendo, ut fides ista vobis constet. Nihil quæro, nihil exigo aliud. Causam hic non reddit, cur non velint domi- nari fidei ipsorum, quia constanter in ea persistant, etsi eò abit commentarius Theophylacti: In his quidem, quæ fidem contingunt, recto statu consisti- tis: Quo fit, ut nil habeam, cujus insimulare vos queam, in cæteris verò infirmiores estis & nuta- bundi, à quibus si pedem non retuleritis emendati, merito nec secus vos pœna afficere & mœrore po- tero, ac ipse vestri ob gratiam tristitia sum affe- ctus. Sed id hoc elogium sibi vult, eosdem omni- no cooperari posse ipsis in gaudio fovendo, & conservando, quia fide stant, per quam gaude- mus & gloriamur etiam in tribulationibus, Rom. V. 3. Fide stare est stare in fide, ut Gal. V. 1. liber- tate stare. Gaudium ac pacem conscientiæ op- ponit tyrannico terrori, simulque proprium Ev- angelii finem facit. Castalio reddidit: Non quod vobis fiduciam derogemus, sed consuluimus vestro gaudio. In quem merito invehitur Beza: Obse- cro verò, quid est summa impudentia, quodvis au- dere in interpretando, si hoc non est?

## 2:1 Argument
CHAPTER II.

ARGUMENT AND DIVISION.

He explains by what reasoning he spared the Corinthians by delaying his arrival, namely so that he would not arrive with sadness, and declaring with tears his affection of mind toward them, whom he holds for his own joy, even toward him for whom he had previously caused sadness, whom he now warns must be forgiven, and teaches that he himself, in the place of Christ, also forgives. Furthermore, he explains why he preached the Gospel in Troas and then proceeded into Macedonia, and gives thanks to God, because He always grants victory in Christ, and manifests the odor of His knowledge everywhere through him, and testifies concerning the sincerity of his doctrine.

There are two parts, I. A declaration of love toward the Corinthians, to v. 10. 11. II. A celebration of divine grace for the manifestation of the odor of saving knowledge, to v. 17.

THE FORMER PART.

A declaration of love toward the Corinthians.

Ἔκρινα δὲ ἐμαυτῷ τοῦτο) ἔκρινα, I decided, as it is in Acts II. 16. XXVII. 1. Ἐμαυτῷ for myself, that is, with myself, in imitation of the Hebrew לִי.

Τὸ μὴ πάλιν ἐν λύπῃ πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐλθεῖν) And here there is a transposition and two words for one. For the sense is μὴ ἀνελθεῖν πρὸς ὑμᾶς καὶ τοῦτο ἐν λύπῃ not to return to you in such a way that my return brings sorrow to you.

While the Apostle explains how he spared the Corinthians by the delay of his arrival: At the same time he dilutes another accusation, namely of excessive severity, and declares his love for them in the sweetest words. There is therefore a transition here from the first part of the apology to the second, and the Apostle shows the end of his plan, namely that he might not be forced by Apostolic authority to use it while present, and therefore preferred to write somewhat more severely while absent, so that they might correct what needed correcting. For it is the way of friends to wish to exclude all sadness from their gathering. Regarding that πάλιν, B. Baldwin says: For that had already been done once through the former epistle, where he had reproved their various sins, especially the tolerance of the incestuous man, and the ἀταξίαν in the Ecclesiastical gatherings, which they had undoubtedly perceived not without sickness of soul. So also Chrysostom. Theodoret warns that that word 'again' is to be joined with the arrival, not with the sadness, so that the sense is: I did not want my arrival to you to be with sadness. Thus also Pelagius and Primasius: I disposed not to come a second time in sadness, I who was with you with joy when you first believed. Which sense Estius, with Cajetan, approves as being in conformity with the Greek text. Thus Beza: For you are the only ones from whom I can now take pleasure: You being affected with trouble again, there is no reason why I should hope for joy from elsewhere.

Latin:

CAPUT II.

ARGUMENTUM ET PARTITIO.

Explicat, qua ratione differendo adventum Corinthiis pepercerit, ne scilicet cum tri- stitia adveniret, & affectum animi erga ipsos, quos pro gaudio suo habet, cum la- crymis declarans, etiam erga eum, ob quem tristem anteà fecerat, cui jam condonan- dum esse monet, & se vice Christi etiam condonare docet. Porro cur in Troade Evangelium prædicârit, & in Macedo- niam dehinc perrexerit, exponit, Deoque gratias agit, quod semper victoriam in Christo concedat, & odorem cognitionis suæ ubique per se manifestet, ac de since- ritate doctrinæ testatur.

PArtes sunt duæ, I. Amoris erga Corinthios de- clamatio, ad v. 10. 11. II. Gratiæ divinæ pro manifestatione odoris cognitionis salutiferæ cele- bratio, ad v. 17.

PARS PRIOR.

Amoris erga Corinthios declaratio.

Ἔκρινα δὲ ἐμαυτῷ τοῦτο) ἔκρινα, constitui, ut est Act. II. 16. XXVII. 1. Ἐμαυτῷ mihi, id est, apud me, ad imi- tationem לִי Hebraici.

Τὸ μὴ πάλιν ἐν λύπῃ πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐλθεῖν) Et hic tra- jectio est & duæ voces pro una. Sensus enim est μὴ ἀνελ- θεῖν πρὸς ὑμᾶς καὶ τοῦτο ἐν λύπῃ non redire ad vos ita, ut reditus meus mœrorem vobis afferat.

Dum explicat Apostolus, quomodo peper- cerit Corinthiis dilatione adventus sui : Simul ἔγκλημα alterum nimiæ scilicet severitatis diluit, ac suavissimis verbis amorem suum ipsis declarat. Μετάβασις ergò hic est à priori loco apologiæ ad alterum, & ostendit Apostolus finem consilii sui, ne scil. Apostolica autoritate cogeretur præsens uti, ideo maluisse absentem scribere aliquanto severius, ut ipsi corrigenda emendarent. Ami- corum enim est velle in conventu suo omnem tristitiam excludere. Ad illud πάλιν B. Baldui- nus: Id enim jam semel factum erat per priorem epistolam, ubi varia ipsorum peccata, imprimis tolerantiam incestuosi, & ἀταξίαν in conventibus Ecclesiasticis reprehenderat, id quod haud dubiè non sine animorum ægritudine perceperant. Ita etiam Chrysostomus. Theodoretus monet, illud iterum, cum adventu non cum tristitia conjun- ctum esse, ut sensus sit: Nolui secundum meum adventum ad vos esse cum tristitia. Sic & Pe- lagius & Primasius: Disposui ne in tristitia secun- do venirem, qui cum primùm credidistis apud vos cum gaudio fui. Quem sensum ceu Græco textui conformem cum Cajetano probat Estius. Ita Be- za: Vos enim ii uni estis, ex quibus nunc possim vo- luptatem capere: Quibus iterum molestia affectis, non est, quod aliunde gaudium sperem.

## 2:2
V. 2. For if I cause you sorrow, and who is there gladdening me) That is, who ought to console me, as his teacher. Unless the one who is saddened by me) And therefore no one: For how will a sad person console another? The singular for the plural as collective.

He protests thus, that he did not cause them sorrow out of a sinister affection, since he wishes to be gladdened by them most of all, whom, if he had made them sad on purpose, he would have had no source from which he could have rejoiced. Thus Beza: For if you have been affected with trouble, who is left who may exhilarate me? For you are the only ones from whom I can now take pleasure: you having been affected with trouble again, there is no reason for me to hope for joy from elsewhere. The singular designates him whom he had ordered to be delivered to Satan, rather than the whole assembly. For because of the same one, he had affected the Corinthians with sorrow, and had ordered them to mourn. And therefore he could not be exhilarated except through the repentance of the same one who had been particularly affected with sorrow by him. Erasmus rightly notes the Vulgate here. Unless he who is saddened by me. He uses 'to be saddened' in his own way for 'to be affected with grief,' which sounds like something else to the Latins.

Latin:

V. 2. Εἰ γὰρ ἐγὼ λυπῶ ὑμᾶς, καὶ τίς ἐστιν εὐφραίνων με) Id est, qui me consolari deberet, ut doctorem suum. Εἰ μὴ ὁ λυπούμενος ἐξ ἐμοῦ) Ac proinde nemo: Quo- modo enim tristis alium solabitur? Singulare pro Plurali ut incellectivis.

Protestatur ita, se non ex affectu sinistro ipsos tristitiâ affecisse, quum per ipsos maximè velit gaudio affici, quos si tristes studio fecisset, mini- mè habuisset, unde lætari potuisset. Ita Beza: Nam si vos molestia affecti estis, quis superstes est, qui me exhilarer? Vos enim ii uni estis, ex qui- bus nunc possim voluptatem capere: quibus iterum molestiâ affectis, non est quod aliunde gaudium sperem. Singularis designat eum, quem jusserat tradi Satanæ, potius quàm totum cœtum. Nam propter eundem tristitia Corinthios affecerat, eosque lugere jusserat. Nec ergò nisi per ejus- dem resipiscentiam, qui ab ipso peculiariter tri- stitia affectus erat, exhilarari poterat. Vulgatam rectè hic notat Erasmus. Nisi qui contristatur ex me. Contristari suo modo ponit pro dolore af- fici, quod aliud quiddam sonat Latinis.

## 2:3
V. 3. And I wrote to you this very thing) In this epistle I wrote to you the reason why I am delaying my return to you, so that you might remove it. That I might not, having come, have sorrow upon sorrow) Among so many dangers in which I have been involved, a new grief on account of the severity of words or matters which I am forced to use against the uncorrected. The Apostle was such as a good Prince is described: Who, as often as he is forced to be cruel, grieves. See below XII. 21. From whom I ought to rejoice) From whose progress I ought to receive the greatest joy: Who will praise a father, if not happy sons? Trusting in you all, that my joy is that of you all) I think so well of you that I believe you wish for nothing more than that I should rejoice. I show the way by which you may attain that; just as the Hebrew בטח is accustomed to draw על after it, so the Greek πέποιθα has ἐπὶ with it, as can be seen in 2 Kings 18:21 and elsewhere.

Chrysostom, Oecumenius, and Theophylactus indeed understand this of this very epistle. But it is more correctly taken as referring to the former epistle. Flacius has not so badly summarized the sum in his gloss: He excuses the writing of the former epistle, especially regarding what pertains to excommunication, for a triple reason: First, that he therefore wished to write more harshly to them by letter, so that he would not have the necessity of dealing with them more harshly in person while grieving and groaning, which he also inculcates below in the thirteenth chapter, verse ten: secondly, in the following verse he says that he did that very thing with the greatest grief of his own mind, just as if he were cutting or cauterizing his own limbs: thirdly, that he did it with the purpose of demonstrating his solicitude for them and his benevolence. By 'this very thing' those things seem to be looked back upon which are contained in the former epistle, chapter 4:21. What do you wish? Shall I come to you with a rod, or in love and a spirit of gentleness? Beza takes it thus: That very thing, namely, that which brought trouble to them and to you; acknowledging that it must be referred to the former epistle. Therefore 'sorrow upon sorrow' does not look to the dangers in which he had been involved, and a new grief, but rather the gravity of sadness, which the phrase sadness upon sadness implies, if he were to look upon those crimes at present, he reports, lest he be consumed by grief on account of those who were (they certainly ought to have been) his chief joy, as he had written concerning the Thessalonians in 1 Epist. II. 20: You are our glory and joy. Nor do the codices have λύπην ἐπὶ λυπῇ, except for very few, as Erasmus and Beza report, nor the Syriac, nor the Greek interpreters, but simply λύπην: they judge that it was transferred hither from Phil. II. 27. But the Apostle thus excuses the harshness of the former epistle. For the Corinthians could say, if you do not wish to affect us with sadness, why then did you write so bitter an epistle to us? In which you traduce us as schismatics, as fornicators, covetous, contentious, incestuous, haters of all good order, and what not? Does not this vehemence of yours stir up bile in us both? Is this what it means to not wish to sadden? The Apostle therefore answers: I wrote this very thing to you, that when I come, I may not have sadness upon sadness, concerning those over whom I ought to have rejoiced, trusting in you all, that my joy is that of you all v. 3. He does not deny the severity of the epistle, but adds the cause, for necessity demanded it: Since they could not truly rejoice in the Lord in any other way than by the removal of these scandals, which disturb all sincere joy of the soul. He therefore wished to affect them with sadness first, so that after repentance was performed, they themselves might be filled on all sides with their Apostle's sincere joy; as the blessed Balduinus conveniently puts it here. So also that πεποιθὼς of Beza: Nay, he says, I hoped altogether that it would be that you would immediately remove what you understood displeased me: because you considered my joys to be common to you. Theophylact: I wrote, he says, trusting that you would eventually return to the way, and that this would be for my joy. For I do not think the affections of my mind are alien from yours, and therefore I also added that, lest I have sadness, considering nothing at all that concerns me, but what concerns you. For I hold it as a more certain thing, that you also rejoice when you see me cheerful and more joyful: and no less, if I were grieving for your sake, that you would grieve as well.

Latin:

V. 3. Καὶ ἔγραψα ὑμῖν τοῦτο ἀυτὸ) In hac epistola scripsi vobis causam, cur reditum ad vos differam, ut eam auferatis. Ἵνα μὴ ἐλθὼν λύπην ἐπὶ λύπην σχῶ) Inter tot peri- cula, in quibus versatus sum, novum mœrorem ob seve- ritatem verborum aut rerum, qua uti cogar adversus inemendatos. Erat Apostolus talis, qualis describitur bo- nus Princeps: Qui, quoties sævus cogitur esse, dolet. Vide infra XII. 21. Ἀφ᾽ ὧν ἔδει με χαίρειν) Ex quorum profectu ego maximum percipere gaudium debebam: Τίς πατίρ᾽ αἰνέσει, εἰ μὴ ἐυδαίμονες ὑιοί; Πεποιθὼς ἐπὶ πάντας ὑμᾶς, ὅτι ἐμὴ χαρὰ πάντων ὑμῶν ἐστι) Ita bene de vobis sentio, ut credam, vos nihil mal- le, quàm ut gaudeam. Monstro viam, qua id consequa- mini, sicut בטח Hebræum solet post se trahere על, ita Græcum πέποιθα secum habet ἐπὶ, ut videre est secun- do Reg. XVIII. 21. & alibi.

De hac ipsa epistola intelligunt sane Chryso- stomus, Oecumenius, & Theophylactus. Sed rectius de priori epistolâ accipitur. Summam non ita malè complexus est Flacius in glossa: Excusat scriptionem prioris epistolæ, præsertim, quod ad ex- communicationem attinet, triplici ratione: Pri- mum quod ideo voluerit durius ad eos per literas scribere, ne haberet necesse coram dolens ac gemens aliquando asperius cum eis agere, quod etiam infra decimo tertio capite versu decimo inculcat: secun- dò versu sequente ait, quod idipsum summo cum animi sui dolore fecerit, perinde ac si propria mem- bra secaret vel ureret: tertiò, quod id studio demon- strande suæ solicitudinis de eis ac benevolentiæ fece- rit. Per τοῦτο ἀυτὸ respici videntur illa, quæ ha- bentur priori epistola cap. IV. 21. Quid vultis? in virga veniam ad vos, an in charitate & Spiritu mansuetudinis? Beza id ita accipit: Illud ipsum, nempe quod illi ac vobis molestiam attulit; agno- scens ad priorem epistolam referendum esse. Non ergò λύπη ἐπὶ λύπη pericula, in quibus versatus erat, spectat, & novum mœrorem, sed gravitatem potius tristitia, quam phrasis tristitia super tristi- tiam importat, si præsens ea crimina intueri debe- ret, refert, ne ob illos mœrore conficiatur, qui e- rant (esse certè debebant) præcipuum suum gau- dium, ut de Thessalonicensibus 1. epist. II. 20. scri- pserat: Vos estis nostra gloria & gaudium. Nec λύ- πην ἐπὶ λυπῇ habent codices, nisi paucissimi, refe- rente Erasmo & Beza, nec Syrus, nec Græci in- terpp. sed simpliciter λύπην: ὲ Phil. II. 27. id huc translatum censent. Excusat autem ita Apostolus prioris epistolæ asperitatem. Dicere enim poterant Corinthii, si nos tristitia afficere non vis, cur ergo tam acerbam ad nos scripsisti epistolam? In qua nos ut schismaticos, ut scortatores, avaros, contentiosos, in- cestuosos, omnis boni ordinis osores, & quid non? traducis. Annon hæc tua vehementia utramque nobis bilem moveat? hoccine est non contristare velle? Re- spondet itaque Apostolus: Hoc ipsum scripsi vobis, ut non cum venero, tristitiam super tristitiam habeam, de quibus oportuerat gaudere me, confidens omnibus vobis, quia gaudium meum omnium vestrum est v. 3. Non negat severitatem epistolæ, sed causam addit, Necessitas enim postulavit: Siquidem alia ratione verè, & in Domino gaudere non potuerint, quam re- motis hisce scandalis, quæ omne sincerum animi gau- dium turbant. Voluisse itaque se ipsos prius tristitia afficere, ut post actam pœnitentiam ipsi cum Aposto- lo sincero suo gaudio undiquaque implerentur; ut hic commodè B. Balduinus. Ita etiam illud πεποιθὼς Beza: Quin, inquit, omninò speravi fore, ut quæ mihi displicere intelligeretis, statim tolleretis: quia mea gaudia existimaris vobis esse communia. Theo- phylactus: Scripsi, inquit, confisus vos aliquando re- dituros in viam, idque mihi & lætitiæ fore. Non enim existimo animi mei affectus esse à vestris alienos, eo- que & illud adjeci, ne tristitiam habeam, nil pror- sus, quæ mea intersunt, sed quæ vestra, considerans. Habeo namque pro re certiori, & vos item lætari, cum hilarem me & latiorem videretis: nec minus, si vicem vestram dolentem, & vos dolituros.

## 2:4
Ver. 4.

(For out of much anguish and distress of heart) Συνοχὴ is anxiety, as in Luke XXI. ver. 25. Judges XI. ver. 3. συνέχεσθαι to be distressed, as in Luke XII. 50. Job XXX. 3.

(Through many tears) διὰ here is worth with. Thus δι᾿ ἀκριβείας to speak with precision in Aristotle.

Theophylact beautifully: For even some physician, who has cut or cauterized a son's wound, must needs grieve for two reasons: Both because the son is not affected with equal health, and because he is forced to cut off a part of the body for him. Otherwise, for the sake of the hoped-for and future health, when he does this, he rejoices, and willingly affects the son with pain by healing. Thus, therefore, I myself, when I see you subject to sins, am partly affected with grief, and partly with joy, because I see you grieving over what you have committed, and the hope of your amendment is offered to me.

(Not that you might be saddened) For this was not the primary will of Paul.

(But that you might know the love which I have more abundantly toward you) And here the locution is by the transposition of words: Then understand περισσοτέρως as more than other churches.

He does not compare the churches among themselves, which he certainly embraced all with distinguished love, but he testifies to the abundance of his love toward the Corinthians. Nor is the Enallage of the Comparative for the Superlative unusual. See Matt. XI. ver. 21. chap. XIIX. ver. 1. We confess, however, that it is not alien to piety to love one church more than another in a certain case, just as the love of parents is sometimes distributed unequally among their children.

Latin:

Vers. 4.

Ἐκ γὰρ πολλῆς συνοχῆς κὰι θλίψεως καρδίας) Συνοχὴ est anxietas, ut Luc. XXI. vers. 25. Judic. XI. vers. 3. συνέχεσθαι angi, ut Luc. XII. 50. Job. XXX. 3.

Διὰ πολλῶν δακρύων) διὰ hic valet cum. Sic δι᾿ ἀκριβείας λέγειν apud Aristotelem.

Pulchre Theophylactus: Nam & medicus quis- piam, qui filii præciderit vel adusserit plagam, dua- bus de causis doleat, necesse est: Cum quia filius va- letudine non æqua sit affectus, tum quia illi corporis partem præcidere cogatur. Alioqui speratæ & futu- ræ salutis gratiâ, cum id agit, lætatur, libensque & filium medendo dolore afficit. Sic itaque ipse, cum vos peccatis obnoxios videam, mœrore partim affi- cior, lætitia partim, quia vos ob commissa mæren- tes intueor, & emendationis spes mihi vestræ offer- tur.

Οὐχ ἵνα λυπηθῆτε) Non enim hoc erat προηγέμενον θέ- λημα Pauli.

Ἀλλὰ τὴν ἀγάπην, ἵνα γνῶτε, ἧν ἔχω περισσοτέρως εἰς ὑμᾶς) Et hic loquutio est per trajectionem vocum: Deinde περισσοτέρως intellige plus, quam Ecclesias alias.

Non Ecclesias comparat inter se, quas omnes utique insigni amore complexus est, sed abun- dantiam amoris erga Corinthios testatur. Non vero inusitata est Enallage Comparativi pro Su- perlativo. Vid. Matth. XI. vers. 21. cap. XIIX. vers. 1. Fatemur tamen, non esse à pietate alie- num, unam Ecclesiam certo casu plus diligere, quam aliam, quemadmodum parentum amor in- æqualiter interdum diffunditur in liberos.

## 2:5
Ver. 5.

(But if any has caused sadness) If any church has affected me with sadness. For this word is understood from the preceding, according to the meaning. But when he says εἴ τις indefinitely, he denotes the church of the Corinthians itself, as the following things show.

Οὐκ ἐμὲ λελύπηκεν, ἀλλ᾽ ἀπὸ μέρους) Here also ὅλη or ὅλος, if you understand λαὸς, is to be understood from the added member ἀπὸ μέρους, not the whole assembly has affected me with sadness, but some, for this is what ἀπὸ μέρους means, Romans XI. 25. above I. 14. Thus also μέρος τι 1 Cor. XI. 18.

Ἵνα μὴ ἐπιβαρῶ πάντας ὑμᾶς) As if he were saying: I express this for this reason, lest anyone think that each of you is being accused by me. Ἐπιβαρεῖν is to be a burden, as first in 1 Thessalonians II. v. 9. 2 Thessalonians III. v. 8. Moreover, an accusation is a certain imposition of a burden, just as the rebukes and threats of the Prophets are called מַשָּׂא, that is, a burden.

The words do not sound concerning the Church, but concerning a certain person who brought sadness to the Church. That ἐπιβαρῶ is not, as the Vulgate has it, joined with πάντας ὑμᾶς by the Syriac and Arabic, but with the verb λελύπηκεν, which Beza also rightly approves: Lest, he says, I burden, that is, lest I add a load to one already burdened by himself, which I rather desire to have removed. Meanwhile, we do not approve that Beza simply wishes to deny that Paul was caused sadness by the incestuous man. For he had already testified to the contrary by the commemoration of πολλῆς τῆς θλίψεως καὶ συνοχῆς καρδίας κὶ πολλῶν δακρύων: (for here too he speaks not of the present, after he had repented, but of the past, when he brought sadness) but with the Arabic and Greek interpreters, that this word μόνον, not me only did he affect with sadness, but ἀπὸ μέρους, in some measure, you all, is to be understood. Nor is it harsh or unusual for non to be taken for non solum. See Matth. X. vers. 20. Actor. V. vers. 4. Ephes. VI. vers. 12. Thus Chrysostom, with Erasmus not disapproving, says: He has not grieved me, but in part (that I may not be severe) all of you. For it was harsh to say: He has not only grieved me, but all of you with me; therefore he relieves him who had sinned by adding in part, as if mitigating what he says, in part, that is, in some measure. Nor are there wanting those who prefer to refer that ἀπὸ μέρους to others who were grieving, as if he were to say: The incestuous man was in part the cause of the sadness: for I do not wish to impose this burden on him alone, or to exaggerate his crime more heavily now, since otherwise he has been grieved more than enough, for now the matter is not about the acknowledgment of the crime, but about the absolution from the crime, as B. Balduinus holds here. To this intention of the Apostle, which is evident from verse 6, the sense which others add, and which ὁ Μακαρίτης includes, by no means corresponds: If I have been affected by any sadness through you, I do not impute that to you all, but primarily to the incestuous man, who caused troubles not only to me, but in part to you, while by your spirit and mine, as a diseased member, he was cut off from your Church. Aretius takes the word ἐπιβαρῶ passively, lest I be oppressed by excessive sadness, as if he were saying: God wills that the grief be shared, lest it be intolerable to me alone. Sharing makes an evil lighter. Which corresponds neither to the word, for that is active, nor to the context.

Latin:

Verf. 5.

Εἰ δέ τις λελύπηκεν) Si quæ Ecclesia me mœrore affecit. Hæc enim vox ex præcedentibus intelligitur, κατὰ τὸ ση- μαινόμενον. Cum autem indefinite dicit εἴ τις, notat ipsam Corinthiorum Ecclesiam, ut ostendunt sequentia.

Οὐκ ἐμὲ λελύπηκεν, ἀλλ᾽ ἀπὸ μέρους) Hic quoque ὅλη vel ὅλος, si λαὸς subaudias, intelligendum ex apposito membro ἀπὸ μέρους, non totus cœtus me mœstitia affe- cit, sed quidam, hoc enim est ἀπὸ μέρους Roman. XI. 25. supra I. 14. Sic & μέρος τι 1. Cor. XI. 18.

Ἵνα μὴ ἐπιβαρῶ πάντας ὑμᾶς) Quasi dicat: Hoc ideo exprimo, ne quis putet singulos vestrum à me accusari. Ἐπιβαρεῖν est oneri esse, ut primo 1. Thessalon. II. v. 9. 2. Thessalonic. III. vers. 8. Est autem accusatio oneris quædam impositio, sicut & Prophetarum objurgationes & minæ vocantur מַשָּׂא, id est, onus.

Non de Ecclesia; sed de persona quadam verba sonant, quæ tristitiam attulit Ecclesiæ. Illud ἐπιβαρῶ non ut vulgata, cum πάντας ὑμᾶς con- jungit Syrus & Arabs, sed cum verbo λελύπηκεν, quod etiam Beza merito probat: Ne, inquit, aggravem, id est, ne jam per se gravato onus adji- ciam, quod potius detractum cupio. Interim non probamus, quod Beza simpliciter Paulum negare vult, sibi tristitiam allatam esse per ince- stuosum. Nam contrarium testatus jam erat πολλῆς τῆς θλίψεως καὶ συνοχῆς καρδίας κὶ πολλῶν δακρύων commemoratione: (nam & hic non de præsente, postquam resipuit, sed præterito, cum tristitiam attulit, loquitur) sed cum Arabe & Græcis Interpp. hanc vocem μόνον non me tantum tristitia affecit, sed ἀπὸ μέρους, quadantenus, vos omnes subaudiendum esse. Nec durum aut in- solens est, non pro non solum accipi. Vid. Matth. X. vers. 20. Actor. V. vers. 4. Ephes. VI. vers. 12. Sic Chrysostomus, Erasmo non improbante, non me contristavit, sed ex parte (ne gravem) omnes. Durum enim erat dicere: Non solum me contri- stavit, sed vos omnes mecum, ideò sublevat eum, qui peccaverat, addens ex parte, velut mitigans, quod dicit, ex parte, hoc est, aliquo modo. Nec desunt, qui illud ἀπὸ μέρους, ad alios contristan- tes referre malint: quasi dicat: Incestuosus ex par- te causa tristitiæ fuit: Nolo enim soli hoc onus im- ponere, vel crimen ejus gravius jam exaggerare, cum alioquin plus satis sit contristatus, jam enim non de agnitione sceleris, sed de absolutione à sce- lere agitur, ut hic habet B. Balduinus. Cui in- tentioni Apostoli, quæ è vers. 6. patet, alius alio- rum, quem ὁ Μακαρίτης addit, sensus haudqua- quam convenit: Si qua per vos affectus sum tri- stitia, id non omnibus vobis imputo, sed imprimis incestuoso, qui non mihi saltem, sed ex parte vo- bis molestias creavit, dum vestro & meo spiritu, ut morbidum membrum ab Ecclesia vestra abscis- sus fuit. Aretius passivè vocem ἐπιβαρῶ acce- pit, ne opprimar nimia tristitia, quasi dicat: Deus vult communem esse dolorem, ne mihi soli intole- rabilis esset. Communicatio levius facit malum. Quæ nec verbo conveniunt, id enim activum est, nec contextui.

## 2:6
Vers. 6.

Ἱκανὸν τῷ τοιούτῳ) Hoc dicit velut digito indicans illum, qui maximum dolorem Paulo attulerat, do- ctus & dives, & novercæ maritus. He says this as if pointing with his finger to him who had brought the greatest grief to Paul, learned and rich, and the husband of his stepmother. Tertullian, in his work on modesty, does not wish for this to be about that man here. For he posits what is true in the early Church, that those who had fallen into adultery or something similar after baptism were never restored to communion: those guilty of other crimes, say incest with a stepmother, were nevertheless kept away longer than that interval of time between the former writing and this second one to the Corinthians. But he is mistaken, along with many others, in that he thinks this is about restoring communion, when it is about removing the disease which Satan had sent upon him at the prayers of the pious Corinthians.

This censure, which is usually performed by the presbytery in the Jewish manner. Canonical punishments are called ἐπιτιμίαι & ἐπιτίμια. It is found in that sense often in the acts of Councils, and in Chrysostom on the Priesthood. It suffices, he says, if one is abstained from communion & certain σκληραγωγίαι are joined to it. If he undertakes these, it will be permitted to pray for him. See John V. v. 16. For the presbytery had already been restored at Corinth and with it the discipline, which had ceased through the distractions of schisms.

Latin:

Vers. 6.

Ἱκανὸν τῷ τοιούτῳ) Hoc dicit velut digito indicans illum, qui maximum dolorem Paulo attulerat, do- ctus & dives, & novercæ maritus. Tertullianus de pu- dicitia non vult hic de illo homine agi. Ponit enim quod verum est in prima Ecclesia post baptismum in adulterium aut simile quid prolapsos nunquam ad communionem re- stitutos: Aliorum criminum reos, puta incestus in nover- cam, diutius tamen abstentos, quam fuit intervallum illud temporis intra scriptionem priorem, & hanc alteram ad Corinthios. Sed in eo cum multis aliis fallitur, quod agi hic putat de restituenda communione, cum agatur de au- ferendo morbo, quem ei Satanas ad preces piorum Co- rinthiorum immiserat.

Ἡ ἐπιτιμία αὕτη, ἡ ὑπὸ πλειόνων) Castigatio illa, quæ à presbyterio fieri solet more Judaico. Pœnæ Canonicæ vocantur ἐπιτιμίαι & ἐπιτίμια. Reperitur eo sensu sæpe in Conciliorum actis, & apud Chrysostomum de Sacerdo- tio. Sufficit, inquit, si abstineatur à communione & σκληραγωγίαι quædam ei adjunguntur. Eas si suscipiat li- cebit pro eo precari. Vide Joh. V. v. 16. Restitutum enim jam erat Corinthi presbyterium & cum eo disciplina, quæ per schismatum distractiones cessaverant.

## 2:7
Vers. 7.

So that on the contrary you should rather forgive and comfort) Μᾶλλον is missing in the Manuscript. But I would wish 'I desire' to be understood here, and τοὐναντίον is opposed to that which might seem to be a complaint against all, as if he were saying, I do not accuse you now as being too remiss. Rather, I urge you of your own accord toward leniency. To forgive and to comfort in this place is to pray to GOD, that that sickness may cease. We have noted that to loose sins is also said of private individuals at Matt. XVIII. 18. χαρίζεσθαι here corresponds to מָחַל. See Esth. IV. v. 32.

Lest such a one be swallowed up by excessive sorrow) καταπίνειν here is בָּלַע, which is indeed properly to absorb, but figuratively to destroy in any way, ἀπολλύειν, in which way that בָּלַע is also sometimes translated. If to the sickness there is added the torment of the soul, death can easily follow from it. Origen on Psalm XXXVII thinks that this passage deals with that husband of a stepmother.

Beza gathers from the word ἱκανὸν that the incestuous man had not been excommunicated by the Corinthians. But that this incestuous man had not been delivered to Satan, he says, but when he had produced an example of notable repentance in the presbytery (for these are they whom Paul calls τοὺς πλείονας in this place) the Corinthians, until they had signified that to Paul, had kept him suspended, appears from the fact that the Apostle says that that censure is sufficient. For if he had been delivered to Satan, he could not have progressed further, not even if they had wished it. Then he also thinks that this is clear from the word κεχάρισμαι, by which is signified a certain remission of the highest right, which they later called an indulgence, and with the greatest error, because what was provided by the ancient canons concerning satisfaction before the Church and the testimony of repentance, was accommodated to satisfaction for sins before God. But which arguments do not prove this. For that ἱκανὸν after the things which Paul had ordered, having been dispatched, could rightly be applied, namely that those things are sufficient, and now it remains that he be received back into favor. Ἱκανὸν, says Aretius, I refer to the first time, that it is sufficient to have been excluded for so long. Then to the authority of the Church, that the authority of the Church and of the Apostle Paul is sufficient for restoring the excluded brother. Χαρίσασθαι, however, concerning forgiveness after repentance has been performed, which indeed followed excommunication, is likewise rightly applied. Concerning a specimen of repentance produced in the presbytery, nothing is found here. Nor is ὑπὸ τῶν πλειόνων the same as 'by the presbytery,' which at that time did not consist of many there, but 'by the Church,' in whose name that censure was done. But what kind that was, we learn from 1 Cor. V. But why could it not be said to be done by the many, which was done before the Church and in the name of the Church? Although indeed the incestuous man had been delivered to Satan for the destruction of the flesh; yet it is not to be thought with Grotius that the Church wished to obtain for him by prayers the infliction of diseases, which is not from Satan, but from God, or certainly to be obtained from God by prayers, if it is to be sought through prayers, nor is that delivery to be opposed to exclusion from the communion of the Church, since this leaven had to be purged out entirely, lest the whole lump be infected: And the Corinthians ought not to have been mixed with such, as they were warned in 1 epist. V. 7. 19, nay rather they are now reminded about reception into favor, so that they may receive him again into the communion of the Church, lest he be swallowed up by more abundant sorrow. Necessarily (he says), with Theophylact as interpreter, is he both to be received and to be raised up by consolation, lest, as if seized by some more savage beast or storm, he be swallowed up by grief, and come at last through desperation, just as Judas did to the noose. Or that he might throw himself headlong, as one who does not tolerate the pain from a harsher and immoderate punishment, and goes headlong into some greater crime. Theophylact also notes the force of the word τοῖῦτος. He did not say 'to that fornicator,' but 'to him who is of such a kind,' just as he did in the previous epistle, in which he did not even wish to explain his name. In this one, however, although pardon is given, he makes no mention of the offense and crime, establishing that we should behave more leniently toward the mourning and the oppressed. He acts otherwise with the stubborn, whose names he does not keep silent, so that they may be avoided by others, as is evident from the example of Hymenaeus, Philetus, Alexander, and Phigellus. The word ἐπιτιμίας for the most part denotes a rebuke joined with infamy, such as was that which was done in public by the many, namely by the Church, which had publicly noted that crime, and thus had delivered him to Satan, excluded from all commerce, as here B. Balduinus, with whom Aretius, Erasmus, Estius, Cornelius à Lapide, Flacius, and others agree. Nor do Origen and most others take the present passage only concerning the incestuous man. Ambrose book 1 de poenit. last chapter. Pacianus in epist. 3 to Symphron. Augustine book III against the epistle of Parm. chapter 1. Gregory the Great book XXXIII Moral. 8. The little arguments which Tertullian, having sailed for his heresy, brought forward to the contrary, are of no moment.

Latin:

Vers. 7.

Ὥστε τοὐναντίον μᾶλλον ὑμᾶς χαρίσασθαι καὶ παρακαλέσαι) Μᾶλλον deest in Manuscripto. Subintelligitur autem hic velim, & τοὐναντίον opponitur ei, quod videri posset de omni- bus queri, quasi dicat, nihil vos accuso nunc ut nimium remissos. Imo ad lenitatem ultro hortor. Condonari & solari hoc loco est DEUM orare, ut morbus ille desinat. Solvere peccata etiam de privatis dici notavimus ad Matth. XVIII. 18. χαρίζεσθαι hic respondet מָחַל. Vide Esth. IV. v. 32.

Μὴ πρὸς τῇ περισσοτέρᾳ λύπῃ καταποθῇ ὁ τοιοῦτος) κατα- πίνειν hic est בָּלַע, quod proprie quidem est absorbere, translate vero quovis modo perdere, ἀπολλύειν, quomodo & interdum vertitur illud בָּלַע. Si ad morbum accedat animi cruciatus, facile inde mors sequi potest. De illo nover- cæ marito hic agi censet & Origenes ad Psalm. XXXVII.

Beza ex voce ἱκανὸν colligit, non fuisse ince- stuosum à Corinthiis excommunicatum. Non fuisse verò, inquit, hunc incestuosum Satanæ tradi- tum, sed cum insignis resipiscentiæ exemplum in pres- byterio edidisset (hi sunt enim, quos τοὺς πλείονας ap- pellat Paulus hoc loco) Corinthios, donec istud Paulo significassent, suspensum illum tenuisse, apparet ex eo, quod dicit Apostolus istam ἐπιτιμίαν sufficere. Nam si Satanæ traditus fuisset, ulterius progredi non po- tuisset, ne si voluissent quidem. Deinde id etiam li- quere arbitratur ex verbo κεχάρισμαι, quo significa- tur remissio quædam de summo jure, quod indulgen- tiam postea vocarunt, & maximo cum errore, quod de satisfactione apud Ecclesiam, & resipiscentiæ testi- monio veteribus canonibus fuit cautum, ad satisfa- ctionem pro peccatis apud Deum fuit accommòda- tum. Quæ verò argumenta id non probant. Nam il- lud ἱκανὸν post ea quæ jusserat Paulus, expedita, re- ctè adhiberi poterat, ea nempe sufficere, nunc resta- re, ut iterum in gratiam recipiatur. Ἱκανὸν, inquit Aretius, refero ad tempus primum, quod sufficiat tamdiu fuisse exclusum. Deinde ad autoritatem Ec- clesiæ, quod sufficiens sit autoritas Ecclesiæ & Aposto- li Pauli ad restituendum fratrem exclusum. Χαρίσα- σθαι autem de condonatione post actam pœnitentiam, quæ vero sequuta est excommunicationem, rectè itidem adhibetur. De resipiscentiæ specimine in presbyterio edito nihil hic invenitur. Nec verò ὑπὸ τῶν πλειόνων idem est, quod à presbyterio, quod tum non multis ibi constabat, sed ab Ecclesia, cu- jus nomine illa ἐπιτιμία fiebat. Qualis autem illa fuerit è 1. Cor. V. discimus. Cur verò non à pluribus facta dici possit, quæ coram Ecclesia & nomine Ec- clesiæ facta? Quanquam verò Satanæ traditus in- cestuosus fuerit ad interitum carnis; non tamen cum Grotio censendum, quod Ecclesia precibus ob- tinere ei voluerit morborum immissionem, quæ non à Satana, sed à Deo est, aut certè à Deo precibus obtinenda, si per preces expetenda, neque oppo- nenda ea traditio exclusioni ab Ecclesiæ commu- nione, quum expurgandum omnino fuerit hoc fermentum, ne tota massa inficeretur: Et commi- sceri cum talibus non debuerint Corinthii, uti 1. epist. V. 7. 19. monebantur, imò ideò nunc de re- ceptione in gratiam commonefiunt, ut scilicet de- nuo in communionem Ecclesiæ eum recipiant, ne abundantiori tristitiâ absorbeatur. Necessario (in- quit), interprete Theophylacto, est ille & suscipien- dus & consolatione erigendus, ne veluti ab efferatio- re aliqua bellua vel procella arreptus, absorbeatur mœrore, veniatque tandem per desperationem, quem- admodum & Judas ad laqueos. Vel se præcipitem saltu ferat, utpote qui ex acriori & immoderata ca- stigatione dolorem non toleret, & eat in scelus aliquod majus præceps. Notat etiam Theophylactus vim vo- cis τοῖῦτος. Non dixit fornicanti illi, sed ei, qui ejus- modi est, quemadmodum & in superiori epistola fe- cit, in qua neque illius nomen voluit explicare. In hac vero etsi venia data, nullam tamen facit delicti & sceleris mentionem, instituens, uti erga mœrentes & oppressos clementius nos geramus. Aliter agit cum pertinacibus, quorum nomina non tacet, ut ab aliis caveantur, ut exemplo Hymenæi, Phyleti Alexandri & Phigelli constat. Vox ἐπιτιμίας ple- rumque notat increpationem cum infamia conjun- ctam, qualis erat, quæ in publico facta à pluribus, ab Ecclesia nempe, quæ scelus illud publice nota- verat, & sic eum Satanæ tradiderat exclusum omni commercio, ut hic B. Balduinus, cui Aretius, E- rasmus, Estius, Cornelius à Lapide, Flacius & alii consonant. Nec de incestuoso Origenes tantum, sed etiam plerique alii accipiunt locum præsen- tem. Ambrosius l. 1. de pœnit. cap. ult. Pacianus in epist. 3. ad Symphron. Augustinus lib. III. contra epist. Parm. cap. 1. Gregorius M. libr. XXXIII. Moral. 8. Ratiunculæ, quas in contrarium Tertul- lianus, hæresi suæ velificatus, adduxit, nullius sunt momenti.

## 2:8
Vers. 8. Therefore I beseech you to confirm love toward him) Κυρῶσαι is properly to give to some thing its own legitimate form and thus to make it ratified and firm; here by translation it is to show by deed. For he who does this, in some way ratifies what he had in his mind. But the deed which is required here is the prayers of the whole Church for him who is gravely afflicted.

On the word κυρῶσαι, Erasmus is more correct: That it is almost equivalent to saying, see to it that charity toward him has weight and authority. For he speaks as if to judges and an assembly, by whose votes he wishes him to be absolved, who had been delivered to Satan. For κυρία signifies an assembly in which magistrates are created, which the Latins call comitia, and a day appointed for the sake of some matter, and the right of doing something. Moreover, the Greeks call an authentic document κύριον, according to the authorities Hesychius and Suidas. It seems to me that the opinion which had prevailed in the votes was called κυρία, whence the proverb, αὕτη κυρία. Κῦρος likewise signifies effective proof or weight, and the authority of a sentence, which is called κύρωσις.
