In it, therefore, not only the elements of the world, but also the weak and beggarly elements are called so, v. 9, and Christians are deterred from their servitude as from idolatry. But Crocius himself notes wrongly with Pareus: The Apostle, he says, understands the ceremonies of the law — Crocius — not only, but the whole legal pedagogy, and therefore also the moral law, by which He terrified the Fathers and as it were compelled them by the threat of punishments and the fear of the curse.

For this office of the moral law has no end, nor did it regard the Fathers only, nor was it the Apostle's purpose to treat of it here. But he was speaking of tutors, whose authority lasted until the προθεσμίαν τοῦ πατρός (appointed time of the father), so that he might establish the difference between the time and state of Christians under the New Testament, and the time and state of the Israelitish people under the Old Testament, against the Pseudo-Apostles who were abolishing it, and might root out that Judaical error.

The Apostle dealt with the fact that they were rightly Jews: just as he had taught, having concluded the chapter, that all men were shut up under the law. The trope of the Apostle, says the blessed Luther in his former Commentary, fol. 32, must be preserved. For to be under the law is not that which is to live in the time and by the decree of the law. Thus neither Job, nor Naaman the Syrian, nor the woman of Sarepta of Sidon were under the law, but it is to be a debtor to the law, not to have wherewith you may fulfill it, and to be guilty of all the punishments set by the law. ἐξαγορασμὸς is not to be explained as an improper and metaphorical redemption, as the Socinians wish, to whom Grotius does not here dissent, but as a true, satisfactory, and meritorious redemption: because that word is always understood in the scriptures of a true redemption which is made by a price, and is explained by λύτρωσιν, which introduces λύτρον or the price of redemption, Matt. XX. 28, Mark X. 45, 1 Tim. II. 6, 1 Pet. I. 19, Rom. III. 25. Then Christ redeemed us, who were under the law, when he was made under the law for us by perfectly fulfilling it, Matt. V. 17, and by sustaining its curse, Gal. III. 13. In whatever way, therefore, we were under the law, in that same way he also subjected himself to the law, that he might redeem us from the law. But we were under the law, both as to the rigid and absolute obedience to be rendered to it, and as to the punishment to be paid on account of the curse of the law for committed sins. Therefore he also subjected himself to the law in that manner. Which is certainly not a bare or simple liberation but a meritorious and satisfactory redemption. But more has been said about these things in the Socinismo Profligato. Furthermore, that ἐξαγορασμὸς concerns not just a few men, or Jews only, who were under the ceremonial law, but all who have been, are, or ever will be. Because all are under the law, as many as are propagated from Adam, equally as Adam. Compare Romans III. ch. v. 9 and 19. But those who are under the law, they have been redeemed by Christ, which the Apostle affirms here. Concerning this former end, the blessed Hunnius on this passage: The Son of GOD, he says, was the Lord of the law, who did not once bring the law upon himself on Mount Sinai, but upon others. He, to procure the work of our redemption, subjected himself to the law in assumed flesh, so that both by obedience perfectly rendered to the law, and by its curse derived upon himself, he might free us both from the curse of the moral law, and from the forced compliance with the same, which is placed in the oldness of the letter, and from the yoke of the Levitical law and the burden of Mosaic ceremonies, and thus assert us from servitude into the liberty of the sons of God. For this was the end of the mission of the Son of GOD into this world, our redemption, which is soon followed by another clearly divine benefit, ὑοθεσία, or adoption into sons, with every right and privilege that depends upon it.

The other end, therefore, is designated by these words: "Ἵνα τὴν ὑοθεσίαν ἀπολάβωμεν," that we might receive the adoption: Or as Erasmus rendered it: That we might receive the right of the adoption of sons. Because we are not only redeemed from the execration of the law and the exaction of rigorous observation, but also the paternal grace of GOD and ὑοθεσία has been acquired for us, so that we may be adopted into the sons of GOD: So that we who are children of wrath may become children of grace and children of God, be regenerated from God, and be adopted by God, and enjoy the grace and favor of God, as his beloved sons, and be constituted heirs of eternal salvation. This adoption, according to the blessed Feuerborn, fascic. V. Disp. 1. §. 59, here denotes not only the faithful possession of the blessing and heavenly inheritance obtained for us by the merit of Christ, which is common to us with the pious of the Old Testament, but also the free use, void of Levitical shadows and Mosaic ceremonial constitutions. Which until now was lacking to the pious men of the Old Testament, insofar as they were δεδουλωμένοι ὑπὸ τὰ στοιχεῖα τοῦ κόσμου v. 3. Thus especially Pareus: Indeed the Fathers, he says, were also sons and heirs: But as little children serving under the yoke of the law, differing nothing from servants, as the Apostle had said. Therefore they did not receive the adoption. But we, after the redemption was made, have received the adoption: because after the Father's προθεσμία was finished, the inheritance was handed over to us, as if now adults, emancipated from tutors, as it were into our hands. Adoption, therefore, here does not so much signify the very calling into sons, as if GOD finally adopted us after them, as it signifies the possession of adoption and the handing over of the inheritance: Therefore he does not say, that we might be adopted, but that we might receive the adoption, namely to be freely used and enjoyed, which the fathers indeed had, but by right rather than by use, in that they were compelled to serve under the guardianship of the law. The word ἀπολάβωμεν, which the old [translator] rendered 'we might receive back,' does not signify any debt or merit of ours, but an induction, as it were, into our own property. The Apostle remains in the metaphor. For heirs who are little children, after the Father's προθεσμία has passed, having grown up, demand the inheritance from the tutors, they ἀπολαμβάνουσιν, they receive: Thus, he says, we adult heirs receive the inheritance once entrusted to tutors into our right, into our hands. In sum: By this word he now says what he intends by the whole similitude of tutors; that this benefit has happened to us over the fathers by the redemption of Christ: that while both indeed were sons and heirs: They, as little children, served under the guardianship of the law, we, as adults, emancipated from the yoke of the law and admitted into the inheritance of adoption. Thus he establishes an illustrious distinction between the Old and New Testament: and opposes our liberty to the servitude of the ancients. So also Crocius: They (the ancients) did not enjoy the liberty of emancipated sons. The Son of God came sent into the flesh, that we might receive it. Not that we might finally become sons, but that we might be sent into the possession of the inheritance as if handed over by tutors, and thereby receive the fruit of adoption. In which manner this Pauline sentence seems to be accepted, as if the abrogation of legal ceremonies were primarily attributed here to the ἐξαγορασμῷ or redemption of Christ.

It may, however, be a matter of doubt whether the abrogation of them, and the emancipation from the guardianship of the Levitical laws, should properly be ascribed to the λύτρῳ [ransom] of the blood of Christ, both because the price of redemption, which this ἐξαγορασμὸς [redemption] in this place by the confession of all introduces, had to be paid on account of captivity under the power of Satan, and wrath, and divine justice, so that satisfaction might be made to divine justice, and not truly for that reason properly, so that we might be freed from the yoke of ceremonies: and also because the Levitical ceremonies for the most part foreshadowed the expiation made by the blood of Christ, and therefore there was no need for them to be abdicated through ἐξαγορασμὸν [redemption], but upon Christ arriving in the fullness of time, as the substance itself and the body and the antitype of the ceremonies, that shadow fled of its own accord, and those typical things ceased of themselves; nor did they formerly foreshadow the ἀντίλυτρον [ransom] and ἐξαγορασμὸν [redemption] and ἱλασμὸν [propitiation] of Christ, and therefore, having been instituted on account of Christ and the benefits of Christ, they seem conveniently to be called meritorious things taken away from us by the price of the payment and redemption of Christ: and also because that economy of the Old Testament properly expired through the πλήρωμα [fullness] of time, since it ought to have lasted only until that point, which the προθεσμίαν τοῦ πατρὸς [appointed time of the Father] introduces; but it was not the case that a price had to be paid to divine justice in order for it to expire. Neither Crocius nor even Pareus himself in such a prolix διηγήσει [narrative] could explain how the inheritance was, as it were, delivered into our HANDS after the death of Christ and through his redemption, namely the inheritance of eternal life, which they themselves understand: or how the fathers [held] it by right or how the fathers [held it] rather by right, rather than they had use of; but to us the use of it has fallen by the redemption of Christ before the Fathers, and we have been brought into the inheritance of adoption.

For did the Fathers have a right only to the inheritance of eternal life, and were they not admitted to the inheritance itself? Do the faithful under the New Testament have that inheritance in this life by actual use, or if they are said to have it after this life, do they have it before the Fathers? And are not the benefits of the redemption made through the death of Christ common to the whole world and to all men even under the Old Testament, both as regards the acquisition and as regards the divine intention of communication, and even as regards the benefit of adoption itself? Therefore the Apostle seems to return to his principal scope, as one he never neglects, but always presses, that the redemption of those who were under the curse of the law, made through the ransom of one Christ, may be explained, that we might use the adoption: and so also that we might obtain the inheritance of eternal life or salvation, and consequently even justification solely through faith in Christ's redemption. Yet because he was made under the law, not only by undergoing the curse of the law due to us, but also by rendering obedience to the universal law, under which the ceremonial is also comprehended, as far as the observation of the same could fall upon him, therefore by the power of this subjection under the law we are made partakers of the righteousness and obedience of the same through faith, and are thus justified, and we have no need for the sake of obtaining justification of the observation of the law, whether moral or ceremonial, which itself also expired in him, because the appointed time was fulfilled, and the fullness of time had arrived.

And this is what B.

Luther most urges here as the principal theme of the Apostle concerning the present aphorism of the Apostle: which shines in this treatment like gold and a most precious gem. To which also contributes the inference of the Apostle elucidated by Theophylact in this way: Wherefore since we are sons and heirs, not of something vain or frivolous, but of GOD himself, and the inheritance is to be shared by us with the only-begotten, why are we made servants, and why do we plainly repudiate that which had led us into adoption, and why do we become vacant of the law?

B.

Luther in his Commentary says: He himself, he says, is the Lord of the law, therefore the law has no right over him, it cannot accuse him, because he is the Son of GOD.

Since therefore he was not under the law, he subjected himself to the law of his own accord. There the law exercised all its tyranny upon him, as it did upon us. But it accuses and terrifies us, subjects us to sin, wrath, death, and condemns us to its judgment. And it does this by right, because we are all sinners, and naturally children of wrath. On the contrary, CHRIST did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth, therefore he owed nothing to the law.

And yet the law raged against one so innocent, holy, just, and blessed, just as it did against us sinners, the cursed, and the damned, and much more atrociously. For it accused him as a blasphemer and seditious person, it made him guilty before GOD of all the sins of the whole world, finally it so saddened and terrified him that he sweated blood, and lastly by its own sentence condemned him to death, and that of the cross. This is truly a wonderful duel, where the law of the creature thus engages with the Creator, and exercises all its tyranny beyond all right upon the Son of GOD, which it exercised upon us children of wrath. Because therefore the law sinned so horribly and impiously against its GOD, it is called to justice and accused. There CHRIST says, Mistress law, most powerful and cruel empress and Queen of the whole human race!

What have I committed, that you have accused, terrified, and condemned me, the innocent one? Here the law, by which it had previously condemned and killed all men, since it has nothing with which to defend or purge itself, is in turn so condemned and killed, that it loses its right, not only in CHRIST (against whom it raged and killed unjustly) but also in all who believe in him. And further: By this victory of his, therefore, CHRIST has driven the law from our conscience, so that it can no longer confound us in the sight of GOD, drive us to despair, and condemn us.

It does not indeed cease to show sin, to accuse, and to terrify. But the conscience, apprehending this word of the Apostle, Christ has redeemed us from the law, is raised up by faith, and conceives consolation. Finally, with a certain holy pride it insults the law, saying: I fear not your terrors and threats, because you have crucified the Son of GOD, and you have crucified him with the greatest injury. Therefore the sin which you have committed against him is irremissible, you have lost your right, and now for the future you are not only conquered and strangled by Christ, but also by me who believe in him, to whom he has given this victory. Thus the law has perished for us forever, provided we remain in Christ.

Thanks therefore to GOD, who has given us the victory through our Lord JESUS CHRIST. These things also pertain to this, that we are justified by faith alone: Because when this duel was fought between the law and Christ, no works or merits of ours intervened at all, but CHRIST alone was there, who, having put on our person, subjected himself to the law, and with the greatest innocence sustained all its tyranny. Therefore the law, like a thief and sacrilegious murderer of the Son of GOD, loses its right, and deserves to be condemned, so that wherever CHRIST is, or at least is named, it is forced to depart far away and flee from this name, as the Devil is forced to flee from the cross. Wherefore we believers are free from the law through CHRIST, who triumphed over it by himself.

And so this glorious triumph won for us by Christ is apprehended by no works, but by faith alone. Therefore faith alone justifies. Item: Thus CHRIST, a divine and human person, born of GOD from eternity, from a virgin in time, did not come to establish the law, but that he might feel and conquer its terrors in the highest degree, and by that means take them away.

He was not made a Doctor of the law, but a Disciple obedient to the law, that by this his obedience he might redeem those who were under the law. These things are entirely alien to the doctrine of the Papists, who have made CHRIST a legislator, and indeed one more severe than Moses. Paul teaches the exact opposite here, namely that God cast his Son under the law, that is, forced him to bear the judgment and curse of the law, sin, death, etc. For Moses, the minister of sin, wrath, and death, took, bound, condemned, and killed CHRIST, this he himself endured. Christ therefore behaved himself toward the law passively, not actively. He is not therefore a legislator, or a Judge according to the law, but in that while he subjected himself to the law, bearing its condemnation, he freed us from its curse. But that Christ in the Gospel delivers precepts and teaches the law, or rather interprets it, this does not pertain to the place concerning justification, but to good works.

Furthermore, it is not the proper office of Christ, for which he chiefly came into the world, to teach the law, but it is accidental. Of which kind was also this, that he healed the sick, raised the dead, benefited the unworthy, comforted the afflicted, etc. These are indeed glorious and divine works and benefits, but they are not proper to Christ. For the Prophets also taught the law, and performed miracles. But CHRIST is GOD and man, who, fighting with the law, suffered its extreme cruelty and tyranny. condemned our most hostile enemy, the law, and took it out of the way, so that it can no longer condemn and kill believers. Wherefore it is the true and proper office of Christ to struggle with the law, sin, and the death of the whole world, and to struggle in such a way that he might endure these things, and by enduring might conquer and abolish them in himself, and in this way liberate believers from the law and all evils.

All these things B.

Luther. Wherefore he does not explain υἱοθεσίαν [adoption] as the enjoyment of freedom from the ceremonial law, but as the adoption into the sons of GOD, proper to all believers of all times, fol. 101.

That we might receive the adoption of sons, that is, divine sonship, Paul copiously explains and adorns this place in Gen. XXII.

In thy seed &c.

Above he called that blessing, supported by the seed of Abraham, the promise of the Spirit, life, redemption from the law, the testament, &c. Here he calls it sonship and the inheritance of eternal life. The word blessing encompasses all these things. For when the curse—which is sin, death, &c.—is removed by this blessed seed, a blessing succeeds in its place, that is, righteousness, life, and all good things.

From these, the Grotian glosses can now be easily estimated.

Who ineptly first introduces the Firstborn, to whom, in the absence of the father, the care pertained. For GOD the Father is never and nowhere absent, who is everywhere always present. Nor is the Son of GOD a firstborn as if from many, since he is said to be sent in this place; but he is μονογενής, only- and fully-begotten, inasmuch as he is the only one born from the essence of the Father and that unique Son of GOD coessential and ὁμοούσιος [consubstantial] with the Father.

But the Son of GOD being sent is wrongly explained as that which becomes an extraordinary power given to him by the Father. For the mission took place by the arrival into the world and the incarnation of the Son: which formally is not a communication of divine power, let alone an extraordinary one, I know not of what kind.

And what care is appropriate for a firstborn over brothers placed under tutors, who are subject to him, not to the firstborn brother, the ἀρχή τῆς προθεσμίας πατρός [the beginning of the father's appointed time].

CHRIST is not subject to the law because he was born a Jew, or by reason of his birth, but because he willed to be our Redeemer, or by reason of spontaneous subjection. He truly liberated those subject to the law, not only the Jews, but all of us: And not from vices, and from the obligation of the law, but from the punishments of sin and sins, and from the condemnation and rigorous exaction of the law.

But by υἱοθεσίαν [adoption], the permission of the father is understood, by which sons are permitted to have certain things of their own, and to do certain things by their own judgment, namely, while obedience to the Father remains, but without special precepts (which gloss of Grotius is truly new and unrefined), how will it be proved?

The πέτασις [digression] was not dealing with a living father here, if one wishes to refer to it; but with a deceased Father, when he refers to free sons placed under the power of tutors. But those who are exempt from that are not only permitted to have certain things of their own, but enjoy the full liberty of inheritance. What, therefore, those things mean in the ἀποδόσει [application] I confess I do not understand, namely, that the sons of GOD, or those who have received υἱοθεσίαν, only have certain things of their own: what likewise those things mean, that they are permitted to do certain things by their own judgment.

If one considers the freedom from the obligation of ceremonies, or ceremonial laws, it will have to be denied that the ancients were sons of GOD, or had received adoption, inasmuch as they did not have that freedom: But not even of us in the New Testament is it to be said that we are permitted to do certain things by our own judgment in those matters which pertain to religion, GOD, and salvation.

Since ἐθελοθρησκεία [will-worship] of GOD is disapproved, and GOD is worshipped in vain by them, Matt. XV.

Verse.

Latin:

Vers. 5. Ἵνα τὲς ὑπὸ νόμον ἐξαγοράσῃ) Ut legi subditos liberaret a vitiis primum, deinde & ab obligatione legis, οἱ ὑπὸ νόμον, Judaei & Proselyti, 1. Cor. IX. 21.

Ἵνα τὴν ὑοθεσίαν ἀπολάβωμεν) Pariter scilicet Judaei & gentes sublato vallo, quo dispescebantur. Sicut filios pueros comparaverat servis, ita persequens hanc similitudinem ὑοθεσίαν vocat illud permissum patris, quo permittuntur filii, res suas quasdam habere, & suo arbitratu res quasdam agere, nempe manente in Patrem obsequio, sed sine specialibus praescriptis. Vide quae dicta ad Luc. XVII. 10.

Explicat jam Apostolus προθεσμίαν τῦ πατρὸς verbis luculentis, ὅτε δὲ ἦλθε τὸ πλήρωμα τῦ χρόνε. Plenitudo temporis dicitur, quia in arcano praedefinitum a Patre tempus (προθεσμίας) tunc impletum fuit, cum scilicet missus est a Deo Filius, natus ex muliere, factus sub lege, ut redimeret eos, qui sub lege erant, ut ea redemptione, quae veteribus ceu pupillis sub elementis mundi figurata erat, reapse praestita, cessaret illa servitus, & ὑοθεσίαν plene consequeremur. Jus & ἀξίωμα filiorum, qui non amplius sub tutela sua jam emancipati sunt, & plena libertate filiorum DEI, cum libertate ab externis illis elementis & servitute sub tutoribus frueremur. Temporis plenitudo per consuetum Ebraismum est plenum seu completum tempus. Quod nomine dierum posteriorum venit Mich. IV. 1. & tempus dicitur acceptum, ac dies salutis 2. Cor. VI. 1. annus beneplaciti Esa. LXI. 1. de quo vid. Dan. IX. Hagg. II.

Deus Pater dicitur misisse Filium, quia ipse principium & origo est Filii, qui ab aeterno ipsum genuit, nuit, sed in plenitudine temporis eundem misit. Filius non tantum primogenitus, sed μονογενής foli- & unigenitus missus est in mundum, factus hominis filius, ut nos filii DEI efficeremur. Missio enim ista facta in incarnatione Johan. XIV. cap. I. vers. 14. Job. III. v. 16. non vero in legatione, quæ post baptismum suscepta, ut Sociniani volunt, quo de vide, quæ de Praexist. Filii Dei contra ipsos tractata. Non ergo emissio est localis aut separativa, quia Filius semper est in Patre, & Spiritu Patris Johan.

I. vers. 18. cap. IIX. vers. 16. 29. cap. XIV. vers. 10. cap. XVI. vers. 32. & unum est cum Patre Johan. X. vers. 30. I. Johan. V. vers. 7. Non servilis missio, quia missio Filii Dei unigeniti & proprii. Sed ut August. ad CHRISTUM tract. 36. in Johann. Missio tua incarnatio tua est. Et ut Lyranus: Ideo missum intelligere debemus, quia ex illo incomprensibili, inenarrabilique secreto majestatis profundæ Dei Verbum non solum ubi se exinaniret, sed etiam cum habitaret in nobis.

Augustinus libr. IV. de Trinit. cap. 20. de eo ita habet: Secundum hoc jam potest intelligi, non tantum ideo dici missus Filius, quia Verbum caro factum est, sed ideo missus, ut Verbum caro fieret, & per præsentiam corporalem illa, quæ scripta sunt, operaretur: id est, ut non tantum homo missus intelligatur, quod Verbum caro factum est, sed & Verbum missum, ut homo fieret: quia non secundum imparem potestatem, vel substantiam, vel aliquid, quod DEO Patri non sit æquale, missus est, sed secundum id, quod Filius a Patre est, non Pater a Filio.

Ideo additur, quod missus γενόμενον ἐκ γυναικὸς factus ex muliere, quod in incarnatione factum: Cum in utero matris conceptus, & ex ea natus est, secundum carnem. Unde dicitur missus in similitudine carnis peccati Johan. IIX. vers. 3. Verbum ἐξαπέστειλε non caret emphasi. Nam innuitur & missus e cœlo, & inæstimabili luce in has terras, quod alias voce πέμπειν exprimitur Job.

IV. 34. cap. V. 23. 24. 37. c. VI. 37. 38. 40. 44. cap. VI. 16. 18. 28. 33. In quibusdam Codicibus legitur γεννώμενον natum. Ast plerique nostræ lectioni favent, & sic natus est ex virgine Maria, ut ex ea factus, id est, ex substantia ejus vere formatus fit juxta carnem, ac proinde nobis vere fit ὁμοούσιος, nisi quod non generatus ex virili semine, sed a Spiritu sancto creatus & formatus ex substantia matris virginis.

Quia enim non ex humano semine concreta est caro Domini in utero virginis & corpus effecta, sed effectu & virtute Spiritus sancti, ideo dicit Apostolus factum non natum, interprete Lyrano. Aliud enim est semine admixto & sanguine coagulato generare: Aliud est non permixtione sed virtute procreari. Possunt enim homines generare liberos, sed non facere. Thom. apud B. Glassium duos errores duos ait, 1.

Valentini, dicentis CHRISTUM non sumpsisse corpus de virgine, sed attulisse illud de cœlo, & per beatam virginem, sicut per fistulam seu canalem transivisse. Sed contra Apostolus hic dicit: Factus ex muliere. Hæc autem præpositio Ex causam materialem designat. 2. Nestorii, dicentis, beatam Virginem non esse matrem Filii DEI, sed filii hominis. Sed contra Apostolus dicit, quod DEUS misit Filium suum, factum ex muliere. Qui enim fit ex muliere, est filius ejus.

Si ergo Filius Dei est factus ex muliere, scilicet ex beata Virgine, manifestum est, quod beata virgo est mater Filii Dei, &c. Theophylactus notat, quod dicatur ex muliere factus, non per mulierem, ne occasionem inveniant, qui per virginem afferunt tanquam canalem Dominum processisse in mundum, id falso omnino existimantes, sed ex muliere, hoc est ex ipsius mulieris substantia corpus accipientem uteri virginalis fructum prodisse.

Mulierem autem pro virgine dixit. Nam idiotismo Hebræo אשה etiam puram virginem notat Gen. II. vers. 22. Quo nomine, inquit Augustinus Tom. III. libr. 2. de Trinit. cap. 5. quis Catholicus nesciat, non eam perditionem virginitatis, sed differentiam sexus Hebræo loquendi more significare voluisse. Cum sexum fœmineum tantum nominat, idem est, cum dicit factum ex muliere, ac si diceret, factum ex virgine, ait B. Lutherus hoc loco. Conf. Gen. III. 15.

Es. VII. 14. Porro γεννώμενον ὑπὸ νόμον, factum sub lege dicit, quod per se legi non fuerit obnoxius per nativitatem, quia Dominus legis natus est, ut hic agnoscit Calvinus, quod contra Piscatorem aliosque notandum: Sed ultro se legi subjecerit nostri causa; non autem ὑπὸ νόμον dicitur factus, quod sub legem ceremonialem, de qua hic peculiariter differere Apostolum monuimus, aut quod sub legem moralem solum se subdere voluerit, ut Piscatori visum; sed id de tota lege Mosis intelligendum, quæ per omnia præstare voluit, quia omnem justitiam legis implere debuit Matth.

III. & per obedientiam suam liberaturus nos erat ab universæ legis rigore, uti etiam agnoscit Pareus, quod Pater Filium incarnatum fecerit sub lege 1. Forensi & Politica, quatenus eum voluerit nasci ex populo subjecto legi, seu stante adhuc politia legis Mosaica; 2. Ceremoniali, quatenus voluerit eum circumcidi in subjectione totius legis;

3. Morali, quatenus eum voluerit præceptis moralibus per omnia conformem esse, & in sua innocentia execrationi legis & morti obnoxiu fieri. Ubi tamen Pareus, erroribus Piscatoris affinis, contraditionibus se involvit, cum Christum vor. dicit per se obnoxium legi ceremoniali & politica, ceu semen Abrahæ. Et Morali etiam legi obedientiam præstare debuit, siquidem homo sit & frater noster. Atqui Christus est Dominus legis etiam ceremonialis Marc.

II. 28. Non ergo per se eidem obnoxius aut servus ejusdem. Nec apparet, quomodo Judæos a lege ceremoniali & forensi redimere potuerit, si eidem se non ultro subjecit, quibus proinde ob violationem istarum legum sub execratione manendum fuisset, si ab execratione earundem liberati non essent. Quapropter hic merito a B. Balduino notatus est Pareus pag. 817. CHRISTUM hominem fuisse legi natura subjectum. Hoc est, inquit, ex Domino legis facere debitorem legis.

Oportet autem Christi obedientiam, quam legi præstitit, esse indebitam, alias non posset esse nobis meritoria: Nemo enim suis debitis aliis aliquid promereri potest: ideo dicit ipse Dominus, se solvisse, quod non rapuit Psal. LXIX. v. 5. Sequutus autem omnino est Pareus Piscatorem suum, qui obedientiam Christi activam ad opus redemptionis necessariam esse negavit, de quo errore in Grund-lichem Beweiss diximus pag. 248. seqq.

Finem autem geminum subjectionis Filii sub lege assignat Apostolus: Priorem ἵνα τοὺς ὑπὸ νόμον ἐξα-γοράση, ut eos, qui sub lege (erant) redimeret. Per Christi eos, qui sub lege erant, non intelligit eos tantum, lege. quæ sub lege ceu tutore fuerunt, sed in genere omnes homines, quia omnibus lex incumbebat servanda, omnes premebat legis execratio, totusque mundus erat legi obnoxius Rom. III. etsi lex ceremonialis & forensis Judæorum propria erat, moralis tamen lex erat omnium, ut sub initium capitis de ceremoniali lege, sub qua peculiariter, Veteris potestatis dignitas.

Deinde observanda in ἀποδοσέως veteris populi dignitas: quam e προθεσμίας tantum colligendam relinquit Apostolus. Nam etsi fere servilis erat conditio veteris populi, erat tamen haeres & Dominus omnium. Sub tutela quidem serviebat, nec in possessionem haereditatis & Dominium plenum namissus erat: Vere tamen ad eundem spectabat haereditas & dominium.

Unde veteres etiam fideles Dei filios fuisse, ac promissam habuisse haereditatem vitae caelestis, ejusque spem & fiduciam aeque ut nos manifestum est (conf. XIII.) & Dominus haereditatis, adeoque per fidem non minus atque nos servatos fuisse. Quod temere negant Sociniani, Anabaptistae, & qui eos sequuntur et Grotius non semel a nobis jam notatus. Nec vero obstat, quod parvuli fuerunt. Nam & parvulum haeredem omnium dixit Dominum Apostolus.

Est quidem Dominus spe tantum & expectatione, sed & jus dominii habet & usumfructum, hoc est alimenta & sustentationem reipsa percipit. Sic populus Veteris Testamenti spe & expectatione Dominus erat, quoad plenam fruitionem libertatis, quae Dominorum est, bonis tamen fruebatur haereditatis, quia ipsi prospiciebatur de spirituali sustentatione, quantum opus erat. Neque extendendum simile extra tertium comparationis, quod nominatim & expresse designat Apostolus, quod nempe fuerint in servitutem redacti sub elementis mundi, ut ratione libertatis ab iisdem distinguantur fideles in Novo Testamento, qui servire iisdem non tenentur.

Domini illi erant omnium sed in servitutem redacti. Durationis tempus. Tertio notandum est durationis tempus: Quousque se extenderit illa tutela & servitus: Usque ad tempus quod Pater prafinierat, vel donec veniret πλήρωμα χρόνης plenitudo temporis.

Tum ergo cessare debuit. Id urget contra Pseudo-Apostolos, convincens eosdem ita solidissime: Quum Deus ipse noluerit tutelam aut curatelam illam perpetuam esse, sed usque ad προθεσμίαν, ad tempus a praefinitum, quod in sua potestate reservarat. Perperam sub servitutem iterum Pseudo-Apostolos redigere Christianos: quum servitutem legis perpetuam fingere, & Ecclesiae Christianae obtrudere velle, non minus absurdum fit, quam tutelam perpetuam facere, & sub eadem haeredes adultos & majores factos continere velle.

Unde porro in proclivi est concludere, ceremoniis in Nov. Test. nihil opus esse, nedum easdem ad justificationem & salutem necessarias censeri posse: Quae ne quidem in Vet. Test. ceu ad salutis haeredes erant per fidem, necessariae erant, sed tantum, ut sub tutela adhuc continerentur haeredes, ordinatae erant, quia adhuc νήπιοι erant, donec adulti emanciparentur illa tutela & ad libertatem Evangelicam admitterentur.

Licet ergo ad illos tantum legitimos haeredes pertinerent omnino bona caelestia, quae etiam consequuti sunt per fidem in futurum Messiam, tamen adhuc sub tutore & curatore agebant nimirum in servitutem redacti Crocius, quod elementorum illorum tem- refellit Cal-pus in finem seculi differat. In eo videtur (magnus ginum, interpres: sic eum vocat) longius provehi, quod sub his elementis non esse putat usque ad secundum Christi adventum.

Finem ponit Apostolus in primo adventu. In illo ergo non elementa solum mundi, sed & infirma & egena elementa v. 9. vocantur, & ab illorum servitute ceu idololatria absterrentur Christiani. Perperam autem Crocius ipse cum Notatur Pareo: Apostolus, inquit, intelligit ceremonias legis Crocius. non solum, sed totam legalem paedagogiam, adeoque & legem moralem, qua Patres terrebat & velut cogebat poenarum comminatione & metu maledictionis.

Nam hoc legis moralis officium nullum finem habet, nec ad Patres tantum spectavit, neque de eo hic agere propositum erat Apostolo. Sed de tutoribus, quorum numus erat usque ad προθεσμίαν τοῦ πατρός, ut differentiam temporis & status Christianorum sub Novo Testamento, a tempore & statu Israëlitici populi sub Veteri Testamento contra Pseudo-Apostolos illam tollentes stabliret, eumque errorem Judaicum profligaret.

riter Judæi fuerunt, egit Apostolus: Ita quod omnes homines sub lege conclusi fuerint, con- cluso capite docuerat. Tropus Apostoli, inquit in priori Commentar. B. Lutherus fol. 32. servandus est. Non enim sub lege esse est id, quod tempore & de- creto legis vivere. Sic nec Job, nec Naaman Syrus sub lege fuerunt, nec Sareptana Sydonis mulier, sed est, esse debitorem legis, non habere quo impleas & reum esse omnium pœnarum, a lege positarum. 'Εξα- γορασμὸς non explicandus est de redemptione impropria & Metaphorica, ut Sociniani volunt, quibus hic non abnuit Grotius, sed de redemptio- ne vera satisfactoria & meritoria: quia vox illa sem- per de vera redemptione, quæ pretio facta in scri- pturis accipitur, & per λύτρωσιν, quæ λύτρον vel redemptionis pretium infert, explicatur Matth. XX. 28. Marc. X. 45. 1. Timoth. II. 6. 1. Petr. I. 19. Rom. III. 25. Deinde Christus nos, qui sub lege eramus, redemit, cum factus fuit pro nobis sub lege eam perfecte implendo Matth. V. 17. & ma- ledictionem ejus sustinendo Gal. III. 13. Quo ergo modo nos sub lege fuimus, eo & ipse se subjecit legi, ut nos a lege redimeret. At nos fuimus sub lege, tum quoad rigidam & absolutam obedientiam ei præstandam, tum quoad pœnam ob legis male- dictum propter commissa peccata luendam. Ergo & ipse ea ratione se legi subjecit. Quæ utique non est nuda aut simplex liberatio sed meritoria & sa- tisfactoria redemptio. Sed de his in Socinismo Profligato uberius dictum. Porro ἐξαγορασμὸς ille concernit non paucos tantum homines, aut Ju- dæos solum, qui sub lege ceremoniali erant, sed omnes, qui fuerunt, sunt, aut erunt unquam. Quia omnes sub lege sunt, quotquot ex Adamo pro- pagantur æque ut Adam. Confer. Roman. III. cap. v. 9. & 19. Qui autem sub lege sunt, illi a Christo redempti sunt, quod hic affirmat Apostolus. De hoc priori fine B. Hunnius ad hunc locum: Filius DEI, inquit, erat Dominus legis, qui sibi olim in monte Sinai non tulit legem, sed aliis. Is ad pro- curandum opus redemptionis nostræ semetipsum in assumpta carne legi subdidit, ut & obedientia legi perfecte præstita, & illius maledictione in semet- ipsum derivata nos & a maledictione legis moralis, & ab ejusdem obsequio coacto, quod in litera vetusta- te positum est, & a legis Leviticæ jugo, ceremoniarum- que Mosaicarum onere nos liberaret, atque sic e ser- vitute in libertatem filiorum Dei assereret. Hic enim erat finis missionis Filii DEI in hunc mundum re- demptio nostra, quam mox excipit aliud beneficium plane divinum ὑοθεσία, seu adoptio in filios, cum omni jure ac privilegio, quod ab ea dependet.

Alter ergo finis designatur his verbis: "Iνα τὴν ὑοθεσίαν ἀπολάβωμεν, ut adoptionem acciperemus: Vel ut Erasmus reddidit: Ut adoptione filiorum jus reciperemus. Quia non tantum redempti sumus a legis execratione, & rigorosæ observationis exa- ctione, sed etiam acquisita nobis est gratia DEI paterna & ὑοθεσία, ut adoptari possimus in filios DEI: Ut qui filii iræ sumus, filii gratiæ & filii Dei evadamus, ex Deo regeneremur, & a Deo adopte- mur, gratia & favore Dei fruamur, ceu dilecti ejus filii, & hæredes salutis æternæ constituamur. Hæc adoptio juxta B. Feuerbornium fascic. V. Disp. 1. §. 59. hic non tantum notat benedictionis, & hæ- reditatis cœlestis nobis merito Christi partæ κτῆσιν fidelem, quæ nobis cum piis Veteris Testamenti communis est, sed & liberam, umbrisque Leviticis & Mosaicis constitutionibus ceremonialibus va- cuam χρῆσιν. Quæ hactenus defuit piis Veteris Testamenti hominibus, quatenus fuerunt δεδυ- |λωμένοι ὑπὸ τὰ στοιχεῖα τοῦ κόσμυ v. 3. Sic imprimis Pareus: Sane Patres, inquit, etiam filii fuerunt & haeredes: Sed parvuli sub legis jugo servientes, nihil a servis differentes, uti dixerat Apostolus. Adoptio- nem igitur illi non acceperunt. Nos vero post redem- ptionem factam adoptionem accepimus: quia post finitam Patris προθεσμίαν nobis quasi jam adultis, emancipatis haereditas a tutoribus quasi in manus est tradita. Adoptio igitur hic non tam ipsam arroga- tionem in filios significat, quasi DEUS nos demum & post illos adoptaverit, quam adoptionis possessio- nem & hereditatis traditionem significat: Ideo non dicit, ut nos adoptaremur, sed ut nos adoptionem ac- ciperemus, nempe libere utendam fruendam, quam patres habuerunt quidem sed jure potius, quam usu, eo quod sub legis tutela servire cogerentur. Verbum ἀπολάβωμεν, quod vetus reddidit, reciperemus, non debitum aut meritum aliquod nostrum significat, sed immissionem quasi in rem nostram. Manet Apostolus in Metaphora. Haeredes enim parvuli postquam προ- θεσμία Patris exacta adoleverunt haereditatem a tutoribus exigunt ἀπολαμβάνουσιν accipiunt: Ita in- quit nos haeredes adulti haereditatem tutoribus olim creditam, recipimus in jus nostrum, in manus no- stras. Summa: Hoc nunc verbo dicit, quod tota si- militudine tutorum intendit; nobis prae patribus be- neficium hoc contigisse Christi redemptione: ut cum ambo quidem filii haeredes essemus: Illi tanquam par- vuli sub legis tutela servirent, nos tanquam adulti jugo legis emancipati inque adoptionis haereditatem immissi sumus. Sic illustre inter Vet. & Nov. Testament. discrimen statuit: & libertatem nostram veterum servituti opponit. Ita & Crocius: Non frue- bantur (veteres) libertate filiorum emancipatorum. Missus venit Filius Dei in carnem, ut eam accipe- remus. Non ut demum fieremus filii, sed ut in haere- ditatis a tutoribus quasi extraditae possessionem mit- teremur, eoque fructum adoptionis acciperemus. Quo pacto videtur haec Paulina sententia eo accipi, ac si imprimis ceremoniarum legalium abrogatio τῷ ἐξαγορασμῷ seu redemptioni Christi hic tribua- tur.

Dubium tamen esse queat, an abrogatio earum, & emancipatio e tutela legum Leviticarum λύτρῳ sanguinis Christi proprie adscribenda sit, tum quia pretii redemptionis, quod hic ἐξαγορασμὸς hoc loco omnium confessione infert, ob captivitatem sub potestate Satanae, & ira, ac justitia divina solven- dum erat, ut justitiae divinae fieret satisfactio, non vero ideo proprie, ut a jugo ceremoniarum libe- raremur: tum quia ceremoniae Leviticae magnam partem expiationem sanguine Christi factam ad- umbrabant, adeoque non opus erat, ut abdicaren- tur per ἐξαγορασμὸν, sed adventante Christo in temporum plenitudine, ceu substantia ipsa & cor- pore atque antitypo ceremoniarum umbra illa ul- tro fugit, & typica illa per sese cessarunt; neque ἀν- τίλυτρον & ἐξαγορασμὸν ac ἱλασμὸν Christi adum- brarunt olim, adeoque propter Christum & bene- ficia Christi institutae sunt, per pretium solutionis & redemptionis Christi commode dici videntur meritoria a nobis ablata: tum quia oeconomia illa Veteris Testamenti per πλήρωμα temporis pro- prie expiravit, quum eo usque durare tantum de- buerit, quod προθεσμίαν τοῦ πατρὸς infert; non autem ut expiraret, pretium persolvendum erat justitiae divinae. Neque explicare vel Crocius vel etiam in tam prolixa διηγήσει Pareus ipse po- tuit, quomodo haereditas nobis post Christi mor- tem & per ejus redemptionem sit quasi in MA- NUS tradita, haereditas nempe vitae aeternae, quam ipsi intelligunt: aut quomodo patres illam jure potius, quam usu habuerint; nobis autem usus ejus prae Patribus Christi redemptione obtigerit, nosque in adoptionis hereditatem immissi fimus.

Num enim Patres jus tantum ad hereditatem vitae aeternae habuerunt, non vero ad hereditatem ipsam admissi sunt? Num fideles sub Novo Testamento usu ipso in hac vita hereditatem illam habent, aut si habere dicantur post hanc vitam, anne prae Patribus eam habent? Et annon redemptionis per mortem Christi factae beneficia toti orbi facta omnibusque hominibus etiam sub Veteri Testamento communia sunt, quod acquisitionem, ut & quoad communicationis intentionem divinam, etiam quoad ipsum υἱοθεσίας beneficium? Redire ergo videtur Apostolus ad principalem scopum, utpote quem nunquam negligit, semper premit, ut explicetur, redemptionem eorum, qui sub legis execratione erant, per unius Christi λύτρον factam, nos uti adoptionem: ita & hereditatem vitae aeternae vel salutem, adeoque etiam justificationem unice per fidem in Christi redemptionem consequi. Quia tamen factus sub lege est, non solum subeundo execrationem legis nobis debitam, sed etiam praestando legi universae, sub qua ceremonialis etiam comprehenditur, obedientiam, quatenus ejusdem observatio in ipsum cadere poterat, ideo vi hujus subjectionis sub legem justitiam, & obedientiam ejusdem per fidem participes reddimur, adeoque justificamur, nec ad justificationem consequendam opus habemus legis sive moralis, sive ceremonialis, quae ipsa etiam eo expiravit, quod προθεσμία impleta sit, & πλήρωμα τὰ χρόνος advenerit, observatione.

Atque hoc, quod B.

Lutherus maxime hic urgeat principale Apostoli thema circa praesentem Apostoli aphorismum: qui auri & gemmae pretiosissimae instar in hac tractatione effulget. Quo facit etiam illatio Apostoli à Theophylacto hoc modo dilucidata: Quocirca cum filii simus nos & haeredes, non rei alicujus inanis aut frivolae, sed DEI ipsius, & partienda nobis cum unigenito hereditas fit, cur servi efficimur, & plane repudiamus, que nos in adoptionem deduxerat, poster. & cur legi vacamus?

B.

Lutherus in Commentar. poster. fol. 100. Ipse, inquit, est Dominus legis, ideo lex non habet jus in eum, non potest eum accusare, quia est Filius DEI.

Cum igitur non esset sub lege, sua sponte legi se subjecit. Ibi lex in eum exercuit omnem tyrannidem, quam in nos. Accusat autem & terret nos, subjicit nos peccato, irae, morti, ac judicio suo condemnat. Ac hoc jure facit, quia omnes peccatores, & naturaliter filii irae sumus. Contra CHRISTUS peccatum non fecit, neque inventus est dolus in ore ejus, ideo legi nihil debuit.

Et tamen lex in tam innocentem, sanctum, justum, & benedictum aeque saeviit, ac in nos peccatores, maledictos, & damnatos, & multo atrocius. Accusavit enim ut blasphemum & seditiosum, fecit eum reum coram DEO omnium peccatorum, totius mundi, denique sic contristavit & pavefecit, ut sudaret sanguinem, postremo sua sententia condemnavit ad mortem & quidem crucis. Hoc profecto mirabile duellum est, ubi lex creatura cum Creditore sic congreditur, & praeter omne jus omnem tyrannidem suam in Filio DEI exercet, quam in nobis filiis irae exercuit. Quia ergo lex tam horribiliter & impie peccavit in DEUM suum, vocatur in jus & accusatur. Ibi CHRISTUS ait, Domina lex, imperatrix & Regina potentissima ac crudelissima totius generis humani!

Quid commisi, quod accusasti, perterrefecisti & condemnafti me innocentem? Hic lex, qua damnaverat & occiderat prius omnes homines, cum non habeat, quo se defendat aut purget, vicissim ita damnatur & occiditur, ut amittat jus suum, non solum in CHRISTO, (in quem injuste saeviit & occidit) sed etiam in omnibus, qui credunt in eum. Et porro: Hac ergo victoria sua fugavit CHRISTUS e conscientia nostra legem, ut amplius non possit nos confundere in conspectu DEI, in desperationem adigere & damnare.

Non definit quidem ostendere peccatum, accusare & perterrefacere. Sed conscientia apprehendens hoc Apostoli verbum, Christus a lege nos redemit, fide erigitur, & consolationem concipit. Denique sancta quadam superbia legi insultat, dicens: Nihil morror terrores & minas tuas, quia crucifixisti Filium DEI, & summa injuria crucifixisti. Ideo peccatum, quod in eum commisisti, est irremissibile, amisisti jus tuum, & nunc in posterum non solum Christo victa & strangulata es, sed etiam mihi credenti in eum, cui donavit hanc victoriam. Sic lex periit nobis in sempiternum, modo in Christo permaneamus.

DEO igitur gratia, qui dedit nobis victoriam per Dominum nostrum JESUM CHRISTUM. Ista quoque huc pertinent, quod sola fide justificemur: Quia cum hoc duellum gebum est inter legem & Christum, nulla prorsus opera aut merita nostra intervenerunt, sed solus CHRISTUS ibi fuit, qui induta persona nostra subjecit se legi, & summa innocentia sustinuit omnem ejus tyrannidem. Ideo lex tanquam latro & sacrilegus homicida Filii DEI amittit jus, & meretur damnari, ut ubicunque est, vel saltem nominatur CHRISTUS, procul discedere & fugere hoc nomen, ut Diabolus crucem cogatur. Quare credentes liberi sumus a lege per CHRISTUM, qui de ea triumphavit per semetipsum.

Itaque hic gloriosus triumphus per Christum nobis partus nullis operibus, sed sola fide apprehenditur. Ergo sola fides justificat. Item: Sic CHRISTUS persona divina & humana, natus ex DEO ab aeterno, ex virgine in tempore non venit ad condendam legem, sed ut terrores ipsius in summo gradu sentiret & vinceret, ac per eam tolleret.

Non factus est Doctor legis, sed Discipulus obediens legi, ut hac sua obedientia redimeret eos, qui sub lege erant. Hac prorsus aliena sunt a doctrina Papistarum, qui CHRISTUM fecerunt legislatorem, & quidem Mose severiorem. Paulus hic omnino contrarium docet, scilicet Deum projecisse Filium suum sub legem, hoc est, coegisse eum ferre judicium & maledictionem legis, peccatum, mortem &c. Moses enim, minister peccati, irae & mortis, cepit, ligavit, condemnavit & occidit CHRISTUM, hoc ipse pertulit. Habuit ergo Christus se ad legem passive, non active. Non est igitur legislator, aut Judex secundum legem, sed in eo dum se subjecit legi, ferens ejus condemnationem, à maledicto ejus nos liberavit. Quod autem Christus in Evangelio praecepta tradit & legem docet seu potius interpretatur, hoc non ad locum de justificatione, sed de bonis operibus pertinet.

Deinde etiam non est proprium Christi officium, propter quod praecipue venit in mundum, docere legem, sed accidentale. Cujusmodi erat & hoc, quod sanabat infirmos, excitabat mortuos, beneficiaebat indignis, consolabatur afflictos &c. Ea quidem gloriosa ac divina opera & beneficia sunt, sed non propria Christi. Nam Prophetae docuerunt etiam legem, & miracula ediderunt. CHRISTUS vero est DEUS & homo, qui pugnans cum lege, passus est extremam ipsius savitiam & tyrannidem. Et hoc ipso, quod fecit & sustinuit legem, vicit eam in semetipso, ac postea resurgens à morte, legem infestissimum hostem nostrum damnavit, & e medio sustulit, ut amplius damnare & occidere credentes non possit. Quare Christi verum ac proprium officium est, luctari cum lege, peccato & morte totius mundi, & sic luctari, ut ista sustinueriteat, & sustinendo in semetipso vincat & aboleat, & hoc modo credentes a lege & omnibus malis liberet.

Hæc omnia B.

Lutherus. Quapropter υἱοθεσίαν non explicat de fruitione libertatis a lege ceremoniali, sed de adoptione in filios DEI omnium credentium, omnium temporum propria, fol. 101.

Ut adoptionem filiorum acciperemus, id est, filiationem divinam Paulus copiosè explicat & ornat hunc locum Genes. XXII.

In semine tuo &c.

Supra appellavit benedictionem illam feminis Abrahæ fultiam, promissionem Spiritus, vitam, redemptionem a lege, testamentum &c. Hic filiationem & hereditatem vitæ æternæ appellat. Ista omnia completitur vocabulum benedictionis. Nam sublata per hoc semen benedictum maledictione, qua est peccatum, mors &c. succedit in locum ejus benedictio, hoc est, justitia, vita, & omnia bona.

Ex his facile æstimari jam glossæ Grotianæ pollunt.

Qui inepte primum ingerit Primogenitum, ad quem absente patre cura pertinebat. Nam DEUS Pater nunquam & nusquam absens est, qui ubique semper præsens est. Neque primogenitus est Filius DEI ceu è multis, cum hoc loco missus dicitur; sed est μονογενής uni- & foligenitus, utpote solus ex essentia Patris natus & unicus ille Filius DEI coessentialis & ὁμοούσιος Patri.

Missum autem Filium DEI perperam explicatur, quod fit potestatem ei a Patre datum eximiam. Nam missio facta est adventu in mundum & incarnatione Filii: Quæ formaliter non est potestatis divinæ, nedum eximiæ, nescio cujus communicatio.

Et quæ cura convenit primogenito in fratres sub tutoribus constitutos, qui illi subsunt non fratri primogenito ἀρχή τῆς προθεσμίας πατρός.

Subditus autem legi non est CHRISTUS, quia Judæus natus, vel ratione nativitatis, sed quia noster Redemptor esse voluit, seu ratione spontaneæ subjectionis. Liberavit vero subditos legis non Judæos tantum, sed nos omnes: Nec a vitiis, & ab obligatione legis, sed a peccati & peccatorum suppliciis & condemnatione ac rigorosa exactione legis.

Per υἱοθεσίαν autem permissum patris intelligi, quo permittuntur filii res quasdam suas habere, & suo arbitratu res quasdam agere, nempe manente in Patrem obsequio, sed sine specialibus præceptis, (quæ glossa Grotii est nova profecto & incondita) quomodo probabitur?

De patre vivente hic non agebat πέτασις, si eam respici velit; sed de Patre defuncto, quum filios liberos sub potestate tutorum constitutos referat. Qui vero ab illa exempti non tantum res quasdam suas habere permittuntur, sed plena hereditatis libertate fruuntur. Quid ergò illa sibi velint in ἀποδόσει fateor me non intelligere, quod nempe filii DEI, vel qui acceperunt υἱοθεσίαν, res tantum quasdam suas habere: quid item illa, quod suo arbitratu res quasdam agere permittantur.

Si respiciatur libertas a ceremoniarum, vel legum ceremonialium obligatione, veteres fuisse filios DEI, vel adoptionem accepisse, negandum erit, utpote, qui libertatem non habebant: At ne de nobis quidem in Novo Testamento dicendum, quod nos opes quasdam nostro arbitratu agere permittamur in iis, quæ ad religionem, DEI, & salutem pertinent.

Quum ἐθελοθρησκεία DEI improbentur, iisque frustra DEUS colatur, Matth. XV.

Vers.

## 4:6
6. Ὅτι δέ ἐστε υἱοὶ [And because ye are sons] Made similar to GOD, through a heart cleansed from vices.

To be a Son of GOD (by adoption) is not to be made similar to GOD through the cleansing of the heart from vices. That cleansing is a consequence of υἱοθεσίας [adoption], just as sanctification follows justification.

But the Apostle now interchanges υἱοθεσίας [adoption] and ἑότητα [sonship], because we thus attain adoption, so that we are truly sons of GOD not by nature, but by grace, and enjoy the full right of sons. Which is an ἀξίωμα [dignity] and privilege, but the name of Son does not make for a similarity with GOD; it pertains to the category of Relation, not of quality.

But the ancients are not to be excluded from that denomination of sons of GOD or υἱοθεσία [adoption], inasmuch as the same obedience and redemption of CHRIST was equally acquired for them, and they were likewise transferred from a state of wrath into a state of grace through faith, and when they were sons of wrath by nature and natural generation, they became sons of GOD through regeneration.

And thus it coheres very well with the Antecedents: For lest anyone be able to doubt concerning such great φιλανθρωπία [love for mankind] of GOD adopting us as sons, the Apostle shows the benefit of υἱοθεσίας [adoption] confirmed for us by the Spirit sanctifying in our hearts that we are sons of GOD. Ἐξαπέστειλεν ὁ Θεὸς τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ [GOD sent forth the Spirit of his Son].

As a part of the inheritance, given as a loan. Fathers are accustomed sometimes to give something of the inheritance to children to spend.

See Luke XV. verse.

12. But that Spirit is obtained, John XIV. v. 16. the sense is the same in this place, as in Rom.

VIII. v. 15. 16. Εἰς τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν [Into your hearts] Not into the skin, where circumcision is.

The manuscript ἰμῶν [of us] is not bad. Κράζον [crying] That is, making us cry out. A Hebraism, which he interprets in that place equal to this one to the Romans. Ἀββᾶ ὁ πατήρ [Abba, Father] The voice of sons, testifying their love toward their Fathers.

See the said place Romans VIII. v. 15. & the sayings.

However the Holy Spirit may be described elsewhere, that he is the earnest of salvation: Here, however, he is not presented by the Apostle in that respect; and those things are distinct, to testify concerning our adoption, and to be an earnest of future inheritance, although both befit the Holy Spirit.

Can someone not testify in judgment concerning the fact that Titius is made the son of Maevius, if there is doubt about it: but who would say that he is the earnest of the inheritance of Titius? Nor is the Spirit the earnest of our inheritance for that reason, as Fathers are accustomed to give something of the inheritance to sons to spend.

We have said concerning that, how he is called an earnest at 2 Cor. I, which we do not repeat here.

But the Spirit of CHRIST is called the Holy Spirit, not only because he is obtained through CHRIST, John XIV. verse 16. or by the intercession of Christ; but also and primarily, because he proceeds from Christ from eternity or is the breath of the mouth of Christ, Is.

XI. verse 2.

2 Thess. III. Just as he is called the Spirit of the Father, because he proceeds from the Father from eternity.

For his origin from the Son is not to be excluded, concerning which in System. Theol. Tom. III.

The Apostle could indeed have simply named him the Holy Spirit, or the Spirit of God, or the Spirit of the Father: But he purposely names him the Spirit of the Son in this place, to show that to the adoptive sons of God, by the grace of adoption, is conferred that same Spirit which the Son possesses in the Deity by nature, as here B.

Hunnius.

But that he is sent in time through Christ is to be attributed not only to his intercession, but also to his merit. For Christ merited this for us by his obedience, passion, and death, so that the Holy Spirit might be given to us.

Therefore he says this Spirit was sent, as if from the eternal seat of the Deity, into our hearts. Which is not a certain local emission, since He is present everywhere and fills the whole world, Wisdom 1. But the grace of the Holy Spirit is insinuated, poured into our hearts, which exerts and declares itself through motions, which He generates in the hearts of the elect, ineffable, especially while praying, just as he adds: Crying Abba Father. *Abba* is a Syriac expression, descending from the Hebrew אבא, but that it is reduplicated, and a Greek expression is added to the Syriac word, is done not so much for the sake of interpretation, as for the sake of a certain singular emphasis, to express the filial affection of believers toward GOD as a most beloved Father. Therefore, Luther, looking to the affection and love of those invoking, renders it: *Abba lieber Vater* [Abba dear Father]. It must be noted, however, in what sense the cry is attributed to the Holy Spirit, certainly not that He Himself invokes GOD (for this would derogate from His eternal majesty, since He is one with the Father and the Son, GOD), but that He effects in the elect that they themselves, with most ardent prayers, call upon and invoke GOD as their Father. And it is a similar phrase to that which was in Romans 8, where the Spirit of GOD is said to intercede for us with ineffable groanings, that is, He effects in us such motions and groanings that the prayer is not cold or languid, but ardent and devout, and flowing from a clearly filial confidence, which melts and resolves into those ineffable cries and groanings; just as it was rightly explained by the Blessed Hunnius. Nor did the Blessed Luther interpret it otherwise in his later Commentary, fol. 103: "In serious terrors and struggles of conscience, we indeed apprehend CHRIST, and believe Him to be our Savior. But the law then terrifies most, and sin disturbs us. Finally, the Devil attacks us with all his machines and fiery darts, and tries with all his might to snatch CHRIST from us and shake off all consolations. There, it is little short of us succumbing and despairing. For we are then that bruised reed and smoking flax. Meanwhile, however, the Holy Spirit helps our weaknesses, and intercedes for us with ineffable groaning, and gives testimony to our spirit that we are the children of GOD. In this way, in terrors, the mind is raised, sighs to its Savior and High Priest JESUS Christ, overcomes the infirmity of the flesh, and again conceives consolation and says: Abba Father. That groaning, therefore, which we scarcely feel, Paul calls a cry and an ineffable groaning, which fills heaven and earth. Then he also calls it the cry and groaning of the Spirit, because the Spirit excites this cry in our heart for us who are weak and tempted. So that even if the law, sin, and the Devil utter great and terrible cries against us, which seem to fill the whole heaven and earth, and far surpass the groaning of our heart, yet they cannot harm us. For the more these enemies of ours press, accuse, and torment us with their cries, the more we, groaning, apprehend Christ, invoke Him with heart and mouth, have Him in us, and believe Him to have been made under the law for us, that He might redeem us from the curse of the law, and that He might destroy sin and death. And thus, having apprehended Christ by faith, we cry through Him Abba Father. And that cry of ours far surpasses the cry of the Devil, etc." To which we add what the Blessed Luther further has on fol. 104: "You will also observe what Paul says, that the Spirit does not intercede for us in temptation with many words or long interrogation, but only with a groaning, yet ineffable, nor does it strongly testify the cry with a voice with tears and say: Have mercy on me GOD, etc. But only to utter the very voice of the cry and groaning, which is: Abba Father! Which is indeed a very short voice, but

embraces everything. Not the mouth, but the affection speaks there in this manner: "Even if I am in anguish on all sides, and seem deserted and utterly cast out from your face, I am nevertheless a son, you are Father, on account of Christ, I am beloved on account of the Beloved." Wherefore the little word, Father, formally spoken in the heart, is an eloquence which Demosthenes, Cicero, and whoever were the most eloquent who ever were in the world, cannot express. The matter is thus expressed not by groanings, but by words, which are not expressed by all the words of all Rhetoricians. For they are ineffable. It must be observed, however, that this testimony and this cry of the Holy Spirit in our hearts is against the doubt concerning the grace of GOD and the Antichristian dogma, by which it was sanctioned in the Council of Trent. The cause of this certainty of ours, as well as of the Popish doubt and uncertainty, was again excellently explained by the Blessed Luther, gravely warning that if all things in the Papacy were safe, yet that monster of uncertainty would surpass all monsters. "This," he says, "is our foundation. The Gospel commands us to look not at our good deeds or perfection, but at God Himself promising, at CHRIST Himself the Mediator. On the contrary, the Pope commands us to look not at God promising, not at CHRIST the High Priest, but at our works and merits. There, doubt and despair necessarily follow: Here, true certainty and joy of the Spirit. Because I cling to God, who cannot lie. For He says: Behold, I deliver my Son into death, that He may redeem you by His blood from sins and death. There I cannot doubt, unless I wish to deny God entirely. And this is the reason why our Theology is certain, because it snatches us from our own sight, and places us outside ourselves, so that we do not rely on our own strength, conscience, sense, person, or works, but rely on that which is outside us, that is, on the promise and truth of GOD, by which He cannot deceive." The Pope, therefore (as Megalander most rightly concludes), by this impious dogma, by which he commanded one to doubt the favor of God toward himself, removed God and all promises concerning the Church, overwhelmed the benefits of Christ, and abolished the whole Gospel. These inconveniences necessarily follow, because men do not rely on the promising God, but on their own works and merits. Where this happens, it is impossible for a man to be certain of the will of God; nay, it is necessary for him always to doubt it, and at length to despair. Nowhere can it be seen what God wills, what pleases Him, except in His Word. This makes us certain that God has cast away all wrath and hatred toward us, when He delivered His only-begotten Son for our sins, etc. The sacraments, the power of the keys, etc., also make us certain, which, unless God loved us, He would not have delivered to us. With such infinite testimonies of His favor toward us, God overwhelms us. Wherefore, having exploded this plague of uncertainty, with which the whole Church of the Pope is infected, let us certainly conclude that God is propitious to us, that we please Him, and are cared for on account of Christ, and that we have the Holy Spirit, who intercedes for us with an ineffable cry and groaning.

That gloss of Grotius: "Not into the skin, as circumcision, but into the hearts," is very frivolous. The heart is naturally the principle of life, of motions, of vital actions. The same is the principle of spiritual life, motions, and actions supernaturally. As, therefore, the vital spirit is infused into the physical heart for natural life: So the Spirit of the Son of God is infused into regenerated hearts for spiritual life. But as the vital spirit in the sensible heart by its *entelecheia* [actuality] is an infallible argument to a man of his life: So the Spirit of the Son of God in the hearts of the regenerated by its sensible testimony is an infallible *criterion* of his regeneration and grace as a son of God, as Pareus not badly [states] here. But this cry is both internal of the heart and external of the mouth. But this is common to the children of God with hypocrites: That is proper to the children of God.

Sometimes the heart cries without the mouth in the faithful, by the example of Moses, Exod. XIV. Often the mouth cries without the heart, by the example of hypocrites, Matth. VII. 22.

Drusius, book VII, passes over it: he says Abba is a name of dignity. But Dievius, on Romans VIII, verse 15, more correctly notes that the Chaldean Abba means 'my Father'. For where in Hebrew it is אבא, the Chaldean text has Abba. Yet in this he does not deserve assent, because it was an artificial word, by which they would claim a Father for themselves to be adopted, or acknowledge the first father of those adopted. Verse 7. (υἱὸς καὶ κληρονόμος). Thou Galatian. Namely, by full right, of age.

The Vulgate has it in the third person: Therefore he is not a servant. But in the sources, and also among the Greeks, it is held in the second person, and the Apostle addresses every believer, not just the Galatian, as if he were saying: Whoever you are, who truly and from the heart believe in Christ, I would have you certainly conclude that you are no longer a servant of the law, but are free from its servile obedience and also from its condemnatory sentence, and therefore a son in God, living by full right and of age.

Therefore, it is not precisely about a son, as B. Hunnius rightly says, in years, as it seemed to some, fully, as if he were called a servant who still lives under ceremonies. As Crocius after Pareus: He addresses the truly faithful and, from the received seal of the Holy Spirit, crying in the heart: Abba Father, he infers that he is no longer in a servile condition, under tutors and curators, but an emancipated son, whereas before the faithful differed nothing from servants, when they lived under the burden of the law.

But this inference pertains also to the faithful of the Old Testament, who certainly were not servants, but sons, and can no more be excluded from υἱοθεσία or the right of sonship than from the inheritance of life. For these things are connected, if indeed sons, then also heirs to God through Christ. Wherefore B. Luther more correctly: To be a servant in this place according to Paul, he says fol. 105, is to be guilty and a captive under the law, under the wrath of God and death, to look upon God not as a Father of mercies, but as a torturer, an enemy, a tyrant. This is truly to act in servitude and Babylonian captivity, and to be tormented most cruelly in it. For the law does not liberate from sin and death, but reveals and increases sin, and works wrath.

That servitude, he says, ceases, it no longer presses and saddens us, etc. Paul says in the concrete: He shall no longer be a servant. But the meaning will be clearer if we express it in the abstract: There shall be no servitude in Christ, but mere sonship. For when faith comes, that servitude ceases, as he says above in chapter 3, quest.

Which sense B. Balduinus also followed in his aphorisms, page 819. The reborn are not servants, but sons, v. 7, whose hearts are temples of the Holy Spirit, 1 Cor. VI. 19, therefore they do not approach God with servile fear, but with filial reverence, and commend their affairs to Him as to a most beloved Father.

And just as they are no longer bound to fear as servants of the eternal and omnipotent Father God, nor to perform works pleasing to God out of fear of punishment: So conversely, as sons, they ought to fear God as a most Clement Father, and do with a prompt mind what has been divinely commanded. For if I am a Father, where is my honor, and if I am a Lord, where is my fear, says the Lord, Malach. I, verse 6. Hence Christ to his disciples: You are my friends, if you do what I command you: I no longer call you my servants, because a servant does not know what his Lord does, etc. John XV. 14.

Latin:

6. Ὅτι δέ ἐστε υἱοὶ Similes facti DEO, per cor à vitiis mundatum.

Filium DEI esse (per adoptionem) non est DEO similem factum esse per cordis à vitiis mundationem. Mundatio illa consequens est υἱοθεσίας, uti sanctificatio sequitur justificationem.

Permutat autem Apostolus jam υἱοθεσίας & ἑότητα, quia nos ita adoptionem consequimur, ut vere simus DEI filii non natura, sed gratia, ac pleno filiorum jure fruamur. Quod ἀξίωμα est & privilegium, non vero ad similitudinem cum DEO facit Filii nomen, ad prædicamentum Relationis, non qualitatis pertinet.

Non autem ab illa filiorum DEI denominatione vel υἱοθεσία excludendi veteres sunt, utpote quibus eadem æque obedientia ac redemptione CHRISTI acquisita est, quique è statu iræ in statum gratiæ per fidem pariter translati, & quum filii iræ natura & naturali generatione essent, filii DEI facti sunt per regenerationem.

Atque ita cohæret optime cum Antecedentibus: Ne enim de tanta φιλανθρωπία DEI adoptantis nos in filios, quisquam dubitare possit, ostendit Apostolus beneficium υἱοθεσίας confirmatum nobis per Spiritum sanctificantem in cordibus nostris, quod simus filii DEI. Ἐξαπέστειλεν ὁ Θεὸς τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ.

Tanquam partem de hæreditate, pro mutuo datam. Solent interdum Patres de hæreditate aliquid liberis dispendandum dare.

Vide Luc. XV. vers.

12. Spiritus autem ille eximitur obtinetur, Joh. XIV. v. 16. sensus idem hoc loco, quâ Rom.

VIII. v. 15. 16. Εἰς τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν Non in cuticulam, ubi est circumcisio.

Manuscriptus ἰμῶν non male. Κράζον Id est, clamare nos faciens. Hebraismus, quem interpretatur ille par huic ad Romanos locus. Ἀββᾶ ὁ πατήρ Vox filiorum, amerem suum erga Patres testantium.

Vide dictum locum Roman. VIII. v. 15. & dicta.

Utut Spiritus Sanctus describatur alias, quod sit arrha salutis: Hic tamen eo respectu non sistitur ab Apostolo; & distincta illa sunt, testificari de adoptione nostra, & arrham esse hereditatis futuræ, licet utrumque Spiritui Sancto conveniat.

Annon testari aliquis in judicio potest de eo, quod Titius fit filius Mævii, si dubium de eo fit: quem vero arrham hereditatis Titii esse quis dixerit? Nec ea ratione Spiritus arrha hereditatis nostræ est, uti Patres solent aliquid filiis de hæreditate dispendandum dare.

Diximus de eo, quomodo arrha dicatur ad 2. Corinth. I. quæ hic non repetimus.

Spiritus autem CHRISTI vocatur Spiritus Sanctus, non solum quia obtinetur per CHRISTUM, Johan. XIV. vers. 16. vel intercessione Christi; sed etiam & imprimis, quia à Christo ab æterno procedit seu spiraculum oris Christi, Es.

XI. vers. 2.

2. Thess. III. Quemadmodum Patris Spiritus dicitur, quia ab æterno procedit à Patre.

Nam origo ejus à Filio excludenda non est, de quo in System. Theol. Tom. III.

Potuisset quidem Apostolus eum simpliciter nominare Spiritum Sanctum, aut Spiritum Dei, aut Patris Spiritum: Verum data opera nominat hoc loco Spiritum Filii, ut ostendat, filiis Dei adoptivis per gratiam adoptionis conferri eundem illum Spiritum, quem Filius in Deitate possidet per naturam, ut hic B.

Hunnius.

Quod vero in tempore mittitur per Christum, non intercessioni tantum ejusdem, sed merito quoque tribuendum est. Nam promeruit id Christus nobis obedientia, passione & morte sua, ut Spiritus Sanctus nobis donaretur.

Hunc ergo Spiritum ait velut ex æterna Deitatis sede, emissum in corda nostra. Quae non est emissio quaedam localis, cum ubiq; sit praesens & repleat orbem terrarum, Sapient. I. Sed insinuatur Spiritus Sancti gratia, effusa in corda nostra, quae se exerit & declarat per motus, quos in cordibus electorum gignit inenarrabiles, praesertim inter precandum, quemadmodum subjicit: Clamantem Abba Pater. Abba Syriaca dictio est, descendens ab Hebraeo אבא, quod autem reduplicatur, & Syriacae voci Graeca dictio adjungitur, non tam fit interpretationis gratia, quam singularis cujusdam emphaseos causa, ad exprimendum filialem affectum credentium erga DEUM tanquam Patrem dilectissimum. Ideo Lutherus ad affectum & amorem invocantium respiciens, reddit: Abba lieber Vater. Notandum autem est, quo sensu Spiritui Sancto clamor attribuatur, non certe, quod ipsemet DEUM invotet, (hoc enim aeterna ipsius majestati derogaret, cum sit unus cum Patre, Filioque DEUS) sed quod efficit in electis, ut ipsi ardentissimis precibus DEUM ut Patrem suum inclament & invocent. Estque confimilis phrasis, qualis erat Roman. VIII. ubi Spiritus DEI dicitur intercedere pro nobis gemitibus inenarrabilibus, hoc est, efficit in nobis tales motus atque gemitus, ut precatio non sit frigida aut languida, sed ardens & devota, ac promanans ex fiducia plane filiali, quae in illos inenarrabiles clamores atque gemitus liquescit atque resolvitur; quemadmodum recte à B. Hunnio exposita. Neque aliter illa interpretatus est B. Lutherus in poster. Commentar. fol. 103. In feriis pavoribus & certaminibus conscientia apprehendemus quidem CHRISTUM, & credimus eum Salvatorem nostrum. Sed lex tum maxime terret, & peccatum conturbat nos. Impugnat denique Diabolus nos omnibus machinis & ignitis telis suis, & conatur totis viribus eripere nobis CHRISTUM & omnes consolationes excutere. Ibi parum abest, ne succumbamus & desperemus. Sumus enim tum arundo illa contrita, & linum fumigans. Interim ramen Spiritus Sanctus adjuvat imbecillitates nostras, & interpellat pro nobis gemitu inenarrabili, datque testimonium Spiritui nostro, quod simus filii DEI. Hoc modo in terroribus erigitur mens, suspirat ad Salvatorem ac Pontificem suum JESUM Christum, vincit infirmitatem carnis, atque iterum consolationem concipit & dicit: Abba Pater. Istum ergo gemitum, quem nos vix fentimus, vocat Paulus clamorem & gemitum inenarrabilem, qui replet calum & terram. Deinde etiam clamorem & gemitum Spiritus vocat, quia nobis infirmis & tentatis excitat Spiritus hunc clamorem in corde nostro. Ut maxime igitur lex, peccatum, Diabolus magnus & terribiles edant contra nos clamores, qui videntur totum calum & terram replere, ac longissime vincere gemitum cordis nostri, tamen non possunt nocere nobis. Nam quo plus hi hostes nostri instant, accusant, & cruciant nos suis clamoribus, hoc magis ingemifcentes apprehendimus Christum, corde & ore invocamus cum, habemus in eo, & credimus eum pro nobis factum sub legem, ut nos à maledicto legis redimeret, utque peccatum & mortem destrueret. Atque sic apprehenso Christo fide, clamamus per eum Abba Pater. Isque clamor noster longe superat clamorem Diaboli &c. Quibus addimus, quae porro habet B. Lutherus fol. 104. Observabis etiam, quae Paulus dicit, Spiritum non multis verbis aut longa interrogatione intercedere pro nobis in tentatione, sed tantum gemitu, inenarrabili tamen, nec fortiter voce testari clamorem cum lacrymis & dicere: Miserere mei DEUS &c. Sed tantum ipsam clamoris ac gemitus vocem edere, quae est: Ab Pater! Quae quidem brevissima est vox, sed

omnia complectitur. Non os, sed affectus ibi loquitur ad hunc modum: Etiamfi angustia fint mihi undique, & videar desertus ac prorsus à fizic tua projectus, sum tamen filius, tu Pater, propter Christum, sum dilectus propter dilectum. Quare vocula, Pater, formaliter dicta in corde, est eloquentia, quam Demosthenes, Cicero, & quique eloquentissimi, qui unquam fuerunt in mundo, non possunt exprimere. Res ita non gemitibus, sed verbis exprimitur, qui omnibus verbis omnium Rhetorum non exprimuntur. Sunt enim inenarrabiles. Observandum autem immis hoc testimonium & hic clamor Spiritus Sancti in cordibus nostris adversus dubitationem de gratia DEI & dogma Antichristianum, quo id sancitum est in Concilio Tridentino. Caufam hujus nostrae certitudinis, ut & Papisticae dubitationis & incertitudinis optime exposuit iterum B. Lutherus, graviter monens, siomnia in Papatu salva essent, tamen illud, monstrum incertitudinis superare omnia monstra. Hoc, inquit, fundamentum est nostrum. Evangelium jubet intuernos non benefacta perfectionemve nostram, sed ipsum Deum promittentem ipsum CHRISTUM Mediatorem. Contra Papa jubet respicere non Deum promittentem, non CHRISTUM Pontificem, sed opera nostra & merita. Ibi necessario sequitur dubitatio & desperatio: Illic vera certudo & gaudium Spiritus. Quia in Deo haereo, qui mentiri non potest. Dicit enim: Ecce trado Filium meum in mortem, ut te sanguine suo redimat à peccatis & morte. Ibi non possum dubitare, nisi velim prorsus Deum negare. Atq; haec est ratio, cur nostra Theologia certa fit, quia rapit nos è conspectu nostro, & ponit nos extra nos, ut non nitamur viribus, conscientia, sensu, persona, operibus nostris, sed eo nitamur, quod est extra nos, hoc est, promissione & veritate DEI, qua fallere non potest. Papa igitur (uti rectissime concludit Megalander) hoc impio dogmate, quo jussit dubitare de favore Dei erga fe, sustulit Deum & omnes promissiones de Ecclesia, obruit beneficia Christi, & abolevit totum Evangelium. Ista incommoda necessario sequuntur, quia homines non promittenti Deo, sed suis operibus & meritis nituntur. Hoc ubi fit, impossibile est, hominem certum esse de voluntate Dei, imd necesse est, cum semper ambigere de ea, ac tandem desperare. Nusquam cerni potest, quid Deus velit, quid ei placeat, nisi in Verbo ipsius. Hoc certos nos reddit, Deum abjecisse omnem iram ac odium erga nos, cum tradidit Filium suum unigenitum pro peccatis nostris &c. Reddunt item nos certos sacramenta, potestas clavium &c. qua, nisi diligeret nos Deus, non tradidisset nobis. Talibus infinitis testimoniis de favore suo erga nos obruit nos Deus. Quare explosa hac peste incertitudinis, qua tota Ecclesia Papa infecta est, certo statuamus, Deum nobis propitium, nos illi placere, & cura esse propter Christum, nos habere Spiritum Sanctum, qui interpellat pro nobis clamore & gemitu inenarrabili.

Gloffa illa Grotii: Non in cuticulam, ut circumcifio, sed in corda, perquam frivola est. Cor principium vite, motuum, actionum vitalium est naturaliter. Idem principium vite, motuum, actionum spiritualium supernaturaliter. Ut igitur Spiritus vitalis immittitur cordi physico ad vitam naturalem: Ita Spiritus Filii Dei immittitur cordibus regeneratis ad vitam spiritualem. Ut vero Spiritus vitalis in corde sensibili sua ἐντελεχεία infallibile est hominivitae fue argumentum: Ita Spiritus Filii Dei in cordibus regeneratorum sensibili sua testificatio-ne infallibile est filii Dei regenerationis fue & gratia κριτήριον, ut hic non male Pareus. Est autem hic clamor tum internus cordis, tum externus oris. Sed hic communis est filiis Dei cum hypocritis: Ille filiorum Dei proprius est.

Clamat interdum cor fine ore in fidelibus exemplo Mosis, Exod. XIV. Clamat sæpe os fine corde exemplo hypocritarum, Matth. VII. 22.

Drusius libr. VII. præterit: Abba dicit nomen dignitatis esse. Sed rectius Dievius ad Roman. IIX. vers. 15. Chaldaicum Abba Patrem meum notare. Ubi enim in Hebræo אבא est, Chaldaum textum Abba habere.

In eo tamen assensum non meretur, quod vox artificialis fuerit, qua adoptandi sibi Patrem asciscerent, vel adoptati patrem primum agnoscerent. Vers. 7. (υἱὸς καὶ κληρονόμος). Tu Galata. Nempe pleno jure, major annis. Vulgatus habet in tertia persona: Itaque non est servus. Sed in fontibus, at & apud Græcos secunda persona habetur, & alloquitur Apostolus quemlibet fidelem, non Galatam tantum quemvis, quasi dicat: Quisquis es, qui in Christum vere & ex corde credis, certo statuas velim, te non esse servum amplius legis, sed ab illius servili obsequio nec non sententia condemnatoria es liber, & proinde filius in Deo viventis pleno jure & majori.

Non ergo præcife de filio, ut recte B. Hunnius, annis, ut nonnullis visum, pleno, quasi servus dicatur, qui sub ceremoniis adhuc degit. Quomodo Crocius post Pareum: Vere fidelem alloquitur & ex accepto Spiritus Sancti signaculo, clamantis in corde: Abba Pater, infert, non esse amplius in conditione servili, sub tutoribus & curatoribus, sed filium emancipatum, cum ante fideles nihil à servis differrent, cum sub onere legis versarentur. Ast illatio hæc pertinet & ad fideles Veteris Testamenti, qui utique non servi erant, sed filii, nec magis ab υἱοθεσία vel jure filiationis, quam hæreditate vitæ excludi possunt. Sunt enim hæc connexa, si vero servis, & hæres Deo per Christum.

Quapropter rectius B. Lutherus: Servum esse hoc loco secundum Paulum, inquit fol. 105. est esse reum & captivum sub lege, sub ira Dei & morte, aspicere Deum non ut misericordiarum Patrem, sed ut tortorem, hostem, tyrannum. Hoc vere est agere in servitute & captivitate Babylonica, fæviffimæque torqueri in ea. Lex enim non liberat à peccato & morte, sed peccatum revelat & auget, & iram operatur. Illa servitus, inquit, desit, non amplius premit & contristat nos &c.
