4. Quomodo facta sit reconciliatio? Addit Apostolus, ἀποκτείνας τὴν ἔχθραν ἐν ἀυτῷ, quod recte de σταυρῷ cum Syro, Chrysostomo, Oecumenio & Theophylacto intelligitur, etsi nonnulli legisse videantur ἐν ἑαυτῷ in seipso, ut cum Vulgata reddidit B. Lutherus, & in Codd. quibusdam se invenisse testatur Beza. Res eodem recidit: quia in seipso, scil. immolato in cruce, per quam reconciliationem factam jam dixerat, inimicitias sustulit, in qua chirographum affixit, Col. II. v. 14. ut tolleretur Dei & hominum inimicitia. Ex peccato illa enata erat, ob quod DEUS hominem juste aversatus, homo vero male sibi conscius Deum fugit. Peccato igitur per sacrificium crucis ablato inimicitia illa perempta est. Διὰ τῶ σταυρᾶ inquit Photius, γὰρ λύσας τῷ θανάτῳ ἀυτῶ τὴν ἁμαρτίαν καὶ τὴν ἔχθραν ἔλυσεν.

## 2:17
Vers. 17. Καὶ ἐλθὼν ἐυηγγελίσατο ἐιρήνην ὑμῖν τοῖς μακρὰν καὶ τοῖς ἐγγύς.) Taken from Is. LVII. 19. Ἐλθὼν and πορευθεὶς are words often redundant, as we have said elsewhere, or if they signify anything, they signify diligent effort. Christus ἐυηγγελίσατο is a word of simple action for a double action. For the sense is, he caused peace to be preached. See Matt. XXVIII. v. 19, Mark XVI. v. 15, Luke XXIV. 47, Acts I. 8. Those who were far off, namely from the knowledge of the truth, are the Gentiles: Those near, the Jews, because of the prophecies concerning the Messiah, and the traditions concerning eternal life. See above 13. In the Manuscript: Εἰρήνην ὑμῖν τοῖς μακρὰν, καὶ εἰρήνην ὑμῖν τοῖς ἐγγύς.

This is the third thing, an addition pertaining to the covenant of grace. It was not enough that peace was acquired through the cross with the enmity removed. It had to be announced through the Gospel of peace, so that we might enjoy the same, and be admitted to the covenant of grace, which on the part of GOD was sanctioned on the cross, but on our part is accepted through the Gospel. Nor is there need that we take the word of simple action here for a double action. For Christ himself announced it, and through the Apostles, who are his ministers. Conf. Gal. II. 8, 2 Cor. V. 18, 19, 20, Acts X. 36. The Jews were near not only because of the prophecies both concerning the Messiah and those which they had concerning eternal life, unless it had been revealed by God, but also because of their actual reception into the covenant of grace through the sacrament of circumcision.

Latin:

Vers. 17. Καὶ ἐλθὼν ἐυηγγελίσατο ἐιρήνην ὑμῖν τοῖς μακρὰν καὶ τοῖς ἐγγύς.) Sumptum ex Es. LVII. 19. Ἐλθὼν & πορευθεὶς voces sunt sæpe παρέλκυσαι, ut alibi diximus, aut si quid significant, significant operam diligentem. Christus ἐυηγγελίσατο est vox actionis simplicis pro actione duplici. Sensus enim est, fecit ut pax prædicaretur. Vide Matth. XXVIII. v. 19. Marci XVI. v. 15. Luc. XXIV. 47. Actor. I. 8. Qui longe erant, nempe à cognitione veri, sunt gentes: Qui prope Judæi, ob prophetias de Messia, & traditiones de vita æterna. Vide supra 13. In Manuscripto: Εἰρήνην ὑμῖν τοῖς μακρὰν, καὶ εἰρήνην ὑμῖν τοῖς ἐγγύς.

Tertium hoc est, ad fœdus gratiæ pertinens προσκείμενον. Non satis erat, acquisitam per crucem dempta inimicitia pacem. Annuncianda ea erat per Evangelium pacis, ut eadem frueremur, & ad fœdus gratiæ admitteremur, quod ex parte DEI in cruce sancitum est, ex parte autem nostri per Evangelium suspicitur. Non autem opus est, ut vocem actionis simplicis pro actione duplici hic accipiamus. Nam Christus ipse annunciavit, & per Apostolos, qui Ministri ejus sunt. Conf. Gal. II. 8. 2. Cor. V. 18. 19. 20. Act. X. 36. Judæi prope fuerunt non tantum ob prophetias tum de Messia, tum eas quas de vita æterna habebant, nisi à Deo ea revelata fuisset, sed etiam ob actualem per sacramentum circumcisionis in fœdus gratiæ receptionem.

## 2:18
Vers. 18. Ὅτι δι' ἀυτῶ ἔχομεν τὴν προσαγωγὴν ἀμφότεροι ἐν ἑνὶ πνέυματι πρὸς τὸν Πατέρα) ἐν here is placed twice for per: Those who have received the Holy Spirit, they are certain that they are children of GOD, and therefore with great freedom and confidence they address GOD as their Father, Rom. VIII. 15. Gal. IV. 6. concerning the word προσαγωγὴ see Rom. V. 2. it occurs also below III. 12. Προσαγωγὴ is an approach as if to a King. Προσάγειν is to admit, to give access, 1. Pet. III. 18.

Latin:

Vers. 18. Ὅτι δι' ἀυτῶ ἔχομεν τὴν προσαγωγὴν ἀμφότεροι ἐν ἑνὶ πνέυματι πρὸς τὸν Πατέρα) ἐν hic bis pro per positum: Qui Spiritum sanctum accepere, illi certi sunt, se esse DEI filios, ac proinde magna cum libertate ac fiducia DEUM ut Patrem suum alloquuntur, Rom. VIII. 15. Gal. IV. 6. de voce προσαγωγὴ vide Rom. V. 2. occurrit & infra III. 12. Προσαγωγὴ aditus quasi ad Regem. Προσάγειν admittere, aditum dare, 1. Petr. III. 18.

## 2:19
Vers. 19. Therefore then you are no longer strangers and sojourners) You are no longer excluded from the right of citizenship in the people of God as before. See above 12. Ξένοι are those who are traveling abroad: Πάροικοι are those who have a domicile in some place, without the right of citizenship, inhabitants in the digests, and elsewhere.

But fellow-citizens of the saints) For the Church is a certain polity, not a fellowship of places, but of laws. In the Glossary συμπολίτης is a fellow-citizen. But the Latins say, my citizen, my fellow-townsman, that is, of the same city or municipality.

And of the household of God) belonging to the family of God, ὀικεῖοι as Gal. VI. 10. 1. Tim. V. 8. or ὀικιακοὶ, as Matth. X. 25. 36. In Hebrew and Syriac בּנֵי בַיִת are those who belong to the family of someone, such as in the first place are the children of the family.

This fourth thing is the addition of free access and admission to God: Which the Apostle uses at once either as an argument for the announced peace, or explains peace in this way exegetically, that it consists in this, that we both have access through Christ as Mediator. This is a sign of friendship, free access to a friend: Which had been blocked by sin, but now has been opened by Christ the only Mediator, John XIV. 16. 1. Tim. II. 5. Moreover, it is not found in the more approved Greek Codices ἐν

him, but through him. Through Christ in one Spirit we have access to the Father. A notable testimony here of the most holy Trinity. The persons are distinguished by their properties ad extra, Christ is the Mediator: the Holy Spirit is the Paraclete, instructing, governing, and teaching us. The Father is the fountain and origin of grace. For here it is regarded κατ' ἔξω with respect to the sons not by nature, but by adoption. Whom he embraces with fatherly love on account of Christ the only-begotten Son. Now therefore the communion of the covenant is in the open: For those to whom the Gospel of peace has been preached, or peace has been announced, and who have access through Christ to the Father's grace in the Holy Spirit, they are no longer outside the covenant of grace. Thus at the same time that most grievous misery is excluded, that they were previously ἄθεοι without the knowledge of the true GOD. For through the Gospel we receive the knowledge of the true GOD: And who can be destitute of the knowledge of the true GOD, who know the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, and have access to the Father through the Son and the Holy Spirit. The Apostle therefore infers from these things that the Ephesians are not guests and strangers. Believers are indeed called sojourners and strangers, 1. Pet. II. 8. but with respect to the world and earthly life, Heb. XI. 25. but not with respect to the heavenly kingdom, and the Church, conf. Ps. XXXIX. 13. He infers that they are no longer outside the covenant, or strangers to the covenant.

He infers that they are no longer without God, nay rather that they are fellow-citizens of the saints, and of the household of God, fellow-citizens of the saints, and also of one polity with the faithful Israelites, or rather with the holy Patriarchs of all ages, Kings, and other Elect, who already act in the heavenly polity, and with those who, living in the Church, have their citizenship in heaven, Phil. III. 20. and thus just as they are received into the covenant with God, and are also members of God's household. Crocius succinctly explains the metaphor of the city here thus: A city has a Magistrate and citizens, it has its own laws, its own exercises, its own privileges, its own weapons. So also the Church. Christ has been given by the Father as ruler and head, the saints are the citizens, of whom some triumph in heaven, others fight on earth, each placed in his own place and order divinely. It has the law of faith and works or charity. It has its own works, common and proper to each order. Common are the exercises of piety, the fruits of the Spirit placed in all goodness, justice and truth, Eph. V. 9. Gal. V. 22. the privileges are adoption, remission of sins, access to the Father, being heard, consolation in adversities, defense, sanctification, the right of eternal life, freedom from the ceremonial law, from condemnation, from the kingdom of sin, from the power of Satan, from eternal death. The weapons of this city are prayers and tears. The Ephesians have attained the communion of all these. And the Apostle called them not only citizens of GOD but members of the household. Therefore they do not act in the world without GOD, but use GOD familiarly. In a family there is domestic and civil society and conversation; And it is more to be a member of the household of a Prince than a citizen of the Republic over which he presides. Thus also the city Gal. IV. 25. Heb. XII. 22. and the house of God 1. Tim. III. 15. is called the Church.

Latin:

Vers. 19. Ἄρα ὦν ὀυκέτι ἐςὲ ξένοι καὶ πάροικοι) Non ultra estis exclusi à jure civitatis in populo Dei ut ante. Vide supra 12. Ξένοι sunt, qui peregrinantur: Πάροικοι, qui domicilium in aliquo loco habent, sine jure civitatis, incolæ in digestis, & alibi.

Ἀλλὰ συμπολῖται τῶν ἁγίων) Est enim Ecclesia πολιτεία quædam, non locorum, sed legum consortio. In Glossario συμπολίτης Concivis. At Latini dicunt, civis meus, municeps meus, id est, ejusdem civitatis aut municipii.

Καὶ ὀικεῖοι τῶ Θεῶ) ad familiam Dei pertinentes, ὀικεῖοι ut Gal. VI. 10. 1. Tim. V. 8. vel ὀικιακοὶ, ut Matth. X. 25.36. Ebraice & Syriace בּנֵי בַיִת sunt ii, qui ad familiam alicujus pertinent, quales primo loco sunt filii familias.

Quartum hoc est προσκείμενον liberi aditus & admissionis ad Deum: Quo simul vel tanquam argumento utitur Apostolus annunciatæ pacis, vel ἐξηγητικῶς ita pacem explicat, quod in eo sita sit, quod utrique aditum habemus per Christum ceu Mediatorem. Indicium hoc est amicitiæ, liber ad amicum aditus: Qui interclusus erat per peccatum, jam vero apertus est per Christum Mediatorem unicum, Joh. XIV. 16. 1. Tim. II. 5. Cæterum non habetur in Codd. Græcis probatioribus ἐν

αὐτῷ sed δι' αὐτῦ. Per Christum in uno Spiritu ad Patrem habemus accessum. Insigne hic sacrosanctæ Trinitatis testimonium. Distinguuntur personæ suis proprietatibus ad extra, Christus Mediator est: Spiritus S. Paracletus, nos instruens, gubernans & docens. Pater est fons & origo gratiæ. Nam respicitur hic κατ' ἔξω respectu filiorum non φύσει, sed θέσει. Quos paterno amore propter Christum Filium unigenitum complectitur. Jam ergo fœderis communio in aprico est: Quibus enim Evangelium pacis prædicatum, vel pax annunciata est, quique aditum per Christum habent ad Patris gratiam in Spiritu Sancto, illi non sunt amplius extra fœdus gratiæ. Ita simul excluditur illa miseria gravissima, quod antea ἄθεοι fuerint sine veri DEI notitia. Nam per Evangelium veri DEI notitiam accipimus: Et qui cognitione veri DEI destitui possunt, qui Patrem, Filium & Spiritum S. cognoscunt, & ad Patrem per Filium & Spiritum Sanctum aditum habent. Infert itaque Apostolus ex hisce, Ephesios non esse hospites & peregrinos. Dicuntur quidem fideles advenæ & peregrini, 1. Pet. II. 8. sed respectu mundi & terrenæ vitæ, Ebr. XI. 25. non autem respectu cœlestis regni, & Ecclesiæ, conf. Psal. XXXIX. 13. Infert, eosdem non esse amplius extra fœdus, aut peregrinos à fœdere.

Infert, eos non esse amplius sine Deo, imo esse συμπολῖτας τῶν ἁγίων, καὶ ὀικείς τῶ Θεῶ, concives sanctorum, nec non unius politiæ cum Israëlitis fidelibus, vel potius sanctis omnium seculorum Patriarchis, Regibus, aliisque Electis, qui in cœlesti jam politia agunt, & cum illis, qui in Ecclesia viventes, πολίτευμα suum in cœlis habent, Phil. III. 20. adeoque perinde, ut illos in fœdus receptos cum Deo, nec non domesticos Dei. Metaphoram civitatis succincte hic ita explicat Crocius: Civitas habet Magistratum & cives, suas habet leges, sua exercitia, sua privilegia, sua arma. Sic quoque Ecclesia. Christus à Patre datus est rector & caput, sancti sunt cives, quorum alii triumphant in cœlo, alii militant in terra, suo quisque loco & ordine divinitus collocati. Habet legem fidei & operum seu charitatis. Habet sua opera communia & cujusque ordinis propria. Communia sunt exercitia pietatis, fructus Spiritus positi in omni bonitate, justitia & veritate, Eph. V. 9. Gal. V. 22. privilegia sunt adoptio, remissio peccatorum, aditus ad Patrem, exauditio, consolatio in adversis, defensio, sanctificatio, jus aternae vitae, libertas a lege ceremoniali, a condi- mnatione, a peccati regno, a potestate Satanae, ab eterna morte. Arma hujus civitatis sunt preces & lacrymae. Horum omnium communionem assecuti sunt Ephesii. Nec cives tantum DEI sed dome- sticos dixit Apostolus. Non ergo sine DEO in mundo agunt, sed DEO utuntur familiariter. Familiae inest domestica & civilis societas & con- versatio; Et plus est, esse Domesticum Principis, quam civem Reipublicae, cui praeest. Sic & civi- tas Gal. IV. 25. Ebr. XII. 22. & domus Dei 1. Tim. III. 15. vocatur Ecclesia.

## 2:20
Vers. 20. Built upon the foundation of the Apostles and Prophets) Prophets, namely of the New Testament, who are next in dignity to the Apostles, 1 Cor. XII. 28. Below III. 5. IV. 11. Words used by way of metaphor are applied differently by different people; Jesus is the foundation, 1 Cor. III. 11, and the Apostles are the foundations, Rev. XXI. 14. The testimony of the Apostles concerning those things which they saw, heard, and handled, agreeing with the Prophetic predictions, makes the faith of Christians unshakable, just as foundations do the Jerusalem temple 1 Kings V. 17. VII. 9.

Being himself Jesus Christ the cornerstone) who is the head of the corner, Matt. XXI. 42, from Ps. CXVIII. 22. The very word cornerstone is in the Greek. Isa. XXVIII. 16. In the corners is the chief strength by which buildings are supported, as we said regarding that passage in Matthew. A cornerstone is that from which angled structures take their beginning.

Latin:

Vers. 20. Ἐποικοδομηθέντες ἐπὶ τῷ θεμελίῳ τῶν Ἀποστό- λων καὶ Προφητῶν) Prophetarum, nempe Novi Testamenti, qui proximi dignitate Apostolis, 1. Cor. XII. 28. Infra III. 5. IV. 11. Voces per translationem usurpatae aliis aliter aptantur, Jesus fundamentum, 1. Cor. III. 11. & Apostoli fundamenta, Apoc. XXI. 14. Apostolorum testimonium de iis, quae viderunt, audiverunt, palparunt, congruens cum praedictionibus Propheticis, inconcussam facit fidem Chri- stianorum, sicut fundamenta templum Hierosolymitanum 1. Reg. V. 17. VII. 9.

Ὄντος ἀκρογωνιαίου αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦ χριστοῦ) qui κεφαλὴ γων- νίας, Matth. XXI. 42. ex Psal. CXVIII. 22. ipsa vox ἀκρο- γωνιαίου est in Graeco. Esa. XXVIII. 16. in angulis praecipua vis est, qua aedificia sustinentur, ut ad illum Matthaei lo- cum diximus. Ἀκρογωνιαῖος λίθος est is, unde angulatae structurae initium ducunt.

## 2:21
In whom all the building fitly framed together) In the glosses I fit together. It is the same as being joined together by joints and bands, Coloss. II. 19. But there the likeness is drawn from the human body, here from the building of a temple. In a structure, some stones are closer to the foundation, others more remote, and that through many degrees: In the body there is the head, there are arteries, there are veins, there are muscles, there are nerves. Thus in the Church there are and always ought to be degrees, through which the Spirit of God flows even to the smallest parts.

Grows) That is, rises up. It is a metaphor in an allegory. For to be increased properly belongs to a natural body. It is customary to say of buildings that they rise: Whose walls now rise. But neither is the other outside of usage.

Into a holy temple in the Lord) Just as the oracle is the adytum of the highest heaven, so the palace is the figure of the Church. In the Lord means through Christ: And it is a noun for the relative pronoun him after the manner of the Hebrews.

Latin:

Ἐν ᾧ πᾶσα ἡ οἰκοδομὴ συναρμολογουμένη) In glossis συν- αρμολογῶ compagino. Idem est δι' ἀφῶν καὶ συνδεσμῶν συμ- βιβαζόμενον, Coloss. II. 19. Sed ibi a corpore humano similitudo ducitur, hic a templi aedificio. In structura la- pides sunt alii propiores fundamento, alii remotiores, idque per multos gradus: In corpore est caput, sunt arteriae, sunt venae, sunt musculi, sunt nervi. Sic in Ecclesia sunt & semper esse debent gradus, per quos DEI Spiritus ad minimas usque partes influit.

Αὔξει) Id est assurgit. Est translatio in Allegoria. Nam augeri proprie est corporis naturalis. Surgere de aedificiis dici solet: Quorum jam maenia surgunt. Sed nec alterum extra usum est.

Εἰς ναὸν ἅγιον ἐν κυρίῳ) Sicut דְּבִיר adytum caeli summi, ita הֵיכַל Ecclesiae figura. Ἐν Κυρίῳ per Christum: Et est nomen pro relativo Pronomine αὐτῷ more Ebraeorum.

## 2:22
V. 22. In whom you also are built together for a habitation of God in the Spirit) Through Christ and through his Spirit you also are the temple of God. For habitation signifies a tabernacle, Exod. XV. 17, and afterwards a temple, which succeeded into the place of the tabernacle. Not only the whole collection of the faithful, but also individual believers are rightly called a temple, because the Spirit of God dwells in their minds, 1 Cor. III. 16, 17. VI. 19. 2 Cor. VI. 16. Philo on rewards: For it is in truth a palace and house of God, the wise mind.

The Apostle makes the faithful not only a member of God's household, but also the house and temple of God: in which God wills to dwell no differently than he dwelt in the tabernacle and temple, nay, in a far more intimate way, because that temple was only a type of the mystical temple, in which he dwells through faith, and which he fills with all divine fullness, Eph. III. 17, 19. Note here 1. the foundation, 2. the cornerstone, 3. the structure, 4. the building, 5. the architect, 6. the end of the building. The foundation of the Apostles and Prophets is called the doctrine, comprised in the holy scripture. By Prophets, however, not the Prophets of the New, but of the Old Testament are to be understood. For only thus is the foundation adequate. For the whole Church must lean upon it. The proclamation of the Prophets, however, who were under the New Testament, extends itself to a few, whereas on the contrary the doctrine of the Prophets of the Old Testament, which is comprised in the code of the Old Testament, together with the doctrine of the Apostles exhibited in the books of the New Testament, is the foundation of the whole Church, outside of which no other can be named that is of divine origin, that is solid and immovable, that is invariable and perpetual, for all believers and all times. Whence this understanding of the Prophets of the New Testament by William Estius is utterly disapproved.

For it is nowhere read that the Church is founded upon the doctrine of such Prophets: But rather, the prophecies of such were to be judged by the Church according to the rule of Apostolic and Prophetic doctrine, according to that saying in 1 Cor. XIV: Let two or three prophets speak, and let the others judge. Which, indeed, would not be said of the Apostles sent by Christ, who are joined here with the Prophets. Theodoret also explained this regarding the Prophets of the Old Testament, saying they are not Prophets of the New Testament, but of the Old. He placed the Apostles first, however, because we received the preaching through them. Thus also Theophylact, with Chrysostom, says that the Apostles were placed first, even though they were later in time, which was done, according to Chrysostom, because it is manifestly certain that they laid this foundation, but the Prophets are added afterward, lest the foundation appear to have been laid recently, but rather that minds might be led back to ancient times, in which the very same foundation was laid, and the old Church built upon it, indeed the Ephesians themselves. Therefore, Chrysostom says it is to be understood that here the Gentiles also have the Patriarchs in the place of a foundation. Guil. Estius brings forward these reasons why the Apostles were placed first, having regard not to time but to dignity: 1. because the Apostles saw and heard Christ present and teaching: 2. because they received greater gifts of grace: 3. which pertains most to the present matter, because the Apostles are foundations closer to the Church, as those who not only left behind them the doctrine of the true faith, by which the Church is founded, as the Prophets did, but also, by their preaching, converted multitudes from among the Jews and Gentiles, and founded and built up the Church according to the state of the New Testament. Hence it is that the Church is called Apostolic in the symbol of faith from them as such founders and planters: not likewise Prophetic from the Prophets. Nevertheless, just as Christ alone is the primary foundation of the Church: so only the Apostles and Prophets, by reason of the doctrine delivered and to be held by faith, are acknowledged by the Church as its secondary foundation. Whence it follows that the Christian and Catholic faith, although it can and ought to be explained by other Prelates and Doctors of the Church, can nevertheless not be increased at all, just as it cannot be diminished. Thus Estius. Which things are to be duly noted, and opposed to the twin hypothesis of the Papists: the one concerning Peter as the foundation of the Church after Christ, to whom they attribute this prerogative as proper to him above the rest of the Apostles, and Bellarmine applies the very passage of Isaiah XXVIII. 16 to this; the other concerning the power of the Roman Pontiff to increase the Christian faith with new articles of faith. Most Reformed—Bullinger, Musculus, Aretius, Zanchius, Hemingius, Beza, along with Anselm and Lombard—call Christ the foundation of the Apostles and Prophets. But Christ is the cornerstone here, in the foundation of the Apostles and Prophets. Crocius does not think there is any difference in the matter, because Christ is the nucleus of the doctrine, Acts X. 43, 1 Cor. I. 23. But since the Apostle distinguishes between the foundation and the cornerstone, it is not right to confuse them. Nor is Christ called the foundation of the Apostles and Prophets, either because they laid it by their ministry, or because they, with others, are built upon Christ. Musculus, Gualtherus, and Aretius join both these causes; Crocius approves only the former. The Apostles and Prophets are not viewed here as Architects who laid the foundation: But their doctrine is called the foundation, upon which the faithful are built: In which doctrinal foundation the doctrine concerning Christ stands out. Nor are the Apostles and Prophets viewed here by reason of their persons, insofar as they themselves, just as others, are built upon the foundation of the Church, but by reason of their doctrine, which God willed to be the foundation of the Church. Blessed Nic. Hunnius says in his Treatise on the Dissent of the Reformed and Calvinists, that it is an organic or ministerial foundation, §. 83. But he calls Christ the substantial foundation. I find no reason why we should not follow him. Thomas on this passage says: The Apostles are called foundations (Rev. XXI. 17) insofar as their doctrine announces Christ, Matthew XVI: Upon this rock I will build my Church. Estius is not inappropriate on this passage: Christ himself cannot be understood in this place by the foundation of the Apostles and Prophets, of whom it is said in 1 Cor. III: No one can lay another foundation besides that which is laid, which is Jesus Christ. For in the following words he calls Christ the highest cornerstone, as distinct from this foundation. Therefore, the foundation of the Apostles and Prophets must be interpreted intransitively, that is, the foundation which the Apostles and Prophets are. Whence also in Rev. XXI the twelve Apostles are called the twelve foundations of the heavenly Jerusalem. But Christ is called the foundation in one way, and the Apostles and Prophets in another. He is the primary foundation: They are the secondary. For Christ is the foundation of the Church insofar as the entire building of the Church is solidified and sustained by faith in him placed upon the foundation. Which indeed pertains to Christ alone, because there is salvation in no other, for there is no other name under heaven given to men in which it is necessary to be saved, Acts IV. The Apostles and Prophets, however, are foundations, or, as is said here, the foundation of the same Church through their ministry, insofar as they announced to men the doctrine of salvation, which is in Christ alone, received divinely—the Prophets indeed more obscurely, but the Apostles more manifestly and fully.

II. The cornerstone is Christ, whom David teaches that God has made the cornerstone of His Church, as he was rejected in his passion by the architects, the priests, and the Pharisees, Ps. CXVIII. 22, as interpreted by Christ himself, Matt. XXI. 42, Mark XII. 10, Luke XX. 17, by Peter, Acts IV. 11, 1 Pet. II. 6, 7, and also by Saint Paul, Rom. IX. 33. And Isaiah calls that stone a tried and precious foundation stone, a cornerstone well founded, in whom he who believes does not flee or is not confounded, chap. XXVIII. 16, 1 Pet. II. 6, Rom. X. 11. He is called the cornerstone, however, because he unites as if joined together both walls of the ecclesiastical building, and as if connecting Jews and Gentiles, sustains the whole building. Because the Jews and Gentiles were two different walls, therefore he places Christ in the corner, who unites both, says Crocius from Calvin. Theophylact says, Christ is he who embraces all things. For this cornerstone grasps the walls and foundations on both sides. Observe, however, how he sometimes confesses that Christ binds together the entire mass of the building in the upper part, when he calls him the head. Sometimes in the lower part, when he calls him the cornerstone, and elsewhere he also names him the foundation.

III. As regards the structure, the Apostle uses a genuine word, ἐποικοδομηθέντες, which has reference to the foundation upon which the faithful are built up, as a building must be built upon a solid foundation if it is to stand firmly, Matt. VII., and συναρμολογημένη (οἰκοδομὴ), which word Grotius explains not inappropriately. Ambrose renders it compacted, Jerome joined together, elsewhere suitably joined, because not just any part, or any whatsoever, as Zanchius and Heinsius with Erasmus, but the whole Church is understood as joined together by the reason of all its parts, as Estius and Crocius acknowledge. The Church is united and glued to its head, Christ, as to a foundation through faith: all its parts also are fitted and united among themselves through the unity of faith and mutual charity.

IV. The building which is erected is called a temple; because the building of the mystical temple or Church was prefigured by the Solomonic temple, which is called a holy temple in the Lord, because it has all holiness in Christ the Lord: The Jerusalem temple was called holy relatively, by reason of those things which were done in it, of the divine manifestation, and of sacred functions and offices, Ps. 79:1, Dan. 8:11. With better right the Church is called a holy temple, in which the Lord dwells by his grace, which he sanctifies both by the imputation of Christ's righteousness and by the sanctification of his Spirit. Gentiles and the profane and the impure were kept away from the Jerusalem temple. But to the mystical temple, the Church, the Gentiles called and gathered were no less than the faithful from the Jews. In the building of the Jerusalem temple there was various material, precious stones, gold, silver, and others, Exod. 25:3 ff. In this temple of hearts is the wood of incorruptibility, the purple and scarlet of the blood of Christ, which is red, the gems of the various gifts of the Holy Spirit, the gold of faith, living stones, that is, believers, 1 Pet. 2:5. Its construction was done without great sound and noise, 1 Kings 6:7. Thus in silence and without noise is the construction of the mystical temple done. Is. 30:15, Luke 17:20. But it is especially worthy of admiration that in this temple there are so many temples, that is, living stones, and yet it is one temple, which was not found in the Jerusalem temple.

V. The architect is the Holy Spirit, so that you may be a habitation of God, ἐν πνεύματι, the Vulgate in the Holy Spirit. But the name ἁγίῳ is not in the Greek text; it is certain, however, that the Holy Spirit is understood. Chrysostom wishes a spiritual temple to be signified. But it is more convenient that the supreme Architect be designated. And Theophylact and Oecumenius have διὰ Πνεύματος. Through him the Apostles and Prophets as secondary architects both laid foundations and built upon them. Through his grace we also are built up as living stones. 1 Pet. 2.

VI. Finally, the end is shown in the Ephesians, in whom (the Lord Christ Jesus) you also are built. Some understand the temple. But a temple is not built in a temple, but in the Lord. Whether it is viewed as a foundation, or as the cornerstone of the foundation, as Estius, that is, upon which cornerstone, as one joining different walls, you also Ephesians, who are Gentiles, together with the faithful who are from the Jews, are built, and by that very building you are made a habitation of God, that is, a temple in which God may dwell, and that through the operation of the Holy Spirit. The end, therefore, is that they may be a habitation of God, namely a temple, in which God may delight to dwell, such as are the truly penitent and faithful. Is. 57, John 14:23, Eph. 3:17, 1 Cor. 3:17, ch. 6:16, 2 Cor. 6:16. If the end of those who build is a gift, not so that the house may be empty, but that it may be inhabited: the end of the temple of the Lord, which he himself builds, is certainly that it may be a habitation of the Lord. Cf. Ps. 132:13, 14.

Latin:

V. 22. Ἐν ᾧ ὑμεῖς συνοικοδομεῖσθε εἰς κατοικητήριον τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐν Πνεύματι) Per Christum & per ejus Spiritum vos quo- que sitis DEI templum. Nam מִשְׁכָּן κατοικητήριον si- gnificat tabernaculum, Exod. XV. 17. & postea templum, quod in tabernaculi locum successit. Non tantum tota fidelium collectio, sed & fideles singuli recte appellantur templum, quia in ipsorum mentibus Spiritus Dei habitat, 1. Cor. III. 16, 17. VI. 19. 2. Cor. VI. 16. Philo de praemiis: Καὶ γάρ ἐστι τῷ ὄντι βασίλειον καὶ οἶκος Θεοῦ, σοφῶ διάνοια.

Non modo domesticus DEI, sed & domum & templum DEI facit Apostolus fideles: in quo Deus habitare velit non secus, atque habitavit in tabernaculo, & templo, imo longe intimiori modo, quia templum illud typus tantum erat mystici templi, in quo per fidem habitat, quodque omni plenitudine divina replet, Eph. III. 17. 19. Notan- tur autem hic 1. fundamentum, 2. lapis angularis, 3. structura, 4. aedificium, 5. architectus, 6. finis aedificii. Fundamentum Apostolorum & Propheta- rum dicitur doctrina, scriptura sacra comprehen- sa. Per Prophetas autem non Novi, sed Veteris Te- stamenti Prophetae intelligendi. Nam ita demum adaequatum est fundamentum. Ei enim inniti de- bet tota Ecclesia. Prophetarum autem, qui sub Novo Testamento fuere, praeconium ad paucos sese extendit, cum contra Prophetarum Veteris Testamenti doctrina, quae codice Veteris Testa- menti comprehensa est, cum doctrina Aposto- lorum libris Novi Testamenti exhibita totius Ecclesiae fundamentum sit, extra quod nullum aliud, quod divinae originis, quod solidum & im- motum, quod invariabile ac perpetuum, omnium fidelium, omnium temporum sit, nominari po- test. Unde Guilielmo Estio de Prophetis Novi Te- stamenti haec intelligi prorsus improbatum est.

Nam super hujusmodi Prophetarum doctrina fundatam esse Ecclesiam, nusquam legitur : Quin potius talium Prophetiæ juxta regulam Apostolicæ & Propheticæ doctrinæ ab Ecclesia dijudicandæ erant, secundum illud 1. Cor. XIV. Prophetæ duo aut tres dicant, & cæteri dijudicent. Quod profecto de Apostolis à Christo missis, qui hic cum Prophetis junguntur, non diceretur. De Prophetis Veteris Testamenti etiam exposuit Theodoretes, Prophetas dicit non Novi Testamenti, sed Veteris. Præposuit autem Apostolos, quia per eos prædicationem accepimus. Ita quoque cum Chrysostomo Theophylactus prius Apostolos positos, etsi fuere tempore posteriores dicens, quod ideo factum Chrysostomo, quod manifeste constet, eos hoc fundamentum posuisse, subjungi autem Prophetas, ne videatur fundamentum recens positum, sed deducantur animi ad vetera tempora, quibus idem prorsus fundamentum sit jactum, & super eo vetus Ecclesia structa, imo ipsi Ephesii. Ideo Chrysostomus intelligi inquit, hic & gentes fundamenti loco Patriarchas habere. Guil. Estius has causas affert, cur præpositi sint Apostoli, non temporis sed dignitatis habita ratione, 1. quia Apostoli Christum præsentem ac docentem viderunt, & audiverunt : 2. quia dona majora gratiæ accepere : 3. quod ad rem præsentem maxime facit, quia Apostoli sunt fundamenta Ecclesiæ propinquiora, ut qui non tantum doctrinam veræ fidei, qua fundatur Ecclesia, post se reliquerunt sicut Prophetæ, sed & sua prædicatione multitudines ex Judæis & gentibus convertendo, fundarunt & ædificarunt Ecclesiam secundum statum novi Testamenti. Hinc est quod ab illis tanquam ejusmodi fundatoribus & plantatoribus Ecclesia in symbolo fidei vocatur Apostolica: non item à Prophetis Prophetica. Veruntamen sicut solus Christus est primarium Ecclesiæ fundamentum : Ita soli Apostoli & Prophetæ ratione doctrinæ traditæ ac fide tenendæ agnoscuntur ab Ecclesia ut fundamentum ejus secundarium. Unde consequens est, fidem Christianam & Catholicam, etsi per alios Ecclesiæ Prælatos & Doctores explicari possit & debeat : augeri tamen omnino non posse, sicut nec minui. Hæc Estius. Quæ probe notanda, & geminæ Pontificiorum hypothesi opponenda, alteri de Petro post Christum fundamento Ecclesiæ, cui hanc prærogativam propriam faciunt præ reliquis Apostolis, & Bellarm. locum ipsum Esa. XXVIII. 16. applicat : alteri de potestate Pontificis Romani augendi fidem Christianam novis fidei articulis. Reformati plerique Bullingerus, Musculus, Aretius, Zanchius, Hemingius, Beza cum Anselmo & Lombardo Christum fundamentum Apostolorum & Prophetarum dicunt. Sed Christus hic lapis angularis est, in fundamento Apostolorum & Prophetarum. Non putat quidem, in re ullam esse differentiam, Crocius, quia Christus doctrinæ nucleus est, Act. X. 43. 1. Cor. I. 23. Sed quum distinguat Apostolus fundamentum & lapidem angularem, non fas est ea confundere. Nec fundamentum Christus dicitur Apostolorum & Prophetarum, sive quia id illi suo ministerio posuerint, sive quod illi cum aliis Christo superstructi. Quam utramque causam conjungunt Musculus, Gualtherus, & Aretius, priorem tantum approbat Crocius. Non hic Apostoli ac Prophetæ spectantur ut Architecti, qui fundamentum posuere : Sed doctrina eorum dicitur fundamentum, cui superstructi fideles sunt: In quo doctrinali fundamento eminet doctrina de Christo. Neque hic spectantur Apostoli & Prophetæ ratione personarum suarum, prout ipsi æque ac alii superstructi sunt fundamento Ecclesiæ, sed ratione doctrinæ suæ, quam Deus voluit esse Ec- clesiæ fundamentum. B. Nic. Hunnius dicit in T. de dissensu Reform. Calvin. fundamentum organi- cum, vel ministeriale, §. 83. Christum vero vocat fundameutum substantiale. Quem cur non sequa- mur, nullam invenio rationem. Thomas in h. l. Apostoli, inquit, in tantum dicuntur fundamenta, (Apoc. XXI. 17.) in quantum eorum doctrina Chri- stum annunciat, Matth. XVI. super hanc petram ædificabo Ecclesiam meam. Non inconvenien- ter Estius in hunc locum: Non potest hoc loco per fundamentum Apostolorum & Prophetarum ipse Christus intelligi, de quo 1. Cor. III. fundamentum aliud nemo potest ponere præter id, quod positum est, quod est Christus Jesus. Verbis enim sequentibus Chri- stum vocat summum angularem lapidem, tanquam ab hoc fundamento diversum. Igitur fundamentum Apostolorum & Prophetarum intransitive expo- nendum, id est, fundamentum, quod sunt Apostoli & Prophetæ. Unde & Apoc. XXI. duodecim Apo- stoli vocantur duodecim fundamenta cælestis Jeru- salem. Aliter autem Christus, aliter Apostoli & Prophetæ fundamentum vocantur. Ille primarium fundamentum: Isti secundarium. Christus enim fundamentum est Ecclesiæ, quatenus per ejus fidem in fundamento collocatam solidatur & sustentatur universum Ecclesiæ ædificium. Quod quidem soli Christo competit, quia non est in alio aliquo salus, nec enim aliud nomen est sub cælo datum homini- bus, in quo oporteat salvos fieri, Act. IV. Apostoli vero & Prophetæ sunt fundamenta, vel, ut hic dicitur, fundamentum ejusdem Ecclesiæ per suum ministerium, quatenus doctrinam salutis, quæ in solo Christo est, divinitus acceptam hominibus an- nuntiarunt, Prophetæ quidem obscurius, Apostoli autem manifestius ac plenius.

II. Lapis angularis est Christus, quem David, prout in passione rejectus ab Archite&is, sacer- dotibus & Pharisæis, Deum angularem lapidem Ecclesiæ suæ fecisse docet Psal. CXVIII. 22. in- terprete ipso Christo, Matth. XXI. 42. Marc. XII. 10. Luc. XX. 17. Petro, Act. IV. 11. 1. Petr. II. 6. 7. nec non sancto Paulo, Rom. IX. 33. Et Esaias la- pidem illum fundamenti lapidem probatum & pretiosum, lapidem angularem probe fundatum, in quem qui credit, non fugit aut confunditur, cap. XXVIII. 16. 1. Petr. II. 6. Rom. X. 11. Dicitur autem lapis angularis, quod utrumque quasi mu- rum Ecclesiastici ædificii coagmentatum uniat, ac quasi connectens Judæos & gentes totum ædificium sustentet. Quia duo diversi parietes erant Judæi & gentes, ideo Christum in angulo ponit, qui utrosque coadunet, inquit Crocius è Calvino. Theophylactus, qui cuncta, inquit, complectitur, Christus est. Angularis namque hic lapis utrinque parietes prehendit & fundamenta. Adverte autem, quemadmodum nonnunquam superiori in parte constringere Christum universam ædificii molem fatetur, cum eundem caput appellat. Nonnunquam inferiori, cum angularem dicit, alibi præterea & hunc fundamentum nuncupat.

III. Structuram quod attinet, voce genuina uti- tur Apostolus, ἐποικοδομηθέντες, quæ respectum habet ad fundamentum, super quod extruuntur fi- deles, ut ædificium super fundamentum solidum extruendum est, si inuote consistere debeat, Matth. VII. & συναρμολογημένη (οἰκοδομὴ) quod verbum non inconcinne explicat Grotius. Compactum red- dit Ambrosius, compaginatum Hieron. congruen- ter coagmentatum alibi, quia non tantum pars ali- qua, vel quævis, ut Zanchius & Heinsius cum Erasmo, sed tota Ecclesia omnium partium ratione coag- mentata, ut Estius & Crocius agnoscunt, intelli- gitur. Ecclesia unitur, & conglutinatur capiti Christo, ceu fundamento per fidem: Omnes e- tiam partes ejus inter se coaptantur & uniuntur per unitatem fidei & charitatis mutuam.

IV. Ædificium, quod extruitur, templum dici- tur; quia per templum Salomonæum præfigura- tum fuit ædificium templi mystici vel Ecclesiæ, quæ templum sanctum in Domino dicitur, quia omnem sanctitatem habet in Christo Domino: Templum Hierosolymitanum sanctum dicebatur relative, ratione eorum, quæ in illo fiebant, ma- nifestationis divinæ, & functionum ac officio- rum sacrorum, Psal. LXXIX. v. 1. Dan. IIX. vers. 11. Potiori jure Ecclesia templum sanctum dicitur, in qua habitat Dominus gratia sua, quam sanctificat tum justitiæ Christi imputatione, tum Spiritus sui sanctificatione. A templo Hierosolymitano arce- bantur gentiles ac profani & impuri. Ad templum autem mysticum Ecclesiam non minus gentes vo- catæ sunt & aggregatæ, quam fideles e Judæis. In templo Hierosolymitano extruendo varia erat materia, lapides pretiosi, aurum, argentum, & alia, Exod. XXV. 3. seqq. In hoc templo cordium lignum incorruptibilitatis est, purpura, & cocci- num sanguinis Christi rubicundi, gemmæ vario- rum Spiritus sancti charismatum, aurum fidei, la- pides vivi, hoc est, credentes, 1. Petr. II. 5. Illius extructio sine sonitu magno & strepitu fiebat 1. Reg. VI. 7. Ita in silentio & absque strepitu fit extructio templi mystici. Es. XXX. 15. Luc. XVII. vers. 20. Sed imprimis admiratione dignum est, quod in hoc templo tot sint templa, quod lapides vivi, & tamen unum sit templum, quod in templo Hierosolymitano non inveniebatur.

V. Architectus est Spiritus sanctus, ut sitis ha- bitaculum Dei, ἐν πνεύματι, Vulgatus in Spiritu sancto. Sed nomen ἁγίῳ non est in Græco textu; Intelligi tamen Spiritum sanctum certum est. Chrysostomus vult significari templum spirituale. Sed convenientius est, designari Architectum su- premum. Et Theophylactus & Oecumenius habent διὰ Πνεύματος. Per ipsum Apostoli & Prophetæ ceu secundarii architecti & fundamenta jecerunt, & superstruxerunt. Per ipsius gratiam & nos su- perextruimur ceu lapides vivi. 1. Petr. II.

VI. Finis denique in Ephesiis monstratur, in quo (Domino Christo Jesu) & vos ædificamini. Aliqui templum intelligunt. Sed templum in tem- plo non ædificatur, sed in Domino. Sive ut funda- mentum spectetur, sive ut lapis fundamenti angu- laris, ut Estius, hoc est, super quo lapide angulari, tanquam diversos parietes conjungente, etiam vos Ephesii, qui gentiles estis, una cum fidelibus, qui ex Judæis sunt, ædificamini, ipsaque ædificatione effici- mini habitaculum Dei, id est, templum, in quo Deus habitet, idque per operationem Spiritus sancti. Finis ergo est, ut sint habitaculum Dei, templum nem- pe, in quo gestiat Deus habitare, quales sunt vere pœnitentes & fideles. Es. LVII. Joh. XIV. v. 23. Eph. III. 17. 1. Cor. III. 17. cap. VI. 16. 2. Cor. VI. 16. Si finis eorum, qui ædificant, donum est, non ut va- cua sit domus, sed inhabitetur: Templi Domini, quod ipse extruit, finis utique est, ut habitaculum id sit Domini. Conf. Psal. CXXXII. 13. 14.

## 3:1 Argument
CHAPTER III. ARGUMENT & PARTITION.

The Apostle proceeds in celebrating the grace shown to the Gentiles, and in these Ephesians, for whose sake he was a prisoner, and who had known the dispensation of the grace given to him for them, and from those things which he wrote a little before, they could know his wisdom in the mystery of Christ, which was not once so known, but now has been revealed through the Holy Spirit. He celebrates, however, especially that the Gentiles are co-heirs of eternal life, partakers of the promise through the Gospel, of which he himself was made a minister among the Gentiles to enlighten them, what the dispensation of the mystery is, so that the manifold wisdom of God may be made known even to the Angels themselves according to the eternal purpose which he made in Christ, in whom we have confidence and free access; whence he prays that they may not grow weary because of his afflictions. He prays to God, however, that he may strengthen them, and that Christ may dwell in them through faith, that they may know his immense love, and be filled with all the fullness of God, and he vows that he be glorified perpetually in the Church.

There are two parts; the former is Didactic-Paranetic, in which he teaches through the Gospel concerning that greatest grace, that the Gentiles have the hope of a heavenly inheritance, warning them not to fail on account of their afflictions, up to verse 13. The latter is εὐκτική, in which he prays for the strengthening of the Ephesians and the glorification of God up to verse 22.

PART I. DIDACTIC-PARANETIC.

Concerning the hope of the Gentiles for a heavenly inheritance.

Ver. 1. Τουτου χαριν εγω Παυλος) It not infrequently happens to Paul that, having begun a discourse and not finished it, he interjects a huge parenthesis. Then, when he is about to return to that which he had conceived in his mind, he introduces another construction, which agrees with the former not in words but in sense. Here the parenthesis begins with the words ειγε ηκουσατε, and ends with the words τῆς δυναμεως αυτου. Then, when according to grammatical rules he should have said, ελαχιστοτερῳ παντων ελαβον την χαριν ταυτην, he says, εμοι τῳ ελαχιστοτερῳ παντων εδοθη ἡ χαρις αυτη, clearly in the same way as in Gal. II. 6, when he had said, απο των δοκουντων, and one would expect, ουδεν ελαβον, he subjoined ουδεν προσανεθεντο.

Ο δεσμιος του χριστου Ιησου) This genitive denotes the cause for which. Thus also 2 Tim. I. 8 and Philem. verses 1 and 9, for which he said below in IV. 1, δεσμιος εν Κυριῳ. Thus the bonds of the Gospel, Philem. 13. This epistle was written, as were also those to the Colossians, the Philippians, the other to Timothy, and that to Philemon, within that two-year period during which Paul lived in Rome bound to a soldier, Acts XXVIII. 16, 30.

ὑπερ ὑμων) because I called the uncircumcised Gentiles to the Gospel, I was accused by the Jews, and because of that I came to Rome in chains.

Among the antitheses of the state of misery and the state of grace, that one still remains, that the Ephesians were once without hope of eternal life, but now have the hope of the inheritance of eternal life, which he has reserved for the last place, intending to assert this benefit somewhat more fully as the most eminent one. This is the goal of all benefits. For the fact that they have Christ as Mediator, that they are in the Church of Christ, that they rejoice in the covenant with GOD in the promises of grace, that they are members of God's household, and through Christ have access to the Father in the Holy Spirit, all those things are directed toward this, that they may finally obtain the inheritance of eternal life, and be heirs of GOD and co-heirs of Christ. But in order that this may be asserted, and so that the Ephesians may be confirmed in all those things, and the Apostle not be troubled by affliction and chains, he establishes his divinely given office and the heavenly revelation of the mystery concerning Christ, and also concerning the calling of the Gentiles, and from this, indeed, that supreme benefit he explains, that the Gentiles are fellow-heirs, and fellow-members of the body, and fellow-partakers of the promise of God in Christ, and he makes them most certain of it through the Gospel and his ministry entrusted to him among the Gentiles through the mystery of the divine dispensation, through the increase of angelic knowledge in the multiform wisdom of God, through the eternal purpose of God, through the confident and free access to God the Father. Τούτου χάριν he refers himself to the preceding, For His sake, because you are built up with other Gentiles by my ministry upon the foundation of the Apostles and Prophets, I Paul am the prisoner of Jesus Christ. The Devil cannot bear this, nor his instruments the Jews, Christ-killers, enemies of the Gentiles. But I am a prisoner, not only for your sake, but also for your good. There is no need here for hyperbaton, much less that we should, with Jerome, impute a solecism to Paul. For how easy it is to understand the substantive verb 'am'? Which Camerarius does not deny, although he is prone to hyperbaton, and that a rather long one, not up to v. 7 inclusive, but up to the end of v. 12, so that, namely, there is no need for a change of case in v. 8. This hyperbaton, he says, if it is less approved by anyone, he must complete it by understanding the sentence, which is in the words ἀποσιώπησις: As if this were said, for these things, I am that Paul, who am held prisoner for your sake, Gentiles: Or for this cause I that prisoner Paul for the Gentiles write these things. Chrysostom, Theophylact, Anselm, Haymo, Erasmus, Bucer, Bullinger, Musculus, Beza, Hyperius, Crocius, and others, also supply with us the verb AM, so that the discourse is completed in this verse, and does not hang until v. 7, as the Greek scholia and Grotius, or even until 14, as others wish. ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν is not because I called the Gentiles to the Gospel. That was already included in the previous τούτου χάριν, but for your good, as Grotius himself, the text so requiring, is soon about to explain.

Latin:

CAPUT III. ARGUMENTUM & PARTITIO.

Progreditur Apostolus in celebranda gratia gen- tibus exhibita, & in his Ephesiis, quorum gratia vinctus erat, quique dispensationem gratiae sibi in ipsos datae cognoverant, & ex iis, quae paulo ante scripsit, sapientiam suam co- gnoscere poterant in mysterio Christi, quod olim non ita cognitum fuit, nunc per Spiri- tum sanctum revelatum est. Celebrat autem imprimis, quod gentes sint cohaeredes vitae ae- ternae, participes promissionis per Evangeli- um, cujus ipse minister factus inter gentiles ad illuminandos eos, quaenam sit mysterii di- spensatio, ut etiam Angelis ipsis nota fiat multivaria Dei sapientia secundum aeter- num propositum, quod in Christo fecit, in quo fiduciam & aditum liberum habemus; Unde precatur, ne segnescant ob afflictiones ipsius. Deum autem orat, ut eos corroboret, utque Christus habitet in ipsis per fidem, ut cogno- scant amorem ejus immensum, & omni ple- nitudine Dei impleantur, eumque glorificari perpetuo in Ecclesia vovet.

Partes duae sunt, prior est Didactico-Parane- tica, qua de gratia, maxima illa, quod gentes spem haereditatis coelestis habeant, per Evange- lium docet, monens, ne ob afflictiones suas de- ficiant, ad v. 13. Posterior est ευκτικη, qua orat pro confortatione Ephesiorum, & glorificatione Dei ad vers. 22.

PARS I. DIDACTICO- PARÆNETICA.

De spe gentilium de haereditate coelesti.

Vers. 1. Τουτου χαριν εγω Παυλος) Non raro evenit Paulo, ut inchoato, nec absoluto sermone, interjiciat ingentem παρενθεσιν. Deinde ubi rediturus est ad id, quod animo conceperat, inferat aliam constructionem, quae non verbis sed sensu cum prioribus consonat. Hic παρενθετικη incipit in verbis ειγε ηκουσατε, finit in verbis τῆς δυναμεως αυτου. Deinde cum secundum Grammaticas regulas dicendum fuisset, ελαχιστοτερῳ παντων ελαβον την χαριν ταυτην, dicit, εμοι τῳ ελαχιστοτερῳ παντων εδοθη ἡ χαρις αυτη, plane, quo- modo Gal. II. 6. cum dixisset, απο των δοκουντων, & expe- ctaretur, ουδεν ελαβον, subintulit ουδεν προσανεθεντο.

Ο δεσμιος του χριστου Ιησου) Hic Genitivus causam ob. quam denotat. Sic & 2. Tim. I. 8. & Philem. vers. 1. & 9. pro quo infra IV. 1. dixit, δεσμιος εν Κυριῳ. Sic δεσμα Ευαγγελιου, Philem. 13. scripta haec epistola, ut & ad Co- lossenses, Philippenses, altera ad Timotheum, & illa ad Philemonem, intra biennium illud, quo Paulus militi alligatus Romae vixit Act. XXVIII, 16. 30.

ὑπερ ὑμων) quia gentes incircumcisas vocavi ad Evan- gelium, accusatus sum a Judaeis, & ex eo vinctus Romam veni.

Inter αντιθεσεις status miseriae & status gratiae, illa adhuc superest, quod Ephesii quondam sine spe fuerint aeternae vitae, jam vero spem habeant haereditatis vitae aeternae, quam postremo loco reservavit, aliquanto plenius hoc beneficium ceu eminentissimum asserturus. Meta haec est omnium beneficiorum. Nam quod Christum habeant Me- diatorem, quod in Ecclesia Christi sint, quod in foedere cum DEO gratiae promissionibus gau- deant, quod domestici Dei sint, & per Christum in Spiritu sancto accessum ad Patrem habeant, ea omnia eo directa sunt, ut tandem haereditatem vitae aeternae consequantur, ac haeredes DEI & cohaeredes Christi sint. Ut autem hoc asseratur, adeoque tle omnibus illis confirmentur Ephesii, nec afflictione & vinculis turbentur Apostoli, officium suum divinitus datum, & coelestem my- sterii de Christo, nec non de vocatione gentium revelationem adstruit, hinc vero supremum illud beneficium exponit, quod gentiles sint συγκληρο- νόμοι, καὶ σύσσωμοι, καὶ συμμέτοχοι τῆς ἐπαγγελίας Θεῦ ἐν χριστῷ, & de eo illos quam certissimos reddit per Evangelium & ministerium suum inter gen- tes sibi creditum per dispensationis divinæ myste- rium, per cognitionis Angelicæ in multiformi Dei sapientia incrementum, per æternum Dei proposi- tum, per fiducialem & liberum ad Deum Patrem accessum. Τούτου χάριν refert sese ad præcedentia, Ejus causâ, quod vos superstruamini cum aliis gentibus meo ministerio super fundamentum A- postolorum & Prophetarum, ego Paulus vinctus sum Jesu Christi. Ferre non potest id Diabolus, nec organa ejus Judæi, Christicidæ, gentium ho- stes. Vinctus autem sum, non tantum propter vos, sed etiam vestro bono. Nullo hic opus hyperbato, nedum ut cum Hieronymo Solœcismum Paulo im- pingamus. Quam proclive enim est, subintellige- re verbum substantivum sum? quod non diffitetur Camerarius, tametsi pronus in hyperbaton, idque longiusculum, non usque ad v. 7. inclusive, sed us- que ad finem v. 12. ut scilicet opus non sit mutatio- ne casus in v. 8. Hoc inquit, hyperbaton, si cui minus probatur, eum perficere intelligendo sententiam opor- tet, quæ est in verbis ἀποσιώπησις: Quasi hoc dica- tur, ob hæc, ego Paulus ille sum, qui teneor vinctus propter vos gentes: Vel hac de causa ego ille vinctus Paulus propter gentes hæc scribo. Chrysostomus, Theophylactus, Anselmus, Haymo, Erasmus, Bu- cerus, Bullinger, Musculus, Beza, Hyperius, Cro- cius, alii, supplent etiam nobiscum verbum SUM, ut hoc versu sermo absolvatur, non pendeat ad v. 7. usque, ut Græca scholia & Grotius, vel etiam ad 14. ut alii volunt. ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν non est, quod gentes vocavi ad Evangelium. Illud in prioribus τούτου χάριν jam comprehensum erat, sed vestro bono, ut mox Grotius ipse, textu sic requirente, exposi- turus est.

## 3:2
V. 2. Ἔιγε ἠκούσατε) For your good these things happened to me, namely if only you have well understood those things which I have already said and will say. The Hebrew שמע is properly to hear, but elsewhere it is εἰδέναι and γνώσκειν, through which words it is also sometimes translated.

Τὴν οἰκονομίαν τῆς χάριτος τοῦ Θεῦ, τοῦ δοθείσης μοι εἰς ὑμᾶς) מנת תחנות אל עלי: that part of the Apostleship to me which pertains to the Gentiles, Gal. II. 7. 8. Acts XI, 15. In the Manuscript it is τῆς χάριτος αὐτοῦ. Οἰκονομία is called the assignment of parts, such as stewards are accustomed to make in a household, 1 Cor. IX. v. 17. above I. v. 10. But he calls the Apostleship itself χάριν κατ᾿ ἐξοχὴν, the highest honor in the Churches, as also Gal. II. 9. Thus Rom. I. 5. χάριν καὶ ἀποστολὴν, that is, the grace of the apostleship. He adds εἰς ὑμᾶς: עליכם, the apostleship, I say, to be administered concerning you.

There is no need for the word ἠκούσατε to be abstracted from its proper meaning, which it also includes, since hearing through report and proclamation, through which it had undoubtedly become known to the Ephesians during that three-year stay among the Ephesians, from Paul's own mouth, is designated as joined with understanding. If only you have understood by hearing the dispensation of the grace of God, which is given to me for you. Chrysostom and Theophylact understand it concerning revelation; but that is explained more distinctly in the following verse. More correctly, therefore, others understand the office οἰκονομίαν with Musculus and Aretius: because ministers are stewards of goods not their own, but of their Lord. By the grace of GOD, not metonymically the Gospel, as Zanchius and Hyperius, but properly the grace, by which God makes friends out of enemies, His own household and children out of strangers, saved out of the lost, and that freely, without any merit of ours, Crocius understands. But that it is more conveniently explained concerning the Apostleship, the words εἰς ὑμᾶς teach. The ministry of the Gospel is indeed a dispensation of the grace of God, but because it is added not concerning the dispensation, but concerning the grace of God, which is given to me among you, there is no doubt that the Apostleship among them is understood. To which also the translation of the Blessed Luther goes. Crocius explains. Given, that is, entrusted, so that he may dispense among you, that is, the Gentiles. That is rightly said of the Apostleship, that it was entrusted to the Apostle among the Gentiles, Acts IX. 25. ch. XXII. 2. ch. XXVI. 17. 18. not so conveniently of saving grace. Therefore, the grace of the Apostleship entrusted to Paul among the Gentiles, or the dispensation of that grace. He does not say τὴν οἰκονομίαν τὴν δοθεῖσαν, but τῆς χάριτος τῆς δοθείσης, and to that grace of the Apostleship entrusted to him, the mystery concerning Christ was revealed to him, of which v. 3. Finally, the Apostle himself explains the grace thus in v. 8.

Latin:

V. 2. Ἔιγε ἠκούσατε) Vestro bono mihi hæc evenere, vi- delicet si modo ea bene intellexeritis, quæ jam dixi & dicam. שמע Ebræum proprie est audire, sed alibi εἰδέναι & γνώ- σκειν per quas voces etiam vertitur interdum.

Τὴν οἰκονομίαν τῆς χάριτος τοῦ Θεῦ, τοῦ δοθείσης μοι εἰς ὑμᾶς) מנת תחנות אל עלי: partem illam Apostolatus mihi quæ ad gentes pertinet, Gal. II. 7. 8. Act. XI, 15. In Manu- scripto est τῆς χάριτος αὐτοῦ. Οἰκονομία dicitur assignatio partium, qualem in familia facere solent dispensatores, 1. Cor. IX. vers. 17. supra I. v. 10. χάριν autem κατ᾿ ἐξοχὴν vocat ipsum Apostolatum, summum in Ecclesiis honorem, ut & Gal. II. 9. Sic Rom. I. 5. χάριν καὶ ἀποστολὴν, id est χάριν ἀποστολῆς. Addit εἰς ὑμᾶς: עליכם Apostolatum inquam circa vos administrandum.

Non opus est, ut verbum ἠκούσατε a proprio si- gnificatu abstrahatur, quem etiam includit, cum auditus per famam & præconium, per quod E- phesiis sine dubio id intra triennium illud commo- rationis inter Ephesios, innotuerat ex ipsiusmet Pauli ore, cum intellectu conjunctus designatur. Si modo intellexistis audiendo dispensationem gratiæ Dei, quæ mihi data est in vos. Chrysostomus & Theo- phylactus de revelatione intelligunt; Sed ea distin- ctius exponitur versu sequ. Rectius ergo alii offi- cium οἰκονομίαν intelligunt cum Musculo & Aretio: quia ministri dispensatores sunt bonorum non propriorum, sed Domini sui. Per gratiam DEI non Evangelium metonymice, ut Zanchius & Hyperius, sed proprie gratiam, qua Deus ex ini- micis amicos, ex alienis domesticos ac filios suos, ex perditis salvos facit, idque gratis, nullo nostro merito, intelligit Crocius. Sed de Apostolatu con- venientius exponi illud εἰς ὑμᾶς docet. Est qui- dem Evangelii ministerium dispensatio gratiæ Dei, sed quia additur non de dispensatione, sed de gratia Dei, quæ data est mihi apud vos, Apo- stolatum inter ipsos intelligi, minime est dubium. Quo etiam abit Beat. Lutheri translatio. Crocius explicat. Datum, id est concreditum, ut dispenset apud vos, id est, gentes. Id de Apostolatu recte dicitur, concreditum fuisse Apostolo inter gentes, Act. IX. 25. cap. XXII. 2. cap. XXVI. 17. 18. non ita commode de gratia salutifera. Gratia ergo Apostolatus credita Paulo inter gentes, vel dispensatio gratiae ipsius. Non dicit τὴν οἰκονομίαν τὴν δοθεῖσαν, sed τῆς χάριτος τῆς δοθείσης, & ad illam χάριν Apostolatus ipsi creditam revelatum est ipsi mysterium de Christo, quo de v. 3. Denique ita gratiam explicat Apostolus ipse v. 8.

## 3:3
V. 3. Ὅτι κατ' ἀποκάλυψιν ἐγνώρισέ μοι τὸ μυστήριον) In the Manuscript ἐγνωρίσθη μοι, just as the Latin and the Syrian read: namely, not only by that first revelation, of which Acts IX, but also by many subsequent ones, of which 2 Cor. XII. 1. 7. It was made clear to me, he says, more openly than to Peter himself, that the burdens of Jewish rites were not only not to be imposed upon the Gentiles, but not even to be observed by the Jews henceforth as if by necessity of precept, see Rom. VII and Gal. IV. Therefore Paul, being more enlightened in this matter as a Prophet, enlightened Peter. He rightly calls it a mystery, because it had not been sufficiently clear even to the chief of the Apostles before.

Καθὼς προέγραψα ἐν ὀλίγῳ) προέγραψα ἐν ὀλίγῳ, that is ὀλίγῳ πρότερον ἔγραψα, I wrote a little before: namely in the two preceding chapters, where many things were said about this mystery.

Latin:

V. 3. Ὅτι κατ' ἀποκάλυψιν ἐγνώρισέ μοι τὸ μυστήριον) In Manuscripto ἐγνωρίσθη μοι, quomodo & Latinus legit & Syrus: nempe non tantum prima ista revelatione, de qua Act. IX. sed & multis subsequentibus, de quibus 2. Cor. XII. 1. 7. patuit mihi, inquit, apertius, quam ipsi Petro, rituum Judaicorum onera non modo non imponenda gentibus, sed ne a Judaeis quidem observanda posthac quasi ex praecepti necessitate, vide Rom. VII. & Gal. IV. itaque Paulus in hac re, ut Propheta magis illustratus Petrum illustravit. Merito autem μυστήριον vocat, quod etiam Apostolorum praecipuis non satis patuerat antea.

Καθὼς προέγραψα ἐν ὀλίγῳ) προέγραψα ἐν ὀλίγῳ, id est ὀλίγῳ πρότερον ἔγραψα, paulo ante scripsi: nempe capitibus duobus praecedentibus, ubi multa de hoc mysterio dicta.

## 3:4
V. 4. Πρὸς ὃ) that is, by which you may more certainly believe that I was given by God as an Apostle to the Gentiles.

Δύνασθε ἀναγινώσκοντες) Repeating several times those things which I have already written, δὶς καὶ τρὶς τὰ καλά.

Νοῆσαι τὴν σύνεσίν με ἐν τῷ μυστηρίῳ τοῦ χριστοῦ) You will be able to perceive from thence, how far I, God granting, have penetrated into the knowledge of that secret.

Latin:

V. 4. Πρὸς ὃ) id est, quo certius credatis me a Deo datum Apostolum gentibus.

Δύνασθε ἀναγινώσκοντες) Repetentes aliquoties ea, quae jam scripsi, δὶς καὶ τρὶς τὰ καλά.

Νοῆσαι τὴν σύνεσίν με ἐν τῷ μυστηρίῳ τοῦ χριστοῦ) Percipere inde poteritis, quousque ego in illius arcani cognitione, Deo dante, penetraverim.

## 3:5
V. 5. Which in other generations was not made known to the sons of men) לבני אדם. For those things which are in Isaiah, and others of the ancient Prophets, are very general, and before the event were very obscure.

As it is now revealed to his holy Apostles and prophets in the Holy Spirit) Namely, according to the promise of Christ, John XVI. 12. Understand the prophets of the New Testament, as we said above II. 20. Peter had learned something in the matter of Cornelius, Paul more afterwards, and others after Paul.

The mystery, which was revealed to Paul, is not to be restricted to the secret concerning the calling of the Gentiles. He said τὸ μυστήριον in general, the mystery of Christ or concerning Christ, the mystery which became known to him through revelation. But not only that was made known to him, that the Gentiles were to be called: But the whole mystery concerning Christ was manifested to him through divine revelation, Gal. I. 12. which is situated neither solely, nor chiefly in the calling to the kingdom of Christ: much less in the doctrine concerning the burdens of Jewish rites no longer being imposed: Nor are many things found handed down concerning it in the two previous chapters, since they were touched upon almost lightly, and by occasion of the called Gentiles, with mention of the middle wall of partition being removed, and the law being made void. Furthermore, that understanding of the Apostle in the mystery of Christ, which they could know from the reading of the two preceding chapters, extends itself more widely than to that doctrine. For he had treated of many other notable mysteries of the Evangelical doctrine, of spiritual blessing in Christ, of election in Christ, of the adoption of the sons of God and predestination to the same through Christ, of grace and love in Christ the beloved Son of God, of redemption through the blood of Christ, of the remission of sins on account of Christ, of the recapitulation of all things in Christ, of the inheritance to which we are predestined, who first hoped in Christ; of the sealing of the Holy Spirit and the earnest of the inheritance, of faith in Christ, of the Spirit of wisdom and revelation, of the hope of our calling, of the excitation of faith, of the resurrection of Christ, and exaltation above all things, of Christ the head of the Church, of the death of sin and the punishment of sins, concerning the immense grace of God in Christ, concerning our spiritual vivification in Christ, concerning resurrection and translation into the heavenly places, concerning salvation, concerning the state under gentilism, or outside of Christ; concerning the state of grace in Christ, concerning reconciliation made through the cross of Christ, concerning free access to the Father through Christ, concerning the foundation of the Apostles and Prophets, in which Christ is the cornerstone, and what other many things occur in those chapters, most full of heavenly doctrines.

Meanwhile, we do not deny that the abolition of Jewish rites is specifically regarded, or rather the calling of the Gentiles to the inheritance of the heavenly kingdom: since the Apostle in explaining this mystery concerning Christ primarily directed his finger to the same, because this, now revealed with other things pertaining to the confessedly great mystery to the holy Apostles and Prophets, is more abundantly [revealed], 1 Tim. III. 16, just as he expressly designates it here v. 6. That καθὼς προέγραψα ἐν ὀλίγῳ, not only the blessed Ægidius Hunnius refers to another Epistle formerly written to the Ephesians, which does not exist today, but others also have referred to it among Theodoret and Hugo Cardinalis, and also Calvin, but there is no need to refer to it, since the preceding chapters are conveniently regarded, as has been observed by Theodoret, Theophylact, Lyranus, Bullinger, Musculus, Zanchius, Aretius, Beza, and Crocius, and also Cornelius a Lapide. Nor indeed [does] ἐν ὀλίγῳ [mean] a little while ago, but in few words; because he has briefly comprised those things which he had delivered more prolixly in speech, when he explained to them the whole counsel of God concerning salvation, Acts XX. verse 27. There is no reason, therefore, why the words of the Apostle should be inverted and supplemented here in the Grotian manner. But it is a doubt, in what way the mystery concerning Christ is said to be unknown to the sons of men in other ages? Where it must be said entirely that this is to be understood concerning some part of the mystery concerning Christ, not concerning the whole mystery: See Heb. XIII. 8, Acts XV. verse 11, that indeed it was not known in part, just as this ignorance is restricted to that, that the Gentiles are co-heirs, which part is of the mystery totally spoken of. Then that perhaps the sons of men designate the Gentiles, who were in the world without Christ, but not all who are sons of God, as Bullinger explained. For the promise made to the Patriarchs Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob was clear, and in the Patriarchal Church without doubt clearly proposed concerning the blessing of all the nations of the earth in the Messiah, and the explicit prophecy of Jacob concerning Shiloh, to whom the Gentiles shall adhere, Gen. XLIX. 10. Or if this is understood with Chrysostom, Theophylact, Jerome, and others concerning all mortals, even the pious among the Jewish people, nay even the Prophets, it must be accepted κατά τι, that is, that that mystery was not so known to other ages as it is now manifested, since neither the time nor the manner of the calling of the Gentiles was clearly established to the holy Peter himself, Acts X, namely, whether without the obligation of circumcision and other ceremonies, or indeed, in the manner of proselytes in the Old Testament, when, and how, or by what means the Gentiles are to be admitted in the New Testament. Yet that it was not entirely unknown that the Gentiles were to be called to the Church, the Prophetic prophecies sufficiently teach: And therefore one must distinguish between general and special knowledge: The former is not to be denied to previous ages, even if the latter was reserved for the times of the New Testament. The words themselves testify that the Apostle is speaking comparatively and in a certain respect, ὡς νῦν ἀποκαλύφθη, as it is now revealed. Someone will say, says Theophylact, what then? Did not the Prophets also foresee this? Otherwise, how would Christ say these things, 'Moses and the Prophets wrote of me,' and, 'Search the scriptures: for they are they which testify of me'? First, indeed, Paul means this, that the mystery was not revealed to all men, then that it did not become known to the aliens, the sons of men, and finally that this sacrament was not equally known to the Prophets as it is now opened to the Apostles. And those things which are in the new testament have been made known to the Prophets through the Holy Spirit. For if the Spirit had not instructed Peter in the least, he would not have received Cornelius himself, nor those who were with Cornelius. But this revelation was made both to the Apostles and to the Prophets, who were so called in the New Testament, 1 Cor. XIV. verse 3 seqq., but by the immediate inspiration of the Spirit, because it is added BY THE SPIRIT. Nor would it have been restricted to the Apostles and Prophets if it were a matter of any manifestation whatsoever. For thus it extends itself to all the faithful. The blessed Franzius in Schol. Sacrific. disp. IX. th. 90, explaining the mode of revelation, that is, that in this way the Gentiles under Christ the head were to coalesce into one body with the people of God, is taxed by Cloppenburg in Syntagm. Exercit. disp. XII. th. 19. But rashly. For the Apostle explicitly notes the mode ὡς νῦν. Nor is that head of the mystery, that now the Gentiles belong by equal right to the inheritance, to the mystical body of Christ, and to the participation of the promises, nay that the Patriarchal Church is to be established and erected among the Gentiles as the sons of promise, Rom. IX. 8, because the Jews were repudiated on account of their hardness of heart. This is surely new, and unheard of in all ages before this; whence such a calling of the Gentiles is rightly proposed by the Apostle as an illustrious example of our gratuitous reconciliation with God. But indeed from that, Cloppenburg wrongly infers that the Gentiles were called in no way under the Old Testament. But what is said in Deut. X. 14, 15, that God chose only the Israelites before all peoples, pertains to establishing the dwelling of the Church under the O.T., not to designating the limits of grace. Thus also Amos III. 2, 'you only have I known,' pertains to the prerogatives of grace, not to grace itself.

Latin:

V. 5. Ὃ ἐν ἑτέραις γενεαῖς οὐκ ἐγνωρίσθη τοῖς υἱοῖς τῶν ἀνθρώπων) לבני אדם. Nam quae sunt apud Esaiam, & Prophetarum veterum alios, valde generalia sunt, & ante eventum erant perobscura.

Ὡς νῦν ἀπεκαλύφθη τοῖς ἁγίοις Ἀποστόλοις αὐτοῦ καὶ προφήταις ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ) Nempe ex promisso Christi, Joh. XVI. 12. Prophetas intellige Novi Testamenti, ut diximus supra II. 20. Aliquid didicerat Petrus in re Cornelii plus postea Paulus, & post Paulum alii.

Mysterium, quod revelatum Paulo, non restringendum ad arcanum de vocatione gentium. Dixit τὸ μυστήριον in genere, mysterium Christi vel de Christo, mysterium quod sibi innotuit per revelationem. Non autem id tantum ipsi innotuit, quod gentes vocandae sint: Sed universum de Christo mysterium ipsi per divinam revelationem manifestatum est, Gal. I. 12. quod nec unice, nec praecipue in vocatione ad regnum Christi situm est: nedum in doctrina de rituum Judaicorum oneribus non amplius imponendis: Nec de ea multa tradita reperiuntur prioribus duobus capitibus, cum fere leviter, & ex occasione vocatarum gentium ea tacta, mentione sublati parietis intergerini, & evacuatae legis. Porro σύνεσις illa Apostoli in mysterio Christi, quam e relectione duorum praecedentium capitum cognoscere poterant, latius se porrigit, quam ad illam doctrinam. Egerat enim de multis aliis insignibus doctrinae Evangelicae mysteriis, de benedictione spirituali in Christo, de electione in Christo, de adoptione filiorum Dei & praedestinatione ad eandem per Christum, de gratia & dilectione in Christo Dei Filio dilecto, de redemptione per sanguinem Christi, de remissione peccatorum propter Christum, de recapitulatione omnium in Christo, de hereditate, ad quam praedestinati sumus, qui prius speravimus in Christum; de obsignatione Spiritus sancti & arrha hereditatis, de fide in Christum, de Spiritu sapientiae & revelationis, de spe nostrae vocationis, de excitatione fidei, de resuscitatione Christi, & exaltatione super omnia, de Christo Ecclesiae capite, de morte peccati & poena pecca- torum, de immensa Dei gratia in Christo, de vivi- ficatione nostri spirituali in Christo, de resuscita- tione & translatione in cælestia, de salvatione, de statu sub gentilismo, vel extra Christum; de statu gratiæ in Christo, de reconciliatione per crucem Christi facta, de libero accessu ad Patrem per Chri- stum, de fundamento Apostolorum & Prophetarum, in quo lapis angularis Christus est, & quæ alia plu- ra in illis capitibus, doctrinis cælestibus refertis- simis occurrunt.

Interim rituum Judaicorum sublationem specia- tim respici non abnuimus, vel potius vocationem gentium ad hæreditatem regni cælestis: Siquidem hoc in mysterio de Christo explicando imprimis ad eandem digitum intenderit Apostolus, quod id revelatum nunc cum aliis ad ὁμολογουμένως μέ- γα μυστήριον pertinentibus S. Apostolis & Prophetis uberius sit, 1. Tim. III. 16. quemadmodum id exprefse hic designat v. 6. Illud καθὼς προέγραψα ἐν ὀλίγῳ, non Beat. Ægid. Hunnius tantum, ad aliam ad Ephesios quondam scriptam Epistolam refert, quæ hodie non extet, sed retulerunt etiam alii apud Theodoretum & Hugo Cardin. nec non Calvinus, sed eo non opus est referre, quum præcedentia capita commode respiciantur, ut ob- servatum Theodoreto, Theophylacto, Lyrano, Bul- lingero, Musculo, Zanchio, Aretio, Bezæ; & Cro- cio, nec non Cornelio a Lapide. Nec vero ἐν ὀλί- γῳ paulo ante, sed paucis; quia breviter com- plexus est ea, quæ prolixius sermone tradiderat, cum omne consilium Dei de salute ipsis exposuit, Act. XX. vers. 27. Non ergo est, quod hic inver- tantur & suppleantur Apostoli verba more Gro- tiano. Dubium autem est, qua ratione aliis ætati- bus filiis hominum mysterium de Christo ignotum dicatur? Ubi omnino dicendum, quod id de par- te aliqua mysterii de Christo, non de toto myste- rio accipiendum sit: Vid. Ebr. XIII. 8. Act. XV. vers. 11. quod nimirum id ex parte cognitum non fuerit, quemadmodum hæc ἄγνοια restringitur ad illud, quod gentes sint cohæredes, quæ pars est mysterii totaliter dicti. Deinde quod vel filii ho- minum designentur gentes, quæ sine Christo fuere in mundo, non vero omnes, qui DEI filii, sicut Bullingerus exposuit. Nam clara erat promissio Patriarchis Abrahamo, Isaaco & Jacobo facta, & in Ecclesia Patriarchali sine dubio luculenter pro- posita de benedictione omnium nationum terræ in Messia, & disertum vaticinium Jacobi de Schi- lo, cui adhæsuræ sint gentes, Gen. XLIX. 10. Vel si de universis mortalibus, etiam piis in po- pulo Judaico, imo Prophetis quoque hoc intel- ligatur cum Chrysostomo, Theophylacto, Hiero- nymo & aliis, κατά τι hoc accipiendum erit, quod nempe non adeo notum fuerit illud mysterium aliis ætatibus, uti nunc manifestatum est, quum nec tempus nec ratio vocationis gentium plane constiterit ipsimet sancto Petro, Act. X. num sci- licet sine circumcisione aliarumque ceremonia- rum obligatione, an vero, more proselytorum in Veteri Testamento, quando, & quomodo aut quibus mediis adsciscendæ sint gentes in Novo Testamento. Non tamen prorsus incognitum fuisse, gentes vocatum iri ad Ecclesiam, vaticinia Prophetica satis docent: Ideoque distinguen- dum inter cognitionem generalem & specialem: Illæ prioribus ætatibus deneganda non est, etsi hæc reservata fuerit temporibus Novi Testamen- ti. Comparatè & secundum quid loqui Aposto- lum, verba ipsa testantur, ὡς νῦν ἀποκαλύφθη sic- ut nunc retectum est. Dicet aliquis, inquit Theophylactus, quid ergo? Nonne & id præscive- runt Prophetæ? Alioqui quo pacto Christus hæc diceret, Moses & Prophetæ de me scripserunt, &, Scrutamini scripturas: Illæ enim sunt, quæ de me testificantur? Primum quidem id Paulus sentit, non cunctis fuisse hominibus mysterium revela- tum, deinde neque alienigenis illud innotuisse filiis hominum, demum haud æque Prophetis fuisse hoc cognitum sacramentum, ut in præsenti Apostolis apertum est. Et qui in novo sunt testamento Pro- phetis per Spiritum sanctum notiora sunt facta. Nam si Petrum minime Spiritus instruxisset, nec Cornelium ipse, nec qui cum Cornelio erant, una excepisset. Hæc autem revelatio facta est tum Apo- stolis, tum Prophetis, qui sic vocabantur in Novo Testamento, 1. Cor. XIV. vers. 3. seqq. sed imme- diato Spiritus afflatu, quia additur PER SPIRI- TUM. Neque restringenda fuisset ad Apostolos & Prophetas, si de manifestatione quacunque age- retur. Ita enim porrigit sese ad omnes fideles. Beat. Franzius in Schol. Sacrific. disp. IX. th. 90. de revelationis modo explicans, quod sc. hoc mo- do gentes sub Christo capite in unum corpus cum populo DEI coalituræ essent, taxatur a Cloppen- burg. in Syntagm. Exercit. disp. XII. th. 19. Sed temere. Diserte enim Apostolus modum notat ὡς νῦν. Neq; illud mysterii caput, quod nunc gen- tes æquali jure ad hæreditatem, ad corpus Christi mysticum & ad participationem promissionum pertineant, imo quod Judæis propter σκληροκαρ- δίαν repudiatis inter gentes tanquam filios promis- sionis Rom. IX. 8. Patriarchalis Ecclesia sit consti- tuenda, & erigenda. Hoc sane novum est, & omni- bus ætatibus antehac inauditum; Unde recte talis gentium vocatio tanquam illustre παράδειγμα reconciliationis nostræ gratuitæ cum Deo propo- nitur ab Apostolo. At vero ex eo Cloppenburg male infert, gentes sub Vet. Test. nullo vocatas fuisse modo. Quod vero Deut. X. 14. 15. dicitur, tantum Israëlitas elegisse Deum præ omnibus popu- lis, ad domicilium Ecclesiæ sub V. T. constituen- dum pertinet, non ad designandos terminos gratiæ. Sic & Amos III. 2. solum vos agnoveram, ad prærogativas gratiæ pertinet, non ad ipsam gratiam.

## 3:6
V. 6. That the Gentiles are fellow-heirs and of the same body and partakers of his promise in Christ) Understand by Gentiles those born of the Gentiles, remaining in their own liberty: not made proselytes. Fellow-heirs, called by equal right to the heavenly life, which is called an inheritance, see Rom. VIII. 17. Heb. XI. v. 9. 1. Pet. III. 7. of the same body, parts of the same body, that is, of the Church, see above II. 16.

Partakers of his promise) partakers of the Holy Spirit, who is called the promise of God, as we saw above I. verse 13. For his here refers to that God, which preceded at a sufficient distance. In Christ, through Christ, who obtained these goods for us.

Through the Gospel) as if through an instrument, which Christ uses to effect those things. Through the Gospel the Church is gathered, to those who believe is given the right to the heavenly life, and in the meantime the gifts of the Spirit.

The Apostle now explains the hope of the Gentiles regarding the heavenly inheritance, for the sake of which he had especially premised that concerning the revelation of this mystery, and he determines to discourse further on his ministry. Namely, that the Gentiles are 1. fellow-heirs, which Jerome understands with respect to Christ, whose co-heirs we are called, Rom. VIII. 17; others more conveniently understand it with respect to the Jews, who had had the hope of eternal life, when the Gentiles were without hope in the world. But now the Apostle affirms that they are co-heirs regarding the hope and right to eternal life. The Jews did not come to the Gentiles, but the Gentiles to the Jews, therefore they are called their co-heirs. 2. Of the same body, the Gentiles are of the same body, because they belong to one mystical body, whose unity
