II. v. 13. asfertur, ψευδερμηνείαν Grotianam sapit, qualis ange ipsum non facile citra ullum locum observata, quem vel de electio- ne ἀπ' ἀρχῆς, id est, ab æterno facta, vel de electio- ne ipsorum, ceu primitiarum inter gentes, alii ac- ceperunt, non verò quod inter primos è Judæis ad fidem Christi conversos ipsi fuerint. Quomo- do enim inter Judæos illi primi, & ἀπ' ἀρχῆς ab initio primitivæ Ecclesiæ conversi, qui per Evange- lium Pauli, Silvani & Timothei conversi, qui nec ab initio prædicarunt Evangelium: Pau- lus quippe id persecutus primum est. Timotheus verò tardius demum assumptus est ad Pauli con- sortium, Actor. XVI. v. 1. nec Thessalonicensem Ecclesiam viderant, nisi postquam Paulus eo con- cesserat, quod non ante 50, à nato Christo an- num, & post Caji demum tempora accidisse in confesso est. De sensu vocis προηλπικότες Eph. I. v. 12. non est, quod hic dicamus. Dictum est de eodem ad illum locum. Nec etiamsi Judæi pri- mum conversi sint, Thessalonicenses Ecclesiam constitisse, non è gentibus, sed unicè è primum conversis Judæis consequens est. Quæ de Jasone, quod fuerit inter eos, qui Stephani tempore con- versi sunt, quodque propinquus Silæ & Timothei fuerit, mere arbitrariæ sunt hypotheses, quem- admodum & illa, quod Timothei majores Thessalo- nicæ habitarint, cui locus Act. XX. 4. nihil favet, si non contrariatur omnino. Nam Thessalonicen- ses ibi dicuntur Aristarchus & Secundus, Gajus verò dicitur Derbensis, cui conjungitur Timo- theus, sorte quod Lystrensis, & è vicinia Derben- sium, quæ duodecim tantum distabant milliaribus Act. XV. 24. Aristarcho & Secundo conjungen- dus, si Thessalonicensis fuisset.

Tertiò, nomen Ecclesiæ immutat Grotius, fin- gitque paucas tantum personas ad fidem conver- sas Thessalonicæ egisse, è Judæa è persecutione post cædem Stephani, quum epistola ex adverso inscripta sit integræ Ecclesiæ, æque ut præcedanea: Τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ Θεσσαλονικέων, quemadmodū utro- bique habet ἐπιγραφὴ: non verò pauculis tantum personis sine Doctore, sine ministerio in exilio ibidem agentibus: Nam ad integram Ecclesiam illo ipso titulo directam esse alteram epistolam, extra controversiæ aleam positum est. Argumen- tum illud perquam leviculum est, quod presbyte- rium illic nullum fuerit, quia scilicet jubentur, qui ex regula Christi non vivunt vitari ab aliis non ex- communicari; nam nec excommunicandi omnes ἄτακτοι statim sunt, nec vitatio illa excommuni- cationem excludit, ac injungitur vitatio etiam il- lic, ubi Ecclesia integra cum presbyterio habetur, ut exemplo sunt Roma cap. XVI. 17. & Corinthus quoque, 1. Cor. V. 9. 11.

Quartò, si occasionem respiciamus Epistolæ, ea fuit quorundam ἑτεροδοξία, qui spargebant, quasi à Spiritu revelatum, aut à Paulo traditum sive sermone, sive literis, Christi diem præ foribus esse: cujus πρόφασιν aut ansam arripuisse videntur è priori epistola, retundente securitatem empačta- rum, qui de adventu Domini dicebant: Pax est, non est periculum, 1. Thess. IV. v. 2. 3. Inde ergò causam habuit Apostolus posteriori hac epistola Thessalonicenses informandi, quod prius ventu- rus sit Anti-Christus, cujus impietati ac seductioni finem allaturus sit Christus gloriosa apparitione adventus sui ad judicium. Quæ omnia itidem per- vertuntur à Grotio. Contendit quippe, ea quæ prædicta sunt cap. II. ante finem mundi eventura, spectare ad res, quæ intra unius vitæ spatium po- terant contingere: quod Paulus opinatus sit, se vivo posse evenire judicium novissimum. Quam Paulo opinionem fuisse, nullo constat documen- to, nec nisi è falso intellectis locis Apostoli colligi certum est. Nam nec vaticinia præsentia, nec alia, quæ prædixit, 1. Tim. IV. 1. 2. 3. 2. Tim. III. 1. seqq. admittunt, ut erroneam talem opinionem Paulo hæsisse credamus.

Quintò itaque quod ad scopum attinet Apo- stoli, primarius illi scopus erat, sorem illam profligare de jam imminente die novissima; cui vero contra frigidam adfudisset, si id innuisset, non posse tantum intra unius vitæ spatium adveni- re Christum, sed etiam ea brevi, & intra unius aut alterius anni intervallum certo eventura, quæ an- tecessura extremum judicium monuerat, ut ne crederetur, id tam propinquum & præ foribus esse. Quod annon est pervertere vel potius penitus evertere scopum Apostolicum? Sic scopus alter erat, confirmare Thessalonicensium Ecclesiam in fide agnita, revocare illis in memoriam, tum quæ Thessalonicæ Paulus cum collegis prædicarat, tum quæ priori Epistola iis commendarat, & ad perse- verantiam in illis commonefacere, illos etiam co- ercere, & quomodo coerceri in Ecclesia ista de- beant, edocere: quem verò prorsus elidit iterum Grotius, negans ibi Ecclesiam integram, negans presbyterium ibi fuisse, negans Paulum, Silvanum, & Timotheum, cum hæc exararent, Thessalonicæ unquam docuisse, negans eosdem literas ad Thessa- lonicensem Ecclesiam dedisse, prioremque Episto- lam prius ad ipsos perscriptam esse.

Sextò, argumentum primarium Epistolæ esse adventum & descriptionem Anti-Christi palam emersuri ac manifestandi ante supremum Christi adventum, inter omnes interpretes veteres & re- centiores hactenus constitit. Grotius ex adverso, ut ne desit Anti-Christo Romano, alia omnia com- mentus est, nimirum non de aliis cap. II. agi, quam de Cajo Imperatore, & de Simone Mago, tametsi lu- ce clarius constet, nec tempus convenire, nec ver- ba Apostoli, de quibus suo loco, adeo ut nemo hactenus ex illis vel per febrim somniarit prædi- čtionem de Cajo, omnes illo tempore Cajum jam vita defunctum fuisse fateantur, quo hæc vaticinia consignata sunt, eoque tempore jam Simonem Magum à Petro confusum esse, Act. VIII. 20.

Septimò, Chronologiam etiam confundere non veretur Grotius, Petavium in subsidium vocans, sed contra mentem Petavii. Quod quum in præ- loquio in priorem ad Thessalonicenses jam osten- sum sit, non opus est denuo ostendere. Petavii sententia est, Paulum conversum esse ad fidem Christianam anno à Christo & Stephani morte tertio, part. I. lib. V. Ration. temp. c. 1. sub finem, anno nempe Christi XXXVII. in quem & mortem Tiberii, & Caji Caligulæ regnandi initium incidif- se Petavius docet part. II. lib. IV. cap. 5. p. 229. ut & partis I. loco citato. Caji ergo tertius & quar- tus fuit Christi 40. & 41. uti secundus Cajani prin- cipatus, quo hanc epistolam scriptam fingit Gro- tius, incidit in annum Christi 39. qui secundus et- iam Pauli conversi est. At Paulum secundo statim à conversione anno hanc ad Thessalonicenses ex- arasse epistolam, in qua λευκάδι Φωνῇ, cap. II. tra- dit, quomodo Thessalonicæ fuerit, ibique Evan- gelium sparserit, somnium est sine somno. Scri- ptam autem longè post excessum Caji, ut omnes Interpretes & Doctores ὁμοθυμαδὸν consentiunt, ne exceptis quidem Pontificiis, ita prædicere A- postolum voluisse ea, quæ jam pridem contige- rant, qui affirmarit, ei helleboro opus esse, omnes sani judicabunt.

Quae octavo de occultatione diuturna huius epistolae nugatur Grotius, gerris ficulis vaniora sunt. Quomodo occultari vel potuerat vel debuerat, quae toti Ecclesiae inscripta erat, quae publice praelegenda erat, ut caverentur ab omnibus seductoribus, & falsi Prophetae, utique vitarentur inordinatione, & alia monita Apostoli observarentur.

Sed de hoc commento iam diximus loco laudato. Nono causa, quod haec epistola postremum locum inter omnes, quae Ecclesiae inscripta sunt, obtineat, non est, quod Vespasiano demum imperante eadem divulgata sit: quod temere, & sine ulla auctoritate affirmat Grotius, sed quod posterior fit tempore scriptionis ad Thessalonicenses, & priorem digito demonstret, & inter omnes Paulinas brevissima. Nam praemissae sunt prolixiores illae ad Romanos & ad Corinthios, tum vero breviores subjunctae, & inter has primus locus assignatus illi, quae ad fideles per Galatiam universam spectabat, subjuncta eidem, quae ad Ephesios aeque prolixa, & ad nobilissimam Ecclesiam exarata, postmodum quae ad Philippenses, & quae ad Colossenses, quarum illa prior est scriptionis tempore. Thessalonicenses denique ut tempore posteriores fuere, quantum ad ipsorum conversionem, ita etiam locum ultimum illis inscriptae epistolae fortita sunt, quae paucioribus quoque verbis constant.

Decimo status epistolae iam minime obscurus est, quod nempe fit Paraneticus-Didacticus. Nam hortatur ad constantiam in fide adversus persecutiones, & dehortatur a seductione falsorum doctorum, de iam imminente Christi adventu: adeoque informat eosdem de Anti-Christo prius venturo ac dominaturo in Ecclesia, ejusque tum detentione, tum manifestatione, tum interfectione ac fine. Denique hortatur ad preces, observantiam, & vitationem eorum, qui inordinate ambulant, ac otiosorum.

Partes tres sunt juxta tria capita: Prima est epenetica, quam elogiis Thessalonicensium, testificatione iudicii divini, ac voto pio insinuat paranein ad constantiam in persecutionibus, cap. I. Altera est Didactico-Paranetica, qua de adventu Christi novissimo nondum venturo, donec Anti-Christus emergat & manifestetur, docet, ac de custodienda doctrina Apostolica monet, cap. II. Tertia est Paranetica de precatione, ac vitandis, indicandisque inordinate viventibus,

cap. III. PARS I. EPISTOLAE PARANETICA.

## 1:1 Argument
CAPUT I. ARGUMENTUM & PARTITIO.

After the inscription and the initial vow, he testifies that thanks are to be given to God by him, for the increase of faith, and charity, and patience in adversities, which are an indication of just divine judgment, and he prays that God may perfect in them the work of faith.

There are two parts besides the title and the vow: The first εὐχαριστικὴ [eucharistic] for their faith and charity, to verse 10. The second εὐκτικὴ [euctical/supplicatory] for the completion of faith, verses 11 and 12.

PARS I. Εὐχαριστικὴ [Eucharistic] for the increase of effective faith.

Verse 1. Παῦλος καὶ Σιλουανὸς, καὶ Τιμόθεος [Paul and Silvanus, and Timothy]) I think it is true, what Jerome notes here, that Silas was formerly written, not Silvanus, although indeed it is the same name variously inflected, yet the former was more accommodating to the Hebrews, the latter to the Romans. But there were many Romans in Macedonia. And so this little word can be seen to have been changed after the example of the other epistle written to the Thessalonians collected from the Gentiles, although in whichever way it is written, it does not matter much. But these Silas and Timothy were kinsmen of that Jason perhaps and of other Jews, who having embraced the Christian faith lived in Thessalonica. There is no cause why we should think that the name Silvanus was substituted here in place of Silas, even if we do not deny that the same person is designated by both names, nor does the commentary which is ascribed to Jerome teach that the name was changed after the example of another epistle.

But the hypothesis of Grotius, that this epistle was written to others than the preceding one, is merely fictitious. It is directed to the same Church, and openly refers itself to the preceding one: It commends equally as the former the faith and charity of the Thessalonians, and what he had prayed for, and had warned in the former, that they might become fuller, chap. III. 12, chap. IV. 1. 10. he now proclaims the increase of their faith and love, 2. Thess. I. 3. when he had testified in individual chapters, 1. epist. I. 10. chap. II. 19. chap. III. 13, chap. IV. 16. 17. chap. V. 2. seqq. concerning the day of the advent of Christ, now because of that attestation of faith received he celebrates them, 2. epist. chap. I. 10. when he had reminded those who had done so, concerning the advent of the Lord, 1. epist. chap. V. 2. now he informs more correctly those who were terrified, as if the day of the Lord were already imminent, an opportunity seized from the sinister sense of the words of the Apostle, 2. epist. II. 2. seqq. when 1. epist. IV. 11. he had exhorted to labors and honest conversation, but many still lived inordinately, and were given to idleness, those same were to be avoided, and, if they did not amend themselves through the epistle, to be pointed out 2. epist. chap. III. 6. 10. 12. 14. memor. That fabrication concerning the fable of the exiled Jews, to whom this epistle was inscribed, devised to adorn it, concerning Silas and Timothy, kinsmen to Jason and other Jews who lived in Thessalonica, does not need refutation; because it rests on no conjecture even probable in appearance.

Why does he not with equal facility make Paul also a kinsman of Jason? Moreover, not without cause does the Apostle again join Silvanus and Timothy to himself. They had been companions of the Evangelical ministry, and heralds of the praises of the Church of Thessalonica in the former epistle: That the same mind concerning them was still in them, was manifest. The sense also of the epistle written by them before had to be vindicated by them with unanimous opinion, which some understood less dexterously, and the precepts handed down by them seemed to need to be inculcated again by common effort. He also wished thus to testify his consensus with these teachers, and at the same time to procure for them greater authority in the Church.

Yet that the Apostle, not Silvanus nor Timothy, wrote this epistle, who was governed by the immediate inspiration of God — this is evident enough not only from the style and thread of the discourse, and from the notable and truly Prophetic foretelling, but also from the peculiar sign which he appended at the end and wished to be noted. Τῇ Ἐκκλησίᾳ Θεσσαλονικέων [To the Church of the Thessalonians]) Few persons are rightly called a Church also, as Rom. XVI. 5. 1. Cor. XVI. 19. Tertullian in the exhortation to chastity: Where three are, there is a Church, even though they are laics. See what Beza has on this matter on Act. XXI. 4. We do not deny that even few are called a Church: But when the domestic Church is spoken of, such as was that of Aquila and Prisca, Rom. XVI. 5. 1. Cor. XVI. 19.

But this inscription does not pertain to any domestic Church, for it is not named, as a house is there, but to the universal one, which was gathered at Thessalonica, the Church of Christ, which is evident from the collation of the former epistle chap. I. 1. For there is no cause why we should interpret this inscription otherwise. He warns here chap. III. 1. that the Thessalonians should pray for Paul and Silvanus and Timothy at Athens, or, as it pleases Grotius, while they were staying at Corinth, so that the Word of the Lord might run and be preached there, just as it was at Thessalonica: The Church of Thessalonica, therefore, did not consist of a small number or a single house at that time.

He warns in chap.

6 that they should withdraw themselves from every brother who does not walk according to the tradition which they had received from Paul and his colleagues.

It is necessary, therefore, that many who belonged to the Church existed there, not just a few exiles of Paul. (In God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ) That is, to that Church which was made, which existed, by the benefit of God the Father first, then of Christ.

What does that division of the Father and Christ mean, as if the Father works prior to Christ either in order of time or dignity, when the actions of the most holy Trinity ad extra are indivisible, and whatever the Father works, ταῦτα, the same things, ὁμοίως, similarly, the Son also works, John

V. 19.

Latin:

CAPUT I. ARGUMENTUM & PARTITIO.

Post inscriptionem & votum initiale gratias sibi agendas Deo testatur, pro incremento fidei, & charitatis, ac patientia in adversis, qua indicio sunt iusti iudicii divini, oratque, ut perficiat in ipsis Deus opus fidei.

Partes duae sunt praeter titulum & votum: Prima εὐχαριστικὴ pro fide ac charitate ipsorum, ad verf. 10. Altera εὐκτικὴ pro fidei complemento verf. 11. & 12.

PARS I. Εὐχαριστικὴ pro fidei efficacis incremento.

Verf. 1. Παῦλος καὶ Σιλουανὸς, καὶ Τιμόθεος) Puto esse verum, quod notat Hieronymus hic Σίλας olim scriptum fuisse, non Σιλουανὸς, quamquam enim idem est nomen varie inflexum, illud tamen Ebraeis, hoc Romanis erat accommodatius. Multi autem in Macedonia erant Romani. Itaque videri potest haec vocula immutata ad exemplum alterius epistolae scriptae ad Thessalonicenses ex gentibus collectos, quamquam utro modo scribatur, non multum refert. Erant autem Silas isti & Timotheus cognati Iasonis illius forte & aliorum Judaeorum, qui Christianam fidem amplexi Thessalonicae habitabant. Nulla est causa, cur putemus, nomen Σιλουανὸς in locum Σίλας hic surrogatum esse, etiamsi eandem personam utroque nomine designari non negemus, nec qui Hieronymo adscribitur commentarius, ad exemplum alterius epistolae nomen immutatum docet.

Hypothesis vero Grotii, quod haec epistola ad alios scripta sit, quam antecedanea, mere fictitia est. Ad eandem directa est Ecclesiam, & ad praecedentem sefe aperte refert: Commendat aeque ut prior fidem & charitatem Thessalonicensium, & quam precatus sit, ac monuerit in priori, ut pleniores evaderent, cap. III. 12, cap. IV. 1. 10. iam incrementum fidei & dilectionis ipsorum praedicat, 2. Thess. I. 3. quum singulis capitulis testificatus fuerit, 1. epist. I. 10. cap. II. 19. cap. III. 13, cap. IV. 16. 17. cap. V. 2. seqq. de die adventus Christi, iam ob testificationem illam fide susceptam eos celebrat, 2. epist. cap. I. 10. quum eos, qui fecerierant, de adventu Domini commonefecerit, 1. epist. cap. V. 2. jam illos, qui terrebantur, quasi immineret jam dies Domini, anfa e sinistro verborum Apostoli sensu arrepta, rectius informat, 2. epist. II. 2. seqq. quum 1. epist. IV. 11. ad labores & honestam conversationem hortatus fuerit, multi autem adhuc inordinate viverent, otioque dediti essent, eosdem vitandos, ac, si non emendarint sefe per epistolam, indicandos 2. epist. cap. III. 6. 10. 12. 14. memor. Commentum illud ad fabulam de Judaeis exulibus, quibus inscripta haec epistola, ornandam excogitatum, de Sila & Timotheo, Iasoni aliisque Judaeis, qui Thessalonicae habitarunt, cognatis, refutatione non indiget; quia nulla nititur vel in speciem faltim probabili conjectura.

Cur non parili facilitate Paulum etiam cognatum Iasonis facit? Caeterum non fine causa iterum Silvanum & Timotheum sibi jungit Apostolus. Fuerant illi socii ministerii Evangelici, & praecones laudum Ecclesiae Thessalonicensis in priori epistola: Illis adhuc eundem esse de ipsis animum, manifestum erat. Sensus etiam epistolae ab illis antea perscriptae ab iisdem vindicandus erat unanimi sententia, quem nonnulli minus dextre intelligebant, ac praecepta tradita ab ipsis denuo communi opera inculcanda videbantur. Testari etiam ita voluit suum cum hisce doctoribus consensum, iisque simul auctoritatem in Ecclesia ampliorem conciliare.

Apostolum tamen, non Silvanum nec Timotheum hanc epistolam scripsisse, qui immediato Dei afflatu regebatur, non tamen ex stylo & filo orationis, & ex praeditione insigni vereque Prophetica, sed etiam ex peculiari signo, quod sub finem apposuit, ac notari voluit, manifestum est fatis. Τῇ Ἐκκλησίᾳ Θεσσαλονικέων) Recte Ecclesiae dicuntur etiam pauci, ut Rom. XVI. 5. 1. Cor. XVI. 19. Tertullianus exhortatione castitatis: Ubi tres, Ecclesia est, licet laici. Vide quae hac de re habet Beza Act. XXI. 4. Ecclesiam dici etiam paucos non diffitemur: Sed cum de domestica Ecclesia sermo est, qualis erat Aquilae & Priscae, Rom. XVI. 5. 1. Cor. XVI. 19.

At haec inscriptio non ad aliquam domesticam Ecclesiam pertinet, nec enim nominata est, ut illic domus, sed ad universam, quae Thessalonicae colligebatur, Christi Ecclesiam, quod e collatione prioris epistolae cap. I. 1. patet. Causa enim non est, cur hanc inscriptionem aliter interpretemur. Monet hic cap. III. 1. ut precentur Thessalonicenses pro Paulo & Silvano & Timotheo Athenis, vel, ut Grotio placet, Corinthi agentibus, ut illic ita Verbum Domini currat & prædicetur, quemadmodum Thessalonicæ: Non ergo paucorum numero vel una domo tum constitit Ecclesia Thessalonicensis.

Monet cap.

6 ut ab omni fratre sese abstineanttrahant fideles, qui non ambularit secundum traditionem, quam à Paulo & collegis acceperant.

Oportet ergo plures illic extiterint ad Ecclesiam pertinentes, non pauli aliqui exules. Ἐν Θεῷ Πατρὶ ἡμῶν, καὶ Κυρίῳ Ἰησοῦ χριστῷ) Id est, ei Ecclesiæ, quæ facta est, quæ extitit, beneficio Dei Patris primi, deinde Christi.

Quid illa sibi divisio Patris, & Christi vult, quasi vel ordine temporis vel dignitatis prior operetur Pater, quam Christus, quum actiones sacrosanctæ Trinitatis ad extra sint indivisæ, & quæcunque operatur Pater, ταῦτα, eadem, ὁμοίως, similiter operetur & Filius, Job.

V. 19.

## 1:2
Vers. 2. (Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ) This manner of greeting, begun here, Paul often retains in other epistles, as 1.

Cor. I. 3. & elsewhere. It is falsely said that this manner of greeting was begun here: For the same formula of salutation is used in exactly the same words in the former epistle, which we have previously shown from undoubted γνωρίσμασι [marks/signs] to be truly prior to this one, whatever trifles Grotius may utter.

Theophylact elegantly says of the wish itself: When God imparts His grace to anyone, there will be nothing that he will take amiss, since the adversities that are opposed to him are easily dissolved. Paul, therefore, knowing well what grace of GOD would provide for all, prays for this very thing for them.

Which, indeed, as soon as it was present with them, they would feel no temptations that are brought upon them: But having received divine peace at the same time, they will act in tranquility and will remain immovable. He reminds them, moreover, of divine grace, so that as soon as pressures invade, remembering this grace by which they were saved, they may be greatly consoled.

And having obtained a more certain hope from past and greater benefits, they will not defer anything in lesser evils. By grace, says the Blessed

Hunnius, he understands the gratuitous favor of GOD toward us, by which through and for the sake of Christ He adopts us as sons, but by Peace, the tranquility of hearts reconciled with God, blossoming from the effective sense of that favor of God. At the same time, however, (though less principally) the word peace in the Hebrew phrase also embraces external prosperity and goods of every kind.

Vers.

Latin:

Vers. 2. Χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη ἀπὸ Θεῦ Πατρὸς ἡμῶν καὶ Κυρίῳ Ἰησοῦ χριστῷ) Hunc salutandi morem hic inceptum in aliis epistolis sæpe retinet Paulus, ut 1.

Corinth. I. 3. & alibi. Hic inceptum esse illum salutandi morem falso dicitur: Eadem enim salutationis formula iisdem prorsus verbis adhibita est in priori epistola, quam vere hac priorem esse, quicquid nugetur Grotius, antehac ex indubitatisγνωρίσμασι ostendimus.

De voto ipso eleganter Theophylactus: Cum suam Deus cuiquam gratiam impertitur, nihil erit, quod moleste sic ferat, quandoquidem facile dissolvuntur, quæ illi objiciuntur adversa. Paulus itaque nihil ignarus que DEI gratia cunctis præstaret, vel hanc ipsam his comprecatur.

Que utique ut primum his aderie, nullas sentirent, quæ inferuntur tentationes: Sed pace simul divina accepta in tranquillo agent, & immobiles manebunt. Commonefacit eos præterea divina gratiæ, ut cum primum pressura invaserint, hujusce gratiæ recordati, qua salvi sunt facti, maxime consolentur.

Et ex præteritis & majoribus beneficiis, certiorem spem nacti, nihil in minoribus malis defferent. Per gratiam, inquit B.

Hunnius, DEI gratuitum erga nos favorem intelligit, quo per & propter Christum in filios nos adoptat, per Pacem vero cordia cum Deo reconciliati tranquillitatem, ex efficaci sensu illius favoris Dei efflorescentem. Simul autem, (etsi minus principaliter) externam quoque prosperitatem, omnisque generis bona pacis vox phrasis Ebræa complectitur.

Vers.

## 1:3
3. (We are bound to thank God always for you, brethren, as it is fitting, because your faith grows exceedingly) A similar thanksgiving

Rom. I. 8. 1 Cor. I. 4. 5. Phil. I. 3. 4. He gives thanks not only for their faith, but also that that faith is growing.

Theophylact observes that three things are excellently taught here: First, that if anything is done by us in the best way, we should give thanks to God, and not ascribe it to our own virtue, and attribute to Him the sum of all things, nor become insolent for any reason because of a well-performed deed.

Second, that the things they themselves suffer are by no means worthy of mourning and tears, but are of such a kind that thanks can be given to God for them. Wherefore they ought to be filled with joy, not consume their mind with grief, or despair entirely. Third, that one should by no means envy the virtues of others, but rather congratulate them, and thanks should be given to GOD for the progress of the brethren.

Whence it happens that those who are afflicted with pain because of the virtue of others, without doubt curse GOD. Chrysostom and Theophylact explain that ὑπεραυξάνει [grows exceedingly] by a metaphor: For when a flood of temptations has invaded you, and nothing has blocked you, nor do you succumb to them, they will certainly present nothing other than your greatest growth and the sublimity of your faith.

He said "super-grows" [grows exceedingly], from a certain similarity to that ancient cataclysm, which by no means easily blocked all the highest peaks, and although it covered them, as soon as it began to recede, they emerged; he also argues for the magnitude of their faith when he added "super-grows." (And the love of every one of you all toward each other abounds) He well joined in the thanksgiving two greatest things, faith and love, in which is τὸ πᾶν [the whole] of Christianity.

So also Eph. I. 15. 16. πλεονάζειν [to abound] N.J.W ἄξιον, that is, just, right.

Thus Demosthenes: Ἄξιόν ἐστι σιωπᾶν [It is fitting to be silent]. Note, Theophylact warns, what kind of charity it is, for it does not embrace one and reject another, but is equally diffused among all.

For that is what he designates when he says, of each one of you and toward one another. For if, having rejected the others, we had bestowed all our charity well upon some one person, it would not be called charity, but discord.

For if all are to be pursued with benevolence for the sake of God's grace, observe and cultivate all equally. But if you yourself have embraced someone privately with charity, this will surely be human, not divine, charity. Note, however, that the conjunction of minds and the mutual bond of benevolence are of great value for repelling temptations.

Latin:

3. Εὐχαριστεῖν ὀφείλομεν τῷ Θεῷ πάντοτε περὶ ὑμῶν, ἀδελφοὶ, καθὼς ἄξιόν ἐστι, ὅτι ὑπεραυξάνει ἡ πίστις ὑμῶν) Similis gratiarum actio

Rom. I. 8. 1 Cor. I. 4. 5. Philipp. I. 3. 4. Non tantum de fide eorum agit gratias, sed & quod fides ea crescat.

Eximie tria hic doceri Theophylactus observat: Primum ut si quid optime per nos geritur, gratias Deo agamus, nec nostræ virtuti id ascribamus, & illi accenseamus rerum omnium summam, nec quocumque paullo ob rem bene gestam insolescamus.

Secundo quemadmodum nequaquam sint luctu & lacrymis digna, quæ ipsi perpetiuntur, sed ejusmodi, ut agi Deo pro his gratie possint. Quocirca debere eos gaudio affici, non mærore conficere animum, vel penitus desperare. Tertio quod alienæ virtutibus nequaquam sit invidendum, sed congratulandum potius, & pro fratrum profectu DEO dicenda sint gratiæ.

Quo fit, ut qui ex aliorum virtute dolore afficiuntur, DEO procul dibio maledicant. Illud ὑπεραυξάνει per Metaphoram explicat Chrysostomus & Theophylactus: Cum enim vos invaserint tentationum diluvium, nec aliquod vos intercluferit, nec illis succumbitis, nihil certe aliud preferent, quam vestra maxima incrementa, & fidei vestræ sublimitatem.

Supercrefcit autem dixit, ex quadam veteris cataclysmi illius similitudine, qui nequaquam facile summa quæque fastigia interclusit, etsi ille operuit, ut primum capit decrescere, hæc emerse; arguit etiam istorum fidei magnitudinem, cum supercrefcit, intulit. Καὶ πλεονάζει ἡ ἀγάπη ἑνὸς πάντων ὑμῶν εἰς ἀλλήλους) Bene conjunxit in gratiarum actione duas res maximas, fidem & dilectionem, in quibus est τὸ πᾶν, Christianismi.

Sic & Ephes. I. 15. 16. πλεονάζειν N.J.W ἄξιον, id est, æquum, rectum.

Sic Demosthenes: Ἄξιόν ἐστι σιωπᾶν. Adverte, monet Theophylactus, qualem se habeat charitas, neque enim hunc complexa alium respuit, sed æque in omnes diffunditur.

Id enim designat, cum inquit, unius cujusque vestrum & in invicem. Nam si cæteris rejectis in unum aliquem charitatem omnem bene contulerimus, haudquaquam charitas, sed diffidium diceretur.

Nam si Dei ob gratiam universi sint benevolentiæ prosequendi, omnes pariter observâ & cole. Si vero privatim aliquem ipse fueris charitate complexus, humana profecto erit non divina hæc charitas. Adverte autem animorum conjunctionem, & mutuum benevolentiæ nexum ad propulsandas tentationes valere plurimum.

## 1:4
Vers. 4. (So that we ourselves boast of you in the Churches of God) Καυχᾶσθαι [to boast] is often to rejoice, to exult, sometimes to reveal that joy in words. Ἐν ὑμῖν [in you] from you, on your occasion.

In the Manuscript: ἠγαυχᾶσθαι, which word is found in the Greek, Ps.

LII. 3. LXXIV. 4. XCVII. 7. CVI. 47. Καυχᾶσθαι here is not to rejoice, but to glory, which is also the more accepted meaning of this word.

For Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy were glorying in the Churches of GOD about the Thessalonian Church, which was to them a στέφανος καυχήσεως, καὶ δόξα [crown of boasting and glory], 1.

Thess. II. 19. 20. He did not say, which Theophylact observes, we boast to others about you, for their faith had already become known everywhere, 1.

Thess. I. 8. but we glory in you, and we consider your progress as glory. If we, therefore, give thanks to God for you, and glory greatly among men, it was much more fitting for you to do likewise in adverse circumstances, and not succumb to temptations. (For your patience and faith in all your persecutions and tribulations, which you endure) There is here also a διὰ δυοῖν [figure of speech using two words for one idea].

For ὑπομονῆς καὶ πίστεως [patience and faith] is the same as ὑπομονῆς ἐν πίστει [patience in faith], perseverance in faith. For the same, ὑπομονῇ ἐλπίδι [patience of hope], 1.

Thess. I. 3. For faith begets hope, and sometimes hope is included under the name of faith. This fits well, however, those miserable Jews who, having been cast out of Judea into Syria, and from there compelled to seek other places after other places, had preferred to bear all those inconveniences rather than desert the faith.

The interpretation of the words is correct: But the application is fictitious.

For the idea that converted Jews, cast out of Judea, crossed the sea through Syria and came to Thessalonica is a Grotian fable. That they are understood in this place is an inept gloss. These things were written to the Church, which Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy had gathered from the Jews at Thessalonica, but especially from the Gentiles by their preaching, when they were staying there, 2.

Thess. II. 14. 15. chap. III. 2. seqq. Acts

XVII. 1. seqq. and which Timothy, sent there by Paul, had further confirmed in the faith, 1.

Thess. III. 2. seqq. about which they boasted so much because of the faith, love, and patience 1. Thess. I. 3. demonstrated in tribulations, chap. I. 6. by which they offered themselves as a pattern to all the faithful, not only in Macedonia and Achaia, so that their faith was celebrated everywhere, v. 7. 8. of whose afflictions constantly overcome the Apostle glories 1.

Thess. II. 14. whom they testified to be their hope, joy, and crown, v. 19. for whose perseverance they professed they could never give enough thanks to GOD, chap.

III. 9. Which, as they consonant with this eulogy from affection: so all these things are to be understood about the same Thessalonians. That it was preached to the Thessalonians in both epistles is so clear that nothing can be clearer. How that persecution began while the Apostle and his fellow-workers were present is described in Acts 17, and how it continued is manifest if 2 Thess. 2:14 and chapter 3:3 are compared with this passage.

He shows, says Theophylact, that you indeed have been afflicted for a long time and much by temptations. For patience is not demonstrated in two or three days, but by the endurance of long-lasting evils. That patience seems to be in them, who, although they have not yet received those good and promised heavenly things, nevertheless endure by waiting and suffering. But now he designates that greater [patience], which is argued for in persecutions and pressures. And indeed, for those who had to deal with implacable enemies, a firmer endurance was necessary, and in these very things the primary beginnings of dedication.

Latin:

Vers. 4. Ὥστε ἡμᾶς αὐτοὺς ἐν ὑμῖν καυχᾶσθαι ἐν ταῖς Ἐκκλησίαις τῷ Θεῦ) Καυχᾶσθαι sæpe est gaudere, exultare, interdum illud gaudium verbis prodere. Ἐ ὑμῖν ex vobis, vestri occasione.

In Manuscripto: ἠγαυχᾶσθαι, quæ vox reperitur in Græco, Ps.

LII. 3. LXXIV. 4. XCVII. 7. CVI. 47. Καυχᾶσθαι hic non est gaudere, sed gloriari, quæ Καυχᾶσθαι etiam verbi hujus receptior significatio est.

Nam in Ecclesiis DEI de Thessalonicensi Ecclesia gloriabantur Paulus, Silvanus, & Timotheus, quæ erat ipsis σέφανος καυχήσεως, καὶ δόξα, 1.

Thess. II. 19. 20. Non dixit, quod observat Theophylactus, infruimus alios de vobis, nam innotuerat ubique jam fides ipsorum, 1.

Thess. I. 8. sed gloriamur in vobis, vestrumque profectum gloria ducimus. Si nos itaque Deo pro vobis gratias agimus, & apud homines tartopere gloriamur, multo magis vos oportebat adversis in rebus itidem faclitare, & tentationibus succumbere. Ὑπὲρ τῆς ὑπομονῆς ὑμῶν καὶ πίστεως ἐν πᾶσι τοῖς διωγμοῖς ὑμῶν, καὶ ταῖς θλίψεσιν, αἷς ἀνέχεσθε) Est & hic & διὰ δυοῖν.

Nam ὑπομονῆς καὶ πίστεως idem valet, quod ὑπομονῆς ἐν πίστει perseverantiæ in fide. Pro eodem ὑπομονῇ ἐλπίδι, 1.

Thess. I. 3. Fides enim spem gignit, & interdum spes sub fidei nomine comprehenditur. Bene autem hoc convenit miferis illis Judæis, qui è Judæa ejecti in Syriam, inde alia atque alia loca quærere adacti, omnia ista incommoda ferre maluerant, quam fidem deserere.

Interpretatio verborum recte se habet: Sed applicatio fictitia est.

Judæos enim conversos è Judæa ejectos è Syria per mare trajecisse, ac Thessalonicam venisse, fabula Grotiana est. Eos intelligi hoc loco glossa inepta. Ad Ecclesiam hæc perscripta sunt, quam Paulus, Silvanus & Timotheus è Judæis Thessalonicæ, maxime autem è gentibus præconio suo, cum ibi agerent, collegerant, 2.

Thess. II. 14. 15. cap. III. 2. seqq. Aθ.

XVII. 1. seqq. quamque ulterius Timotheus, ed à Paulo ablegatus, confirmarat in fide, 1.

Thess. III. 2. seqq. de qua tantopere gloriabantur ob fidem, dilectionem, & patientiam 1. Thess. I. 3. in tribulationibus demonstratam, cap. I. 6. qua sese typum præbebant omnibus fidelibus, non tantum in Macedonia & Achaia, adeo ut ubiq; fides ipsorum celebraretur, v. 7. 8. de cujus afflictionibus constanter superatis gloriatur Apostolus 1.

Thess. II. 14. quos spem, gaudium, & coronam sibi esse testabantur, v. 19. ob quorum perseverantiam DEO sese nunquam gratias agere posse profitebantur, cap.

III. 9. Que ut huic elogio ex affe consonant: ita de iisdem Thessalonicensibus hæc omnia intelligenda sunt. Thessalonicensibus in utraque epistola praedicari tam clarum est, ut nihil possit esse clarius. Quomodo jam praesentibus Apostolo & συνεργοῖς illa persecutio coeperit, Aa. XVII, descriptum est, quomodo continuarit, 2 Thess. II, 14, cap. III. 3, si cum hoc loco conferantur, manifestum est.

Ostendit, inquit Theophylactus, vos quidem diu ac multum fuisse tentationibus afflictatos. Neque enim biduo triduoque patientia demonstratur, sed diuturnorum malorum tolerantia. Illis etiam inesse patientia ista videtur, qui cum bona illa & promissa caelestia nondum acceperint, sustinent tamen operiendo & patiuntur. Nunc vero majorem illam designat, qua in persecutionibus & pressuris arguitur. Et his quippe, quibus cum hostibus res erat implacabilibus, necessaria erat firmior tolerantia, & in ipsis praecipua dedicationis primordiu.

## 1:5
Verse 5. ἔνδειγμα τῆς δικαίας κρίσεως τοῦ θεοῦ. Theophylact has it more clearly: εἰς ἔνδειγμα, and the Syriac reads it no differently.

These things are therefore allowed by God to happen, so that God may at some time have the material to demonstrate His justice. So also Rom. 3:9, οἷς ἔνδειξιν τῆς δικαιοσύνης αὐτοῦ, and a little later, πρὸς ἔνδειξιν τῆς δικαιοσύνης αὐτοῦ. Εἰς τὸ καταξιωθῆναι ὑμᾶς τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ θεοῦ, ὑπὲρ ἧς καὶ πάσχετε. God has called you to the heavenly kingdom, under the condition of suffering, having fulfilled the condition; you shall therefore be judged worthy, who attain that kingdom; see Matt. 10:10, Luke 10:7, 1 Tim. 5:18, Rev. 3:4, 16:6.

Add Luke 20:35.

One might object with that passage in Rom. 8:18, ὧν ἄξια τὰ παθήματα πρὸς τὴν μέλλουσαν δόξαν ἀποκαλυφθῆναι εἰς ἡμᾶς. The answer is easy: the reward, both eternal and heavenly, is infinitely greater than any suffering and work, but that which is unequal in it is equalized by the force of the promise. For there is one equality of the thing, and another of the covenant. The sense is clear in itself, even with the preposition omitted.

Nor does God allow these things to happen so that He may have material to demonstrate His justice. For God does not need a sinner, Sir. 15:12.

But He could show His justice without such things, both by word and by deeds. And He had already demonstrated His vindicating justice in the devils. Moreover, ἔνδειγμα is more correctly explained in the Greek scholia as ἀπόδειξις καὶ ἔλεγχος, rather than by example: although it may be taken from an example, it is the ἀπόδειξις of the righteous judgment of God. For since in this life the faithful and pious suffer afflictions, while the unfaithful and impious often flourish and triumph, the fact that the judgment of GOD remains in the other world is an argument that divine justice demands that such faithful ones who are afflicted should obtain ἄνεσις, but the unfaithful and impious who afflict them should obtain θλῖψις.

And on this occasion, the Apostle descends to the principal state (of this chapter indeed), notes B. Hunnius, which is about patience in persecution. Where he indeed directly deals with this, so that he may praise and commend the memorable constancy of the past time in the Thessalonians: but obliquely he simultaneously adds a certain spur, so that they may also henceforth endure afflictions with unbroken spirits for the sake of the profession of the truth to be expelled.

The reasons for this Proposition of his, placed somewhat obscurely, he soon assigns. And among these, this first one, which he just touched upon briefly, he will soon explain and illustrate more fully, namely, taken from the future retribution on the day of judgment, of which it is a sign, and to this shown moderation are interwoven other things also taken from God's counsel and the manner of introduction into eternal life, in this sense: God deems no one worthy of His blessed kingdom, nor does He decree or ordain it for anyone, unless, when the use of the Gospel doctrine demands it, he suffers something. Just as no one is considered worthy of a crown or prize unless he has first descended into the arena to fight with an adversary and has defeated him. Therefore, you are to be praised, who, having followed this counsel of GOD and this order, think that in this age you must first sweat and struggle under the contest of tribulations, so that you may then be crowned as proven and distinguished soldiers. The connection and paraphrase is elegant, which is rendered by Theophylact: Or from that, the things said above, he comforted them, and especially from that which he said, we give thanks and glory in you.

But now he infers that which every man who is grieving and affected by sorrow seeks, namely, that he himself might escape the pressures, and demand the punishments of those who have oppressed him. But what he says is such: Endure with a calm mind the angers that are inflicted upon you, so that later the judgment of God may be revealed, which will indeed make you worthy of the heavenly empire because of this your endurance. For He will reward with a crown you who have been oppressed and trampled, and will torment those who have oppressed you or inflicted violence. Thus God will set forth His justice before Himself. But that which is added is false, that they obtain the heavenly empire not by grace, but by right as a reward for labors and sweat, because they manfully resist those temptations.

For ἄξιομα is a gratuitous gift of GOD in Christ Jesus, eternal life is obtained for us solely by His merit, Rom. 6:v. ult., nor are the sufferings, however great they may be, worthy of that glory which shall be revealed in us, Rom. 8:v. 17. The equality of the thing is rightly distinguished by Grotius from the equality of the covenant: But neither does that covenant of grace make any dignity not-faithful worthy of the kingdom of God, and it is uniquely founded on the dignity of the merit of Christ. The faithful, constant in persecutions, are held worthy of the kingdom of God, but not through suffering or patience, but through persevering faith, which uniquely seeks all dignity for the heavenly kingdom in the obedience and passion of Christ, by which He acquired it for us; and He renders us worthy, when He gives us His merits, which faith apprehends and appropriates to us.

Therefore, the blessedness which is of the heavenly kingdom is said to be his, to whom GOD imputes justice without works, Rom. 4:5. What is that justice without works, if not the obedience of Christ, by which we are constituted righteous, Rom. 5:19. It must also be observed that in the Vulgate they are not said to be worthy, but to be held worthy, and so the dignity is not to be understood as active from the merit of works, but passive, from the benefit of grace.

Whence Cajetan: He did not say, he says, you are worthy, since the sufferings of this time are not worthy of the future kingdom, but that you may be held worthy by God Himself. And Salmero, disp. 2 in Col. 1: We are called worthy, where the inheritance comes to us by no merits of our own, which is clear in infants, who are certainly included here as well.

For to little ones, says Bellarmine, book 5 de justif. cap. 3, who die soon after baptism, eternal life is given solely by the right of inheritance, not from their own merits.

Add that the Vulgate uses the word of dignity where no merit has a place, Esth. 1:7, Esd. 32:8, and ἄξιαν is rendered by merit where no work is regarded, Sir. 10:31, cap. 38:18.

It is not denied by us, says B. Hunnius, in this place, that Scripture here and in Luke 20 pronounces some worthy of eternal life. But those are not worthy by their own dignity, but by the dignity and merit of Christ.

For it is God who in Christ Jesus has made them worthy and fit for the participation of the lot of the saints in the light, Col. 1. Therefore they are held worthy of eternal life, because God Himself, through and on account of the merit of His Son, mercifully reckons them as worthy through faith. But as for the fact that that little word of dignity seems to be transferred by the Apostle to the tolerance of persecution, it must be held that it is done for no other reason than in respect of probation and declaration.

For just as a Lydian stone does not make gold, but proves the gold and declares it: so the cross and affliction do not make us worthy of the other world, but prove, if we are worthy, or or otherwise. And when we are found constant under persecutions, then certainly that cross by the very fact proves, shows, and declares that we are endowed with a true and by no means feigned faith, inasmuch as we suffer ourselves not to be shaken by any fear of persecutions, by any dread or sense of adversities or dangers, and consequently that we are of the number of those whom God in CHRIST deems worthy.

Dignitas duplex Therefore, dignity is twofold:. one from works, which the Apostle excludes, and removes from Abraham himself in the matter of salvation: The other from grace, which he asserts; one from proper merits, which in relation to the heavenly kingdom are nothing: The other from the merits of Christ, which are also most sufficient and the only true merits.

The justice of GOD is not viewed here absolutely either, but as it is to be exercised, given the merit of Christ, which those who receive through faith obtain the crown of justice, 2 Tim. IV, 5. those who reject it suffer destruction by the just judgment of GOD, namely, eternal destruction from the face of the Lord, which they rejected, because they suffer it, who know not God, nor obey the Gospel of Christ.

The reward for passions, says B. Hunnius, to be rendered to the pious, if we look at it, he rightly says is also just before God.

If indeed you do not look at the absolute justice of GOD, according to which He owes us nothing at all, as Paul says: Who has given to Him anything first, that He might repay him? But if you look at the justice of GOD, as it is now in Christ tinctured and tempered with a merciful affection toward us. Where God weighs the passions of His own with eternal glory, truly out of grace and not out of debt, if you look at the quality of the passions themselves, which (certainly as was said before) can by no means merit that eternal weight of glory.

But insofar as this remuneration is promised by the Word of God, now by virtue of the promise it falls in a certain way into debt, so that after the promise is made it is just and worthy of God to keep what He promised, lest His truth be brought into jeopardy.

Nor is the same thing ἄξιον (worthy) as merit, as is evident from Matt. III, 8. Acts XXVI, 20: nor are our works or passions expressed here as the causes of our dignity, but it is attributed solely to the grace of GOD, who deems us worthy by His calling (ἀξίωσιν) and fulfills all the good pleasure of His goodness in us, and the work of faith in power, v. 11. Furthermore, the Apostle could have named life and salvation or joy here: but he names the kingdom, which embraces all these things, and denotes more.

For he who reigns, he is saved, he lives, he rejoices; but he is not just somehow, he lives, and rejoices, but gloriously. Verf.

For both are usually placed αἰτιολογικῶς (causally). It is, however, an argument from the lesser to the greater. It is just before God to repay tribulation to those who afflict you. V. 7. And to you who are afflicted, rest with us) prayer.

In Hebrew it signifies everything that is in some way just and accords with reason. Even if God had promised nothing, nor had threatened, yet it was just, and worthy both of His goodness and of His severity, for the sake of God Himself to inflict punishments on those bringing evils; how much more is this just, when both promise and threat have intervened. It is natural, that: If indeed you suffer what He will show, let it be a just recompense for your own deeds.

Item, from natural equity, there are counter-gifts, say the Jurisconsults. I will not omit here the saying of Athenagoras: Man, who here is needy, requires food; as mortal, succession; as rational, justice. To repay is said both of good things, as Ps. XVIII, 24, and of evil things, as Ps. CIII, 10. to you . It is opposed to tribulation, and signifies solace, Acts XXIV, 25. In the Glossary, rest. The same as repose rest. The Vulgate renders it, if indeed, but it is more convenient, if indeed.

That it is placed, says Chrysostom, in those things about which it is very much settled, so that they cannot be contradicted; for that which is very just, as if GOD hates the wicked, so that He compels them to say that He hates them. For judgments of this kind are by no means doubtful, seeing that even those very men do what is just.

For if this is just among men, much more before God. Which we admit, if the discourse concerns the recompense (ἀνταπόδοσιν) owed simply to those afflicting and to those afflicted.

For then it accords with reason, and is judged just even among men. But here it is a matter of eternal retribution: to which reason does not rise.

The Apostle did not wish to prove the δικαιοκρισίαν τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ Θεοῦ. Therefore in the reasoning by which he proves it, θλῖψις is to be understood not generically, but as that of eternal destruction, just as it is afterwards expounded v. 9: So also ἄνεσις is to be expounded per λυτρότητα, so that not a bare relaxation but τὸ ἐνδοξασθῆναι is at the same time implied, v. 10. But of eternal destruction, and of eternal glory and blessedness, reason knows nothing, nor is natural equity regarded in that ἀνταποδόσει, especially since death and eternal condemnation are owed to all of us by way of retribution according to the law of GOD on account of sin, while eternal life is owed by justice to no one, however afflicted and for whatever cause, however patient under afflictions; it comes to all out of the grace of GOD, and only on account of the merit of Christ.

For the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord, Rom. VI, 23. Whence it is clear that the justice of GOD is not to be viewed here absolutely, but, as we have said, given the meritorious satisfaction of Christ, since as regards the faithful, to whom the kingdom of GOD and eternal glory are attributed, the justice of GOD is alleged viewed with the tempering of grace acquired through Christ: but as regards the infidels, the cause of condemnation is not sin, or the unjust affliction of the pious, inasmuch as Christ died even for the ungodly, and was made a propitiation for the sins of the whole world, but infidelity, through which they reject the satisfaction performed for them by Christ, and thus perish eternally.

When therefore a doubt is raised, how for a temporal affliction eternal destruction is to be undergone, something is indeed said, when Crocius answers; Although they themselves afflict the pious only for a time, since however this happens from this, not that they do not wish to afflict always, for they would wish to punish with eternal death, but because they cannot, because they do not live here perpetually, furthermore by persecuting them they sin against God Himself, it is altogether just that eternal affliction be rendered. But such a response does not suffice at all.

For the chief cause is omitted, namely the contempt and rejection of the infinite satisfaction, and the immense merit of Christ, who since He is the eternal God, blessed forever above all, by His blood acquired and sustained eternal death for the whole human race, that He might redeem it from eternal death. Those therefore who neglect and repudiate this merit of infinite price, why should they not deserve eternal destruction by the just judgment of God.

Concerning retribution it is also to be observed, that there is one retribution of one for another, as when for labor there is rest, another of one on account of another; as when wages are rendered on account of labor: The former is of simple exchange; the latter however is of due compensation: The former we admit here, the latter however we deny to have place here; for there is no equality between our afflictions and the future heavenly glory, Rom. VIII, 18. In vain therefore do the Pontificians adduce this retribution for their merits. In the revelation of Jesus from heaven I think that and the following can be read as to test: and these in the revelation to be referred to that which he commands, that you may be counted worthy of the kingdom of God.

He calls it revelation, which elsewhere παρουσία, because in Hebrew it is called גלה, that is, ἀποκάλυψις, everything which appears, when it had not appeared before, as Prov. XXVII 25. Rom. VIII. 18. Ἐν τῇ ἀποκαλύψει denotes the time: as ἐν παρουσίᾳ 1. Thess. II. 19. III. 13. Ἀποκάλυψις is said, because then the presence will be manifested, so that it may be hinted that it is not indeed absent now, for He promised that He would be present with us until the consummation of the age, Matth. XXIX. 29. but not that He would appear, but that He would appear to all on that day. Thus also through revelation, apparition, manifestation is described the advent of CHRIST, 1. Cor. I. 7. Col. III. 4. 2. Thess. II. 8. 1. Tim. VI. 14. 2. Tim. IV. 1. 1. Petr. I. 7. cap. V. 4. 1. Job. II. 28. Which is done entirely so that no one might conclude from the total absence of Christ according to his human nature from his advent: Just as eternal life is present to believers, but hidden, Col. III. 24. so Then indeed it will be manifested. But Ἀπ' οὐρανοῦ it will be revealed, not because He is now confined to heaven; but because in the heavens He manifests Himself gloriously to the elect & Angels: but then He will be revealed from heaven with the power of Angels.

But let the figments of human reason be absent concerning a material heaven and a local and slow progressive descent from heaven into the air, which do not at all suit the glory of Christ sitting at the right hand of GOD. For will He leave the right hand of God? Or will heaven be emptied of Angels? Can He not be manifested in the air, unless He lets Himself down into the air from the highest heaven through many thousands of miles? Where however we do not deny, that He who is now invisibly present with us at the right hand of God, will then be to be manifested on the day of judgment, when according to the propriety of his body He will descend visibly in a cloud from on high. - Μετ' ἀγγέλων δυνάμεως αὐτοῦ) See what has been brought to the said place 1. Thessal. III. 13. Ἀγγελοι δυνάμεως αὐτοῦ, that is, Angels of his power, who serve his Majesty.

See what has been brought to the said place 1. Thessal. III. 13. Ἀγγελοι δυνάμεως αὐτοῦ, that is, Angels, who serve his Majesty. See Matth. XXIV. 64.

By δύναμιν he understands an army indeed, Drusius in book VII. Praeterit. as also Cornelius à Lapide, as 1. Maccab. III. 34. 37. cap. IV. 3. 4. 31. to which sense the comparison of Psal. CIII. 21. Psal. CXLII. 2. Luc. II. 13. seems to favor. But because it is not said with the power of Angels, as the Syrian rendered it, but with the Angels of his power, the Greek scholia & Theophylactus understand powerful Angels, which can be illustrated by the Hebrew idiom: Others simply understand Angels of the power of the Lord, which He exercises and demonstrates through them, as Lombard, B. Luther, Calvin explain, to whom Grotius here accedes and we do not deny.

Latin:

Vers. 5. ἔνδειγμα τῆς δικαίας κρίσεως τοῦ θεοῦ Theophylactus clarius habet: εἰς ἔνδειγμα, nec aliter legit Syrus.

Hac ideo à Deo fieri sinuntur, ut aliquando Deus materiam habeat demonstrandae justitiae suae. Sic & Rom. III. 9, οἷς ἔνδειξιν τῆς δικαιοσύνης αὐτοῦ, & paulo post, πρὸς ἔνδειξιν τῆς δικαιοσύνης αὐτοῦ. Εἰς τὸ καταξιωθῆναι ὑμᾶς τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ θεοῦ, ὑπὲρ ἧς καὶ πάσχετε Vocavit vos Deus ad regnum celeste, sub conditione patiendi, impletis conditionem; digni igitur judicabimini, qui regnum illud adipiscamini; vide Matth. X. 10, Luc. X. 7, 1 Tim. V. 18, Apoc. III. 4, XVI. 6.

Adde Luc. XX. 35.

Objici potest illud Rom. VIII. 18. ὧν ἄξια τὰ παθήματα πρὸς τὴν μέλλουσαν δόξαν ἀποκαλυφθῆναι εἰς ἡμᾶς. Responsio facilis, praemium & aeternum & caeleste infinito esse majus omni sufferentia & opera, sed quod in eo insequale est, aequari vi promissi. Eit enim alia aequalitas rei, alia pacti. Sensus per se patet, etiam omissa praepositione.

Nec vero haec fieri finit Deus, ut materiam habeat demonstrandae justitiae suae. Neque enim Deus indiget peccatore, Sir. XV. 12.

Sed monstrare justitiam suam fine talibus poterat, tum verbo, tum factis. Et vindicatricem quoque justitiam demonstrarat jam in Diabolis. Caeterum ἔνδειγμα rectius explicatur in scholiis Graecis ἀπόδειξις καὶ ἔλεγχος, quam per exemplum: licet ab exemplo petatur, illa τῆς δικαίας κρίσεως τῆς θεοῦ ἀπόδειξις. Quum enim in hac vita afflictiones patiantur fideles & pii, ex adverso floreant & triumphent non raro infideles & impii, judicium DEI superesse in altero seculo, id argumento est, quod justitia divina postulet, ut afflictis ejusmodi fidelibus ἄνεσις obtingat, infidelibus vero, atque impiis, qui illos affligunt, θλῖψις.

Atque hac occasione hunc descendere Apostolum ad principalem (hujus quidem capitis) statum, notat B. Hunnius, qui est de patientia in persecutione. Ubi directe quidem hoc agit, ut in Thessalonicensibus laudet & commendet praeteriti temporis memorabilem constantiam: Oblique autem simul quoddam calcar subdit, ut & porro infractis animis perferant afflictiones ob professionem veritatis expellandas.

Cujus suae Propositionis, obscurius aliquanto posita, rationes mox assignat. Atque inter has primam hanc, quam modo attigit brevibus, mox autem explicatius evolvet & illustrabit, sumptam scilicet à retributione futura in die judicii, cujus signum esse dinius, huic ostense moderationi intertexta alia quoque sumpta à Dei consilio & modo introductionis in vitam aeternam, hoc sensu, Deus neminem beato regno suo dignum effimat, nec cuiquam illud decernit aut disponit, nisi propter Evangelii doctrinam, cum usus postulat, patiatur aliquid. Sicut nemo corona seu brabeo censetur dignus, nisi prius in arenam descendens cum adversario depugnarit, eumque devicerit. Ergo laudandi estis, qui hoc DEI consilium, hunc ordinem secuti in hoc seculo prius sub tribulationum certamine desudandum vobis dimicandumque arbitramini, ut deinde tanquam probati spectatique milites coronemini. Συνέχεια & παράφρασις concinna est, quae redditur à Theophylacto: Vel ex eo, superius dicta sunt, consolatus est eos, & ex eo praecipue, quod dixit, gratias agimus & gloriamur in vobis.

Nunc vero id infert, quod dolens quisque & maerore affectus, conquirit, ut pressuras scilicet & ipse evadat, & illorum deposcat, qui se oppresserint, poenas. Quod autem inquit, tale est: Aequo animo tolerate, qui vobis inferuntur, angores, ut postmodum Dei judicium pateat, quod sane vos ob vestram hanc tolerantiam am caelesti imperio dignos efficiet. Vos enim, qui oppressi estis & conculcati, corona donabit, & cruciabit, qui vos oppreffere, aut vim inferunt. Sic Deus prae se suam justitiam feret. Falsa autem est, quae additur, non per gratiam, sed jure eos consequi in laborum & sudoris mercedem imperium caeleste, quia viriliter tentationibus illis obsistunt.

Nam ἄξιομα donum gratuitum DEI est in Christo Jesu, solo ejus merito nobis partum vita aeterna, Rom. VI. v. ult. nec condigna sunt passiones, quantaecunque etiam fuerint, gloria illa, quae in nobis manifestabitur, Rom. VIII. v. 17. Aequalitas rei à Grotio merito ab aequalitate pacti distinguitur: Sed nec pactum illud gratiae aliquam dignitatem non-fidelis digni regno Dei tantum illud efficit, uniceque in merito Christi dignitatem fundatum est. Digni habentur fideles, in persecutionibus constantes, regno Dei, sed non per sufferentiam vel patientiam, sed per fidem perseverantem, quae unice omnem dignitatem ad regnum caeleste quaerit in Christi obedientia & passione, qua illud nobis acquisivit; eosque nos dignos reddit, cum merita sua nobis donat, quae fides apprehendit, nobisque appropriat.

Ideo beatitudo, quae regni caelestis est, dicitur ejus esse, cui DEUS imputat justitiam sine operibus, Rom. IV. 5. quae illa fine operibus justitia, nisi obedientia Christi, qua justi nos constituimur, Rom. V. 19. Observandum etiam, quod in Vulgata non dicantur digni esse, sed digni haberi, adeoque non intelligenda fit dignitas activa ex operum merito, sed passiva, ex gratiae beneficio.

Unde Cajetanus: Non dixit, inquit, digni sitis, quoniam non sunt condignae passiones hujus temporis ad futurum regnum, sed ut digni habeamini ab ipso Deo. Et Salmero disp. II. in Col. I. Digni dicimur, ubi hereditas nullis nostris meritis nobis obvenit, quod in infantibus clarum est, qui utique hic simul includuntur.

Nam parvulis, dicente Bellarmino libr. V. de justif. cap. III. qui mox à baptismo decedunt, vita aeterna donatur solo jure hereditatis, non ex propriis meritis.

Adde quod Vulgata voce dignitatis utatur, ubi nullum meritum locum habet, Esth. I. 7. Es. XXXII. 8. & ἄξιαν per meritum reddatur, ubi nullum opus respicitur, Sir. X. 31. cap. XXXIIX. 18.

Non negatur à nobis, inquit B. Hunnius, hoc loco, quod & hic & Luc. XX. scriptura quosdam dignos vita aeterna pronunciet. Verum dicui illi sunt non dignitate sua propria, sed Christi dignitate atque merito.

Deus enim est, qui in Christo Jesu dignos fecit, & idoneos ad participationem fortis sanctorum in lumine Coloss. I. Digni igitur habentur vita aeterna, quod Deus ipse per & propter Filii sui meritum pro dignis misericorditer reputat per fidem. Quod vero ea vocula dignitatis ad persecutionem tolerantiam videtur transferri ab Apostolo, tenendum, id non alia fieri ratione, quam probationis & declamtionis respectu.

Quemadmodum enim lydius lapis non facit aurum, sed probat aurum & declamat: Sic crux & afflictio non efficit nos dignos seculo altero, sed probat, simune digni, vel secus. Et quando constantes sub persecutionibus reperimur, tum certe crux ea facto ipso probat, ostendit & declarat, nos esse vera, minimeque simulata fide preditos, quippe quam nulla formidine persecutionum, nullo adversitatum periculorumve metu aut sensu excuti nobis patiamur, & proinde esse nos ex eorum numero, quos Deus in CHRISTO pro dignis reputat. Dignitas duplex

Dignitas ergo duplex est, una ex operibus, quam excludit Apostolus, & ab Abrahamo ipso removet in negotio salutis: Altera ex gratia, quam adstruit; una è propriis meritis, quæ in ordine ad regnum cœleste nulla sunt: Altera è meritis Christi, quæ & sufficientissima, & unice vera merita sunt.

Justitia DEI etiam hic non absolute spectatur, sed prout ea exercenda, supposito Christi merito, quod qui per fidem recipiunt, coronam justitiæ consequuntur, 2. Tim. IV, 5. qui respuunt, justo DEI judicio exitium patiuntur, ὄλεθρον nempe αἰώνιον ἀπὸ προσώπου τοῦ Κυρίου, quem reprobarunt, quia patiuntur id, qui Deum nesciunt, neque obediunt Evangelio Christi.

Premium pro passionibus, inquit B. Hunnius, retribuendum piis si spectemus, recte id quoque coram Deo ait esse justum.

Non quidem ab absolutum DEI justitiam intucaris, juxta quam nihil quicquam debet nobis, dicente Paulo: Quis dedit ei aliquid prior, ut retribuat ei? Sed si spectes DEI justitiam, quemadmodum illa jam in Christo est misericordi erga nos affectu tincta & temperata. Ubi Deus passiones suorum pensat æterna gloria, ex gratia sane & non ex debito, si videlicet ipsarummet passionum qualitatem spectes, quæ (certe ut prius dictum) pondus æternum illud gloriae promereri nequaquam possunt.

Quatenus autem remuneratio hæc Verbo Dei promissa est, nunc vi promissionis ista facta in debitum quodammodo cadit, ita ut post factam promissionem justum Deoqe dignum sit servare, qua promissit, ne veritas ipsius in discrimen vocetur.

Neque ἄξιον idem est, quod meritum, ut è Matth. III, 8. Actor. XXVI, 20. constat: nec causæ dignationis nostræ exprimuntur hic opera vel passiones nostræ, sed DEI gratiæ unice illa tribuitur, qui dignatur nos vocatione (ἀξίωσιν) & complet omne beneplacitum bonitatis fuæ in nobis, & opus fidei ἐν δυνάμει, v. 11. Porro poterat Apostolus hic vitam & salutem aut gaudium nominare: Havlt regnum, quod ista omnia complectitur, & plus notat.

Qui enim regnat, is salvus est, is vivit, is gaudet; non autem utcunque quoque est, vivit, & gaudet, sed gloriose. Vers. 6. (Εἴπερ) Siquidem.

Utrumque enim poni soles αἰτιολογικῶς. Est autem argumentum à minori ad majus. Δίκαιον παρὰ Θεῷ ἀνταποδόναι τοῖς θλίβουσιν ὑμᾶς θλῖψιν. V. 7. Καὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς θλιβομένοις ἄνεσιν μεθ' ἡμῶν) δέησιν .

Ebræis significat omne id, quod aliquo modo æquum est, & rationi congruit. Etiam si nec Deus promissit quicquam, nec comminatus esset, tamen æquum erat, & ipsus tum bonitate tum severitate dignum, ipsius Dei causa mala ferentibus inferre pœnas, quanto magis hoc æquum est, cum & promissio & comminatio intercesserint, naturale est illud: Εἴπερ πάθετε τὰ ἃ δείξει, δίκην ἃ ἴδια γένοιτο.

Item ex æquitate naturali esse τὰ ἀντίδωρα ajunt Jurisconsulti. Non omittam hic dictum Athenagoræ: Ἄνθρωπος, ὃς ὧδε ἐνδέης δεῖται τροφῆς· ὡς δὲ θνητὸς, διαδοχῆς· ὡς δὲ λογικὸς, δίκης. Ἀνταποδῶναι est, diciturque tam de bonis rebus, ut Ps. XVIII, 24. quam de malis ut Ps. CIII, 10. ὀν-βυσιν ὑμᾶς . מִנּוֹכִים Opponitur θλῖψιν, significatque solatium, Actor. XXIV, 25. In Glossario ἄνεσις requies. Idem quod ἀνάπαυσις מְנוּחָה. Vulgata reddit, si tamen, sed convenientius est, siquidem.

Quod poni, ait Chrysostomus, in iis, de quibus valde constat, ut contradici non possit; pro eo, quod est valde justum, ut si DEUS odio habeat malos, ut eos cogat dicere, quod odio habeat. Sunt enim ejusmodi sententia minime dubiæ, utpote, quod & illi ipsi fiant, quod justum est.

Nam si hoc justum est apud homines, multo magis apud Deum. Quod admittimus, si de ἀνταποδόσει affligentibus & afflictis debita simpliciter sermo fit.

Tum enim ea rationi congruit, & apud homines etiam æqua judicatur. Sed hic de æterna retributione agitur: ad quam ratio non assurgit.

Non probare τὴν δικαιοκρισίαν τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ Θεοῦ volebat Apostolus. Ideo in ratione, qua eam probat, ut θλῖψις non generatim, sed illa æterni exitii est, quemadmodum postea exponitur v. 9. intelligenda: Ita & ἄνεσις per λυτρότητα explicanda, ut non nuda relaxatio, sed τὸ ἐνδοξασθῆναι simul inferatur, v. 10. De exitio autem æterno, ac de gloria & beatitudine æterna nihil novit ratio, nec in illa ἀνταποδόσει equitas naturalis respicitur, maxime quum omnibus, nobis secundum jus DEI retributionis loco propter peccatum debeatur mors, & condemnatio æterna, nulli, quantumcunque & quacunque de causa afflicto, quantumcunque patienti in afflictionibus, ex justitia debeatur vita æterna, omnibus contingat ex gratia DEI, nec nisi propter meritum Christi.

Stipendium enim peccati mors est, donum autem Dei vita æterna in Christo Jesu Domino nostro, Rom. VI, 23. Unde liquet, non hic justitiam DEI absolute spectandam esse, sed, ut diximus, supposita satisfactione Christi meritoria, quum quod ad fideles, quibus regnum DEI & gloria æterna tribuitur, justitia DEI allegetur cum temperamento gratiæ per Christum acquisitæ spectata: quantum vero ad infideles, causa condemnationis non peccatum, vel injusta afflictio piorum fit, siquidem etiam pro impiis Christus mortuus fit, & propitiatio factus pro peccatis totius mundi, sed infidelitas, per quam reprobant illi satisfactionem Christo se præstitam, & ita æternum pereunt.

Cum ergo dubium movetur, quomodo pro temporali afflictione æternum subeundum fit exitium, aliquid quidem dicitur, cum respondet Crocius; Etsi ipsi affligant pios tantum ad tempus, cum tamen hoc ex eo fit, non quod non velint semper affligere, optarent enim æterna morte multare, sed quod non possint, quod non perpetuo hic vivant, præterea illos persequendo in ipsum Deum æternum peccent, omnino justum est, reddi afflictionem æternam. Neutiquam vero sufficit ejusmodi responsio.

Nam omittitur præcipua causa, contemptus nempe ac reprobatio infinitæ satisfactionis, & immensi meriti Christi, qui cum æternus Deus est, benedictus in secula super omnia, sanguine suo acquisivit, & æternam mortem pro toto genere humano sustinuit, ut à morte æterna id redimeret. Hoc ergo meritum infiniti pretii qui negligunt & repudiant, quidni æternum justo Dei judicio mereantur exitium.

De ἀνταποδόσει etiam observandum, aliam esse retributionem unius pro alio, ut cum pro labore quies, aliam unius propter aliud; ut cum merces propter laborem redditur: Illa est simplicis commutationis; hac vero est debitæ compensationis: Illam hic admittimus, hanc vero locum hic habere negamus; quæ nulla est inter afflictiones nostras & futuram cœlestem gloriam æqualitas, Rom. IIX, 18. Fructra ergo Pontificii pro meritis suis hanc ἀνταποδόσει adducunt. Εν τῇ ἀποκαλύψει τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἀπ' οὐρανοῦ Putem illa ἄνε & sequentia posse per πειράζειν legi: & hæc ἐν τῇ ἀποκαλύψει referri ad id, quod præcepit, καλαξιωθῆναι ὑμᾶς τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ Θεοῦ.

Vocat autem ἀποκάλυψιν, quod alibi παρουσία, quia Ebraeis dicitur גלה, id est, ἀποκάλυ-ψις, omne id, quod apparet, cum ante non apparuerit, ut Prov. XXVII 25. Rom. VIII. 18. Ἐν τῇ ἀποκαλύψει denotatio temporis: ut ἐν παρουσίᾳ 1. Thess. II. 19. III. 13. Ἀποκάλυψις dicitur, quia tum manifestabitur praesentia, ut innuatur, jam quidem non abesse, promisit enim, se praesto nobis futurum usque ad consummationem seculi, Matth. XXIX. 29. non vero tamen apparere, sed in illa die appariturum omnibus. Sic etiam per revelationem, apparitionem, manifestationem describitur adventus CHRISTI, 1. Cor. I. 7. Col. III. 4. 2. Thess. II. 8. 1. Tim. VI. 14. 2. Tim. IV. 1. 1. Petr. I. 7. cap. V. 4. 1. Job. II. 28. Quod omnino ideo fit, ne quis omnimodam absentiam Christi secundum humanam naturam ex ejus adventu colligat: Sicut vita aeterna credentibus praesens est, sed abscondita, Col. III. 24. sic Tum vero manifestabitur. Ἀπ' οὐρανοῦ vero patefiet, non quod caelo jam conclusus fit; sed quia in coelis sese electis & Angelis gloriose manifestat: tum autem de caelo patefiet cum Angelis potentia.

Absint autem humanae rationis figmenta de caelo materiali & descensu locali ac moro progressivo e caelo in aerem, quae gloriae Christi ad dextram DEI sedentis minime conveniunt. Num enim deferet Dei dextram? Aut evacuabitur caelum Angelis? Num manifestari nequit in aere, nisi demittat sese in aerem e supremo caelo per multa milliarum millia? Ubi tamen non negamus, cum qui nunc invisibiliter ad Dei dextram nobis adest, tunc fore in die judicii manifestandum, quando juxta proprietatem sui corporis e sublimi visibiliter in nube defendet. - Μετ' ἀγγέλων δυνάμεως αὐτοῦ)

Vide quae allata dicto loco 1. Thessal. III. 13. Ἀγγελοι δυνάμεως αὐτοῦ, id est, Angeli, qui Majestati ejus interviunt. Vide Matth. XXIV. 64.

Per δύναμιν exercitum quidem intelligit Drusius libr. VII. Praeterit. ut & Cornelius à Lapide, ut 1. Maccab. III. 34. 37. cap. IV. 3. 4. 31. cui sensui collato Psal. CIII. 21. Psal. CXLII. 2. Luc. II. 13. favere videtur. Verum quia non dicitur cum virtute Angelorum, ut Syrus reddidit, sed cum Angelis virtutis suae, scholia Graeca & Theophylactus Angelos potentes intelligunt, quod per idiotismum Ebraeum illustrari potest: Alii simpliciter Angelos virtutis Domini, quam per eosdem exercet atque demonstrat, ut Lombardus, B. Lutherus, Calvinus explicant, quibus hic Grotius accedit, neque nos abnuimus.

## 1:8
Verf. 8. Εν πυρὶ φλογὸς) with flaming fire. The same is πῦρ φλογὸς as here, and φλὲξ πυρὸς, Pf. XXVIII. 7. Ef. XXIX. 6. LX. 6. Joël. II. 5. Apoc. XIX. 12. because what is in the Hebrew dative, it has sometimes the meaning of the subject, sometimes of the adjunct, e.g.: it is worth with. Concerning the sense see Matth. V. 22. XVIII. 8. 9. XXV. 41. Marc. IX. 43. 45. 2. Petr. III. 7. Judae v. 7. it is accustomed to be attributed to all judgments of God as a flaming fire, as can be seen in the said places of the Old Testament: but by special right to this extreme and universal one, Whether Grotius understands the fire as flame or flaming, or the fire of hell, I would not say?

Concerning the infernal fire, by which the impious will be tortured, most of the adduced places treat, Matth. V. 22. cap. XII. 8. 9. cap. XXV. 41. Marc. IX. 43. 45. Concerning which Theodoret also interprets the present place.

Others concerning the fire with which the Lord of Majesty will come for the sake of judgment.

Which Crocius explains with Bonaventura concerning fire properly so called and natural, since the water of the flood was also natural, 2. Pet. III. 7. But that collection is less firm. For natural water was not lacking there, but in heaven, whence Christ will come, I do not believe that natural fire will call Crocius, unless he says the empyrean heaven, or perhaps the third heaven itself with the Scholastics, which we explode in System. Theol. Art. V. §. II. q. V. But if it is asked what the use of this fire will be, Crocius attributes the conflagration of the world to it.

Some Scholastics among Justinian with Augustine, (Dionys. Carthuf. in 1. Thess. IV. Tostato in Matth. XXIV.) [attribute] the consumption of all mortals, who will be survivors on the last day; which, that all the pious alike as well as the impious, are to be burned by fire, is not only not probable, but also repugnant to the Apostolic sentence 1. Thess. IV. proposed concerning the faithful, who then being survivors, are to be caught up alive to meet the Lord. Others ascribe to this flame of fire the purgation of all mortals recalled to life, which opinion Justinian assigns not only to Lactantius and Origen, but also to Basil the Great, Ambrose, Jerome, Hilary, Caesarius, nay even to Augustine, pronouncing it however false and impious, and not undeservedly.

Barnadius in book IX. comment. in Conc. Evangel. cap. II. p. 59. ascribes three things to that flame of fire: 1. the combustion of the earth, and the consumption of all living men: 2. the purgation of the burned men: 3. the expurgation of the world. But scripture predicts the dissolution of the world. But it knows nothing of the consumption or purgation of men by fire. This one thing therefore remains, that this fire be considered παυτολέθρως, by which heaven and earth with the elements will perish ignited by fire, 2. Petr. III. 7. the type of which is constituted by the fire, which consumed Sodom and Gomorrah Gen. XIX. 24. 2. Petr. III. 9. To which it contributes, that the advent of the Lord to judgment is also designated in other places in the sacred scriptures as being about to be with fire, Pf. XI. 6. Psal. XCVII. 3. Ef. LXVI. 15. 16. Dan. VII. 9. Sopb. I. 18. cap. III. 8. Apoc. IV. 5. c. XX. 9. But which fire is most different from the infernal, the inspection of the places teaches. Διδόντα ἔκδικησιν) διδόντα refers to that more remote τῷ Κυρίῳ Ἰησοῦ χριστῷ. This διδόντα ἔκδικησιν is the same as ποιεῖν ἐκδίκησιν, Luc. XVIII. 7. 8. Act. VII. 24. The same locution as here, Ezech. XXV. 14. and elsewhere. Τοῖς μὴ εἰδόσι Θεόν)

Who do not know God, that is, do not acknowledge, who do not care for Him any more than Pharaoh Exod. V. 2. see 1. Thess. IV. 5. Καὶ τοῖς μὴ ὑπακούουσι τῷ Εὐαγγελίῳ τῷ Κυρίῳ ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ χριστῷ)

For from that law judgment is rendered against those, to whom the Gospel has been announced, Rom. II. 16. Ὑπακούειν Εὐαγγελίῳ here and Rom. X. 16. 2. Thess. I. 8. is to receive the Gospel, as having proceeded from God, and to institute life according to it.

A double kind of those who will feel the just punishment at the coming of the Lord, he notes: The one of those who have not known God, that is, not only those who did not want to acknowledge and care for Him, as Pharaoh, to whom He showed Himself by Word and miracles, but of all who remained in their natural corruption and blindness, such as the Gentiles, Turks, and Jews, then adults, who either did not inquire after or did not acknowledge the true God Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, then infants. The other of those who rejected the Evangelical doctrine, or did not receive the obedience of faith: Both of whom are included in the number of non-believers, for he who does not believe is condemned, Job. III. 17. Mark XVI. 16. He does not say those who afflict you, as before, but those who have not known God, and have not obeyed the Gospel. Which Theophylactus observed with Chrysostom: Above he said those oppressing you, but now commonly to all who are ignorant of God, prudently affirming that, it will be entirely that God will avenge these. For even if He were doing it for our sake, He is nevertheless about to take punishment from the enemies for the sake of Himself. And further: If He punishes and tortures those who do not obey the Gospel at all, much more those who hinder others, so that they do not obey the Gospel, such as these are, who vex you at present.

Latin:

Vers. 8. Εν πυρὶ φλογὸς) cum igne flammante. Idem est πῦρ φλογὸς ut hic, & φλὲξ πυρὸς, Ps. XXVIII. 7. Es. XXIX. 6. LX. 6. Joël. II. 5. Apoc. XIX. 12. quia quod Ebraeis dicitur dative est, id modo subjecti, modo adjuncti habet significationem, e. g.: valet cum. De sensu vide Matth. V. 22. XVIII. 8. 9. XXV. 41. Marc. IX. 43. 45. 2. Petr. III. 7. Judae v. 7. omnibus Dei judiciis solet attribui flammeus igne, ut dictis locis Veteris Testamenti videre est: at eximio jure isti extremo atque universali, Ignem flamma vel flammeum, sive flammam ignis, an de gehenna intelligat Grotius nec ne, haud dixerim?

De igne infernali, quo cruciabitur impii, loca pleraque adducta agunt, Matth. V. 22. cap. XII. 8. 9. cap. XXV. 41. Marc. IX. 43. 45. Quo de interpretatur praesentem etiam locum Theodoretus.

Alii de igne, cum quo veniet Dominus Majestatis causa ad judicium.

Quem cum Bonaventura de igne proprie dicto ac naturali explicat Crocius, siquidem aqua diluvii etiam naturalis fuerit, 2. Pet. III. 7. Sed collectio illa minus firma est. Aqua enim naturalis ibi non deerat, sed in caelo, unde veniet Christus, non credo ignem naturalem locaturum Crocium, nifo coelum empyraeum dicat, vel fortassis ipsum coelum tertium cum Scholasticis, quod explodimus in System. Theol. Art. V. §. II. q. V. Quis autem ignis istius usus futurus sit, si quaeratur, Crocius conflagrationem mundi eidem tribuit.

Scholastici nonnulli apud Justinianum cum Auguſtino, (Dionys. Carthus. in 1. Thess. IV. Tostato in Matth. XXIV.) absumptionem omnium mortalium, qui in novissimo die superstites erunt; quos omnes pios pariter atque impios, igne crematum iri, non modo probabile non est, sed repugnat etiam Apostolicae sententiae 1. Thess. IV. propositae de fidelibus, qui tum superstites, vivis in occursum Domini rapiendis. Alii adscribunt isti flammae ignis mortalium omnium ad vitam revocatorum purgationem, quam sententiam non Lactantio tantum & Origeni, sed etiam Basilio M. ambrosio, Hieronymo, Hilario, Casario, imo Augustino quoque assignat Justinianus, eam tamen falsam atque impiam, nec immerito, pronuncians.

Barnadius libr. IX. comment. in Conc. Evangel. cap. II. p. 59. tria illi flammae ignis adscribit: 1. terrae combustione, & omnium hominum viventium absumptione: 2. Combustorum hominum purgationem: 3. Mundi expurgationem. Sed scriptura mundi dissolutionem praedicit. De hominum vero per ignem vel consumptione vel purgatione nihil novit. Id ergo unum restat, ut ignis iste censeatur παυτολέθρως, quo caelum & terra cum elementis igne accensa peribunt, 2. Petr. III. 7. cujus typus constituitur ignis, qui Sodomam & Gomorrham consumpsit Gen. XIX. 24. 2. Petr. III. 9. Quo facit, quod adventus Domini ad judicium etiam alias in sacris literis cum igne futurus designetur, Ps. XI. 6. Psal. XCVII. 3. Es. LXVI. 15. 16. Dan. VII. 9. Sopb. I. 18. cap. III. 8. Apoc. IV. 5. c. XX. 9. Quem vero ignem ab infernali maxime diversum inspectio locorum docet. Διδόντα ἔκδικησιν) διδόντα refertur ad illud remotius τῷ Κυρίῳ Ἰησοῦ χριστῷ. Est hic διδόντα ἔκδικησιν idem, quod ποιεῖν ἐκδίκησιν, Luc. XVIII. 7. 8. Act. VII. 24. Eadem quae loquutio, Ezech. XXV. 14. & alibi. Τοῖς μὴ εἰδόσι Θεόν)

Qui Deum non noscunt, id est, non agnoscunt, qui non magis eum curant, quam Pharao Exod. V. 2. vide 1. Thess. IV. 5. Καὶ τοῖς μὴ ὑπακούουσι τῷ Εὐαγγελίῳ τῷ Κυρίῳ ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ χριστῷ)

Nam ex ea lege judicium redditur in eos, quibus Evangelium annuntiatum est, Rom. II. 16. Ὑπακούειν Εὐαγγελίῳ hic & Rom. X. 16. 2. Thess. I. 8. est Evangelium, ut à Deo profectum recipere, & secundum id instituere vitam
