Duplex genus eorum, qui justam poenam in adventu Domini sentient, notat: Alterum eorum, qui non noverunt Deum, hoc est, non modo, qui agnoscere ac curare noluerunt, ut Pharao, cui se Verbo & miraculis demonstravit, sed omnium, qui in naturali sua corruptione ac caecitate manserunt, quales sunt gentes, Turcae, ac Judaei, tum adulti, qui verum Deum Patrem, Filium, & Spiritum Sanctum vel non inquisiverunt, vel non agnoverunt, tum infantes. Alterum eorum, qui Evangelicam doctrinam reprobarunt, vel obedientiam fidei haud receperunt: Qui utrique non credentium numero comprehenduntur, qui enim non credit, damnatur, Job. III. 17. Marci XVI. 16. Non dicit eos, qui vos affligunt, ut antea, sed qui Deum non noverunt, & Evangelio non obtemperarunt. Quod cum Chrysostomo Theophylactus observavit: Superius dixit vos opprimentibus, nunc vero cunelis communiter, qui Deum ignorant, prudenter illud affirmans, futurum omnino, ut hos vindicet Deus. Nam etsi id nostri de causa faceret, sui tamen ipsius ob gratiam sumpturus de hostibus supplicium est. Et porro: Si eos, qui Evangelio nihil obsequuntur, punit & cruciat, longe magis, qui alios interpellant, ne Evangelio pareant, quales bi sunt, qui vos impraentiarum divexant.

## 1:9
Verf. 9. οἵτινες δίκην τίσεσι They shall pay the penalty. Thus δίκην καὶ τίνεσα Euripides Iphigenea in tauris. The same in Phryxo τιμωρίαι ἴτισε. Theodectes: Τίνεσι ποινάς, another, τίσεσ' ἀμοιβάς. Thus ζαμίαν τίσεσι Prov.

1. ὄλεθρον αἰώνιον He explains what the future punishment will be: namely, than which there is none more grievous. ὄλεθρον, as 1.

Thess. V. 3. elsewhere ὄλεθρον Matth. VII. 13. Rom. IX. 22. Phil. III. 19. αἰώνιον, thus πῦρ αἰώνιον, Matth. XVIII. 8. XXV. 41. Jude verf. 7 ῥείων αἰώνιον Marc. III. 29.

Grotius does not sufficiently explain what he understands by destruction, lest heretical opinions might be hidden under that general term. Moreover, the Apostle understands by ὄλεθρον destruction not of the body only, nor of the soul only, but of soul and body, Matth. X. 28. not annihilation, as the Socinians, concerning whom in Socinismo profligato, but eternal affliction, because their worm shall not die, and their fire shall not be quenched, Is. LXVI. 21. Mark IX. 44. Therefore they shall seek death, but shall not find it, Apoc. IX. 6. Destruction is called eternal not improperly, concerning an eternity that will have an end, as the Origenists dreamed, but concerning eternity properly so called, which will never cease and is interminable.

For as life is called eternal, because it will have no end: So also destruction is called eternal, because it will have no end. How is it an eternal destruction? ἀπὸ προσώπου τοῦ Κυρίου καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς δόξης τῆς ἰσχύος αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ here designates the cause as Rom. I. 7. 2. Cor. I. 2. and elsewhere often.

If you ask, he says, whence that punishment? From the face, that is, from the mouth, from the sentence of his own magnificence, through which he executes what is judged. Thus ἀπὸ προσώπου, but in a good sense beas Acts III. 20. These words seem to be taken from Isa. III. 10. & 19. Photius and Theophylact refer this not so much to the cause as to the ease of the execution, by which the Judge will be present.

Others, whom Grotius follows, to the speed of the execution: There will be no long delay, no long process. As soon as the Judge appears, the wicked will undergo their punishments. They will not be able to contend, they will not want to: they will not be able to bear the sight of the Judge, but struck by his mere presence or by lightning they will fall into the fire. But that does not seem to correspond in every way to the process of judgment described in Matth. XXV. Others explain it concerning rejection from the face of the Lord by subaudition of the word ἀπωσάμενοι rejected.

Although we do not admit that this is to be understood, much less inserted into the text with Beza, yet we do not understand only the bare presence and appearance of the judge in this way: The wicked will sustain the eternal judgment, to which they will be adjudged by Christ Jesus, who will appear in his own person with his glorious presence, which explanation B. Gerhardus LL. CC. on hell §. 19. brought forward, not only the bare cause, as Grotius interpreted, not only the ease of execution with Theophylact: He explains in this place how easy it is for God to inflict torture.

Nor will there be any difficulty for him in inflicting these, since by his mere aspect the rebellious and contumacious will be tortured, since with the divine presence it will indeed bring splendor to these, but to those punishments. For he is not to come simply, but with glory and power, so that neither does this glory lack power, nor does power lack glory, but he will come as some most powerful Emperor. But since all these things well consist together, we think all those things are insinuated, and furthermore it is noted, that this destruction will be an abjection or exclusion from the face of GOD, for he who experiences destruction from the face of the Lord, does not stand before the face of the Lord, but is cast away from it, which will be the most grievous punishment for the reprobate, to suffer destruction from the face of the Lord, that they may not see it, and be eternally reprobated and rejected by it, by which very thing they also suffer destruction and casting away from the glory of his power, and there is also included eternal condemnation; for where are they cast from the face of GOD, if not into hell, that they may feel destruction there eternally?

For punishments are said to be about to give eternal destruction from the face of the Lord, and from the glory of his power, or from his glorious power, because the power of GOD will preserve them in the midst of the flames of the infernal regions, so that they may not be reduced to nothing by the infernal fire, just as the fire of judgment will reduce heaven and earth to nothing, as B. Gerhardus has it l. c. §. 31.

If we understand from the face of GOD not the gracious one, whose vision is eternal life, but the angry one, just as the face of GOD imports the wrath of GOD, Psalm XXXII. 17. Psalm LXIIX. 3. Jerem. XXI. 10. 1. Pet. III. 12. Apoc. VI. 16. to suffer destruction from the same, and rejection from grace and glory, and reprobation to eternal punishment and ignominy is brought about without doubt.

For where there is nothing but the angry face of GOD, there is no mercy, nor can anything follow but a horrible and intolerable punishment, Apoc. VI. verf. 16. Where ὄλεθρον or destruction from the face of the Lord is, there is not only a privation of all grace, of all good, but also a heap of punishment, of all evil.

They will feel, according to the Hunnian paraphrase, that the face of GOD does not shine upon them, with the lovable brightness of grace, as it does for the pious, but in aspect threatens them with nothing but horrible indignation. They will feel the strength of the infinite fortitude of God, by whose intolerable weight they will be pressed far more grievously than if they had the vast globe of the earth imposed upon their necks.

Therefore mention is made of the wine of the wrath of God Apoc. XIV. 10. mixed with pure τὸ κεκερασμένης;

Apoc. XIV. verf. 10. which is so called, because it will be full of the turbid dregs of various punishments, but it is called unmixed, because it is not tempered with the vital water of mercy, like the cup of the cross, which is offered to the pious in this life, Psalm LXXV. verf. 9. Luc. XVI. verf. 28. All of which are hinted at here.

Concerning the wrath of GOD see Deuter. XXXII. verf. 22. Psalm II. verf. 12. Job XXVIII. verf. 36. Job X. verf. 30. By his mere advent, says Hyperius: Thus God in that advent to judgment will shake the hearts of the wicked, so that for their greatest tortures they will have to see God, the angry judge.

Nor will GOD simply terrify the wicked with his countenance, but will also move them with the admirable glory of his fortitude. Since his majesty and power will yield to the wicked for the augmentation of pain: Punishments will increase for them, when they have beheld the most ample glory of GOD. Chrysostomus homil. XXIV. in Matth. cap. VII. A thousand hells, he says, punishments, and nothing is like being excluded from God, and being held in hatred by God.

Augustinus in libr. de tripl. habitac. The absence of Christ regarding vision surpasses all other torments, and is more intolerable than all punishments. Calvin interprets concerning eternity, when he comes to the words from the face of the Lord: by opposition, he says, he shows what kind of punishment it is, of which he had made mention, namely destruction lacking an end, and immortal death. The perpetuity of death is proved from this, that it has the glory of Christ coming upon it, as that which is eternal, and has no end.

Therefore its force will never cease. He also explains concerning the quality of the punishment. Thence, he continues, the atrocity of the terrible punishment can be gathered, because it will be as great as the glory and majesty of Christ is.

Latin:

9. οἵτινες δίκην τίσεσι Poedant poenam. Sic δίκην καὶ τίνεσα Euripides Iphigenea in tauris. Idem in Phryxo τιμωρίαι ἴτισε. Theodectes: Τίνεσι ποινάς, alius, τίσεσ' ἀμοιβάς. Sic ζαμίαν τίσεσι Prov.

1. ὄλεθρον αἰώνιον Explicat qualis fit futura poena: nempe qua gravior nulla. ὄλεθρον, ut 1.

Thess. V. 3. alibi ὄλεθρον Matth. VII. 13. Rom. IX. 22. Phil. III. 19. αἰώνιον, sic πῦρ αἰώνιον, Matth. XVIII. 8. XXV. 41. Judæ vers. 7 ῥείων αἰώνιον Marc. III. 29.

Non explicat satis Grotius, quid per exitium intelligat, quin sub ista generali natione occultari possent sententiae haereticae. Ceterum Apostolus ὄλεθρον exitium intelligit non corporis tantum, nec tantum animae, sed animae & corporis, Matth. X. 28. non annihilationem, ut Sociniani, de quibus in Socinismo profligato, sed aeternam afflictionem, quia vermis eorum non morietur, & ignis eorum non extinguetur, Es. LXVI. 21. Marc. IX. 44. Ideo mortem quaerent, sed non invenient, Apoc. IX. 6. Aeternum dicitur exitium non improprie, de aeternitate finem habitura, ut Origeniani somniarunt, sed de aeternitate proprie dicta, nunquam desitura & interminabili.

Ut enim vita aeterna dicitur, quia finem non habebit: Ita & exitium dicitur aeternum, quod finem habiturum non est. Quomodo aeternum exitium sit? ἀπὸ προσώπου τοῦ Κυρίου καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς δόξης τῆς ἰσχύος αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ hic designat causam ut Rom. I. 7. 2. Cor. I. 2. & alibi saepe.

Si quaeris, inquit, unde illa poena? A facie, id est, ab ore, à sententia ipsius magnificentia, per quam judicatum exequitur. Sic ἀπὸ προσώπου, sed in bonam partem beas Act. III. 20. Videntur autem haec verba sumpta ex Esa. III. 10. & 19. Id non tam ad causam, quam ad facilitatem executionis, qua praesens erit Judex, refert Photius & Theophylactus.

Alii, quos Grotius sequitur, ad celeritatem executionis: Non longa erit mora, non longus processus. Quam primum Judex apparuerit, impii subibunt poenas. Non poterunt contendere, non volent: Conspectum Judicis ferre non poterunt, sed solo adfetu perculsi vel fulmine prostrati ruent in ignem. Sed id non usquequaque videtur congruere processui judicii Matth. XXV. descripto. Alii de rejectione exponunt à facie Domini subintelligendo verbum ἀπωσάμενοι rejeći.

Quanquam vero id subaudiendum esse non admittamus, nedum textui cum Beza inferendum, non tamen nudam tantum praesentiam & comparitionem judicis intelligimus hoc modo: Impii sustinebunt aeternum judicium, cui adjudicabuntur à Christo Jesu, qui in propria persona apparebit cum gloriosa sua praesentia, quam explicationem adduxit B. Gerhardus LL. CC. de inferno §. 19. non nudam tantum causam, ut Grotius interpretatus est, non facilitatem modo executionis cum Theophylacto: Hoc loco quam Deo facile fit cruciatus inferre, exponit.

Neque enim illi aliqua erit in inferendis his difficultas, quippe cujus vel solo aspectu rebelles & contumaces cruciabuntur, quandoquidem cum divina praesentia his quidem splendorem est allatura, illis supplicia. Non enim simpliciter ille, sed cum gloria & virtute est adventurus, ita ut neque hujus gloria potentia caveat, nec potentia fit gloria expers, sed tanquam potentissimus Imperator aliquis veniet. Sed quum ista omnia simul probe consistant, omnia illa insinuari censemus, ac praeterea notari, exitium id fore à facie DEI abjectionem vel exclusionem, qui enim exitium à facie Domini experitur, coram facie Domini non consistit, sed ab illa projicitur, quae gravissima reprobis poena erit, exitium pati à facie Domini, ne eam videant, & ab ea in aeternum reprobari ac rejici, quo ipso à gloria potentiae ejus etiam patiuntur exitium ac projectionem, quin includitur etiam condemnatio aeterna; quo enim projiciuntur à facie DEI, nisi in infernum, ut aeternum ibi sentiant exitium?

Nam dicuntur poenae daturi aeternum exitium à facie Domini, & à gloria virtutis ejus, vel à gloriosa ejus virtute, quia virtus DEI in mediis inferorum flammis conservabit eos, ne ab igne infernali in nihilum redigantur, sicut ignis judicii coelum & terram in nihilum rediget, ut habet B. Gerhardus l. c. §. 31.

Si de facie DEI non gratiosa, cujus visio est aeterna vita, sed irata intelligamus, quemadmodum facies DEI iram DEI importat, Psal. XXXII. 17. Psal. LXIIX. 3. Jerem. XXI. 10. 1. Petr. III. 12. Apoc. VI. 16. exitium ab eadem pati, & rejectio à gratia & gloria, & reprobatio ad aeternam poenam & ignominiam citra dubietatem infertur.

Ubi enim non est nisi irata DEI facies, ibi nulla misericordia est, nec nisi poena sequi potest horrenda atque intolerabilis, Apoc. VI. vers. 16. Ubi ὄλεθρον vel exitium à facie Domini, ibi non privatio tantum omnis gratiae, omnis boni, sed etiam cumulus poenae, omnis mali.

Sentient, juxta paraphrasin Hunnianam, faciem DEI sibi non lucere, amabili fulgore gratiae, veluti piis luce, sed im-aspectu nil nisi horribilem indignationem ipsis minitari. Sentient robur infinitae fortitudinis Dei, cujus intolerabili pondere longe prementur gravius, quam si vastum terrarum orbem suis cervicibus impositum haberent. Ideo mentio fit vini ira Dei Apoc.

XIV. 10. mixti mero τὸ κεκερασμένης; Apoc. XIV. vers. 10. quod ita appellatur, quia turbidis variarum poenarum fecibus erit plenum, ἄκρατον vero dicitur, quia non est misericordiae aqua vitali temperatum, sicut calix crucis, qui in hac vita piis propinatur, Psalm.

LXXV. vers. 9. Luc. XVI. vers. 28. Que omnia hic innuuntur.

De ira DEI vid. Deuter. XXXII. vers. 22. Psalm. II. vers. 12. Job XXVIII. vers. 36. Job X. vers. 30. Solo adventu suo, inquit Hyperius: Sic Deus in illo adventu ad judicium concutiet impiorum corda, ut pro maximis cruciatibus habituri sint videre Deum, iratum judicem.

Neque vero simpliciter suo vultu DEUS terrebit impios, sed etiam commovebit eos admirabili gloria fortitudinis fue. Siquidem majestas illius & potentia impiis cedet ad doloris augmentum: Crescent illis poenae, quando conspexerint amplissimam DEI gloriam. Chrysostomus homil. XXIV. in Matth. cap. VII. Mille gehennas, inquit, poenas, & nihil tale est, quale est excludi à Deo, & odio haberi à Deo.

Augustinus in libr. de tripl. habitac. Absentia Christi quoad visionem omnia alia tormenta superat, & omnibus poenis intolerabilior est. Calvinus de aeternitate interpretatur, cum ad verba à facie Domini: per oppositionem, inquit, ostendit, qualis sit poena, cujus meminerat, nempe interitus fine carens, & mors immortalis. Mortis perpetuitas ex eo probatur, quod Christi gloriam sibi habet advenientem, ut quae aeterna est, nec finem habet.

Itaque vis ejus nunquam cessabit. Explicat etiam de qualitate poenae. Inde, pergit, & terribilis poena atrocitas colligi potest, quia tanta futura est, quanta est Christi gloria & majestas.

## 1:10
Verf. 10. ὅτι ἔλθῃ ἐνδοξασθῆναι ἐν τοῖς ἁγίοις αὐτοῦ καὶ θαυμασθῆναι ἐν πᾶσι τοῖς πιστεύουσι He said the same in the Hebrew manner, then it will come to pass, he says, when Christ, by raising the believers, and the same as saints, into the highest brightness, will obtain the glory to be admired from this fact. The sight of another's happiness aggravates the pain. You have θαυμάζεσθαι in this sense in Isa. LXI. verf. 6. 4. Reg. V. verf. 1. Sap. VIII. v. 12. XXXVIII. v. 3.

Concerning the admirable glorification of Christ in the saints, by which glory he is to be irradiated and illustrated, Apoc. XXII, 5. Rom. II. 10. these words properly sound, for which Christ himself will be glorified by the Elect for ages. He does not say that he may glorify, but that he may be glorified, declaring that it is of interest to the divine glory that the faithful obtain the reward. He does not say in himself, but in the saints. In himself he is glorious. But when he works glorious things in his own, he is glorified Ezech. XXVI. 15. chap. XXIV. vers. 23. Beautifully Theophylact: For when those who, while they were among the living, showed themselves in no way obedient to GOD, but were puffed up and elated, shall behold those whom they had afflicted with scourges now possessed of infinite glory, that will surely redound to the glory of God. Since indeed this glory will be common to them with GOD. Wherefore he increases the saints with honors, when he extols himself, for as he holds the faithful here for riches, so that will redound to his glory, when there are those who shall enjoy his goods. And to those; And may he be made admirable in all believers, that is, through all believers. For when GOD shall deem worthy of such clarity and splendor those who were miserable and vexed and affected by all injuries, then surely all his divine power will be revealed. B. Glassius: He will be glorified, he says in his exegetical annotations on this passage, Christ in the saints, 1. because he will communicate his glory to them as his own members. The glory of the head will be the glory of the members. 2. Because he will be glorified by them for all eternities. And he was to be admired in all believers. Because that glory, which Christ will communicate to believers, surpasses all reason and all the glory of the world. The Syrian: And he may show his wonders in his faithful ones. He names the faithful, however, to testify that the saints are not such by their own powers and merits, but through faith, and that true holiness has no place without faith in Christ, and that Christ will not acknowledge any as his own, unless they have believed in him.

Because our testimony was believed among you in that day) The sense is: Because on that day that testimony which we brought to you will be clearly proven, namely, concerning the future coming of the judgment. Ἐπιστεύθη first for אמן, it was made firm, it was made ratified, because things which are such are accustomed to be believed. Then it is an Aorist, signifying a thing which, at that time of which it is treated, will have been completed: how the Syrian rightly takes it here. Just as, on the contrary, by the future is announced what is now present, but was once expected as future, Matth. XI. v. 14. Ἐφ' ὑμᾶς עליכם, as ἤγγικεν ἐφ' ὑμᾶς Luc. X. 1.

Grotius's explanation concerning the confirmation of the truth of the Apostolic testimony does not seem inappropriate, by which the faithful were entirely confirmed in patience and perseverance in the Apostolic doctrine they had received. But it would perhaps be more fitting if it were said that the application of the sayings is made here to the Thessalonians, because that glory is to come to them which he promised to believers. For the reason is rendered here why ἄνεσις is certainly to be hoped for by them here, namely because faith was held by them in the Evangelical proclamation, and why believers among them, already sustaining ignominy and persecution, are to obtain admirable glory from the Lord on that day of the Lord, because indeed they have embraced with true faith the testimony concerning Christ, of whom the Apostles were witnesses even among them. Crocius says the cause is rendered from their admirable faith, because faith was held not in high peace, but among dangers, terrors, passions, because of the testimony held, which such vile, such despised, such hated persons held. But concerning that quality of faith, that it is indeed admirable; nothing is held in this place. Blessed Hunnius, however, notes that a tacit antithesis is included here, and he renders this paraphrase not inappropriately: Just as they hasten eternal punishments for themselves by their disobedience: So the elect, who had faith in the testimony of the holy Apostles, or the Evangelical sermon concerning Christ, will feel on the last day the fruit of their faith, neither to be repented of nor to perish, namely that reciprocal glorification of God and the elect, of which he had just spoken. Flacius's gloss favors our opinion concerning the application made here: That he inserted as if by parenthesis that his testimony was believed toward them, seems to declare that preceding 'to believers', as if he were saying, which glory also pertains to you, since you have believed our preaching.

PART II. OF CHAPTER I. A prayer for the completion of the faith of the Thessalonians.

Latin:

Vers. 10. ὅτι ἔλθῃ ἐνδοξασθῆναι ἐν τοῖς ἁγίοις αὐτοῦ καὶ θαυμασθῆναι ἐν πᾶσι τοῖς πιστεύουσι Isdem idixit more Ebrao, tum id fiet, inquit, cum Christus credentes, eosdemque sanctos in summam claritatem evehendo, admirandam ex hoc facto gloriam consequetur. Gravat dolorem felicitatis alienae conspectus. θαυμάζεσθαι hoc sensu habes Esa. LXI. vers. 6. 4. Reg. V. vers. 1. Sap. VIII. v. 12. XXXVIII. v. 3.

De glorificatione admiranda Christi in sanctis, qua gloria ejus irradiandi & illustrandi sunt, Apoc. XXII, 5. Rom. II. 10. hæc proprie sonant, ob quam glorificabitur ipse Christus ab Electis in secula. Non dicit ut glorificet, sed ut glorificetur, declarans, interesse divinæ gloriæ, ut præmium consequantur fideles. Non dicit in seipso, sed in sanctis. In seipso est gloriosus. Sed cum in suis operatur gloriosa, glorificatur Ezech. XXVI. 15. cap. XXIV. vers. 23. Pulchre Theophylactus : Cum enim qui dum in humanis agerent, nihil se DEO morigeros præstitere, sed tumidi extitere & elati, eos conspicabuntur, quos flagris afflixerant, infinita gloria jam esse potitos, id sane in Dei gloriam cedet. Quippe cum communis sit his cum DEO futura hæc gloria. Quocirca sanctos ille honoribus auget, cum seipsum extollit, nam ut fideles hic pro divi- tiis habet, sic illud in ejus gloriam est concessurum, cum extent, qui suis bonis sint fruituri. Et ad illa; Et admirabilis fiat in omnibus credentibus, hoc est, per omnes credentes. Nam cum miseros quosque & divexatos, & ab omnibus affectos injuriis tanta cla- ritate & splendore dignabitur DEUS, tunc sane ejus vis omnis divina patebit. B. Glassius: Glori- ficabitur, inquit in exeget. annotat. ad h. l. Chri- stus in sanctis, 1. quia ipsis tanquam membris suis communicabit gloriam suam. Gloria capitis erit gloria membrorum. 2. Quia in omnes æternitates ab ipsis glorificabitur. Et admirandus fuit in omni- bus credentibus. Quia gloria illa, quam credenti- bus Christus communicabit, superat omnem ra- tionem, omnemque gloriam mundi. Syrus: Et ostendat mirabilia sua in fidelibus suis. Nominat autem fideles, ut testetur, non suis viribus & me- ritis sanctos esse, sed per fidem, nec locum habe- re veram sanctitatem citra fidem in fidem in Christum, nec pro suis Christum agniturum, nisi qui crediderint in ipsum.

Ὅτι ἐπιστεύθη τὸ μαρτύριον ἡμῶν ἐφ' ὑμᾶς ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκεί- νῃ) Sensus est : Quia die illa plane probatum erit illud te- stimonium, quod nos vobis attulimus, nempe de futuro ju- dicii adventu. Ἐπιστεύθη primum pro אמן, firmum fa- ctum est, ratum factum est, quia quæ talia sunt, iis credi solet. Deinde est Aoristus, significans rem, quæ illo tem- pore, de quo agitur, exacta erit : quomodo recte hic acce- pit Syrus. Sicut contra per futurum enuntiatur, quod nunc præsens est, sed olim, ut futurum expectabatur, Matth. XI. v. 14. Ἐφ' ὑμᾶς עליכם, ut ἤγγικεν ἐφ' ὑμᾶς Luc. X. 1.

Non inconcinna videtur Grotii explicatio de veritatis testimonii Apostolici articuli compro- batione, qua confirmabantur omnino fideles in patientia & perseverantia in suscepta doctrina A- postolica. Sed magis forte conveniens fuerit, si dicatur, hic applicationem dictorum fieri ad Thessalonicenses, quod ea gloria ipsis obventura sit, quam credentibus promisit. Nam redditur hic ratio, quare ipsis ἄνεσις hic certo speranda sit, quia scilicet fides ab ipsis habita est præconio Evangelico, & quare credentes inter ipsos jam ignominiam & persecutionem sustinentes in illa Domini die gloriam admirandam à Domino con- secuturi sint, quia nempe vera fide amplexi sunt testimonium de Christo, cujus testes fuere Apo- stoli etiam apud ipsos. Crocius causam reddi ait ab admirabili ipsorum fide, quod fides habita non in alta pace, sed inter pericula, terrores, passio- nes, quod testimonio habito, quod tam viles, tam contemptæ, tam exosæ personæ habuere. Sed de illa qualitate fidei, quod illa nempe admi- rabilis sit; nihil hoc loco habetur. Beat. Hunnius vero tacitam antithesin hic includi notat, hancque non incommode reddit paraphrasin : Sicut illi sua inobedientia sibi æternas pœnas accelerant : Sic electi, qui testimonio sanctorum Apostolorum, seu Evangelicæ concioni de Christo fidem habuerunt, sentient in die novissimo fructum fidei suæ, nec pœ- nitendum nec periturum, videlicet glorificationem reciprocam illam Dei & electorum, de qua modo dixerat. Nostræ sententiæ de applicatione hic facta favet glossa Flacii: Quod vero quasi per pa- renthesin inserferit, suum testimonium erga illos cre- ditum esse, videtur declarare illud præcedens credenti- bus, quasi diceret, qua gloria etiam ad vos pertinet, quandoquidem credidistis nostræ prædicationi.

PARS II. CAPITIS I. Εὐκτικὴ pro complemento fidei Thessa- lonicensium.

## 1:11
Vers. 11. Wherefore מטל הנא the Syrian. We pray always for you) Coloss. I. 3. 4. That our GOD may deem you worthy of the calling) That GOD may render you worthy of the calling, (that which happens through the Gospel). Thus we explain from Eph. IV. 1. יִרֶה. And thus the Syrian took it here, using the same word which is in Coloss. I. 12.

The calling includes the kingdom of God and celestial blessedness as its end: therefore there is no need to understand blessedness by a Metonymy of the adjunct with Aretius and Piscator. For those who are worthy of the calling, must be worthy of the kingdom of grace, worthy of the kingdom of glory and celestial blessedness, because they have been called to the kingdom of GOD. Which dignity, however, is from nowhere else than from the merit of Christ, from the grace of God. Therefore it must be obtained by prayers, that he may render us worthy, by giving faith, when we are not yet regenerated, or by confirming and perfecting the same in us, especially so that we do not fall from it in temptations and persecutions. Not that he may deem them worthy of the calling, so that they may first be called to the kingdom of God, but that he may make them worthy by that calling, lest they be rendered unworthy of the same through apostasy from the faith, or sins against conscience. Crocius understands this not of the beginning of the act of calling, but of its continuation and completion. Grotius more correctly: That he may render them worthy of the calling. Which Blessed Hunnius explains more fully in this way: Just as we rejoice, and give thanks to God for the joyful beginnings and increases of your Evangelical knowledge and piety; So in turn, mindful of human weakness and the snares of Satan, we pray to God unceasingly, that he may confirm you, who have been held worthy in Christ of the heavenly calling to eternal life, and found and declared worthy even under the examination of the cross, furthermore also with his powerful right hand, lest you ever fall from this most holy and most blessed calling.

Καὶ πληρώσῃ πᾶσαν εὐδοκίαν ἀγαθωσύνης) May He perfect in you all goodness pleasing to Him. You have a similar meaning of the word πληροῦν in Rom. VIII. 4. & 1. Corinth. X. 6. Εὐδοκίαν ἀγαθωσύνης, that is, goodness, in which there is pleasure for Him. See Luke II. 14.

Εὐδοκίαν ἀγαθωσύνης, which is of God, Castellio with Thomas refers to the Thessalonians. For he renders it thus: May He perfect that you may pursue and complete both most willingly and bravely goodness and the work of faith. Grotius understands it concerning goodness or holiness to be perfected. But the Apostle notably says not ἀγαθωσύνην τῆς εὐδοκίας, or in which there is pleasure for Him, but πᾶσαν εὐδοκίαν ἀγαθωσύνης. Therefore Chrysostom more correctly explains it concerning the purpose of God, and the Greek scholia, that God may fulfill all His good counsel toward you. But counsel, he adds, and the pleasure of God is that all men be saved, and that they obtain eternal goods. Which Crocius praises and defends (which is to be noted against other Calvinists): Anthony Scaymus, he says, claims to oppose this, because in the Apostle might pray for this manner, that he may fulfill the purpose or good pleasure of God's goodness, which is absurd to say, since every good pleasure of GOD is always perfect in every respect, so that no addition of goodness can be made to it. Therefore he prefers the gloss of Thomas concerning the will of the Thessalonians. It is indeed absurd that the good pleasure of God should be perfected by the addition of goodness, because it previously labored under imperfection, for no imperfection falls upon the goodness of GOD. But it is by no means absurd that εὐδοκίαν ἀγαθωσύνης, that is, the best and gratuitous benevolence, that is, should be carried out most fully. For that does not argue imperfection, but the liberty and constancy of GOD. That the Apostle prays for this follows from the Greek interpretation; that the Apostle prays for the former does not follow. The interpretation of the blessed Hunnius agrees: We pray to Him with suppliant vows, that He may complete in you πᾶσαν εὐδοκίαν ἀγαθωσύνης, every good pleasure of goodness, so that what He paternally determined from eternity concerning your being called to His kingdom, and has now in time mercifully begun to execute: He may hereafter also mercifully continue, and at length happily complete and perfect in all its parts with a full complement. Which εὐδοκίαν, as Crocius rightly opposes to merits, because the Apostle does not say, may He complete your merits, but εὐδοκίαν, that is, gratuitous benevolence not at all suspended upon your merits: Thus it must be taken with a grain of salt, lest the absolute decree of predestination be introduced, or that most absolute grace, the heart and palladium of the Reformed Church, mentioned in the Synod of Dort, which are added: Yet he does not stop here, but adds πᾶσαν, because He predestinated not only the completion of eternal salvation itself, but very many things necessary for attaining it. The Apostle prays for the completion of all those things. Indeed, because he cannot sufficiently extol the benevolence exhibited in CHRIST, he adds the word ἀγαθωσύνης, to declare the singular and in every way most absolute goodness of God, as if he were naming the most benevolent and best will of God. We acknowledge that our merits are excluded by this divine εὐδοκίαν ἀγαθωσύνης; the merit of Christ apprehended by faith cannot be excluded, because without it there is no εὐδοκία, Matt. III. verse 17, just as without faith it is impossible to please GOD, Heb. XI. verse 6. Therefore that grace of God is not absolute, but founded in the merit of Christ, which comes to us on account of Christ apprehended by true faith. Which is the reason why it is added: And the work of faith: Because without faith the εὐδοκία ἀγαθωσύνης, the most benign and most benevolent good pleasure of God, cannot be completed in us, Eph. I. verse 5 seqq.

Καὶ ἔργον πίστεως) A change of number for ἔργα πίστεως. Thus also 1 Thess. I. 3. Those works finally please God which are born of faith.

Ἐν δυνάμει) Powerfully. Thus Coloss. I. 29.

The phrase of the Apostle must be explained: He does not say; ἔργα πίστεως, but ἔργον πίστεως. Concerning which see 1 Thess. I. 3. Not works to be completed or perfected, but faith, which is the ἔργον τοῦ θεοῦ. Works are never completed here. For we are in the state of wayfarers, not of those who have arrived, as the Scholastics say. Nor are we rendered worthy of heavenly beatitude, by which works that are born of faith in us are completed. For beatitude is a gift of God: and by the grace of GOD we are saved through faith, not from works, Eph. II. 8, 9. Rom. VI. 23. Christ alone renders us worthy by His merit, which is imputed to us through faith. Therefore rightly the blessed Hunnius: He just now remembered all that good which happened to the Thessalonians. Now he expresses the principal part of that whole, faith, inasmuch as it alone, as a hand, apprehends and possesses all spiritual goods and gifts, which remaining safe, all our reason for salvation remains safe and

unshaken, but if it is weakened and extinguished, all the rest are immediately lost. He prays therefore specifically that the work of faith may be completed in them with power, that is, that faith in Jesus Christ may be kept unshaken to the very end in the Thessalonians by the power and virtue of God. Furthermore, he calls it a work in respect of GOD working it in us, just as in John chapter six faith is called the work of God, when the Lord answers the Jews: This is the work of God, that you believe in him whom he sent. To which can be reduced the explanation of Chrysostom and Theophylact, that patience is the work of faith, because ὑπομονὴ, perseverance in faith, is that work of faith which God for His εὐδοκία completes in us ἐν δυνάμει, 1 Pet. I. 5, ἵνα μὴ ἐκλυώμεθα, that we may not be dissolved, or fail, as Chrysostom has it. It is called τὸ δόκιμον τῆς πίστεως by Peter in his 1st epistle I. 7. as we call the work of agriculture, agriculture, as we call the work of building, a building: Thus the Apostle calls faith the work of faith. He could have said faith, as the Greek scholia note, he preferred to say the work of faith, to note that he is speaking not of opinion, not of verbal faith, but of true and efficacious faith, as if he were saying, we pray above all that the structure of that living and efficacious faith, which He began in you, He may henceforth perfect and complete in all parts and numbers, as Crocius does here, alleging also Thomas to that effect. Therefore the observation of Cornelius a Lapide is foreign, that faith is only the beginning of salvation to be received through good works. For we do not begin to be saved by faith, but we are fully saved, Eph. II. verse 8, and are guarded unto salvation, 1 Pet. I. v. 5.

Latin:

Vers. 11. Εἰς ὃ) Quapropter מטל הנא Syrus. Προσευχόμεθα πάντοτε περὶ ὑμῶν) Coloss. I. 3. 4. Ἵνα ὑμᾶς ἀξιώσῃ τῆς κλήσεως ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν) Ut DEUS vos vocatione, (ea quæ per Evangelium contingit) dignos red- dat. Ita exponimus ex Eph. IV. 1. יִרֶה. Et ita accepit hic Syrus, utens eodem verbo, quod est Coloss. I. 12.

Vocatio terminum includit regnum Dei & bea- titudinem cœlestem: ideo non opus est per Meto- nymiam adjuncti beatitudinem intelligere cum A- retio & Piscatore. Nam qui vocatione digni sunt, digni sint oportet regno gratiæ, digni regno glo- riæ & beatitudine cœlesti, quia ad regnum DEI vocati sunt. Quæ vero dignitas non aliunde est, quam à merito Christi, à gratia Dei. Precibus er- go impetrandum, ut dignos nos reddat, fidem donando, cum nondum regeniti sumus, aut ean- dem in nobis confirmando ac perficiendo, maxi- me ut in tentationibus ac persecutionibus eadem ne excidamus. Non ut dignetur ipsos vocatione, ut primum ad regnum Dei vocentur, sed efficiat illa vocatione dignos, ne per apostasiam à fide, aut peccata contra conscientiam eadem indigni reddantur. De vocationis actu non inchoando, sed continuato perfectoque intelligit Crocius. Re- ctius Grotius: Ut vocatione dignos reddat. Quod plenius explicat Beat. Hunnius hoc modo: Sicut gaudemus, Deoque grates persolvimus pro lætis ini- tiis & incrementis Evangelicæ vestræ cognitionis & pietatis; Sic vicissim memores humanæ imbecillitatis & insidiarum Satanæ, Deum indefinenter oramus, ut vos cœlesti vocatione ad vitam æternam dignos in Christo habitos, dignos etiam sub examine crucis in- ventos & declaratos, porro etiam potenti sua dextera confirmet, ne hac tam sancta tamque beata vocatio- ne excidatis unquam.

Καὶ πληρώσῃ πᾶσαν εὐδοκίαν ἀγαθωσύνης) Perficiat in vobis omnem bonitatem sibi gratam. Similem significa- tionem vocis πληροῦν habes Rom. VIII. 4. & 1. Corinth. X. 6. Εὐδοκίαν ἀγαθωσύνης, id est ἀγαθωσύνην, ᾗ ἐστιν ἀυτῷ εὐδοκία. Vide Luc. II. 14.

Εὐδοκίαν ἀγαθωσύνης, quæ Dei est, ad Thessa- lonicenses refert Castellio cum Thoma. Sic enim reddit: Perficiat ut bonitatem ac fidei opus & li- bentissime & fortiter persequamini, atque absol- vatis. Grotius de bonitate vel sanctitate perfici- enda intelligit. Sed Apostolus notanter dicit non ἀγαθωσύνην τῆς εὐδοκίας, vel ᾗ ἐστιν ἀυτῷ εὐδοκία, sed πᾶσαν εὐδοκίαν ἀγαθωσύνης. Ideo rectius Chrysostomus de proposito Dei explicat, & scholia Græca, ἵνα πληρώσῃ πᾶσαν ἀυτοῦ τὴν ἀγαθὴν βου- λὴν εἰς ὑμᾶς ὁ Θεός. Βουλὴ δὲ, addit, καὶ εὐδοκία Θεοῦ τὸ πάντας ἀνθρώπους σωθῆναι, καὶ τὸ αἰωνίων τυχεῖν ἀγαθῶν. Quæ laudat ac defendit, (quod contra alios Calvinianos notandum) Crocius: An- tonius Scaymus, inquit, huic refragari dicit, quod in hunc modum Apostolus precaretur, ut impleat pro- positum seu beneplacitum Dei bonitate, quod sit ab- surdum dictu, cum omne beneplacitum DEI sit un- dequaque semper perfectum, ut nulla ad ipsum possit accessio fieri bonitatis. Ideo præfert Thomæ glossam de Thessalonicensium voluntate. Absurdum sane, beneplacitum Dei bonitatis accessione perfici, quod prius imperfectione laborarit, nulla enim in DEI bonitatem cadit imperfectio. At minime absurdum, εὐδοκίαν ἀγαθωσύνης, id est, optimam gratuitamq; benevolentiam, id est executioni mandari plenissi- me. Id enim non arguit imperfectionem, sed DEI libertatem & constantiam. Hoc Apostolum precari sequitur ex interpretatione Græca, prius non sequi- tur precari Apostolum. Consonat B. Hunnii inter- pretatio: Precamur illum supplicibus votis, ut com- pleat in vobis πᾶσαν εὐδοκίαν ἀγαθωσύνης, omne beneplacitum bonitatis, ut quod de vobis ad regnum suum vocandis paterne statuit ab æterno, & jam in tempore clementer cœpit exequi: Posthac etiam mi- sericorditer continuet, & pleno tandem complemen- to feliciter omnibus suis numeris absolvat & perfi- ciat. Quam εὐδοκίαν ut recte opponit Crocius me- ritis, quod non dicat Apostolus, compleat vestra merita, sed εὐδοκίαν, id est gratuitam benevolen- tiam à vestris meritis minime suspensam: Sic cum grano salis accipienda, ne scilicet ingeratur abso- lutum prædestinationis decretum, vel gratia illa absolutissima, cor & palladium Ecclesiæ Refor- matæ, nuncupata in synodo Dordrecena, quæ ad- duntur: Non tamen hic subsistit, sed addit πᾶσαν, quia non solum ipsum salutis æternæ complementum, sed plurima prædestinavit ad illud consequendum necessaria. Illorum omnium completionem precatur Apostolus. Imo quia benevolentiam in CHRISTO exhibitam non satis potest extollere, addit vocem ἀγαθωσύνης, ut singularem atque omnibus modis ab- solutissimam Dei bonitatem declaret, quasi nomina- ret benevolentissimam optimamque Dei voluntatem. Merita nostra per hanc εὐδοκίαν ἀγαθωσύνης di- vinæ excludi agnoscimus, meritum Christi fide ap- prehensum excludi non potest, quia sine illo nulla est εὐδοκία, Matth. III. vers. 17. ut sine fide impossi- bile est DEO placere, Ebr. XI. vers. 6. Ideo non absoluta est illa Dei gratia, sed in merito Christi fundata, quæ obtingit nobis propter Christum vera fide apprehensum. Quæ causa est, quod ad- ditur: Et opus fidei: Quia sine fide compleri in no- bis nequit εὐδοκία ἀγαθωσύνης beneplacitum Dei benignissimum & benevolentissimum, Eph. I. vers. 5. seqq.

Καὶ ἔργον πίστεως) Ἐναλλαγὴ numeri pro ἔργα πίστεως. Sic & 1. Thessal. I. 3. Ea demum opera Deo placent, quæ ex fide nascuntur.

Ἐν δυνάμει) Potenter. Sic Coloss. I. 29.

Exponenda est phrasis Apostoli: Non dicit; ἔργα πίστεως, sed ἔργον πίστεως. De quo ad 1. Thes- sal. I. 3. Non opera complenda vel perficienda, sed fides, quæ ἔργον τοῦ θεοῦ. Nunquam hic complen- tur opera. Sumus enim in statu viatorum, non comprehensorum, ut loquuntur Scholastici. Nec digni reddimur beatitudine cœlesti, qua complen- tur opera, quæ ex fide nascuntur in nobis. Do- num enim Dei est beatitudo: & gratia DEI sal- vamur per fidem, non ex operibus, Eph. II. 8. 9. Rom. VI. 23. Dignos nos reddit solus Christus merito suo, quod per fidem nobis imputatur. Ideo recte B. Hunnius: Meminerat modo totius illius boni, quod obtigit Thessalonicensibus. Nunc ejus totius principalem partem exprimit fidem, quippe quæ sola seu manus apprehendit & possidet omnia bona & dona spiritualia, quæ permanente salva, salva &

inconvulsa manet omnis nostra salutis ratio, labefa- ctata vero & extincta ea protinus amittuntur uni- versa reliqua. Orat igitur speciatim, ut opus fidei compleatur in eis cum potentia, hoc est, ut fides in Jesum Christum potentia & virtute Dei in Thessa- lonicensibus ad finem usque servetur inconcussa. Ca- terum opus illam nominat respectu DEI operantis eam in nobis, quemadmodum & Johannis sexto fides appellatur opus Dei, cum Judæis respondet Dominus: Hoc est opus Dei, ut credatis in eum, quem ille misit. Quo reduci potest explicatio Chrysostomi & Theo- phylacti, patientiam opus esse fidei, quia ὑπομονὴ perseverantia in fide opus illud fidei est, quod Deus pro ἐυδοκία sua in nobis ἐν δυνάμει perficit, 1. Petr. I. 5. ἵνα μὴ ἐκλυώμεθα, ne dissolvamur, vel deficiamus, ut habet Chrysostomus. Vocatur τὸ δόκιμον τῆς πίστεως à Petro 1. epist. I. 7. ut opus agriculturæ agriculturam, ut opus structuræ stru- cturam nominamus: Sic Apostolus fidem opus fi- dei nominat. Poterat dicere fidem, ut annotant Græca scholia, maluit dicere opus fidei, ut notaret, se loqui non de opinione, non de verbali fide, sed de vera & efficaci fide, quasi dicat, imprimis ora- mus, ut vitæ & efficacis illius fidei structuram, quam in vobis cœpit, deinceps omnibus partibus & nume- ris perficiat ac absolvat, ut hic Crocius, allegans in eam sententiam etiam Thomam. Aliena igitur Cornelii à Lapide observatio, quod fides tantum sit inchoatio salutis accipiendæ per bona opera. Fide enim non incipimus servari, sed plene ser- vamur, Eph. II. vers. 8. & custodimur ad salutem, 1. Petr. I. v. 5.

## 1:12
V. 12. Ὅπως ἐνδοξασθῇ τὸ ὄνομα τῦ κυρίε ἡμῶν Ἰησῦ χριστῦ ἐν ὑμῖν) Through you, through your words and deeds: but especially through the sufferings of Christians, John XXI. 19. See Job XII. 28. Gal. I. 24. 1 Pet. IV. 14. We had the verb ἐνδοξάζεσθαι for δοξάζεσθαι also above at 10, and Exod. XIV. 14, XXXIII. 16, 2 Kings XIV. 10, Is. XLV. 25, XLIX. 3, Ezek. XXVIII. 22, Ps. LXXXIX. 8.

It is not only a question of the glorification of the name of the Lord, which takes place in this life, concerning which Theophylact explains, but also of that which will take place in the other life by the elect for eternity. Here they glorify the name of the Lord, that is, his grace, power, and wisdom, both by words, in celebrating, and by deeds, in doing good. They glorify it both immediately and directly themselves, when they preach the name of Jesus, and mediately, indirectly, when they provide examples to others, or excite others to glorify the name of the Lord: They glorify it both as a physical cause, not by procuring glory for God, but by manifesting the same; and morally, while they move others to glorify the name of the Lord, by word, example, and other ways. If these things, he says, with Theophylact as interpreter, which we have said, are performed by you, even in this life, the name of the Lord will attain glory in you. For when men perceive you, because of your charity toward the Lord, bearing temptations with an even mind, how will they not ascribe that to the glory of God. In itself, indeed, and in respect of itself, He can in no way be glorified more or sanctified further. But He is said to be illustrated and sanctified by a certain phrase of Scripture, when that name, which remains holy and illustrious in itself at the supreme height without any increase or diminution, becomes known to us men also, and is recognized and preached as being such (namely, holy and glorious). Therefore the Thessalonians were illustrating the name of Christ when they were both celebrating Him as the incomparable restorer of their salvation, and by their example were giving others also the occasion of doing the same, as here B. Hunnius.

Kaὶ ὑμεῖς ἐν αὐτῷ) For nothing is more glorious than to suffer the worst things for the best cause. In the manuscript: καὶ ὑμεῖς. Theophylact explains it similarly: It redounds to the praise of the servants, when they have kept faith with the Lord. Or otherwise: It will be glory for us, when we are greatly distressed for Christ, and afflicted with many evils. For these things make us more glorious, who, although we are offered to death daily, are nevertheless proven to have overcome death. B. Hunnius refers this to future glory: Since it is certain that the Thessalonians are renewed by the benefit of Christ to a glory not only pristine, which had shone in our first parents before the fall, but also that they attain a far greater one in the other age. For it is CHRIST who calls his elect, justifies them, and finally glorifies them. However, the glory of the faithful can be well joined in this and the future age. For although pious martyrs become illustrious here, and obtain an immortal name, they are nevertheless held by their enemies as damned. But one day their glory in Christ will be manifest to all, as Crocius rightly says here. He adds, they will consequently attain glory in him. He said, however, 'in it,' because the glory of Christ as the head will redound upon them. But that ἐν αὐτῷ concerning Christ is not to be understood only as the head of glory. For he himself will be our glory by irradiating us with the light, splendor, and Majesty of his glory, through which we shall shine gloriously forever.

According to the grace of GOD as the internal impulsive cause, which they call προηγουμένην, because this is a merely gratuitous benefit, according to the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, as the external meritorious cause, so that we may understand that that whole excellent work of faith and perseverance is to be attributed not to our own powers, but to divine grace exhibited to us through and on account of the merit of Christ. Or, he says, interpreting Theophylact, it should be ascribed to GOD himself, not to us. And it is done by his grace, when he himself attains glory in us: for we prefer nothing to him, since he is the sweetest of all. And let us claim praise in him, from whom we receive the power to endure all things.

Latin:

V. 12. Ὅπως ἐνδοξασθῇ τὸ ὄνομα τῦ κυρίε ἡμῶν Ἰησῦ χριστῦ ἐν ὑμῖν) Per vos, per vestra dicta & facta: maxime vero per Christianorum perpessiones, Johan. XXI. 19. Vid. Job. XII. 28. Gal. I. 24. 1. Petr. IV. 14. Verbum ἐνδοξάζεσθαι pro δοξάζεσθαι habuimus & supra 10. & Exod. XIV. 14. XXXIII. 16. 2. Reg. XIV. 10. Es. XLV. 25. XLIX. 3. Ezech. XXVIII. 22. Psal. LXXXIX. 8.

Non tantum de glorificatione nominis Domini, quæ in hac vita fit, de qua Theophylactus explicat, sed etiam quæ in altera vita ab electis in æternum fiet, agitur. Hic glorificant nomen Domini, id est, gratiam, potentiam, & sapientiam ejus, cum verbis, celebrando, tum factis, bene operando. Glorificant tum ἀμέσως & directe ipsi, cum præ- dicant nomen Jesu, tum ἐμμέσως, indirecte, cum aliis exemplis præbent, vel alios ad nomen Do- mini glorificandum excitant: Glorificant tum ut causa physica, non gloriam Deo conciliando, sed eandem manifestando; tum moraliter, dum alios movent ad nomen Domini glorificandum, verbo, exemplo, aliisque modis. Si hæc, inquit, Theophy- lacto interprete, quæ diximus, per vos peragentur, vel in hac vita, Domini nomen in vobis gloriam as- sequetur. Cum enim vos perspexerint homines pro vestra in Dominum charitate, tentationes æquo ani- mo ferre, quo pacto non Deo id sunt ad gloriam ad- scripturi. Per se quidem suique respectu glorificari magis aut sanctificari ulterius neutiquam potest. Tum autem illustrari sanctificarique phrasi quadam Scripturæ dicitur, quando nomen illud per se in su- premo fastigio sine omni vel incremento vel immi- nutione sanctum & illustre permanens jam nobis quoque hominibus innotescit, & tale esse (nempe san- ctum & gloriosum) agnoscitur & prædicatur. Pro- inde illustrabant Thessalonicenses Christi nomen cum & pro salutis suæ incomparabili reparatore illum cele- brabant ipsi, & exemplo suo aliis quoque occasionem dabant idipsum faciendi, ut hic B. Hunnius.

Kaὶ ὑμεῖς ἐν αὐτῷ) Nihil enim gloriosius, quam optima de causa pati pessima. In manuscripto: καὶ ὑμεῖς. Similiter id explicat Theophylactus: Cedit id servis ad laudem, cum Domino fidem servarint. Vel aliter: Gloria futurum est nobis, cum pro Christo maxime angimur, & malis plurimis affligimur. Hæc namque nos faciunt clariores, qui cum quoti- die morti offerimur, mortem tamen superasse ar- guimur. B. Hunnius id refert ad futuram glo- riam: Quandoquidem constat, Thessalonicenses Christi beneficio renovari ad gloriam non modo pri- stinam, quæ in primis parentibus ante lapsum ful- serat, sed etiam consequi longe majorem in seculo altero. CHRISTUS enim est, qui electos suos vo- cat, justificat, tandemque glorificat. Bene autem conjungi gloria fidelium in hoc & futuro seculo potest. Etsi enim hic pii martyres fiunt illustres, & immortale nomen consequuntur, habentur ta- men ab hostibus pro damnatis. At olim patebit omnibus illorum gloria in Christo, ut recte hic Cro- cius. Addit, in se consequentur gloriam. Di- xit tamen in ea, quia Christi ut capitis gloria in eos redundabit. Verum illud ἐν αὐτῷ de Christo non tantum ut capite intelligendum gloriæ. Erit enim ipse nostra gloria nos irradiando gloriæ suæ lu- mine, splendore ac Majestate, per quam gloriosi fulgebimus in æternum.

Κατὰ τὴν χάριν τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡμῶν καὶ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ χριστοῦ) Secundum DEI gratiam ceu causam impulsi- vam internam, quam προηγουμένην vocant, quia mere gratuitum hoc est beneficium, secundum gratiam Domini Jesu Christi, ceu causam meri- toriam externam, ut intelligamus, universum illud præclarum opus fidei & perseverantiæ non no- stris viribus, sed divinæ gratiæ per & propter me- ritum Christi nobis exhibitæ acceptum ferendum esse. Vel ipsum DEO, inquit, Theophylacto inter- prete, non nobis debet adscribi. Et illius gratia fit, cum ipse vel gloriam in nobis assequitur: quippe qui ei nihil anteponimus, cum omnium sit ille dulcissi- mus. Et nos in illo laudem vendicemus, à quo vir- tutem ad omnia toleranda accipimus.

## 2:1 Argument
PART II. DIDACTIC-PARÆNETIC EPISTLE. CHAPTER II.

ARGUMENT, AND PARTITION.

He informs them about the most recent coming of Christ, which some wished to be persuaded was near, and teaches that the Lord will not come unless first the Anti-Christ, whose malice already creeps secretly, the obstacle being removed, breaks forth, and is manifested, and is killed by the Spirit of the mouth of the Lord, whom finally Christ will cut off at his coming, having first seduced many with various lying signs, who do not receive the truth; he therefore warns them to give thanks to God, because they have been chosen in faith for salvation, called through the Gospel, and persist in the doctrine delivered, praying that they may be confirmed by God.

There are two parts: I. Didactic concerning the coming of Christ & the Anti-Christ to v. 12. II. Parænetic concerning thanksgiving and perseverance in the recognized truth to v. 17.

PART I. OF CHAPTER II. Didactic, concerning the coming of Christ & the Anti-Christ.

Vers. 1. Ἐρωτῶμεν δὲ ὑμᾶς ἀδελφοὶ) Regarding the word ἐρωτῶμεν see what has been said, 1 Thess. IV. 1. V. 12.

὘πὲρ τῆς παρουσίας τῦ Κυρίυ ἡμῶν Ἰησῦ χρισῦ) ὑπὲρ here is placed for περὶ, as Rom. IV. 10. 2 Cor. VIII. 23. 24. & 1 Thessal. III. 2. in the manuscript; the παρουσία of Christ can, as we have said elsewhere, be understood concerning the judgment of Christ upon the Jews, according to a sufficiently common manner of speaking in scripture. But since the Apostle Paul believed that the universal destruction would follow not long after the destruction of the Jewish state, there is no harm if we take παρουσία here for both judgments of Christ, both upon the Jews and upon the human race.

Καὶ ἡμῶν ἐπισυναγωγῆς ἐπ’ αὐτὸν) that is, πρὸς αὐτὸν, as above I. 10. Luke X. 9. This ἐπισυναγωγὴ will be joined to that coming. The angels will lead us gathered to Christ, which is ἐπισυνάξουσι, Matt. XXV. 31. Mark XIII. 27. The word ἐπισυναγωγῆς also appears in 2 Maccab. II. 7.

To these we subjoin what Grotius had handed down in his commentary on the second epistle to the Thessalonians, chapter II.

Verse 1. Ἐρωτῶμεν δὲ ὑμᾶς ἀδελφοὶ) We beseech you, brethren. Many things from the common Latin speech crept into the Greek language after the Romans held Judea and the neighboring lands. Such is ἐρωτῶ for I pray, because the Latins say rogo; see Matt. 15:23, John 13:16, Acts 23:20.

὘πὲρ τῆς παρουσίας τῦ Κυρίυ ἡμῶν Ἰησῦ χρισῦ. Concerning the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ) The coming of God, as rightly noted by Maimonides, in the Old Testament signifies either the benefits of God or His judgments. Moreover, things that are attributed to God in the Old Testament are accustomed to be attributed to the Messiah in the New, as appears in many places; and indeed the holy writers love to use almost the same words concerning the universal judgment and the judgment upon the Jewish people, because the latter is an image and pledge of the former. Thus, some rightly, I think, explain ἐσχάτην ὥραν in John as the time that not long preceded the destruction of the Jewish nation, and the judgment upon the Jewish nation is no less accustomed to be attributed to Christ than to God, just as that which is to follow is universal. See Matt. 21:44, John 5:22. But this judgment upon the Jews is most openly ascribed to Christ in Luke 19:12, 14, 27, where it is noted by the word ἐπανελθεῖν, that he might return, which is noted here by the word παρουσίας, coming. Christ had predicted the destruction of the city and the temple. The Christians were expecting it, not only as a proof of a truthful Master, but also as a comfort for the many calamities they had suffered from the Jews. It was of great importance to the Church that, if they had presumed in their mind and expectation that it was too near, they might not eventually begin to doubt the authority of the whole Gospel. Therefore, to meet this evil, and by a new prediction of those things which God Himself had revealed, to show that he speaks with God as the author, he says that two notable things would precede that judgment of Christ, of which one was to be an evil common to Jews and Christians; the other a temptation peculiar to Christians; so that this is a certain explanation of those words of Christ: Ἀλλ’ οὔπω ἐσὶ τὸ τέλος, but the end is not yet, and πάντα δὲ ταῦτα ἀρχὴ ὠδίνων, but all these things are the beginning of sorrows.

Καὶ ἡμῶν ἐπισυναγωγῆς ἐπ’ αὐτόν. And our gathering together unto him) That judgment upon the Jews had to precede that time when the elect of Christ would be gathered from everywhere, when the angels ἐπισυνάξουσι τὺς ἐκλεκτὺς αὐτῦ, shall gather together his elect, Matt. 24:31, Mark 15:27. But how great an interval of time there would be between the destruction of the city and the Jewish nation and the resurrection of the dead, God, since He did not wish it to be known, had not revealed it to the Christians through the Apostles, nor to the Apostles themselves. And so the Apostles always speak of the time of the resurrection indefinitely, without any indication of time; see 1 Thess. 4:5. If, however, anyone wishes to interpret ἐπισυναγωγὴν, gathering together, here as the assembly of Christians, just as in Heb. 10:25 and 2 Macc. 2:8, so that ἐπ’ αὐτὸν, unto him, may be for his sake, in the way that ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς, upon you, is taken in James 2:7. He will be able to refer these words to that free opportunity of assembling, not only in individual cities but also from many places of the earth, which, once the Jewish nation was destroyed—which had everywhere slandered the Christians as a third race and a new sect—happened to the Christians in the times of Vespasian and Titus. Tertullian in his Apology: What then are the laws which the impious, unjust, base, cruel, vain, and mad alone execute against us, which Trajan partly frustrated by forbidding Christians to be sought out, which no Hadrian, although an explorer of all curiosities, no Vespasian, although a conqueror of the Jews, no Pius, no Verus has impressed. Eusebius, History, book 3, 17: Τῦ Οὐεσπασιανῦ μηδὲν καθ’ ἡμῶν ἄτοπον ἐπινοήσαντος, when Vespasian had devised nothing harsh against us. This is συνέρχεσθαι, συνάγειν, to come together, to gather, in the edict of Norbanus, and often in Philo, or what amounts to the same thing, συνέ-

δες ποιεῖν, or συγκροτεῖν, which was often forbidden to Christians by edicts, but granted by Constantine to the Emperors and Presidents of old. See Eusebius. That also may be added, that when the temple and the Jewish republic were destroyed, Christians professed Christ more freely without the imitation of Jewish rites.

That by παρουσίαν τοῦ κυρίου the judgment of Christ upon the Jews is understood, as also the universal judgment of the whole world, can neither be taught by any parallel, nor is it evident from the present treatment of the Apostle. Such ambiguity is utterly foreign to the words of the Holy Spirit, that the same term should signify such diverse things at once. The signification of a judgment upon the Jews is foreign to the description of τῆς παρουσίας κυρίου, which is treated here: since that is joined with ἐπισυναγωγῇ, the gathering unto the Lord, which is to be on the last day. Nor does παρουσία τοῦ κυρίου, when placed absolutely, ever denote the coming of the Lord to a particular judgment. The passage Matth. XXIV. verse 3. speaks not of a judicial coming, but of a mystical coming through the proclamation of the Gospel, according to Grotius himself, if not according to the erroneous mind of the inquiring disciples, certainly according to the mind of Christ who is answering, which is by no means ambiguous: Conf. verse 3. & 27. Luc. XIX. vers. 12. 14. 23. in the parable concerning the departure and return of a nobleman, it is treated, but the judgment or coming to judgment against the Jews is not denoted by the name of παρουσίας τοῦ κυρίου. I add from the blessed Hülsemann, what he has concerning this passage in Brev. extens. page 473. Although the prophecies of CHRIST concerning the day of judgment, whether the particular one of the Jews or the universal one of the whole world, have nothing to do with the determination of the time of the coming of the Anti-Christ circumscribed by the Apostle: yet it is most false that that sudden coming of the day, of which Luke chap. XIX. verse 15. in which rewards and punishments will be distributed to faithful and unfaithful servants, verse 21. that long time from which the King is to return to demand an account from his servants, Matth. XXV. verse 19. signifies the time of the city being destroyed by Titus: for none of the circumstances now recited fits this time. And what is more certain from a comparison of the preceding epistle, and the antecedents and consequents in this epistle, than that by παρουσίαν τοῦ κυρίου no other coming of Christ can be understood than the last? See 1. epistle chap. III. verse 1. 3. chap. IV. verse 14. 15. 18. c. V. 1. 2. 23. 2. epist. I. verse 3. 6. 7. 10. The passage Acts II. verse 10. does not treat of the day of judgment against the Jews, but of the first coming of Christ. Which Lyranus, Isidorus, Vatablus, and Cornelius à Lapide explain concerning the last day; Grotius explained the parallel passage Joel II. concerning the judgment against the Jews by Nebuchadnezzar. See his annotations and ours on the Prophetic passage. Furthermore, if the words of CHRIST in Matth. XXIV. verse 6. 8. are explained here in our passage, these must have been written by the force of Grotius's annotators on that passage, after Gaius had already prepared for his image to be brought into the temple. How therefore would that be predicted here at last? That the Apostle was also of the opinion that the end of the world would follow not long after the destruction of the Jews is a most vain persuasion of Grotius, not consistent with the promise of CHRIST concerning the Apostles being led into all truth by the Holy Spirit, nor with the divine inspiration of the divine word, but this information of the Apostle also refutes it, as by it he expressly overthrows the opinion of those who believed that the coming of CHRIST was already imminent. Concerning which Theophylact: He explains nothing about the time when the resurrection will be. He teaches, however, that it is by no means imminent at present. For there were some deceivers who plainly asserted that the end of all things was already imminent, and that the coming of CHRIST was at hand. The divine Apostle therefore commands, as Theodoret taught long before, not to believe those who say that the time of the consummation is imminent, and that the Lord is about to appear immediately. Moreover, Grotius rightly acknowledges that the particle ὑπὲρ is taken objectively, just as the blessed Luther also rendered it, der Zukunfft halber: How much less conveniently the Old Interpreter and the Reformed explain it by, so that it may be an adjuration: By the coming of Christ. The Apostle had no need of such an adjuration among the Thessalonians in this Didactic chapter: such as he was accustomed to use rather in difficult admonitions concerning those things for which an account will have to be rendered on the day of the coming of the Lord, 2. Timoth. IV. verse 1. The Apostolic authority was already finding faith in these, because they received His Word, not as the word of man, but as the Word of God, 2. Thessal. II.

But that Grotius in his commentary on this passage understands by ἐπισυναγωγὴν the free faculty of assembling, which the Church, through the coming of Christ for the destruction of Jerusalem in the time of Titus and Vespasian, was to have at last, being gathered by the Angels, so that it might be united to CHRIST: The man now seems to have been ashamed of that fiction, because he now mentions nothing about the coming for the destruction of Jerusalem, as far as this ἐπισυναγωγὴν is concerned, but only teaches that it will be in the last coming. And how can such diverse meanings be affixed to the same word in the same passage, so that it might indicate both the free faculty of assembling that the Church was to have on this earth around the time of the Jerusalem destruction, and denote that the elect were to be gathered to CHRIST not on earth, but in heaven towards the end of the world. That this discourse is indeed about this congregation is clear and confessed, as much from chapter IV of the preceding epistle as from the collation of passages which Grotius himself wishes to be collated here. Theodoret, Chrysostom, Theophylact, Oecumenius, and other interpreters, both ancient and modern, have also explained this, if you except Bullinger, who interprets it concerning the mystical union of the saints with Christ, whose opinion Crocius himself rejected. To say nothing of the fact that ἐπισυναγωγὴ indeed in Heb. X, verse 25, signifies the congregation of a particular Church, but nowhere denotes the free faculty of assembling. Johannes Crocius observes that the Apostle preferred to say ἐπισυναγωγὴν rather than συναγωγὴν, because there are already many with Christ in glory, to whom we shall approach in reality, just as we have approached, Heb. XII, verses 12, 13; and therefore he deservedly rejects the disjunctive of Haymo, that the multitude of the Elect is to be understood, either that which will come with Christ, or that which will meet Him for judgment; since both are to be understood. For the bodies of the blessed, who will come with Christ from heaven, will also be gathered to Him, having been raised from the dust of the earth.

Latin:

PARS II. EPISTOLÆ DIDACTICO - PARÆNETICA. CAPUT II.

ARGUMENTUM, ET PARTITIO.

Informat de adventu Christi novissimo, quem prope esse nonnulli persuasum cupiebant, docetque non venturum Dominum, nisi prius Anti-Christus, cujus jam malitia ser- pat occulte, remoto obstaculo, prorumpat, ac manifestetur, & interficiatur Spiritu oris Domini, quem denique exscindet Christus sub adventum suum, seducturum prius va- riis mendacibus signis plurimos, qui veri- tatem non recipiunt; monet itaque gratias Deo agant, quod electi sint in fide ad salu- tem, vocati per Evangelium ac persistant in doctrina tradita, vovens, ut à Deo con- firmentur.

PArtes duæ sunt: I. Didactica de adventu Chri- sti & Anti-Christi ad v. 12. II. Parænetica ad gratiarum actionem & perseverantiam in veritate agnita ad v. 17.

PARS I. CAPITIS II. Didactica, de adventu Christi & Anti- Christi.

Vers. 1. Ἐρωτῶμεν δὲ ὑμᾶς ἀδελφοὶ) De voce ἐρωτῶμεν vide quæ dicta, 1. Thess. IV. 1. V. 12.

὘πὲρ τῆς παρουσίας τῦ Κυρίυ ἡμῶν Ἰησῦ χρισῦ) ὑπὲρ hic est positum pro περὶ, ut Rom. IV. 10. 2. Cor. VIII. 23. 24. & 1. Thessal. III. 2. in manuscripto; παρουσία Christi potest, ut alibi diximus de judicio Christi in Judaeos intelligi, se- cundum loquutionem scripturae satis usitatam. Sed cum Apostolus Paulus crediderit, non multo post excidium Ju- daici status secuturum excidium universale, nihil mali est, si παρουσίαν hic accipiamus pro utroque Christi judicio, tum in Judaeos, tum in humanum genus.

Καὶ ἡμῶν ἐπισυναγωγῆς ἐπ’ αὐτὸν) id est, πρὸς αὐτὸν, ut supra I. 10. Luc. X. 9. Haec ἐπισυναγωγὴ conjuncta erit isti adventui. Angeli nos ad Christum congregatos adducent, quod est ἐπισυνάξουσι, Matth. XXV. 31. Marc. XIII. 27. Vox ἐπισυναγωγῆς extat & 2. Maccab. II. 7.

His subjicimus, quae tradiderat Grotius in com- mentatione ad II. epist. ad Thessal. cap. II.

Vers. 1. Ἐρωτῶμεν δὲ ὑμᾶς ἀδελφοὶ) Rogamus autem vos fratres. Multa in Graecum sermonem vulgi externa irrepsere ex Latino sermone, postquam Judaeam & vici- nas terras tenuere Romani. Tale est ἐρωτῶ pro precor, quia Latini rogo dicunt, vide Matth. XV. 23. Joh. XIII. 16. Act. XXIII. 20.

὘πὲρ τῆς παρουσίας τῦ Κυρίυ ἡμῶν Ἰησῦ χρισῦ. De ad- ventu Domini nostri Jesu Christi) Dei adventus, ut recte notatum Maimonidae, in veteri foedere, aut beneficia Dei aut ejus judicia significat. Solent autem, quae in ve- teri foedere Deo tribuuntur, in novo tribui Messiae, ut multis locis apparet, tum vero amant sancti scriptores easdem ferme voces usurpare de judicio universali, & de judicio in populum Judaicum, quod hoc sit illius imago atque arrhabo. Sic ἐσχάτην ὥραν ad Johannem re- cte, ut puto, quidam exponunt de tempore, quod exci- dium Judaicae gentis non longe antecessit, neque minus judicium in gentem Judaicam, quam quod sequuturum est universale, tam Christo quam Deo tribui solet. Vide Matth. XXI. 44. Joh. V 22. Apertissime autem hoc in Ju- daos judicium Christo adscribitur, Luc. XIX. 12. 14. 27. ubi voce ἐπανελθεῖν, ut rediret, notatur, quod hic voce παρουσίας adventus. Praedixerat Christus urbis templique excidium. Expectabant id Christiani, non tantum ut do- cumentum veracis Magistri, sed & ut calamitatum, quas ab Judaeis multas pertulerant, solatium. Multum inter- erat Ecclesiae, ne si id tanquam nimis propinquum prae- sumpsissent animo & expectatione, tandem inciperent de totius Evangelii autoritate dubitare. Ideo ut huic oc- currat malo, & nova praedictione eorum, quae Deus ipse aperuerat, ostendat Deo autore se loqui, duas dicit res in- signes illud Christi judicium antecessuras, quarum alte- ra malum erat futurum Judaeis & Christianis commune; altera tentatio propria Christianorum; ita ut hic expli- catio quaedam sit illorum Christi verborum: Ἀλλ’ οὔπω ἐσὶ τὸ τέλος, sed nondum est finis, & πάντα δὲ ταῦτα ἀρ- χὴ ὠδίνων, haec autem omnia initia dolorum sunt.

Καὶ ἡμῶν ἐπισυναγωγῆς ἐπ’ αὐτόν. Et nostrae congrega- tione in ipsum) Debebat judicium illud in Judaeos praece- dere tempus illud, cum electi Christi undique colligen- tur, cum Angeli ἐπισυνάξουσι τὺς ἐκλεκτὺς αὐτῦ, congrega- bunt electos ejus, Matth. XXIV. 31. Marc. XV. 27. Quan- tum vero intervallum futurum esset temporis inter exci- dium urbis gentisque Judaicae, & resurrectionem mor- tuorum, id Deus, cum innotescere nollet, neque Christia- nis per Apostolos, neque ipsis Apostolis aperuerat. Itaque de tempore resurrectionis loquuntur Apostoli semper indefinite nulla temporis indicatione, vide 1. ad Thessal. IV. 5. Si quis tamen ἐπισυναγωγὴν congregationem hic velit interpretari conventum Christianorum, sicut Ebr. X. 25. & 2. Macc. II. 8. ut ἐπ’ αὐτὸν in ipsum, sit propter ipsum, quomodo ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς super vos sumitur Jac. II. 7. Poterit haec verba referre ad liberam illam conveniendi non tantum in singulis urbibus, sed & ex multis terra- rum locis facultatem, quae excisa Judaeorum gente, quae Christianos, ut tertium genus & novam sectam ubique erat calumniata, Christianis contigit Vespasia- ni Titique temporibus. Tertullianus Apologetico: Quae- les ergo leges, quas adversum nos soli exequuntur impii, injusti, turpes, truces, vani, dementes, quas Trajanus ex parte frustratus est, vetando inquiri Christianos, quas nullus Adrianus, quanquam curiositatum omnium ex- plorator, nullus Vespasianus, quanquam Judaeorum de- bellator, nullus Pius, nullus Verus impressit. Eusebius Historiae libr. III. 17. Τῦ Οὐεσπασιανῦ μηδὲν καθ’ ἡμῶν ἄτοπον ἐπινοήσαντος, cum Vespasianus nihil in nos durum, molitus esset. Hoc est συνέρχεσθαι, συν- άγειν convenire, congregare, in edicto Norbani, & apud Philonem saepe, aut quod idem valet συνέ-

δες ποιεῖν, aut συγκροτεῖν, quod sæpe Christianis ve- titum edictis, veterum Imperatorum & Præsidum con- cessum à Constantino. Vide Eusebium. Addi & illud potest, quod exciso templo ac republica Judaica, Chri- stiani Christum liberius sine Judaicorum rituum imita- tione professi sunt.

Per παρουσίαν τοῦ κυρίου judicium Christi in Ju- dæos intelligi, ut & judicium universale totius mundi, nec ullo parallelo doceri potest, nec ex præsenti Apostoli tractatione constat. Aliena prorsus est ejusmodi ambiguitas à λέξεσι Spiritus sancti, quod eadem voce simul tam diversa signi- ficentur. Aliena est significatio judicii in Judæos à descriptione τῆς παρουσίας κυρίου, de qua hic agi- tur: Siquidem illa conjuncta sit cum ἐπισυναγωγῇ, congregatione ad Dominum, quæ in novissimo die futura est. Neque uspiam παρουσία τοῦ κυρίου, absolute posita adventum Domini ad judicium particulare notat. Locus Matth. XXIV. vers. 3. non de judiciali, sed de mystico per præconium Evangelii adventu secundum ipsummet Grotium loquitur, si non quoad mentem quærentium disci- pulorum erroneam, certe quoad mentem respon- dentis Christi minime ambiguam: Conf. vers. 3. & 27. Luc. XIX. vers. 12. 14. 23. in parabola de profectione & reditu nobilis agitur, non vero judicium vel adventus ad judicium adversus Ju- dæos nomine παρουσίας τοῦ κυρίου notatur. Addo è B. Hülsemanno, quæ de hoc loco habet in Brev. extens. pag. 473. Quanquam & CHRISTI vaticinia de die judicii sive particularis Judæorum, sive universalis totius orbis, determinationem tem- poris venturi Anti-Christi ab Apostolo circumscri- ptam nihil attineant: Falsissimum est tamen, illam subitaneam superventionem diei, de qua Lucas cap. XIX. vers. 15. in qua præmia & pænæ servis fidelibus & infidelibus distribuentur, vers. 21. illud longum tempus à quo rediturus est Rex ad rationem exigendam à servis suis, Matth. XXV. vers. 19. significare tempus destruendæ urbis per Titum: nul- la enim circumstantiarum jam recitatarum huic tempori quadrat. Et quid certius è collatione præcedentis epistolæ, & antecedentium ac con- sequentium in hac epistola, quam quod per pa- ρουσίαν τοῦ κυρίου nullus alius adventus Christi pos- sit intelligi, quam novissimus? Vide 1. epistolæ cap. III. vers. 1. 3. cap. IV. vers. 14. 15. 18. c. V. 1. 2. 23. 2. epist. I. vers. 3. 6. 7. 10. Locus Actor. II. vers. 10. non de die judicii adversus Judæos, sed de adven- tu primo Christi agit. Quem Lyranus, Isidorus, Vatablus, Cornelius à Lapide de die novissimo ex- plicant; Grotius locum parallelum Joel. II. de ju- dicio adversus Judæos per Nebucadnezarem expo- suit. Vid. annotata ejus & nostra ad locum Prophe- ticum. Porro si hic explicantur in loco nostro verba CHRISTI Matth. XXIV. vers. 6. 8. oportet hæc vi annotatorum Grotii ad istum lo- cum scripta esse, postquam Cajus jam parasset ima- ginem suam templo inferri. Quomodo ergo hic illud institutum prædiceretur demum? Aposto- lum etiam in ea opinione fuisse, non multo post excidium Judæorum sequuturum finem mundi, vanissima est Grotii persuasio, non conveniens promissioni CHRISTI de Apostolis à Spiritu sancto in omnem veritatem ducendis, nec ver- bi divini θεοπνευσίᾳ, sed & refragatur hæc in- formatio Apostoli, utpote qua illorum opinio- nem, qui adventum CHRISTI jam immi- nere credebant, ex instituto profligat. Quo de Theophylactus: Quo tempore futura sit resurre- ctio, nihil explicat. Edocet tamen nequaquam, hanc in præsenti instare. Erant enim deceptores non- nulli, qui plane assererent, instare jam rerum rura omnium finem, adesseque CHRISTI adventum. Præcipit ergo, quod pridem ante Theodoretes do- cuit, divinus Apostolus, non credere iis, qui di- cunt instare tempus consummationis, & Domi- num statim esse appariturum. Cæterum recte par- ticulam ὑπὲρ objective accipi, agnoscit Grotius, quemadmodum etiam B. Lutherus reddidit, der Zukunfft halber: Quam minus commode Vetus Interpres & Reformati exponunt per, ut obtesta- tio sit: Per adventum Christi. Tanta obtestatio- ne non opus habebat Apostolus, penes Thes- salonicenses, in hoc capite Didactico: qualem po- tius in arduis ad ea commonitionibus solitus est ad- hibere, de quibus in die adventus Domini red- denda erit ratio, 2. Timoth. IV. vers. 1. Fidem jam in hisce inveniebat Apostolica autoritas, quia sus- cipiebant Verbum ejus, non ut Verbum hominis, sed ut Dei Verbum, 2. Thessal. II.

Quod vero per ἐπισυναγωγὴν Grotius liberam conveniendi facultatem in sua commentatione ad hunc locum intelligit, quam Ecclesia per Chri- sti adventum ad excidium Hierosolymæ Titi & Vespasiani tempore sit habitura tandem ab Angelis colligenda, ut CHRISTO uniatur: Ejus commenti nunc videtur virum puduisse, quia jam nihil de adventu ad excidium Hieroso- lymæ, quantum ad hanc ἐπισυναγωγὴν, meminit, sed tantum eandem in novissimo adventu fore do- cet. Et quomodo tam diversa significata eidem voci affingi poterunt in eodem loco, ut & libe- ram conveniendi facultatem Ecclesiam in his ter- ris circa tempus excidii Hierosolymitani habitu- ram indicet, & electos non in terris, sed in cœlo ad CHRISTUM sub finem mundi congregatum iri notet. De hac vero congregatione sermonem hic esse, tam e præcedentis epistolæ capite IV. quam e collatione locorum, quæ hic ipse Grotius conferri vult, luculentum & in confesso est. Qua de etiam exposuere Theodoretus, Chrysostomus, Theophylactus, Oecumenius & alii communiter cum veteres tum recentiores Interpretes, si Bul- lingerum excipias, de unione sanctorum cum Christo mystica interpretantem, cujus senten- tiam Crocius ipse rejecit. Ut taceam, quod ἐπισυν- αγωγὴ quidem Ebr. X. vers. 25. congregationem Ecclesiæ particularis significet, nuspiam autem fa- cultatem conveniendi liberam denotet. Johannes Crocius observat, quod Apostolus maluerit ἐπι- συναγωγὴν dicere, quam συναγωγὴν, quia jam mul- ti sunt cum Christo in gloria, quibus nos accede- mus reipsa, sicut ipe accessimus, Ebr. XII. vers. 12. 13. ideoque disjunctivam Haymonis merito repro- bat, intelligi multitudinem Electorum, vel quæ cum Christo veniet, vel quæ ei obviabit ad judi- cium; siquidem utraque intelligatur. Nam & bea- torum, qui cum Christo e cœlo venient, corpora colligentur ad ipsum e terræ pulvere suscitata.

## 2:2
Vers. 2. Εἰς τὸ μὴ ταχέως σαλευθῆναι ὑμᾶς ἀπὸ τοῦ νοὸς) That you may not easily be moved from that opinion, namely, which you imbibed while I was teaching, that some great things must precede before GOD exercises His vengeance upon the Jews, and then also upon the human race. I explain νοῦς here as opinion, as in Rom. XIV. 5, 1 Cor. I. 10. So also Job VII. 19, XXXIII. 16, and elsewhere. Σαλεύειν is עֶרֶץ. See Acts XVII. 13.

Concerning him thus in the commentary:

Vers. 2. Εἰς τὸ μὴ ταχέως σαλευθῆναι ὑμᾶς ἀπὸ τοῦ νοὸς) that you may not quickly be moved from the sense. I understand νοῦς here as that opinion which they had already received from the Apostles, that the destruction of the nation was not as near as was thought. Thus the word νοῦς is taken in Rom. XIV. 5, 1 Cor. I. 10.

But how had the Thessalonians imbibed that opinion while the Apostle was teaching, if neither Paul Did he inform them in person at Thessalonica, and did he not write an epistle to them, which Grotius denies both? By the word ταχέως he indicates that they were scarcely taught by Paul and his fellow-workers in the truer opinion, and therefore it would be a sign of inconstancy and levity if they allowed themselves to be quickly moved. The word σαλεύεσθαι is a metaphor from a ship which is tossed here and there by the waves, with its anchor cast off, not without danger.

Μήτε θροεῖσθαι) So also Matt. XXIV. v. 6, Mark XIII. 7. This is added for this reason, because if anything unforeseen arrives, it terrifies more.

Μήτε διὰ πνεύματος) Every prophecy is called πνεῦμα, whether it truly be from GOD, or be said to be such, 1 Cor. XII. 22, 1 John IV. 1, 2, 3. But no prophecy was to be received which was contrary to the sayings of either Christ or the Apostles, whom Christ had willed to be heard in his stead.

Μήτε διὰ λόγε) By rumors about us, as if we were now saying something other than what we said before. For it must be understood here, ὡς δι’ ἡμῶν, from the following member.

Μήτε δι ἐπιστολῆς ὡς δι’ ἡμῶν) For many were fabricating epistles under the name of the Apostles. Whence that caution of the Apostle below III. 17.

In the commentary he has it thus:

Μήτε θροεῖσθαι) nor be terrified. Those to whom unexpected dangers suddenly rush in are accustomed to be more gravely terrified.

Μήτε διὰ πνεύματος,) nor by the Spirit. If anyone, calling himself a Prophet, should prophesy contrary to what we have said. For because some were falsely assuming to themselves the name of Prophets, therefore Christians are commanded to examine such things as are brought to them in the name of prophecies, 1 Corinth. XII. v. 10, 1 Thess. V. v. 21, 1 John IV. v. 1. But the best examination was the comparison of those sayings with the sayings of Christ himself or the Apostles, whom the Spirit led into all truth, to whose authority Christ himself had willed all Christians to look.

Μήτε διὰ λόγε) nor by word. It is a zeugma. For it must be understood ὡς δι ἡμῶν, as if by us, nor by rumors brought, as if we were now teaching other things about this matter than we taught before. For many, teaching false things, were prefixing the authority of the Apostles to their own sayings. Thus some were abusing the name of Peter against Paul, and the Gnostics were prefixing the sayings of Matthias and others to their own inventions.

Μήτε δι’ ἐπιστολῆς ὡς δι’ ἡμῶν,) Nor by an epistle as if sent by us. Forgers were also putting forward epistles in the name of the Apostles, which is the reason why Paul so solicitously fortified his epistles with his own hand and other marks, so that they might be distinguished from the false ones, below III. verse 17.
