And that he revealed the impiety of that Simon under Claudius, the most ancient of the Christians whom we have clearly note: Justin in his second apology and Irenaeus in book I, chapter XX, and no otherwise in history Eusebius, in his Catechesis Cyril, and in his heretical fables Theodoret. But that Philastrius and certain later ones refer these things to the times of Nero, I think is an error arisen from the ambiguity of the name. For Claudius also was of the family of the Neros, and his father had the name Nero, as Suetonius teaches us; whence also the same name was given by him to the son whom he had adopted, the Nero most notorious for his crimes.

Shall be revealed.) Shall be revealed. The same word which we had above concerning Gaius. Simon will uncover his impiety, which he had hitherto hidden by associating himself with the Christians. See Acts VIII. 24. Clement of Alexandria concerning him: 'He obeyed Peter as he was preaching.' Philastrius concerning the same: 'Who, having been baptized by the blessed Apostle, departed from their faith.'

The wicked one.) That iniquitous one. Thus the Greek interpreters of the New Testament translate the word עשׂה, as can be seen in Isaiah LIII, verse 12, Mark XV. 28, Luke XXII. 27. Thus, however, those who are deliberately evil are called by the Hebrews. It fits Simon perfectly, whom Clement of Rome called wicked, a "foul-mouthed" (δύσφημον ςόμα) man, Cyril says, whether you look at his dogma, which Justin calls "impious and deceitful" (ἀσεβὲς καὶ πλάνον) in his first Apology, and on account of which Simon is called by Irenaeus the prince of the most impious knowledge, and by Philastrius as having sown a wicked and pernicious heresy, or whether you look at his deeds, which were also shameful to speak of, "unspeakable acts and unspeakable deeds" (ἀῤῥητεργίας καὶ ἀῤῥητοποιΐας), as Eusebius says, "mysteries of filth" (μυσήρια αἰσχρότητος), as Epiphanius speaks, not unlike the crimes of the Sodomites, who are called "lawless" (ἄνομος) on account of this, 2 Pet. 2:8. Irenaeus said that the mystic priests lived lasciviously. Augustine says: He taught detestable filth by constantly using women. Theodoret: Those who are of his sect gave themselves boldly to every lust and intemperance. For these reasons, Simon is deservedly called by Cyril "the first dragon of malice" (ὁ πρῶτος τῆς κακίας δράκων). This man disturbed the Church vehemently, as is in Clement. He had deceived many, as Justin says in his second Apology, and Augustine from him, so that a statue was set up to him as a god in Rome, as the same Justin, Irenaeus, and others record. He had driven many into a stupor, says Irenaeus, and he calls all who adulterate the truth his successors. Wherefore this is a notable mark of the time.

This depravation and tearing apart of the text is too bold and violent. For there is one and the same subject in the Apostolic text: "the man of sin," "the son of perdition," "the one who opposes," and "the lawless one." He does open violence to this when he pretends that the "lawless one" (ἄνομov) must now be understood as a completely different subject, and contends that Simon Magus is being pointed out. For he saw well that the following things could not be applied to Gaius in any way, so he preferred to tear the text apart and introduce another subject now, rather than abandon his most inept gloss about Gaius. Furthermore, what is clearer than that "and then" (καὶ τότε) refers to him who was being held back, lest he break forth, until "the one who holds back" (ὁ κατέχων) and "that which holds back" (τὸ κατέχον) should be taken out of the way or removed; upon whose removal from the middle, the man of sin, who had been held back until now so that he would not be revealed, is said to be about to be revealed. These things are clearer than the sun when it shines at midday. But that Simon Magus had been held back so that he would not be revealed, even by Grotius's own admission, is "alien" (ἀλλότριον) and completely foreign to the truth, for he went into all other things rather than his own inventions. Nor indeed could the Apostle have designated that same man of sin more clearly, whether as subject, as predicate, or as a circumstance of time, than when he calls the "lawless one" (ἄνομov) the "man of sin" in the place of the subject, and indeed with the demonstrative article "the lawless one" (ὁ ἄνομος), whose hidden seeds he had designated by the "mystery of lawlessness" (μυσήριον τῆς ἀνομίας); and in the place of the predicate he placed the same verb "he will be revealed" (ἀποκαλυφθήσεται): and the circumstance of time, which he had indicated with the words "in his own time" (ἐν ἑαυτῦ καιρῷ), so that he might be revealed in his own time, he now explains more expressly, with the obstacles removed, "and then the lawless one will be revealed" (καὶ τότε ἀποκαλυφθήσεται ὁ ἄνομος). When Grotius tries to cast darkness upon these things, what else does he deserve but the detestation of all whose eyes are not dim, or whose eyes the god of this age has not blinded, just as he has blinded his own mind? Rightly, therefore, Maresius in his dissertation on the Anti-Christ, page 68: "The commentator interprets what remains of this chapter by changing the characters of the fable, although no one besides him has yet seen two suns in this sky." All the circumstances of the text prove that the latter things are to be understood concerning the same person as the former. "And then" (Καὶ τότε) refers, not as he thinks to the discovered plans of Gaius regarding the statue to be erected to himself in the temple, after which, with some space of time intervening, namely under Claudius his successor, that great impostor, Simon Magus, was to come forth: But it refers evidently to that which immediately preceded, concerning the revelation of him who was then holding back the son of perdition, by his removal from the middle, that is, the abolition of the Roman empire, after which the Anti-Christ was to be uncovered openly, as the event has proven. For what is called the empire today is nothing but a mask of that ancient one of the Romans, and has nothing from it except the name. Erycius Puteanus, intending to complete an epitome of barbaric history in six books, professes in the title of the work that he will relate the decline and ruin of the Roman empire in that manner. Machiavelli, in his Florentine History inscribed to Clement VII, book I, expressly asserts that the empire was utterly overturned, and that from its diminution and disasters the dignity and authority of the Popes grew. Baronius himself, at the year of Christ 476, no. 1, notes that the Western empire gave no consul in that year, because, shaken by frequent concussions, it was already tottering toward its imminent fall (which he describes more fully a little later). This invention is also solidly refuted by chronology; for Simon had already been uncovered and revealed before, when Paul was writing these things: He had already fallen away from the faith immediately after the Apostles Peter and John had departed from Samaria, and thus before Paul himself had been converted to the faith. Grotius therefore mocks the Apostle, whom he introduces as predicting as future things that had already happened before and were known to the Churches. Nor must we admit what Grotius asserts, even if on the authority of Jerome, that Peter went to Rome in the second year of Claudius to occupy Simon Magus, who had not yet been in Rome when Paul said that he was prepared to evangelize the Romans, Rom. 1:15, as one who did not want to build upon another's foundation, Rom. 15:20. How could Peter have flown to Rome in the second year of Claudius to oppress Simon Magus, when Baronius proves with many arguments that Simon was extinguished by Peter under Nero in his twelfth year, at the year 44, no. 7, and at the year 67, no. 7, 8? None of those whom the commentator cites says that Simon was defeated by Peter under Claudius, who had come to Rome under Claudius, but most say that it happened in the times of Nero. Certainly the contest of Peter with Simon Magus, which is said to have taken place at Rome, cannot pertain even to the times of Claudius, because if there is anything among profane writers that favors this drama in appearance, it is that which Suetonius has in Nero ch. XII. Icarus, at his very first attempt, fell down near his chamber and bespattered him with blood. Nor is it true that the impiety of Simon was revealed at Rome at last, and that under Claudius. For not only had his malice been uncovered in Samaria by the blessed Peter, Acts VIII. 23, so much so that immediately after the Apostles had departed from there, he returned to his vomit, as Baronius asserts at the year 35, no. 12, but also in the time of Tiberius himself, and not long after his denied faith, if one is to believe the same Baronius from Josephus, Antiquities 18. ch. 5, it broke out into open sedition with his Samaritans, and was scattered and dispersed by Pilate before he left the province, by the sending in of soldiers, as Maresius again in his dissertation opposed to Grotius. What? That Grotius himself thus destroys the Popish inventions about the Anti-Christ, when he most desires to serve them. For while he divides what the Papists acknowledge to have been predicted here concerning the Anti-Christ between those two, Caligula and Simon, and extends it through the life of each of them, he acknowledges that the duration of the Anti-Christ cannot be limited to three years. Nor did the Pontifical interpreters see Simon Magus here, but the Anti-Christ, who according to Cornelius à Lapide is antonomastically called ὁ ἄνομος, whom, as Estius says, he calls the wicked one by way of eminence in Greek τὸν ἄνομον, and the fountain of iniquity, as Jerome interprets, because he will undoubtedly be the author of all departing from God and His law. For the Greek word signifies a lawless man, that is, one who is held by no reverence for laws, who tramples upon all divine and human right and justice. How truly these things fit the Roman Pontiff, not only as the lawless one, but also as the teacher and author of lawlessness, to whom not even Simon Magus can be compared, whether you consider the variety of his iniquitous doctrine or the multitude of those led astray. Truly the lawless one, as Maresius says, differs. p. 77. He who constitutes himself an outlaw, to be judged by no one, although he judges all, and sets himself above the law and Word of God, and who both approves and teaches crimes: I bear witness to the art of lying with impunity, devised by recent Doctors of the Pope through equivocations and mental reservations; the dogma that faith is not to be kept with heretics, which a recent writer in these provinces, with the approval of the Apostolic Vicar, Francis Dusseldorpius of Lyons, also strives to establish among spouses; the tribunal of the inquisition, the privileges of harlots and the tax from brothels: the lawful killings of Princes whom he himself has excommunicated, even by any private individual; dispensations in degrees of consanguinity prohibited by the law of God, and six hundred things of that kind: I bear witness to Gregory XIII, extolling the Parisian slaughter with the highest praises: I bear witness to Sixtus V, [regarding] Henry III. the unspeakable parricide of the King of the Gauls, comparing it with the work of our redemption: I bear witness to all those whose crimes in this seat have been so graphically produced by the monuments of historians. Mysteries of turpitude, not unlike the crimes of the Sodomites, who are also called ἄνομοι, 2 Pet. 2:8, which a commentator reports from the ancients among the disciples of Simon, he would have found more abundant among those who are the colonists of the scarlet harlot and citizens of that Babylon, which is spiritually called Egypt and Sodom, Apoc. 11:8. Whence Jul. Scaliger interprets the mother of πορνῶν, Apoc. 17:5, as the mother of catamites. How much filth of that kind the harsh law of celibacy has brought in is well known; likewise what kind of lovers and bulls of most powerful harlots those were, who in the tenth century, according to Baronius, occupied this most holy seat: Nor were the following ones better, as Petrus Damianus, Pelagius Alvares, Nicolaus de Clemangis, Petrarch, and others abundantly testify in their complaints concerning the corrupt state of that Church. Note the encomiums of Sodomy published in poems by Johannes Casa, an Italian Archbishop: Note the monstrous life of Paul II, Alexander VI, Innocent VIII, and the like: Indeed, Sixtus IV gave license to some to practice Sodomy during the three summer months of the year, as Weselius of Groningen has it in his work on indulgences. Nor undeservedly does the Mantuan Monk say: The holy field serves scoundrels, the venerable altar serves catamites, the temples of the gods serve Ganymedes. This is Maresius. To which Grotius could not find what to reply; all things placed in the light.

Whom the Lord will consume with the Spirit of his mouth, and will destroy by the manifestation of his coming) Twice the same in the Hebrew manner. For the same ἀναλίσκειν and καταργεῖν mean to finish, בטל to destroy. A manuscript, however, has ἀνελεῖ instead of ἀναλώσει. And this seems taken from Is. 11:21, where in the Greek: In the spirit through his lips he will destroy the ungodly. They tend to the same thing again, the Spirit of the mouth of the Lord, and his illustrious advent. For these show how easy it will be for Christ to destroy that magician, namely, how easily chaff is blown away by the breath of the mouth, Ps. 1:4, or as clouds are dissipated by the advent of the Sun, Hos. 6:4. You have both similes joined in Hos. 13:3; to this place Paul seems to have looked. But ἐπιφάνεια does not always signify something that is seen in reality. For it is enough if its power becomes known through its effect. And thus you have the ἐπιφάνεια of God three or four times in the third book of Maccabees, as we noted there, likewise 2 Maccab. 12:22, 14:15, 15:27. Thus also in Tit. 2:11, 3:4, ἐπιφαίνειν is used. But it is well said that Christ did what he did through Peter. For thus he is also said to have preached to the Gentiles, Eph. 2:17.

Grotius had handed these things down more prolixly in his commentary.

Whom the Lord Jesus will kill with the Spirit of his mouth. The Apostles are the mouth of Christ, Matt. 10:19, and what they do, they do in the name of Christ, Acts 3:6, 16, 4:10, 30. Peter in Clement of Rome: I was praying with all my mind to God, that through our Lord Jesus Christ he might break that wicked one. Arnobius, book 2, speaking of the Romans: For they had seen the course of Simon the magician, and the fiery chariots blown away by the mouth of Peter (behold almost the very words of Paul) and having named Christ, he had vanished. Eusebius: Ἐπιδημήσαντος ἀυτοῖς τῶ θείου λόγου

· the power of Simon was extinguished and immediately destroyed along with the man, when the divine Word had come to them, the power of Simon immediately collapsed with the man himself. Cyril says he was cast down by the weapon of Christ's prayers as promised. Phylastrius: Overcome by the prayer of the Apostle Peter, and struck by an Angel. Augustine on heresies: In which city the Blessed Apostle Peter extinguished him by the true power of almighty God. Palladius in the life of Chrysostom, when he had spoken about this very Simon: Indignant at these things, he who catches the wise in their craftiness, spoke through the mouth of Peter, etc. Maximus of Turin on Peter: He had even cast down that magician Simon from the void of the air by his prayers with a precipitous fall. And these things indeed regarding the matter. As far as the manner of speaking is concerned, that of Chrysostom at the end of his commentary on the Romans does not depart from this: Τοῦτο τῦ σώματος ἐβυλόμην τὴν κόνι ἰδεῖν δι᾿ ὗ τὰ μεγάλα κὶ ἀπόῥῥητα χριστὸς ἐλάλησε, κὶ μείζονα ἡ δι᾿ ἑαυτῦ. As he worked greater things through the disciples, so also he spoke, I would wish to see the ashes of that mouth, through which Christ spoke great and ineffable things, nay, greater than through himself. For just as he performed greater things through the disciples: So also he spoke greater things. Add also Isaiah 15:19 and 1 Pet. 3:19, where Christ is said to have preached to the Gentiles.

And he will destroy him by the illustration of his advent. An explanation of the former in the Hebrew manner; παρουσία is said of every judgment. The illustration of the advent is an illustrious advent, likewise in the Hebrew manner, one through two. Thus the word ἐπιφάνεια is used in 2 Maccab. 3:24, where the old interpreter made it the evidence of his manifestation. The sense which is in these words is rightly expressed by Phylastrius: He deserved to perish in such a way that the evident lie of his magic might be laid open to all men. Theodoret on Peter: He stripped him (Simon) of the feathers of his fraud. Isidore, book 13 of letters: The wretch fell headlong from on high into a death most celebrated in speech by many.

The Apostle had not injected a single word about Simon Magus. Nor did anyone here dream of Simon Magus. All interpreters agree entirely that the subject is the dissolution and destruction of the Anti-Christ. Nor is it to be admitted that the same thing is said twice in this place. The word ἀναλίσκειν does not mean to kill, but to alter and to consume gradually. Whence in Aristophanes, according to Suidas, it is to expend, to incur expenses, by which wealth is gradually worn away. For it is not ἀνελεῖ, he will kill, as the Vulgate rendered it, which is for the most part taken in that way, but ἀναλώσει, he will finish, he will consume, namely not in one moment, but gradually and successively, just as the Anti-Christ was not raised to such a height in one moment, but gradually, as D. Quirinus Reuter notes. Καταργεῖν is to abolish utterly, which difference Erasmus also observed. For one manuscript cannot prejudice the other codices. The former corresponds to the word אכל, to eat, metaphorically to gnaw, to consume, to feed upon, which is applied to fire, which by spreading first consumes and feeds upon. Nor is ἀναλωθῆτε, Gal. 5:15, otherwise. Furthermore, that blowing away of the Magus by Peter is not so certain that Crocius should have had to underpin his new commentaries on this passage with it. That the Apostle Peter descended into a contest with Simon as to which of them would perform greater miracles. That Nero sat as spectator and judge of the dispute, that the magus flying through the air and striving for the heavens fell to the earth at the prayers of Peter in confusion, and broke his leg, from which he later died. That Caesar, witness to the miracle along with all of Rome, nevertheless set up altars and cushions for the charlatan, and shackles and a prison for the victor Peter, let the Jew Apella believe that. The narrators of that fable indeed agree so little among themselves that they scarcely deserve any credence. Ambrose himself, or whoever is the author of the commentary on the epistles which are attributed to Ambrose, in the passage cited by the commentator on chapter 7 of Romans, speaks quite doubtfully about this matter. Nor, if a mighty work has been done by someone, as it is said to have been done by Simon Magus, who is said to have flown up into the air so that he might be a scandal to the people of Christ, ought it to diminish our faith, as Maresius argues against Grotius in his dissertation, pages 79, 80. The prayers by which Peter is imagined to have interrupted Simon's flight cannot be called the Spirit of the mouth of the Lord, for prayers to GOD and the Word of GOD to men ought not to be confused or taken for the same thing. What? That not all say Simon was killed by Peter, but many and the older ones, Clement and Hegesippus, report him to have been punished only by such a dislocation or breaking of his legs, after which he left Rome and betook himself to Aricia, and died there. To say nothing of the fact that Cyril, Sulpitius, Hegesippus, and Maximus of Turin join Paul to Peter here, and therefore say that Nero inflicted the ultimate punishment on both, which and many other dissensions and uncertain reports make that whole narrative uncertain; which many Romans say is false in Augustine, Epistle 56 to Casulanus. Whatever, however, may be the case regarding it, it certainly has no bearing on the present matter. The Spirit of the mouth of the Lord is the Holy Spirit exerting himself through the efficacy of the Word, Isaiah 11:4, Hebrews 4:12. Revelation 1:16. He could have said, says Crocius, by the proclamation of his Word. He does not say so, but uses a much more effective phrase, both to commend the virtue of the word, which that lawless one will presume to trample underfoot. Christ himself will breathe upon the Word through ministers, as if through his own mouth, not they speaking, but the Spirit of God speaking in him. By the appearing of his coming is understood the final advent of the Lord, 2 Timothy 4:1, Titus 2:13, through which at last he will be thoroughly destroyed, not that his person is to be annihilated, inasmuch as it is to be cast into the lake of fire, Revelation 19:20, but that all his power is to be utterly abolished, 1 Corinthians 15:24-25. Concerning which B. Hunnius most correctly: As if he were to say: Christ will first destroy his adversary the Anti-Christ in the minds of men, who had been thoroughly occupied by the opinion of holiness conceived about him, and absorbed into his religious adoration. But he will destroy him not with external weapons: But just as the wickedness was spiritual, fixed most deeply in the very hearts of men: So Christ will fight against him with spiritual weapons also, namely the Spirit of his mouth, and will finish him. By the Spirit of the mouth of Christ, however, the Holy Spirit is understood. For it is he who convicts the world of sin, righteousness, and judgment, and that through the preaching of the Word. Therefore, that same Spirit of Christ was to overcome the Anti-Christ by the virtue of his rising Word of the Gospel. Moreover, what he adds: And will abolish him by the brightness of his coming: He openly hints that the Anti-Christ, though detected and defeated in the minds of innumerable men, will nevertheless endure until the illustrious second coming of Christ: where at last he is to be utterly abolished by the most glorious majesty of his very appearance: So indeed, that an end is put to his whole kingdom; he himself, however, with his fellowship is to be cast into the infernal lake burning with fire and brimstone. To which contributes the explanation of certain Roman Catholics, not disapproved by Estius: Others understand the Apostle thus: Whom the Lord Jesus, before he comes to judgment, will kill with the Spirit of his mouth. But in his very advent he will destroy all his remnants. For Cajetan opines not improbably that after the Anti-Christ is killed, his followers will endure until the appearance of the coming Christ. Therefore, what the Papists say, that the Anti-Christ will be destroyed 45 days before the judgment, is a fable, contrary to the Apostle. Not 45 days before the coming of Christ, but by his illustrious coming Christ is to destroy the Anti-Christ. Thus also the fiction of the Chiliasts is refuted, that Christ is to reign on earth with his own for a thousand years, with all heresies destroyed. For the Anti-Christ will flourish until the final coming of Christ, nor will he be destroyed except with the final coming of Christ.

Latin:

V. 8. Καὶ τότε ἀποκαλυφθήσεται ὁ ἄνομος.) Τότε id est, bi- ennio aut triennio post. Solet enim τότε convertere tempora etiam multo magis distantia, ut Matth. II. 7. III. 13. IV. 11. XV. 12. XVII. 10. XIX. 3. 27. XXIV. 3. 14. 30. Sophoniæ III. 9. Amos IX. 11. & alibi sæpe. Ἀποκαλυφθήσεται rursus est prodet se, nudabit se, ὁ ἄνομος nempe alter ille, de quo itidem in Syria sum loquutus vobis. Hactenus impium Principem descripsit, nunc venit ad impium Doctorem, alteram Chri- stianorum & maxime eorum, qui ex Judæa erant, tentatio- nem. Recte autem impius dicitur Simon magus, qui paulo post initia Claudiani principatus Romam venit, ut homi- nes à Christo abduceret, sibique manciparet, omnibus libi- dinibus, quibus dediti erant Romani, commeatum faciens, eo quod diceret, legem non mœchaberis, & similes, non esse à Deo, sed ab Angelis Dei injussu: & fide homines servari sine justis operibus. Hæc alibi latius explicavimus ex Justi- no, Irenæo, Philastrio, Cyrillo, Theodoreto & aliis.

Assanias istas antea eadem pene ratione propo- suerat in commentatione sua Grotius, sed uberius.

Καὶ τότε) Et tunc. Non antequam id evenerit, quod dixi, magnus impostor se visendum dabit, non minore cum periculo. Solet sæpe τότε poni ad temporis etiam aliquo intervallo distantis significationem, Matth. II. 7. IV. 5. XXIV. 14. & 30. & alibi. Illud ergo τότε intelligen- dum de initio principatus Claudii, qui Cajum Principem excepit. Nam anno Claudii secundo Romam ivit Petrus ad occupandum Simonem Magum, ut Hieronymus nos docet de scriptis Ecclesiasticis. Et sub Claudio aperuisse se Simonis illius impietatem, diserte notant Christiano- rum, quos habemus, vetustissimi, Justinus apologetico secundo & Irenæus l. I. c. XX. nec aliter in historia Euse- bius, in Catechesi Cyrillus, & in hæreticis fabulis Theo- doretus. Quod autem Philastrius & posteriores quidam ad Neronis tempora hæc referunt, errorem esse puto or- tum ex ambiguo nominis. Nam & Claudius ex Neronum erat gente, patrique ejus nomen fuerat Nero, ut Sueto- nius nos docet; Unde & idem nomen ab ipso datum ei, quem adoptaverat, filio, sceleribus suis notissimo Neroni.

Ἀποκαλυφθήσεται) revelabitur. Eadem vox, quam supra de Cajo habuimus. Impietatem suam Simon nuda- bit, quam hactenus, Christianis se aggregando, occulta- verat. Vide Act. VIII. 24. Clemens Alexandrinus de eo: Κηρύσσοντι τῷ Πέτρῳ ὑπήκουσε. Philastrius de eodem: Qui baptizatus à beato Apostolo recessit à fide eorum.

Ὁ ἄνομος) ille iniquus. Ita vertunt Græci interpretes novi fœderis vocem עשׂה, ut videre est Ef. LIII. vers. 12. Marc. XV. 28. Luc. XXII. 27. Sic autem vocantur Hebræis ii, qui consulto mali sunt, Convenit optime Simoni, quem scelestum dixit Clemens Romanus, δύσφημον ςόμα, impurum os, Cyrillus, sive dogma ejus respicias, quod ἀσεβὲς καὶ πλάνον vocat Justinus Apologetico priore & propter quod Simon princeps impiissimæ scientiæ Irenæo dicitur, Philastrio autem sceleratam & perniciosam hæresin seminasse, sive facta ipsius etiam effatu turpia, ἀῤῥητεργίας καὶ ἀῤῥητοποιΐας, ut Eusebius ait, μυσήρια αἰσχρότητος, mysteria turpitudinis, ut loquitur Epiphanius, non dissimilia Sodomitarum sceleribus, qui propter id ἄνομος iniqui, 2. Petr. II. 8. Libidinosè vivere mysticos Sacerdotes dixit Irenæus. Docebat detestandam turpitudinem indefinenter usurpando fœminas, ait Augustinus. Theodoretes: Qui ejus sectæ sunt, se audacter omni libidini & intemperantiæ dedebant. Ob hæc merito Cyrillo Simon dicitur ὁ πρῶτος τῆς κακίας δράκων primus malitiæ draco. Hic Ecclesiam vehementer perturbavit, ut apud Clementem est. Deceperat multos, ut Justinus ait Apologetico secundo, & ex eo Augustinus, ita ut statua ei tanquam Deo Romæ poneretur, memorante eodem Justino, Irenæo, aliisque. Multos in stuporem coëgerat, ait Irenæus, & omnes qui adulterant veritatem, ejus successores vocat. Quare insignis hæc est nota temporis.

Nimis audax & violenta hæc textus est depravatio & dilaceratio. Nam unum idemque subjectum in Apostolico textu est, ὁ ἄνθρωπος τῆς ἁμαρτίας, ὁ υἱὸς τῆς ἀπωλείας, ὁ ἀντικείμενος, & ὁ ἄνομος. Cui aperte vim facit, cum ἄνομov jam de alio prorsus diverso subjecto intelligendum esse fingit, ac Simonem magum indigitari contendit. Vidit enim probe, sequentia non posse ullatenus applicari Cajo, ideo maluit textu discerpto aliud jam subjectum invehere, quam glossam ineptissimam de Cajo deserere. Porro quid luculentius, quam illud καὶ τότε respicere eum, qui detinebatur, ne erumperet, donec ὁ κατέχων & τὸ κατέχον de medio fieret vel tolleretur; quo è medio sublato revelandus homo peccati hactenus detentus, ne revelaretur, dicitur. Quæ Sole, cum in meridie lucet, sunt clariora. Jam autem detentum fuisse Simonem Magum, ne revelaretur, Grotio ipso fatente, ἀλλότριον, & à veritate alienum prorsus est, qui in omnia alia potius commentis suis ivit. Neque vero magis perspicue eundem illum peccati hominem, tum quà subjectum, tum quà prædicatum, tum quà temporis circumstantiam designare poterat Apostolus, quam cum subjecti loco ἄνομov vocat ἄνθρωπον τῆς ἁμαρτίας, & quidem cum articulo demonstrativo ὁ ἄνομος, cujus occulta semina per μυσήριον τῆς ἀνομίας designarat; prædicati vero loco idem posuit verbum ἀποκαλυφθήσεται: ac temporis, quod vocibus, ἐν ἑαυτῦ καιρῷ, ut reveletur in suo tempore, indicarat, circumstantiam jam expressius, remotis remoris, explicat, καὶ τότε ἀποκαλυφθήσεται ὁ ἄνομος. Quibus cum tenebras offundere conatur Grotius, quid aliud quam detestationem meretur omnium, quibus non caligant oculi, vel quibus Deus hujus seculi pariter, atque ipsi non excæcavit oculos mentis. Recte ergo Maresius in dissert. de Anti-Christo pag. 68. Quod superat ex hoc capite, mutatis fabulæ personis Commentator de Simone mago interpretatur, quamvis nemo adhuc præter eum geminos Soles in hoc cœlo viderit. Omnes textus circumstantiæ evincunt, de eodem posteriora esse intelligenda, de quo agunt priora. Καὶ τότε & tunc refertur, non uti putat ad Caji retecta consilia de statua sibi in templo erigenda, post quæ, aliquo temporis interposito spatio, nempe sub Claudio ejus successore, prodire debebat magnus ille impostor, Simon magus: Sed evidenter ad id, quod immediate præcessit, de ejus, qui tunc obtinebat, filii perditionis patefactionem retardabat, sublatione è medio, id est, abolitione imperii Romani, post quam retegendus erat palam Anti-Christus, uti eventus comprobavit. Quod enim hodie imperium dicitur, antiqui illius Romanorum non nisi larva est, nihilque præter nomen habet ex illo. Erycius Puteanus, barbaricæ historiæ epitomen libris sex comple- xurus, profitetur in operis titulo, se imperii Romani occasum & ruinam ea ratione relaturum. Machiavellus Florentina historia Clementi VII. inscripta libr. I. diserte asserit, imperium penitus eversum, & ex illius imminutione ac cladibus Pontificum dignitatem atque autoritatem excrevisse. Baronius ipse ad ann. Christi 476. n. 1. notat, eo nullum consulem dedisse imperium Occidentale, quod crebris concussionibus agitatum, jam ad proximum casum (quem paulo post fusius describit) vacillaret. Solide etiam è chronologia refellitur hoc commentum; Nam retectus jam antea erat, & revelatus Simon, cum Paulus hæc scriberet: Jam à fide defecerat statim, postquam Apostoli Petrus & Johannes Samaria discesserant, adeoque antequam ipse Paulus ad fidem esset conversus. Illudit ergo Grotius Apostolo, quem prædicentem introducit tanquam futura, quæ jam antea contigerant, notaque erant Ecclesiis. Nec admittendum, quod asserit Grotius, etsi autore Hieronymo, anno Claudii secundo Romam ivisse Petrum ad occupandum Simonem Magum, qui nec dum adhuc Romæ fuerat, cum Paulus dicebat, se paratum evangelizare Romanis, Rom. I. vers. 15. utpote qui nolebant alterius fundamento inædificare, Rom. XV. 20. Qui potuisset Petrus Romam advolare secundo Claudii anno Simonem Magum oppressurus, cùm Baronius multis evincat, Simonem extinctum fuisse à Petro sub Nerone anno ejus duodecimo ad ann. 44. n. 7. & ad an. 67. n. 7. 8. Nemo eorum quos citat commentator, dicit sub Claudio Simonem debellatum à Petro, qui sub Claudio Romam venerat, confectum fuisse, plerique vero dicunt id Neronis temporibus contigisse. Certe nec ad Claudii tempora potest pertinere certamen Petri cum Simone mago, quod Romæ dicitur fuisse, quia si quicquam est apud profanos scriptores, quod huic dramati in speciem faveat, illud est, quod habeat Suetonius in Nerone c. XII. Icarus primo statim conatu juxta cubiculum ejus decidit, ipsumque cruore respersit. Neque verum est Romæ demum, idque sub Claudio se aperuisse Simonis impietatem. Non solum enim retecta fuerat ipsius malitia Samariæ à B. Petro, Act. VIII. 23. adeo ut statim, postquam inde discessissent Apostoli, ad vomitum suum redierit, uti asserit Baronius ad ann. 35. n. 12. sed etiam ipsius Tiberii tempore, nec multo post abnegatam fidem, si eidem Baronio fides ex Josepho antiq. 18. cap. 5. in apertam erupit seditionem cum suis Samaritanis, à Pilato priusquam provincia excederet, milite immisso disjectus & disturbatus, ut iterum in dissertatione sua Grotio opposita Maresius. Quid? quod destruat ita ipse Grotius Papistica de Anti-Christo commenta, cum maxime illis inservire discupit. Dum enim, quæ de Anti-Christo hic prædicta agnoscunt Papistæ, inter duos illos Caligulam & Simonem partitur, & per utriusque illius vitam extendit, durationem Anti-Christi triennio minime finiri posse agnoscit. Neque hic Simonem Magum viderunt Interpretes Pontificii, sed Anti-Christum, qui juxta Cornelium à Lapide antonomastice dicitur ὁ ἄνομος, quem κατ᾽ ἐξοχὴν, dicente Estio, iniquum vocat Græce τὸν ἄνομον, & fontem iniquitatis, ut Hieronymus interpretatur, quia nimirum autor erit omnibus à Deo atque lege ejus recedendi. Nam Græca vox hominem significat exlegem, id est, eum qui nulla legum reverentia tenetur, qui jus & fas omne divinum atque humanum conculcat. Quæ quam vere Romano Pontifici conveniant non ἀνόμῳ tantum, sed ἀνομίας etiam Doctori & auctori, cui nec Simon Magis conferri queat, sive varietatem doctrinæ iniquæ, sive deductorum multitudinem respicias. Vere ἄνομος, inquit Marefius differt. p. 77. qui se exlegem, a nemine judicandum, licet de omnibus judicantem, & supra Dei legem & Verbum constituit, quique scelera & probat & docet: Testor artem impune mentiendi a nuperis Pontificis Doctoribus, per æquivocationes & retentiones mentales excogitatam, dogma de fide hæreticis non servanda, quod etiam inter conjuges stabilire annititur nuperus in his provinciis scriptor, approbante Vicario Apostolico, Franciscus Dusseldorpius Lugdunensis, tribunal inquisitionis, meretricum privilegia & vectigal ex lupanaribus: Principum quos ipse excommunicaverit licitas cædes, a quovis etiam privato; dispensationes in gradibus consanguinitatis lege Dei prohibitis, & sexcenta ejusmodi: testor Gregorium XIII. lanienam Parisiensem summis laudibus evehentem: testor Sixtum V. Henrici III. Galliarum Regis parricidium nefandum, cum opere redemptionis nostræ conferentem: testor eos omnes, quorum scelera in hac sede, tam graphice historiarum monumentis prodita. Mysteria turpitudinis, non dissimilia sceleribus Sodomitarum, qui & ἄνομοι dicuntur, 2. Petr. II. 8. quæ apud Simonis discipulos ex veteribus refert commentator, copiosiora apud eos reperiisset, qui purpuratæ meretricis coloni & Babylonis illius cives sunt, quæ spiritualiter Ægyptus & Sodoma dicitur, Apoc. XI. 8. Unde Jul. Scaliger matrem πορνῶν Apoc. XVII. 5. catamitorum matrem interpretatur. Quot sordes istius generis invexerit dura lex cœlibatus, est in comperto; quales item fuerint illi potentissimarum meretricum amasii & tauri, qui decimo seculo apud Baronium, sacerrimam hanc occuparere sedem: Nec sequentia meliora, ut Petrus Damianus, Pelagius Alvares, Nicolaus de Clemangis, Petrarcha, & alii in suis de corrupto statu illius Ecclesiæ querelis fuse testantur. Nota encomia Sodomiæ a Johanne Casa Archiepiscopo Italo carminibus edita: Nota Pauli II. Alexandri VI. Innocentii VIII. & similium portentosa vita: Quin Sixtus IV. licentiam fecit nonnullis Sodomiam exercendi tribus æstivis anni mensibus, ut habet Weselius Gröningensis de indulgent. Nec immerito Mantuanus Monachus: Sanctus ager scurris, venerabilis ara cynædis Servit, honorandæ divûm Ganymedibus ædes. Hæc Maresius. Ad quæ quid reponeret Grotius non invenire potuit; omnia in luce posita.

Ὃν ὁ Κύριος ἀναλώσει τῷ Πνεύματι τῶ στόματος αὑτῶ, καὶ καταργήσει τῇ ἐπιφανείᾳ τῆς παρουσίας ἀυτῶ) Bis idem more Ebræo. Idem enim ἀναλίσκειν & καταργεῖν conficere בטל destruere. Manuscriptus autem pro ἀναλώσει habet ἀνελεῖ. Et videtur sumptum hoc ex Es. XI. 21. ubi in Græco: Ἐν πνέυματι διὰ χειλέων ἀνελεῖ ἀσεβῆ. Eodem rursus tendunt, Spiritus oris Domini, & illustris ejus adventus. Ostendunt enim hæc quam facile Christo futurum id illum magum destruere, nempe quam facile halitu oris difflatur gluma Psal. I. 4. aut sicut Solis adventu dissipantur nebulæ, Os. VI. v. 4. Utramque similitudinem conjunctam habes Os. XIII. v. 3. ad locum videtur hic Paulus respexisse. Ἐπιφάνεια autem non semper significat aliquid quod in re conspicitur. Satis enim est si per effectum vis ejus innotescat. Et sic Dei ἐπιφάνεια habes ter, quater in Maccabaico tertio, ut ibi notavimus, item 2. Maccab. XII. 22. XIV. 15. XV. 27. Sic & Tit. II. 11. III. 4. sumitur ἐπιφαίνειν. Bene autem dicitur Christus fecisse quod fecit per Petrum. Nam sic & gentibus prædicasse dicitur, Eph. II. 17.

Prolixius hæc tradiderat in commentatione sua Grotius.

Ὃν ὁ Κύριος ἀναλώσει τῷ πνέυματι τῶ στόματος ἀυτῶ) quem Dominus Jesus interficiet Spiritu oris sui. Apostoli sunt os Christi Matth. X. 19. & quæ faciunt, Christi faciunt nomine, Act. III. 6. 16. IV. 10. 30. Petrus apud Clementem Romanum: Tota mente supplicabam Deo, ut per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum frangeret scelestum illum. Arnobius libr. II. de Romanis loquens: Viderant enim cursum Simonis magi, & quadrigas igneas Petri ore difflatus (en ipsa ferme Pauli verba) & nominato Christo evanuisse. Eusebius: Ἐπιδημήσαντος ἀυτοῖς τῶ θείου λόγου

· ἡ μὲν τῦ Σίμωνᾶ ̔ ἀπέσβη καὶ παραχρῆμα κὶ σὺν τῷ ἀνδρὶ καταλέλυτο δύναμις, cum ad eos Verbum divinum venisit, statim Simonis potentia cum ipso homine concidit. Cyrillus ex promisso Christi precum telo dejectum ait. Phylastrius: Devictum oratione Petri Apostoli, atque percussum ab Angelo. Augustinus de hæresibus: In qua urbe B. Apostolus Petrus eum vera omnipotentis Dei virtute extinxit. Palladius in vita Chrysostomi, cum de hoc ipso Simone loquutus esset: Indignatus ad hæc ille, qui comprehendit sapientes in astutia sua, per os Petri loquutus est &c. Maximus Taurinensis de Petro: Etiam magum illum Simonem orationibus suis de aërislvacuo præcipiti ruinaprosternerat. Et hæc quidem de re. Loquendi genus quod attinet, non abit hinc illud Chrysostomi fine ad Romanos: Τοῦτο τῦ σώματος ἐβυλόμην τὴν κόνι ἰδεῖν δι᾿ ὗ τὰ μεγάλα κὶ ἀπόῥῥητα χριστὸς ἐλάλησε, κὶ μείζονα ἡ δι᾿ ἑαυτῦ. Ὡσπερ γὰρ ἐιργάσατο μείζονα διὰ τῶν μαθητῶν, ὕτω κὶ ἐφθέγξατο, illius oris optarem videre cineres, per quod magna & ineffabilia Christus loquutus est, imo majom, quam per se. Nam sicut per discipulos majora effecit: Ita & majora est loquutus. Adde & Esaiam XV. 19. & 1. Petr. III. 19. ubi Christus prædicasse gentibus dicitur.

Καὶ καταργήσει τῇ ἐπιφανείᾳ τῆς παρουσίας) & destruet illustratione adventus sui eum. Ἐπεξήγησις explicatio priorum more Ebræo παρουσία dicitur de omni judicio. Ἐπιφάνεια παρουσίας adventus illustratio est ἐπιφανὴς παρουσία illustris adventus, item Ebræo more δὶ δυοῖν, unum per duo. Sic ἐπιφάνειας vox sumitur 2. Maccab. III. 24. ubi interpres vetus fecit suæ ostensionis evidentiam, Sensus qui in his verbis est, recte exprimitur à Philastrio: Sic meruit interire, ut ejus magiæ evidens mendacium cunctis hominibus patefieret. Theodoretes de Petro: Fraudis eum (Simonem) pennis nudavit. Isidorus libr. epist. XIII. Ex alto miser in mortem multorum sermone celebratissimam præceps ruit.

Nullum de Simone Mago verbulum injecerat Apostolus. Nec quisquam hic Simonem Magum somniavit. De Anti-Christi dissolutione, & excidio agi omnes consentiunt ex asse Interpretes. Neque bis idem hoc loco dici admittendum. Vox ἀναλίσκειν non est interficere, sed alterare, & tractim consumere. Unde Aristophani apud Suidam est expendere, sumptus facere, quibus opes paulatim atteruntur. Non enim ἀνελεῖ est interficiet, ut Vulgata reddidit, quod plerumque sic accipitur, sed ἀναλώσει conficiet, consumet, scilicet non uno momento, sed paulatim ac successive, sicut Anti-Christus non uno momento, sed paulatim ad tantam sublimitatem evectus est, notante D. Quirino Reutero. Καταργεῖν est abolere penitus, quam differentiam etiam observavit Erasmus. Unum enim Manuscriptum non potest cæteris codicibus præjudicare. Prius respondet verbo אכל edere, Metaphorice arrodere, absumere, depasci, quod de igne adhibetur, qui gliscendo primum absumit, & depascitur. Nec aliter ἀναλωθῆτε, Gal.V.15. Porro non tam certa illa Magi per Petrum disfufflatio, ut eam Crocius suis de hoc loco novis commentis debuerit substernere. Petrum Apostolum in certamen cum Simone descendisse, uter majorapatraturus esset miracula. Neronem dissidii spectatorem sedisse & judicem, magum per aëra volantem & nitentem in cælos ad preces Petri in terram cecidisse confusum, & crus alterum sibi confregisse, ex quo post obierit. Cæsarem miraculi cum tota Roma testem nihilo minus agyrtæ aras & pulvinaria, victori Petro compedes & ergastulum statuisse, credat Judæus Apella. Istius sane fabulæ enarratores tam parum inter se conveniunt, ut vix ullam mereantur fidem. Ipse Ambrosius, aut quisquis est autor comment. in epistolas, quæ Ambrosio tribuuntur, loco à commentatore citato in caput VII. Rom. hac de re subdubitanter admodum loquitur. Neque si virtus ab aliquo facta fuerit, sicut dicitur facta à Simone Mago, qui dicitur in aëra sursum, ut populo Christi scandalo esset, volasse, fidem nostram debebit minuere, ut contra Grotium in dissert. sua Maresius pag. 79. 80. Preces, quibus fingitur Petrus interrupisse Simonis volatum, non possunt dici Spiritus oris Domini, nec enim debent confundi aut pro eodem sumi preces ad DEUM & Verbum DEI ad homines. Quid? quod non interfectum omnes dicunt Si- monem a Petro, sed plerique ac vetustiores, Cle- mens & Hegesippus, eum referunt tali luxatione tantum aut crurifragio mulctatum, post quod Ro- ma egressus Aritiam se contulerit, ibique mortuus sit. Ut taceam, quod Cyrillus, Sulpitius, Hege- sippus, Maximus Taurinensis, hic Petro Paulum adjungant, & ideo Neronem utrumque ultimo supplicio affecisse dicant, quae & multae aliae dis- sensiones & incertae relationes incertam reddunt totam illam narrationem; quam plerique Roma- ni falsam dicunt apud Augustinum epist. 56. ad Casulanum. Quicquid autem de ea sit, nihil pro- fecto ad rem praesentem facit. Spiritus oris Do- mini est Spiritus sanctus per Verbi efficaciam sese exerens, Es. XI. vers. 4. Ebr. IV. 12. Apocal. I. 16. Poterat dicere, inquit Crocius, Verbi sui praeconio. Non dicit, sed utitur phrasi multo efficaciori, tum ut verbi virtutem commendet, quam ille exlex pe- dibus conculcare praesumet. Christus ipse Verbum afflabit per ministros, tanquam per os suum, non ipsis loquentibus, sed Spiritu Dei in ipso loquente. Per ἐπιφάνειαν τῆς παρουσίας αὐτῦ intelligitur ad- ventus Domini novissimus, 2. Tim. IV. 1. Tit. II. 13. per quem demum penitus destruetur, non quod persona annihilanda sit, utpote quae in stagnum ignis conjicienda, Apoc. XIX. 20. sed quod omne imperium ejus delendum penitus sit 1. Cor. XV. vers. 24. 25. Quo de B. Hunnius rectissime: Quasi dicat: Christus adversarium suum Anti-Christum primo destruet in hominum animis, qui sanctitatis opinione de ipso concepta occupati penitus, & in il- lius religiosam adorationem absorpti fuerant. De- struet autem illum non armis externis: Sed quemad- modum nequitia spiritualis erat, ipsis cordibus ho- minum altissima infixa: Sic spiritualibus quoque armis nempe Spiritu oris sui pugnabit adversus illum Christus, eumque conficiet. Per Spiritum oris Christi vero Spiritus sanctus intelligitur. Hic enim est, qui arguit mundum de peccato, justitia & judicio, idque per Verbi praedicationem. Proinde idem ille Christi Spiritus virtute exorientis Verbi sui Evangelii ex- pugnaturus erat Anti-Christum. Caeterum quod subjungit: Et abolebit eum claritate adventus sui: Palam innuit, Anti-Christum licet detectum, & in hominum innumerabilium animis debellatum, du- raturum tamen esse usque ad illustrem Christi ad- ventum alterum: ubi demum majestate gloriosissi- ma ipsius apparitionis prorsus sit abolendus: Ita nimirum, ut toti regno ejus finis imponatur; ipse vero cum suo sodalitio praecipitetur in infernalem lacum igne & sulphure ardentem. Quo facit Ro- mano-Catholicorum quorundam Estio non im- probata explicatio: Alii sic Apostolum intelligunt: Quem iniquum Dominus Jesus, priusquam venit ad judicium, Spiritu oris sui interficiet. Caeterum in ipso suo adventu destruet omnes ejus reliquias. Nam post interfectum Anti-Christum sequaces ejus duraturos usque ad apparitionem advenientis Christi, Cajetanus haud improbabiliter opinatur. Quod ergo Papistae dicunt Anti-Christum 45. dies ante judicium deletum iri, fabula est, Apostolo contra- ria. Non 45. diebus ante adventum Christi, sed illustri adventu suo Christus destructurus est Anti- Christum. Refellitur etiam ita commentum Chi- liastarum, quod Christus mille annis cum suis in terra regnaturus sit, deletis omnibus haeresibus. Anti-Christus enim vigebit usque ad adventum Christi novissimum, neque nisi cum adventu Chri- sti novissimo delebitur.

## 2:9
V. 9. Whose coming is after the working of Satan with all power and signs, and lying wonders) He shows how great this is, which he says Christ will effect so easily: a matter, indeed, desperate for all men. But why? Because the coming, that is, the display, of that Simon had as a companion great efficacy, not of God indeed, but of Satan, and that with displays, prodigies, and portents of lying, that is, serving a lying doctrine. The same words are used both of Christ and of Satan, or his ministers, as the word 'coming' is used of Christ by the Apostles: here of Simon. And 'working' is used of God and Christ often, of Satan here and below in verse 11. And the verb 'to work' in Ephesians 2:22. Thus 'power', 'signs', 'wonders' are attributed to Christ in Acts 2:22, here however to Satan, as also in Matthew 24, just as in Exodus Jannes and Jambres are said to have done the same as Moses: namely, up to a certain degree, God permitting it. Whence, therefore, were these to be distinguished? I will say. In the Old Testament, miracles were of the truth, which led to the one God; of lying, which led to many gods, Deuteronomy 13:1 and following. In the New Testament, however, truthful ones, which lead to Jesus Christ; fallacious ones, which show other Christs, or teachers other than Christ, 1 Corinthians 12:3, 1 John 4:1, for what is said in these places about prophecy is to be applied with equal right to miracles. For prophecies also are miracles. But this must also be added: Just as God prescribed a certain limit to Jannes and Jambres, so also a limit was prefixed by him to this Simon Magus and later to Apollonius of Tyana: namely, that they would not suddenly heal all kinds of diseases, that they would not speak in all languages, that they would not raise the dead in such a way that they could be seen by all to survive for a long time in this life. Why this? Namely, so that if any were to follow new teachers, and say that they were led to this by miracles, they could be refuted by the fact that Christ and the Apostles had done not only more, but also greater things: Whence it followed that they had addicted themselves to those new Masters for no other reason than that their dogmas flattered the flesh, which happens even now, with miracles ceasing. Lying wonders are those which serve a false doctrine. For what is in place of the genitive among the Hebrews often signifies the end, which end the words of Christ explain, Matthew 24:24, which follows here in verse 11. You have these magical displays and prodigies of Simon explained in Justin, Irenaeus, Tertullian, Cyril, Theodoret, and Epiphanius.

Latin:

V. 9. Ὃυ ἐστιν ἡ παρουσία κατ' ἐνέργειαν τοῦ Σατανᾶ ἐν πάσῃ δυνάμει καὶ σημείοις, καὶ τέρασι ψεύδους) Oftendit quantum hoc sit, quod dicit Christum tam facile effecturum: rem nempe omnibus hominibus desperatam. Quare vero? Quia Simonis illius παρουσία, id est, ostentus, comitem habuit ma- gnam efficaciam, non Dei sane, sed Satanæ, idque cum osten- tis, prodigiis, portentis mendacii, id est, mendaci doctrinæ inservientibus. Eadem verba & de Christo usurpantur, & de Satana, aut ejus ministris, ut vox παρουσίας modo de Chri- sto per Apostolos: hic de Simone. Et ἐνέργεια de Deo & Christo sæpe, de Satana hic & infra 11. Et verbum ἐνεργεῖν Eph. II. 22. Sic δύναμις, σημεῖα, τέρατα tribuuntur Christo Act. II. 22. hic vero Satanæ, ut & Matth. XXIV. quomodo & in Exodo Jamnes & Mambres dicuntur fecisse paria Mosi: nempe ad aliquem usque gradum Deo id permittente. Un- de ergo hæc erant dignoscenda? Dicam. In Veteri Testa- mento miracula τῆς ἀληθείας erant, quæ ad Deum unum du- cebant, ψέυδους quæ ad plures Deos, Deut. XIII. v. 1. & se- quentibus. In Novo vero Testamento, veridica, quæ ad Jesum Christum ducunt, fallacia, quæ alios monstrant Chri- stos, aut alios à Christo Doctores, 1. Cor. XII. 3. 1. Joh. IV. v. 1. quod enim istis locis de prophetia dicitur, pari jure ad miracula aptandum est. Nam & prophetiæ sunt miracula. Sed & illud addendum est: Sicut Deus terminum quemdam præscripsit Jamni & Mambri, ita & præfixum ab eo termi- num Simoni huic Mago & Apollonio Tyanæo postea: nempe ne omnia morborum genera subito sanarent, ne omnibus linguis loquerentur, ne mortuos ita excita- rent, ut diu in hac vita superstites ab omnibus conspici possint. Cur hoc? Nempe ut si qui novos Doctores secta- rentur, & dicerent se miraculis ad hoc adductos, refelli pos- sent inde, quod non plura tantum, sed & majora fecissent Christus & Apostoli: Unde sequebatur illos non alia de causa semet addixisse illis novis Magistris, quam quia dog- mata eorum carni blandirentur, quod etiam nunc, miracu- lis cessantibus evenit. Τέρατα ψέυδους sunt ea, quæ falsæ do- ctrinæ inserviunt. Nam quod vice Genitivi est apud Ebræos, sæpe finem significat, quem finem explicant verba Christi, Matth. XXIV. 24. quod hic sequitur 11. ostenta ista & pro- digia Simonis magica explicata habes apud Justinum, Ire- næum, Tertullianum, Cyrillum, Theodoreturn, Epiphanium.

## 2:9
Ὃυ ἐστιν ἡ παρουσία) whose is the coming. Ἐπάνοδος, a retrogression. For from the destruction of Simon he retrogresses to his deeds, so that he may more openly designate the man. Παρουσία, as just now of Christ, so here is said of Simon, and signifies the operation through which he made himself noble, ἐπίδειξιν; thus Cyril calls Simon ἐπιδεικνῦντα, showing himself off.

Κατ' ἐνέργειαν τοῦ Σατανᾶ) According to the operation of Satan.) Effectively through him, as formerly through Jannes and Jambres, acting not by God but by Satan. Justin Martyr in his second Apology concerning Simon Magus: διὰ τῆς τῶν ἐνεργούντων τέχνης δυνάμεις ποιήσας μαγικὰς, performing magical powers through the art of those who work. And shortly after concerning the same man and Menander: Ὃι καὶ φυσικὰς δυνάμεις ποιήσαντες πολλοὺς ἐξηπάτησαν, who also, performing natural powers, deceived many. Irenaeus concerning the Simonians: Love charms also and incantations and what are called familiars and dream-senders, and what other curious arts (read perierga from Acts 19:19) are studiously practiced among them. Tertullian on Idolatry: Magic punished in Simon. The same in his Prescription against Heretics: The Simonians, however, in the discipline of magic serving angels, was certainly itself also reckoned among idolatry, and was condemned by the Apostle Peter in Simon himself. Arnobius says he was trusting in false gods. Cyril: Ἐπαγ- γελλόμενον γὰρ τῷ Σίμωνι μετεωρίζεσθαι ἐπ' ὀφανὲς, κὶ ἐπ' ὀχήματος δαιμόνων ἐπ' ἀέρος φερομένου, for when Simon promised that he would be carried up into the sky, and was carried through the air on a vehicle of demons. Theodoret: He used every kind of incantation and trickery. Epiphanius: Ἐφαντα- σίαζε τὸ γένος τῶν Σαμαρειτῶν μαγγανείαις. He was deceiving the Samaritan race with magical arts, and shortly after: Πρόχειρος ὢν ἀπὸ τῆς ἑαυτοῦ κακίας τὰ βαρβαρικὰ καὶ δαιμόνων πράγματα

through his own sorcery to display. Since he was always ready, from his own malice to show off barbaric things, and the works of demons through his own magical ministry. But Sulpitius Severus concerning Simon: Who, when he had flown up with magical arts, supported by two demons, to prove himself God. Augustine: This man had deceived many with magical fallacies.

In all power and signs and wonders) in all power & signs & prodigies. Clement spoke of signs & prodigies in the history of Simon. Ambrose in VII to the Romans: nor if a mighty work has been done by someone, as it is said to have been done by Simon Magus, who is said to have flown up into the air so that he might be a stumbling block to the people of Christ, will it have to diminish our faith. Theodoret: By the operations of many wonderful & prodigious things which he performed, he persuaded them to approach him.

Lying) lying. He calls wonders of falsehood those things by which men are led into error. See Matt. XXIV. verse 23. & add Apocal. XIII. verse 24. where men are said to be deceived by those signs & prodigies. Simon sowed most grievous errors, when he drew the deeds of Christ, as also those of the Father and the Holy Spirit, to himself, denied that Christ truly suffered, said the world was made by Angels ignorant of the true GOD, that the Prophets were inspired by the same Angels, that men are saved by grace and faith in him in such a way that there was no need for pious deeds to be added, since by nature good and bad actions did not differ, but [only] by the institution of those Angels: Therefore also that martyrdoms were not to be undergone: but that they are free who follow him to do what they wish, even to worship idols, that the dead were not going to be resurrected. Irenaeus book I. chap. XX. For according to his own grace men are saved; but not according to just works. Add Origen, Cyril, Epiphanius, Augustine, Theodoret, following these up. This passage of Justin in his dialogue with Trypho pertains to certain Jews and at the same time to the Simonians: Not as you deceive yourselves and others like you in this, who say that even if they are sinners, provided they know God, the Lord will not impute sin to them. Not as you deceive yourselves, & others like you, who say that, even if they be criminals, while they know God, God will not impute crimes to them.

Latin:

Ὃυ ἐστιν ἡ παρουσία) cujus est adventus. Ἐπάνοδος, retro- gressio. Nam ab interitu Simonis retrogreditur ad fa- cta ejus, ut apertius hominem designet. Παρουσία ut mo- do de Christo, ita hic de Simone dicitur, significatque operationem per quam ille se nobilem fecit, ἐπίδειξιν, sic ἐπιδεικνῦντα ostentantem se Simonem Cyrillus dicit.

Κατ' ἐνέργειαν τοῦ Σατανᾶ) Secundum operationem Satanæ.) Efficaciter per ipsum, ut olim per Jamnem & Mambrem agente non Deo sed Satana Justinus Martyr Apologetico secundo de Simone Mago διὰ τῆς τῶν ἐνερ- γούντων τέχνης δυνάμεις ποιήσας μαγικὰς, magicas virtutes edens arte Dæmonum. Et mox de eodem & Menandro: Ὃι καὶ φυσικὰς δυνάμεις ποιήσαντες πολλοὺς ἐξηπάτησαν, qui & mira in rerum natura efficientes multis imposuerunt. Ire- næus de Simonianis: Amatoria quoque & agogima & quæ dicuntur paredri & oniropompi, & quæ sunt alia parerga (lege perierga ex Act. 19, 19.) apud eos studiose exercentur. Tertullianus de Idololatria: Magia in Simone punita. Idem de præscriptione hæreticorum. Simoniani autem magiæ disciplina Angelis serviens, utique & ipsa inter idololatriam deputabatur, & à Petro Apostolo in ipso Simone damnab- tur. Fidentem Diis falsis ait Arnobius. Cyrillus: Ἐπαγ- γελλόμενον γὰρ τῷ Σίμωνι μετεωρίζεσθαι ἐπ' ὀφανὲς, κὶ ἐπ' ὀχήματος δαιμόνων ἐπ' ἀέρος φερομένου, cum promitteret Simon in cælum se subvectum iri, & Dæmonum vehiculo per aerem ferretur. Theodoretus: Omni incantationum & præstigiarum genere utebatur. Epiphanius: Ἐφαντα- σίαζε τὸ γένος τῶν Σαμαρειτῶν μαγγανείαις. Samaritanam gentem artibus magicis decipiebat, & mox: Πρόχειρος ὢν ἀπὸ τῆς ἑαυτοῦ κακίας τὰ βαρβαρικὰ καὶ δαιμόνων πράγματα

διὰ τῆς ἑαυτῦ μαγγανείας ἐπιδείκνυσθαι. Cum semper promptus esset, ex sua ptemalitia ostentare res barbaricas, daemonumque opera per magicum suum ministerium. At Sulpitius Severus de Simone: Qui cum magicis artibus, ut se Deum probaret, duobus suffultus daemonibus evolasset. Augustinus: Hic magicis fallaciis deceperat multos.

Ἐν πάσῃ δυνάμει καὶ σημείοις καὶ τέρασι) in omni virtu- te & signis & prodigiis. Signa & prodigia in historia Si- monis dixit Clemens. Ambrosius in VII. ad Rom. ne- que si virtus ab aliquo facta fuerit, sicut facta dicitur à Si- mone mago, qui dicitur in aëra sursum, ut populo Christi scandalo esset, volasse, fidem nostram debebit minuere. Theodoretus: Admirabilium & prodigiosarum, quas effecit, rerum operationibus multis persuasit, ut ei acce- derent.

Ψεύδυς) mendacibus. Vocat τέρατα ψεύδυς ea, per quæ in errorem inducuntur homines. Vide Matth. XXIV. vers. 23. & adde Apocal. XIII. vers. 24. ubi per signa illa & prodigia decipi dicuntur homines. Gravissimos autem errores sevit Simon, cum Christi facta, ut & Patris & Spiritus sancti ad se traheret, Christum nega- ret vere passum, mundum diceret factum ab Ange- lis, DEI veri ignaris, ab iisdem Angelis inspiratos Prophetas, gratia, & in ipsum fide ita servari homi- nes, ut non opus esset pia facta accedere, quippe cum natura actiones bonæ malæque non differrent, sed ex Angelorum illorum instituto: Itaque nec martyria subeunda: sed liberos eos esse, qui se sectentur ad a- genda quæ velint, etiam ad idola adoranda, mortuos non iri resuscitatum. Irenæus libr. I. cap. XX. Secun- dum enim ipsius gratiam salvari homines; sed non se- cundum operas justas. Adde Originem, Cyrillum, Epi- phanium, Augustinum, Theodoretum, hæc exequen- tes. Ad Judæos quosdam simulque ad Simonianos pertinet Justini hic locus colloquio cum Tryphone: Ὀυχ ὡς ὑμεῖς ἀπατᾶτε ἑαυτὺς καὶ ἄλλοι τινὲς ὅμοιοι κατὰ τῦτο, οἱ λέγυσιν, ὅτι κὰν ἁμαρτωλοὶ, ὦσι, Θεὸν δὲ γινώσκω- σι, ὐ μὴ λογίσηται αὐτοῖς Κύριος ἁμαρτίαν. Non ut vos decipitis vosmetipsos, & alii quibusdam vobis similes, qui di- cunt, etiamsi criminosi sint, dum Deum norint, non impu- taturum ipsis Deum crimina.

## 2:10
V. 10. Καὶ ἐν πάσῃ ἀπάτῃ τῆς ἀδικίας) And this genitive signifies the end. For his deception tended toward this, that it might impel men to wicked deeds, or detain them in wicked deeds. Ἀδικία among Hebrew words has as its closest equivalent עָוֶל, which is translated both as παρανομία and ἀσέβεια, and it comprehends all more serious crimes, in which way this word is taken also in Luke 13:27, Rom. 1:18, 29, 2:8, 6:13, 2 Tim. 2:19.

Ἐν τοῖς ἀπολλυμένοις) In the manuscript, τοῖς ἀπολλυμένοις without ἐν, so that the dative depends on ἔστιν ἡ παρουσία. Nor does the Latin read it otherwise. It is, however, a present for a future. Men who are about to perish miserably are deceived by him. Thus 1 Cor. 1:18, 2 Cor. 2:15, 4:3. He understands the Samaritans first, then also the Romans.

Grotius has these things thus in his commentary.

Latin:

V. 10. Καὶ ἐν πάσῃ ἀπάτῃ τῆς ἀδικίας) Et hic Genitivus finem significat. Eo enim tendebat ejus deceptio, ut homi- nes ad flagitia impelleret, aut in flagitiis detineret. Ἀδικία inter Ebræas voces maxime respondentem habet עָוֶל, quod & παρανομία & ἀσέβεια vertitur, comprehenditque omnia crimina graviora, quomodo hæc vox sumitur & Luc. XIII. vers. 27. Rom. I. 18. 29. II. 8. VI. 13. 2. Tim. II. 19.

Ἐν τοῖς ἀπολλυμένοις) In Manuscripto, τοῖς ἀπολλυμένοις sine ἐν, ut dativus pendeat ab ἔστιν ἡ παρουσία. Nec aliter le- git Latinus. Est autem præsens pro futuro. Decipiuntur ab eo homines male perituri. Sic 1. Cor. I, 18. 2. Cor. II. 15. IV. 3. intelligit Samaritas primum, deinde & Romanos.

De his ita Grotius habet in sua comentatione.

## 2:10
And in all deception of iniquity) & in all seduction of iniquity. Such was the deception of Simon, that it drove men into very many crimes, which is sufficiently manifest from what was said before. Again here, according to the Hebrew custom, the effect is expressed by the Genitive case. He said all deception on account of the manifold deceptions, among which were also those fables about the harlot, whether Selene or Helene, whom he called the first thought. He mixed, however, the superstition of the Jewish Angel-worshippers with the fables of the Greeks, whose writings he had diligently read. An image of Simon was made and worshipped in the figure of Jupiter, [and one] of Selene in the figure of Minerva. See Irenaeus.

In those who are perishing) to those who are perishing. Among those who did not wish to believe the Gospel, and therefore are about to perish. Thus the same word is taken in 2 Cor. IV. verse 13. He understands, however, both the Samaritans and the Romans, and among these both the senate and the people, as Justin explains in his Apology II. Eusebius adds that sacrifices and libations were made to him.

These things cannot be referred to the arrival of Simon, when he came to Rome, because his tricks had already been exposed enough and more than enough in Syria. He explains as now continued what he had begun to say about the working of iniquity in verse 7. Whence these things cannot be snatched away to a different subject with Grotius, nor should they be dragged immediately to Simon Magus, which are read among the ancients concerning the working of Satan, since he has had his working in various [people], but especially in the Anti-Christ, also through Simony, which took its name from Simon, and magical arts, which shone forth sufficiently in the lives of the Pontiffs Sylvester II, Benedict IX, John XIII, Gregory VII, Alexander VI, Paul III, etc. & miracles, which were boasted of a thousand times more in the Papacy than by Simon, or even Apollonius of Tyana, whom Grotius, too easily deceived, rashly believed to have truly brought the dead back to life, and through fallacious dogmas, by which the Roman Anti-Christ strives to give assurance of faith through miracles no less than Simon Magus, among whose errors, while it is recorded that he ascribed salvation to grace without the merits of works, he could and should have learned from Irenaeus that he attributed it to his own grace and faith in himself as Simon, which Scripture refers to the grace of GOD and the life-giving faith of Christ. Moreover, when he names the arrival, he does not point to one single portent by which he was about to appear in the world, as if the efficacy of Satan were to exert itself in that alone, but he embraces the whole time of his reign. Nor indeed does he note a miraculous conception of the demon from a virgin, which fiction is attributed to Rabanus by Rupert and Bellarmine, and is defended as possible by Justinian, to the detriment of the miraculous conception of Christ from the Virgin Mary, Is. VII. verse 14, Jer. XXXI. verse 22. Furthermore, just as the Anti-Christ is not a singular person, so the things which Papists hand down concerning his conception, infancy, and manly age are mere dreams, unwritten, nay, counter-written. By power, not authority with Hugo, Lombard, Lyra, Hyperius, Aretius, which is already designated in verse 4, but wonder-working power is to be understood with Chrysostom and Theophylact, just as mighty works are called miracles, Matt. VII. verse 22, chap. XI. verse 21, 23, Luke IX. verse 3, 2 Cor. XII. 12.

Moreover, they will be τέρατα ψεύδος, lying wonders, both by reason of their form, because they are mere impostures, as when images are feigned to speak, to shed blood, to weep; and by reason of their end, because they are directed toward seduction into errors and lies. The Anti-Christ does not only employ his fabricated miracles to confirm lies, but he also wishes to be recognized by them, as if by a mark, as the Church, which is a true mark of the Anti-Christian communion. This is the principal reason for the designation. For they are called lying wonders, not so much because there is never anything preternatural or supernatural in them, as because they are designed to persuade of a ψεῦδος and ἀπάτην, a lie and an error. Ψεῦδος does not always, or rather rarely, signify fabricated things and actions, but for the most part the fiction of the end. Indeed, in this very doctrine concerning the Anti-Christ, it signifies falsity and error, distinct from hypocrisy, which hypocrisy is the midwife of a lie, 1 Tim. IV. verse 2. ψευδολόγων ἐν ὑποκρίσει, etc. Although, therefore, certain wonders of the Anti-Christ might be hyperphysical as to their substance, as those of other false prophets in the same place, Matt. XXIV. and VII. verse 23, yet by purpose and intention they are always lies, when they tend toward that which is not founded in the divine Word, and is called by the phrase of Scripture a lie, iniquity, etc. Job XIII. verse 4, Jerem. VIII. verses 5, 8, 10, Apoc. XXI. verse 27, chap. XXII. v. 15, to work a lie, to love a lie, etc., as the blessed Hülsemann rightly states in Brev. Extens. chap. XXII. page 457. Ἀπάτη τῆς ἀδικίας is an iniquitous seduction, and one toward iniquity, that is, error and sin. For the son of perdition was not to establish his authority at the beginning by force and arms, but primarily by seduction and fallacies. The Apostle names πᾶσαν ἀπάτην on account of the manifold deceptions not of Simon, but of the Anti-Christ and his ministers. Cornelius à Lapide reports a sixfold fallacy of his: affability in seeking the favor of men, feigned holiness, wisdom and eloquence, promises and largesse, signs and wonders, terrors and torments. These could easily be demonstrated concerning the Roman Anti-Christ and his retinue, whose kingdom is defended by (1) lies, (2) calumnies, (3) feigned revelations, (4) feigned miracles, (5) equivocations, (6) frauds and impostures, (7) false citations, (8) corruptions of Scripture, as Crocius proves at length here on page 326 and following. Τοῖς ἀπολλυμένοις not badly

Grotius explains that those who were unwilling to believe the Gospel, and are therefore about to perish, Joh. III. 18. Which name corresponds to the appellation of the seducer, who therefore is not different but that very one who is called υἱὸς τῆς ἀπωλείας, it is clear, who is also for that reason called Abaddon and ἀπολλύων Apoc. IX. 11.

Ἀνθ' ὧν τὴν ἀγάπην τῆς ἀληθείας οὐκ ἐδέξαντο εἰς τὸ σωθῆναι αὐτούς) Ἀνθ' ὧν signifies a just retribution, Luc. I. 20. XIX. 14. Act. XI. 23. Ἀγάπη ἀληθείας is said by metonymy to be God's benefit in revealing the truth to us, namely the Evangelical. By metonymy in the word ἀγάπης, Rom. V. 5. οὐκ ἐδέξαντο, they had not received, namely with effect. Thus we have δέχεσθαι Act. VIII. 14. XI. 1. XVII. 1. 2. Cor. XI. 4. & λαμβάνειν, Joh. I. 12. III. 11. Εἰς τὸ σωθῆναι αὐτοὺς, for if they had received the Gospel, they too would have been saved: and God was doing this προηγουμένως: But through their hardness another purpose succeeded, ὑπόμενον.

Latin:

Καὶ ἐν πάσῃ ἀπάτῃ τῆς ἀδικίας) & in omni seductione iniquitatis. Talis erat Simonis deceptio, ut homines in plurima scelera impelleret, quod ex ante dictis satis manifestum est. Iterum hic more Ebræo effectus per Genitivum casum exprimitur. Πᾶσαν ἀπάτην omnem deceptionem dixit propter multiplices deceptiones, inter quas & illæ fabulæ de scorto, sive Selene, sive Hele- ne, quam primam ἔννοιαν cogitationem dicebat. Misce- bat autem Judæorum Angelicolarum superstitionem cum Græcorum fabulis, quorum scripta diligenter le- gerat. Imago Simonis facta cultaque in figura Jovis, Selenes in figura Minervæ. Vide Irenæum.

Ἐν τοῖς ἀπολλυμένοις) iis qui pereunt. Apud eos, qui Evangelio credere noluerunt, ac propterea perituri sunt. Sic eadem vox sumitur 2. Cor. IV. vers. 13. In- telligit autem tum Samaritas tum Romanos, & in his tam senatum, quam populum, ut explicat Apologeti- co II. Justinus. Sacrificia ipsi & libamina facta addit Eusebius.

Non possunt hæc referri ad Simonis adven- tum, cum Romam venit, quia jam satis superque in Syria ejus technæ retectæ fuerant. Quæ de ἐνεργείᾳ τῆς ἀνομίας cœpta dixerat v. 7. jam con- tinuata explicat. Unde non possunt hæc ad di- versum subjectum abripi cum Grotio, nec ad Si- monem Magum illico trahenda, quæ de ἐνεργείᾳ τῦ Σατανᾶ apud veteres leguntur, quum in variis suam habuerit ἐνέργειαν, apprime autem in Anti- Christo, etiam per Simoniam, quæ à Simone no- men traxit, & artes magicas, quæ satis eluxere in vitis Pontificum Sylvestri II. Benedicti IX. Johan- nis XIII. Gregorii VII. Alexandri VI. Pauli III. &c. & miracula, quæ millies plura in Papatu ja- ctata, quam à Simone, vel etiam Apollonio Tya- næo, quem tamen vere mortuos in vitam revo- cœsse, nimis facilis decipi temere credidit Gro- tius, & per dogmata fallacia, quibus per miracula fidem facere Anti-Christus Romanus satagit cum suis non minus, quam Simon Magus, inter cujus errores dum refertur, quod salutem gratiæ adscri- pserit sine operum meritis ex Irenæo disci pote- rat ac debebat, suæ gratiæ & fidei in se Simoneæ tribuisse, quæ Scriptura refert ad DEI gratiam, & vivificam Christi fidem. Cæterum cum ad- ventum nominat, non unum tantum ostentum, quo proditurus erat in mundum, quasi in eo ef- ficacia Satanæ se sit exertura, sed totum tempus regni complectitur. Nec vero conceptionem mira- culosam opera dæmonis ex virgine futuram notat, quod commentum Rabano tribuitur à Ruperto & Bellarmino, & ceu possibile defenditur, in fraudem miraculosæ conceptionis Christi è Ma- ria virgine, Es. VII. vers. 14. Jer. XXXI. vers. 22. à Justiniano. Porro Anti-Christus uti non est singularis persona; ita quæ de conceptione, in- fantia, & virili ejus ætate Papistæ tradunt, mera somnia sunt ἄγραφα, imo ἀντίγραφα. Per δύνα- μιν non potestas cum Hugone, Lombardo, Ly- rano, Hyperio, Aretio, quæ jam vers. 4. desi- gnata, sed δύναμις θαυματουργικὴ intelligenda cum Chrysostomo & Theophylacto, uti δυνάμεις mi- racula dicuntur, Matth. VII. vers. 22. cap. XI. vers. 21. 23. Luc. IX. vers. 3. 2. Cor. XII. 12.

Erunt autem τέρατα ψεύδος prodigia mendacia tum ratione formæ, quia meræ imposturæ, ut cum simulacra finguntur loqui, sanguinem fun- dere, lacrymari; tum ratione finis, quia dire- cta ad seductionem in errores & mendacia. Non tantum adhibet Anti-Christus conficta sua mi- racula ad mendacia confirmanda, sed etiam inde agnosci vult, ceu per notam, Ecclesiam, quæ nota vera est Anti-Christianæ communionis. Præcipua hæc est ratio appellationis. Dicuntur enim pro- digia mendacia, non tam quod in iis nunquam sit aliquid præter aut supernaturale, quam quod ad persuadendum ψεῦδος & ἀπάτην mendacium & errorem sint comparata. Ψεῦδος non semper, imo rarius confictas res & actiones significat, sed plerumque fictionem finis. Quin & in hac ipsa doctrina de Anti-Christo falsitatem & errorem si- gnificat, distinctum ab hypocrisi, quæ hypocrisis est obstetrix mendacii, 1. Tim. IV. vers. 2. ψευδολό- γων ἐν ὑποκρίσει, &c. Quanquam igitur quædam prodigia Anti-Christi quoad substantiam suam essent hyperphysica, ut aliorum Pseudo-prophetarum d. l. Matth. XXIV. & VII. vers. 23. Proæresi tamen & intentione semper sunt mendacia, quan- do tendunt ad id, quod in Verbo divino fundatum non est, & phrasi Scripturæ vocatur mendacium, iniquitas, &c. Job. XIII. vers. 4. Jerem. VIII. vers. 5. 8. 10. Apoc. XXI. vers. 27. cap. XXII. v. 15. operari mendacium, diligere mendacium, &c. ut recte Beat. Hülsemannus Brev. Extens. cap. XXII. pag. 457. Ἀπάτη τῆς ἀδικίας est seductio iniqua, & ad iniquitatem, hoc est, errorem & pecca- tum. Non enim vi & armis suam initio stabili- turus erat autoritatem filius perditionis, sed ma- xime seductione & fallaciis. Πᾶσαν ἀπάτην no- minat Apostolus propter multiplices deceptiones non Simonis, sed Anti-Christi & ministrorum ejus. Cornelius à Lapide sextuplicem refert illius fallaciam: comitatem in hominum captanda gratia, simulatam sanctitatem, sapientiam & elo- quentiam, promissiones & largitiones, signa & prodigia, terrores & tormenta. Quæ facile de Romano Anti-Christo ejusque satellitio demon- strari possent, cujus regnum propugnari (1.) men- daciis, (2.) calumniis, (3.) fictis revelationibus, (4.) fictis miraculis, (5.) æquivocationibus, (6.) fraudibus & imposturis, (7.) falsis citationibus (8.) corruptelis Scripturæ, prolixe hic probat Crocius pag. 326. seqq. Τοῖς ἀπολλυμένοις non male

Grotius exponit eos, qui Evangelio credere nolue- runt, ac propterea sunt perituri, Joh. III. 18. Quod nomen respondet appellationi seductoris, quem proinde non esse diversum sed illum ipsum, qui υἱὸς τῆς ἀπωλείας dictus est, patet, qui & ideo A- baddon atque ἀπολλύων dicitur Apoc. IX. 11.

Ἀνθ' ὧν τὴν ἀγάπην τῆς ἀληθείας οὐκ ἐδέξαντο εἰς τὸ σωθῆναι αὐτούς) Ἀνθ' ὧν justam retributionem significat, Luc. I. 20. XIX. 14. Act. XI. 23. Ἀγάπη ἀληθείας dicitur per Μετωνυ- μίαν Dei beneficium in patefacienda nobis veritate, nem- pe Evangelica. Per μετωνυμία in voce ἀγάπης, Rom. V. 5. οὐκ ἐδέξαντο, non acceperant, nempe cum effectu. Sic δέχε- σθαι habemus Act. VIII. 14. XI. 1. XVII. 1. 2. Cor. XI. 4. & λαμβάνειν, Joh. I. 12. III. 11. Εἰς τὸ σωθῆναι αὐτοὺς, nam si accepissent Evangelium, servati & ipsi fuissent: idque age- bat Deus προηγουμένως: Sed per eorum duritiem succeslit propositum aliud ὑπόμενον.

## 2:10
Ἀνθ' ὧν τὴν ἀγάπην τῆς ἀληθείας οὐκ ἐδέξαντο) Because they did not receive the charity of the truth. That ἀνθ ὧν signifies a just retribution of God, Luc. I. 20. XIX. 14. Act. XII. 23. Understand Ἀγάπην τῆς ἀληθείας as the highest benefit of God sending His Gospel to them, Rom. IV. v. 8. And note that the first purpose of God is to do good to those to whom the word of salvation is announced, but by the fault of men another purpose succeeds.

Εἰς τὸ σωθῆναι αὐτούς) that they might be saved. For they too could have been saved through the Gospel, with God seriously acting for it.

Latin:

Ἀνθ' ὧν τὴν ἀγάπην τῆς ἀληθείας οὐκ ἐδέξαντο) Eo quod charitatem veritatis non receperunt. Illud ἀνθ ὧν justam Dei retributionem significat, Luc. I. 20. XIX. 14. Act. XII. 23. Ἀγάπην τῆς ἀληθείας intellige summum Dei be- neficium Evangelium suum ad eos mittentis, Rom. IV. v. 8. Et nota primum Dei propositum esse, ut benefa- ciat iis, quibus annuntiatur sermo salutaris, sed homi- num culpa succedere propositum alterum.

Εἰς τὸ σωθῆναι αὐτούς) ut salvi fierent. Poterant enim & illi servari per Evangelium serio id agente Deo.

## 2:11
Vers. 11.

Καὶ διὰ τοῦτο πέμψει αὐτοῖς ὁ Θεὸς ἐνέργειαν πλάνης) Manuscript, πέμπει, as if in the present tense. GOD sends upon the despisers of the Gospel a most powerful seduction, such as that of Simon was.

Εἰς τὸ πιστεῦσαι αὐτοὺς τῷ ψεύδει) So that they might give credence to a false doctrine. Compare the passage Prov. I. 29. 30. 31. For it pertains greatly to this.

Latin:

Vers. 11.

Καὶ διὰ τοῦτο πέμψει αὐτοῖς ὁ Θεὸς ἐνέργειαν πλάνης) Ma- nuscriptus, πέμπει, tanquam in re præsente. Evangelii con- temptoribus immittit DEUS seductionem prævalidam, qualis erat illa Simonis.

Εἰς τὸ πιστεῦσαι αὐτοὺς τῷ ψεύδει) Ita ut fidem adhibeant falsæ doctrinæ. Confer locum Prov. I. 29. 30. 31. Valde enim huc pertinet.

## 2:11
Καὶ διὰ τοῦτο πέμψει αὐτοῖς ὁ Θεὸς) therefore God will send to them. By wise permission and direction.

Ἐνέργειαν πλάνης) The operation of error. That is, most efficacious frauds, both by the ostentation of learning, and by the illusions of signs, and especially by that, that they flatter the flesh. Clement of Rome: And I have weakened the power of the demons for the fraud and destruction of men who are acting illicitly.

That they should believe the lie) that they may believe the lie. This is now the second purpose against the contumacious, of God punishing their contumacy, as if the light were withdrawn.

Latin:

Καὶ διὰ τοῦτο πέμψει αὐτοῖς ὁ Θεὸς) ideo mittet illis Deus. Sapienti permissu & directione.

Ἐνέργειαν πλάνης) Operationem erroris. Id est, frau- des efficacissimas, tum eruditionis ostentatione, tum si- gnorum præstigiis, tum eo maxime, quod carni blan- diantur. Clemens Romanus: Et Dæmonum vim labe- factavi in fraudem ac perniciem hominum illicitentium.

Εἰς τὸ πιστεῦσαι αὐτοὺς τῷ ψεύδει) ut credant men- dacio. Hoc jam secundum est adversus contumaces Dei propositum, contumaciam eorum ulcifcentis, velut sub- ducto lumine.

## 2:12
Ἵνα κριθῶσι πάντες οἱ μὴ πιστεύσαντες τῇ ἀληθείᾳ) that is, the Gospel.

Ἀλλ' εὐδοκήσαντες ἐν τῇ ἀδικίᾳ) A flagitious life pleases them, and they prefer Simon Magus to Christ: not because of miracles, which are greater and more divine in Christ, so that for that reason it may appear that they are rightly condemned, 1. Tim. IV. 3. The same Joh. III. 18. VII. 17. When some were worthy of his destruction, they remained in his discipline, says Clement concerning Simon.

He had handed down similar things in his commentary, which it pleases me to subjoin here also, so that one might have nothing to desire regarding the Grotian views. For thus he finishes that commentary of his on the present passage.

Latin:

Ἵνα κριθῶσι πάντες οἱ μὴ πιστεύσαντες τῇ ἀληθείᾳ) id est, Evangelio.

Ἀλλ' εὐδοκήσαντες ἐν τῇ ἀδικίᾳ) Placet illis vita flagitio- sa, & Simonem Magum Christo præferunt: non ob mira- cula, quæ in Christo majora & diviniora, ut ob id appareat, recte eos damnari, 1. Tim. IV. 3. Idem Joh. III. 18. VII. 17. Quidam cum essent pernicie illius digni, remanserunt in ejus disciplina, ait Clemens de Simone.

Similia tradiderat in commentatione, quæ hic etiam subjicere placet, ut nihil de Grotianis quis desiderare habeat. Sic enim finit suam illam ad locum præsentem commentationem.

## 2:12
That all might be judged who did not believe the truth) that all may be judged who had not believed the truth. That they may be convicted of their own malice. For since they believe such men because of certain prestige, why did they not rather believe Christ and his Apostles, who produced such great, such solid, and truly divine miracles? See Theodoret comparing these things.

But having taken pleasure in unrighteousness) But they consented to iniquity. This is the true reason why they believed Simon rather than Christ, because Simon's dogma provided them with a passage for enjoying whatever pleasures they wished, even the most iniquitous, a matter we have already dealt with. Those whose actions are evil prefer the darkness of false dogmas to the light of the Gospel, John III. 18. But he who wishes to do the will of the Father judges rightly concerning the dogma of Christ, John VII. 17. Lactantius, book VII of the Divine Institutes, chapter I, concerning men of this sort: They prefer that it be a fiction, by which they are compelled to renounce their desires. Likewise: Those who, incited by the furies of their lusts, as the Poet says, rush into furies and fire, certainly say that we bring forward incredible things, because we prohibit them from their pleasures, to which they have adjudged their soul along with their body. Clement of Rome concerning Simon: Some, while being worthy of his destruction, remained in his discipline.

These things, if you remove Simon, are correct, and therefore are undeservedly marked with censure by Maresius, to whom it is not approved that the love of the truth denotes the highest benefit of God in revealing the Evangelical truth; he prefers that it signify the love and study of truth (where, however, if anyone explains the love of the truth as the lovable truth, as Eph. 1. 18, the riches of glory, that is, rich glory, and 2 Thess. 1. 4, the fire of flame, that is, fiery flame, we will not object); those things which are said concerning the antecedent and consequent will are not approved; because he rashly and falsely calls it Socinian, and alien to the immutability of God. We showed the contrary in Vol. II of the System of Theology. Those things concerning those who perish are not approved.
